### Using RealPage Accounting Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 13*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

One of the backbones of company financial insight is reporting. There are many different types of reports, each 

with its own value to the company. If your company was created with a QuickStart setup template, financial and 

other standard reports are included. 

In addition to standard reports that are built into applications, you can create any number of financial and custom 

reports. You can start from nothing or install reports from libraries and customize them to meet your needs. 

Report Types 

There are three types of reports: 

• 
Standard 

• 
Financial 

• 
Custom 

You can create reports online or process and store them offline. You can also save (memorize) reports to run over 

and over again, saving you time. 

In This Chapter

#### Reports Center
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*



##### Finding and Filtering Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reports Center 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center`


The Reports center is a single page that provides visibility into all reports you can access, 

organizing them by application and type for easy access. From this page, you can: 

• 
Open, edit, and export a report 

• 
Set favorite reports 

• 
Create new reports 

• 
Filter the reports by application 

• 
View memorized and scheduled reports 

• 
View, edit, and run OneSite reports 

Finding and Filtering Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center`


You can search for reports by name or filter a list of reports by specific criteria to find the report 

you need.  

Searching for a Report 

You can find a report using the search function. 

To use the search function: 

• 
In the Search report center field, enter the report name or part of the report name as a 

search term. The system displays the results matching the search criteria. 

---


<!-- Page 15 -->
Chapter 1: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Using Default Filters 

Over time, companies create and use a large number of reports in addition to the standard 

reports for each application. Finding a report from a long list of reports can be daunting. In the 

Reports Center, however, you can limit which reports you want to see using filters. 

To use the default filters: 

1. 
Open the list of reports. 

2. 
Go to one of the following tabs which serve as the default filter options. 

• 
Favorites: Reports that you marked as favorites. You can make any report a favorite. 

• 
All reports: Public reports and reports that you have permission to access. You can use 

All reports in combination with an application filter to see all reports for one specific 

application. For example, you could select All reports and General Ledger to see all 

the G/L reports that are public and that you have permission to access. 

• 
Memorized: Standard reports that you memorized, or others memorized and made 

public. Memorizing a report gives the report a name and retains the report settings, so 

you don’t have to select them each time you want to run or display the report. 

• 
Scheduled: Reports that have a schedule and that you can access. You can schedule 

financial reports, memorized reports, and report groups. 

• 
My reports: Reports you own, created, or memorized; your report groups; reports 

memorized by others that you can access; and your financial reports and graphs. 

• 
Custom reports: Reports you create based on a variety of criteria. These reports can 

be saved to run again in the future or schedule an email delivery. 

• 
OneSite reports: Specific reports that you can view and run. 

Using Default Filter Icons 

Visual cues enable you to see some information immediately about a report. When a report uses 

a default filter element such as favorite or scheduled, an icon appears next to the report in the list. 

The icons are displayed even when the report isn’t selected. 

To use default filter icons: 

1. 
Open the list of reports. 

2. 
Use the following default filter icons as visual cues to identify a report: 

• 
Graph 

• 
Public report 

• 
Favorite 

• 
Memorized 

• 
Scheduled 

---


<!-- Page 16 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Report group 

Reports in the list can have multiple icons. 

Using Application Filters 

By default, your favorite reports are listed in the Favorites area, separated by type. To further 

refine the reports listed, select only the application you want reports for. The reports that the 

system shows must also meet the filter criteria above. For example, if you have the filter criteria 

set to show only Favorites, only the reports that are marked as favorites in the selected 

application are displayed. You can have one application selected at a time. 

To use the application filter: 

1. 
Open the list of reports. 

2. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select an application view to filter the list of reports. 

• 
All applications: Displays reports from all applications in the list. For example, if you 

are in the Reports center, you can select the Favorites tab as a primary filter and then 

select All applications to narrow the list of reports to ones that are marked as favorites 

across all applications. 

• 
Financial reports: Displays only financial reports. 

• 
(Application): Displays reports that are specific to one application. For example, you 

could select a filter that displays reports for Cash Management, Company, and so on. 

• 
Report groups: Report groups that meet the default filter criteria. For example, you 

can see all of your report groups across all reports.

#### Standard Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 17*



##### Filtering Standard Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 17*

Chapter 1: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Standard Reports 

Standard reports are reports that are typical to an application and have already been created for 
you. You can run standard reports as is or make modifications, such as setting filters to specify 
which items or time period to include or selecting from formatting options. 

Standard reports have predefined settings and defaults, such as the current month or day. You 
can set your report options to include only the data you want to display. 

Before you can export a standard report or add it to a group, you need to memorize the report 
(on page 24). 

The following list shows some examples of each type of standard report. 

Accounts Payable 

• 
Vendor aging 

• 
A/P invoice register 

• 
A/P recurring 

Accounts Receivable 

• 
Customer aging 

• 
A/R invoices analysis 

• 
Sales tax 

Cash Management 

• 
Cash balances 

• 
Cash analysis 

• 
Bank register 

General Ledger 

• 
Account balances 

• 
Trial balances 

• 
Journals 

• 
Chart of accounts 

Job Cost 

• 
Job cost activity 

• 
Cost code structure 

• 
Draw detail 

Filtering Standard Reports 

You can configure reports specific to your needs by setting filters. Depending on the report, you 
can select up to 30 filter options such as accounting period, custom date ranges, detail level, 
summary views, sorting, grouping, and dimensional analysis. 

Some standard reports are available in more than one application but usually have 
application-specific variations in filters and format.

#### Reporting by Application
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reporting by Application 

Each application has reports relating to that application, and you can create your own custom 

reports based on the company’s needs and uses. 

You can access reports in a couple of ways: 

• 
Most applications include a Reports menu with a list of common reports for that type of 

application. 

• 
For centralized report management, you can access all reports from a single location in 

Reports Center (on page 14). 

Report Settings Page 

The parameters you specify determine the content and format of the report. Most report settings 

pages include the following sections: 

• 
Time period 

• 
Filters 

• 
Format 

• 
Titles 

After filling out the report settings, click the View button to display the report with your specific 

data. To modify your settings, click the Customize button to return to the report settings page. 

You can save any modified settings to run the report at a later time. To save your report settings, 

click the Memorize button. Except for settings that you specify via prompts, the system 

remembers most settings for reports and displays your last selections when you return to them. 

This way, you don’t have to customize the settings each time you run a report. 

Report Page 

Click the View button on the report settings page to display the report in a format optimized for 

viewing in a browser. The following image shows an example of the Adjust Available Cash report 

page. 

You can click any link to display more details. 

Report Buttons and Output Options 

The following lists the available buttons and actions on the report settings page. 

• 
View: This button displays the report in your browser. 

• 
Print: This button displays the report in PDF format so you can print it or save it to your 

local drive. 

• 
Process & store: This button generates the report and stores it for later access. Available

#### Memorized Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Memorized Reports 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Memorizing a report retains the report parameters so you don’t have to select them each time 

you want to run or display the report. When you memorize a report, you can assign it a unique 

name so you can add the report to dashboards or report groups or schedule it to run on a 

recurring basis. We recommend that you test run the report with the desired parameters to verify 

that the report output is correct before memorizing the report. 

A memorized report can be public or private. Public reports are available to all system users. 
Private reports are available only to the report owner and system administrators. 

Memorized Reports Locations 

Memorized reports appear in the Memorized reports list and in the Reports center (on page 14). 

The Memorized reports list is accessible from most RealPage Financial Suite applications; 

however, it displays only the reports that were memorized in the application you access it from. 

For example, if you click the Memorized reports option in the Cash Management menu, then the 

list will include only reports memorized in Cash Management.

Filling In the Run This Report Section 

Use this section to define the time period that you want the report to cover.

Type the date or click the 
 Calendar button to select the date in the As of date field.

### All Units Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 29*



#### All Units Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 29*

Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

All Units Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > All Units`


The All Units report shows the unit SqFt, market rent (in dollars and per square foot rate), and 

make-ready status for each unit at the property. Occupied units show the resident’s name, 

move-in date, lease dates, lease rent, actual rent (in dollars per square foot), the current deposit 

amount on hand, and effective rent. Vacant units show lease and effective rents. 

The floor plan summary gives occupancy rates and square footage totals. It also lists the average 

market and lease rents, rent totals, loss to lease totals, the number of units made ready and not 

ready, and down units. 

An additional statistical summary is provided at the end of the report. It shows a variety of 

information to help make this one of your most useful reports. This section shows physical 

occupancy grand totals, the current exposure to vacancy by number and percentage, the recent 

moves and transfers, and a make ready status review. Finally, there is an analysis of rent totals by 

cost per square foot and percentage for occupied and vacant units. 

All Units Report Columns 

By default, the All Units report contains the following columns: 

• 
Bldg/Unit: This column displays the building and unit number. 

• 
Floorplan: This columns display the name of the floorplan used for the unit. 

• 
SQFT: This column displays the total amount of square footage for the unit. 

• 
Market Rent: This column displays the market rent price for the unit. 

• 
Amt/SQF: This column displays the amount per square foot for the unit. 

• 
Lease Rent: This column displays the lease rent for the unit. 

• 
Actual Amt/SQFT: This column displays amount per square foot for the unit based on the 
lease rent amount. 

• 
Name: This column displays the resident’s name of the unit. 

• 
Move-in: This column displays the date the resident moved into the column. 

• 
Lease Start: This column displays the date the lease term starts. 

• 
Lease End: This column displays the date the lease term ends. 

• 
Deposits On Hand: This column displays the amount of deposit was put down on the unit. 

• 
Made Ready: This column displays whether or not the unit was made ready in advance to 
move in. 

• 
Effective Rent: This column displays the current rent rate for the unit. 

These are the columns that appear when you initially install the report from the System financial 

reports list. You can configure additional columns by editing the report in the Financial report 

writer.

chose to include it on the report options page. Each column is totaled, with the exception of the 

first two columns. The totals consist of transaction code level balances and may not equal the

columns. 

Variance explanation This is the explanation for the variance. 

0-30 days 
This is the amount you owe to your vendor that is up to 30 days past

61-90 days

Delinquent and Prepaid Details: [Property]

This is the identifier of the unit described in the row.

Using RealPage Accounting Reports

Name 
This is the tenant name and contact information. 

• 
If you have started eviction proceedings on the tenant, an 
asterisk (*) appears beside the name. 

• 
If this is a business or corporation, an asterisk (*) or caret (^) 
appears beside the name, depending on the placeholder that 
was entered as the first name of the business. 

• 
If the business is also under eviction, the system flags the 
account with an asterisk; therefore, you may see “**” or “^*” 
beside the name of a business that is under eviction. 

Status 
This is the occupancy status, such as current tenant or applicant. 

Move-in/Out 
This is the date the tenant moved in or is scheduled to move in. If this is 
a former tenant, this is the move-out date. 

Charge code 
This is the charge code description. 

If a payment is allocated to a future charge and you chose to show 
prepaids as allocated, the code has “Future:” as a prefix. 

If there are multiple transactions, a Subtotals row appears below the 
last transaction. Separate totals are calculated for prepaid, delinquent, 
net balance, and aged amounts. 

Account 
This is the account number associated with the unit. 

Total prepaid 
This is the total amount of all open payments or credits associated with 
this charge code as of the current property date. 

Total delinquent 
This is the total of all open (or unpaid) transactions associated with this 
code as of the current property date. If a dagger symbol (†) appears 
beside an amount, the charge is delinquent due to NSF activity on the 
ledger. If a double dagger symbol (‡) appears, the charge is 120+ days 
past due. 

Net balance 
This is the net ledger balance as of the current property date. A negative 

amount is a prepaid balance; a positive amount is a delinquent balance. 

If the household has multiple transactions, the net balance prints in the 

Subtotals row and the total is: 

Total Prepaid (Subtotals) + Total Delinquent (Subtotals) 

If the subtotal has both a prepaid and delinquent balance resulting in a 
net balance of zero, the manual cash application feature is enabled in 
A/R settings, so credits (the prepaid balance) are not automatically 
applied to charges (the delinquent balance).

G/L account

Charge code

Similarly, the total net change of all G/L accounts will equal the grand 

total net change for the property.

The Bank Deposit Details (Excel) report lists the deposit receipts for a specific bank deposit control

### Lost Rent Summary Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 48*



#### Lost Rent Summary Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 48*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Lost Rent Summary Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Lost Rent 
Summary Report`


The Lost Rent Summary report reconciles lost revenue from concessions, miscellaneous credits, 

and vacancies. For each unit, the report lists market rent, lease rent (this is zero for vacant units), 

rent charged, the loss or gain to rent from vacancies, and concessions. 

Calculations 

The report calculates the non-revenue, vacancy loss, and vacancy recap amounts as of the last 

time the pre-close or close period process was run. For example, if you pre-close or close the 

period on February 16, the amounts reflect the vacancy costs calculated on February 16. If you 

advance the property date and generate the report again, the amounts do not reflect vacancy 

costs for the new date, but are the same amounts calculated on February 16. To show accurate 

vacancy costs, run the pre-close or close period process before generating the report. 

The data in this report ties to the Monthly Transaction Summary report. Generate this report to 

get additional information. 

Lost Rent Summary Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Lost Rent 
Summary Report`


The following columns print from left to right on the page. 

• 
Bldg-Unit: This is the building number (if used) and unit number. 

• 
Name: This is the head of household name. For vacant units, this is Vacant. 

• 
From/To: This is the fiscal period start and end date with these exceptions: 

• 
If a move-in occurred after the fiscal period start date, this is the new resident’s 

move-in date. 

• 
If a move-out occurred after the fiscal period start date, this is the resident’s move-out 

date. 

• 
If the dates are blank, this is an applicant, a former applicant whose lease was canceled 

or denied in a prior period, or a former resident who moved out in a prior period with 

rent (CA-types), concessions (PW-types), miscellaneous credits (PN-types), or gain/loss 

adjustments posted in the period. 

• 
Market Rent: This is base rent, floor plan, and unit amenities. If no amount is displayed, this 

is an applicant, a former applicant whose lease was canceled or denied, or a former resident. 

• 
Lease Rent: This is total CA-type charges and credits in scheduled billing. 

• 
Rent Charged: This is total rent (CA-type charges and credits) posted in the period. The 

difference between this item and Market Rent determines the Loss/(Gain) for the period. 

---


<!-- Page 49 -->
Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Concessions + Misc. Credits: This is total miscellaneous credits and concessions (PN- and 

PW-type codes). 

• 
Loss/(Gain): This is the loss or gain to lease in the period. Calculated as Market Rent - Lease 

Rent. 

• 
Loss/(Gain) Recap: This is the loss or gain to lease recaptured from the prior period. 

• 
Non-Revenue: This is the vacancy loss/gain to lease for this unit as of the last time the 

pre-close or close period process was run. OneSite calculates non-revenue costs only for 

units that are vacant and flagged as unavailable in property setup. 

• 
If the close or pre-close process has never been run during the period, this column 

shows 0.00 amounts for vacant units. 

• 
Vacancy Loss: This shows any amount of loss on the unit due to vacancy. It is the total 

vacancy loss/gain to lease on this unit as of the last time the pre-close or close period 

process was run. 

• 
If the close or pre-close process has never been run during the period, this column 

shows 0.00 amounts for vacant units. 

• 
Vacancy Recap: This is the total vacancy recapture for this unit as of the last time the 

pre-close or close period process was run. Recapture occurs when, for example, the fiscal 

period closing date is on the 25th and the prior month was closed with a unit that was 

vacant on the 25th. If a new resident moves into that unit on the 27th, a portion of the 

vacancy loss reported last month is recaptured at the close of the current month due to the 

prorated rent payment. 

• 
If the close or pre-close process has never been run in the period, this column shows 

0.00 amounts for vacant units. 

• 
Lost Rent: This is the amount of lost rent for this unit in the period. Calculated as 

Non-Revenue + Vacancy Loss + Vacancy Recap.

### Monthly Transaction Summary Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 50*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Monthly Transaction Summary Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Monthly 
Transaction Summary Report`


The Monthly Transaction Summary report shows delinquency and prepaid amount changes in the 

selected fiscal period and calculates the monthly rental potential. Use it to reconcile transactions 

with the general ledger when your accounting method is accrual. 

If you use the cash accounting method or the modified accrual to cash accounting method, then 

generate the Monthly Income Summary report each month to reconcile your general ledger. 

Your property should also use Site Data Exchange (SDE) to extract data. 

Report Sections 

This report has the following sections: 

• 
(By Group and Code): This section lists transactions by A/R category (CA – PZ) and 

calculates year-to-date and current month totals by transaction code. The last group on the 

page shows deposits created from prepaid funds during the FAS close account process 

(batch 935 transactions). 

• 
(Delinquency and Prepaid Balances): This section shows the delinquency and prepaid 

balances at the beginning of the period, the change during the period, and the balance at 

the end of the period. 

• 
If this section begins with a summary and includes information for subjournals, your 

property uses the advanced A/R processing method (multiple receivable accounting). 

Refer to Monthly Transaction Summary with G/L Account Detail for more information. 

• 
(By Group, Code, and G/L Account): This section lists current month transactions by group 

(CA - PZ), code, and description. G/L account numbers are listed along with the total debit 

and credit amounts for each transaction type. 

• 
(Monthly Rental Potential and Collection Losses): This section computes the monthly rental 

potential and categorizes rent into gross market rent and gain/loss to old lease. 

Out of Balance Conditions with Accounting 

Transactions not extracted as journal entries to your accounting system cause this report to be 

out of balance with accounting reports when you run it in the middle of the period. That is, this 

report will tie to reports in your accounting system only after you close the period and before you 

advance the property date into the new period. You should wait until you close the period before 

attempting to reconcile this report with your accounting reports. 

The conditions below outline the possible reasons why this report can be out of balance with your 

accounting reports: 

---



#### Monthly Transaction Summary Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 51*

Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Transactions have been posted in OneSite that haven’t been extracted to your accounting 

system yet. 

• 
Changes to transaction code settings, the accounting method, or G/L mappings were made 

during the month. 

Monthly Transaction Summary Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Monthly 
Transaction Summary Report`


The Monthly Transaction Summary report provides property A/R balances. 

The following columns print, from left to right on the page. 

(By Group and Code) 

This section groups transactions into charges, payments, and deposits (C, P, and I transaction 

categories) and totals each group separately. 

• 
Group: This column shows the A/R transaction category code. The last group on the page is 

the 935 batch or transaction group. 

• 
Code: This column shows the A/R transaction code. 

• 
Description: This column shows the transaction code description. 

• 
YTD at End of Last Month: This column shows the total posted for this transaction code 

through the end of the previous fiscal period. 

• 
Activity for This Month: This column shows the total posted for this transaction code in the 

fiscal period. 

• 
YTD Through This Month: This column shows the total posted for this transaction code 

year-to-date through this month. 

• 
Total: This row prints below each group and totals each of the monthly activity columns. 

(Batch 935 Transactions) 

This section appears if you have 935 batch transactions. 935 batches occur when the system 

moves prepaids between the resident and deposits ledgers during the FAS close account or edit 

account process. 

• 
Group: This column indicates 935 batch transactions from FAS activities. 

• 
Code: This column shows the payment code the system used to move prepaid transactions 

to the deposits ledger during the FAS process or the resulting deposit code. (The system 

uses the codes specified on the Transactions – General Settings page.) 

The IU-DEPMoveDep total is the total amount of deposits created from prepaid funds during the 

FAS close account process. 

The PZ-type items are the total prepaid items (payments and non-cash credits) moved between 

ledgers during the close account process. Non-cash credits are any P-type transactions other than 

---


<!-- Page 52 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports

PZ transactions. The PMTMoveDep system code totals all non-cash credits. You may or may not 

see this code as it depends on whether any non-cash credits were moved during the FAS process. 

The PZ-type items sum to the IU-DEPMoveDep total. 

To reconcile the IU-DEPMoveDep total, generate the Bank Deposits Detail report for batch 935 for 

the current period, or generate the Resident Deposit Activity report to determine the applicants 

or residents who have “deposit split from payment” transactions. You can then look up these 

transactions on each respective resident ledger to reconcile the prepaid monies moved. Any 

“deposit split from payment” transaction associated with batch 920 indicates a payment moved to 

the deposits ledger manually in the current fiscal period.

transaction code. 

•

ledgers. 

•

This section shows delinquency and prepaid balances at the beginning of the period, the change 

during the period and the balance at the end of the period. 

• 
Description: This column describes the following delinquency and prepaid amounts: 

• 
Delinquency at beginning of period: This delinquent amount is the past due balance as of 

the beginning of the reporting period. 

•

during the current report period. 

• 
Total delinquent at end of period: This total is the past due balance as of the end of the 

reporting period. 

• 
Prepaid at beginning of period: This prepaid amount is the balance as of the beginning of 

the reporting period. 

•

report period. 

•

reporting period.

•

Delinquent Amount column. If the difference is negative, then a prepaid balance

If there is G/L activity that has not been posted or extracted to your accounting 

system, then the following note appears below the total: 

§§ There is A/R activity in this report that has not been posted as a journal entry to 

accounting. As a result, this report may not balance to accounting. 

The note is for informational purposes only and serves as a reminder that the 
Monthly Transaction Summary report will not balance with your accounting system 
when non-extracted data exists. After you close the period, the system finalizes all 
journal entries and posts them to your accounting system. If you run the report after 
you close the period but before you forward the property date into the new fiscal 
period, the report should balance with your accounting reports at that time. 

(Monthly Rental Potential Computation and Monthly Collection Losses) 

This section shows the monthly potential rent and possible monthly collection losses by category. 

(Category Name) 

Monthly Rental Potential Computation 

This column lists the possible revenue from rent per the current leases. 

• 
Gross market rent: This total is the possible rental income for the property based on market 

rent. OneSite uses the current market rent either on the first day of the month or the last 

day of the current period per the “calculate vacancy based on first of month billing” setting 

---


<!-- Page 54 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

in A/R setup. The system calculates the potential value for a unit as (Market Rent ÷ 

Maximum Number of Days in the Month) × Days Occupied = Potential Value. 

• 
If the number of days occupied is less than the maximum number of days in the 

month, then this is the potential value. If the number of days occupied equals the 

maximum number of days in the month, then the potential value (or gross market 

rent) equals the market rent. 

• 
Gain to old lease: This column shows the total of any gains in market rent for existing 

leases. If the number is negative, it is a gain to lease. Calculated as Potential Value – Actual 

Charged Rent. 

• 
Loss to old lease: This column shows the total of any losses in market rent for existing 

leases. If the number is positive, it is a loss to lease. 

• 
Gross potential monthly per leases: This column shows the gross potential revenue per 

lease. Calculated as Total Gross Market Rent + Gains to Old Leases – Losses to Existing 

Leases. 

• 
Total other monthly charges: This section totals each non-rent charge posted in the period. 

• 
Total possible monthly collections: The total possible monthly revenue. Calculated as  

Gross Potential Monthly Per Leases + Total Other Monthly Charges. 

Less Monthly Collection Losses 

This section lists any concessions and discounts given during the period, any deposits applied to 

charges, losses to uncollectibles, and miscellaneous credits. If you have batch 935 transactions, 

the “Prepaids moved to deposit ledger (935 batch)” total is also provided. 

Less Adjustments 

• 
Adjust prior gross market rent: This row shows any adjustments (changes) made to market 

rent in the prior period. 

• 
Adjust gain to old lease prior month: This row shows any adjustment to last month’s close 

due to move-ins, move-outs, and manual postings before the first day of this calendar 

month. If you decrease the rent while an existing lease is still in effect, then there will be a 

gain to the old lease until the lease expires, and this adjustment offsets that gain. 

• 
Adjust loss to old lease prior month: This row shows any adjustments to last month’s close 

due to move-ins, move-outs, and manual postings before the first day of this calendar 

month. If you raise the rent while an existing lease is still in effect, then there will be a loss to 

the old lease until that lease expires, and this adjustment offsets that loss. 

• 
Adjust last month vacancy: This occurs when, for example, the fiscal period closing date is 

on the 25th and the prior month was closed with a unit vacant. A new resident moved into 

the vacant unit on the 27th, so at the close of the current month, a portion of the vacancy 

loss from last month is recaptured due to the new resident’s prorated rent payment. 

• 
Less adjustments: The total of the preceding adjustments.

Past Dues/Prepaids

Past due end of prior month: The total of past due charges unpaid as of the end of the 

prior month. 

• 
Prepaid end of prior month: The total of payments un-applied to charges as of the end of 

the prior month. 

• 
Past due end of current month: The total of unpaid charges that will become past due at 

the end of the current month. 

•

to charges in the current month.

(Totals): The following totals print at the bottom of the page:

(PZ-type transactions). 

• 
Current monthly refundable deposits: The total deposits received in the current month 

(I-type transactions). 

• 
Total monthly collections: Calculated as Current Monthly Rental Collections + Current 

Monthly Refundable Deposits.

### Rent Roll Detail (Excel) Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 56*



#### Rent Roll Detail (Excel) Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 56*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports

Rent Roll Detail (Excel) Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Rent Roll Detail 
(Excel) Report`


The Rent Roll Detail (Excel) report is a comprehensive snapshot of units at your property as of a 

specified date. It lists resident billings and lease data, providing the same information as the 

standard Rent Roll Detail report, except in an Excel format, which makes it easy to sort and filter 

information. 

Sheet 1 shows the detailed unit and lease information. For each unit, the floor plan, square 

footage, occupancy status, and market rent are reported. For occupied units, the report shows the 

head of household name, lease dates, deposits on hand, and the ledger balance as of the report 

date. It also lists resident scheduled billings by transaction code and the billing amount of each 

code. If a current resident has a Renewed status, the report displays information for both the 

current and renewal leases. 

Sheet 2 shows average market and lease rents by floor plan. Sheet 3 calculates rent and potential 

rent by occupancy status, and summarizes billings by transaction code and subjournal. 

Rent Roll Detail (Excel) Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Rent Roll Detail 
(Excel) Report`


For each unit, current lease information prints on the first row; additional rows print for applicants 

and former residents. Dates print in the mm/dd/yyyy or dd/mm/yyyy format depending on the 

country selected for the property in the regional options settings.

associated with the lease at notice.

(Rent): The column name is the rent type selected in the Show unit rent as option at report 

generation: 

Market Rent: This is base rent plus amenity rent. Base rent is the total of CA-type 

transactions scheduled for the floor plan and unit. Amenity rent is the total of 

unit-priced amenities assigned to the unit. 

Market +Addl: This is market rent plus the total of non-CA type transactions 

scheduled for the floor plan or unit, and the transactions are not grouped in the 

effective rent transaction code group. 

Effective Rent: If the property uses transaction code groups in New OneSite and has 

an effective rent group in effect as of the report date, this amount is calculated as 

[(Total Charges in Scheduled Billing in the Effective Rent Group × Number of Months 

in Lease Term) – (Concessions Posted in the Resident Ledger + Next Scheduled 

Concession)]  ÷ Number of Months in Lease Term.  

If no effective rent transaction code group is enabled or in effect, this is calculated as 

[(Total CA-Type Charges in Scheduled Billing × Number of Months in Lease Term) – 

(Concessions Posted in the Resident Ledger + Next Scheduled Concession)] ÷ Number 

of Months in Lease Term. 

The effective rent calculation applies to the All Units (PDF and Excel) and Box Score 

reports.

Resident Balances by Fiscal Period Report (Reports) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Resident Balances 
by Fiscal Period Report`


The Resident Balances by Fiscal Period report shows ledger information for applicants and 

residents by fiscal period and subjournal. When generated for all resident statuses, the report 

includes miscellaneous income balances. 

For each account, the report shows beginning balances, total charges and credits posted during 

the fiscal period, ending balances, and the net change. The report also includes deposit balances, 

move-out or lease end dates, and summaries by transaction code and G/L account.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Resident Balances

The Resident Balances by Fiscal Period report provides account balances by name and subjournal 

and totals all accounts in the fiscal period. The Resident Balances by Fiscal Period report columns 

print from left to right on the page. 

• 
Bldg/Unit: This column shows the building number (if used) and unit number. This is blank 

for miscellaneous income accounts.

the first day of the fiscal period for this account.

fiscal period for this account. Calculated as Beginning Prepaid Balance + Beginning 

Delinquent Balance.

For transfers, the report shows the resident’s name and balances under the new unit.

*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 69*

Resident Deposit Audit by Fiscal Period Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports > Resident Deposit 
Audit by Fiscal Period Report`


The Resident Deposit Audit by Fiscal Period report is helpful when you are reconciling misplaced 

payments or overpayments. It lists the total required deposit transactions in the deposits ledger, 

the amount of deposits paid in (deposits on hand), and the variance for applicants and residents 

accounts. The report excludes former residents with no deposits on hand and no deposits 

required because these accounts have no deposits to reconcile. 

Online Leasing 

If your property uses Online Leasing and you include applicants in the report, then deposits from 

online applications entered through the leasing portal are also reported. Reconcile these deposits 

using the online application fees ledger on the Miscellaneous Income page.

Audit by Fiscal Period Report`

Transaction Summary by Unit Report

Summary by Unit Report`


The Transaction Summary by Unit report summarizes charges, payments, and deposits activity by 

unit number. Generate this report for all units or a specific unit number and for miscellaneous 

income. 

Waitlists 

Transactions post to the ledger by unit number “Wait” for applicants on the waitlist. After the 

applicant selects a unit, the report lists it in order by unit number along with the total transactions 

posted to the applicant’s ledger by charge or payment category. To view a report that lists 

transactions by resident rather than unit, generate the Resident Summary Balances report instead. 

Transaction Summary by Unit Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > OneSite Reports >Transaction 
Summary by Unit Report`


The Transaction Summary by Unit report provides charge, payment and credit, and deposit 

activity for the date range or scheduling period. The following columns print from left to right on 

the page. 

• 
Bldg-Unit: This is the building number (if used) and unit number. For miscellaneous income 

activity, Misc appears. For waitlisted applicants, Wait appears. 

Activity posts by unit number. For waitlisted applicants, activity posts to the unit number 
named Wait at the bottom of the report. Upon selecting a unit, the applicant’s new activity 
posts to the unit number. The report lists the waitlist activity separately from the unit 
activity, so a person who starts on the waitlist appears twice in the report. 

• 
Name: This column lists the head of household name. For miscellaneous income activity, 

this is the account description. 

Prepaids moved to deposit ledger appears below the name for a former resident or 
applicant whose ledger had prepaid transactions moved to the deposits ledger during the 
FAS close account or edit account process. 

• 
PCF: This column lists the one-letter resident status code. This column is blank for 

miscellaneous income and waitlisted applicants. 

• 
P is a pending resident. 

• 
C is a current resident. 

• 
F is a former resident.

•

### Custom Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 81*

Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Custom Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > Custom Reports`


In addition to standard and financial reports, you can build custom reports. Create custom reports 

to get insight and answers from the unique information stored in your system. Financial reports 

are based on account groupings such as assets and liabilities, while custom reports and 

dimension structures are based on records and fields either grouped together or separately. 

For example, you can create a custom report that displays vendor contact information. You can 

control which vendors you want to display, such as active vendors in certain regions, and select 

the details to include about the vendors. You can then sort and display the results to highlight 

what is most important to you. 

With a custom report, you can: 

• 
Report on fields from almost any record or transaction in the system, and any related data. 

• 
Customize the report for your needs. 

• 
Run the reports, export them in another format, or add them to dashboards. 

Before you can export a report or add it to a group, you need to memorize the report (on 
page 24).  

Creating Custom Reports 

Custom reports are created with the custom report wizard, which walks you through the steps to 

create a report. Only users who have permission to Customization Services can add and edit 

reports by going to the Custom Reports list on the Customization services menu. 

You can run the custom report from the Reports application. 

Adding a Custom Report to an Application’s Menu 

If you use a custom report on a regular basis, you can add the custom report to an application’s 

menu. For example, a report with payables-related data can be added to the Accounts Payable 

menu. After adding a custom report to the A/P menu, you can run the custom report by clicking 

the Custom Reports menu option, which displays a list of all of the custom reports that you have 

added to the Accounts Payable menu. 

The Custom Reports option displays on menus only after you (or someone else) has added at 

least one custom report to the application’s menu. The Custom Reports option does not appear 

on a menu if no one has added any custom reports to the application’s menu.

### Custom Report Wizard

#### Selecting the Primary Data Source
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 84*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Custom Report Wizard 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > 
 Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
 Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > New Report > Custom Report > 
Create with Custom Report Wizard`


Use the Custom report wizard to create specialized reports from your company data. Unlike 

financial and standard reports, custom reports can include financial or non-financial data, or both, 

drawing on data from existing fields or your company’s custom fields. 

Selecting the Primary Data Source 

Choose a record or transaction as a starting point for your report. 

Records 

A record is any piece of information in your company. The records available for selection are 

based on your user permissions; you cannot select a record you don’t have access to. When a 

record is selected, other related information is available for inclusion in your report. 

For example, if you select Customer as your primary data source, you can include column 

information from the Contact, Parent customer, or Customer type records. 

When you run a custom report for Reconciliation Records, this custom report displays all general 
ledger transactions included in a pending bank reconciliation list, giving you clearer visibility into 
reconciliation status and progress. To see a complete list of your pending bank reconciliations, 
see Pending Bank Reconciliations List. 

Transactions 

You can select a transaction type as your primary data source, such as A/P invoice, A/R 

adjustment, or Deposits. These options include all header information in the transaction record. If 

you want to include the header information plus any amounts and line-item details from the 

transaction, then select the data source option labeled “detail,” such as A/P invoice detail, A/R 

adjustment detail, or Deposits details. This allows you to access transaction amounts and use the 

custom report writer to add calculated columns later in the process. 

For example, to list all invoices with line items over $10,000, you can start by choosing the data 

source A/P invoice detail. Your report can include columns of information from A/P invoice 

details and related data. 

When you run a custom report for User Permission Activity, this custom report only shows 
permissions which have been explicitly activated by an administrator. There are other 
permissions which are switched on by other applications, called derived permissions. To see a 
complete list of your permissions, run a User Permissions report.

#### Defining Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 85*

Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Defining Columns 

Define the columns in your report using the following procedures. 

Add Columns 

Select the data that you want to add to your report. Each check box represents one column in the 

report. 

It is better to include more information than you need at this point in creating your report. In 
later steps, you can refine which data to display. 

The following icons are used to help you identify information you want to use in your report: 

• 
: identifies a linked field. When you run the report, you can see more information by 

clicking the link. 

• 
: identifies a custom field. 

Viewing custom fields is dependent on your permissions. If you include custom fields in 
your report and then deploy the report to an application, the custom fields might or might 
not be visible to other users, depending on their permission levels. 

• 
: identifies an expandable subsection of the primary data source. If a subsection is also a 

data source, when you expand it, the system displays the data source’s subsections with 

additional data, possibly even additional subsections, that you can include as columns in 

your report. 

For multi-entity companies: Click Created at entity information below a transaction or object, 
and then select what you want to track. For anything created at the top level, the report will 
show a blank entry. 

Add Calculated Columns 

The custom report writer also allows you to create column calculations based on the columns you 

selected. 

---


<!-- Page 86 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

For example, you can calculate an employee’s commission by multiplying their commission rate 
by the total number of sales invoices attributed to that employee. When you run the report, the 
system displays the calculation in the report in a column with the name you assigned. 

You can add calculations by creating a formula uses columns of information from your data 
source. This lets you perform operations on other columns in your data source and then show 
results in your report. 

The formulas created follow the mathematical order or operations. Keep the following order of 
operations in mind when you create a formula: 

• 
Calculations inside parentheses are performed first. 

• 
All multiplications and divisions are performed next, working from left to right. 

• 
Lastly, all additions and subtractions are performed, working from left to right. 

To create a formula for a calculated column: 

Calculations can only be applied to columns containing numbers. 

1. 
Click the Add button. 

The system opens the Formula Editor box. Use this editor to create a formula from any of 
the information in your primary data source. You can add multiple columns and operator, 
depending on the calculation you want to display. 

2. 
In the Available Report Columns pane, select the column containing the data you want to 
include in the calculation. For example, select AP Invoice Detail Total Due. 

The system adds an expression in the Formula pane. 

---



#### Filtering the Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 87*

Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

3. 
Use the basic math operators (addition +, subtraction -, multiplication *, and division /) and 

parentheses to create a formula. For example, click the subtraction operator under the 

Operators column. 

4. 
In the Available Report Columns pane, select the column containing the date included in 

the calculation. For example, select AP Invoice Detail Transaction amount. 

The system displays an expression for the transaction in the Formula pane. 

5. 
In the Calculated column type drop-down list, select the formula format. 

6. 
In the Calculated column name field, enter a label for the column. 

Select the Column Sequence 

1. 
Drag columns into the order that you want the system to display them in your report. 

2. 
Optionally, use the text box to rename columns in the report. 

Add Column Totals 

Select the check boxes next to the columns for which you want to display a summary. You can 

only perform mathematical summaries, such as count, sum, average, std deviation, variance, 

largest, and smallest, on numeric data fields. Text fields are limited to count summaries. 

In a report without grouping, the system displays the calculations at the bottom of the report for 

the entire table. In a report with grouping, the system displays the calculations for each subgroup 

and for the entire table. 

Sort the Columns and Set the Priority 

1. 
Click the drop-down list next to each column title. 

2. 
Select whether you want to sort the column in Ascending or Descending order, or None. 

You can assign an ascending or descending order to a maximum of four columns. 

3. 
Drag and drop the columns in the list to change the sorting priority. 

The column in the first position will be sorted first, the next column down will be sorted 

within the first, and so on. 

Filtering the Report 

You can use filters in your report to limit the data the system displays to the criteria that you 

choose. 

Select a Filter 

You set the first group of filters when you select the columns from your primary data source. 

Other information related to your primary data source are available to use as filters as well and 

are listed under the first group of filters as expandable objects. 

1. 
Expand the object that has the column or field you want to filter. 

---


<!-- Page 88 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

2. 
In the Columns column, click a drop-down list, and then select the column by which you 

want to filter. 

3. 
In the Operator column, select the operator you want to use to filter the column. 

See the list of available operators (on page 93). 

4. 
In the Value column, enter the corresponding value. 

This can be a number or a string of text depending on the chosen operator. If you choose 

Includes or Excludes, the value could be a comma delimited list of numbers or text strings. 

5. 
Click the Add filter link below the columns to add more filters in the object. 

6. 
Click the Delete last filter link to remove a filter field. 

Refine the Filters 

By default, all filter conditions are combined with an AND logic. In this step, you can apply more 

advanced logic using OR conditions and group filters. 

1. 
Review the filters you added in the previous step. 

The system displays filter position numbers, which you can use to create your advanced 

filter statement. 

2. 
In the Filter expression field, combine filter position numbers using logical operators and 

parentheses. 

For example, you want to filter a report to display transactions for customer accounts within 

the 2010-3010 range or the 6010-7010 range, and the total paid amount is greater than 0.

#### Grouping Data
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 89*

Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Grouping Data 

Enable Grouping 

Set the level of detail you want the system to display in your report by selecting the appropriate 

grouping option. 

• 
No grouping: Select this format if you want to display a flat list of information, with the 

option to show a grand total at the bottom. For example, you can use this format to display 

a list of employees with their contact information, or a list of invoices with their total dollar 

value. 

• 
Grouping: Select this format if you want to arrange the information together and show 

subtotals for grouped rows. By default, the report shows subtotals based on the groups you 

select in succeeding steps. The system automatically includes totals by group. For example, 

you can use this format to display invoice subtotals by customer and invoice totals for all 

customers. 

Group Data by Columns 

You can only group data by columns if you enable the Grouping option in the previous step. 

1. 
Expand the object that contains the column by which you want to group the report. 

2. 
Select the column from the drop-down list. 

When you select multiple columns, the system creates subgroups in the report. 

Grouping the data by more than three columns could distort the data. As a best practice, 
only group by three or less columns. 

Order the Groups 

You can set which groups take priority when sorted. The system sorts the items first by the first 

column, and then by the second column, and so on, creating multiple levels of summary 

information. 

1. 
In the Position column, select the button next to the column you want to move. 

2. 
If a column has child columns, select the Include Children check box to enable the feature. 

3. 
Use the 
 Top, 
 Up, 
 Down, and 
 Bottom arrows to change the sorting priority 

of the column. 

4. 
In the Sort column, use the corresponding drop-down list to select whether you want to 

sort your columns in ascending or descending order. 

Group Totals 

In a report with grouping, the system displays the calculations for each subgroup and for the 

entire table. Select the desired column totals in the Add more totals step. For more information, 

see Defining columns (on page 85).

Setting the Report Date and Title 

You can set parameters for running the report, such as the reporting period and the title of the 

report. 

1. 
Select a reporting period or a range of dates. 

• 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select monthly, quarterly, or annual options 

that include next, current, and past periods. You can modify this time period by adding 

an As of date value. 

• 
In Start date and End date fields, select an exact date range for the report. 

2. 
Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

your company is comprised of multiple entities with multiple base currencies, set the 

location and department. 

• 
Select the Location and Department for which you want to run the report. 

• 
In the Show for drop-down list, select whether you want to display All locations, This 

location, or Child locations, regardless of the location you selected in the Location 

field. 

If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule 

Financial Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box 
to schedule reports and reports groups to run at that time. 

3. 
In the Show details field, select whether you want to hide or display the detail lines that 

make up the calculated amounts. Hiding the detail gives you a high-level breakdown of the 

data, showing just subtotal and total calculations. 

4. 
Set the report title and footer. 

• 
In the Report title 1 and Report title 2 fields, enter the first and second lines of the 

report title, respectively. 

• 
In the Footer text field, add information you want to display at the bottom of the 

report pages. 

Titles and footers can use letters, numbers, spaces, and most punctuation. The system 

does not support wild cards and variables. 

Defining the Chart Output 

You can choose to run a chart format to visually display your information. 

1. 
In the Chart type drop-down list, select the type that works best for your report. The default 

option is the Column type. 

To view examples of each type of chart, see Creating graphs from custom reports (on page 

96).

Sometimes a graph is an easier way to view report information. After defining the chart output,

Adding Prompts 

The additional prompts you can add at runtime are similar to filters, in that they filter the data 

according to the criteria you set. Unlike filters, these prompts are set up as fields that the user 

specifies at the time they run the report. For example, if you want the user running the report to 

specify the A/R status regarding the invoice from which the item comes, you can add a prompt 

for the A/R Account Label object, and then select the Status field. 

To select a runtime prompt: 

1. 
Expand the section for the object that contains the field. 

2. 
Select the check box next to the field for which you want to add a prompt. 

3. 
Repeat the steps to add more prompts. 

You can select up to six runtime prompts. 

If you run the report from the Custom reports list, the system ignores the filters and runs the 

report without any prompts. To ensure that all your filters and prompts are applied, run the 

custom report from the application in which you saved it. Learn more about saving a report to a 

menu (on page 92). 

Labeling and Grouping Prompts 

You only need to label and organize prompts if you chose to include additional prompts in the 

previous step of the custom report writer. 

This page allows you to control how a prompt field will be labeled, how multiple fields will be 

grouped, and whether it will have a prompt at runtime.

Change the Prompt Label 

By default, the name of the field is provided as the Prompt Label. 

To change the Prompt Label, click the Prompt label field and type the label you prefer. 

Group Prompts 

The Group field allows you to present your prompts in groups when you run the report. 

For example, if you want to group several fields together in a section titled A/R Parameters, for 

each field, type “A/R Parameters” in the Group column. 

On a report with several prompts, grouping fields with meaningful labels can save time for the 

person running the report. 

To add a group, click the Group field, and then type the name of the group you are creating. 

To group all prompts under one label, enter one group name in the top Group field. To group 
prompts under different group names, put different group names in the Group field.

Saving the Report 

The final step of the custom report writer allows you to save your report and add your report to 

an application menu. This makes it available to other users who have access to that application. 

Save and Deploy Your Report to an Application Menu 

1. 
In the Name field, type your preferred report name. 

2. 
Select the Add to menu check box. 

To access your report only through the Custom reports list, leave the Add to menu check 
box clear. However, we recommend that you add your custom report to an application 
menu. If you run the report from the Custom reports list, the system omits filters and 
prompts. When you run the report from the application menu, the report presents all 
prompts and filters. 

3. 
In the Application drop-down list, select the application to which you want to add the

Make the Custom Report Available in Other Places 

One of the advantages of custom reports is that you can schedule them to run at different times 

with the same settings and make them available in dashboards and report groups. To take 

advantage of this feature: 

• 
Memorize the report so it can be run again with the same settings. 

• 
Add a memorized report to a dashboard or report group. 

• 
Schedule a memorized report. 

Operator Definitions 

The following operators are available for use when filtering: 

• 
Equals: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column matches the text or 
number in the Value field. 

• 
Less than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is less 
than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 
greater than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Less or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 
less than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen 

column is greater than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Not equal to: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column does not match 

the text or number in the Value field. 

• 
Contains: Displays all records in which a character or group of characters in the chosen 

column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The characters must 

match in the same order. For example, “ox” typed in the Value field may return records for 

Oxygen Inc., Boxing Agency, and Clorox, if those were values in the chosen column. 

• 
Does not contain: Displays all records in which no character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. 

• 
Starts with: Displays all records in which the first character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you have an item ID scheme that 

---



#### Running a Custom Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 94*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

uses initial letters to identify the product type, you can select the item ID column and set the 

Value field to these letters to display all records for that product type. 

• 
Ends with: Displays all records in which the last character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you tag the end of the item ID for 

all custom order items with the letters “CO,” you can select the item ID column and set the 

value to CO to display all records for custom order items. 

• 
Includes: Displays all records that match items in a comma delimited list in the Value field. 

• 
Excludes: Displays all records that do not match items in a comma delimited list in the 

Value field. 

• 
Field equals null: Displays all records that have a null or empty field. 

• 
Field not equals null: Displays all records that do not have a null or empty field. 

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns. 

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 
Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 
of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

% bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank,” like Metropolis Bank. 

Running a Custom Report 

When a custom report is created, the report designer has the option to add (or “deploy”) the 

report to an application, such as General Ledger, Accounts Payable, or Accounts Receivable. 

Deploying the report to an application makes the report available from the application menu and 

from the Report Center. 

To run a report from the Reports center page, go to Running a Report from Reports Center (on 

page 21). 

To run a custom report from an application menu: 

1.

Using the Custom report wizard, you can create charts that can be displayed on their own or

Copying a Custom Report from One Company or Entity to Another 

If you’re using the Custom report wizard and have a report that you want to copy from one 

company to another, you can create a custom package document to transfer your custom report. 

You must have administrator-level privileges to access the Platform Services (or Customization 
Services) application. 

Creating a Report Definition Package 

1. 
Sign into the company whose report definition you want to copy. 

2. 
In the Applications menu, select Platform Services (or Customization Services), and then 

select the Custom reports option. The Custom reports page opens. 

---

3.

Custom report wizard opens. 

4. 
In the Step drop-down list, select Save and add to menu. 

5. 
Click the Export def button. The system downloads the report to your local drive as an XML 

file. 

Preparing the Package 

Modify the package to prepare it for importing to the second company or entity. 

1. 
Open a text edit and paste the following XML wrapper text into a new file: 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 

<customErpPackage 
xmlns:xsi=“http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance”> 

<packageDescription> 

<name>INSERT NAME HERE</name> 

<description>INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE</description> 

<author>AUTHOR NAME</author> 

</packageDescription> 


> **Navigation Path:** `<customReports>`


<!-- Paste the contents of the file here--> 


> **Navigation Path:** `</customReports>`


</customErpPackage> 

1. 
Do not close the file. 

Adding the Definition to the XML File 

1. 
Using a text editor, open the report XML file you downloaded to your local drive. 

2. 
Copy the entire contents of the file. 

3. 
Go back to the XML wrapper file you created in the previous procedure. 

4. 
Paste the report code into the XML wrapper file in the space after the text <!--Paste the 

contents of the file here-->. 

5. 
Delete the following text: 

<!--Paste the contents of the file here--> 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 

Only delete the second instance of <?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?>. 
This is included in the report XML. The first instance at the top of the file should remain. 

---


<!-- Page 98 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

6. 
Inside the XML wrapper section, replace the following with your own information: 

• 
INSERT NAME HERE 

• 
INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE 

• 
AUTHOR NAME 

7. 
Save the file with a new name. 

The new file should look similar to the following. The actual report definition was edited for 

this example. 

Importing the Report Definition Package 

1. 
Sign into the company where you want to copy the report. 

2. 
Open the Platform Services (or Customization Services) menu, and then select the Custom 

packages option. 

The system opens the list of packages. 

3. 
Click the New package link. 

The system opens the Import customization package page. 

4. 
In Customization package location, click the Choose file button. 

5. 
Browse to and select the XML file you created. 

6. 
Click the Import button.

Financial Reports 

See the How to Get Here (on page 110) topic for a list of ways to access financial reports. 

Financial reports are available from the General Ledger, Reports, and Reporting Portal 

applications. You can create financial reports using the Financial report writer, or, if your 

company was created using a QuickStart template, you can access standard financial reports by 

clicking the Financial reports library button in the Financial reports list. 

To use one of the standard reports, you need to map your chart of accounts to the system 

categories, and the reports become live with your data. This helps speed up the otherwise 

time-consuming process of manually creating account groups that contain the appropriate G/L 

accounts and then creating financial reports and graphs using those account groups. 

Each application includes a set of standard reports that you can run to produce basic, common 

reports quickly. You can create, run, view, export, and memorize the following types of reports: 

• 
Standard reports available from the Reports section of each application menu and from the 

Reports center. 

• 
Financial reports and graphs using the Financial report writer. 

You cannot change the report structure after creating the report. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use financial reports.

Reports 
Permissions

Financials

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

How to Get Here 

You can access Financial Reports from several applications. The paths below show the most direct 

options for accessing financial reports. Choose one of these paths to follow.

Financial Reports List

The Financial reports list provides access to all of the financial reports that have been defined for 

your company. 

From this list, you can: 

•

• 
Generate reports in HTML, CSV, PDF, or Excel format. 

• 
Schedule a report to run at a future date, or on a recurring schedule. 

• 
Create reports using standard templates from the Financial reports library. 

• 
Run financial reports at the console level. 

When you run a console financial report at the entity level, you get data solely for that entity. 

Creating a Financial Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 110) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

The Financial report writer provides options for controlling all aspects of your financial report, 

from building your rows and columns to setting precise formatting options. 

Adding a Financial Report 

To create a report using the Financial report writer: 

1. 
In the Financial reports list, click the Add button. The Financial report writer opens. 

2. 
Name your report. 

3. 
Select your basic report structure (Report info tab (on page 137)). 

---


<!-- Page 113 -->
Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

4. 
Review the options in the Report structure section of the Report info tab, using the report 

samples as a guide. After you create a report, you can’t change the report structure. 

5. 
Select either Accounts or Dimensions, depending on what you’d like to see on your report 

rows. 

6. 
Build your account rows. 

Depending on the report structure you selected on the Report info tab, you’ll either build 

rows from account groups or dimension structures. For existing reports, the headings that 

you see along the left side of the tab reflect the account groups or dimension structures 

that have already been added to the report. 

       Type of rows  
         Description 

Accounts on rows (Rows 

tab) 

In this type of report, you select the account groups 

that you want to appear on the left side of your 

report. For example, a balance sheet report might 

include “Assets” and “Liabilities and Equity.” 

Dimensions on rows (Rows 

tab) 

In this type of report, you select the dimension 

structures that you want to appear on the left side 

of your report. For example, you might want to 

show rows for customers, or certain locations or 

departments. 

Setting Up Columns (Columns Tab) (on page 154) 

1. 
Choose the columns you want to include in the report. 

2. 
Decide what value you want to include in each column. For example, you might want to see 

the account names or dimension names on the left, followed by actual columns for different 

reporting periods. 

3. 
Column values can be based on calculations, such as summary calculations that operate on 

two or more columns (such as computing the average of a set of columns). For reports that 

feature account groups on rows, you can define more complex calculations on the 

Computations tab. 

4. 
Select the Account group purpose. This is displayed in the list and in the report. 

Filtering the Report (Filters Tab (on page 192)) 

You can set options such as the “as of date” and reporting method. You can also filter the report 

by dimension, such as filtering for a particular set of locations. 

In practice, many reports are designed to prompt the user for the “as of date” and other criteria 

when the report is run. That way you can create a single report and let the user choose the criteria 

when the report is run.

Multi-Entity Companies: Private Reports 

By default, financial reports are set to Public. 

This means that everyone can see them. If a report is private, only the users in the entity and with 

permissions can see the report. Top-level admins can also see private reports if they check 

Include Private in the list of reports. 

To make entity-level financial reports private by default, disable the Set default permissions to 

public setting at the top-level General Ledger configuration.

Viewing Financial Reports 

Reports can be either public or private. Everyone who uses the application can view public 

reports. For each report in the Financial reports list, you see the name of the report that you 

entered in the Report name field on the Report info tab of the Financial Report Writer. You also 

see the name of the owner of the report or “public” if everyone has access to the report. 

Only those who have been assigned permission by the administrator or the person who created 

the report can view private reports. (To grant permission to a private report for a user or group, 

click the Edit link for the report, and then click the Permissions tab.) 

Multi-Entity Companies 

Making a report private means that the report will not be visible to other operating entities. 

Administrators can choose whether new reports are created as public or private by default. Public 


> **Navigation Path:** `is the default setting. To change that setting at the top level, go to Company > Setup >`


Subscriptions, and then click the Configure link for General Ledger. 

Viewing a Financial Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 110) topic for a list of ways to access the Financial reports list. 

To view a financial report: 

1. 
On the Financial reports page, click one of the following links to view the report: 

•

Scheduling a Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > Financial 
Reports > Schedule`


For each report that you schedule, you can set a different schedule and choose how the report 

should be delivered. For example, you might want to email the report to yourself and selected 

people and send the report to a Dropbox folder where it can be stored and accessed by others. 

For more details about scheduling, see About Report Schedules. 

To schedule a report: 

1. 
Locate the desired report. You can schedule reports from the Reports center, the 

Memorized reports list, or the Financial reports list. 

To schedule a report group, see Scheduling a Report Group (on page 417). 

2. 
Click the Schedule link next to the report. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups (on page 195), then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or 

more G/L account groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use.

If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule Financial 

Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box to schedule reports 

and reports groups to run at that time. 

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system 
will run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.
