#### Best Practices
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 198*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Best Practices 

When you generate a report, the data that’s included is based on what you add to your rows and 

columns, and any filters that you apply. 

• 
All financial reports include account groups, which indicate which accounting data should 
be included in the report. For example, a balance sheet might include account groups for 
“Assets” and “Liabilities & Equity.” These account groups can include filters in their 
definitions, although this is not recommended in most cases. 

• 
Financial reports can also include segment structures that represent a set of segment data 
that you want to include on rows and columns. For example, you might want your rows or 
columns to include selected departments, customers by type, or items by product line. By 
nature, these segment structures limit the data to be displayed in the report. 

• 
Additionally, you can apply report-level filters on the Filters tab. For example, you might 
filter a report for a particular location or a location group that includes a specific set of 
locations. 

• 
In general, filters that you add to the Filters tab and filters on account groups are applied 
first, followed by any other filtering. For maximum flexibility, it’s recommended that you 
don’t use account group filters. 

Best Practices for Filtering 

When defining reports, it’s best to keep your approach simple to avoid situations in which there’s 

a conflict between the data on rows and columns and any filtering you’ve applied. 

• 
Avoid adding filters to your account group definitions. 

Although you can define filters for an account group—for example, filtering a Cost of Goods 
Sold account group for a particular location—it’s recommended that you don’t add any 
filters to account groups. Instead of filtering your account groups: 

• 
Define your account groups without filters. 

• 
On a report-by-report basis, use the options available in the Financial Report Writer to 
select the data you want to see. 

• 
When filtering for a specific set of members (or members that meet certain criteria), define 
your filters in only one place. 

In general, avoid situations in which you select one set of segment data on rows and 
columns, and then set a report-level filter that includes a different set of data. Instead, do 
either of the following: 

• 
Apply filters on the Filters tab. To filter the entire report for a specific set of segment 
data, you can select one or more segment groups on the Filters tab. For example, you 
might filter a report for “West Coast locations.” 

• 
Select and filter data on the Rows and Columns tabs. On each tab, you can select the 
data you want to see in your rows and columns. Depending on the type of report you 
are creating, different options will be available. For example, you could add Cost of 
Goods sold to your report rows and then create columns that compare by different 
locations.

Using Alternate Accounts for a Financial Report 

Running Financial Reports on Alternate Reporting Accounts 

When a financial report is displayed using an alternate account set, the system uses reporting 

accounts in place of General Ledger accounts. 

To let the user choose a reporting account set when the report is generated: 

1. 
Leave the Reporting accounts field empty or choose a default set. 

2. 
Select the Prompt check box. 

Users can choose any reporting account set to which they have access, or they can choose 

General Ledger to display the report using standard accounts. 

In the General tab, in the Accounts section, you can either predefine a reporting account set to be 

used for the report or set up a prompt dialog to prompt for reporting account set selection when 

a user generates a financial report. 

Showing and Hiding Zero Balance Rows and Columns 

The zero number options let you adjust how zero balance rows and columns are handled in the 

report. 

By default: 

• 
Sections of a report are hidden if the total or subtotal is zero and all detail rows are also 

zero. 

Regardless of the options you select for the Numbers field, the logic for including a section 

in a report is as follows: 

• 
If all rows for a section are zero, the section is hidden. For example, suppose that you 

didn’t have any charitable contributions for the reporting periods shown in a report. In 

this case, the Charitable Contributions section would be hidden. 

• 
If the total for a section is zero, but it contains some detail rows that have a balance, 

the section is included in the report. For example, a Headcount section would appear if 

there was a total of 0 headcount growth, but there was +2 headcount for one 

department and -2 headcount for another department. 

• 
Detail rows with a zero balance are hidden unless you select the option to Display zero 

balance with activity. 

• 
Columns of a report are displayed even if the total and detail rows are zero unless you clear 

the Display zero balance columns option. 

• 
Calculations are displayed by default, even if the result is 0.00, unless you select the Do not 

display zero value calculation option. 

---


<!-- Page 202 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Zero Numbers Options 

• 
Display zero balance with activity: Shows detail rows that have zero balances as long as 

there were transactions posted during the reporting period. 

This is a report-wide setting. However, you can use the Always display option on the Rows 
tab to select specific sections where you want to display the total and all detail rows, even 
if the amount is zero. 

• 
Display zero for future periods: Shows zero amounts for any column where the reporting 

period is in the future. 

This feature is useful if your report is set up for 12 months, but you only want to see actual 

amounts for the past and current periods, even if there are future transactions. If, for 

example, you have a report set up with columns for every month of the year and you run 

the report as of June 30, then even though your columns contain actual amounts, you can 

see numbers for future dates, such as for the Month Ended July. However, you can select 

this check box to zero all future numbers and clean up your report. 

This applies to actuals only. 

• 
Display zero balance columns: Clearing this option automatically hides any columns that 

have only zero amounts. This can be particularly useful if you sometimes compare report 

data by time period or segment and you want to automatically hide any columns that don’t 

have data. 

• 
Do not display zero value calculation: Select this option to exclude zero-value calculations 

(0.00) in the report. This setting affects the Computation on actual and Computation on 

budget column types. 

Departments, Locations, and Other Segments 

The options for segments allow you to control how departments, locations, and other segments 

are listed in rows and columns. These options apply in either of the following situations: 

• 
If you change the detail level for rows to show segment detail 

• 
If you expand columns by segment or segment structure 

For example, you might expand an actual column so that it is split into multiple columns by 

location. 

The following lists the segment options. 

• 
Show departments: Choose whether to display departments by name only, by ID only, or by 

name and ID. 

• 
Show locations: Choose whether to display locations by name only, by ID only, or by name 

and ID.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Show other: Choose whether to display other segments by name only, by ID only, or by 

name and ID. 

• 
Sorting (alphabetically sort Department or Location Group): If you filter the report by a 

department or location group, the report automatically displays departments and locations 

in the order in which they are defined in the group. Select this option if you prefer to sort 

departments and locations alphabetically. 

If you don’t filter by a segment or location group, the report will always display 
departments and locations in alphabetical order. 

Defining Report Headers and Footers 

Page Header 

By default, printed reports start with your company name, followed by the report title, and a 

subtitle that spells out the report’s “As of date” in words. Using the options in the Page header 

and Page footer sections, you have the option to: 

• 
Change the report title. 

• 
Include additional lines of header text and optionally change how and where the date is 

displayed. 

• 
Include your company logo in the header. 

• 
Include footer text, including dynamic information that specifies the page number and 

date/time when the report was printed. 

The list describes the header information that is included when the report is displayed in printable 

(PDF) format. As noted in the table, some header elements (such as the report title) also appear 

when the report is displayed in Excel or HTML format. 

• 
Logo options (displayed in PDF): Include your logo at the top of the report, aligned to the 

left, top, or center. 

If you have not uploaded your logo, you can do so on the Company information page. See 
Adding and Editing General Information for instructions. 

• 
Report title (displayed in PDF, HTML, Excel): Enter the title you want to display in the report. 

By default, the report uses the report name that you entered on the Report Info tab as the 

title.

If your company is linked to an outside firm (such as your CPA), that firm can add a footer to 
your financials. For example, the footer might say, “For Management Use Only.” You can’t alter 
or remove this footer as long as your companies are linked. However, the external company can 
change the footer. 

Selecting Fonts 

The options in the Fonts section let you specify the combinations of font, size, color, and style 

(that is, italics and bold) you want for specific report elements. Your font selections are used for all 

output formats (HTML, PDF, and Excel), with the exception of font color, which applies only to PDF 

output. 

In the Fonts section, you can choose the fonts for: 

• 
Page header information (report title, company name, subtitle 1, and subtitle 2) 

• 
Column headings 

• 
Row headings, with separate settings for the main Headings and Totals and another for 

Subgroups and Totals 

• 
Body text (detail rows, such as those listing individual accounts) 

• 
Page footer information (page number, date, time, and footer text) 

The font size you select for column headings applies to column headings 1 and 2. The column 
title (typically, the column type such as “Actual”) appears two points smaller than the font size 
you select. 

Other text not specified above uses the same font as the body text. For example, fonts for account 

names are the same as that for body text. 

Setting Other Options 

Page Settings 

By default, your report is set up to print in Portrait orientation on letter-size paper. The system 

will determine where columns break across pages, and the report may be more than one page 

wide. However, you can choose other options that allow you to control how the report prints 

across pages. 

---


<!-- Page 206 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The choices you make in the Page settings section determine how much control you have over the 

printed page. 

• 
Default page settings: This is the default setting. If you select this option, column size and 
breaks are determined automatically. However, you can change the report from Portrait 
orientation to Landscape to fit more columns across the page. 

• 
Fit to x page(s) wide: Select this option if you want to specify how many pages wide the 
report should be (for example, fitting it to one page wide), but still have the column width 
set automatically. 

• 
Page orientation: By default, pages are set to Portrait. Select Landscape from the 
drop-down list to change the orientation of the report pages. 

• 
Measurements: If you select Custom page size you can choose to see the measurements 
for margins and column widths as points or inches. 

• 
Custom page size, column widths, and column breaks: Select this option if you want more 
control over the printed report, including the ability to select a different page size, set 
column widths, and set the page margins. 

Column Options and Fonts 

You can use the Column options, breaks, and fonts section to control the look of particular 

columns on reports. Available options depend on your page settings selection. Some options 

apply only when the report is output as a PDF. 

• 
Hide filter details on column titles: Hide the details of filtered columns, such as the account 
group and segment structure display on the column header. This option applies to all 
outputs. It allows user to use the column filter to preset the column data without showing 
all details on the report presentation of column header. to hide column filter such as 
account group and segment structure display on the column header. This option applies to 
all outputs. It allows user to use the column filter to pre-set the column data without 
showing all details on the report presentation of column header. 

• 
Repeat segment name/ID as 1st column on reports more than 1 page wide: When a report 
is more than one page wide, enable this feature to ensure that the first column is repeated 
on each page, making it easier to follow the column information. 

The following lists the available column options: 

• 
Width (PDF only): Width of the column on printed (PDF) reports. Not available if you chose 
the Default page settings option. 

By default, the margins and column widths are specified in points, but you can use the 
Measurement drop-down list in the Page settings section to switch to inches. 

• 
Break (PDF only): Places a page break after the selected column on printed (PDF) reports. 
Available only if you chose Custom page size, column widths, and column breaks. 

• 
Font type, Font size: Changes the font type and size for the selected column. 

• 
Color (PDF only): Changes the color of the selected column on printed (PDF) reports only. 

• 
Bold, Italic: Makes the text in the selected column bold or italic.

### Format Tab FAQs
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 210*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Format Tab FAQs 

How do I control the width of the report? 

The width of the report is affected by the number of columns in the report, and the font sizes you 

selected. If you want to control how many pages wide your report is, you can have the system fit 

the report to a certain number of pages wide, or you can use column breaks to select how many 

columns are on each page. You can also fit more columns on a page by switching to landscape 

orientation. 

To control the width of the report, perform one of the following options: 

Fit the report to one page wide (or a selected number of pages). 

1. 
In the Page Settings section, select the Fit to x pages wide option. 

2. 
Specify how many pages wide the report should be. 

Select where page breaks fall. 

1. 
In the Page Settings section, set the custom page size, column breaks, margins, and column 

specific fonts. 

2. 
In the Column Options, Breaks, and Fonts section, locate the column after which you want 

the first column break. Any remaining columns will appear on the next page. 

If your report is more than two pages wide, set additional column breaks as needed. 

Set page orientation to landscape. 

• 
In the Page Settings section, select the Landscape option as the page orientation. 

How do I control page breaks? 

You can control where page breaks are in the report by inserting a page break at the end of a 

certain section. 

To insert a page break after a specific section: 

1. 
Go to the Rows section of the Format tab. 

2. 
Locate the section after which you want a page break. For example, if you want a page 

break after your Fixed Assets group, locate the row for that group. 

3. 
In the Row formatting column, select the check box for Page Break After.

#### Assigning Report Access

#### Selecting Default Permissions
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 211*

Permissions Tab 

The Permissions tab identifies the report owner and specifies who can and can’t access this 

report. Users who don’t have access to a report won’t see it in the Financial reports list page, and 

it won’t appear in their Reports Center or dashboards. 

Assigning Report Access 

Depending on how your General Ledger was set up, the default permissions to financial reports 

may either grant or deny access to all users (the group called Group/Everyone). For example, if 

the default access privileges for financial reports are set up to deny access, you can selectively 

give access to users or user groups by adding them to the Access list. 

When a user or group is added to the Access list, even though the Exclusion list is set to 

Group/Everyone, the Access list takes precedence and any user or group specifically included in 

the Access list is granted access to the report. 

If access is granted to Group/Everyone but one user is added to the Exclusion list (even if that 

user is part of a group given access), that user can’t access the report. 

To set the report owner and permissions: 

1. 
If necessary, select the person who is responsible for the report as Report owner. 

By default, the person who creates the report is the report owner. However, if the report will 

be maintained by someone else, you can select that user from the list. 

2. 
Set permissions for the report by reviewing the Access list and Exclusion list. 

• 
To add a user or user group to either list, click the Add button. 

• 
To remove a user or user group from either list, select the user or group and click the 

Remove button. 

In addition to adding individual users, you can select groups of users. Learn more about adding 

user groups. 

Selecting Default Permissions 

A preference in the General Ledger determines whether financial reports are available to everyone 

by default. 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to General Ledger > Setup > Configuration.`


2. 
Scroll down to the Financial reports section and locate the option to Set default 

permissions to public.

#### Adding a Report to a Dashboard

*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 212*

Using RealPage Accounting Reports

Next Steps Tab 

When you’ve finished designing your report, it’s time to start using it. 

Although you can always run your report by going to the Financial reports list page or by going 

to the Reports Center, you can do more to highlight and use your report. 

Adding a Report to a Dashboard 

Dashboards give you an at-a-glance view of the areas of your business that matter most to you. 

From the Next steps tab, you quickly add your financial report as a component on any dashboard 

that you own. 

To use the Next steps tab to add the financial report to a dashboard: 

1. 
Click the Add this report to a dashboard link. 

2. 
Select the dashboard, give it a name and location, and enter other details as needed. 

Learn more about the options for report components. 

If you see a message that you don’t have any dashboards that you can add components to, but 
you know that you have dashboards, you probably aren’t the owner of those dashboards. In this 
case, you can still edit the dashboard from the Dashboards list and then add the component. 

Can I add this report to someone else’s dashboard? 

Yes, you can add this report to any dashboard that you can see on the Dashboards list, provided 

that you have permissions to edit dashboards. However, if you’re not the owner of the dashboard, 

you’ll need access the dashboard from the Dashboards list to add the component. 

Learn more about adding a component to a dashboard. 

Scheduling a Report 

You can schedule a report to run automatically on a recurring basis, such as weekly or monthly. 

When you schedule the report, you can set it up to be delivered by email or stored. 

To schedule a report from the Financial Report Writer: 

1. 
On the Next steps tab, click Schedule this report to run periodically. 

2. 
When prompted, click the Save and schedule button to save the report and proceed. 

3. 
On the Schedule financial report page, set up a schedule for the report and select how you 

want it to be delivered. 

Learn more about the options for scheduling a report (on page 117). 

In addition to having the report emailed to you, you can also have it stored. Learn how to access 

stored reports in the Reports Center.

report group, which runs all member reports immediately or according to schedule.

### Schedule Financial Report Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 235*

Book II: Using RealPage Accounting Reports

Schedule Financial Report Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reporting > 
 Financial Reports > Schedule`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Financial Statements > 
 Financial Reports > 
Schedule`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > 
 Financial Reports > Schedule`


Use the Schedule financial report page to schedule a financial report to run automatically and 

routinely. You can schedule a financial report from the Financial reports list or from the Reports 

center. If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule 

Financial Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box to 

schedule reports and reports groups to run at that time. 

This page contains three sections: 

• 
Filters: Use this section to filter the scheduled report by specific criteria. 

• 
Schedule: Use this section to define the report schedule. 

• 
Delivery options: Use this section to choose how you want to deliver and store the report. 

Fields 

Financial Reports List 

Name 
This is the name of the financial report. 

Owner 
This is the name of the person who created the report. 

Report type 
This is the report type that the owner assigned at the time of creation. 

Report types let you filter your reports to find reports that would be 

relevant to users with certain roles or permissions. 

Report audience 
This is the report audience that the owner assigned at the time of creation. 

Process and store 

(link) 

Runs the financial report and then store it in the system for future 

reference. 

HTML (link) 
Generates the financial report in HTML format. 

CSV (link) 
Generates the financial report in CSV format. 

PDF (link) 
Generates the financial report in PDF format. 

Excel (link) 
Generates the financial report in Excel format. 

Schedule (link) 
Opens a box where you can schedule the financial report. 

Not scheduled 

Status (link) 

This status appears if the report has not been scheduled. 

Opens the execution log of the scheduled report.

When you create a financial graph, your choices for data series represent how you want to 

categorize the data. For example, a revenue graph can be broken down in multiple ways, such as 

by quarter, location, or customer. 

Primary vs. Compare Data Series 

Think of the Primary data series as the main way you want to categorize values, such as by 

reporting period, account group, segment, or segment structure (waterfall charts only). 

For some types of graphs, you have the option of showing a comparison within the primary data 

series. A Compare data series is available for all chart types except pie, doughnut, and waterfall. 

---


<!-- Page 246 -->
Using RealPage Accounting Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Data Series Options 

The way that data are displayed depends on the graph type. 

• 
Account groups: Categorizes data by one or more account groups. Example: Revenue vs. 

expense. 

• 
Reporting periods: Categorizes data by one or more reporting periods. Example: Four 

consecutive quarters. Although you can select individual reporting periods by moving them 

from Available to Selected, the quickest way to create a trend over time is to use the Period 

comparison options. 

• 
Budget comparison: Lets you compare Actual values against one or more budgets. 

This option is not available for pie, doughnut, or waterfall graphs. 

• 
Dimension: Categorizes data by the selected dimension. By default, the graph shows all 

members of each dimension. However, you can filter on a dimension group to show a 

subset of members. For example, suppose that you choose Locations as a data series. 

• 
By default, the graph shows all locations. 

• 
To restrict the list of locations, expand the Filters section. From the Location 

drop-down list, select a dimension group that represents the locations you want to 

include. 

• 
Dimension structure: In waterfall charts, categorizes data based on the substructures in a 

hierarchical dimension structure. 

This option is available only for waterfall graphs. 

Selecting a dimension structure, rather than a dimension, gives you the freedom to create 
intermediate columns based on how you want to organize and label the data.

##### Standard vs. User-Defined Dimensions
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 257*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Standard vs. User-Defined Dimensions 

You have a set of standard dimensions right out of the box, ready to be enabled. You can use 

them as is or repurpose them as needed. 

If you need a unique dimension, defined to reflect your individual business needs, you can create 

a user-defined dimension. For example, if you are a software company with various product lines, 

you might create a user-defined dimension called Line of Business. The values you could add are 

Direct Customers, Channel Partner, and OEM. Your dimension becomes available throughout the 

company wherever dimensions are displayed and is used the same way as any standard 

dimension. 

Additional fees may apply for some dimensions, including user-defined dimensions. Contact 
your account representative for more information. 

Territories can be optionally set up in Accounts Receivable, enhancing filtering in certain A/R 
reports. However, territory isn’t a dimension and can’t be used for tagging transactions. Learn 
more about Territories and Territory Groups. 

Types of Dimensions 

Mix and match standard and user-defined dimensions to report on all aspects of your business. 

• 
Standard dimensions: These dimensions are provided when your company is set up. They 

are commonly useful and can be repurposed as needed. Standard dimensions include 

Location, Department, Customer, Employee, and Vendor. 

• 
User-defined dimensions: These are dimensions you can create to organize and sort 

categories of data unique to your business activities. 

Additional subscription fees may apply when creating user-defined dimensions. 

---



##### Using Dimensions for Reporting
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 258*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension Examples 

• 
Location: You can create a hierarchy of locations to reflect how locations are organized 

within your company. For example, West Coast Division, California, Northern/Southern, and 

so on. 

• 
Department: You can create a hierarchy of departments to reflect how departments are 

organized within your company. For example, Engineering, Software/Hardware, Sales, 

Marketing, and so on. 

• 
Distribution method: You can create a user-defined dimension for different distribution 

methods such as VAR or Direct. 

Using Dimensions for Reporting 

If you use dimensions for reporting, you can filter them by selecting the appropriate combinations 

in their respective drop-down boxes. You can also select pre-defined dimension groups. For 

example, if you select the department group ENG, which includes hardware and software 

engineering plus Quality Assurance, the report will include the data for those three departments 

only. In multi-entity shared companies, location groups also include entities. 

For multi-entity shared companies with multiple base currencies 

Reports that you run at the top level require a location to ensure that the system will display all 

amounts in the same base currency. 

To use dimensions for reporting: 

• 
Enter the desired dimensions information in the drop-down boxes in this section. To do this, 

either: 

• 
Type your entry directly in the drop-down box, or 

• 
Click the icon to display a list, and then click Select next to the entry you want. 

Some of the dimensions have an additional corresponding drop-down filter you can use to focus 

your report and refine (or filter) the results. These additional drop-down boxes are: 

Dimension 
Corresponding additional filters 

Customers 
Customer type 

Departments 
Department type 

Employees 
Employee type 

Locations 
Location type 

Vendors 
Vendor type 

Include Subs, Individual Reports, and Prompt on Run 

These options provide additional control about over how dimensions are handled in the report. 

---


<!-- Page 259 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Include subs 
Includes subdimensions, such as child locations or child customers, 

when filtering. Clear this check box if you don’t want the system to 

include children of the dimension when filtering. 

Individual reports 
If you select a department group and location group, this option 

creates a separate report for the individual department and location 

combinations. 

The order in which individual reports are created is determined by 

the order of the locations and departments in the groups. 

You can include additional report header text for each 
department or location. Learn more about creating individual 
reports by department or location. 

Prompt on run 
If you want to be able to choose a department or location and time 

period each time you run the report, select this check box. 

If you select a department or location and also select the “Prompt 

on run” option, the system completes the department or location 

that you selected but allows you to choose a different one at 

run-time.

#### Dimension Relationships
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 260*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 260*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension Relationships 

If you create transactions where the value of one dimension is based on the value of another, you 

can create a relationship between the two dimensions to auto-populate the related value. For 

example, if you always use the same location for a specific customer, you can create a relationship 

between the Customer and Location dimensions to set the Location value to auto-populate every 

time you create a transaction against that customer. 

Specifically, dimension relationships are useful for: 

• 
Auto-populating dimension values: For example, you can select a customer and the system 

auto-populates the related location. 

• 
Filtering and validating dimensions: For example, you can select a specific location and the 

system displays only a subset of departments. 

• 
Cascading dimensions: For example, select a specific customer, and the system populates 

the related location, and the project, which is dependent on the selected location and 

department. 

Creating relationships between dimensions automates and speeds up data entry and lowers the 

incidence of data-entry errors. You can create relationships between: 

• 
User-defined dimensions 

• 
Standard dimensions 

• 
User-defined dimensions and standard dimensions 

In fact, you can create relationships between dimensions that enable many values on one or 

either side of the relationship. These are typically called one-to-many, or many-to-many 

relationships. 

To create relationships between dimensions, you must be subscribed to Platform Services and 
have Administrator permissions. 

You can’t export or import an application package that contains standard-to-standard dimension 
relationships. Import or export the package first, and then manually create the relationships. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to work with dimensions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with dimensions:

Selecting the Base Dimension 

To create a relationship between two dimensions, you select the base dimension, the dimension 

whose value will determine the value of the second dimension. For example, Customer and 

Location can be set up in a relationship in which the value of customer, the base dimension, 

determines the value of location in transactions involving that customer. 

To select the base dimension: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Platform Services, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select the Objects option. The Objects list is displayed. 

3. 
Locate the base dimension, and then click the corresponding Edit link. 

For example, if you want to create a relationship that specifies the value for location every 

time you use a specific customer, click Edit beside Customer, which is the base dimension in 

this example. 

4. 
In the Status options section, select the Auto-Fill Related Objects check box. 

5. 
Leave Enable Override of Auto-Filled Objects unselected if you want a fixed relationship. 

---



##### Creating a Relationship Between Two Dimensions
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 262*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

In a fixed relationship case, enabling override defeats the purpose of creating the 
relationship because the user can pick any value from the drop-down list. Conversely, if 
you want to default to a suggested value, but also want to leave the user free to select 
another value as appropriate, enable override. Remember, if you’ve set up priority for 
possible conflict between multiple dimension relationships, enabling override won’t be 
respected. 

The option to override auto-populated dimension fields works only for newer pages, such 
as in Cash Management. 

6. 
Click Save to return to the object list. 

Creating a Relationship Between Two Dimensions 

After editing the base dimension to enable auto-population of related objects, you’re ready to 

create the relationships between the two dimensions. 

To create a relationship between two dimensions: 

1. 
In the Object definitions list, locate the base dimension, and then click the corresponding 

link in the Object column. In this example, click Customer. 

The system opens the Object definition page. 

2. 
At the top of the page, click the Relationships link, or scroll down to the Relationships 

section. 

3. 
Click the New relationship link. 

The system opens the New relationship page for the selected dimension. 

4. 
Select the dimension with which you want to create the relationship. You can select either a 

standard or user-defined dimension. In this example, select Location. 

5. 
Click the Next button. 

---


<!-- Page 263 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

The system opens the next page which defines the relationship you just created. For 

example, Customer: New relationship with location page. 

6. 
Select the Relationship type. Each type is described here and on the page itself. 

Many-to-Many is the most common relationship type. 

Dimension relationships are reciprocal. In other words, creating a relationship from 

customer to location is the same as creating a relationship from location to customer. What 

distinguishes relationships is the relationship type. The relationship type determines the 

drop-down list that you create in the related object. For example, in the relationship 

between customer and location, if you pick a one-to-one relationship, in the customer 

record, you can pick just one value for the location. 

• 
One Customer to One Location 

Each customer can be related to, at most, one location 

Each location can be related to, at most, one customer 

• 
One Customer to Many Locations 

Each customer can be related to many locations 

Each location can be related to, at most, one customer 

• 
Many Customers to One Location 

Each customer can be related to, at most, one location 

Each location can be related to many customers 

• 
Many Customers to Many Locations 

Each customer can be related to many locations 

Each location can be related to many customers 

Auto-fill doesn’t work in many-to-many relationships. 

7. 
Click Save to confirm the relationship. 

The system returns you to the Object definition page for the dimension.

Testing the Dimension Relationship 

After creating a dimension relationship, you can easily test it in any transaction that uses the two 

dimensions. For example, if you created a customer/location relationship, you could test the 

relation by creating a transaction against that customer. The system automatically completes the 

location dimension with the value that you selected for the customer. In addition, because you 

didn’t enable override when you created the relationship, the user can view the location value but 

can’t change it. 

The user can view this value but can’t override it. 

Setting the Value that Wins in a Transaction with Overlapping Relationships 

If you have transactions with overlapping dimension relationships—that is, the base dimensions 

are different and the related dimension is the same, but with different values—you can set the 

priority for which related dimension value wins. For example, if you have two relationships where 

the two base dimensions are Customer and Department, and the related dimension is Location, 

you can configure the priority-order setting so that Location takes it value from the 

Customer/Location or the Department/Location relationship whenever the two relationships 

overlap in a transaction. 

To prioritize related dimensions: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. The General ledger setup page appears. 

3. 
Scroll down to the Dimension relationships table. 

4. 
In the Priority Order column for the appropriate related dimension, drag the handle of the 

dimension that should take precedence to the top of the list. 

Filtering and Restricting Values in Transactions With Overlapping Relationships 

Unlike simple relationships in which the single value of one dimension is set by the single value of 

another, many-to-many relationships can have multiple values on both sides of the relationship. 

You can filter for and populate lists of values to transactions that include many-to-many 

---


<!-- Page 267 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

dimension relationships. The system is smart enough to handle overlapping relationships in the 

same transaction. 

Here’s how the system populates the values list for such relationships in a transaction: 

• 
If there are common values between the multiple relationships, the system populates the 

overlapping values to the related-dimension list. 

Example relationships: 

• 
Customer and Location 

• 
Department and Location 

• 
If no common values exist, the system populates the combined values to the related 

dimension list. 

Example relationships: 

• 
Customer and Location 

• 
Department and Location 

---

3. 
Scroll to the desired item in the dimension’s list, and then click the Edit link.  

4. 
On the dimension page, scroll to the bottom, and, in the related dimension field, enter or 

select an appropriate value. 

5. 
Continue adding values until the list is complete.

#### About Dimensions
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 270*



##### Making a Dimension Inactive
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 270*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Dimensions 

A dimension is a category of data that you can organize and sort in meaningful ways. RealPage 

Accounting provides the following pre-defined dimensions: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

In addition, RealPage Accounting enables you to define new dimensions to suit your needs. These 

user-defined dimensions enable you to organize and sort categories of data unique to your 

business. For example, if you are a software company with various product lines, you might create 

a user-defined dimension called Line of business. The values you could add are Direct customers, 

Channel partner, and OEM. 

Dimensions enable you to collect, sort, analyze, and report on data within one category, or 

between categories, so you can identify key factors such as: 

• 
Your most profitable or most costly customers. 

• 
The return on investment of a location or department. 

• 
Whether and to what degree a new product or product line is successful. 

• 
Which way a particular aspect of your business is trending. 

RealPage Accounting dimensions give you fine control over data definition and data hierarchy. 

With dimensions, you can customize financial reports around specific business activities, get 

greater visibility into how the business is doing, and make faster, more meaningful business 

decisions. 

Additional fees may apply for user-defined dimensions. Contact your RealPage account 

representative for more information. 

Making a Dimension Inactive 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Dimensions > 
Customer/Vendor/Department/Location/Employee`


If, for any reason, you no longer use a dimension value that’s been associated with past 

transactions and records, you can make that dimension value inactive in your system so that you 

don’t see it on any future lists or transactions. 

You cannot make user-defined dimensions inactive. 

To make a dimension value inactive: 

---


<!-- Page 271 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

1. 
In the Dimensions section, select the desired dimension, such as Department. 

2. 
In the list, find the dimension (find the department) that you want to inactivate, and then 

click the Edit link. The system opens the dimension’s information page. 

3. 
In the Status drop-down list, change the status to Inactive. 

4. 
Click the Save button. 

To view inactive dimensions on reports and lists, select the Include Inactive check box at the top 

of the report or list. 

To include data from inactive dimensions on financial reports, you can use dimension groups for 

filtering (on page 356).

Use the Vendors (Suppliers) list to add and manage vendor records. From this list, you can:

Adding Vendor (Supplier) Records 

See the How to Get Here (on page 273) topic for a list of ways to access the Vendors list. 

Adding Vendor Records 

Add vendor records when you want to pay A/P invoices.  

When you add a vendor, you can type key descriptive information about that vendor and select 

the payment method that the vendor prefers, such as by check, credit card, or ACH (electronic 

payment). 

If you enabled the Single Scan Upload feature in your preferences and have previously 
downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the software 
when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, purchase order, service 

---


<!-- Page 275 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

contract, or document. When this occurs, download the new software; there is no need to 
uninstall the previous version. 

To add a basic vendor record: 

1. 
In the ID field, type a unique identifier for the vendor record. 

Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, V0001 for a vendor ID. 

When you save the record, the system converts the vendor ID to all uppercase to prevent 

duplication. You can prevent this conversion by clearing the Set IDs to uppercase check 

box. For information, see Disabling Vendor ID Capitalization. 

After creating a vendor ID, you can only change it with the Customer Utility Tool. Most users 

do not have access to the tool as it requires administrator privileges. Contact your system 

administrator if you need to change a vendor ID. 

2. 
In the Name field, type the vendor’s name. The system completes the Print as field in the 

Primary Contact section. 

3. 
Select the One-time use check box to designate the vendor as a one-time or occasional use 

vendor that you don’t want to include in your standard vendor lists. An example of a 

one-time use of a vendor record is when you issue a customer’s deposit refund. 

These vendors won’t appear in the Vendors (Suppliers) list unless you select the Include 

one-time option at the top of the list. 

4. 
Select the Corporate vendor check box as needed. When you add an invoice for a corporate 

vendor, the system marks the invoice as a corporate invoice and prevents it from appearing 

in Site Experience. Also, corporate vendors do not appear in Site Experience. 

5. 
Select the This vendor is an owner check box when the vendor is also the owner of the 

company. 

6. 
In the Status list, select the Active option if you want vendors to have A/P invoices entered 

and payments issued. You can also select the Inactive option to prevent A/P invoices from 

being entered and payment issued. 

You can inactivate multiple vendors at a time using the Customer Utility Tool’s Inactivate 

Vendors option. 

7. 
Select the appropriate Storefront supplier code. This code is the vendor’s code for use with 

the Storefront application associated with Spend Management.  

If your company does not use Spend Management, then this option does not appear. 

8. 
Select the Require PO – Spend check box option when your company requires that you 

create a manual or online purchase order before creating an online A/P invoice on behalf of 

---


<!-- Page 276 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

the vendor. If a purchase order is not available to match with the A/P invoice, then the user 

cannot submit the A/P invoice for the vendor. 

The Require PO – Spend check box appears only when your company has purchased and 
installed Spend Management. 

9. 
Select the Send Offline Purchase Orders to Vendor check box. When enabled, when the 

user adds or edits a purchase order in the Submitted or Partially Approved state, the option 

Send purchase order to vendor appears.  

To use this feature, the vendor’s subscription type must also be set to Invoice Submission 

Service, and a Storefront Supplier Code must be defined for the vendor. 

If this option is ever disabled, the system continues to show the Send purchase order to 

vendor option on historical purchase orders.  

10. 
Select Keep active to prevent the vendor from being automatically changed to Inactive.  

Use this option for vendors that should remain available, even if they meet conditions that 

would normally make them inactive. For example, companies that use the AI Finance Agent 

may have rules that automatically inactivate vendor records based on configured criteria. 

When Keep active is selected, the vendor stays active and can continue to be used. 

11. 
Select the Exclude from Full Service check box to prevent the vendor from syncing with 

Invoice processing full service. You can enable syncing again at any time. 

12. 
Select the Exclude from Auto Request Storefront Account check box to prevent the system 

from sending an automatic request for the vendor for a Storefront account.  

13. 
Select the Preferred vendor check box to identify this vendor as one your company prefers 

or recommends using. This setting helps users distinguish preferred vendors from other 

vendors in the vendor list. 

14. 
Select the Do not itemize invoices check box if you do not want the AI Agent to itemize this 

vendor’s invoices when its invoices are scanned. The system will define only one line item 

for the total amount of each invoice when the AI Agent scans this vendor’s invoices. This 

setting is useful when, after scanning in an invoice, you find that you have to delete line 

items after the AI Agent has broken out charge details into multiple line items.  

If you do not select this check box, the AI Agent creates a line item for each charge it finds 

in invoices when it scans invoices.  

15. 
Select the OneSite resident check box if the vendor is a resident in a OneSite-managed 

property. 

16. 
Select the Sync to external systems check box to allow RealPage Accounting to sync the 

vendor record with Procore or other external systems. 

---


<!-- Page 277 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

This field appears only if you have configured the Procore integration in Job Cost & 
Reserves. 

17. 
Select the RequirePO check box when the vendor requires a purchase order. The A/P 

invoice must be matched to a purchase order before you save and post it. 

This field does not apply to actions performed in the RealPage Financial Suite system. The 

RequirePO check box appears only when your system is integrated with OPSTechnology. 
When the RequirePO check box is selected, it causes the OPS system to validate the 
purchase order record in OPS. 

Filling In the Tax Information Section 

The fields in this section vary based on the country where the vendor is located.  

1. 
In the Country field, type the country where the vendor is located.  

2.

Security Number.  

If the vendor is located in the United Kingdom, then the fields reflect UK tax requirements:

In the Company name as registered field, type the company name as it is registered with 

the tax jurisdiction. 

2. 
In the Address field, type the address of the vendor’s tax jurisdiction. 

3. 
In the VAT reg no field, type the vendor’s VAT registration number.  

4. 
In the Date tax number last validated field, type the date that the tax number was last 

validated.  

Filling In the Primary Contact Section 

1. 
Fill in the name and address of the primary contact for the vendor. 

2. 
In the Print as field of the Primary contact section, verify that the name appears the way you 

want it to appear on checks. Revise the Print as name if necessary. If this vendor requires 

joint checks, then fill in the names of the two required signers. This field is required. 

3. 
In the Primary phone field, type the phone number of the primary contact. 

4. 
In the Mobile field, type the cell phone number of the primary contact. 

5. 
In the Pager field, type the pager number of the primary contact. 

6. 
In the Fax field, type the fax number of the primary contact. 

7. 
In the Email address field, type the email address of the primary contact. 

8. 
In the Secondary email address field, type a second email address of the primary contact.

Vendor (Supplier) Information Page 

See the How to Get Here (on page 273) topic for a list of ways to access the Vendors (Suppliers) 

list. 

Use this page to add and edit vendor records. A vendor record has six tabs: 

• 
Vendor (Supplier): This tab has two sections, the Summary section, and the Primary contact 

section. Use the Summary section to determine how the vendor is handled in the system, 

and the Primary contact section to record all of the contact details for the primary contact of 

the vendor. 

• 
Additional information: This tab has five sections: Vendor details, Billing details, Email 

template options, Vendor merge, and CA DE 542. Use this tab to record details about the 

vendor and billing, select email templates to associate with a transaction type, view details 

about vendor merges, and indicate when a California form DE 542 is required and note the 

date the form was sent. 

• 
Contact list: This tab has two sections, Pay to/Return to and Contact list. Use this tab to 

define the contact to whom to direct payments and to list all contacts associated with this 

vendor. 

• 
Payment information: This tab has three sections: Payment details, Payment services, and 

Vendor account number. Use this tab to define how and when to pay this vendor. 

• 
Restrictions: This tab has one section. Use this tab to restrict access to this vendor. This tab 

appears only when your system has multiple entities. 

• 
Insurance/License: This tab has three sections for three insurance policies and licenses. Use 

this tab to maintain details about insurance and licenses that cover this vendor.

Vendor Information Page 

Fields 

ID 
The system provides two mutually exclusive ways to add vendor IDs. You 

can type your own unique ID, or you can have the system automatically 

add them from a present numbering scheme. Set up automatic 

numbering for vendors, 

This ID can’t be overwritten after the vendor is created. 

Best practices for creating identifiers 

An ID enables your company to keep track of a specific type of 

information, such as G/L account, department, location, transaction, 

vendor, and customer. You can create IDs by adding them on the fly or 

by having the system automatically add them from a preset numbering 

scheme. 

Whichever method you choose, we recommend against using leading 

zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can cause errors when you 

import information into your company from Excel because Excel 

removes the leading zeros. 

Best practice: Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, C0001 

for a customer ID. 

Workaround: If you must use leading zeros in IDs, then convert the 

column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file 

content. Excel won’t remove the leading zeros when you save the file. 

Remember to do this every time you use a template to import 

information that requires IDs. 

Name 
The name of the vendor as it will appear on lists and menus across your 

company.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with customer records: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts Receivable 
Customers 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a

You must be at the top level to add and import customers.

#### Customers List
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 299*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Customers List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 297) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Use the Customers list to view and manage customer records. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add new customers. 

• 
Edit or view existing customer details. 

• 
Import customer records. 

• 
Export the list of customers. 

• 
Open a customer’s A/R ledger. 

• 
View the total amount that a customer owes to an entity. 

By default, the Customers list uses icons and indentation to show how parent and child customers 

are related. This hierarchical view is helpful when you have customers that belong to the same 

parent customer, such as when you are doing business with subsidiaries or divisions of the same 

company and need to separately track their contact and billing information. 

The list also provides access to related information, including: 

a) Customer’s A/R ledger: Click the customer’s name to open the customer’s A/R ledger. 

b) Customer totals box: Click the amount in the Total due column to open the Customer 

totals box and view the individual amounts due from the customer.  

If you are working in a multi-entity, multi-currency company, then a View due link appears 
in place of an amount in the Total due column. Click this link to open the Customer totals 
box to see the total amount due for each entity.

##### Adding Customers
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 300*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding Customers 

See the How to Get Here (on page 297) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

The Customer information page has multiple tabs that contain basic information about the 

customer, such as company name, address, and phone numbers. 

To add a customer: 

1. 
From the top level, click the Applications menu, and then select Accounts Receivable. 

2. 
Select 
 Add next to Customers. 

Filling In the Customer Section 

To fill in the customer’s company and contact information. 

1. 
In the ID field, type a unique identifier for the customer. 

After creating and saving a customer record, you can only change the Customer ID with 
the Customer Utility Tool. Most users do not have access to the Customer Utility tool. 
Contact your system administrator if you need to change a Customer ID. 

2. 
In the Name field, type the name of the company as it should appear in lists and menus. 

3. 
Select the One-time use check box to designate the customer as a one-time or occasional 

use customer that you don’t want to include in your standard customer lists. 

These customers won’t appear in the Customers list unless you select the Include 

one-time check box at the top of the list. 

4. 
Select the Status of the customer record, either Active or Inactive. Inactive customers do not 

appear in any system lists or drop-down lists. 

Filling In the Tax Information Section 

The Tax information section appears when you use the international version of the RealPage 
Financial Suite.  

1. 
Select the country where the customer files taxes in the Country drop-down list. 

2. 
In the VAT reg no field, type the customer’s VAT registration number so that you can track 

VAT taxes. 

Filling In the Primary Contact Section 

1. 
Type the name, address, and contact information for the person who is your primary contact 

associated with the company. 

2. 
In the Print as field, type the name of the company as it will appear on payments and 

notices. 

---


<!-- Page 301 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

When you create a new customer, the system automatically creates a related contact record 

for you. The Print as field is used in coordination with the Customer ID to create the 

suggested contact name, which is the unique contact ID used throughout the system that 

can’t be edited after creation. This is also the name that appears in all lists and drop-down 

lists. See Contacts for more detailed information. 

Duplicate information is shared between the Customer tab and the Contact list tab. 

Therefore, if you change the data in the Customer tab, the changes are reflected in the 

Contact list tab and vice versa (provided you have not selected the Exclude from the 

company contact list check box). 

3. 
Open the Additional information tab. 

Filling In the Additional Information Tab 

Enter accounting details for this customer: 

1. 
Select the customer’s type in the Type ID drop-down list. 

2. 
In the Sales rep drop-down list, select the user who is responsible for this customer’s 

account. 

3. 
If this customer account is a subsidiary of another customer, click the Parent drop down list, 

and then select the name of the parent company. 

4. 
To use a G/L group other than the default, select it in G/L group drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Territory ID drop-down list, select the sales territory to which you assigned the 

customer. You can also add a territory by clicking the Add link in the drop-down list. 

6. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, add an attachment to associate with the customer 

record. See Adding attachments to a record. Learn more about who can add attachments in 

Permissions for attachments. If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your 

file in the Attachments box to attach the file to this record. 

Filling In the Invoicing Details Section 

1. 
In the Term drop-down list, select the credit terms to extend to the customer. The selected 

term becomes the default term whenever you perform transactions related to the customer. 

You can also add a new term by clicking the Add link and filling in the A/R Terms 

Information box. 

2. 
In the Default revenue account drop-down list, select the G/L account that you want the 

system to use for revenue transactions. When you select an account, the system completes 

the G/L account field with the selected account in revenue transactions, but you can change 

it. 

If your system is an international system, the A/R account drop-down list appears instead.  

---


<!-- Page 302 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To use an alternative A/R account to override the default G/L A/R account, select it in the 

A/R account drop-down list. The system populates the A/R override account you select 
here to every invoice or adjustment transaction that includes this customer. See 
Overriding the G/L account in A/R transactions for more information.  
In Accounts Receivable, this feature applies to invoices and adjustments only. It doesn’t 
apply to recurring invoices, manual deposits, quick check entry, quick invoice entry, or 
advances. 

3. 
In the Shipping method drop-down list, select how you will ship goods to the customer. 

You can also add a new shipping method by clicking the Add link and filling in the Shipping 

method information box. 

4. 
If the customer is a reseller of your products and services, type the customer’s resale 

number in the Resale number field. 

5. 
Select the Taxable check box if regular purchases from this customer are taxable. 

6. 
In the Tax group drop-down list, select the contact tax group to associate with the 

customer. 

This setting applies only when the customer is international. The contact tax group helps 
the system determine which tax maps and tax details to use to calculate tax for this 
customer for applicable documents in the Accounts Receivable application. 

7. 
In the Tax ID field, type the government tax ID number for the customer. (US only) 

8. 
To define a credit limit for this customer, type the amount of credit you are willing to extend 

to the customer in the Credit limit field. 

9. 
To prevent anyone from entering invoices for this customer, select the On Hold check box. 

10. 
In the Statement/Invoice delivery section, select how you want to deliver the customer’s 

statement: 

• 
Print: Mail the customer a printed copy of his invoice. 

• 
Email: Send a copy of the invoice through email. 

• 
Both: Mail the printed copy and send a copy of the A/R invoice through email. 

11. 
In the Default invoice message drop-down list, select the message that you want to include 

in this customer’s invoices. You can also add a standard message by clicking the Add link 

and then filling in the Customer Messages box. 

12. 
In the Comments field, make note of anything that others may need to know about this 

customer. 

13. 
The Currency field appears if your system is configured for multiple currencies. Select the 

currency that the customer uses. 

---

Filling In the Printed Document Templates Section 

Administrators can set up printed document templates in the Platform Services application. See 

Custom document templates workflow. 

Use this section to select a specific template to use for customer communication with each type 

of transaction: 

• 
A/R invoice (A/R sales invoice) 

• 
Quote 

• 
Order 

• 
List 

• 
Invoice 

• 
Adjustment 

• 
Other 

Filling In the Contact List Tab 

1. 
Open the Contact list tab, and then select the appropriate contact to use for 

communicating with the customer. 

• 
Primary contact 

• 
Bill-to contact 

• 
Ship-to contact 

2. 
In the Contact list section, add categories and contacts to associate them with this customer. 

For example, a customer may have a phone number for the warehouse that you may need 

to call. Enter warehouse for the category and select the contact from the Contact 

drop-down list. 

Refer to Configuring A/R payments for details. 

You must first create contact records before you can select them for these customer 
contacts.  
Go to Company > All > Contacts to create contact records. 

Filling In the Restrictions Tab 

The Restrictions tab appears when your company has multiple shared entities. 

Use the Restrictions tab to select the restriction level for this customer. The restriction level 

determines which entities can view and access the customer record. 

• 
Unrestricted customer: Visible to all entities at all levels. 

• 
Restricted to top-level only: Visible only to the top-level entity. 

• 
Restricted customer: Activates Location/Location group and Department/department 

group selection boxes.

##### Viewing or Editing a Customer
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 304*



##### Deleting or Inactivating a Customer
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 304*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Selected locations or departments will be able to view this customer. See Using the 

multi-select box for help on selecting locations and departments. 

When setting up location groups or department groups, keep in mind that restrictions can 
be based on groups that contain specific locations or departments, but can’t be based on 
groups that filter dynamically based on the value of certain fields (such as locations where 
the status equals “Active”). Location groups and department groups that contain dynamic 
filtering won’t appear on the Restrictions tab for you to select. 

Viewing or Editing a Customer 

See the How to Get Here (on page 297) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

The Customers menu item appears on both the All and Setup tabs of Accounts Receivable. Both 
menu options open the same Customers list, and the lists’ settings are exactly the same. 

To view or edit customer details: 

1. 
In the Customers list, click the View or Edit next to the customer record. 

The Customer information page opens. 

2. 
View or edit the record as needed, and then click Done or Save. 

Deleting or Inactivating a Customer 

See the How to Get Here (on page 297) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

If you haven’t used a customer for any transactions in your company, you can click the Delete link 

in the Customers list to remove the customer. 

Customers that have already been used can’t be deleted. However, you can make that customer 

inactive, effectively removing the customer from drop-down menus and lists throughout the 

company. 

To make a customer inactive: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Accounts receivable. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab. 

3. 
Select Customers. The Customers list appears. 

4. 
Locate the customer that you want to make inactive and click Edit next to the Customer ID. 

5. 
On the Customer tab, change the Status for the customer to Inactive.  

After you’ve inactivated a customer, you can still access the customer’s record by selecting 

Include inactive at the top of the Customers list. 

6. 
Click the Save button.

#### Customer Information Page

Customer Information Page 

See the How to Get Here (on page 297) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

Use the Customer information page to add and change customer details. From this page, you 

can: 

• 
View or edit customer details. 

• 
Duplicate the customer record. 

• 
Print the customer details. 

• 
Export the customer details in XML format. 

• 
View the audit trail. 

Each customer record has four tabs: 

• 
Customer: This tab contains general information about the customer, such as their unique 

identifier, name, status, primary contact information. 

• 
Additional information: This tab contains additional information about the customer, such 

as their customer type, sales rep, parent company, invoicing details, transaction printing 

options, and email template. 

• 
Contact list: This tab contains the customer’s billing and shipping information. 

• 
Restrictions: This tab allows you to control who can view and edit the customer record. 

Fields 

Customers List Columns 

Customer ID 
This column contains a unique identifier assigned to the customer. 

Customer name 
This column contains the name of the customer, which is usually the 

company name. 

City 
This column contains the city where payments and statements should be 

sent. 

State/province 
This column contains the state or province where payments and 

statements should be sent. 

ZIP Code 
This column contains the ZIP Code or postal code for location where 

payments and statements should be sent. 

Customer type ID 
This column contains the category assigned to the customer (for 

example, Consultants, Subcontractors, or Equipment). You can search for 

or add a Customer Type ID. The Customer Type ID must exist before you 

can assign it to a customer.

Parent

Attachments 
An attachment is a bundle of one or more supporting files. It can include 

as many files and combination of file types as you like, such as scanned 

images, spreadsheets, and word-processor documents. You can replace 

or delete an attachment or continue to add or delete files in an 

attachment as needed. 

To reference an attached document, you must first load the scanned 

image, spreadsheet, or word-processor document. You can provide 

permanent, safe storage of supporting documents by uploading them to 

the system as attachments. Learn more about who can add attachments 

in Permissions for attachments. 

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file in the 

Attachments box to attach the file to this record. 

Invoicing Details Section 

Term 
The term designates the credit terms extended to the customer by you, 

such as Due Upon Receipt and Net 30. Either select a Term from the

 Add to add a new Term. Terms must be 

defined before you can assign one to a customer record. The system 

uses terms to calculate discounts and penalties on customers’ invoices. 

When you define a term for a customer, it becomes the default term 

whenever you perform transactions related to that customer.

##### Adding an Employee
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 316*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Employees List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 313) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Use the Employees list to view a list of the employees in your company. You can sort and filter the 

list to view a specific group of employees as needed. 

From the Employees list, you can: 

• 
Add a new employee record. 

• 
Edit and view an employee’s details. 

• 
Delete or inactivate an employee. 

• 
Export the list of employees. 

If you have long employee lists in external data files, you can upload them in CSV format. See 
Importing employees (on page 313) for more information. 

Adding an Employee 

See the How to Get Here (on page 313) topic for a list of ways to access this page. 

A basic employee record contains an employee ID and a primary contact name that is used to 

reference the employee throughout the system. 

To add an employee, complete the following fields on the Employee information page: 

1. 
In the Employee ID field, type a unique identifier for the employee. An employee ID can 

consist of numbers, letters, or both. 

You can create employee IDs by adding them manually or by creating a document 

numbering sequence to automatically generate them from a preset numbering scheme. 

---



##### Viewing and Editing Employees
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 317*



##### Deleting Employees
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 317*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

As a best practice, do not use leading zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can 

cause errors when you import information into your company from Excel because Excel 

removes the leading zeros. 

If you must use leading zeros in your ID, be sure to convert the column of ID numbers to 

text format in Excel before importing the file content so that Excel does not remove the 

leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you use a template to 

import information that requires IDs. 

2. 
In the Primary contact name drop-down list, select the contact name that is used to 

reference the employee throughout the system and in printed output. If needed, create a 

new contact. 

The Status drop-down list defaults to Active. Do not change this value to Inactive unless you 

no longer want the employee to appear in Employee drop-down lists throughout the 

system. 

Viewing and Editing Employees 

See the How to Get Here (on page 313) topic for a list of ways to access employee records. 

To view an employee’s details: 

1. 
In the Employees list, locate the employee record that you want to view, and then click the 

corresponding View link. 

The Employee information page opens. 

2. 
To view or edit the employee’s contact information, click the Primary contact name link. 

The Contact Information box opens. See Adding a contact for more information. 

3. 
When you are finished, click Done to return to the Employees list. 

To edit an employee’s details: 

1. 
In the Employees list, locate the employee record that you want to edit, and then click the 

corresponding Edit link. 

The Employee information page opens. 

2. 
Make the required changes. 

3. 
Click the Save button. 

Deleting Employees 

See the How to Get Here (on page 313) topic for a list of ways to access employee records. 

Deleting an Employee 

You can delete a dimension such as an employee if it hasn’t been associated with a transaction or 

record. 

---


<!-- Page 318 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

After you delete an employee record, it cannot be restored. 

To delete an employee: 

1. 
In the Employees list, find the employee record that you want to delete, and then select the 

corresponding Delete check box. 

2. 
Click the Delete button. 

A delete confirmation box opens. 

3. 
Click OK. 

Inactivating an Employee 

If you do not want to delete an employee record, but you still want to exclude it from employee 

drop-down lists, you can set its Status to “Inactive.” 

1. 
In the Employees list, find the employee record that you want to delete, and then click the 

corresponding Edit link. 

The Employee information page opens. 

2. 
On the Employee information tab, set the Status field to “Inactive.” 

3. 
Click the Save button.

Departments 

Although departments are optional, they are useful for filtering and categorizing data in many 

areas of the system. For example, you may want to generate financial reports and graphs based 

on departments. Additionally, many companies set up transaction approvals to be routed to the 

department manager. 

You can create a hierarchy of departments to reflect how departments are organized in your 

company. The hierarchy is established by defining parent and child relationships between 

departments. For example, you could have a parent department called West Coast Division that 

contains several child departments including Engineering, which itself has two additional child 

departments, Software Engineering and Hardware Engineering. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with department dimensions: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Departments 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing department records. You may have additional 

options based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Departments`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Company, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, select Departments. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > Departments`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Forecasting & Planning, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, select Departments.

For users in a multi-entity shared organization, departments can either be common (accessible) 
to all entities, or exclusive (private) to a specific entity. Departments are also a filter object used 
to restrict user access. 

Adding and Editing Departments 

See the How to Get Here (on page 322) topic for a list of ways to access the Departments list. 

All you need to create a department is to assign an ID and name for it. 

To add a department: 

1. 
Enter an ID and a Name. See Best Practices for Creating Identifiers. 

You cannot change the Department ID after creating and saving the department record. 
However, the administrator can change the Department ID using the Customer Utility Tool. 
Contact your system administrator if you need to change a department ID. 

2. 
If the department belongs to a hierarchy of departments, select its Parent department from 

the drop-down list.

longer use the department and do not want it to appear in lists, select Inactive. The

Importing Locations

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file containing 

data. 

Downloading the Template 

When you download templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been 

tailored to your specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses.  

1. 
Open the Company menu.  

2. 
Click the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Locations row, and then click the 

Template link. 

The system either downloads the Locations.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling In the Locations Template 

Add your data using the correct formatting as explained in the template.  

1. 
Open the template in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type a unique identifier for the location. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
LOCATION_NAME: Type a location name of up to 40 characters. 

• 
START_DATE: Type the start date related to the location.  

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type a contact name. This column is required if the contact is 

specified. 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.
