After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 

mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common errors, 

Best practices. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format [File > Export > CSV (Comma delimited file)]. 

6. 
Import the location data’s CSV file (Company > All > Import Data > Locations > Import). 

7. 
In the Date format field, unless your dates are already in MM/DD/YYYY format, select a date 

format that you want to use. The system supports 24 date formats.  

8. 
In the File encoding field, leave the setting as auto detect unless you are unable to import 

your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of 

file encoding. 

9. 
Select the Process offline check box if you are importing a large quantity of data or if you 

are unsure how much time your import will take. Some imports can take considerable time, 

depending on their size and how much processing the system must do on the imported 

data. The Process offline feature allows the system to process the data when system activity 

is lighter. If you prefer to wait until the import process is complete, do not select the 

Process offline check box. 

10. 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. When the system 

completes the import process, it sends an email to the address with either a message about 

the success or failure of the import, including any errors that occurred in the process. 

11. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row in the file that starts with a # symbol. 

12. 
Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors.

From the Locations list, you can:

Adding and Editing Locations 

See the How to Get Here (on page 331) topic for a list of ways to access the Locations list. 

To add a location: 

1. 
Type the ID and Name of the location as you want it to appear in the system. 

After saving the record you cannot change the location ID.  

If you must change the ID, contact your system administrator and have them run the 

RealPage Accounting Customer Utility tool to change the Location ID/Property ID.

If the location belongs to a hierarchy of locations, then select its Parent location.

including California, Nevada, and Utah. When you define California, Nevada, and Utah, 

select West Coast Division as the parent.

If you have a multi-entity company that also uses multiple base currencies, then you 

must assign each location to an entity so that the system knows which base currency 

to use for that location. In this case, you can’t change the Parent location. 

You can change the parent of a location only when your system uses one base 
currency.

maximum of 50 characters per line. 

To save time, you can run a financial report or other general ledger report for a group of 

entities/locations or departments and have the system automatically split the report into multiple 

individual reports. In this case, the report header for the “individual report” displays the name of 

the department, entity, or location, plus any title text you enter in the Location title field, instead

#### Classes
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 343*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Classes 

Just like any other standard dimension, classes are tags with a set of values which you can 

associate with transactions to create and filter reports. However, unlike other dimensions, classes 

aren’t linked to any specific information in other areas of the system like vendors, customers, or 

employees are. For example, you can rename vendor dimension to something more meaningful 

like “Supplier,” but because the vendor dimension is used for a specific purpose across many 

applications, you can’t repurpose the vendor dimension. 

Classes, instead, can be both renamed and repurposed to track anything you want. For example, if 

your business requires you to track the industry of all of your customers, you could rename Class 

to Industry, add a few custom fields, and then build reports off your new Industry dimension. 

As with all dimensions, associate only one class per detail transaction line. You can co-mingle 

multiple class groupings, depending on which transactions you choose to use with class. For 

example, you can use a class to track loan types on loan invoice transactions and use a class to 

track cost transactions on internal projects.

*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 350*

About Dimension Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Dimension Groups`


In addition to the default dimensions for departments and locations, your company can use other 

standard dimensions that are available out-of-the-box, as well as user-defined dimensions that 

you create for your own unique tracking requirements. These dimensions let you filter or display 

information in multiple ways, for instance by showing data from only certain locations or projects. 

A dimension group is a name for a particular set of members in a dimension, or a set of members 

that meet certain criteria. For example, you might create customer groups for a particular set of 

customers, customers located in a particular state, or customers with the greatest open balance. 

Finding Each Type of Dimension Group 

The following table lists the menus in which you can find each type of dimension group. 

Availability depends on the dimensions that are set up for your company and your own 

permissions to each application.

##### Where Dimension Groups Can and Can’t Be Used
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 351*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Where Dimension Groups Can and Can’t Be Used 

The following describes where you can and cannot use dimension group filters: 

Financial Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Financial reports allow filtering by dimension groups in Applications > General Ledger > All >`



> **Navigation Path:** `Financial Reporting > Financial Reports.`


When you define a report, you can specify the filters as part of the report definition, or you can 

prompt the user to filter the report at runtime. 

Financial Graphs 


> **Navigation Path:** `Financial graphs allow filtering by dimension groups in Applications > General Ledger > All >`


Financial Reporting > Financial Graphs. 

When you define a graph, you can specify the filters as part of the graph definition, or you can 

prompt the user to filter the graph at runtime. 

Standard General Ledger Reports 

Standard G/L reports listed on the G/L menu, such as the Journals or Trial Balance report, allow 

filtering by dimension groups. 

When you run a G/L report, you can select the filters to use, or you can create a pre-filtered report 

by memorizing the report with your selected filters. 

Dashboards 

Dashboards allow filtering by dimension groups, but filtering is limited to components for 

performance cards, financial reports and graphs, and standard G/L reports. You can also pre-filter 

dashboard components for a dimension group. See Dashboard filtering. 

Other Reports 

Currently, reports outside of the G/L do not support dimension groups: 

• 
Standard reports outside of the G/L 

• 
Custom reports created with the Custom Report Writer 

---



#### Dimension Groups in Reports and Dashboards
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 352*



##### How Dimension Groups Are Used in Financial Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 352*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension Groups in Reports and Dashboards 

Defining a dimension group gives you additional control over what appears in reports and 

dashboards. In general, any dimension group that you create will appear as additional filter 

choices. 

With a dimension group, you can: 

• 
Filter for a particular set of members, such as specific customers, vendors, or locations. 

• 
Filter to show data from members that meet certain criteria, such as items of the same type 

or locations with the same parent location. 

• 
Take advantage of dimension count to post to statistical journal entries automatically. 

How Dimension Groups Are Used in Financial Reports 

In financial reports, dimension groups can be used in several ways: 

• 
Filtering for multiple dimension members, or for members that meet certain criteria 

• 
Controlling the order in which the members appear in report columns and rows 

• 
As the basis for report structures 

Dimension report structures (on page 372) enable dimensions to be used on the rows or columns 

of financial reports. The following graphic shows a simple location report structure named South, 

which contains a location group entitled Southern offices. 

a) Dimension groups are custom groupings that are meaningful to your company. 

b) Dimension report structures can contain one or more dimension groups.

of dimension group, you can define multiple groups for different purposes, such as groups that 

filter customers by type, amount due, country, or even a combination of criteria.

Selecting Specific Dimension Members and Setting Their Order 

When you select Specific members of a dimension, you are picking the individual locations, 

departments, customers, employees, or vendors that you want to include. For example, you might 

want to create a Customer group that contains certain customers. 

To select specific members: 

1. 
Set the Group type to Specific Members. 

2. 
Use the Members list to select the members to include. 

The sort order that you choose will be used in any reports that show dimensions in columns 

or rows. 

a) 
Drag and drop to reorder 

b) 
Add another member below this one 

c) 
Delete member 

Selecting Entity-Specific Members in a Multi-Entity Shared Environment 

If you’re creating a dimension group at the top level, you can’t include members that belong to 

an entity. Try creating the dimension group from the entity itself. 

Filtering Groups 

Use filters on dimension groups to affect what appears in reports. This page describes a few 

examples of how you can apply filters to dimension groups. You can: 

• 
Filter with field values. 

• 
Filter for employees, locations, or departments managed by the current user. 

• 
Combine multiple filters. 

---


<!-- Page 357 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Create dimension groups that contain both active and inactive members (on page 358). 

Filtering with Field Values 

You can add filters that select dimension members based on the value of certain fields. For 

example, you might want to select customers of a certain type or vendors that have a payment 

priority of urgent. 

1. 
Select the field you want to filter on. 

2. 
Choose the operation and value you want to filter for. 

The options you’ll see depend on the field you choose. 

By default, if you add more than one filter, members are included only if they match all 

criteria. However, you can change this behavior using the options in the Filter conditions 

section. 

Filtering for Employees, Locations, or Departments Managed by the Current User 

Dimension groups can automatically show managers only the information that’s relevant to them. 

For example, you can set up an Employee dimension group called My employees, which 

dynamically filters for employees managed by the current user. Similarly, groups can be used to 

filter for departments or locations managed by the current user. 

The current user is the user who is currently logged into the system. 

When you set the filter to current user, you limit the user to see only the group—such as 

employees or locations—that is associated with the user. For example, if you set a filter where the 

field is Manager and the operator is current user, when the manager runs the report, he or she will 

only see his or her own employees. To create a group that filters for the current user: 

1. 
Create a new group of type Department or Location. 

2. 
Define the group by giving it a name that users will recognize. 

For example — My department. 

3. 
In the Filters section, select a field that is connected to an employee who is a user in the 

system. For Department or Location dimension groups, you can select the Manager field. 

Not all contact fields are connected to a user. For this reason, filtering for the current user 
is restricted to the Manager field. 

4. 
Set the Operator to is current user. 

Combining Multiple Filters 

If you have multiple filters, the default behavior is to match only members that meet all of the 

criteria. However, you can change how this works using the Filter conditions section. 

---

Filter Conditions 

All (AND) 
Include members that match all criteria (the default). 

Any (OR)

Expression

For example, the following expression matches members that either meet criteria 1 

and 2, or that meet criteria 3. 

(1 AND 2) OR 3 

If you want to select one of something, such as departments where the manager is either Jim, 
Sue, or Terri, create several filters and use the Any (OR) filter condition. 

Creating a Dimension Group Filter for Both Active and Inactive Members 

If you want to include inactive dimensions in reports, you can create a dimension group that 

filters for both active and inactive members. To do this:

Open the Reports menu.

In the Dimension groups section, select the dimension type to filter (for example, 

departments or locations.) 

3. 
Select the dimension group to filter, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
In the Filters section, create two filters: 

• 
Status equals active  

• 
Status equals inactive 

Make sure the filter conditions are set to All (AND). 

5. 
Save your changes.

Location Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Groups > Location`


In RealPage Accounting, you can create a location group so that you can generate reports for 

more than one property at a time. A property can be a member of more than one location group. 

For example, you can have one location group for all of your Texas properties, and another 

location group that contains all properties. 

There are a number of ways to use a location group: 

• 
All active properties 

• 
Specific properties 

• 
Reporting all location groups for specific members 

• 
Reporting the locations in a location group 

• 
By manager 

• 
Where the manager is the current user 

• 
With the same parent property 

• 
With a particular base currency 

It’s also possible to create a location group that includes only your company’s entities, thereby 

representing an “entity group” in reporting. See Creating Entity Groups (on page 365) for more 

information. 

For companies using OpsTechnology with RealPage Accounting, OpsTechnology does not 
recognize location groups. When you restrict a vendor to a location group in RealPage 
Accounting, the system sends this information to OpsTechnology as a list of locations rather 
than the location group. 

Adding a Location Group 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Groups > 
 Location`


To add a location group: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the Dimension groups section, click the 
 Add button next to Location.  

The Location group information page opens. 

---


<!-- Page 362 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
In the Location group ID field, type a unique identifier for the group. 

When displayed elsewhere in the system, the location group will be listed with the ID and 
name together (ID--Name), as in NAOPS--North America Operations. IDs can’t be changed 
after you’ve saved the group, but you can edit the name at a later time. 

4. 
In the Name field, type a descriptive name for the group that other users will understand. 

This is the text that appears in Location, Property, and Entity/Entity group drop-down lists 

throughout the system. 

5. 
In the Description field, type a brief description of what this group includes or how it’s used. 

6. 
In the Location group contact drop-down list, select the user who is responsible for this 

location group. This information is only for your benefit; the system does not use this 

information anywhere else. 

7. 
In the Group type drop-down list, select the type of group you want to create: 

• 
All members: Select this option if you want to filter which locations are included in the 

group based on the criteria of your choice. For example, you might define a “US 

Locations” group which includes all members but then filters the results to only 

locations in the United States. 

• 
Specific members: Select this option if you want to choose specific locations to 

include in the group. 

Tip: To include all active members of a group (such as all customers), select All 

members as the group type. Then, in the Filters section, set the Field to “Status,” the

In the Sort order drop-down list, select whether you want to sort the members of the 

location group in ascending or descending order. 

• 
In the Sort field drop-down list, select the field by which you want to sort the 

members of the location group. 

• 
In the Max matches field, type the maximum number of locations to include in the 

group. Leave this field blank to include all matching members. 

9.

group. 

Creating a dimension structure from a group enables you to add the group to the rows or

used only for filtering reports.

To add more rows to the list, click

Set Up Filter Conditions 

Use this section to set up filters for the location group. With filters, you can: 

• 
Create field/value tests that will determine which locations are included in the group. 

• 
Create an expression with conditions that determine members of the group. 

To set up filters: 

1. 
In the Field drop-down list, select the field that you want to use for a condition’s test. 

2. 
In the Operator drop-down list, select the comparison operator. 

3. 
In the Value drop-down list, type the value to compare. 

4. 
Continue adding rows to the list as needed, especially if you are building conditions for an 

expression: 

• 
Click 
 Add to add another row.  

• 
Click 
 Delete to delete a row. 

Because an expression uses the row numbers in the Filters list, you must write the 
expression last. 

5. 
In the Filter conditions field, select the logic that the system should use when filtering 

locations: 

• 
All (AND): All tests must result in a True state to include a member in the group. 

• 
Any (OR): At least one test must result in a True state to include a member in the 

group. 

---


<!-- Page 364 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Expression: Select to type a Boolean expression in the Condition box below it. 

For example, say you’ve defined three field/value tests in the Filters list: 

• 
Country is the US 

• 
Base currency is USD. 

• 
Location Contact Name starts with “Ed.” 

In this case, you can set filter conditions as follows: 

• 
Select All (AND) to include a location only when all of these tests are true. 

• 
Select OR to include any location in which at least one of these tests is true. 

• 
Select Expression if you want to set up a more complex combination. When you select 

Expression, type the condition logic in the Condition field that appears below. Use the 

row numbers of the Filters list in the expression. 

Example of a Condition 

You want the system to find properties with an amount between $150 and $999. 

Each row is a condition. 

Row 1: 

Field = Status 

Operator = equals 

Value = Active 

Row 2:  

Field = First tax month 

Operator = equals 

Value = January 

Expression Examples 

(1 AND 2) OR (2 AND 3) 

If the first two expressions both evaluate to true OR if the second and third expressions both 

evaluate to true, then the location is included in the group.  

(1 AND 3) OR 2 

If the first and third conditions both evaluate to true or the second condition evaluates to true, 

then the location is included in the group. 

Saving the Location Group 

When finished, click the Save button to save the location group.

Creating an “Entity Group” 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Groups > 
 Location`


You can create an entity group by setting up a location group so that only the parent locations 

representing your company’s entities are included as members of the group. Entity groups are not 

groupings of entity records from the Entities list. When you create an entity group, you are 

actually creating a location group with the location records that represent your company’s 

entities. Any entity groups you create will appear in Location, Property, and Entity/Entity group 

drop-down lists throughout RealPage Accounting, along with locations and location groups. 

To add an entity group: 

• 
Follow the steps to create a location group (on page 361) but select only parent locations in 

the Members section. Set the Group type to Specific members to choose specific locations. 

Making a Location Group Public or Private 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Groups > 
 Location`


Users with full or limited administrative privileges can choose whether to make a location group 

public or private. Public location groups can be viewed and edited by all users. Private location 

groups can be viewed and edited only by the following types of users: 

• 
Users with full or limited administrative privileges 

• 
Users with the Administrator role 

• 
Users with the Location Group Admin role 

You can add the Location Group Admin role if it is not available in your company. 

Select or clear the Private check box on the Location group information page to determine 

whether the location group is public or private. This setting applies to all components of the 

system where location groups are available. 

---

As a non-administrative user, any location groups that you create are always private. 

As an administrator, you can choose to create a private location group or keep it public for all 

users to see.

Dimension Report Structures 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Structures`


Dimension report structures provide a flexible way for you to organize dimension data that you 

want to see on the rows or columns of a financial report. For example, instead of showing all 

locations on a report, you might want to select a Location structure that is named for a particular 

region and includes a subset of locations. 

You can add any number of structures for the dimensions you track. 

The list of standard dimension structures may include: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

If you have additional dimension structures listed in the Dimension structure submenu, they are 

custom structures and are not discussed in this document. 

Creating a dimension structure from a group enables you to add the group to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. 

A dimension structure can only be used for filtering reports if you don’t select the Dimension 

Structure check box when you are creating a dimension group. 

Viewing the Available Dimension Report Structures 

Select a dimension structure option to view the available report structures. 

See also Dimension analysis in financial reports (on page 402) and Dimension structures for 

financial reports (on page 372).

#### Dimension Structures Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 371*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Dimension Structures Overview 

Dimension structures are structures that represent dimensional data that you intend to use on the 

rows or columns of financial reports. 

a) Dimension structure on report rows 

b) Dimension structure on report columns 

For example, you might create dimension structures that show: 

• 
Selected departments 

• 
Locations by region 

You can create any number of dimension structures to represent the different ways you want to 

segment your data. For instance, you might create multiple customer structures that enable you 

to analyze your Customers by type, Customers by sales territory, and so on. After they’re created, 

the re-usable dimension structures can be used across the rows or columns of any number of 

financial reports. 

In the following example, two different dimension structures are added to the rows of a report: 

• 
One hierarchical structure that breaks down customers by industry. 

• 
A flat structure that lists individual items 

When added to the rows of a report, each dimension structure has: 

• 
a heading 

• 
rows for the individual members or substructures in the dimension structure 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 372*



##### Dimension Structures in Lists

How the System Handles Hierarchical Dimensions 

Dimensions are often hierarchical. For example, a department can have one or more child 

departments up to several levels deep.  

When a report filter includes a member of a dimension, data from any members that belong to it 

will also be included. This means that a department group that matches the Engineering 

department will automatically include data from any sub departments (like Development, Quality 

Assurance, and Documentation.) 

When filtering financial reports by department or location, you can decide to exclude sub 

departments or sub locations by clearing the Include Subs option under the filter field. 

Dimension Structures Created from Dimension Groups 

Dimension structures are built from dimension groups, which can contain particular members 

(such as one or more locations) or members that meet certain criteria (such as customers of a 

particular type). Learn more about dimension groups (on page 398). 

---


<!-- Page 378 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The following graphic shows a simple location structure named South, which contains a location 

group that includes a company’s southern offices as its members. 

a) Dimension groups are custom groupings that are meaningful to your company. 

b) Dimension report structures can contain one or more dimension groups. 

c) The dimension report structure is what enables you to add the dimension to the report. 

Dimension groups and dimension structures work together to provide power and flexibility in 

reporting. 

• 
Dimension groups enable you to dynamically filter data at the time you run a report, and 

can be used for standard reports, such as an A/R Ledger, as well as financial reports. 

• 
In addition to creating groups that include particular members, one of the most 

powerful ways to use dimension groups is to select members based on filter criteria. 

For example, a dimension group can filter for customers of the same type, items from 

the same product line, or locations with the same parent location. 

• 
Dimension groups are also used outside of financial reports. For example, you might 

have a dimension group that is used only to filter the A/R Ledger for customers with 

an outstanding balance greater than $500. 

• 
Dimension structures are created specifically for the purpose of adding dimensions to the 

rows or columns of financial reports. 

• 
Depending on how you assemble the groups in structures, you can achieve different 

results on reports. Groups can be assembled into structures that display dimension 

members (such as locations or customers) in a flat list or can be used to create 

multi-level hierarchical structures.

<!-- Page 382 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

In practice, many companies create and manage the majority of account groups and dimension 

structures at the top level of the company. These report structures are then automatically shared 

by all entities, and available for use in financial reports, graphs, and performance cards. 

Best Practices 

To determine whether to create a report structure at the top level or entity level, consider who 

needs to access the structure. 

• 
If a report structure should be available to all entities, create it at the top level. Account 

groups and dimension structures created at the top level automatically appear in the 

corresponding lists in each entity. 

Report structures created at the top level can be edited only at the top level. 

• 
If an entity has particular reporting needs, users can create report structures at the entity 

level. These report structures can then be used within that entity, along with any report 

structures that were inherited from the top level. 

When a user switches to an entity, the user can’t see report structures that were created 
in another entity. 

Top-Level Report Structures 

From the top level of a multi-entity shared company, you can edit and use all reporting structures, 

including those created at the entity level. 

• 
By default, lists initially display only report structures that were created at the top level. 

• 
Click the Include private check box at the top of the list to see report structures that were 

created in an entity. You can edit and use these report structures provided that you have 

access to the entities in which they were created. 

• 
You can Add new top-level report structures and Edit existing structures that were created 

at either the top level or entity level. 

Include Private Does Not Appear on Your Page 

The most common reason that you don’t see this feature is because you’re using a custom view. 

When you select a custom view, some options are hidden. Depending on the page you’re on, the 

Include inactive, Include one-time, Include private, and Display hierarchy options aren’t visible. 

For example, if you’re viewing from a custom view, the Financial reports list won’t provide the 

Include inactive option. 

To see the options again, switch back to View all. See Custom Views for more information. 

Entity-Level Report Structures 

When you switch to an entity, you can use report structures that were created at the top level, 

plus any report structures that were created in that entity.

counts can be reported on by themselves or used to compute metrics such as the recurring 

revenue per customer.

#### Dimension Counts Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 387*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Dimension Counts Workflow 

Setting up dimension count is a multi-step process and requires admin privileges. 

1. 
Create specific statistical accounts to track updates. 

2. 
Configure dimension groups for the counts you want to track. 

3. 
Enable dimension counts and create dimension count rules to provide granularity. 

Step 1. Create a statistical account 

Each dimension count must be posted to a separate statistical account. 

For example, you might create a statistical account for customers located in New York. Based on 

the rule you define for the dimension group; the count of New York customers is tracked 

automatically. When a new customer from New York is added, the statistical account is increased 

by 1. When a New York customer is made inactive (meaning they are no longer a customer), the 

statistical account is decreased by 1. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level statistical accounts are available. You can’t select 
statistical accounts that are private to subsidiary entities. 

See Statistical accounts in online help or download the RealPage Accounting General Ledger User 

Guide. 

Step 2. Configure dimension groups 

A “dimension group” is a name for a particular set of members in a dimension, or a set of 

members that meet certain criteria. For example, you might create customer groups for a 

particular set of customers, customers located in a particular state, or customers with the greatest 

open balance. A dimension group lets you define the rule for updating dimension count. 

For each count to automate, create an appropriate dimension group. There’s a separate 

dimension group list for each type of dimension, and access is controlled by your permissions. 

Some dimension groups, such as customers and vendors, can be accessed from multiple menus. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level dimension groups are available. You can’t select 
dimension groups that are private to subsidiary entities. 

For example, if you want to be able to show only how many of your customers are in New York, 

create a customer group that includes only customers whose main address is in New York. 

If you spell out the state name in the Customer record, set the value to New York. You could also 

add a second filter to include the customer if the value for the State/province equals NY. In this 

case, you would set the filter conditions to Any (OR). Any customer whose record showed the 

state as NY or New York would be included in the group. 

To learn how to create dimension groups, refer to Dimension groups (on page 349). 

---


<!-- Page 388 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Step 3. Create dimension count rules 

Dimension count rules are the foundation of automating statistical account counts. It is these 

rules that allow the finer granularity necessary for insight and analysis. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Create at least one dimension count rule. Each row in General Ledger Setup > Dimension count is`


a separate rule that creates a statistical journal entry when the rule values are met. 

There is no functional limit to the number of dimension count rules you can create, so you can 

automate the process for everything that matches the corporate requirements. 

To learn about creating rules, refer to Dimension count rules (on page 394) and Creating 

Dimension Count Rules (on page 394). 

Step 4. Select the statistical journal 

Select or create the statistical journal into which transactions are posted when a dimension count 

rule is matched. This can be a new statistical journal or an existing one. One statistical journal is 

used for all dimension count transactions. This journal helps you organize dimension counts for 

your audit log, to understand how the counts are updated. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level statistical journals are available. You can’t select 
statistical journals that are private to subsidiary entities. 

Establish a Base Count 

When you enable dimension count, only new updates are included in statistical account updates. 

The existing dimension objects are not included, even if they match the dimension count criteria. 

Enter a manual journal entry to the statistical account to establish a beginning balance as a 

starting point. 

To learn how to enter a manual journal entry, refer to Statistical journal entries. 

Best practice: If you’ve already set up a dimension count rule, don’t disable the dimension. 

Disabling the dimension can cause unexpected behavior. 

---



#### Automated Dimension Count Posting
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 389*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Automated Dimension Count Posting 

Statistical accounts are often used to track the number of dimension members. For example, it’s 

common to track the number of active customers. This information can be reported on by itself or 

used to compute metrics such as the recurring revenue per customer. 

You can: 

• 
Automate counts for any enabled dimension. As you add or remove dimension members, 

the count is automatically updated. 

• 
Set up rules that define what you want to count. For example, in addition to tracking the 

number of active customers, you might set up a separate statistical account for tracking 

different customer types. 

About Dimension Counts 

There are many reasons for automating the dimension count to a statistical account. It saves time 

and effort—especially when you are tracking many dimensions and can increase insight into your 

business. 

Manual vs. Automated Posting 

Your company might already use multiple spreadsheets to track changes for various things like 

new, lost, and long-time customers. With the dimension count posting feature, the system 

updates dimension counts automatically, reducing the need for manual spreadsheets that are 

time-consuming and sometimes error prone. 

You can still post changes manually—for example, when establishing a base count—but 

automating the count eliminates data-entry work by reducing the steps needed to update the 

count accurately and immediately. 

Use in Metrics 

Finely tuned metrics increase insight into your business and provide greater detail when you are 

making business decisions. By providing a way to automate counts, dimension count gives you 

flexibility to ensure that your metrics are appropriate and accurate. 

To increase the granularity of business metrics, analysis, or reporting, different posting rules 

update different statistic counts. You can use the values in computational reports and 

performance cards to increase insight into how your company is doing. 

Dimension counts use a separate dimension group for each dimension rule you create. There is 

no limit to the number of things that can be tracked automatically. 

---


<!-- Page 390 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setup Overview 

A dimension must be enabled for dimension counts to work. For example, to use the Locations 
dimension count, the Location dimension must be active. If you don’t see a particular dimension 
count, verify that the dimension is enabled in Dimension settings. 

The dimension count setup process requires admin privileges and requires setting up a statistical 

account for each dimension count and then defining the rules for posting. Creating a dimension 

count rule is a one-time process. After that, dimension count changes are automatic and don’t 

need any further action. 

For example, you might create a rule to update the count of active customers based in Vermont 

who have a high credit limit. Any time a customer moves into that group, the dimension count 

rule creates a statistical journal entry to increase the count. If a customer moves out of the group, 

then the same dimension count rule creates an entry to decrease the count. 

Best practice: If you’ve already set up a dimension count rule, then don’t disable the dimension. 
Disabling the dimension can cause unexpected behavior. 

For step-by-step setup instructions, refer to Set up dimension count (on page 393). 

Functionality of Automated Posting 

1. 
Create statistical accounts and dimension groups for dimension count to use. 

2. 
Establish the initial base value of the count, such as the customer count as of the date you 

begin automated posting. 

3. 
As you create the dimension count rules, the system automatically monitors increases and 

decreases and posts journal entries to the statistical journal. 

Establishing a Base Count 

When you enable dimension count, only new updates are included in statistical account updates. 

The existing dimension objects are not included, even if they match the dimension count criteria. 

Enter a manual journal entry to the statistical account to establish a beginning balance as a 

starting point. This step is optional, but if you don’t establish a base count, then the count starts 

at zero and only new changes are recorded. There is no historical starting point. 

In many cases, the company could be maintaining a spreadsheet with the information you want to 

track. After a base count is included in the statistical account, you might be able to get rid of 

these spreadsheets and let the system track and count for you. 

---


<!-- Page 391 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

For details on manual journal entries, refer to Statistical journal entries. 

Functionality of Dimension Count Updates 

After a dimension count is set up, the system automatically posts entries when you create and 

save a new object or delete an object that matches the rule. You can’t create an automated post 

for a previous period. 

For example, if you created a customer record on 12/2/2019, then the customer count is 

increased for the date of 12/2/2019, the date that the record was created. Because the count 

update is automated, the transaction date is not configurable in the dimension count rules. 

Adding Counts to the Previous Period 

Continuing the example, suppose that this customer signed the deal on 11/26/2019. In this case, 

you want the customer count to be posted and counted for the month of November, even 

though the customer record wasn’t created until December, but the system would post the record 

for December. You can’t edit any of the system-posted record counts. This preserves the business 

rule audit trail. However, you can manually adjust the count to November by both increasing the 

count with 11/26/2019 and decreasing the count with 12/2/2019 accordingly. 

As you create new dimension count rules, newly created objects that match the rules are posted 

to the journal and added to the statistical account. Existing objects that match the dimension 

count rules are not added, only new objects are. Deleting a rule doesn’t remove the object from 

the statistical account count, but new count changes aren’t updated automatically. 

Editing a Dimension Record That Is Used by Dimension Count 

When you make a change to a record that is used by dimension count, the appropriate journal 

entry is updated at that time. Record changes are made the same way you change any other 

record for that dimension. 

For example, suppose you have a vendor who is included in the dimension group for California 

vendors and is part of a dimension count rule. If this vendor moved to another state, you would 

change the vendor record to reflect the new address. When you change the record, the 

appropriate changes are made by dimension count: the count of California vendors is decreased 

by one. If there is a dimension group/rule for the new state, then that count is increased by one. 

There is one exception to this: employee records and location. 

Special Case: Changing an Employee Location in a Multi-Entity Company 

For multi-entity companies, the employee record requires a location. This tells the system which 

entity the employee belongs with. If you change the location of an employee from one entity to 

another, then the record is changed correctly. But because the dimension count gets the location 

from the employee record, dimension count handles the change a bit differently, and that affects 

how the count is changed. 

---


<!-- Page 392 -->
Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Best practice: To ensure that the count is correct for both the original and the new location, many 

companies find that the following steps are helpful. 

1. 
Make the employee inactive to remove the count from original location. 

2. 
While the employee is still inactive, change the employee location. 

3. 
Set the employee record back to active. 

Alternatively, you can make statistical journal entries manually to reduce the original employee by 

location count by one and add the employee by location count by one. 

The following examples show some of the possible uses of dimension count. 

Customer Retention Rate 

Automate the count of new customers you acquired for a period, how many existing customers 

stayed, and how many customers left. Count by total customers or filter further, such as by 

location or salesperson. 

Suppose you started out with 365 customers for a period. Over the period you added ten new 

customers but lost three. Rather than just reporting that you now have 372 customers, dimension 

count automates the count, making it available for reports. 

Customer Count by Customer Type 

Using dimension count makes it easy to automatically track by customers of a certain type or 

industry—anything from direct and retail sales, by ZIP Code range, state, or country. Knowing how 

many customers of different types can help your company make business decisions. 

Employee Retention 

One of the most important assets a company has is its employees. You need to know not just how 

many employees the company has at a certain period, but how many are new, how many have 

left, and even how long the average employee stays with the company. You can break it down 

even further and see which locations or departments have higher or lower attrition rates at a 

glance. Dimension count can automate that information for inclusion in reports.

Setting Up a Dimension Count 

You have flexibility to automate posting count changes from dimension groups for any 

dimension, such as customers and vendors, to a statistical account using dimension count rules. 

Use it to automate counts for things like: 

• 
customer retention rate 

• 
customer count by type 

Automate Dimension Count Changes 

Dimension count rules automatically post a journal transaction and update the count to a 

statistical journal based on the dimension groups you specify, any time you create a dimension 

member record, such as customer or item, which matches the rule. 

To make sure that counts are always current, dimension count posts a transaction based on the 

system date when the dimension member record is saved or deleted. 

A dimension must be enabled for dimension counts to work. For example, to use the Locations 
dimension count, the Location dimension must be active. If you don’t see a particular dimension 
count, verify that the dimension is enabled in the Dimension settings section of General ledger 
configuration. 


> **Navigation Path:** `See the Dimension Settings section of the General Ledger application. Go to General Ledger >`



> **Navigation Path:** `Setup > Configuration.`


You can configure dimensions to automatically post statistical journal entries whenever their 

counts change, based on the criteria you select. 

You can configure dimensions so that the system automatically updates count changes to a 

statistical account using dimension groups and dimension count rules. You can post and track 

dimension count changes automatically, providing more granular metrics to measure your 

business. Better metrics information means better insight.

##### Creating Dimension Count Rules
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 394*

Dimension Count Rules 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Advanced GL Section > Dimension Count List`


Dimension count rules enable automation of object count updates to statistical accounts. This 

gives you a simple way to track exactly the specifics that you want. For example, automate counts 

for only direct customers, only departments with offices in London, or vendors active in the 

Northeast. These types of counts are often used for averaging and analysis. 

Configuration 

You configure the dimensions you want the system to track and define the statistical journal 

where the system is to track the dimension counts. 

• 
Define the “rules” that control the count of what you’re tracking. (You select the dimensions 

that you want the system to count and the account that the rules apply to.) 

• 
Select the statistical account to use for each dimension count rule. 

Results 

Based on your configuration of the dimension count rules, the system creates statistical journal 

entries and automatically updates dimension counts to a statistical account. As your dimension 

count changes, the increase or decrease is automatically posted to the statistical account. 

Creating Dimension Count Rules 

To create dimension count rules: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select General Ledger, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

The system opens the General ledger setup page. 

3. 
Under the Advanced G/L options section, go to the Dimension count list. 

4. 
Under the Dimensions column, click the drop-down list for a line item, and then select a 

dimension. The system displays all available standard and user-defined dimensions in the 

drop-down list. 

For multi-entity companies: In multi-entity companies, you can set a dimension group 
filter to create the dimensions at either the top or entity level so you can further filter the 
dimension records to find all the dimensions, based on where they were created. 

5. 
Under the Account column, select or create the statistical account to associate with this 

dimension count rule. Only the top-level statistical accounts are available. 

The statistical account you select is the account into which any matching dimension count 

rules are updated. For example, if you select a statistical account for customers in California, 

---


<!-- Page 395 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

that statistical account is updated any time a customer that matches the rule is added or 

removed. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level statistical accounts are available. You can’t 
select statistical accounts that are private to subsidiary entities. 

6. 
Under the Active dimension group column, select the dimension group to match the 

dimension object. 

A “dimension group” is a name for a particular set of members in a dimension, or a set of 

members that meet certain criteria. For example, you might create customer groups for a 

particular set of customers, customers located in a particular state, or even customers with 

the greatest open balance. 

When creating a dimension group for dimension count, you can use a broad set of criteria 

for the group or use filtering to ensure that your update counts match specific needs, such 

as items groups whose average cost is higher or lower than a certain amount. 

If you don’t see a particular dimension group in a menu, ask your administrator to give you 
permission to the dimension group. There are separate permissions for each application 
from which you can access the dimension group list. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level dimension groups are available. You can’t 
select dimension groups that are private to subsidiary entities. 

7. 
Under the Posting description column, enter text for the system to use when the item is 

posted to the statistical journal used to contain dimension count posting. 

8. 
Under the Posting location column, select or create a location to associate with the 

dimension count rule. 

For multi-entity companies: Select a posting entity. Posting entities are required for 
multi-entity companies, because the dimensions are set up at the top level in multi-entity 
companies. Essentially, you need to assign one entity (location) for each transaction rule. 
This ensures that a member of the entity can be responsible for the transaction. 

9. 
Repeat this process for each object to be included in a dimension count. 

You can create multiple dimension count rules. However, the total of all dimension count 
rule information combined is limited to 4,000 characters. If you plan to create a large 
number of dimension count rules, best practice is to limit the size of the posting 
description. 

10. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the statistical journal where you want the system to 

post new transactions.

#### Dimension FAQs
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 398*

Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension FAQs 

How do I create a group for all members of a dimension? 

You can easily create a dimension group that includes all active members of a dimension. 

When creating the dimension group, select the following options: 

1. 
Select All members as the group type. 

2. 
Change the sort order as needed. 

3. 
In the Filters list, filter for all Active members. 

• 
For the Field, select Status. 

• 
For the Operator, select equals. 

• 
For the Value, select Active. 

What do the filter operators mean? 

Depending on the type of field you select, matching can work differently. 

• 
For numerical fields, equals, greater than, and less than are often used to filter based on 

whether the amount is equal to, above, or below the number you enter. 

• 
In general, non-number fields ask you to select a specific record from a list (for example, a 

specific department name or manager). For these types of fields, equals, not equal to, is 

empty, and is not empty are the most useful operators. 

• 
If you want to match records that contain a certain word (for example, project names that 

contain the word design), use the contains operator. Instead of choosing a record from a list, 

enter the word in the Value field. 

What date is used when filter for amounts? 

Some fields, such as amount due and item price, contain data that can change over time. For the 

purposes of filtering reports, amount-based filters are always applied using the most current data, 

even if the as of date for the report is in the past. 

For example, suppose that you create a revenue report that filters for items with the highest price. 

When you run the report, the filter will be applied based on the current price of the items, even if 

the report is being run for a prior reporting period. 

Are filters applied to all members of the dimension, or just the members in the 
Members list? 

The filters operate differently depending on whether you select any specific members in the 

Members list. 

• 
If you use the Members list to select specific dimension members, such as particular 

departments or customers, the filters will be applied only to those specific members.

*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 399*



##### Reports That Support Dimensions
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 399*

Chapter 2: Working with Dimensions

• 
To apply filters to all members of a dimension (for example, selecting all your locations 

where the Status equals Active) do not select any specific members in the Members list. 

Example: Suppose that you have a location group that has three members—California, New York, 

and Oregon (an inactive location)—and you then add a filter for locations where the Status equals 

Active. In this case, when you use the location group to filter reports, the report will include data 

only for California and New York and will not include the inactive location. 

How are hierarchical dimensions handled? 

Dimensions are often hierarchical. For example, a department can have one or more child 

departments, up to several levels deep. 

When a report filter includes a member of a dimension, data from any members that belong to it 

will also be included. This means that a department group that matches the Engineering 

department will automatically include data from any sub departments (like Development, Quality 

Assurance, and Documentation.) 

When filtering financial reports by department or location, you can decide to exclude sub 
departments or sub locations by deselecting the Include Subs option under the filter field. 

How do I include inactive dimensions in reports? 

Create a dimension group that is filtered to include both inactive and active members. Then use 

that dimension group to filter financial reports. 

See the help for the specific dimension. For example, for department, see the details on making a 

dimension inactive.

What Happens After Implementing Dimensions 

After you implement the standard dimensions, you want to use, and create any unique 

dimensions you might need, the system propagates your dimensions everywhere that you want to 

access them: 

• 
Transactions: On the transaction entry pages, you can select the dimensions that you want 

to propagate to the general ledger. By selecting dimensions in various transactions such as 

A/P or A/R invoices, you organize and prepare your operational and financial information to 

be sliced and diced any way that you need to gain insight into your business. 

• 
Reports: Dimensions are a core component of reporting to help you meet the needs of your 

changing business and instantly track performance by different business drivers as your 

strategies and operations change. Using dimensions in reporting, you can create almost 

limitless ways of viewing your information and capturing key metrics. 

What Happens After Inactivating a Dimension Value 

When you inactivate a dimension value, it no longer appears in your drop-down lists. This helps 

prevent the creation of new transactions using that dimension value. However, your dimension 

value still exists within the company, so inactivating a dimension value will not affect your 

financial reporting because the dimension value still rolls up to the top-level of the dimension 

hierarchy at the time the report is run. 

For instance, your California location dimension has a Northern California and Southern California 

child dimension associated with it. Your Southern California location closes in June, so you 

inactivate the dimension value. Users can no longer create transactions against that dimension 

value. However, at the end of the year, you still need to see how you did at that location while it 

was open. You can’t run a report on Southern California because it is inactivated, but you can run 

a report on California for the year. The system automatically rolls up all transactions including the 

Southern California location and displays in your California report. 

How Filters Are Applied to Dimension Groups 

The filters operate differently depending on whether you select any specific members in the 

Members list.

departments or customers, the filters will be applied only to those specific members.  

• 
To apply filters to all members of a dimension (for example, selecting all your locations 

where the Status equals “Active”) do not select any specific members in the Members list. 

Example 

Suppose that you have a location group that has three members—California, New York, and 

Oregon (an inactive location)—and you then add a filter for locations where the Status equals 

Active. In this case, when you use the location group to filter reports, the report will include data 

only for California and New York and will not include the inactive location.

Creating a Cover Letter Template 

To add a cover letter, you must first create a cover letter template. The cover letter template 

contains the text of your cover letter, and you create it using Microsoft Word. 

When you create your cover letter template, you can use merge fields in place of 

company-specific information, such as the company name, address, and reporting period dates. 

Using merge fields makes the template reusable and dynamic. When your memorized report 

group runs, it replaces the merge fields with the actual names, descriptions, and other specific 

information from your company or entity. For example, if you are an accountant, using merge 

fields for the company name and other company-specific information allows you to reuse the 

cover letter template for multiple client companies. 

For descriptions of the different merge fields, see Merge fields for cover letters (on page 405). 

To create a cover letter template: 

1. 
Create a new document in Microsoft Word, and then write your cover letter template. 

2. 
For company-specific information in your cover letter template, substitute the 

corresponding merge field. You can copy and paste merge fields. See the list of merge fields 

(on page 405). 

3. 
Save the cover letter template.

information from your company or entity. For example, if you are an accountant, using merge

Report Groups List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 411) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

A report group provides an efficient and quick way to act upon multiple reports simultaneously. 

For example, instead of having to run or schedule a set of reports one at a time, you can run a 

report group, which runs all of the member reports immediately or according to schedule. 

You can use the Report groups list to: 

• 
Add, edit, view, and delete report group information. 

• 
Run a report group on demand. 

• 
Schedule a date and time you want to run a report group. 

• 
View stored reports associated with a report group. 

• 
View operational reports associated with a report group. 

• 
View the status of a scheduled report group, including a log of executions and errors. 

Report groups that are public are available to any user with permissions to memorized report 
groups. If a report group is private, you can edit or run the report group only if you are the 
report owner or if you have full or limited administrator privileges. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

These permissions are required to work with report groups: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Report Groups 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a

Adding a Report Group 

Report Groups > Add 

See the How to Get Here (on page 411) topic for a list of ways to access the Report Groups list. 

To create a report group, fill in the report group information, add reports to the group, and set up 

any default parameters you want to apply to the report group at large. 

Filling In the Report Group Details 

1. 
Type a Name and Description for the report group. Names should contain letters and 

numbers and can contain single spaces or dashes. Do not use special characters in report 

group names. 

You can’t change the report group name after you’ve saved it. 

2. 
If you want to use a cover letter for the group, then select a Cover letter from the 

drop-down list and set a Cover letter reporting period. 

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to ask the user to select a reporting period at runtime. 

4. 
If you want the reports in this group to be numbered continuously, select the Sequential 

page numbering check box. For example, if the first report ends on page 3, then the next 

report starts on page 4, and so on for all of the reports in the group. 

---


<!-- Page 412 -->
Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
To make this report group available to other users who have permission for the memorized 

report groups feature, select the Public check box. 

6. 
You can add text to the footer that overrides any footer set in a group member. If you enter 

no footer here, then each report defaults to its own footer, if any. A footer can include up to 

400 characters. 

7. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to allow the user to create the footer text at runtime. 

By default, the user who creates the report group is listed as the Report owner. The report 
group can be edited and used by the report owner and any users with limited or full 
administrator privileges. If you mark the report group as Public, the report group is also 
available to other users who have permission to memorized report groups. 

8. 
In the Members list, click the Member drop-down line item, and then select a report to add 

to the group. Select all reports in the listed report groups to help you create complete 

owner reports in RealPage Accounting. 

OneSite reports are the last reports in the report output regardless of the order defined in 
the Members list. 

Setting Up Default Parameters (Optional) 

You can set up default parameters to save time when running or scheduling the report group. The 

system will automatically populate these parameters each time you run or schedule the report 

group; however, you can manually change the fields as needed. 

In the Default parameters section: 

1. 
In the As of date field, type the starting date from which to run the report.  

If you leave this field blank, then it will default to today’s date. 

2. 
In the Location/group drop-down list, select a specific location or location group for which 

you want to run the report. 

Report groups with Bank Reconciliation, Bank Reconciliation with Attachments, Bank 
Reconciliation Outstanding Items, Bank Reconciliation Adjusted Items, Delinquent and 
Prepaids, Security Deposits, and Rent Roll reports can be run on a location group and will 
generate individual reports per location. 

3. 
Select the Grouped by location/entity check box if you want to group the report data by 

location or entity. 

• 
Upon selecting the Grouped by location/entity check box, you can create a separate 

file per location. Select the Separate file per location/entity check box. 

• 
If the Separate file per location/entity check box is not enabled, the system creates 

the report group for each location and combines all reports into one file.

Select the Create zipped file check box to zip the files together when created.

group, then you can define separate account groups for these reports when running the 

report group:

Account group for delinquent and prepaid: Select an account group from the

Viewing a Report Group 

Report Groups > View Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 411) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view a report group on demand instead of waiting for the report’s scheduled run time. 

To view a report group on demand: 

1. 
In the Reports groups list, click the View link next to the report group. The Report Group 

Information page opens. 

2. 
View a list of reports stored in your system. Stored reports can be run at a later time. 

The data in stored reports are only as current as the date on which you ran the report and 
do not reflect any changes since then. However, you can access the actual data if you drill 
down through the report into other pages. 

Running a Report Group On Demand 

Report Groups > Run 

See the How to Get Here (on page 411) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can run a report group on demand instead of waiting for the report’s scheduled run time. 

Depending on the report group, certain conditions may apply: 

• 
If you run a report group with A/P Invoice Packages, the packages will include all invoices 

for the month (with attachments). 

• 
If you run a report group with Leasing & Rents reports or Bank Reconciliations on a location 

group, then the reports will be run as individual reports. 

• 
If you run a report group with Bank Reconciliations, then you will need to specify a location. 

If you have chosen to include Bank Reconciliations and you do not specify a location when 

running or scheduling the report, then the Bank Reconciliations will not be included in the 

report output. 

• 
If you run a report group with OneSite reports, the OneSite reports will be the last reports in 

the report group, regardless of the order defined in the Members list. 

• 
If you run a report group containing the Job Cost Open Invoices or Job Setup Summary 

report on a location group, then the report will include jobs for all locations in the location 

group.

Viewing Stored Report Groups 

Reports run in the report group based on the As of date and/or Location/group you provide. 

When the reports are ready, you can view them in the My stored reports list (on page 460), 

available from the application in which you requested the report to be stored. 

If you have numerous entities, the location box can save you significant setup time. Create one 
generic report group without a location; when you run this generic report, you can specify the 
location you want. This saves you time you would otherwise spend setting up and maintaining 
multiple report groups per month per entity or location or editing each report location prior to 
the group’s scheduled run. 

You can also use the Run link to schedule an “off-cycle” run—that is, you can schedule the group 
in advance to run on any day other than its regularly scheduled day.

group, then the reports will be run as individual reports.

the report group, regardless of the order defined in the Members list.

report on a location group, then the report will include jobs for all locations in the location 

group.

schedule. The Schedule report group page opens.

In the Location/group drop-down list, select a specific location or location group for which 

you want to run the report.

Scheduling the Report Group 

In the Schedule section: 

---


<!-- Page 419 -->
Chapter 3: Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system 
will run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save. 

If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule Financial 

Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box to schedule reports 
and reports groups to run at that time.

Viewing the Status of a Scheduled Report Group 

Report Groups > (Status) 

See the How to Get Here (on page 411) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

If a report group is set to run on an automatic schedule, then you can view an execution log of 

previous runs and an error log for any failed attempts. 

To view the status of a scheduled report group: 

1. 
In the Report groups list, click one of the following links: 

• 
Status: This link appears if the schedule is ongoing. 

• 
Schedule completed with errors: This link appears if the report group has finished 

running for all scheduled occurrences, but one or more executions failed. 

If the report group was not scheduled to run or if it completed all scheduled runs 
successfully, then the status will display as Not scheduled or Schedule complete, 
respectively. Both of these statuses are read-only fields. 

The Schedule report group - Execution log page opens with the following information for 

each transaction log: 

• 
Log created on date: This is the date that the system generated the log. 

• 
Transaction date: This is the date that the run attempt occurred, as determined by the 

report group’s schedule. 

• 
Execution status: This displays whether the run attempt succeeded or failed. If it failed, 

then you can click the Failure link to open the Error log page (on page 427) with the 

details of any errors that occurred. 

2. 
When you have finished, click Done to return to the previous page or click Export to export 

the log to a CSV, Excel, Word, or PDF file.

##### Adding Members to a Report Group
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 423*

Chapter 3: Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Report Group Information Page 

Report Groups > Add/View/Edit 

See the How to Get Here (on page 411) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

A report group is a collection of two or more memorized reports that you can run (or schedule to 

run) at the same time. You can add a report group, edit information for a specific report group, or 

view information on the Report group information page. 

This page has two sections: 

• 
(Top section): Use this section to enter general information about the report group and add 

members to the group. Members can be memorized reports or bank reconciliations. 

• 
Default parameters: Use this section to set up any default parameters you want to apply to 

the report group. The system automatically populates these fields when you run or schedule 

the report group; however, you can override the default parameters as needed. 

Adding Members to a Report Group 

Report Groups > Edit 

See the How to Get Here (on page 411) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

A report group is a collection of two or more memorized reports—or bank reconciliations—that 

you run or schedule to run at the same time. The Report group information page lists all the 

members of a report group. Edit the report group to add and remove members. 

You can add financial, standard, or custom reports to a report group if they have been memorized 

in RealPage Accounting. You can also include operational reports from OneSite Leasing & Rents. 

This includes: 

• 
All Units 

• 
Bank Deposit Details (Excel) 

• 
Bank Deposit Summary 

• 
Delinquent and Prepaid 

• 
Monthly Transaction Summary 

• 
Rent Roll 

• 
Rent Roll Detail 

• 
Rent Roll Detail (Excel) 

• 
Resident Balance by Fiscal Period 

• 
Resident Deposit Audit by Fiscal Period 

• 
Security Deposits 

• 
Transaction Summary by Unit

##### Removing a Report from a Report Group
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 424*

Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

When you run or schedule report groups that include a OneSite Leasing & Rents report, you can 
define whether the OneSite report is for the current or previous Fiscal period. For example, if it 
is March but you are generating a report for February, choose “Previous A/R period.” This field is 
also available as a default parameter (on page 411). 

To add a member to a report group: 

1. 
In the Report groups list, click the Edit link next to the report group for which you are 

adding a member. 

The Report group information page opens. 

2. 
In the Members section, click the first empty row, and then select the memorized report or 

bank reconciliation from the Member drop-down list. 

3. 
Add other members as needed. To remove a memorized report from the group, select it in 

the Members list, and then click the 
 Remove icon. 

4. 
Click Save. 

OneSite reports will be the last reports in the report output, regardless of the order defined in 
the Members list. 

Removing a Report from a Report Group 

See the How to Get Here (on page 411) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

If a report is no longer needed in a report group, you can remove it from the group. 

1. 
In the Report groups list, click the Edit link next to the report group. The Report group 

information page opens. 

2. 
In the Members section, select the report you want to remove, and then click 
 Remove. 

3. 
Click OK to confirm that you want to delete the report. 

4. 
Click Save.

Chapter 3: Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Prompt on run 
Select this check box to prompt for a cover letter reporting period or group 
footnote when you run the report. You can enter a new footnote or replace 
an existing footnote in the prompt box at runtime. 

Sequential page 
numbering 

Select this check box if you want the reports in this group to be numbered 
continuously. For example, if the first report ends on page 3, then the next 
report starts on page 4—and so on—for all reports in the group. 

Public 
Select this check box if you want to make the report group available to other 
users. 

Footer text 
Type footer text here if you want the same footnote to appear for any group 
member that allows footers. Leave this blank if you want to keep any 
individually specified footnotes. A footnote can include up to 400 characters. 

A page footer is created in a client or entity, while an accountant’s footer 
is created at the console level. Each footer can hold up to 400 characters; 
however, they can print and view a combined total of 600 characters. The 
number of characters in the page footer takes priority; if the total of the 
two footers exceeds 600 characters, then the footer text will be truncated 
in the report. For example, if a page footer has 380 characters, then the 
accountant’s footer can print only 220 characters. 

Report owner 
Select the user who is responsible for this report group. 

If the report group is not marked as Public, then only the report owner and 
administrators can view and manage the report group. 

Members 
Use the Members list to include memorized reports and bank reconciliations 
in the report group. You must add at least one memorized report. 

Depending on the report group, certain conditions may apply: 

• 
If you run a report group with A/P Invoice Packages, the packages will 
include all invoices for the month (with attachments). 

• 
If you run a report group with Leasing & Rents reports or Bank 
Reconciliations on a location group, then the reports will be run as 
individual reports. 

• 
If you run a report group with Bank Reconciliations, then you will need 
to specify a location. If you have chosen to include Bank 
Reconciliations and you do not specify a location when running or 
scheduling the report, then the Bank Reconciliations will not be 
included in the report output. 

• 
If you run a report group with OneSite reports, the OneSite reports 
will be the last reports in the report group, regardless of the order 
defined in the Members list. 

• 
If you run a report group containing the Job Cost Open Invoices or Job 
Setup Summary report on a location group, then the report will 
include jobs for all locations in the location group.
