#### Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 436*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 436*

Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reporting Periods 

See the How to Get Here (on page 437) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Reporting periods are used when you create reports and budgets, and when you open and close 

books. They let you limit the information on the report to specific time ranges. 

There are out-of-the-box (system) reporting periods that are most commonly used, such as: 

• 
Prior/Current/Next month 

• 
Prior/Current/Next quarter 

• 
Prior/Current/Next year 

• 
Current <month/quarter/year> to date 

Companies often work on unique schedules. If the out-of-the-box reporting periods don’t meet 

your needs, create additional ones. For information, see Adding Reporting Periods (on page 438). 

There are some system-based reporting periods, like Current month, that you can run repeatedly 

without modification. For some types of reports, that’s all you need. 

For other reports, you need to specify the period that the report spans. Date-driven reports that 

you create are used with specific calendar periods (for example, for budgeting or opening and 

closing books). For these reports, you need to create a matching reporting period. 

There are many reasons you might want a specific reporting period. For example, manually 

creating a reporting period makes sense for some companies that: 

• 
Run and report on a weekly basis 

• 
Don’t end periods at the end of the month 

• 
Work from a 28-day cycle instead of a calendar month 

• 
Need past or future reporting periods 

Reporting periods enable you to limit the data shown on reports based on the way your company 

works. 

Before You Begin 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Permissions 

You must have been granted Reporting Periods permissions. The permissions can be granted 

either in Company, General Ledger, or both. These permissions are required to create and change 

reporting periods.

*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 438*

Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reporting Periods List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 437) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Reporting periods are used when you create reports and budgets, and when you open and close 

books. They let you limit the information in the report to specific time ranges. 

Use this list to work with reporting periods. You can: 

• 
View a reporting period’s details. 

• 
Edit a reporting period’s details. 

• 
Add a new reporting period. 

• 
Delete a reporting period. 

• 
Export the list of reporting periods. 

• 
Use the standard list tools: sorting, filtering, and list views. 
Adding Reporting Periods 

 Reporting Periods 

See the How to Get Here (on page 437) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

To add a reporting period: 

1. 
Click 
 Reporting Periods to create a new reporting period record. 

2. 
Type a Name for the reporting period. 

3. 
Type a Column header for the first column and, optionally, a Column header 2 for the 

second column. 

4. 
Type or select a Start date and an End date for the reporting period. 

5. 
Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. 

To make this reporting period available on the Budgets page, select the Use for budgeting 

check box. 

If you don’t see this check box, then make sure that you have permissions for budgeting. 

6. 
If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule Financial 

Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box to schedule 

reports and reports groups to run at that time. 

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists. 

8. 
Click Save.

Use the Reporting period information page to add a new reporting period or view and edit

books. They let you limit the information on the report to specific time ranges.

company information setup.

#### Weekly Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 446*

Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Weekly Reporting Periods 

The weekly reporting periods are based on the day of the week you set for Week begins on in 

Company Information setup. 

• 
This week: The entire current week, based on the day of the week your company configured 

as the start of the week. For example, Sunday through Saturday. 

• 
Last week: The entire past week, based on the day of the week your company configured as 

the start of the week. 

• 
Today: The current day. 

• 
Yesterday: The prior day. 

---



#### Monthly Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 447*

Chapter 3: Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Monthly Reporting Periods 

These reporting periods are based on the calendar year. 

• 
Next month: The next calendar month, beginning on the first and ending on the last day of 

the month. For example, if the current date is Aug 14, “Next month” would include Sept 1 

through Sept 30. 

• 
Current month: The current month in its entirety, even if the month is not over yet. For 

example, if the current date is Dec 11, “Current month” would include Dec 1 through Dec 31. 

• 
Current month to date: The current month only up to the current date. For example, if the 

current date is Jan 22, “Current month to date” would include Jan 1 through Jan 22. 

• 
Prior month: The prior month in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Dec 11, “Prior 

month” would include Nov 1 through Nov 30. 

• 
Prior month to date: The prior month, to the current date, but of the prior month. For 

example, if the current date is Jul 11, “Prior Month to Date” would include Jun 1 through Jun 

11. 

• 
One year ago month: The same month in the previous year, in its entirety. For example, if 

the current date is June 6, 2019, “One year ago month” would include June 1, 2018 through 

June 30, 2018. 

---



#### Quarterly Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 448*

Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Quarterly Reporting Periods 

These reporting periods are based on the calendar year. Each quarter includes three months: 

Jan-Mar, Apr-Jun, Jul-Sept, and Oct-Dec. 

• 
Next quarter: The next calendar quarter, beginning on the first day of the next quarter and 

ending on the last day of the quarter. For example, if the current date is Aug 14, “Next 

quarter” would include Oct 1 through Dec 31. 

• 
Current quarter: The current quarter in its entirety, even if the quarter is not over yet. For 

example, if the current date is Aug 11, “Current quarter” would include Jul 1 through Sept 

30. 

• 
Current quarter to date: The current quarter up to the current date only. For example, if the 

current date is Feb 22, “Current quarter to date” would include Jan 1 through Feb 22. 

• 
Prior quarter: The prior quarter in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Dec 11, 

“Prior quarter” would include Jul 1 through Sept 30. 

• 
One year ago quarter: The same quarter in the previous year, in its entirety. For example, if 

the current date is June 6, 2019, “One year ago quarter” would include April 1, 2018 through 

June 30, 2018. 

---



#### Yearly Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 449*

Chapter 3: Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Yearly Reporting Periods 

These reporting periods are based on the calendar year (Jan 1–Dec 31). 

• 
Next year: The next calendar year, beginning on the first day of the next year and ending on 

the last day of the year. For example, if the current date is Aug 14, 2019, “Next year” would 

include Jan 1, 2020 through Dec 31, 2020. 

• 
Current year: The current year in its entirety, even if the year is not yet over. For example, if 

the current date is Aug 11, “Current year” would include Jan 1 through Dec 31. 

• 
Current year to date: The current year up to the current date only. For example, if the 

current date is May 22, “Current year to date” would include Jan 1 through May 22. 

• 
Current year through current month: The current year up to the last day of the current 

month only. For example, if the current date is May 6, “Current year through current month” 

would include Jan 1 through May 31. 

• 
Current year through prior month: The current year up to the last day of the previous 

month only. For example, if the current date is May 6, “Current year through prior month” 

would include Jan 1 through Apr 30. 

• 
Prior year: The prior year in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Dec 11, 2019, 

“Prior year” would include Jan 1, 2018 through Dec 31, 2018. 

• 
Prior year current month: The same month in the previous year, in its entirety. For example, 

if the current date is Jun 6, 2019, “Prior year current month” would include Jun 1, 2018 

through Jun 30, 2018. 

• 
Prior year prior month: The previous month of the current one, but in the previous year, in 

its entirety. For example, if the current date is Jun 6, 2019, “Prior year prior month” would 

include May 1, 2018 through May 31, 2018. 

• 
Prior year next month: The next month based on the current date, but in the previous year, 

in its entirety. For example, if the current date is May 6, 2019, “Prior year next month” would 

include June 1, 2018 through June 30, 2018. 

• 
Prior year current quarter: The current quarter based on the current date, but in the 

previous year, in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Oct 6, 2019, “Prior year 

current quarter” would include Oct 1, 2018 through Dec 31, 2018. 

• 
Prior year prior quarter: The previous quarter based on the current date, but in the previous 

year, in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Jul 6, 2019, “Prior year prior quarter” 

would include Apr 1, 2018 through Jun 30, 2018. 

• 
Prior year next quarter: The next quarter based on the current date, but in the previous 

year, in its entirety. For example, if the current date is May 6, 2019, “Prior year next quarter” 

would include Jul 1, 2018 through Sept 30, 2018. 

---



#### Inception Reporting Period
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 450*

Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Inception Reporting Period 

The Inception to date reporting period includes all transactions from the very first one, regardless 

of when it was, up to the current date. 

This reporting period should be used with caution. By including every transaction from the 
beginning, this reporting period can cause a performance slowdown or stoppage. 

---



#### Fiscal Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 451*

Chapter 3: Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Fiscal Reporting Periods 

The fiscal reporting periods are essentially the same as the calendar reporting periods but are 

used when you want to use fiscal reporting periods that are different than the calendar ones. 

Many companies have a fiscal year that differs from the calendar year. In this case, you would use 

the fiscal reporting periods. You need to have defined the company fiscal year during company 

setup. 

The reporting periods are fundamentally the same as those with the calendar year, but based on 

your company’s fiscal year, as configured in Company Information. 

As an example, the following periods use a fictional company whose fiscal year begins Feb 1 and 

ends Jan 31. Fiscal quarters in this configuration would include Feb 1 - Apr 30, May 1 - Jul 31, Aug 

1 - Oct 31, and Nov 1 - Jan 31. 

• 
Fiscal - Next quarter: The next fiscal quarter, beginning on the first day of the next quarter 

and ending on the last day of the quarter. For example, if the current date is Feb 14, “Fiscal - 

Next quarter” would include May 1 through Jul 31. 

• 
Fiscal - Current quarter: The current fiscal quarter, beginning on the first day of the quarter 

and ending on the last day of the quarter. For example, if the current date is Feb 14, “Fiscal - 

Current quarter” would include Feb 1 through Apr 30. 

• 
Fiscal - Current quarter to date: The current quarter up to the current date only. For 

example, if the current date is Feb 22, “Fiscal - Current Quarter to Date” would include Feb 1 

through Feb 22. 

• 
Fiscal - Prior quarter: The prior quarter in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Dec 

11, “Fiscal - Prior quarter” would include Aug 1 through Oct 31. 

• 
Fiscal - Prior quarter to date: The prior quarter, to the current month/date, but of the prior 

quarter. For example, if the current date is Jul 11, “Fiscal - Prior Quarter to Date” would 

include Feb 1 through Apr 11. 

• 
Fiscal - One year ago quarter: The current quarter based on the current date, but in the 

previous year, in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Jul 6, 2018, “Fiscal - One Year 

Ago Quarter” would include May 1, 2017, through Jul 31, 2017. 

• 
Fiscal - Next year: The next year, beginning on the 1st day of the fiscal year and ending on 

the last day of the fiscal year. For example, if the current date is Aug 14, 2017, “Fiscal - Next 

Year” would include Feb 1, 2018, through Jan 31, 2019. 

• 
Fiscal - Current year: The current fiscal year in its entirety, even though the year isn’t over 

yet. For example, if the current date is Aug 11, “Fiscal - Current Year” would include Feb 1 

through Jan 31. 

• 
Fiscal - Current year to date: The current fiscal year only to the current date. For example, if 

the current date is May 22, “Fiscal - Current Year to Date” would include Feb 1 through May 

22. 

---


<!-- Page 452 -->
Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Fiscal - Prior year: The prior fiscal year in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Dec 

11, 2018, “Fiscal - Prior year” would include Feb 1, 2016, through Jan 31, 2017. 

• 
Fiscal - Prior year to date: The prior fiscal year, to the current month/date, but of the prior 

year. For example, if the current date is Jul 11, 2018, “Fiscal - Prior Year to Date” would 

include Feb 1, 2016, through Jul 11, 2017. 

• 
Fiscal - Prior year current quarter: The current fiscal quarter based on the current date, but 

in the previous year, in its entirety. For example. if the current date is Oct 6, 2018, “Fiscal - 

Prior Year Current Quarter” would include Aug 1, 2017, through Oct 31, 2017. 

• 
Fiscal - Prior year prior quarter: The previous fiscal quarter based on the current date, but 

in the previous year, in its entirety. For example, if the current date is Oct 6, 2018, “Fiscal - 

Prior Year Prior Quarter” would include May 1, 2017, through Jul 31, 2017. 

• 
Fiscal - Prior year next quarter: The next fiscal quarter based on the current date, but in the 

previous year, in its entirety. For example, if the current date is May 6, 2018, “Fiscal - Prior 

Year Next Quarter” would include Aug 1, 2017, through Oct 31, 2017. 

• 
Fiscal - Current year through current month: The current fiscal year only to through the last 

day of the current month. For example, if the current date is May 6, “Fiscal - Current Year 

through Current Month” would include Jan 1 through May 31. 

• 
Fiscal - Current year through prior month: The current fiscal year only to through the last 

day of the previous month. For example, if the current date is May 6, “Fiscal - Current Year 

through Prior Month” would include Feb 1 through May 31.

Importing Report Types 

You can use the Import option to add multiple report types in bulk. 

Export and Fill Out the Report Type Template 

To export and fill out the report type template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select Import Data. 

The Import data page opens. 

2. 
In the Setup General Ledger Transactions section, click the Template link in the Report Types 

row. 

The system downloads the template to your local drive. 

3. 
Open the template using a spreadsheet application and then enter the required information. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Import the Report Type File 

To import the report type file: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the More section of the menu, click Report Types. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Import box appears. The box’s title and on-screen instructions 

above the Choose file button reflect the type of data that you are importing. 

4. 
Select the file that you want to import and click the Open button. 

The file you import must be in CSV format. 

5. 
If your data contains dates, then in the Date format field, select the date format used by the 

data that you are importing. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding field set to the default status auto detect. 

7. 
Select the Process offline check box to have the system import the data with the least 

impact to system processing speed.

#### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 460*

Tasks in Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 461) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized—that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead.

#### Storing Standard Reports and Charts
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 463*



##### Viewing a Stored Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 463*

Chapter 3: Tasks in Reports

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

You can process and store the report or chart either before or after viewing it. 

Viewing a Stored Report 

After the system runs the report on the date that you selected, you can find the report in either 

the My stored reports list or the Reports center (on page 14). 

To view a stored report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Open the application where you created the report. 

2. 
Select the My stored reports option located in the Reports column of the menu. 

The My stored reports list opens with a list of reports stored in the application. 

3. 
Find the report that you want to view and then verify the report date in the Run date/time 

column. Verifying the report date helps you avoid missing data. For example, if you 

scheduled the report to run two weeks ago, you would be missing the last two weeks of 

data. 

4. 
Click one of the following links to open your report in the format it was stored:  

• 
HTML: Opens the report in a new browser tab as a web page. 

• 
PDF: Opens a printable PDF version of the report that you can print and download. 

• 
CSV: Downloads a CSV file containing the report data. This is a good format to 

download if you want to import the data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Downloads the report as an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Opens a text version of the report in the web browser. 

• 
View Status: Opens the report in your configured cloud account. If there is no cloud 

link for the report, see Storing a Report in a Cloud Storage Location (on page 468). 

• 
Success: Opens the report in Reporting Portal. If there was an error processing the 

report, then the View status link appears in the column instead. See Viewing a Report 

Error Log for error details. 

If you have not yet processed the report offline, then click the Create offline link to 
process the report.

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or 

Amazon S3. If you are a developer, you can also deliver the report to another application using 

HTTP. 

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets in RealPage Accounting. The targets that you 

define will be available as storage options for reports. 

To store a report in a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime (on page 195). 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand (on page 414). 

3. 
Select the Store in cloud check box. 

4. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the 

report.  

By default, you can choose from cloud-storage targets that either you’ve defined or that 
others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, you can see all cloud 
targets. 

5. 
If you want to override the default path where the report is delivered in the cloud-storage 

target, then type a different path in the Path field. 

6. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report.

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.

## Glossary of Terms
*Source: `RP Accounting Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 477*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

A/P batch 

A group of A/P transactions—such as invoices or 

credits—entered and posted together. 

A/P configuration 

The collection of settings that define how A/P 

functions behave, including approval rules, 

numbering formats, tolerances, and posting 

options. 

A/P workflow 

The routing and approval structure that 

determines how invoices move through review 

and approval before posting. 

A/R Batch 

A group of A/R transactions—such as charges, 

receipts, or adjustments—entered and posted 

together. 

Account balance 

The total amount recorded in a G/L account for a 

given period, including beginning balance, 

activity, and ending balance. 

Account grouping 

A structure used in financial reports to organize 

G/L accounts into meaningful categories such as 

assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses. 

Predefined or custom groupings of G/L accounts 

used for reporting, dashboards, and financial 

analysis. 

Account type 

A classification that determines how an account 

behaves in financial statements (Asset, Liability, 

Equity, Revenue, Expense). 

Accounting period 

Transactions are recorded and separated into 

different reporting periods such as months, 

quarters, and years. The use of reporting periods 

lets you compare past and present performance. 

Accounting reviewer 

A designated role responsible for reviewing and 

approving accounting-related transactions 

before they are posted. 

Accounts 

An account keeps track of what your company 

owns, owes, spends, or receives. Separate 

accounts let you keep separate records for each 

type of asset, liability, equity, revenue, and 

expense. 

Each account can contain several subaccounts, 

which helps organize and manage your finances. 

Each account tracks the activity of its category. 

For example, the Receivables account tracks 

money coming in and the Payables account 

tracks money going out. Each of these accounts 

typically has many subaccounts. For example, the 

Receivables account may have a subaccount for 

each property: 

1201.001 - Accounts Receivable - Fair Haven 

1201.002 - Accounts Receivable - Coconut Grove 

Glossary of Terms

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Each account has a beginning balance. You 

record the increases and decreases for a period, 

and at the end of the period, you have the 

resulting ending balance. 

Accrual accounting 

The accrual method of accounting recognizes 

income in the period earned, and expenses in 

the period incurred. The accrual method is a 

better measure of profit and loss. 

Accrued Expenses report 

A report showing expenses that have been 

incurred but not yet paid, used during close to 

validate balances. 

Accumulated depreciation account 

The G/L account credited when depreciation is 

posted. It offsets the asset’s cost on the balance 

sheet. 

Action card 

A dashboard component that provides quick 

access buttons for common tasks or navigation 

shortcuts. 

Actuals 

Financial results of activity in the general ledger 

and used as the baseline for forecasts and 

budgets. 

Adjustment 

A manual increase or decrease to a customer’s or 

vendor’s balance, used to correct errors or apply 

special credits/charges. 

Adjustment codes 

Predefined codes used to categorize manual 

increases or decreases to a customer’s balance. 

Aging buckets 

Time based categories (e.g., 0–30, 31–60 days) 

used to group outstanding receivables or 

payables for reporting. 

Aging report 

A report that groups outstanding balances (A/P 

or A/R) by how long they have been unpaid (e.g., 

0–30, 31–60 days). 

Allocation 

A process that distributes amounts from one 

account or entity to others based on predefined 

rules or percentages. 

Allocation (Expense Reports) 

A method of distributing an expense across 

multiple projects, tasks, or locations. 

Approval levels 

The hierarchy of users or roles authorized to 

approve invoices based on amount, vendor, or 

other criteria.  

The number of approvers required for a role 

(1–4) when that role is assigned to an approval 

policy. 

Approval policy 

A rule that determines which users or roles are 

authorized to approve a transaction based on 

criteria such as amount, vendor, G/L account, 

job, or payment method.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Approval policy manager 

The page in the Company application used to 

create, edit, and organize approval policies. 

Approval queue 

The list of transactions awaiting approval, 

displayed in the Approval Workbench. 

Approval workbench 

An approval workbench is where users review, 

approve, and decline pending transactions. 

Approval workflow 

The routing process that determines who must 

review and approve a transaction before it can 

be posted or paid. A collection of approval 

policies are applied to specific transaction types 

and properties. 

Approver 

An approver is a person responsible for deciding 

to approve or decline a transaction. There are 

three types of approvers: 

• 
General approvers can approve or decline 

only transactions assigned to them or their 

role. 

• 
Unrestricted approvers can approve or 

decline any transaction. 

• 
Delegate approvers can approve or decline 

transactions assigned to another approver. 

Approver permissions 

The system permissions required to create 

approval policies or approve transactions. 

Asset account 

The G/L account representing the asset’s cost. 

Used when posting depreciation and disposal 

entries. 

Asset Activity report 

A report showing additions, disposals, transfers, 

and depreciation activity for selected assets. 

Asset class 

A category of assets that share the same 

depreciation rules and G/L account structure. 

Determines how depreciation is calculated and 

posted. 

Asset Disposal report 

A report showing assets that have been disposed 

of, including gain/loss calculations. 

Asset List report 

A report showing basic asset details such as cost, 

location, class, and placed in service date. 

Asset Reconciliation report 

A report comparing fixed asset balances to G/L 

balances to identify discrepancies. 

Assets 

The tangible and intangible items used in the 

operation of a business. Tangible assets include 

buildings, equipment, and vehicles. Intangible 

assets include the company’s bank account 

balance and A/R invoices representing future 

income from customers. Assets are tracked 

through acquisition, depreciation, transfer, and 

disposal.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Assumptions 

User defined variables—such as inflation rates, 

occupancy targets, or expense growth—that 

drive forecast calculations. 

Attachments 

An attachment is a bundle of one or more 

supporting documents, such as spreadsheets, 

scanned images, or word processor documents. 

Audit trail 

A system record showing changes made to 

transactions or records, including who made the 

change and when. 

Bank account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on the bank account used. 

Bank accounts 

Financial accounts set up in the system for 

issuing payments, recording deposits, 

withdrawals, and performing reconciliations. 

Bank feed 

An automated connection that imports bank 

transactions into reconciliation for matching and 

reconciliation. 

Bank reconciliation 

The process of matching bank activity to general 

ledger transactions to ensure the bank balance 

and book balance agree. 

Bank register 

A chronological list of all transactions recorded 

in a bank account within the system. 

Baseline forecast 

The initial forecast generated from actuals and 

default assumptions before adjustments or 

scenario modeling. 

Batch 

A group of journal entries entered and posted 

together as a single unit. 

Batch report 

A report that displays all transactions included in 

a specific batch, such as A/P invoices or journal 

entries. 

Beginning balance 

The starting balance of a G/L account at the 

beginning of a fiscal period. 

Billable time 

Hours worked on a project that can be invoiced 

to a customer. The Billable Time page allows 

users to generate invoices for approved billable 

hours. 

Book balance 

The balance of a bank account according to the 

general ledger. It can also be the balance from 

the general ledger of a default general ledger 

account set on the bank account. 

Bookmarks / favorites 

User-defined shortcuts to frequently accessed 

pages or modules. 

Books closed 

The state indicating that the accounting period 

has been finalized for a property. 

---

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Budget 

A financial plan for a future period that outlines 

expected revenue, expenses, and cash flow. In 

Job Cost, a budget is an estimate of expected 

costs for a job. 

Budget version 

A saved iteration of a budget or forecast, 

allowing comparison between drafts, scenarios, 

or approval stages. 

BVA 

Budget Variance Analysis is an analysis of the 

difference between the amount that you 

budgeted for and the actual amount that you 

spent. 

Calculation model 

The logic used to compute forecasted values, 

such as percentage growth, fixed amounts, or 

driver based formulas. 

Cash accounting 

The cash method of accounting recognizes 

revenue in the same reporting period as the cash 

is received, and expenses in the period in which 

cash payments are made. 

Cash flow forecast 

A projection of expected cash inflows and 

outflows over a defined period. 

Certification / skill 

A credential, license, or skill tracked for an 

employee. Users can add, edit, or delete 

certifications and skills in their profile. 

Charge 

A receivable posted to a customer or tenant 

account for rent, fees, utilities, or other billable 

items. 

Charge schedule 

A configuration that defines when recurring 

charges generate, such as monthly rent cycles. 

Chart of accounts (COA) 

The structured list of G/L accounts used to 

categorize financial transactions. 

Check layout 

The format and design used when printing 

checks, including alignment, fields, and MICR line 

settings. 

Check run 

A batch process that selects, reviews, and prints 

multiple vendor payments at once. 

Child location 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, properties are 

called locations. Subproperties are called child 

locations. 

An entity represents the corporate office of one 

or more locations, responsible for locations’ 

taxes. Every location is associated with an entity. 

An entity can be responsible for one location or 

a large group of locations and child locations.  

A company can be composed of one entity or 

multiple entities. See also Multi-entity companies 

(on page 489). 

---

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Cleared transaction 

A payment or deposit that has been matched to 

bank activity during reconciliation. 

Cloned dashboard 

A duplicate of an existing dashboard that can be 

edited independently. 

Close account 

A close account is a G/L account used to track 

job completion. 

Close checklist 

A list of tasks required to complete the financial 

close for a period. Can be generated 

automatically or manually. 

Close console 

A centralized page for managing close activities, 

including generating checklists, opening/closing 

books, and viewing charts. 

Close workbench 

A workspace that displays close tasks, checklists, 

and work paper actions for selected properties. 

Closing period 

The process of finalizing a fiscal period so no 

additional transactions can be posted. 

Coding 

Assigning G/L accounts, properties, entities, and 

other classifications to an invoice or credit. 

Commitment 

A commitment, or purchase order, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount. 

Component 

An individual element displayed on a dashboard, 

such as a chart, list, report, performance card, 

calendar, or smartlink. 

Component controls 

The actions available on each dashboard 

component, such as edit, delete, expand, 

collapse, or move. 

Component group 

A collection of dashboard components grouped 

together for organization or layout purposes. 

Component permissions 

Permissions required to view the underlying data 

of a dashboard component. Users must have 

access to the data source (e.g., A/P invoices, G/L 

accounts) to see the component. 

Concession 

A concession is a negative charge awarded to 

the customer as a short-term incentive. Examples 

of concessions include waived fees, reduced rent, 

nuisance discounts, and renovation credits.  

Console page 

A dashboard style page showing close status, 

charts, and tools for generating checklists and 

managing books.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Consolidation 

Combining financial data from multiple entities 

into a single set of financial statements. 

Contra accounts 

A contra account is an account which offsets and 

reduces or offsets the balance of another 

account. You can have contra accounts for both 

assets and liabilities. 

A contra asset account has a credit balance and 

offsets and decreases the debit balance of the 

related asset account. An example of a 

contra-asset account is Accumulated 

Depreciation Autos & Vehicles account, which 

reduces the Automobiles & Vehicles account to 

arrive at the net value. 

A contra-liability account has a debit balance 

and offsets and decreases the credit balance of 

the related liability account. 

Cost code 

A cost code is a way to track a specific cost 

based on nature or function. 

Cost code policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific cost code. 

Cost coding 

Cost coding is a method of grouping individual 

costs based on their nature, function, or work 

phase. 

Credit memo 

A credit memo increases the overall amount you 

owe a vendor. It is typically a vendor-issued 

document that reduces the amount owed on an 

invoice. 

Custom field 

A user-defined field added to records or 

transactions to capture additional data not 

included in standard RealPage fields. 

Custom field wizard 

The guided tool used to create new custom 

fields, define field types, and configure visibility. 

Custom report 

A user built report that pulls data from Financial 

Suite records, transactions, and custom fields, 

allowing flexible filtering, grouping, and 

calculations. 

Custom report wizard 

A step-by-step tool for building custom reports, 

including selecting data sources, defining 

columns, adding filters, grouping, and setting 

prompts. 

Custom view 

A personalized list view that displays selected 

columns, filters, and sorting for any application’s 

list pages. 

Customer / tenant ledger 

A detailed record of all charges, payments, 

adjustments, and balances for a specific 

customer or tenant. 

Dashboard 

A workspace where users can pin frequently 

used reports for quick access, and display

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

business insights using components such as 

charts, KPIs, lists, and reports. 

Dashboard library 

A collection of prebuilt dashboards available for 

installation, typically provided when a company 

is created using a QuickStart template. 

Data import wizard 

A tool used to import data such as vendors, 

customers, G/L accounts, or transactions into the 

Financial Suite. 

Data mapping 

The process of aligning fields in your import file 

with the corresponding fields in the Financial 

Suite so the system knows where each value 

belongs. 

Data source (primary data source) 

The record or transaction type selected as the 

foundation for a report (e.g., Customer, A/P 

Invoice Detail, G/L entry). 

Data template 

A predefined spreadsheet or CSV layout 

provided by RealPage that specifies the required 

columns and formatting for a successful import. 

Debit memo 

A debit memo decreases the overall amount you 

owe that vendor. 

For example, if you receive a credit memo from a 

vendor, enter it as a debit memo to reduce the 

amount you owe that vendor. 

Debits and credits 

In common use, credit generally has positive 

associations; in accounting, credit is associated 

with decreases in asset, expense, and equity 

accounts. 

Debits increase balances in asset and expense 

accounts and decrease balances in liability 

accounts, revenue accounts, and capital 

accounts. 

Credits increase balances in liability, revenue, 

and capital accounts, and decrease balances in 

asset and expense accounts. 

Debit accounts are asset and expense accounts 

that usually have debit balances; the total debits 

usually exceed the total credits in each debit 

account. 

Credit accounts are revenue (income, gains) 

accounts and liability accounts that usually have 

credit balances. 

Declining balance (100/150/200) 

A depreciation method that accelerates 

depreciation by applying a percentage to the 

asset’s remaining book value. 

Default dashboard 

The dashboard automatically displayed when a 

user logs in. 

Default settings 

Predefined values that automatically populate 

fields when creating records, such as default G/L 

accounts or payment terms (A/P), or default 

charge codes or payment application rules (A/R).

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Delegate 

The approver who assumes your responsibility 

for approving transactions while you are out of 

the office. Any approvals that have been 

delegated while you are out of the office remain 

with your delegate, even if you turn off the 

out-of-office notification before the delegate has 

approved or declined the transaction. 

Deposit 

Funds received and recorded in a bank account, 

often grouped into a deposit batch for posting. 

Deposit batch 

A group of deposits entered and posted 

together. 

Depreciation batch 

A batch of depreciation journal entries generated 

for a period. Can be posted, viewed, or deleted. 

Depreciation expense account 

The G/L account debited when depreciation is 

posted. 

Depreciation journal entry 

The G/L entry created when depreciation is 

posted, debiting expense and crediting 

accumulated depreciation. 

Depreciation schedule 

The system generated schedule showing 

depreciation amounts for each period over the 

asset’s useful life. 

Depreciation schedules (financial vs. 
tax) 

Separate schedules that allow different 

depreciation rules for GAAP and tax reporting. 

Detail data source 

A data source option that includes both header 

and line item information for transactions (e.g., 

A/P Invoice Detail). 

Detail ledger 

A record showing all transactions posted to a 

specific G/L account. 

Detail report 

A report that includes line item or transaction 

level information rather than summarized totals. 

Dimension report structures 

Dimension report structures are named 

structures that you can create for the purpose of 

adding custom analysis to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. You can add dimension 

structures for any dimension that you have in 

your company. 

Disbursement 

Any outgoing cash transaction, such as checks, 

ACH payments, or manual payments. 

Document template 

A customizable Word-based template used for 

printed documents such as invoices, statements, 

sales orders, and purchase orders.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Document type 

The category of document associated with a 

report, such as invoices, statements, or purchase 

orders. 

Draft asset 

An asset imported from an external system that 

has not yet been activated. 

Draft expense report 

An expense report that has been created but not 

yet submitted for approval. 

Draw 

In Job Cost & Reserves, a draw summarizes 

invoiced costs by combining job activity into 

predetermined categories. After it’s summarized, 

you can provide the draw to the funding sources 

of the job. 

Draw model 

A draw model is an agreement between a lender 

and your company that lists the budgeted items 

approved for funds. 

Driver 

A variable that influences forecasted values (e.g., 

occupancy, rent growth, utility usage). 

Due date 

The date by which a vendor invoice must be 

paid. 

eInvoice 

A system-generated A/P invoice created by 

Spend Management Storefront. 

Entity 

An entity record contains a property’s or 

location’s accounting and legal details, such as 

the business name and address as they should 

appear on A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and tax 

forms. An entity contains the accounting 

information of a location/property or property 

management company. 

In a multi-entity environment, entities are 

distinct—but nearly identical—companies or 

business units that are fully owned by a 

corporate or headquarters entity. Entities can 

represent divisions managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized 

payables and receivables and a common chart of 

accounts. 

Exception 

A transaction that does not match bank activity 

during reconciliation and requires review or 

correction. 

Expense report 

A form used to record reimbursable expenses. 

Users can add receipts, allocate expenses, and 

submit for approval. 

FAS 

A final account statement (FAS) is a document 

that provides a detailed record of a transaction’s 

activity. 

Filter 

Criteria applied to limit which records appear in 

a report.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Final work paper package 

The completed, approved set of work papers for 

a period, locked after approval. 

Fiscal calendar 

The structure of accounting periods and fiscal 

years used for reporting and posting. 

Forecast 

A forward looking projection of financial 

performance based on actuals, assumptions, and 

drivers. 

Forecast cycle 

The defined period for creating, reviewing, and 

finalizing forecasts (monthly, quarterly, annually). 

Funding source 

A funding source is a lender for a job. 

G/L account (general ledger account) 

A financial account used to categorize 

transactions for reporting and posting. A G/L 

account is associated with each charge or 

payment. 

G/L account group 

A predefined group of G/L accounts that can be 

selected instead of individual account ranges. 

G/L account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific G/L account or 

account range. 

G/L group 

A collection of G/L accounts grouped for 

reporting, allocations, or approval routing. 

Global (top level) setup 

Configuration performed at the top level that 

applies to all entities in the portfolio. 

Home page 

The landing page provides quick access to 

dashboards, tasks, and frequently used modules. 

Import log 

A system-generated record that shows which 

rows were imported successfully and which 

failed, including error messages. 

Initial posting date 

Revaluation reports help you manage 

unrecognized gains and losses from the 

fluctuation in exchange rates. Set the initial 

posting date on this report as the end of the 

month. 

Injection (smart rules / smart events) 

A dynamic value inserted into a rule or event 

action, such as a field value, date, or user 

information. 

Interim financing 

Interim financing, or construction loan, is a 

deployment of capital for short-term 

development, such as the acquisition and 

renovation of properties. This capital is typically 

provided by a lender.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

When the project is complete, owners pay the 

construction loan and replace it with permanent 

financing. 

In-transit item 

A transaction recorded in the system but not yet 

reflected on the bank statement (e.g., 

outstanding checks, deposits in transit). 

Invoice (A/P) 

A vendor’s bill for goods or services received. 

Invoice (A/R) 

A document generated to bill a customer for 

charges owed. In A/R, invoices may be created 

manually or automatically. 

Invoice entry 

The process of entering vendor invoices into the 

A/P module for approval and posting. 

Invoice matching 

The process of comparing an invoice to purchase 

orders, receipts, or expected amounts before 

approval. 

Invoice numbering rules 

Settings that determine how invoice numbers are 

validated, formatted, or restricted. 

Job 

A job is a method of tracking the work and 

expenses related to construction at a property. 

Jobs are used for job costing and approval 

routing. 

Job policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific job. 

Job type 

A classification of jobs used for approval policies 

and reporting. 

Job type policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a job type. 

Journal entry 

A journal entry documents the movement of 

money. When you add a journal entry, you enter 

an accounting transaction into the records. Every 

journal entry must include at least two equal and 

offsetting entries. This is because every 

transaction involves a change in at least two 

places in the accounting records, and the total of 

all debits and credits must balance. 

Key performance indicator (KPI) 

A measurable metric used to evaluate financial 

or operational performance (e.g., NOI, occupancy 

rate). KPIs can be displayed on performance 

cards on a dashboard to show financial or 

operational performance. 

Late fee 

A charge applied when a customer fails to pay by 

the due date, based on configured rules. 

Late fee rules 

Configuration that determines when late fees 

apply, how they are calculated, and which charge 

codes they use.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Ledger 

The complete set of financial accounts used to 

record all transactions for an entity or portfolio. 

Line item 

An individual revenue or expense entry within a 

transaction such as an invoice, purchase order, 

budget or forecast. 

Loan schedule 

A loan schedule is a list of all payments 

previously paid (historical purposes only) or due 

to the lender for the loan. 

Lookup values 

Reference lists—such as vendors, charge codes, 

or account types—that must exist in the system 

before certain imports can succeed. 

Manual entry 

A bank transaction entered directly into the 

system rather than imported through a bank 

feed or processed by AI. 

Manual journal entry 

A journal entry created directly by a user rather 

than generated by a subsystem such as A/P or 

A/R. 

Matching 

The process of pairing bank activity with 

corresponding G/L transactions during 

reconciliation.  

M-console 

The M-console is the management console used 

by administrators to create and manage multiple 

RealPage Accounting Suite environments. 

M-console access is different from RealPage 

Accounting Suite system access. To access the 

M-console, you must have a separate account in 

the M-console. 

Most implementations of RealPage Accounting 

Suite do not need the M-console. 

Memorized report 

A saved version of a report with preset filters, 

parameters, and formatting for quick reuse. 

Merge field 

A placeholder inserted into a Word document 

template that pulls data from the Financial Suite 

when the document is generated. 

Monthly checklist 

A checklist used for monthly close activities. 

Multi year forecast 

A projection that spans multiple fiscal years, 

often used for long term planning. 

Multi-entity companies 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, a parent property 

is called a location, and a subproperty is called a 

child location. A location must have an entity 

associated with it. The entity handles the 

accounting and tax activities for its location and 

any child locations. 

In a multi-entity shared corporation, entities 

represent a separate tax identification or a 

separately secured, fully balancing set of books. 

Entities typically represent properties, or 

locations, which are managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized

Service. 

Operational report

lease information. 

Outstanding check

cleared the bank. 

Overpayment

invoice in full, but the payment is more than the

Payment 

Money received from a customer and applied to

Payment batch

Payment method policy

Payment methods

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Performance card 

A dashboard component that displays KPIs, 

trends, or financial metrics in a compact visual 

format. 

Period activity 

The total debits and credits posted to an account 

within a specific accounting period. 

Period close 

The workflow used to review, adjust, and finalize 

financial activity before closing an accounting 

period. 

Periodic tasks 

Recurring A/P activities performed on a regular 

schedule, such as check runs, recurring invoice 

generation, or reconciliation. 

Permission 

The rights required to view and work with data 

and access pages. 

A permission allows you to access a single 

function. When RealPage adds a new feature to a 

product, the feature often comes with new 

permissions that you must enable before users 

can use the new feature. The word “Right” and 

the word “Permission” refer to the same thing. 

When you use the Unified Platform, they are 

referred to as rights. When you set up access to 

functions in the Financial Suite, they are referred 

to as permissions.  

Permit 

A permit is a category that organizes job 

attachments by type or function. 

Placed in service date 

The date the asset begins being used. 

Depreciation starts based on this date. 

PO 

An abbreviation for purchase order (on page 

492). 

Policy type 

The category of rule used to determine approval 

routing (User, Amount, Tiered Amount, Vendor, 

Vendor Type, G/L Account, Job, Job Type, Cost 

Code, Accounting Reviewer, Journal Type, 

Payment Method, Bank Account). 

Positive Pay 

Positive pay is an automated service that the 

bank offers to help detect fraud by matching a 

company’s check with the check presented for 

payment.  

You can use the RealPage Financial Suite Positive 

Pay feature to generate a Positive Pay file and 

transmit the list of checks to the bank for review. 

The bank compares the amount, check number, 

and account number to ensure that they match. 

Non-matching checks are flagged and sent back 

to the check issuer for review. 

You can also configure the system to submit 

Positive Pay files on a schedule. When a schedule 

is configured, the system generates the Positive 

Pay files containing a list of checks on the 

scheduled dates and automatically sends them 

to the bank. 

Posting 

The action that finalizes a transaction and 

records it in the general ledger.

When you post a transaction, you are 

transferring the balance of the transaction from 

its journal to the General Ledger. 

Posting date 

The date assigned to a journal entry that 

determines the accounting period in which it 

appears. 

Posting rules 

Settings that determine how transactions are 

posted to the general ledger, including batch 

behavior and posting dates. 

Pre validation 

A system check that reviews your file for 

formatting or data issues before the actual 

import runs. 

Preliminary work paper package 

The initial version of work papers generated 

before variances are resolved. 

Prepayment 

A payment reflecting an invoice that is not yet 

billed. The customer’s account balance is zero. 

Project 

A work assignment used to categorize time 

entries and expenses. Projects must be created 

before they can be used in timesheets. 

Project type 

A classification used to group projects for 

reporting and setup. 

Prompts 

User input fields added to a custom report to 

allow filtering at runtime. 

Properties (entities) 

Individual business units or properties whose 

financial activity is tracked separately. 

PTO (paid time off) 

Time away from work that can be requested and 

approved through the Time & Resources 

application. 

PTO approvals 

The list where approvers review and approve or 

decline PTO requests. 

PTO request 

A request submitted by an employee for paid 

time off. 

PTO types 

Administrator-defined categories of PTO, such as 

vacation, sick leave, or personal time. 

Punchout vendor 

Punchout refers to a digital system in which a 

vendor allows customers to browse his product 

catalogs online and then purchase goods or 

services within the client’s e-procurement 

system. 

Purchase order 

A purchase order, or commitment, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount.

QuickStart template

dashboards, account groups, and structural 

configuration during company creation.

Financial Suite, “receipt” and “payment” are often 

used interchangeably. 

Reclassification (asset) 

Changing the G/L account or asset class 

associated with an asset. 

Reconciliation date 

The date through which the bank account is 

being reconciled. 

Reconciliation workbench 

The tool used to match bank activity with G/L 

transactions and complete bank reconciliations.

transactions during the reconciliation process. 

Record

Recurring charge (property

Recurring invoice (accounting)

new invoices on a set schedule. 

Recurring journal entry 

A journal entry template that automatically 

generates entries on a defined schedule. 

Refresh 

The action that reloads a page’s data to reflect 

the most recent system updates. 

REIT 

Real Estate Investment Trust

Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit 

Report audience 

A report audience is an audience assigned to a

filter the list of reports by audience type later. 

Report center 

The central hub where users browse, run, create,

Report column

amounts, or statuses.

Columns that must be present and populated in

Revaluate 

An adjustment to a country’s official exchange 

rate relative to the base amount. 

Revenue account 

The G/L account associated with a charge code, 

used to classify revenue in financial reporting. 

Reversal 

A journal entry created to negate a previous 

entry, often used for accruals. 

Rights 

A right allows you to access a single function. 

When RealPage adds a new feature to a product, 

the feature often comes with new rights that you 

must enable before users can use the new 

feature. The word “Right” and the word 

“Permission” refer to the same thing. When you 

use the Unified Platform, they are referred to as 

rights. When you set up access to functions in 

the Financial Suite, they are referred to as 

permissions.  

Role 

A group of users who share permissions and 

responsibilities; roles can be assigned as 

approvers. Roles are assigned to users to control 

access to modules and actions. 

RPA 

An abbreviation for RealPage Accounting. 

Segments 

A component used to categorize financial data 

(e.g., entity, department, account). 

You can use segments to organize, sort, and 

report on your company information in 

meaningful ways. It is a type of tag with a set of 

values, which you can associate with transactions 

and G/L entries. 

Sequences 

Document sequences refer to the system’s 

automatic document numbering feature used to 

assign unique identifiers to new records. This 

helps ensure consistency and avoids duplication. 

Automatic numbering, also known as document 

sequencing, is available only for select 

transactions and records in RealPage 

Accounting. Document sequencing uses 

pre-defined numbering plans to assign 

sequential identifiers to new records or 

transactions, such as customer records or A/R 

invoices. Document sequencing is a two-step 

process. First, you configure the numbering 

scheme, then you assign the scheme to the type 

of record or transaction.  

Service charge 

A bank fee recorded during reconciliation to 

adjust the book balance.

panes. Click it to display the menu items 

available to you based on your subscriptions, 

user permissions, and admin privileges. If the

Site Experience 

The Site Experience is a scaled-down version of 

Spend Management in a simplified interface. 

While the Spend Management application in the 

RealPage Financial Suite offers more robust 

functionality, most users can accomplish their 

procurement-to-payment processes from the 

Site Experience. 

The Site View option opens Site Experience. The 

Site View menu option is available in the Spend 

Management, General Ledger, and Accounts 

Payable application menus. 

Smart event

sending an email, making an API call, or posting 

an HTTP request—when conditions are met. 

Smart rule

user behavior when certain conditions are met. 

Smartlink 

A dashboard component that provides a 

clickable link to another page, report, or 

application. 

Source entity 

The paying entity. The entity that is the source of 

the money in a transaction between two or more 

entities. 

Splits 

A line within a transaction that records the 

account and amount of money involved is called 

a split. 

Spread method (budgeting) 

The rule used to distribute annual amounts 

across months (e.g., evenly, seasonally, 

driver-based). 

Staff expenses 

Expense reports created on behalf of staff 

members by administrators or managers. 

Staff timesheets 

Timesheets created or managed by supervisors 

for their staff. 

Standard report 

A pre-built Financial Suite report that cannot be 

modified but can be exported or memorized. 

Statement 

A statement, or Statement of Account, is 

essentially a report. It’s a snapshot that includes 

all open and unapplied transactions at the time 

the snapshot was taken—usually at the end of a 

period. 

Statement balance 

The ending balance shown on the bank 

statement for the reconciliation period. 

Straight line depreciation 

A depreciation method that spreads the asset’s 

cost evenly over its useful life.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Subledger 

A subledger is a ledger containing all of one kind 

of transaction. For example, a subledger may 

contain all accounts receivable transactions, or 

accounts payable transactions, or fixed asset 

transactions. All transactions in all subledgers roll 

up into the general ledger. 

Submitted (timesheet status) 

Indicates that a timesheet has been submitted 

and is awaiting approval. 

Sum of years digits (SYD) 

An accelerated depreciation method that applies 

a decreasing fraction of the asset’s cost each 

year. 

Summary 

Summaries are collections of the same type of 

transactions, grouped together for processing. 

Until you or the system creates a new summary, 

no line items appear in the Summaries list. 

Summaries can be either open or closed. When 

summaries are open in Accounts Receivable, you 

can add invoices, adjustments, and deposits. In 

designing an accounts receivable process, the 

system administrator can give access to the 

pages involved with managing invoices but not 

opening or closing summaries. 

Summary report 

A high level report that aggregates data without 

showing line item detail. 

Suspense account 

A temporary account used to hold transactions 

that require review or correction. 

System journal 

A system journal is a journal that is used by the 

system. Users can designate a journal as a 

system journal. Users cannot add journal entries 

to system journals, and system journals are 

excluded from appearing in manual journals 

drop-down lists. 

Target (budgeting) 

A predefined financial goal used to guide 

budgeting or forecasting (e.g., NOI target, 

expense cap). 

Task (Financial Close Management) 

An individual close activity, such as reconciling a 

subledger or reviewing a report. 

Task (Time & Resources application) 

A specific activity within a project. Tasks must be 

created before they can be selected on 

timesheets. 

Template version (importing) 

The specific RealPage-approved layout for an 

import file. Using an outdated version can cause 

errors. 

Tenant / customer 

The individual or organization responsible for 

paying charges recorded in A/R. 

Three-way tie 

A reconciliation requirement ensuring that the 

bank balance, book balance, and cleared balance 

all match.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Tiered amount policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions 

through multiple approval tiers based on 

increasing amount ranges. 

TIH 

Trust Interest Holder 

Time approvals 

The list where approvers review and approve or 

decline submitted timesheets. 

Timesheet 

A weekly record of hours worked on projects and 

tasks. Users can add comments, submit for 

approval, and track status. 

Timesheet periods 

Defined weekly or biweekly periods used for 

time entry. Administrators open and close 

periods as needed. 

Tolerance percentage 

The allowable variance between an invoice and 

the expected amount before manual approval is 

required. 

Transaction date 

The date the A/R activity occurred, which 

determines how it appears in aging and 

reporting. 

Transaction detail 

Line-level information associated with a 

transaction, such as invoice items or journal 

entry lines. 

Transaction type 

The category of transaction, such as invoices, 

journal entries, or payments. 

Transactions 

A transaction represents money flowing from 

one account to another. Whenever you spend or 

receive money, or transfer money from one 

account to another, it is represented as a 

transaction. 

In double-entry accounting, transactions always 

involve at least two accounts—a source account 

and a destination account. 

Transfer 

A movement of funds between two bank 

accounts within the system. 

Transfer (asset transfer) 

Moving an asset from one location, entity, or 

department to another. 

Trial balance 

A report showing all G/L accounts with 

beginning balances, period activity, and ending 

balances. 

Unapplied payment 

A payment that has been received but not yet 

applied to specific charges. 

Unapplied payment handling 

Rules that determine how payments are stored 

when they cannot be matched to specific 

charges.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Unapproving (Expense report) 

The action of reversing an approval so the report 

can be edited. 

Unapproving (Expense report) 

The action of reversing an approval so the report 

can be edited. 

Uncleared transaction 

A transaction recorded in the system that has 

not yet been matched to bank activity. 

Unit 

A unit is a rentable space on a property. 

Unposted batch 

A batch of journal entries that has been created 

but not yet posted to the general ledger. 

Unrestricted user 

A user who can do a task, such as approve work 

papers on behalf of others, regardless of 

property restrictions. 

An unrestricted user can see all transactions that 

are waiting to be approved. Unrestricted users 

can act on these transactions even when the 

approvals are not assigned to them. 

Useful life (periods) 

The number of periods over which the asset will 

depreciate. 

User 

An individual system account assigned roles, 

permissions, and approval responsibilities. 

Variance (Financial Close 
Management) 

A difference between expected and actual 

balances in work papers, requiring review and 

resolution. 

Variance (Forecasting and Budgeting) 

The difference between actual results and 

budgeted or forecasted values. 

Vendor 

A supplier of goods or services who receives 

payment through the A/P process. 

Vendor categories / vendor types 

Classifications used to group vendors for 

reporting, workflow, or payment processing. 

Vendor defaults 

Preset values applied automatically when 

creating invoices for a vendor, such as G/L 

accounts or payment terms. 

Vendor import 

A file upload that creates or updates vendor 

records, including addresses, payment terms, 

and tax information. 

Vendor policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific vendor or vendor 

range. 

Vendor type 

A classification of vendors used for approval 

routing or reporting.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Vendor type policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on the vendor’s classification. 

Version control (budgeting) 

The system of tracking changes across multiple 

budget or forecast versions. 

Views (manage views) 

Saved list configurations that define which 

columns appear and how data is sorted or 

filtered. 

WHFIT 

Widely Held Fixed Investment Trust 

WIP account 

A WIP account, or work in process account, is a 

G/L account used to track jobs that are in active 

development. 

Work breakdown structure (WBS) 

A work breakdown structure (WBS) is a system 

that organizes a large project into manageable 

sections. In Job Cost, a job, or project, is 

separated into cost codes that help organize the 

job and track progress. 

Work in process account 

A work in process account, or WIP account, is a 

G/L account used to track jobs that are in active 

development. 

Work paper 

A work paper is an accounting document that 

reconciles all subaccounts of an accounting 

category for auditing purposes. Work papers can 

also be used for preparing financial statements. 

Work paper package 

A compiled set of work papers, attachments, and 

supporting documents for a period.

## Introduction to Reporting Portal
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 9*

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Introduction to Reporting Portal 

The Reporting Portal application allows you to share documents with owners and investors through owner portals. 

You can create owners and publish financial reports or other documents to their portal for easy accessibility. 

The system creates default folders based on the reporting periods set up in General Ledger; however, you can 

create custom folders to upload documents to on the Configuration page (on page 246) for the Reporting Portal 

application. After you upload documents to a folder, the owner or investor will receive a notification that their 

documents are ready for review.

Owner List

Use the Owner list to define the owners and investors for whom you are uploading financial 

reports and other documents. From this list, you can add, edit, view, delete, and export owners. 

New owners will automatically appear on the Owner portals list (on page 34). 
Owners and investors who are receiving documents do not need to be set up as a RealPage user.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Adding an Owner 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > 
 Owner`


You can group multiple contacts in the same owner record. All contacts will access the same 

owner portal. For example, you might create an owner for “Jones Investments” or “Jones Family 

Trust” and then add all the users within that owner group to the contact list, such as Amy Jones, 

Bob Jones, etc. 

To add an owner record: 

1. 
Type an Owner ID and Owner name to identify the owner(s). 

2. 
Fill in the owner’s address. 

3. 
Select the Entities/locations associated with the owner(s). 

4. 
Leave the Status as “Active”. 

5. 
In the Contact list section, select one or more Contacts to include as part of the owner 

record. 
Only contacts you’ve marked as an owner
(on page 20 ) will show up in the drop
-down list. 
When you add a contact to an owner record, they will receive an email notification with instructions for logging in to their owner portal.

6. 
Click Save. 

Viewing or Editing an Owner 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Owner > View or Edit`


To view or edit an owner: 

1. 
In the Owner list, click the View or Edit link next to an owner. 

The Owner information page opens. 

2. 
View or edit the details as needed, and then click Done or Save.

##### Inactivating an Owner
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*

Search & Find 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Inactivating an Owner 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Owner > Edit`


If you are no longer using an owner portal, we recommend that you set its status to Inactive. 

Inactivating an owner record retains its information and contact list but removes the record from 

the Owner list (and removes the corresponding owner portal from the Owner portals list). As long 

as the owner is inactive, any owners or investors who were added to the contact list in the owner 

record will not be able to log in to their owner portal and receive documents. 

To inactivate an owner: 

1. 
In the Owner list, click the Edit link next to the owner you want to inactivate. 

The Owner information page opens. 

2. 
In the Details section, set the Status field to “Inactive”. 

3. 
Click Save. 

The system hides the owner from the Owner list and removes it from system drop-down 

lists.

#### Contacts List
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 23*

Chapter 1: Search & Find 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Contacts List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts`


The Contacts list displays all available contacts in your company, including the name and address 

of the contact. Contacts are used across your company in multiple ways: 

• 
To send event notifications  

• 
To determine ship-to/bill-to, and pay-to/return-to addresses in purchasing transactions  

• 
To determine tax on transactions 
Contacts aren’t dimensions like vendors or customers. Instead, think of 
your contacts as a common, shared address book that is used across your company by many people for a variety of purposes.

Use the Contacts list to add, edit, view, or delete the contacts in your company. Because contacts 

are flexible and can often be created at the time of need, there are a variety of ways you can add 

a contact. Most notably, contacts are created when new vendor, customer, user, or employee 

records are added to RealPage Accounting. In each case, the Suggested contact name is created 

from specific fields, which may affect the consistency of your company naming conventions. Be 

sure to review the record for the specific fields when you create a new contact. 

Best Practices for Creating Contacts 

Because contacts are used and can be created by various records and applications in RealPage 

Accounting, they can be set up inconsistently, which may be confusing in the future or even cause 

errors. To avoid these problems when setting up your contacts for the first time: 

• 
Use only supported characters. The Suggested contact name acts as a unique and 

permanent contact ID field in RealPage Accounting. The supported values include: 

• 
Alphanumeric characters 

• 
Various punctuation (periods, hyphens, underscores, parentheses) 

RealPage Accounting does not permit double spaces; using double spaces results in invalid 

contacts or contact records not appearing within drop-down menus. Furthermore, using 

other special characters not listed here (such as # or %) may also result in an invalid contact. 

• 
Establish a naming convention. The Suggested contact name is used in lists and 

drop-downs to identify your contacts. For this reason, we suggest using a naming 

convention that makes it easy to distinguish contacts in a list. 

For instance, you can use the company name of a vendor or customer, such as Example.com 

for the Suggested contact name. If the contact is an individual, you might choose a 

convention like Last Name, First Name or vice versa to keep your contacts consistent and 

easy to scan in lists and drop-downs. 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*

Search & Find 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

How do users and contacts work together? 

A user ID and a password enable an individual to sign in to the company and access company 

information based on the user type. A contact is an individual who isn’t necessarily a user in the 

company, such as a vendor contact or customer contact. 

A contact can be made a user by adding the contact name to a user profile. For example, you 

could associate:  

• 
An employee contact with a user ID. 

• 
A customer contact with a user ID. 

• 
A vendor contact (for example a subcontractor) with a user ID. 

Associate an Existing Contact With a Customer, Vendor, Employee, or User 

Contact records hold the information you need to contact individuals or businesses. Alone, they 

are no more than a shared address book used for a variety of purposes. However, because one 

contact can be associated with many records, contacts become an easy way to manage contact 

information across many records, such as your customer, employee, vendor, and user records. 

Though you can create a new contact automatically when you create a customer, employee, 

vendor, or user, you may want to associate an existing contact with a record instead. 

Whatever the case, it’s important to note that contacts are associated with the records of 

individuals and businesses you interact with, not the other way around. For instance, if you want 

to associate the existing contact Jim West to the employee Jim West, you would go to the 

employee record to make this connection, not the contact record. 
Changing a contact in an existing record only affects transactions and other data records going forward. It won’t affect your historical data.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.
