##### Adding a Contact
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 25*

Chapter 1: Search & Find 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Adding a Contact 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > 
 Contact`


To create a contact quickly, you only need to assign it a unique Suggested contact name and a 

Print as name for documents. 

The Suggested contact name is the most important field in a contact record. It acts as a unique 

contact ID across the RealPage Financial Suite system, which means you can no longer edit the 

suggested contact name after you create the contact record. Furthermore, although you can 

change the printed name of a contact with the Print as field, the Suggested contact name is the 

name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists across RealPage Accounting. You can change 

the Suggested contact name of a contact (on page 21) in limited situations such as when a 

vendor’s name has changed. 

Additionally, when you create a new vendor, customer, employee, or user, a related contact is 

often created simultaneously based on specific fields in the record. See Creating a Contact from a 

Record (on page 23) to learn about which specific fields in each record create the related 

Suggested contact name. 

To create a more detailed contact record, fill in each tab on the Contact information page. 

Filling In Contact Information 

On the Contact information tab: 

1. 
Type the contact name. 

• 
This name isn’t necessarily the name that is used throughout your company because 

actual names aren’t always unique. For example, a name such as “Jose Hernandez” 

could be the same as a completely different contact in your company. 

• 
The system automatically suggests a unique Suggested contact name and Print as 

name based on the naming details you enter. 

2. 
Add the Primary email address, Primary phone number, and Company name for the 

contact.  
In the Property Managementapplication, the system uses the primary em
ail address that you enter here to fill in email addresses for emailing statements. 

3. 
Type a Suggested contact name if you want a different version than the one the system 

auto-populates. This name appears in lists and drop-down lists. 
After you save the contact, the Suggested contact namecan
’t be edited.

4. 
Enter the Print as name if you want a different version to appear on printed documents than 

the one the system auto-populates.

*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 27*

Chapter 1: Search & Find

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Deleting or Inactivating a Contact 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts`


After you delete a contact, you can no longer restore it. If you are not sure whether to delete a 

contact, you can set its status to Inactive. Inactive contacts are hidden from the Contacts list and 

other system drop-down lists. 

You cannot delete a contact referenced in another area of the company. You must delete or 

remove the reference in those areas before deleting the contact. Common areas that refer to 

contact records include: 

• 
Customers  

• 
Vendors  

• 
Employees 

• 
Dimensions  

• 
Recurring transactions 

• 
Owners (Reporting Portal) or Investors (Investor Portal) 

You can configure the system to warn you when you are about to delete a contact. Click your 

username at the top of any page, select the My preferences option, and then select the Warn on 

delete check box in the On-screen messages section. 

Deleting a Contact 

1. 
In the Contacts list, select the Delete check box for each contact you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the Delete button. 

A confirmation box opens. 

3. 
Click OK to confirm. 

Inactivating a Contact 

1. 
In the Contacts list, click the Edit link next to the contact you want to inactivate. 

2. 
Set the Status of the contact to “Inactive.”  

3. 
Click Save.

##### Changing the Suggested Contact Name
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 30*

Search & Find 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Changing the Suggested Contact Name 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts > Edit`


When you change the name of a vendor, customer, user, or employee, the Suggested contact 

name of the related contact doesn’t automatically update because it is a unique ID used across 

the system by various records. Unfortunately, you can’t change the Suggested contact name of a 

contact record after you create the record for the same reason. Instead, you’ll need to create and 

associate a new contact record with the appropriate record and then inactivate or delete the old 

contact record. 

For example, you create a vendor record and contact record simultaneously so that their names 

match. However, a few months later, you are required to change the name of your vendor and 

now the Suggested contact name of your associated contact record does not match the new 

name of the updated vendor record. First, you create a new contact record with the appropriate 

Suggested contact name, and then you associate that contact with your vendor record. 

Afterward, you can inactivate or delete the old contact record. 

To change the suggested contact name: 

1. 
Go to the record for which you want to change the related contact record, and then click the 

Edit link next to the record. For example, if you changed the name of a customer recently, 

go the Customers list in Accounts Payable, then click the Edit link next to the customer. 

2. 
On the Contact list tab, click Add to add a new contact to the record. 

3. 
Click the Contact drop-down list, and then choose the contact with the correct Suggested 

contact name, or click Add to add a new contact to which you can set the correct 

Suggested contact name. See Adding a Contact (on page 17) or Editing a Contact (on page 

18) for more information on your options. 

4. 
Set a Category for your new contact in the Contacts list. 

5. 
Select your new contact from the Primary contact drop-down list from above. Repeat as 

necessary for other required contact fields in the record. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Go to the Contacts list in Company. 

8. 
Inactivate or delete a contact record (on page 19) that no longer has the correct Suggested 

contact name.  
You can no longer restore a contact record after you delete it. If you are unsure, inactivate the record instead.

---



##### Creating a Contact from a Record
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 31*

Chapter 1: Search & Find 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Creating a Contact from a Record 

You can create new contacts as you create new vendor, customer, employee, or user records. The 

related contact, specifically the Suggested contact name, is created from specific fields 

depending on the kind of record you are creating. 

The Suggested contact nameis a unique ID field that can
’t be edited after creating the contact 
record. Be sure that the related field is correct before saving. See Changing the Suggested Contact Name(on page 21 ) for more details.

Record Type 
Suggested Contact Name 

Vendor or Customer 
When you create a new related contact through a new vendor or 

customer record, the Suggested contact name is saved as Print as + V + 

Vendor ID for vendor records and Print as + C + Customer ID for 

customer records.  

For example, a vendor named Example.com with a vendor ID of 142 

would create a contact with the Suggested contact name of 

Example.com (V142). Similarly, a customer named Frank Smith with a 

customer ID of 1557 would create a contact with Frank Smith (C1557) as 

the Suggested contact name. 

Creating a new vendor or customer always automatically creates a new 

related contact unless you specifically select the Exclude from the 

company contact list check box when you create the record. You may 

want to use this option if you want to keep your contacts consistent with 

your company’s naming convention. 

Employee 
You must choose an existing contact or create a new contact using the 

Primary contact name field when you create a new employee record. 

If the employee is also a RealPage Accounting user, you must select the 

same primary contact name that you used for the employee’s user record. 

User 
When you create a new user, the system automatically creates a new 

contact based on the user ID if you do not select a contact in the Contact 

name field.  

For example, if the user ID of the new user is “jwilliams,” then the system 

assigns “jwilliams” as the related contact, unless you select a contact 

name when creating the user account. 

If the user is also an employee in RealPage Accounting, you must select 

the same contact name that you used in the user’s employee record to 

ensure that permissions work properly.

Uploading Reports and Documents to an Owner’s Portal 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Daily Tasks > Upload Documents`

There are multiple ways to upload financial reports and documents to an owner’s portal: 

•

Scheduling reports (or report groups) and storing them in the Reporting Portal

##### Deleting Folders and Files from an Owner Portal
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*

Daily Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Deleting Folders and Files from an Owner Portal 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Daily Tasks > Owner Portals`


You can delete specific files and folders from an owner portal or delete all folders and files at 

once. 

Deleting Individual Files 

To delete a specific file: 

1. 
In the Owner portals list, click the File count link to drill down into a portal’s folders, and 

then click the File count link again to drill down into a folder’s files. 

2. 
Select the Delete check box next to one or more files. 

3. 
Click the Delete button. 

A confirmation box opens. 

4. 
Click OK to confirm. 

Deleting Individual Folders 

Deleting a folder also deletes any files that were published in the folder. 

To delete a folder: 

1. 
In the Owner portals list, click the File count link to drill down into a portal’s folders. 

The Owner portals - Folders page opens. 

2. 
Select the Delete check box next to one or more folders. 

3. 
Click the Delete button. 

A confirmation box opens. 

4. 
Click OK to confirm. 

Deleting All Folders and Files in an Owner Portal 

To delete all folders and files in an owner portal: 

1. 
In the Owner portals list, select the Delete check box next to the owner portal(s) whose 

folders and files you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the Delete button. 

A confirmation box opens. 

3. 
Click OK to confirm. 

The File count resets to 0 and and any files and folders in the owner portal are deleted.

#### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 49*

Chapter 2: Daily Tasks 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized—that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead.

Storing a Report in My Stored Reports 

You can generate reports on demand and store them in the My stored reports list for later 

access. 

To store a report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at runtime. See 
Prompting for Filters at Runtime(on page 174).If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report Group on Demand(on page 264).

3. 
In the Delivery options section, select the Store report option. 

4. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report. 
If you ran the report on a location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the Location IDand 
Nameis added to the end of the stored report name to easily 
identify which property the report is for.

5. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Saves a report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Saves reports in an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Saves the report as a text file. 
Only the Printable and 
Excel options are available for report groups. When storing report 
groups as an Excel file, each report appears on a separate tab.

6. 
Click OK.

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or 

Amazon S3. If you are a developer, you can also deliver the report to another application using 

HTTP. 

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets in RealPage Accounting. The targets that you 

define will be available as storage options for reports. 

To store a report in a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at runtime. See 
Prompting for Filters at Runtime(on page 174).If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report Group on Demand(on page 264).

3. 
Select the Store in cloud check box. 

4. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the 

report.  By default, you can choose from cloud
-storage targets that either you
’ve defined or that 
others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, 
you can see all cloud targets.

5. 
If you want to override the default path where the report is delivered in the cloud-storage 

target, then type a different path in the Path field. 

6. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report. 
If you ran the report on a location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the Location IDand 
Nameis added to the end of the stored report name to easily 
identify which property the report is for.

7. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Saves a report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file.

Viewing a Stored Report 

After the system runs the report on the date that you selected, you can find the report in either 

the My stored reports list or the Reports center. 

To view a stored report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Open the application where you created the report. 

2. 
On the All tab of the menu, find and select the My stored reports option. 

The My stored reports list opens with a list of reports stored in the application. 

3. 
Find the report that you want to view and then verify the report date in the Run date/time 

column. Verifying the report date helps you avoid missing data. For example, if you 

scheduled the report to run two weeks ago, you would be missing the last two weeks of 

data. 

4. 
Click one of the following links to open your report in the format it was stored:  

• 
HTML: Opens the report in a new browser tab as a web page. 

• 
PDF: Opens a printable PDF version of the report that you can print and download. 

• 
CSV: Downloads a CSV file containing the report data. This is a good format to 

download if you want to import the data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Downloads the report as an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Opens a text version of the report in the web browser. 

• 
Cloud: Opens the report in your configured cloud account. If there is no cloud link for 

the report, see Storing a Report in a Cloud Storage Location (on page 45). 

• 
Success: Opens the report in Reporting Portal. If there was an error processing the 

report, then the View status link appears in the column instead. See Viewing a Report 

Error Log for error details. 
If you have not yet processed the report offline, then click the Create offline link to process 
the report.

#### Custom Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 66*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Custom Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > Custom Reports`


In addition to standard and financial reports, you can build custom reports by adding your 

specific records, fields, and calculations. Custom reports are created with the custom report 

wizard, which walks you through the steps to create a report. 

Create custom reports to get insight and answers from the unique information stored in your 

system. Financial reports are based on account groupings such as assets and liabilities, while 

custom reports and dimension structures are based on records and fields either grouped together 

or separately. 

For example, you can create a custom report that displays vendor contact information. You can 

control which vendors you want to display, such as active vendors in certain regions, and select 

the details to include about the vendors. You can then sort and display the results to highlight 

what is most important to you. 

With a custom report, you can: 

• 
Report on fields from almost any record or transaction in the system, and any related data. 

• 
Customize the report for your needs. 

• 
Run the reports, export them in another format, or add them to dashboards. 

Before you can export a standard report or add it to a group, you need to memorize the report.

#### Custom Report Wizard

##### Selecting the Primary Data Source
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 70*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Custom Report Wizard 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > 
 Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
 Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > New Report > Custom Report > 
Create with Custom Report Wizard`


Use the Custom report wizard to create specialized reports from your company data. Unlike 

financial and standard reports, custom reports can include financial or non-financial data, or both, 

drawing on data from existing fields or your company’s custom fields. 

Selecting the Primary Data Source 

Choose a record or transaction as a starting point for your report. 

Records 

A record is any piece of information in your company. The records available for selection are 

based on your user permissions; you cannot select a record you don’t have access to. When a 

record is selected, other related information is available for inclusion in your report. 

For example, if you select Customer as your primary data source, you can include column 

information from the Contact, Parent customer, or Customer type records. 

Transactions 

You can select a transaction type as your primary data source, such as A/P invoice, A/R 

adjustment, or Deposits. These options include all header information in the transaction record. If 

you want to include the header information plus any amounts and line-item details from the 

transaction, then select the data source option labeled “detail,” such as A/P invoice detail, A/R 

adjustment detail, or Deposits details. This allows you to access transaction amounts and use the 

custom report writer to add calculated columns later in the process. 

For example, to list all invoices with line items over $10,000, you can start by choosing the data 

source A/P invoice detail. Your report can include columns of information from A/P invoice 

details and related data. 
When you run a custom report for User Permission Activity, this custom report only shows permissions which have been explicitly activated by an administrator. There are other permissionswhich are switched on by other applications, called derived permissions. To see a complete list of your permissions, run a User Permissionsreport.

---

Defining Columns 

Define the columns in your report using the following procedures. 

Add Columns 

Select the data that you want to add to your report. Each check box represents one column in the 

report. It is better to include more information than you need at this point in creating your report. In later steps, you can refine which data to display.

The following icons are used to help you identify information you want to use in your report: 

• 
: identifies a linked field. When you run the report, you can see more information by 

clicking the link. 

• 
: identifies a custom field. 
Viewing custom fields is dependent on your permissions. If you include custom fields in your report and then deploy the report to an application, the custom fields might or might not be visible to other users, depending on their permission levels.

• 
: identifies an expandable subsection of the primary data source. If a subsection is also a 

data source, when you expand it, the system displays the data source’s subsections with 

additional data, possibly even additional subsections, that you can include as columns in 

your report. 

For multi-entity companies:Click 
Created at entity informationbelow a transaction or object, 
and then select what you want to track. For anything created at the top level, the report will show a blank entry.

---


<!-- Page 72 -->
Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Add Calculated Columns 

The custom report writer also allows you to create column calculations based on the columns you 

selected. 

For example, you can calculate an employee’s commission by multiplying their commission rate 

by the total number of sales invoices attributed to that employee. When you run the report, the 

system displays the calculation in the report in a column with the name you assigned. 

You can add calculations by creating a formula uses columns of information from your data 

source. This lets you perform operations on other columns in your data source and then show 

results in your report. 

The formulas created follow the mathematical order or operations. Keep the following order of 

operations in mind when you create a formula: 

• 
Calculations inside parentheses are performed first. 

• 
All multiplications and divisions are performed next, working from left to right. 

• 
Lastly, all additions and subtractions are performed, working from left to right. 

To create a formula for a calculated column: 
Calculations can only be applied to columns containing numbers.

1. 
Click the Add button. 

The system opens the Formula Editor box. Use this editor to create a formula from any of 

the information in your primary data source. You can add multiple columns and operator, 

depending on the calculation you want to display. 

2. 
In the Available Report Columns pane, select the column containing the data you want to 

include in the calculation. For example, select AP Invoice Detail Total Due. 

---


<!-- Page 73 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

The system adds an expression in the Formula pane. 

3. 
Use the basic math operators (addition +, subtraction -, multiplication *, and division /) and 

parentheses to create a formula. For example, click the subtraction operator under the 

Operators column. 

4. 
In the Available Report Columns pane, select the column containing the date included in 

the calculation. For example, select AP Invoice Detail Transaction amount. 

The system displays an expression for the transaction in the Formula pane. 

5. 
In the Calculated column type drop-down list, select the formula format. 

6. 
In the Calculated column name field, enter a label for the column. 

Select the Column Sequence 

1. 
Drag columns into the order that you want the system to display them in your report. 

2. 
Optionally, use the text box to rename columns in the report.

##### Filtering the Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 74*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Add Column Totals 

Select the check boxes next to the columns for which you want to display a summary. You can 

only perform mathematical summaries, such as count, sum, average, std deviation, variance, 

largest, and smallest, on numeric data fields. Text fields are limited to count summaries. 

In a report without grouping, the system displays the calculations at the bottom of the report for 

the entire table. In a report with grouping, the system displays the calculations for each subgroup 

and for the entire table. 

Sort the Columns and Set the Priority 

1. 
Click the drop-down list next to each column title. 

2. 
Select whether you want to sort the column in Ascending or Descending order, or None. 
You can assign an ascending or descending order to a maximum of four columns.

3. 
Drag and drop the columns in the list to change the sorting priority. 

The column in the first position will be sorted first, the next column down will be sorted 

within the first, and so on. 

Filtering the Report 

You can use filters in your report to limit the data the system displays to the criteria that you 

choose. 

Select a Filter 

You set the first group of filters when you select the columns from your primary data source. 

Other information related to your primary data source are available to use as filters as well and 

are listed under the first group of filters as expandable objects. 

1. 
Expand the object that has the column or field you want to filter. 

2. 
In the Columns column, click a drop-down list, and then select the column by which you 

want to filter. 

3. 
In the Operator column, select the operator you want to use to filter the column. 

See the list of available operators (on page 72). 

4. 
In the Value column, enter the corresponding value. 

This can be a number or a string of text depending on the chosen operator. If you choose 

Includes or Excludes, the value could be a comma delimited list of numbers or text strings. 

5. 
Click the Add filter link below the columns to add more filters in the object. 

6. 
Click the Delete last filter link to remove a filter field. 

---


<!-- Page 75 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Refine the Filters 

By default, all filter conditions are combined with an AND logic. In this step, you can apply more 

advanced logic using OR conditions and group filters. 

1. 
Review the filters you added in the previous step. 

The system displays filter position numbers, which you can use to create your advanced 

filter statement. 

2. 
In the Filter expression field, combine filter position numbers using logical operators and 

parentheses. 

For example, you want to filter a report to display transactions for customer accounts within 

the 2010-3010 range or the 6010-7010 range, and the total paid amount is greater than 0.

##### Grouping Data
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 76*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide

Grouping Data 

Enable Grouping 

Set the level of detail you want the system to display in your report by selecting the appropriate 

grouping option. 

• 
No grouping: Select this format if you want to display a flat list of information, with the 

option to show a grand total at the bottom. For example, you can use this format to display 

a list of employees with their contact information, or a list of invoices with their total dollar 

value. 

• 
Grouping: Select this format if you want to arrange the information together and show 

subtotals for grouped rows. By default, the report shows subtotals based on the groups you 

select in succeeding steps. The system automatically includes totals by group. For example, 

you can use this format to display invoice subtotals by customer and invoice totals for all 

customers. 

Group Data by Columns 

You can only group data by columns if you enable the Grouping option in the previous step. 

1. 
Expand the object that contains the column by which you want to group the report. 

2. 
Select the column from the drop-down list. 

When you select multiple columns, the system creates subgroups in the report. 
Grouping the data by more than three columns could distort the data. As a best practice, only group by three or less columns.

Order the Groups 

You can set which groups take priority when sorted. The system sorts the items first by the first 

column, and then by the second column, and so on, creating multiple levels of summary 

information. 

1. 
In the Position column, select the button next to the column you want to move. 

2. 
If a column has child columns, select the Include Children check box to enable the feature. 

3. 
Use the 
 Top, 
 Up, 
 Down, and 
 Bottom arrows to change the sorting priority 

of the column. 

4. 
In the Sort column, use the corresponding drop-down list to select whether you want to 

sort your columns in ascending or descending order. 

Group Totals 

In a report with grouping, the system displays the calculations for each subgroup and for the 

entire table. Select the desired column totals in the Add more totals step. For more information, 

see Defining columns (on page 62).

Setting the Report Date and Title 

You can set parameters for running the report, such as the reporting period and the title of the 

report. 

1. 
Select a reporting period or a range of dates. 

• 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select monthly, quarterly, or annual options 

that include next, current, and past periods. You can modify this time period by adding 

an As of date value. 

• 
In Start date and End date fields, select an exact date range for the report. 

Type “ p ”in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.

2. 
If your company is comprised of multiple entities with multiple base currencies, set the

In the Show for drop-down list, select whether you want to display All locations, This

• 
In the Report title 1 and Report title 2 fields, enter the first and second lines of the 

report title, respectively. 

•

Defining the Chart Output 

You can choose to run a chart format to visually display your information. 

1. 
In the Chart type drop-down list, select the type that works best for your report. The default 

option is the Column type. To view examples of each type of chart, see Creating graphs 

from custom reports (on page 76). 

2. 
Select the visual options. 

• 
Y-axis: The summary value that is set along the vertical axis of the chart. 

• 
X-axis: The summary value that is set along the horizontal axis of the chart. 

• 
Grouping: Sets a third parameter (from Grouped by) for stacked and parallel charts. 

• 
X label: Sets the position for the label on the horizontal axis. 

• 
Y label: Sets the position for the label on the vertical axis. 

• 
Legend: Sets the position for the graph legend. 

• 
Font size: Sets the size of the text used on the chart. 

• 
Graph size: Sets the size of the grid the chart is set over. 

• 
Width: Sets the overall width of the chart in pixels. 

• 
Height: Sets the overall height of the chart in pixels. 
Sometimes a graph is an easier wayto view report information. After defining the chart output, you can run the custom report and select Graphas the output type.

Adding Prompts 

The additional prompts you can add at runtime are similar to filters, in that they filter the data 

according to the criteria you set. Unlike filters, these prompts are set up as fields that the user 

specifies at the time they run the report. For example, if you want the user running the report to 

specify the A/R status regarding the invoice from which the item comes, you can add a prompt 

for the A/R Account Label object, and then select the Status field. 

To select a runtime prompt: 

1. 
Expand the section for the object that contains the field. 

2. 
Select the check box next to the field for which you want to add a prompt. 

3. 
Repeat the steps to add more prompts. 
You can select up to six runtime prompts.

If you run the report from the Custom reports list, the system ignores the filters and runs the 

report without any prompts. To ensure that all your filters and prompts are applied, run the 

custom report from the application in which you saved it. Learn more about saving a report to a 

menu (on page 71).

Labeling and Grouping Prompts 

You only need to label and organize prompts if you chose to include additional prompts in the 

previous step of the custom report writer. 

This page allows you to control how a prompt field will be labeled, how multiple fields will be 

grouped, and whether it will have a prompt at runtime. 

Change the Prompt Label 

By default, the name of the field is provided as the Prompt Label. 

To change the Prompt Label, click the Prompt label field and type the label you prefer. 

Group Prompts 

The Group field allows you to present your prompts in groups when you run the report. 

For example, if you want to group several fields together in a section titled A/R Parameters, for 

each field, type “A/R Parameters” in the Group column. 

On a report with several prompts, grouping fields with meaningful labels can save time for the 

person running the report. 

To add a group, click the Group field, and then type the name of the group you are creating. 
To group all prompts under one label, enter one group name in the top Group field. To group 
prompts under different group names, put different group names in the Group field.

Use Prompts in Memorized Reports 

You can use your selected prompts again in memorized reports by selecting the Enable when 

memorized check box. 

Change display prompt positions 

To change the display order of your runtime prompts: 

1. 
Select the radio button in the Position column for the parameter you want to move. 

2. 
Move the parameter by using the 
 Top, 
 Up, 
 Down, and 
 Bottom buttons.

Saving the Report 

The final step of the custom report writer allows you to save your report and add your report to 

an application menu. This makes it available to other users who have access to that application. 

Save and Deploy Your Report to an Application Menu 

1. 
In the Name field, type your preferred report name. 

2. 
Select the Add to menu check box. 
To access your report only through the Custom reportslist, leave the 
Add to menucheck 
box clear. However, we recommend that you add your custom report to an application menu. If you run the report from the Custom reportslist, the system omits filters and 
prompts. When you run the report from the application menu, the report presentsall prompts and filters.

3. 
In the Application drop-down list, select the application to which you want to add the 

report. 

4. 
In the Description field, enter optional text to describe your report. 

5. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether you want the report to be Active or Inactive. 

New reports are set to Active by default. 

6. 
Click the Save button at the top of the page to save your report.  

Your report is saved and added to both the application menu you selected and to the list of 

reports. 

Make the Custom Report Available in Other Places 

One of the advantages of custom reports is that you can schedule them to run at different times 

with the same settings and make them available in dashboards and report groups. To take 

advantage of this feature: 

• 
Memorize the report so it can be run again with the same settings. 

• 
Add a memorized report to a dashboard or report group. 

• 
Schedule a memorized report.

##### Operator Definitions
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 81*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Operator Definitions 

The following operators are available for use when filtering: 

• 
Equals: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column matches the text or 

number in the Value field. 

• 
Less than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is less 

than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

greater than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Less or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

less than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen 

column is greater than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Not equal to: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column does not match 

the text or number in the Value field. 

• 
Contains: Displays all records in which a character or group of characters in the chosen 

column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The characters must 

match in the same order. For example, “ox” typed in the Value field may return records for 

Oxygen Inc., Boxing Agency, and Clorox, if those were values in the chosen column. 

• 
Does not contain: Displays all records in which no character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. 

• 
Starts with: Displays all records in which the first character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you have an item ID scheme that 

uses initial letters to identify the product type, you can select the item ID column and set the 

Value field to these letters to display all records for that product type. 

• 
Ends with: Displays all records in which the last character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you tag the end of the item ID for 

all custom order items with the letters “CO,” you can select the item ID column and set the 

value to CO to display all records for custom order items. 

• 
Includes: Displays all records that match items in a comma delimited list in the Value field. 

• 
Excludes: Displays all records that do not match items in a comma delimited list in the 

Value field. 

• 
Field equals null: Displays all records that have a null or empty field. 

• 
Field not equals null: Displays all records that do not have a null or empty field.

##### Running a Custom Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 82*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns. 

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 

Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 

of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

% bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank,” like Metropolis Bank. 

Running a Custom Report 

When a custom report is created, the report designer has the option to add (or “deploy”) the 

report to an application, such as General Ledger, Accounts Payable, or Accounts Receivable. 

Deploying the report to an application makes the report available from the application menu and 

from the Report Center. 

To run a report from the Reports center page, go to Running a Report from Reports Center. 

To run a custom report from an application menu: 

1. 
Go to the application whose report you want to run, and then click the corresponding link 

for the custom report that you want to run. 

2. 
Set the filters as needed. 

3. 
Do one of the following options: 

• 
Click View to display the report in HTML. 

• 
Click Print to display the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
Click the Export drop-down list, select your preferred format, and then click Go.

Creating Charts from Custom Reports 

Using the Custom report wizard, you can create charts that can be displayed on their own or

To create a chart from a custom report, follow the steps in the Custom report wizard (on page 62):

Select the data source (on page 62).

Define the chart output (on page 69). 

5. 
Add any prompts (on page 70).

Save the report.

Copying a Custom Report from One Company or Entity to Another 

If you’re using the Custom report wizard and have a report that you want to copy from one 

company to another, you can create a custom package document to transfer your custom report. 
You must have administrator- level privileges to access the Platform Services (or Customization 
Services) application.

Creating a Report Definition Package 

1. 
Sign into the company whose report definition you want to copy. 

2. 
In the Applications menu, select Platform Services (or Customization Services), and then 

select the Custom reports option. The Custom reports page opens.

file. 

Preparing the Package 

Modify the package to prepare it for importing to the second company or entity. 

1. 
Open a text edit and paste the following XML wrapper text into a new file: 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 

<customErpPackage 
xmlns:xsi=“http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance”> 

<packageDescription> 

<name>INSERT NAME HERE</name> 

<description>INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE</description> 

<author>AUTHOR NAME</author> 

</packageDescription> 


> **Navigation Path:** `<customReports>`


<!-- Paste the contents of the file here--> 


> **Navigation Path:** `</customReports>`


</customErpPackage> 

1. 
Do not close the file. 

Adding the Definition to the XML File 

1. 
Using a text editor, open the report XML file you downloaded to your local drive. 

2. 
Copy the entire contents of the file. 

3. 
Go back to the XML wrapper file you created in the previous procedure. 

4. 
Paste the report code into the XML wrapper file in the space after the text <!--Paste the 

contents of the file here-->. 

5. 
Delete the following text: 

<!--Paste the contents of the file here--> 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 
Only delete the second instance of <?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?>. 
This is included in the report XML. The first instance at the top of the file should remain.

##### Before You Begin

Financial Reports 

See the How to Get Here (on page 91) topic for a list of ways to access financial reports. 

Financial reports are available from the General Ledger, Reports, and Reporting Portal 

applications. You can create financial reports using the Financial report writer, or, if your 

company was created using a QuickStart template, you can access standard financial reports by 

clicking the Financial reports library button in the Financial reports list. 

To use one of the standard reports, you need to map your chart of accounts to the system 

categories and the reports become live with your data. This helps speed up the otherwise 

time-consuming process of manually creating account groups that contain the appropriate G/L 

accounts and then creating financial reports and graphs using those account groups. 

Each application includes a set of standard reports that you can run to produce basic, common 

reports quickly. You can create, run, view, export, and memorize the following types of reports: 

• 
Standard reports available from the Reports section of each application menu and from the 

Reports center. 

• 
Financial reports and graphs using the Financial report writer. 
You cannot change the report structure after creating the report.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use financial reports. 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

General Ledger 
Financials 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

##### Creating a Financial Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 102*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Creating a Financial Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 91) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

The Financial report writer provides options for controlling all aspects of your financial report, 

from building your rows and columns to setting precise formatting options. 

Adding a Financial Report 

To create a report using the Financial report writer: 

1. 
In the Financial reports list, click the Add button. The Financial report writer opens. 

2. 
Name your report. 

3. 
Select your basic report structure (Report info tab (on page 123)). 

4. 
Review the options in the Report structure section of the Report info tab, using the report 

samples as a guide. After you create a report, you can’t change the report structure. 

5. 
Select either Accounts or Dimensions, depending on what you’d like to see on your report 

rows. 

6. 
Build your account rows. 

Depending on the report structure you selected on the Report info tab, you’ll either build 

rows from account groups or dimension structures. For existing reports, the headings that 

you see along the left side of the tab reflect the account groups or dimension structures 

that have already been added to the report. 

       Type of rows  
        Description 

Accounts on rows (Rows 

tab) 

In this type of report, you select the account groups 

that you want to appear on the left side of your 

report. For example, a balance sheet report might 

include “Assets” and “Liabilities and Equity.” 

Dimensions on rows (Rows 

tab) 

In this type of report, you select the dimension 

structures that you want to appear on the left side 

of your report. For example, you might want to 

show rows for customers, or certain locations or 

departments. 

---


<!-- Page 103 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Setting Up Columns (Columns Tab) (on page 142) 

1. 
Choose the columns you want to include in the report. 

2. 
Decide what value you want to include in each column. For example, you might want to see 

the account names or dimension names on the left, followed by actual columns for different 

reporting periods. 

3. 
Column values can be based on calculations, such as summary calculations that operate on 

two or more columns (such as computing the average of a set of columns). For reports that 

feature account groups on rows, you can define more complex calculations on the 

Computations tab. 

4. 
Select the Account group purpose. This is displayed in the list and in the report. 

Filtering the Report (Filters Tab (on page 171)) 

You can set options such as the “as of date” and reporting method. You can also filter the report 

by dimension, such as filtering for a particular set of locations. 

In practice, many reports are designed to prompt the user for the “as of date” and other criteria 

when the report is run. That way you can create a single report and let the user choose the criteria 

when the report is run. 

Setting Up Headers and Footers (Format Tab (on page 179)) 

Set page header, footer, font, and other report format options. 

Row formatting options let you control the appearance and spacing of row headings and totals. 

Click the 
 Help buttons next to Row formatting and Total formatting in the Rows section to 

learn more. 
If any columns are missing when you preview the report, on the Filterstab choose to show zero 
balance columns to force any zero balance columns to display.

Setting Access Restrictions for the Report (Permissions Tab (on page 193)) 

Finish the report with any optional next steps, such as adding the report to a dashboard, making 

it a favorite, or scheduling it to run automatically (Next Steps (on page 194)). 

Multi-Entity Companies: Private Reports 

By default, financial reports are set to Public. 

This means that everyone can see them. If a report is private, only the users in the entity and with 

permissions can see the report. Top-level admins can also see private reports if they check 

Include Private in the list of reports. 

To make entity-level financial reports private by default, disable the Set default permissions to 

public setting at the top-level General Ledger configuration.

Viewing Financial Reports 

Reports can be either public or private. Everyone who uses the application can view public 

reports. For each report in the Financial reports list, you see the name of the report that you 

entered in the Report name field on the Report info tab of the Financial Report Writer. You also 

see the name of the owner of the report or “public” if everyone has access to the report. 

Only those who have been assigned permission by the administrator or the person who created 

the report can view private reports. (To grant permission to a private report for a user or group, 

click the Edit link for the report, and then click the Permissions tab.) 

Multi-Entity Companies 

Making a report private means that the report will not be visible to other operating entities. 

Administrators can choose whether new reports are created as public, or private by default. Public

people and send the report to a Dropbox folder where it can be stored and accessed by others.

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups (on page 174), then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or 

more G/L account groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 
Type “ p ”in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.

If you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use.

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.

that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start dateis on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday.Type “ p ”in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. Se
e Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.

In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report.

in the Every field.

In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save.

##### Deleting, Inactivating, or Reactivating a Financial Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 112*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Deleting, Inactivating, or Reactivating a Financial Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 91) topic for a list of ways to access financial reports. 

If you delete a report, it can’t be restored. Making a report inactive removes it from the list but 

retains the report information in case you need to reactivate it. 

If there is chance that you’ll need to run the report at a later date—perhaps even years later— 

then we recommend that you make it inactive instead of deleting it. For example, you may need 

to make a change to a report due to an audit or generate a copy of the report for legal purposes. 

In this case, if the report is inactive, you can reactivate it and run it or make changes. If the report 

is deleted, you would have to recreate the report from scratch. 

Another reason to choose one over the other might be to keep the original report pristine while 

you incorporate changes to a copy. If the changes don’t work the way you expect, you can keep 

making changes to the copy and still make sure that you can restore the original. By inactivating 

the original, no one can use it and it doesn’t appear in lists. When you’re completely confident 

that the new report works correctly, you can go ahead and delete the original. 

Before You Begin 

Access to financial reports can vary depending on your permissions. The ability to view, add, and 

edit financial reports is controlled by separate General Ledger permissions. Working with financial 

reports can involve multiple tasks, such as running reports, editing reports, navigating into a 

report, and so on. Each of these can require a specific set of permissions, both for the General 

Ledger and for the Company. 

Make sure that you have all of the necessary permissions when working with financial reports. 

Deleting a Financial Report 

Deleting a report removes the report completely. If you are sure you never want to run the report, 

delete it. Otherwise, consider making the report inactive. 

You can configure the system to warn you when you’re about to delete a report. Click your login 

name on any page, then choose My preferences, and on the Preferences page, select the Warn 

on delete check box. 

To delete a custom report: 

1. 
Open the Financial reports list. 

2. 
Locate the report to delete, and then click the Delete link. 

3. 
Click OK to confirm. 

---


<!-- Page 113 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Inactivating a Financial Report 

Inactivating a report removes it from lists within the system. Additionally, if you inactivate a 

custom report, it won’t appear on the Financial reports list unless you select the Include inactive 

option at the top of the list. 

To inactivate a financial report: 

1. 
Open the Financial reports list. 

2. 
Locate the report, and then click Edit. 

3. 
Go to the Next Steps step (the last step of the report writer). 

4. 
Clear the This report is active check box. 

5. 
Save the report. 

Reactivating a Financial Report 

If you inactivate a report and later want to reactivate it, you first need to be able to see the report 

in the list. 

To reactivate a financial report: 

1. 
Open the Financial reports list. 

2. 
At the top of the list, select Include inactive. Now, the inactivated report appears in the list. 

3. 
Locate the report, and then click Edit, then and select the This report is active check box on 

the Report Info tab. 

4. 
Save your changes. The report is now active again.

The Income Statement Budget Comparison report displays your company’s current and 

year-to-date income and expenses compared to the original budget. This report functions the 

same as the Income Statement report but also displays the difference between your company’s 

actuals and budgeted amounts, including the budget variance percentage. 

Click an account category to narrow the report by accounts in that category or click an individual 

account to view the account details in a separate window.

HTML 

•

• 
PDF 

• 
Excel

##### Income Statement Budget Comparison Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 127*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Income Statement Budget Comparison Report Columns 

By default, the Income Statement Budget Comparison report contains the following columns: 

• 
(Accounts): This column displays a list of income and expense accounts in their account 

group hierarchy. 

• 
Month ending: This column section displays account actuals and budgeted amounts for the 

current reporting period. 

• 
Actual: This column displays account actuals for the current reporting period. 

• 
Budget: This column displays the amount budgeted for each account for the current 

reporting period. 

• 
Difference: This column displays the difference between the actuals and budgeted 

amounts for the current reporting period. 

• 
Variance %: This column displays the percent difference between the actuals and 

budgeted amounts for the current reporting period. 

• 
Year to date: This column section displays account actuals and budgeted amounts from the 

beginning of the fiscal year to the current date. 

• 
YTD actual: This column displays account actuals from the beginning of the fiscal year 

to the current date. 

• 
YTD budget: This column displays the amount budgeted for each account from the 

beginning of the fiscal year to the current date.  

• 
YTD difference: This column displays the difference between the year-to-date actuals 

and budgeted amounts. 

• 
YTD variance %: This column displays the percent difference between the year-to-date 

actuals and budgeted amounts. 
These are the columns that appear when you initially install the report from the System financial 

reportslist. You can configure additional columns by editing the report in the 
Financial report 

writer.

#### Financial Report Writer
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 129*

Chapter 3: Reports

Financial Report Writer 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reporting > 
 Financial Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Financial Statements > 
 Financial Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > 
 Financial Reports`


Use the Financial report writer to create and edit financial reports. This includes both standard 

financial reports, such as income statements and balance sheet reports, and an infinite array of 

other reports that analyze or highlight key business metrics, such as revenue by product line. 

The Financial report writer guides you through the process of creating or editing a financial 

report, from adding rows and columns to deciding how your report should be formatted on page 

and in print. 

Some things you can do with a financial report include: 

• 
Selecting groups of accounts to include in your report. 

• 
Adding analysis based on your segment data, such as items by product line, customers by 

type, or selected departments. 

• 
Prompting users to set or change filter criteria at report runtime.  

• 
Expanding or collapsing sections of the report to show or hide account detail. 

• 
Selecting what you want to appear in columns, such as account data, budget data, 

computations, and even non-financial data such as customer email addresses.

Financial Report Writer Workflow 

The Financial report writer provides options for controlling all aspects of your financial report, 

from building your rows and columns to setting precise formatting options. 

The following lists the basic steps in creating a financial report. For detailed instructions, see 

Creating a Financial Report (on page 93). 

1. 
Name the report (on page 123) and select the basic report structure (on page 124). 

2. 
Build your account rows (on page 127). 

3. 
Set up your columns (on page 142). 

4. 
Add computations (on page 163), if applicable. 

5. 
Filter (on page 171) the report and, if desired, prompt users (on page 174) to filter the 

report at runtime. 

6. 
Set up the formatting (on page 179). 

7. 
Set access permissions (on page 193). 

8. 
Finish the report with any optional next steps (on page 194).

Entering Basic Report Information 

To enter basic information for your report: 

1. 
In the Report name field, enter a name that will help you distinguish it from other reports. 

The report name, which is different from the title, is used to identify the report on the 

browser, but doesn’t appear on printed (PDF) reports. 

The report name is used in the following places: 

• 
List of financial reports: The report name appears in the Financial reports list page, 

Reports Center, and other places where you have the option to select, display, or edit 

financial reports. 

• 
Report header (HTML or Excel formats only): When the report is displayed in HTML or 

Excel, the header displays Your company name-Report name. 
To specify the report title, go to the Format tab, select the
Page Setup and Columnssection, and then enter the Report title.

2. 
To assign a Report type, use the drop-down list. For more information, see Report Types. 

3. 
To select the Report audience, use the drop-down list. For more information, see Report 

Audiences. 

Selecting the Report Structure 

When you create a new report, you’re asked to select a basic Report structure. Based on your 

selection, the options on the remaining tabs change to help you create the type of report you’re 

looking for. 

This procedure applies to new reports only.
You can only change the report structure before you save your report. Your choice of report structure changes how the Financial Report Writer works and the options that are available on each tab. For this reason, after you’ve added rows to a report, you can no longer change the 
report structure. To use a different report structure, you must create a new report.

To select a report structure: 

1. 
Select one of the following options to determine your basic report structure. As you select 

options, samples show the type of report output you can expect. 

2. 
In the Report structure section, select Accounts or Segments. The report structure 

determines the basic report structure by selecting what appears in rows. 

• 
Accounts: Displays accounts on report rows. 

• 
Segments: Displays segment data on the left side of the report and the account data 

in columns.

#### Rows Tab
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 135*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Rows Tab 

The main purpose of the Rows tab is to populate the rows in your report. As you work on this tab, 

the choices you make determine what appears along the left side of your report. 

Using this tab, you will determine: 

• 
Which account groups or segment structures appear on the left side of your report. 

• 
Whether you want to show detail or create a summary report. 

Rows Tab Basics 

The Rows tab provides options that let you finely control the content of your report rows. 

1. 
Select which of the following will form the structure of your report: 

• 
Account groups 

• 
Segment structures 

The account groups or segment structures that you choose determine the sections, 

subsections, and individual accounts that appear on the left side of your report. 

2. 
If you selected segment structures in the previous step, select the account groups you want 

to use to display data. 

3. 
Choose the level of detail you want to show. 

4. 
Preview the report and make other optional changes. 

You can always come back to this tab later to make formatting changes. 

Account Groups 

When you select Account groups, then account groups form the rows in your report. 

When you design a report, you start by selecting the account groups that you want to include. 

The account groups that you select: 

• 
Represent the hierarchical groupings you need in the report. For example, “Assets” may 

contain “Current Assets,” “Fixed Assets,” and so on. 

• 
Categorize individual accounts into the appropriate groupings. For example, “Fixed Assets” 

may include individual accounts such as “1500--Equipment,” “1510--Building,” and so on.

Segment report structures are named structures that are created for the purpose of adding

Choosing the Level of Detail for the Entire Report 

Reports are preset to show account groups or segment structures fully expanded, including all 

subgroups/substructures and individual accounts or members. However, you can choose the level 

of detail you want to show.

heading. 

The system opens the Set detail level box. 

2. 
Select one of the following options: 

• 
Details - show accounts: Shows any accounts in the account group 

• 
Summary - hide accounts: Hides the account detail and shows summary amounts only 

3. 
Click the Set button. 

Segment Structures on Rows 

If you selected to display segment structures on rows: 

1. 
On the Define rows page, click the Set detail level link under the Detail level column 

heading. 

The system opens the Set detail Level box. 

2. 
Select one of the following options: 

• 
Details - show members: Shows any members in the segment structure 

• 
Summary - hide members: Hides the segment structure members 

3. 
Click the Set button.

Expand by Segment - Show Options 

When expanding by segment, the Show options allow a more detailed look at each segment. 

Because many segments are hierarchical (for example, a US location might be organized by state, 

with additional locations in certain cities), the Show drop-down list allows you to choose: 

• 
How many levels to show. 

• 
Whether amounts are reported individually, or with amounts rolled up from levels below it. 

The list describes each option: 

• 
One level down, with roll-up: Displays rows that contain summary amounts for one level 

only. For example, you have locations in California, New York, and Florida, with sublocations 

for California. In this case, the report includes rows for California, New York, and Florida but 

doesn’t include rows for sublocations. However, the amounts for sublocations are included 

in the summary amounts for California, New York, and Florida. 

• 
All levels, with roll-up: Displays rows that contain summary amounts for each level. For 

example, your California location has sublocations by city. In this case, the report includes 

rows for California and each city in California and includes amounts from each city in the 

amount for California. 

• 
All levels, with individual balance: Displays all levels, but with each level showing only the 

individual amounts assigned to that level. For example, your California location has 

sublocations by city. In this case, the report includes rows for California and each city within 

California but doesn’t include amounts from each city in the amount for California. In the 

case of expenses, for instance, the row for California would only include expenses attributed 

directly to California and would not include amounts from any city in California. 

• 
Leaf amounts, all levels: Displays only the lowest levels of the hierarchy. For example, you 

have a location in Arizona with no sublocations, but you also have a location in California

##### Previewing the Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 146*



##### Selecting the Basis for Amounts
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 146*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Previewing the Report 

When you’ve added account groups to your Rows tab, you can preview your report to see the 

resulting rows. 

To preview and refine your report rows: 

1. 
Click the Preview drop-down list and select the format in which you want to preview the 

report. 

• 
Live report (HTML): View what the report will look like in the browser 

• 
Print version (PDF): View what the report will look like in print 

• 
Excel: Download the report in Excel 

If this is a new report, you’ll see a default column that shows actual amounts for the current 

month. When you proceed to the Columns tab, you’ll be able to change the columns for 

your report. 

2. 
Go back to the Rows tab to refine your report rows. 

Selecting the Basis for Amounts 
This version of the Rows tab applies o
nly if you created a financial report that features account groups on the rows of the report. Learn more about selecting a report structure(on page 124).

Every account group has a default method of calculating amounts on reports. For example, 

account groups that contain income or expense accounts are typically calculated “For the period” 

so that reports show the income or expense incurred during that reporting period. 

You can leave the default calculation method as is, or you can override this calculation method for 

the rows in your report. You can also set up your report to show cumulative balances across time 

periods or display amounts as a percentage of another account group (for example, current assets 

as a percentage of total assets). 

To change the basis for amounts: 

1. 
On the Define rows page, locate the row for the account group you want to change.

Overriding the Default Amount Type for Report Rows 

Every account group has a default method of calculating amounts on reports. For example, 

account groups that contain income or expense accounts are typically calculated “For the period” 

so that reports show the income or expense incurred during that reporting period. 

To override the default amount type for a section of a report: 

1. 
On the Define rows page, locate the account group in the Row structure column. 

2. 
Click the Basis for amounts column. 

3. 
In the Report amount type drop-down list, select your preferred amount type. 

Displaying Amounts as Cumulative Balances 

In some cases, you might want your income and expense reports to show a cumulative total 

across time periods. 

For example, your rental expenses for each month total $5,000. Instead of showing $5,000 for 

each month, you can display a cumulative balance that shows $5000 for January, $10,000 for 

February, $15,000 for March, and so on. That way, you can see the total amount that you’ve spent 

for the year. 

To display cumulative balances: 

1. 
On the Define rows page, locate the account group you want to display as a cumulative 

balance in the Row structure column. 

2. 
Click the Basis for amounts column. 

3. 
Select the Cumulative Balance check box. 

4. 
On the Columns tab, set up your columns to compare data across consecutive time periods. 

For example, you can show amounts for the “Current Year” and expand your columns to 

compare the data by month.

Adding Computations to Rows 

In addition to standard account groups (such as Revenue or Operating Expense), you can also add 

account groups of type “computation” that display results derived from a calculation. You can use 

a computation account group to define a mathematical computation that you want to include as 

a section in financial reports. For example, you can include a section called “Revenue per Unit,” 

where the amount is computed by dividing revenue by the number of units. 

Unlike computations that appear in the columns of a financial report, a computation account 

group enables you to add a computation to report rows. 

To add a computation in the rows of a report: 
Define the computation in the account group before performing the following steps.

1. 
Create or edit a financial report. 

2. 
On the Rows tab, add the computation account group. 
If you want to see your computation as a single summarized line, select Summary - hide 

accountsoption when choosing the level of detail.

Columns Tab 

Use the Columns tab to specify the number of report columns, the type of value you want in each

basic process is to: 

1. 
Use the Column type drop-down list to select the type of value you want to appear in each

2.

(Optionally) Show segment data in the column.

or another segment. For more targeted analysis, columns can be organized according to

Period Comparison 

This column type displays the amount for a reporting period as the difference or percentage 

difference from the amounts in the previous column. 

• 
Period variance: Displays the percentage of difference between the previous column’s 

reporting period and the current column’s reporting period. 

When showing budget variances, best practice is to choose the normalized option. The 

normalized option uses the normal balance (credit or debit) of the parent-level account 

group to determine whether values should be presented as negative or positive. 

For normalized budget variance: 

• 
When revenue exceeds budget, the normalized variance is presented as a positive 

number. 

• 
When expenses exceed budget, the normalized variance is presented as a negative 

number. 

•

the current report period. 

When showing budget differences, best practice is to choose the normalized option. The 

normalized option uses the normal balance (credit or debit) of the parent-level account 

group to determine whether values should be presented as negative or positive. 

For normalized budget difference: 

• 
When revenue exceeds budget, the normalized difference is presented as a positive 

number. 

• 
When expenses exceed budget, the normalized difference is presented as a negative 

number.
