Budget and Budget Forecast 

These column types allow you to display budget amounts, show the difference between budget 

show and actual amounts, show a working budget, and create forecasts. When you choose a 

budget type column, the system prompts you to choose the budget that you want to use from a 

list. 

• 
Budget: Displays the budget for the reporting period. 

• 
Budget variance or Budget variance (normalized): Displays the variance of actual to budget 

as a percentage. For example, Budget is $10,000, actual expenditure is $12,000, therefore, 

Variance is (20%). 

When showing budget variances, it is best practice to choose the normalized option. The 

normalized option uses the normal balance (credit or debit) of the parent-level account 

group to determine whether values should be presented as negative or positive. For 

normalized budget variance: 

• 
When revenue exceeds budget, the normalized variance is presented as a positive 

number. 

• 
When expenses exceed budget, the normalized variance is presented as a negative 

number. 

• 
Budget difference or Budget difference (normalized): Displays the difference between the 

budget and the actual in dollars. For example: Budget is $18,000, actual is $20,000, 

therefore, the difference displays as ($2,000). 

When showing budget differences, it is best practice to choose the normalized option. The 

normalized option uses the normal balance (credit or debit) of the parent-level account 

group to determine whether values should be presented as negative or positive. For 

normalized budget difference: 

• 
When revenue exceeds budget, the normalized difference is presented as a positive 

number. 

• 
When expenses exceed budget, the normalized difference is presented as a negative 

number. 

• 
Budget ratio: Displays the ratio of actual to budget, as a factor. For example, if the ratio of 

actual expenditures to budgeted expenditures was 2:1, Ratio displays as (2). 

• 
Budget variance notes: Displays budget variance notes in the column. Select the Include 

Variance Amount, Date, and User check box to show the note, the variance amount when 

the note was entered, the date the note was entered, and which user entered it in the 

report. You can include budget variance notes from prior periods by selecting the 
Include prior 

period notescheck box under the 
Reporting period field. This option applies only when you 

---


<!-- Page 156 -->
Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Remaining budget: Calculates the amount remaining in a budget. To calculate, take the 

budget amount for the period and subtract the actual amount so far (up to the As of Date). 

For example, you have a budget of $10,000. As of the middle of the month, the actual 

amount is already $8,000. In this case, the remaining budget is $10,000 - $8,000 = $2,000. 

• 
Forecast: Calculates a mid-period budget forecast. To calculate, take the actual amount so 

far (up to the As of Date) and add the prorated budget amount. 
The budget is prorated based on the number of days between the As of Date and the end of the reporting period.

For example, you have a budget of $10,000. As of the middle of the month, the actual 

amount is already $8,000. In this case the forecast is 8,000 (actual) + 5,000 (prorated 

budget) = 13,000. 

• 
Working budget: Displays a draft of a budget that you are still making changes to as 

defined in Adding a working budget. 

Percentage of Amount 

This column type computes an actual or budget amount as a percentage of another value. To use 

a percentage calculation, you must first define the percentage calculation (on page 140) on the 

Rows tab. This column type is available only for reports that display account groups in rows.

• 
Percent on actual: Computes the actual value as a percentage of another value 

• 
Percent on budget: Computes a budget value as a percentage of another value 

Commitments 

This column type displays commitment values. 

• 
Open commitments: Displays the total value of all approved commitments. 

• 
Pending commitments: Displays the total value of all commitments waiting for approval. 

Other 

This column type creates a blank space between columns. 

• 
Blank column: Displays a blank column to add space between normal columns.

Selecting the Reporting Period 

Reporting periods are always relative to the As of date value for the report. For example, if you 

run a report as of 5/15/2015, the Current month option would show data for 5/1/2015 to 

5/31/15, the Current year option would show data for 1/1/2015 to 12/31/2015, and so on. 
Type “ p ”in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See Specifying 
Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.If you don’t see the reporting period you want, you can create one. Refer to 
Reporting Periods(on page 289 ) for details.

To choose a reporting period, locate the column you want to change and click anywhere in the 

column. The system expands the column to show more options. 
If you use custom accounting periods where leap years may not affect you as calendar year periods, it’s recommended to use the 
Current year to dateoption and a 
- 1 off
set when comparing the financial statement of the previous year (full period) with the statement for the current year.

To specify a relative reporting period using an offset: 

1. 
Select a reporting period. 

2. 
Enter the number of periods in the past (Offset from prior period) or future (Offset from 

future periods). 
Reporting periods work the same way, whether you use account groups or segments and dimensions with your Financial reports. 

Comparisons for Periods in Progress (Such as Current Month to Date) 

If you apply an offset to Current Month to Date, Current Quarter to Date, or Current Year to Date, 

the report dynamically calculates the portion of the current reporting period that has elapsed and 

uses the same partial period for the offset column. 

Using the example of Current Quarter to Date, if you run a report mid-quarter, the system adjusts 

both columns to include data up to the same point in the quarter, enabling you to create true 

comparisons. 

One-Day Comparisons 

For some industries, financial data is often analyzed by the day, such as a single day’s income for 

a restaurant on New Year’s Eve, or a Friday night at a hotel. 

Using the reporting period for the current day in combination with an offset, you can compare 

any day against the same day in another year, quarter, month, or week. 

1. 
On the Columns tab, locate one of the columns you want to compare, and then click 

anywhere in the column. 

---


<!-- Page 158 -->
Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

• 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the Today option. 

2. 
Locate the other column you want to compare, and then click anywhere in the column. 

• 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the Today option. 

• 
In the Offset field, specify the number of prior or future years, quarters, months, 

weeks, or days. 

3. 
On the Filters tab, select the option to prompt for the As of date field. This allows the user 

to select the date that the system uses for comparison at runtime. 

Sample comparisons: 

• 
Select “Today” as your reporting period, Offset = 1 prior year, As of date = 1/1/2015. The 

column will show the amount for New Year’s Day in 2014, which is 1/1/2014. 

• 
Select “Today” as your reporting period, Offset = 1 prior week, As of date = Friday 

7/24/2015. The column will show the amount for 1 week ago, which is Friday 7/17/2015. 

Including Budget Variance Notes from Prior Periods 

If you add the Budget variance notes column to your report, then you have the option to include 

budget variance notes from prior periods by selecting the Include prior period notes check box 

under the Reporting period field. This option applies only when you select a “Year to Date” 

reporting period.  

For example, if you select the option and you run the report on March 31, then the report will 

display notes for January, February, and March. If you do not select the option and you run the 

report on March 31, then the report will display only YTD notes for March.

Highlighting or Comparing by Segment 

You have multiple options for creating column comparisons by location, department, or other

writer. 

• 
Expand by segment: You can expand a single column by segment, such as location. 

• 
Filter a column by segment structure: Instead of looking at all members of a segment, you

criteria. 

• 
Filter and expand by a hierarchical segment structure: For more complex analysis, you can

Selecting an Account Group 

This option appears only if you created a report that features segments on rows when selecting

Creating Quick Column Computations 

Summary calculations perform a simple operation on two or more columns in a financial report. 

Operations that you can perform on columns include average, minimum, maximum, median, add, 

subtract, multiply, and divide. 

For example, you can: 

• 
Compute the average consulting revenue over several reporting periods 

• 
Show the highest monthly revenue 

• 
Divide a quarter of revenue by a year and express the result as a percentage 

If this type of computation doesn’t meet your needs, learn about other ways to create 

computations. See Computation Methods for Financial Reports. 

You create your calculation directly on the Columns tab of the Financial Report Writer. 

To add a simple calculation on two or more columns: 

1. 
On the Columns tab, add a new column anywhere to the right of the columns to which you 

are applying the calculation. 
The column containing the calculation must be located after the columns being operated on. For example, if you are planning to divide column 2 by column 3, the computation can be inserted in Column 4 or after.

2. 
In the new column, select the Summary on columns option in the Column type drop-down 

list.

Adding, Moving, Removing, or Hiding Columns 

You can add, move, remove, or hide columns if you find that you want to include or exclude the 

column data in a report. You can make the changes at any time and then save the report with the 

changes to run the report as usual. 

Add a Column 

You can add columns using the drop-down list at the top of each column. 

To add a new column to a financial report: 

1. 
On the Columns tab, locate a column next to where you want to add a new one and hover 

over the column number. 

2. 
In the drop-down list that appears, click the Add column left or Add column right option, 

depending on where you want the new column to be placed. 

3. 
Enter the column information. See Selecting the Column Type (on page 142). 

Move a Column to a New Location 

You can move columns to change the order in the report. 

To change the order of columns: 

1. 
On the Columns tab, locate the column you want to move and hover over the column 

number. 

2. 
In the drop-down list that appears, select the Move column left or Move column right 

option, depending on where you want the column to be in the report. 

3. 
Repeat moving columns as needed until you achieve the preferred order. 

Delete (Remove) a Column 

To remove a column permanently: 

1. 
On the Columns tab, locate the column you want to delete and hover over the column 

number. 

2. 
In the drop-down list that appears, select the Remove option. 

The system displays a remove confirmation box. 

3. 
Click the OK button to permanently delete the column. 

---

4. 
Repeat these steps for each column you want to remove. 

If necessary, you can always recreate the column by adding a new one later. 

Hide a Column 

The Hide column option lets you hide a column from your report output without removing it 

from the report. You can hide columns when you don’t need them to be displayed. For example, a 

column could contain a calculation that doesn’t need to be displayed, but whose calculations are 

critical to the report. Hiding a column, however, does not decrease the processing time for a 

financial report. 

To hide a column in a financial report: 

1. 
On the Columns tab, locate the column you want to hide and click anywhere in the column. 
The system displays the Hide column option only when the column is selected.

Scroll to the bottom of the page.

Select the Hide Column check box.

Creating a Custom Header 

The Financial Report Writer proposes default column headings, based on your column type and 

reporting period. 

a) Column heading 1: Provides predefined options for the period name. You can also choose 

to omit a heading (No title) or create a custom header. 

b) Column heading 2: Provides predefined options for the period date. You can also choose to 

omit a heading (No title) or create a custom header. 

c) Column title: Pre-filled with the column type (for example, Actual or Budget), but you can 

enter a different title of your choice. If you want to remove the column title entirely, leave 

the field blank. 

To create a custom header: 

1. 
In the Column heading 1 or Column heading 2 drop-down list, select the Custom header 

option. 

The system displays a blank text box under the heading field. 

2. 
In the blank text box, enter your own text, or your own text before or after one of the 

following variables: 

• 
Period_In_Word: Displays the last day of the period with the date spelled out, such as 

December 31, 2013 

• 
Date_Header_1: Displays the start of a date range, such as “12/01/2013 through” 

• 
Date_Header_2: Displays the current date (this is useful if you want to report on 

current month to date) 

• 
Period_Header_1: Displays the end of a reporting period in words, as in “Month 

Ending” or “Quarter Ending”

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

• 
Period_Header_2: Displays the last date of the reporting period in MM/DD/YYYY

#### Other Column Options
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 166*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide

Other Column Options 

Amount Type 

Every account group has a default method of calculating amounts on reports. For example, 

account groups that contain income or expense accounts are typically calculated “For the period” 

so that reports show the income or expense incurred during that reporting period. 

You can stick with the default amount type, or you can override this calculation method for a 

column in your report. If you’ve already set up an amount type for the rows in your report, the 

Apply rows tab settings option uses the amount type that you selected on the Rows tab. 

Show As 

Select a Show as option to change how a value is displayed. For example, you can display an 

Actual or Budget value as-is, using the Number option. You can also display it as an average over 

time. Additional options are available for computations. 

The options that you see in the drop-down list vary depending on the column type and other 

factors. 

• 
Number: Shows the value as a number. For example, 10,000. 

By default, a currency symbol isn’t displayed, except on totals and subtotal rows. However, 

you can use the Rows and totals options in the Format tab to show or hide currency 

symbols for particular rows. 

• 
Daily average, Weekly average, Monthly average, Quarterly average: For actual or budget 

amounts, displays the amount as an average for an amount of time. For example, if your 

reporting period is the current month, you can display the amount as a daily or weekly 

average. 

• 
Annualize by days, Annualize by months: Takes the amounts for the current year-to-date 

and extrapolates the period to an entire year. This allows you to see, for instance, what your 

estimated expenses would be for the year based on what you’ve spent so far. 

These appear only for columns where the reporting period is Current Year to Date.

Set up the column to show amounts for the current year-to-date.

This is a list of options for computed values: 

• 
Number: Shows the value as a number. For example, 10,000. By default, a currency symbol 

isn’t displayed, except on totals and subtotal rows. However, you can use the Rows and 

totals options in the Format tab to show or hide currency symbols for particular rows. 

• 
Amount with currency: Displays amounts with a currency symbol. In this case, the currency 

symbol is displayed for the entire column, even if the Rows and totals option in the Format 

tab is set to hide currency symbols for particular rows. 

• 
Ratio with decimals, Ratio without decimals: Displays the computed value as a ratio 

relative to 1, with or without decimals. Most often used when one value is divided by 

another value. For example, dividing 100 by 400 would result in a 1:4 ratio, which is 

displayed as 4. 

• 
Percent: Applies only to columns of type Computation on actual and Computation on 

budget. For computations that result from division, the result is converted to a percentage 

and displayed with a percent sign. For example, .25 is displayed as 25%. 

• 
Percentage - convert to %: Applies only to columns of type Summary on columns. 

Commonly used for computations that divide two columns, this option converts the result 

of the calculation to a percentage—for example, turning .25 into 25%. 

• 
Percentage - append % sign: Appends a percentage sign, without multiplying by 100 to 

convert to a percentage. For example, .25 is displayed as .25%. Although less commonly 

used, this option is available for columns of type Summary on columns and is the default 

option for period and budget variance columns (which are by definition already 

percentages).

Computations Tab

Computations`



> **Navigation Path:** `General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > Financial Reports > Edit > 
Computations`


The Computations tab lets you define calculations that you plan to use on the Columns tab of 

your financial report. You can add up to 20 calculations. 

In most cases, computations involve accounts or account groups. This topic shows how to 

calculate expenses as a percentage of total expenses by creating a computation that divides the 

amount in rows by the Expenses account group. 

Besides using the Computations tab, there are other ways to add computations to financial 

reports. 

• 
You can add computations to rows. To add a computation to a summary column, see 

Adding computations to rows (on page 140). 

• 
The Computations tab appears only if you selected Accounts as your report structure rather 

than segments or dimensions. However, all types of financial reports provide the option to 

add a summary column that computes a value from other columns, such as computing the 

average across a set of columns. 

How Computations Work 

To understand how computations work, consider a case in which you want to create an expense 

report that calculates your expenses as a percentage of total expenses. 

Column 3 is a computed column of the actual expenses (entries in column 2) divided by total 

expenses (total of column 2) to show percentages. 

To calculate this for your report, you would define a computation on the Computations tab, and 

then use it in the Columns tab. 

---

1. 
On the Computations tab, you define a computation that divides your expense account 

groups by your total expenses (represented by the account group called Expenses). 

• 
Use the drop-down menu at the top of the computation column to create a 

computation for the entire column (All groups). 

• 
You can also click the 
 Edit icon on a row to create a computation for a specific 

account group. 

2. 
On the Columns tab, you apply the computation to the report. 

The computation requires two columns, one that contains the actual amount and another 

column (of type “Compute on actual”) that applies the calculation to the actual column and 

displays the result. 

•

Select the computation you defined and the column to apply it to (column number).

Defining a Computation 

Use the Create computation page to define a computation that you plan to use on the Columns 

tab of your financial report. Learn more about how computations work. 

Defining a Computation 

A computation consists of three parts (account group, operation, and value) and is meant to be 

read from left to right. The following example illustrates the meaning of a computation that uses 

division to calculate amounts as a percentage of total expenses. 

a) This indicates whether the computation applies to the entire column or to a specific account 

group. 

---


<!-- Page 177 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

b) This is the selected operator that the system uses in the computation. 

c) This is the object of the operation. 

In this example, the computation applies to all columns in the report. It divides each account 

group amount by the total for the account group called Expenses. 

When to Create a Calculation for a Specific Group 

You can apply a computation to the entire column or to a specific account group. The 

Computations tab displays your account groups along the left side to give you the option of 

applying different calculations to the different account groups. 

Suppose that you were create an Income & Expense report. You might decide that Computation 1 

should apply a different calculation to income than to expenses. 

• 
For income account groups, you might divide income by headcount. 

• 
For expense account groups, you might divide expenses by total expenses to get the 

percentage spent on each type of expense. 

To define a computation: 

1. 
Verify the account group to which you are applying the computation. 

• 
To apply a calculation to all account groups in the report, open the Computation 

drop-down list at the top of the computation, and then select Set computations. 

• 
To apply a calculation to a specific account group, locate the account group in the 

Computations on groups column, and then click the Computation column. 

---


<!-- Page 178 -->
Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

The Create computation box opens. 

2. 
In the Create computation box, select the operation that you want to perform. You can 

choose from several predefined operations, such as Add, Subtract, Subtract from, Multiply, 

Divide, and Divide into. 

To understand what each operation does, keep in mind that the system applies the 

computation to the amounts in an actual or budget column that you select on the Columns 

tab. 

• 
Add: Takes the actual or budget amount and adds the value that you specify in the 

next step. 

• 
Subtract: Takes an actual or budget amount and subtracts the value that you specify in 

the next step. 

• 
Subtract from: Takes the value that you specify in the next step and subtracts the 

actual or budget amount. 

• 
Multiply: Takes an actual or budget amount and multiplies it by the value that you 

specify in the next step. 

• 
Divide: Takes an actual or budget amount and divides it by the value that you specify 

in the next step. 

• 
Divide into: Takes the value that you specify in the next step and divides it by the 

actual or budget amount. 

• 
Hide report cell: Hides amounts for the selected account group. For example, you 

might want to hide salary amounts or other sensitive information from a report. 
This option applies only to account groups that have not been expanded by dimension.

3. 
Use the Variable type and Variable value options to determine where the report should get 

the value to be used in the computation. 

If you select an account group or account, the value is determined dynamically based on the 

value for the account group or account for the reporting period selected on the Columns 

tab. 

• 
Account group: Sets the value to the total for an account group of your choice. 

• 
Account: Sets the value to the amount for an account of your choice. 

• 
Constant: Sets the value to a number that you specify, such as 100. 

For complex calcula
tions(on page 167 ) (such as x plus y, divided by z), you can use more 
than one computation in combination with hidden columns.

##### Filtering by Location, Department, or Other Dimension
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 180*

Reports

Filtering by Location, Department, or Other Dimension 

In addition to the default dimensions for departments and locations, your company may use 

other dimensions to track transactions. These dimensions let you filter reports in multiple ways; 

for instance, by showing data from only certain locations or customers. 

If you apply more than one filter, then the report will contain the subset of data that meets all of 

the filter criteria. For example, if you choose “Sales” as the department and “Arizona” as the 

location, then the report will include data only for the Sales department at the Arizona location. 

Filter for a Specific Dimension Member 

For any dimension that you’ve enabled, you can select an individual member to filter by. For 

example, you might filter a report for a specific location, department, or customer. 

To filter for a specific location, department, or other dimension member: 

1. 
Locate the dimension filter and select the option for Specific dimension/group. 

For example, to filter for a location, go to the Location drop-down list and choose the 

Specific location/group option. 

2. 
In the drop-down list that appears, select the dimension member by which you want to 

filter. 

• 
Using location as an example, choose the name of the location by which you want to 

filter. 

• 
The drop-down lists contain all available dimension groups, followed by individual 

dimension members, sorted alphabetically by ID. 

3. 
If you want the option to change the filter selection when you run the report, select the 

Prompt check box. 

4. 
When you expand rows or columns by department or location, the report automatically 

combines the data together in a single report. To generate a separate report for each 

department or location, select the Run as individual reports check box. 
When the report is generated as PDF, each individual report starts on a new page. In HTML and Excel, each department or location appears in a separate section.

5. 
To exclude inactive dimensions from reports that meet certain criteria, select the Hide 

Inactive check box. For example, you prevent departments or locations you are no longer 

using from appearing in columns or rows. 

6. 
If you want to generate the report to display only the transactions not associated with any 

dimension, select the Only blank check box. 

If you want a separate report for each department or location, learn more about creating 

individual reports. 

---

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Filter for Two or More Dimension Members Using Groups 

Use dimension groups if you want to filter for two or more dimensions. A dimension group is a 

name for particular set of members in a dimension, or a set of members that meet certain criteria. 

For example, you might create groups for: 

• 
A set of locations (such as your US locations) 

• 
Group by a certain type (such as Vendor type or Customer type) 

• 
Specific customers, customers located in a particular state, or even customers with the 

greatest open balance 

To filter for a dimension group or type: 

1. 
Locate the Define dimension filters in the list of dimensions, and then select the option for 

Specific dimension/group. 

For example, to filter by location, go to the Location drop-down list and choose Specific 

location/group. 

2. 
In the drop-down list that appears, select a dimension group or type, or click Add to create 

a new group on the fly. 

• 
If you’ve defined dimension groups (such as location groups or customer groups), 

these groups will appear first, before any specific dimension members. 

• 
To create a new group, click Add at the top of the drop-down list. 

3. 
If you want the option to change the filter selection when you run the report, select the 

Prompt check box. 

4. 
If you want to generate the report to display only the transactions not associated with any 

dimension, select the Only blank check box. 

Dimension Type 

Many dimensions can be tagged to types and groups. Customer types and vendor types can also 

have parent types for filtering. 

Categorize records according to type for filtering, sorting, and grouping opportunities. These 

types can take advantage of an additional layer of grouping by assigning a dimension type. If you 

assign a dimension type within your types, you can also get a native roll-up of any types assigned 

the dimension type during reporting. 

For example, if you set up the vendor types as Contractor and Subcontractor and make 

Contractor the parent type of Subcontractor—and then you filter financial reports using the 

Contractor vendor type—all vendors assigned to Contractor and Subcontractor will be included in 

the report. 

To filter for a dimension type:

Prompting for Filters at Runtime 

You can prompt users for selected filters when you run the report. 

While it’s typical to prompt users for the “As of date” for a report, it’s also common to prompt for 

the location, department, or other criteria. For example, instead of creating a balance sheet report 

that is always filtered for a particular location, you can use the Prompt option to enable users to 

choose a location or location group. 

How the Prompt Option Works 

If you select the Prompt check box for a segment, the system asks for this information when you 

run the report. The user who runs the report chooses the account group or segment structure to 

filter by. 

By choosing to prompt at runtime, you can set up one report and use it multiple ways, such as 

setting up a balance sheet report and then running it for different locations on the fly. 

If you select specific segment filters and also select the Prompt check box, then the system 

automatically fills in the report prompt with your selections. However, you can override the filters. 

Example: Prompting for G/L Account Groups or Reporting Periods 

You can dynamically run financial reports on a G/L account group other than what the report was 

originally set up for (account groups are defined (on page 130) on the Rows tab of the Financial 

report writer). To do this, enable the Prompt for G/L account groups option in the financial 

report. This allows you to choose an alternate G/L account group when you run the report rather 

than duplicating a report and changing the account group(s). 

Additionally, you can enable the Prompt for reporting periods check box to dynamically run 

financial reports for a reporting period, column heading, and expand by. Columns for Actual, 

Budget, Remaining budget, Open commitments, and Pending commitments appear in the 

prompt.

##### Using Dimension Groups to Specify Order in Rows and Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 185*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Using Dimension Groups to Specify Order in Rows and Columns 

In financial reports, you can expand rows or columns by dimension. For example, you can expand 

an actual column into several columns by location, department, or other dimension. 

To control the order of members in rows or columns: 

Workflow 

1. 
Create a dimension group that contains the desired members. 

In the dimension group, order the members as you want them to be listed in reports. 

2. 
Filter the report by the dimension group. 

How Location and Department Filters Work 

When you make selections for Department and Location, the following rules apply: 

• 
The calculations are based on the combination of the specified department and location. 

For example, if you chose the Manufacturing department and the California location, the 

calculations are based on numbers only for Manufacturing departments that are also 

located in California. 

• 
All children of parent departments and locations are included in the calculations. 

• 
If you created a department hierarchy using a parent/child relationship, you can report on 

the parent department or the individual child department by selecting the department 

name from the drop-down list. If you choose a parent department, the system retrieves all 

the information from the child departments assigned to that parent and displays the 

information with that of the parent as a rolled-up total. 

• 
If you are a multi-entity shared user of the ownership financials and distribution feature, you 

can select a location only if the owner you select in the Report on owner field has some 

percentage ownership in the entity under which the location falls. 

---



##### Best Practices
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 186*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Best Practices 

When you generate a report, the data that’s included is based on what you add to your rows and 

columns, and any filters that you apply. 

• 
All financial reports include account groups, which indicate which accounting data should 

be included in the report. For example, a balance sheet might include account groups for 

“Assets” and “Liabilities & Equity.” These account groups can include filters in their 

definitions, although this is not recommended in most cases. 

• 
Financial reports can also include segment structures that represent a set of segment data 

that you want to include on rows and columns. For example, you might want your rows or 

columns to include selected departments, customers by type, or items by product line. By 

nature, these segment structures limit the data to be displayed in the report. 

• 
Additionally, you can apply report-level filters on the Filters tab. For example, you might 

filter a report for a particular location or a location group that includes a specific set of 

locations. 

• 
In general, filters that you add to the Filters tab and filters on account groups are applied 

first, followed by any other filtering. For maximum flexibility, it’s recommended that you 

don’t use account group filters. 

Best Practices for Filtering 

When defining reports, it’s best to keep your approach simple to avoid situations in which there’s 

a conflict between the data on rows and columns and any filtering you’ve applied. 

• 
Avoid adding filters to your account group definitions. Although you can define filters for an 
account group—for example, filtering a Cost of Goods Sold account group for a particular 
location—it’s recommended that you don’t add any filters to account groups. Instead of 
filtering your account groups: 

• 
Define your account groups without filters. 

• 
On a report-by-report basis, use the options available in the Financial Report Writer to 
select the data you want to see. 

• 
When filtering for a specific set of members (or members that meet certain criteria), define 
your filters in only one place. In general, avoid situations in which you select one set of 
segment data on rows and columns, and then set a report-level filter that includes a 
different set of data. Instead, do either of the following: 

• 
Apply filters on the Filters tab. To filter the entire report for a specific set of segment 
data, you can select one or more segment groups on the Filters tab. For example, you 
might filter a report for “West Coast locations.” 

• 
Select and filter data on the Rows and Columns tabs. On each tab, you can select the 
data you want to see in your rows and columns. Depending on the type of report you 
are creating, different options will be available. For example, you could add Cost of 
Goods sold to your report rows and then create columns that compare by different 
locations.

##### Showing and Hiding Zero Balance Rows and Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 190*

Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Showing and Hiding Zero Balance Rows and Columns 

The zero number options let you adjust how zero balance rows and columns are handled in the 

report. 

By default: 

• 
Sections of a report are hidden if the total or subtotal is zero and all detail rows are also 

zero. 

Regardless of the options you select for the Numbers field, the logic for including a section 

in a report is as follows: 

• 
If all rows for a section are zero, the section is hidden. For example, suppose that you 

didn’t have any charitable contributions for the reporting periods shown in a report. In 

this case, the Charitable Contributions section would be hidden. 

• 
If the total for a section is zero, but it contains some detail rows that have a balance, 

the section is included in the report. For example, a Headcount section would appear if 

there was a total of 0 headcount growth, but there was +2 headcount for one 

department and -2 headcount for another department. 

• 
Detail rows with a zero balance are hidden unless you select the option to Display zero 

balance with activity. 

• 
Columns of a report are displayed even if the total and detail rows are zero unless you clear 

the Display zero balance columns option. 

• 
Calculations are displayed by default, even if the result is 0.00, unless you select the Do not 

display zero value calculation option. 

Zero Numbers Options 

• 
Display zero balance with activity: Shows detail rows that have zero balances as long as 

there were transactions posted during the reporting period. 
This is a report-wide setting. However, you can use the 
Always displayoption on the 
Rows
tab to selectspecific sections where you want to display the total and all detail rows, even if the amount is zero.

• 
Display zero for future periods: Shows zero amounts for any column where the reporting 

period is in the future. 

This feature is useful if your report is set up for 12 months, but you only want to see actual 

amounts for the past and current periods, even if there are future transactions. If, for 

example, you have a report set up with columns for every month of the year and you run 

the report as of June 30, then even though your columns contain actual amounts, you can 

see numbers for future dates, such as for the Month Ended July. However, you can select 

this check box to zero all future numbers and clean up your report. 
This applies to actuals only.

---


<!-- Page 191 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

• 
Display zero balance columns: Clearing this option automatically hides any columns that 

have only zero amounts. This can be particularly useful if you sometimes compare report 

data by time period or segment and you want to automatically hide any columns that don’t 

have data. 

• 
Do not display zero value calculation: Select this option to exclude zero-value calculations 

(0.00) in the report. This setting affects the Computation on actual and Computation on 

budget column types. 

Departments, Locations, and Other Segments 

The options for segments allow you to control how departments, locations, and other segments 

are listed in rows and columns. These options apply in either of the following situations: 

• 
If you change the detail level for rows to show segment detail 

• 
If you expand columns by segment or segment structure 

For example, you might expand an actual column so that it is split into multiple columns by 

location. 

The following lists the segment options. 

• 
Show departments: Choose whether to display departments by name only, by ID only, or by 

name and ID. 

• 
Show locations: Choose whether to display locations by name only, by ID only, or by name 

and ID. 

• 
Show other: Choose whether to display other segments by name only, by ID only, or by 

name and ID. 

• 
Sorting (alphabetically sort Department or Location Group): If you filter the report by a 

department or location group, the report automatically displays departments and locations 

in the order in which they are defined in the group. Select this option if you prefer to sort 

departments and locations alphabetically. 
If you don’t filter by a segment or location group, the report will always display 
departments and locations in alphabetical order.

Defining Report Headers and Footers 

Page Header 

By default, printed reports start with your company name, followed by the report title, and a 

subtitle that spells out the report’s “As of date” in words. Using the options in the Page header 

and Page footer sections, you have the option to: 

• 
Change the report title. 

• 
Include additional lines of header text and optionally change how and where the date is 

displayed. 

• 
Include your company logo in the header. 

• 
Include footer text, including dynamic information that specifies the page number and 

date/time when the report was printed. 

The list describes the header information that is included when the report is displayed in printable 

(PDF) format. As noted in the table, some header elements (such as the report title) also appear 

when the report is displayed in Excel or HTML format. 

• 
Logo options (displayed in PDF): Include your logo at the top of the report, aligned to the 

left, top, or center. 
If you have not uploaded your logo, you can do so on the Company informationpage. See 
Adding and Editing General Information for instructions.

• 
Report title (displayed in PDF, HTML, Excel): Enter the title you want to display on the 

report. By default, the report uses the report name that you entered in the Report Info tab 

as the title. 

• 
Subtitle 1 and Subtitle 2 (displayed in PDF, Excel): For all new reports, Subtitle 1 displays as 

As of [As_of_Date_in_Word]. This displays the words “As of” followed by the date spelled 

out in words (as in “March 31, 2012”). You can enter your own text in either Subtitle 1 or 

Subtitle 2, and you can use the following variables to dynamically include the date either 

spelled out in words or numerically. 

• 
[As_of_Date_in_Word] 

• 
[As_of_Date] 

• 
Title comment (displayed in PDF HTML, Excel): Enter an optional comment that will display 

aligned left, above the report body. 

• 
Company title: Display departments/locations as company title on individual reports 

(displayed in PDF). By default, your company name (as entered in the Company information 

page) is displayed at the top of the page header of printed reports and reports exported to 

Excel. However, if you’re splitting a report that compares data by department or location 

into multiple individual reports, you can choose to display the department or location name 

in the report title instead of the company name. This option applies only if you created 

individual reports by department or location.

Setting Other Options 

Page Settings 

By default, your report is set up to print in Portrait orientation on letter-size paper. The system 

will determine where columns break across pages, and the report may be more than one page 

wide. However, you can choose other options that allow you to control how the report prints 

across pages. 

The choices you make in the Page settings section determine how much control you have over the 

printed page. 

• 
Default page settings: This is the default setting. If you select this option, column size and 

breaks are determined automatically. However, you can change the report from Portrait 

orientation to Landscape to fit more columns across the page. 

• 
Fit to x page(s) wide: Select this option if you want to specify how many pages wide the 

report should be (for example, fitting it to one page wide), but still have the column width 

set automatically. 

• 
Page orientation: By default, pages are set to Portrait. Select Landscape from the 

drop-down list to change the orientation of the report pages. 

• 
Measurements: If you select Custom page size you can choose to see the measurements 

for margins and column widths as points or inches. 

• 
Custom page size, column widths, and column breaks: Select this option if you want more 

control over the printed report, including the ability to select a different page size, set 

column widths, and set the page margins. 

Column Options and Fonts 

You can use the Column options, breaks, and fonts section to control the look of particular 

columns on reports. Available options depend on your page settings selection. Some options 

apply only when the report is output as a PDF. 

• 
Hide filter details on column titles: Hide the details of filtered columns, such as the account 

group and segment structure display on the column header. This option applies to all 

outputs. It allows user to use the column filter to preset the column data without showing 

all details on the report presentation of column header. to hide column filter such as 

account group and segment structure display on the column header. This option applies to 

all outputs. It allows user to use the column filter to pre-set the column data without 

showing all details on the report presentation of column header. 

• 
Repeat segment name/ID as 1st column on reports more than 1 page wide: When a report 

is more than one page wide, enable this feature to ensure that the first column is repeated 

on each page, making it easier to follow the column information.

#### Format Tab FAQs

Format Tab FAQs 

How do I control the width of the report? 

The width of the report is affected by the number of columns in the report, and the font sizes you 

selected. If you want to control how many pages wide your report is, you can have the system fit 

the report to a certain number of pages wide, or you can use column breaks to select how many 

columns are on each page. You can also fit more columns on a page by switching to landscape 

orientation. 

To control the width of the report, perform one of the following options: 

Fit the report to one page wide (or a selected number of pages). 

1. 
In the Page Settings section, select the Fit to x pages wide option. 

2. 
Specify how many pages wide the report should be. 

Select where page breaks fall. 

1. 
In the Page Settings section, set the custom page size, column breaks, margins, and column 

specific fonts. 

2. 
In the Column Options, Breaks, and Fonts section, locate the column after which you want 

the first column break. Any remaining columns will appear on the next page. 

If your report is more than two pages wide, set additional column breaks as needed. 

Set page orientation to landscape. 

• 
In the Page Settings section, select the Landscape option as the page orientation. 

How do I control page breaks? 

You can control where page breaks are in the report by inserting a page break at the end of a 

certain section. 

To insert a page break after a specific section: 

1. 
Go to the Rows section of the Format tab. 

2. 
Locate the section after which you want a page break. For example, if you want a page 

break after your Fixed Assets group, locate the row for that group. 

3. 
In the Row formatting column, select the check box for Page Break After.

Permissions Tab 

The Permissions tab identifies the report owner and specifies who can and can’t access this 

report. Users who don’t have access to a report won’t see it in the Financial reports list page, and 

it won’t appear in their Reports Center or dashboards. 

Assigning Report Access 

Depending on how your General Ledger was set up, the default permissions to financial reports 

may either grant or deny access to all users (the group called Group/Everyone). For example, if 

the default access privileges for financial reports are set up to deny access, you can selectively 

give access to users or user groups by adding them to the Access list. 

When a user or group is added to the Access list, even though the Exclusion list is set to 

Group/Everyone, the Access list takes precedence and any user or group specifically included in 

the Access list is granted access to the report. 

If access is granted to Group/Everyone but one user is added to the Exclusion list (even if that 

user is part of a group given access), that user can’t access the report. 

To set the report owner and permissions: 

1. 
If necessary, select the person who is responsible for the report as Report owner. 

By default, the person who creates the report is the report owner. However, if the report will 

be maintained by someone else, you can select that user from the list. 

2. 
Set permissions for the report by reviewing the Access list and Exclusion list. 

• 
To add a user or user group to either list, click the Add button. 

• 
To remove a user or user group from either list, select the user or group and click the 

Remove button. 

In addition to adding individual users, you can select groups of users. Learn more about adding 

user groups. 

Selecting Default Permissions 

A preference in the General Ledger determines whether financial reports are available to everyone 

by default. 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to General Ledger > Setup > Configuration.`


2. 
Scroll down to the Financial reports section and locate the option to Set default 

permissions to public.

Next Steps Tab 

When you’ve finished designing your report, it’s time to start using it. 

Although you can always run your report by going to the Financial reports list page or by going 

to the Reports Center, you can do more to highlight and use your report. 

Adding a Report to a Dashboard 

Dashboards give you an at-a-glance view of the areas of your business that matter most to you. 

From the Next steps tab, you quickly add your financial report as a component on any dashboard 

that you own. 

To use the Next steps tab to add the financial report to a dashboard: 

1. 
Click the Add this report to a dashboard link. 

2. 
Select the dashboard, give it a name and location, and enter other details as needed. 

Learn more about the options for report components. 
If you see a message that you don’t have any dashboards that yo
u can add components to, but you know that you have dashboards, you probably aren’t the owner of those dashboards. In this 
case, you can still edit the dashboard from the Dashboardslist and then add the component.

Can I add this report to someone else’s dashboard? 

Yes, you can add this report to any dashboard that you can see on the Dashboards list, provided 

that you have permissions to edit dashboards. However, if you’re not the owner of the dashboard, 

you’ll need access the dashboard from the Dashboards list to add the component. 

Learn more about adding a component to a dashboard. 

Scheduling a Report 

You can schedule a report to run automatically on a recurring basis, such as weekly or monthly. 

When you schedule the report, you can set it up to be delivered by email or stored. 

To schedule a report from the Financial Report Writer: 

1. 
On the Next steps tab, click Schedule this report to run periodically. 

2. 
When prompted, click the Save and schedule button to save the report and proceed. 

3. 
On the Schedule financial report page, set up a schedule for the report and select how you 

want it to be delivered. 

Learn more about the options for scheduling a report (on page 99). 

In addition to having the report emailed to you, you can also have it stored. Learn how to access 

stored reports in the Reports Center.

Adding a Report to a Report Group 

A report group provides an efficient and quick way to act upon multiple reports simultaneously. 

For example, instead of having to run or schedule a set of reports one at a time, you can run a 

report group, which runs all member reports immediately or according to schedule. 

To include the report in a report group: 

1. 
On the Next steps tab, click Include this report in a report group. 

2. 
When prompted, click the Save and continue button to save the report and proceed to the 

Report groups list page. 

• 
To add the report to an existing report group, click the Edit link for the report group. 

Then add the report as a member. 

• 
If you don’t have any report groups, you can add one from the Report groups list.

Groups.

Adding Budget Variance Analysis Notes to a Financial Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reports > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Reports > Edit`


If you want to see the budget variance analysis (BVA) notes in a financial report, then you can add 

it to the report as a column. 

To add the BVA notes column to a custom financial report: 

1. 
In the Financial reports list, click the Edit link next to the desired financial report. The 

Financial report writer opens. 

2. 
Click the Columns tab. 

3. 
Find where you want to insert the new column, and then click the drop-down arrow of the 

Column heading to display its submenu. 

4. 
Select Add column left or Add column right. The new column appears to the left or right of 

the selected column. 

5. 
In the Column type field, find the Budget section, and then select the Budget variance 

notes option. 
For information about column types, see Column types in online help or download the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide.

---


<!-- Page 204 -->
Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

6. 
Select the Include variance amount, date, and user check box to display this information in 

the BVA note in the financial report. 

7. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the desired reporting period to include. 
For information about reporting periods, see Reporting periods in online help or download the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide
.

8. 
If you selected a “Year to Date” reporting period, then you can select the Include prior 

period notes check box to include budget variance notes from a previous reporting period. 

For example, if you select this option and you run the report on March 31, then the report 

will display notes for January, February, and March. If you do not select this option and you 

run the report on March 31, then the report will display only YTD notes for March. 

9. 
In the Column heading 1 field, click the drop-down arrow to select a heading from the list. 
If the heading you want to use is not listed, select the Custom header option. A field is 
displayed that allows you to type a custom column heading. Click  Helpfor information 
about the column header.

10. 
In the Column heading 2 field, click the drop-down arrow to select a heading from the list. 
If the heading that you want to use is not listed, select the Custom header option. A field 
is displayed that allows you to type a custom column heading.

11. 
In the Column title field, the column header is pre-populated with the information in the 

Column type field. 

12. 
You can set the Expand by drop-down list to Location or Time period as needed. 

13. 
Select the Hide column check box when you want to hide this column from the financial 

report. 

14. 
When you run the report, the notes made during the budget variance analysis process 

appear in the column that you added, including the variance amount when the note was 

entered, the date the note was entered, and which user entered it.

KPIs in Financial Report Writer 

You can use the Financial Report Writer to enhance the way you look at financial data along with 

operational metrics. The Financial Report Writer can pull real-time metrics of your company’s 

financial and operation KPIs. For example, if you want to know capital expense for each unit 

(vacant units), you can display this by selecting predefined KPI groups in the Financial Report 

Writer. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use KPIs in financial reports. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Entity MR Codes 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

Key Performance Indicators 
List, View, Run/Add, Edit, Delete, 

Lock/Unlock 

KPI Setup 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

Financial Graphs 

Graphs help you visualize trends in your business, telling a story that goes beyond the numbers 

on a page. In addition to standard graphs that are included with applications, you can create any 

number of financial graphs. The graphs you create can be displayed on their own or added to a 

dashboard. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use financial graphs. 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

General Ledger 
Graphs and Performance Cards 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

General Ledger 
Financials 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

Graph Editor Controls 

Controls on the left help you design your graph. The right side is reserved for a graph preview, 

which shows what your graph looks like using your actual data. 

a) Use controls to select the graph data. 

b) Preview shows actual data results. 

c) Click Refresh to start or refresh. 

d) Icons let you switch graph types at any time.

<!-- Page 237 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Preview and Refresh 

When you first create a graph, the preview is empty. Enter some basic graph information, and 

then click Refresh to start seeing the preview. 
To see a preview, enter at least a Name and fill in any required fields in 
Additional parameters. 
Then click the Refresh button above the preview.

As you make changes, make sure to refresh again to see the latest updates. 

To create a financial graph: 

1. 
Enter a Name for the graph. 

2. 
Select the data you want to see in your graph. 

The data displayed by your graph is a combination of the data series (on page 231) you use 

to categorize values (for example, your columns or pie chart slices) and the accounting data 

you specify in Additional parameters. All graphs have at least a Primary data series. 

For some graph types, you can optionally include a Compare data series. 

---


<!-- Page 238 -->
Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Any data that isn’t selected as a data series is specified as Additional parameters. In the 

example above, reporting period is a data series but the main data that is being shown—in 

this case, revenue—is determined by the account group selected in Additional parameters. 

3. 
Select a graph type by clicking the corresponding icon. 

• 
The currently selected graph type appears in color. 

• 
Column graph is the default, but other graph types include pie, doughnut, line, 

column, bar, area, and waterfall. 

• 
Hover over an icon to see name of the graph type. If the graph can be displayed only 

on-screen, “(HTML only)” is appended to the name, as in “Stacked column (HTML 

only).” 

4. 
Use Additional settings to refine your output. 

• 
Title, subtitle, and comment apply to PDF output only. 

• 
In most cases, you’ll want to leave the As of date blank to automatically use the 

current date, at the time the graph is displayed. You can override the date when the 

graph is viewed to see data from different time periods. 

• 
Select Hide zero numbers to remove data points that have no value. For example, if 

your graph compares revenue by customer, select this option to remove data points 

for customers with no associated revenue during the reporting period. 

5. 
Click to expand the Filters section and filter your report as needed. 

Filtering lets you select data based on segment, such as by location or department. You can: 

• 
Filter for a single segment member, such as a particular location. 

• 
Filter for multiple segment members, such as for a group of locations or a particular 

customer type.

##### Selecting Data for Financial Graphs
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 239*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Selecting Data for Financial Graphs 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reporting > 
 Financial Graphs`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > 
 Financial 
Graphs`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > 
 Financial Graphs`


When you create a financial graph, your choices for data series represent how you want to 

categorize the data. For example, a revenue graph can be broken down in multiple ways, such as 

by quarter, location, or customer. 

Primary vs. Compare Data Series 

Think of the Primary data series as the main way you want to categorize values, such as by 

reporting period, account group, segment, or segment structure (waterfall charts only). 

For some types of graphs, you have the option of showing a comparison within the primary data 

series. A Compare data series is available for all chart types except pie, doughnut, and waterfall. 

---


<!-- Page 240 -->
Reports 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Data Series Options 

The way that data are displayed depends on the graph type. 

• 
Account groups: Categorizes data by one or more account groups. Example: Revenue vs. 

expense. 

• 
Reporting periods: Categorizes data by one or more reporting periods. Example: Four 

consecutive quarters. Although you can select individual reporting periods by moving them 

from Available to Selected, the quickest way to create a trend over time is to use the Period 

comparison options. 

• 
Budget comparison: Lets you compare Actual values against one or more budgets. 
This option is not available for pie, doughnut, or waterfall graphs.

• 
Dimension: Categorizes data by the selected dimension. By default, the graph shows all 

members of each dimension. However, you can filter on a dimension group to show a 

subset of members. For example, suppose that you choose Locations as a data series. 

• 
By default, the graph shows all locations. 

• 
To restrict the list of locations, expand the Filters section. From the Location 

drop-down list, select a dimension group that represents the locations you want to 

include. 

• 
Dimension structure: In waterfall charts, categorizes data based on the substructures in a 

hierarchical dimension structure. 
This option is available only for waterfall graphs.Selecting a dimension structure, rather than a dimension, gives you the freedom to create intermediate columns based on how you want to organize and label the data.

Creating a Pie or Doughnut Chart

Use this graph to show values as a percentage of a whole. For example, you might want to show 

the portion of revenue derived from different items, customers, or locations. 

To create a pie or doughnut graph: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then click the 
 Add button next to Financial 

Graphs. 

2. 
Type a name for the graph. 

Filling In the Primary Data Series Section 

Select how you want to categorize the pie or doughnut slices. 

Use the first drop-down list to select the type of data series. The options for both series are the 

same, except that Compare data series can be set to None. 

Filling In the Additional Parameters Section 

1. 
Fill in the remaining required data. For example, if your primary data series is account 

groups, use the additional parameters to select your reporting period. 

2. 
Set the graph type by clicking the desired Pie or Doughnut icon.

A waterfall graph helps you understand how an initial value is impacted by a series of 

intermediate positive or negative values. 

A waterfall graph: 

• 
Captures a beginning and an end. The first and last columns depict a beginning and total 

value. 

• 
Tells the story in-between. Intermediary columns explain the increases and decreases that 

led to the total. For example, the following waterfall chart shows the contribution to revenue 

from different account groups. 

To create a waterfall graph:

Open the General Ledger menu.

Click the 
 Add button next to Financial Graphs.

Type a name for the graph.

To configure the Reporting Portal: 

1. 
In the Send email notifications field, select when to notify the owner that a new document 

has been uploaded into their owner portal: 

•

•

to upload documents to.

your business needs: 

• 
In the Language drop-down list, select the language used in your company. 

• 
In the Singular name field, type the new term in singular form.  

• 
In the Plural name field, type the new term in plural form. 

4. 
Click Save to save the configuration.

Cover Letters 

See the How to Get Here (on page 252) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

A cover letter is a document you can include in a group of reports. When you send the group of 

reports, you can use the cover letter to introduce the reports and describe what information they 

contain. In RealPage Accounting, you can create a cover letter and include it in a memorized 

report group. 

For example, you can use a cover letter to introduce a package of reports sent to a client. 

The Cover letters page displays a list of default and custom cover letters available in your 

company. From this page, you can add, edit, view, and delete cover letters, or export the list of 

cover letters. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with cover letters: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Cover Letters 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

1.

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
In the More section, select Cover letters. 

Creating a Cover Letter Template 

To add a cover letter, you must first create a cover letter template. The cover letter template 

contains the text of your cover letter, and you create it using Microsoft Word. 

When you create your cover letter template, you can use merge fields in place of 

company-specific information, such as the company name, address, and reporting period dates. 

Using merge fields makes the template reusable and dynamic. When your memorized report 

group runs, it replaces the merge fields with the actual names, descriptions, and other specific 

information from your company or entity. For example, if you are an accountant, using merge 

fields for the company name and other company-specific information allows you to reuse the 

cover letter template for multiple client companies. 

For descriptions of the different merge fields, see Merge fields for cover letters (on page 254). 

To create a cover letter template: 

1. 
Create a new document in Microsoft Word, and then write your cover letter template. 

2. 
For company-specific information in your cover letter template, substitute the 

corresponding merge field. You can copy and paste merge fields. See the list of merge fields 

(on page 254). 

3. 
Save the cover letter template. 

---



##### Merge Fields for Cover Letters
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 262*

More 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide

Merge Fields for Cover Letters 

When you create your cover letter template, you will use merge fields in place of 

company-specific information, such as the company name, address, and reporting period dates. 

Using merge fields makes the template reusable and dynamic. When your memorized report 

group runs, it replaces the merge fields with the actual names, descriptions, and other specific 

information from your company or entity. For example, if you are an accountant, using merge 

fields for the company name and other company-specific information allows you to reuse the 

cover letter template for multiple client companies. 

The following lists the available merge fields you can use when creating cover letters: 

«CL_NAME»: Name of the cover letter template 

«CL_DESCRIPTION»: Description of the cover letter template 

«CL_ISDEFAULT»: Indicates that the cover letter template is the default 

«CL_COMPANY_TITLE»: The company ID that you enter when you sign in. 
For multi-entity shared companies, if you run the memorized report group at the entity level, the 
Company ID data merge fields willdisplay entity information instead of top-level company 
information.

«CL_COMPANY_NAME»: The name of the company 

«CL_COMPANY_COUNTRY»: The country for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALNAME»: The legal name of the company 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALCOUNTRY»: The country for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_FEDERALID»: The Federal ID for the company 

«CL_COMPANY_CONTACTNAME»: The contact name for the company 

«CL_COMPANY_CONTACTPHONE»: The contact phone number for the company 

«CL_COMPANY_CONTACTEMAIL»: The contact email address for the company 

«CL_COMPANY_ADDRESS1»: The first line for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_ADDRESS2»: The second line for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_CITY»: The city name for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_STATE»: The state or province name for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALADDRESS1»: The first line for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALADDRESS2»: The second line for the company’s legal address 

---

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALCITY»: The city name for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALSTATE»: The state or province name for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_ZIPCODE»: The ZIP CODE or postal code for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALZIPCODE»: The ZIP CODE or postal code for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_FAX»: The fax number for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_COUNTRYCODE»: The country code for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALCOUNTRYCODE»: The country code for the company’s legal address 

«CL_MRG_NAME»: The name for the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_DESCRIPTION»: The description for the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_MEMBERS»: The member reports for the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_COVERLETTER»: The cover letter name for the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_PUBLICFLAG»: Indicates that the memorized report group is publicly available 

(available to other users who have permission to the memorize report groups feature)

«CL_MRG_ASOFDATE»: As of date for the memorized report group 

«CL_RPI_NAME»: Name of the reporting period

Ended” 

«CL_RPI_HEADER2»: The second line (Column Header 2) shown on the report. Example: 

“September 30, 2000” 

«CL_RPI_START_DATE»: The beginning date of the reporting period 

«CL_RPI_END_DATE»: The ending date of the reporting period 

«CL_RPI_BUDGETING»: Indicates that this reporting is displayed in the list of available reporting 

periods on the budgets page for inclusion in a budget 

«CL_RPI_STATUS»: The status of the reporting period (active or inactive)

Report Groups List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 260) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

A report group provides an efficient and quick way to act upon multiple reports simultaneously. 

For example, instead of having to run or schedule a set of reports one at a time, you can run a 

report group, which runs all of the member reports immediately or according to schedule. 

You can use the Report groups list to: 

• 
Add, edit, view, and delete report group information. 

• 
Run a report group on demand. 

• 
Schedule a date and time you want to run a report group. 

• 
View stored reports associated with a report group. 

• 
View the status of a scheduled report group, including a log of executions and errors.  
Report groups that are public are available to any user with permissions to memorized report groups. If a report group is private, you can edit or run the report group only if you are the report owner or if you have full or limited administrator privileges.

##### Adding a Report Group

Adding a Report Group 

Report Groups > Add 

See the How to Get Here (on page 260) topic for a list of ways to access the Report Groups list. 

To create a report group, fill in the report group information, add reports to the group, and set up 

any default parameters you want to apply to the report group at large. 

Filling In the Report Group Details 

1. 
Type a Name and Description for the report group. Names should contain letters and 

numbers and can contain single spaces or dashes. Do not use special characters in report 

group names. 
You can’t change the report group 
name after you’ve saved it.

2. 
If you want to use a cover letter for the group, then select a Cover letter from the 

drop-down list and set a Cover letter reporting period. 

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to ask the user to select a reporting period at runtime. 

4. 
If you want the reports in this group to be numbered continuously, select the Sequential 

page numbering check box. For example, if the first report ends on page 3, then the next 

report starts on page 4, and so on for all of the reports in the group. 

5. 
To make this report group available to other users who have permission to the memorized 

report groups feature, select the Public check box. 

6. 
You can add text to the footer that overrides any footer set in a group member. If you enter 

no footer here, then each report defaults to its own footer, if any. A footer can include up to 

400 characters. 

7. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to allow the user to create the footer text at runtime. 
By default, the user who creates the report group is listed as the Report owner. The 
report group can be edited and used by the report owner and any users with limited or full administrator privileges. If you mark the report group as Public, the report group is also 
available to other users who have permission to memorized report groups.

8. 
In the Members list, click the Member drop-down line item, and then select a report to add 

to the group. Select all reports in the listed report groups to help you create complete 

owner reports in RealPage Accounting. 
OneSite reports are the last reports in the report output regardless of the order defined in the Members list.

---


<!-- Page 270 -->
More 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up Default Parameters (Optional) 

You can set up default parameters to save time when running or scheduling the report group. The 

system will automatically populate these parameters each time you run or schedule the report 

group; however, you can manually change the fields as needed. 

In the Default parameters section: 

1. 
In the As of date field, type the starting date from which to run the report.  
If you leave this field blank, then it will default to today’s date.

2. 
In the Location/group drop-down list, select a specific location or location group for which 

you want to run the report. 
Report groups with Bank Reconciliation, Bank Reconciliation with Attachments
, Bank 
Reconciliation Outstanding Items, Bank Reconciliation Adjusted Items
, Delinquent and Prepaids
, Security Deposits, and Rent Roll reports can be run on a location group and will generate 
individual reports per location.

3. 
Select the Grouped by location/entity check box if you want to group the report data by 

location or entity. 

• 
Upon selecting the Grouped by location/entity check box, you are presented with the 

option to create a separate file per location. Select the Separate file per 

location/entity check box. 

• 
If the Separate file per location/entity check box is not enabled, the system creates 

the report group for each location and combines all reports into one file. 

4. 
If either the Delinquent and Prepaid or Security Deposits report is a member of the report 

group, then you can define separate account groups for these reports when running the 

report group: 

• 
Account group for delinquent and prepaid: Select an account group from the 

drop-down list for the Delinquent and Prepaid report. This corresponds with the AR - 

Multifamily report in the General Ledger. 

• 
Account group for security deposits: Select an account group from the drop-down 

list for the Security Deposits report. This corresponds with the Security Deposits - 

Multifamily report in the General Ledger. 

If you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use.

##### Running a Report Group On Demand
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 272*

More 

RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide
