Running a Report Group On Demand 

Report Groups > Run 

See the How to Get Here (on page 260) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can run a report group on demand instead of waiting for the report’s scheduled run time. 

Depending on the report group, certain conditions may apply: 

• 
If you run a report group with A/P Invoice Packages, the packages will include all invoices 

for the month (with attachments). 

• 
If you run a report group with Leasing & Rents reports or Bank Reconciliations on a location 

group, then the reports will be run as individual reports. 

• 
If you run a report group with Bank Reconciliations, then you will need to specify a location. 

If you have chosen to include Bank Reconciliations and you do not specify a location when 

running or scheduling the report, then the Bank Reconciliations will not be included in the 

report output. 

• 
If you run a report group with OneSite reports, the OneSite reports will be the last reports in 

the report group, regardless of the order defined in the Members list. 

• 
If you run a report group containing the Job Cost Open Invoices or Job Setup Summary 

report on a location group, then the report will include jobs for all locations in the location 

group. 

Getting Started 

To run a report group on demand: 

• 
On the Reports groups page, click the Run link next to the report group you want to run. 

The Storage options page opens. 

Setting the Report Group Parameters 

In the Run this report section, set the parameters on which to run the report group. If you set up 

any default parameters for the report, these fields will populate automatically; however, you can 

override them as needed. 

1. 
In the As of date field, type the starting date from which to run the report.  
If you leave this field blank, then it will default to today’s date.

2. 
In the Location/group drop-down list, select a specific location or location group for which 

you want to run the report. 
Report groups with Bank Reconciliation, Bank Reconciliation with Attachments
, Bank 
Reconciliation Outstanding Items, Bank Reconciliation Adju
sted Items, Delinquent and Prepaids
, Security Deposits, and Rent Roll reports can be run on a location group and will generate 
individual reports per location.

3. 
Select the Grouped by location/entity check box if you want to group the report data by 

location or entity. 

• 
Upon selecting the Grouped by location/entity check box, you are presented with the 

option to create a separate file per location. Select the Separate file per 

location/entity check box. 

• 
If the Separate file per location/entity check box is not enabled, the system creates 

the report group for each location and combines all reports into one file. 

4. 
If either the Delinquent and Prepaid or Security Deposits report is a member of the report 

group, then you can define separate account groups for these reports when running the 

report group: 

• 
Account group for delinquent and prepaid: Select an account group from the 

drop-down list for the Delinquent and Prepaid report. This corresponds with the AR - 

Multifamily report in the General Ledger. 

• 
Account group for security deposits: Select an account group from the drop-down 

list for the Security Deposits report. This corresponds with the Security Deposits - 

Multifamily report in the General Ledger. 

If you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use.

If a OneSite Leasing & Rents report is a member of the report group, then the Fiscal period 

field appears. Select a fiscal period for the report group:

Current AR period: Runs the report group for the current A/R fiscal reporting period. 

• 
Previous AR period: Runs the report group for the previous A/R fiscal reporting 

period.

, Rent Roll 
Detail,Rent Roll Detail (Excel)
,Resident Balance by Fiscal Period

Fiscal Period reports.

Scheduling the Report Group 

In the Schedule section: 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  
Typically, the Start dateis a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start dateis on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday.Type “ p ”in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save.

reporting period

Select this check box to prompt for a cover letter reporting period or group 

footnote when you run the report. You can enter a new footnote or replace

Sequential page 

numbering 

Select this check box if you want the reports in this group to be numbered 

continuously. For example, if the first report ends on page 3, then the next 

report starts on page 4—and so on—for all reports in the group. 

Public 
Select this check box if you want to make the report group available to other 

users. 

Footer text 
Type footer text here if you want the same footnote to appear for any group 

member that allows footers. Leave this blank if you want to keep any 

individually specified footnotes. A footnote can include up to 400 characters. 
A page footer is created in a client or entity, while an accountant’s footer 
is created at the console level. Each footer can hold up to 400 characters; however, they can print and view a combined total of 600 characters. The number of characters inthe page footer takes priority; if the total of the two footers exceeds 600 characters, then the footer text will be truncated in the report. For example, if a page footer has 380 characters, then the accountant’s footer can print only 220 characters.

Report owner 
Select the user who is responsible for this report group. 
If the report group is not marked as Public, then only the report owner and 
administrators can view and manage the report group.

#### Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide.pdf`, Page 295*

Chapter 5: More 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Reporting Portal User Guide 

Reporting Periods 

See the How to Get Here (on page 288) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Reporting periods are used when you create reports and budgets, and when you open and close 

books. They let you limit the information on the report to specific time ranges. 

There are out-of-the-box (system) reporting periods that are most commonly used, such as: 

• 
Prior/Current/Next month 

• 
Prior/Current/Next quarter 

• 
Prior/Current/Next year 

• 
Current <month/quarter/year> to date 

Companies often work on unique schedules. If the out-of-the-box reporting periods don’t meet 

your needs, create additional ones. For information, see Adding Reporting Periods (on page 290). 

There are some system-based reporting periods, like Current month, that you can run repeatedly 

without modification. For some types of reports, that’s all you need. 

For other reports, you need to specify the period that the report spans. Date-driven reports that 

you create are used with specific calendar periods (for example, for budgeting or opening and 

closing books). For these reports, you need to create a matching reporting period. 

There are many reasons you might want a specific reporting period. For example, manually 

creating a reporting period makes sense for some companies that: 

• 
Run and report on a weekly basis 

• 
Don’t end periods at the end of the month 

• 
Work from a 28-day cycle instead of a calendar month 

• 
Need past or future reporting periods 

Reporting periods enable you to limit the data shown on reports based on the way your company 

works. 

---

In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists.

Click Save.

Reports–Using Reports Quick Steps 

RP Financial Suite Reports–Using Reports Quick Steps 
Doc ID [407131] 
9/3/2024 

Using Accounting Reports 

With the Reports application, you can create any number 
of financial, standard, and custom reports. You can start 
from nothing or install reports from libraries and customize 
them to meet your needs. You can create reports online or 
process and store them offline. You can also save 
(memorize) reports to run over and over again, saving you 
time. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All`


Using the Report Center 

The Reports center is a single page that lists all reports 
you can access, organizing them by application and type 
for easy access. 
To use the search function: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Report Center`


1. On the Reports center page, on the default All reports 
tab, select an application from the first drop-down list. 
2. In the Search report center field, enter the report 
name or part of the report name as a search term. The 
system displays the results matching the search 
criteria. 
To use a default filter: 

1. On the Reports center page, select a report filter tab 
along the top of the page. 
2. Complete any necessary fields to generate results. 
To run a financial report: 

1. On the Reports center page, select a report filter tab 
along the top of the page. 
2. In the Search report center field, enter the report 
name or part of the report name as a search term. The 
system displays the results matching the search 
criteria. 
3. Click the report name. The system runs the report and 
displays it on a separate tab. 
4. If the financial report is configured to prompt for filters 
at runtime, then the Report prompt page opens. Filter 
the report as needed, and then click OK to run the 
report. 
To create a new report: 

1. On the Reports center page, click 
 New report, 
and then select an option from the drop-down list. 
2. Complete the required steps for the selected report. 
3. Click Save. 
To set a favorite report: 

1. On the Reports center page, select a report filter tab to 
view a list of corresponding report types. 
2. Click the 
 Favorite icon next to the report name. 
The icon turns yellow and is added to the Favorites 

tab. 
To run a standard report: 

1. On the Reports center page, select the Memorized 
tab. 
2. If there are no results showing, in the first drop-down 
field, select an application, Report groups, or OneSite 
reports. 
3. Click the report name. The system runs the report and 
displays it on a separate tab. 

Creating Custom Reports 

The Custom reports list page displays all custom reports 
that have been created for your company, including basic 
information about each report. By default, the list shows 
only active reports. To view all reports, click the Include 
Inactive check box at the top of the list. 
To create a custom report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. In the Operational reports section, select Custom 
reports. The Custom reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The Custom report wizard page 
appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Operational reports section, click 
 Add next to Custom reports. 
3. Follow the steps in the Custom Report Wizard Quick 
Steps. 

Working with Custom Reports 

Deploying a custom report to an application makes the 
report available from the application menu and from the 
Report Center. 
To run a custom report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. In the Operational reports section, select Custom 
reports. The Custom reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Run link for the custom report that you want to 
run. A report window opens. 
3. Select a report type from the drop-down list, and then 
click OK. 
4. Depending on the report type, results will either open 
another window or download a file. 
To edit a custom report: 

1. In the Operational reports section, select Custom 
reports. The Custom reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Edit link for the custom report that you want to 
run. The Custom report wizard – (report name) page 
opens in edit mode. 
3. Using the Custom Report Wizard Quick Start, change 
any data as needed on the page, and then click Next to 
advance to the next page. 

4. Repeat as needed. 
To duplicate a report: 

1. In the Operational reports section, select Custom 
reports. The Custom reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Duplicate link for the custom report that you 
want to run. The Custom report wizard – (report 
name) page opens. 
3. Change the report name and make any changes 
needed. 
4. Click Save. 
To make a custom report inactive: 

1. In the Operational reports section, select Custom 
reports. The Custom reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Duplicate link for the custom report that you 
want to run. The Custom report wizard – (report 
name) page opens. 
3. Change the report name and make any changes 
needed. 

Installing the Financial Report Library 

When your company is set up, you also get a library of 
financial reports that you can use right away listed in the 
Financial Reports Library. Here you will find a set of 
report templates that you can run as-is or install and 
configure to suit more specific requirements. 
To install or re-install a financial report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reports`


1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
reports. The Financial reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Financial reports library button. The System 
financial reports page appears. 
3. Click the Install link next to the report you want to 
install. The Save financial report as box appears. 
4. Leave the default report name or rename the report. 
5. Click Save. The report appears in the main Financial 
reports list. 

Creating a Financial Report 

Financial reports provide access to all of the financial 
reports that have been defined for your company. 
To create a financial report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reports`


1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
reports. The Financial reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The Financial report wizard 
page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Financial reporting section, click 
 Add next to Financial reports. 
3. Follow the steps in the Financial Report Wizard Quick 
Steps.

Managing Financial Reports 

To view a financial report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reports`


1. Under the Operational reports section, select Financial 
reports. The Financial reports list page appears. 
2. Click one of the format links (HTML, CSV, PDF, or 
Excel) to view the report. The format of the report 
determines the method of viewing the report, either live, 
downloading, or opening in a corresponding 
application. 
3. If the financial report is set to prompt for filters at 
runtime, then the Report prompt page opens before 
displaying the report in your browser. Set the report 
filters as needed, and then click OK to display the 
report. 
To edit a financial report: 

1. In the Operational reports section, select Financial 
reports. The Financial reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Edit link for the financial report that you want 
to change. The Financial report wizard page opens in 
edit mode. 
3. Using the Financial Report Wizard Quick Start, change 
any data as needed on the page, and then click the 
next left navigation tab to advance to the next page. 
4. Repeat as needed. 
5. Click Save. 
To inactivate or reactivate a financial report: 

1. In the Operational reports section, select Financial 
reports. The Financial reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Edit link for the financial report that you want 
to change. The Financial report wizard page opens in 
edit mode. 
3. On the Report info tab, clear the This report is active 
check box to inactivate the report. 
• Alternatively, select the This report is active check 
box to activate the report. 
4. Click Save. 

Processing System Financial Reports 

When you install a report from the System financial 
reports list, the system automatically adds it to the main 
Financial reports list where you can customize and run the 
report. You can also run a report directly from the System 
financial reports list. 
To run a system financial report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reports`


1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
reports. The Financial reports list page appears. 
2. Click one of the format links (HTML, CSV, PDF, or 

Excel) to run the report. The format of the report 
determines the method of viewing the report, either live, 
downloading, or opening in a corresponding 
application. 
3. Make changes as needed. 
4. Click Save. 
To customize a system financial report: 

1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
reports. The Financial reports list page appears. 
2. Click the Edit link next to the report. The Financial 
report wizard appears. 
3. Make changes as needed. 
4. Click Save. 

Installing the Graphs Library 

When your company is set up, you also get a library of 
financial graphs that you can use right away listed in the 
Graphs Library. Here you will find a set of graph templates 
that you can run as-is or install and configure to suit more 
specific requirements. 
To install or re-install a financial report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Graphs`


1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
graphs. The Financial graphs list page appears. 
2. Click the Graphs library button. The System financial 
graphs page appears. 
3. Click the Install link next to the graph you want to 
install. The Save financial graph as box appears. 
4. Leave the default graph name or rename the graph. 
5. Click Save. The graph appears in the main Financial 
graphs list. 

Creating a Financial Graph 

To create a financial graph: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Graphs`


1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
graphs. The Financial graphs list page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The General ledger graph – 
new graph page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Financial reporting section, click 
 Add next to Financial graphs. 
3. Complete all required fields and any optional fields 
needed. 
4. Click the Refresh button to view a preview of the 
graph. 
• Optionally, switch between graph types by clicking 
an icon to the right of the graph preview. Hover over 
a graph icon to display a tool tip with the name of the 
graph type. Graphs that can’t be displayed as a PDF 

are noted as “HTML only.” 
5. Click to expand the Filters section, and filter your report 
as needed. 
6. Click Save. 

Viewing Financial Graphs 

To view a financial graph: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Graphs`


1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
graphs. The Financial graphs list page appears. 
2. Click the View graph link next to the graph you want to 
view. The graph page opens. 
3. Change graph characteristic settings. Depending on the 
filter setup for the graph, additional drop-down lists 
might appear for you to filter on department, location, or 
other segments. 
4. Click the Refresh button to view your changes to the 
graph. 

Working with Financial Graphs and Types 

To run a financial graph: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Graphs`


1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
graphs. The Financial graphs list page appears. 
2. Click the Graphs library button. The System financial 
graphs page appears. 
3. Click the View graph link next to the graph you want to 
run. 
4. Complete or select any chart settings. 
5. Click the Refresh button to apply your selections. 
6. Click Save. 
To set graph types: 

1. In the Financial reporting section, select Financial 
graphs. The Financial graphs list page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The General ledger graph – 
new graph page appears. 
3. Complete required fields and any additional helpful 
information. 
4. Set the graph type by clicking a graph icon to the right 
of the graph preview pane. 
5. Click the Refresh button to apply your selections.

Reports–Financial Report Writer Quick Steps 

RP Financial Suite Reports–Financial Report Writer Quick Steps 
Doc ID [195554] 
9/12/2024 

About the Financial Report Writer 

Use the Financial Report Writer to create and edit 
financial reports. The Financial Report Writer guides you 
through the process of creating or editing a financial report, 
from adding rows and columns to deciding how your report 
should be formatted on page and in print. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports`


Entering Basic Report Information 

The Report info tab is the first page of the Financial Report 
Writer. Type a name for the report and select a basic report 
structure. 
To enter basic information for your report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Report Info`


1. In Reports, click the All tab. 
2. In the Financial reporting section, select 
 Financial 
reports. 
3. On the Report info tab, type a Report name. 
4. To assign a Report type, use the drop-down list. 
5. Select a Report audience to designate who the report 
is for. 
6. Select the Report structure: 
• Accounts: Displays accounts on report rows. 
• Segments: Displays segment data on the left side of 
the report and account data in columns. 
7. Depending on your selection, select whether to filter the 
rows by segment structure or account data. 
8. When you are done, click the Rows tab to proceed with 
your report. 

Adding Rows 

The Rows tab is where you populate the rows in your 
report. Add report rows using account groups or segment 
structures. 
To populate the rows in your report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Rows`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Rows tab. 
2. Click Select account groups or Select segment 
structures. 
3. For account groups, select the Account group you 
want to include in the report. For segments, select the 
Section/row type, and then select the Segment 
structure you want to include in the report. 
4. Click Include in report >. 
5. Add additional account groups or segment structures 

as needed. 
6. Click OK. 
7. In the Detail level column, click Set detail level. 
8. Select the level of detail you want to show for the entire 
report. 

Click an individual cell in the Detail level column to set 
the level of detail for a specific account group or 
segment structure. 

9. If you are using account groups as rows, you can leave 
the account group’s default calculation method as is or 
change the Basis for amounts to: 
• Override the default amount type for report rows. 
• Display amounts as cumulative balances. 
• Calculate amounts as a percentage of another 
account group. 
10. By default, reports include only sections that have data. 
To force a row to display, select the Always display 
column. 

Adding Columns 

Use the Columns tab to specify the number of report 
columns, the column data type, and the reporting periods 
for which you want data. You can also move a column 
location or delete column on the Column tab. 
Although you have many options for controlling what 
appears in each column of your report, the basic process is 
to: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Columns`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Columns tab. 
2. Select the drop-down arrow next to a column, and then 
select Add column left or Add column right. 
3. Select a Column type to set the type of value that 
appears in the column. 
4. Choose a preset Reporting period or combine a 
reporting period with an Offset to specify a reporting 
period relative to another period. 
5. Define column headings: 
• Column heading 1 and Column heading 2 provide 
predefined options for the period name and period 
date. 
• Column title pre-fills with the column type, but you 
can type a different title. 
6. Configure other column options as needed: 
• Account group: Select an account group for any 
actual or budget columns. This field is required only 
if you structured the report by segments. 
• Amount type: Override the default method of 
calculating amounts for the selected account group. 

• Expand by: Split one column into multiple columns 
by time period, account group, or another segment. 
• Show as: Change how the column value displays in 
the report. 
• Precision: Customize the number of decimal 
places. 
• Reporting book: Combine amounts from other 
reporting books. 
• Visual indicators: Apply a visual indicator to 
emphasize and highlight the meaning behind 
numbers. 
• Hide column: Select this option to hide the column 
from your report output but keep its calculations. 
Move a column to a new location using the drop-down 
menu. 

1. In the Financial report writer, click the Columns tab. 
2. Click the column drop-down arrow, and then select 
Move column left or Move column right. 
Delete report columns using the drop-down menu. 

1. In the Financial report writer, Click the Columns tab. 
2. Click the column drop-down arrow, and then select 
Remove. 
3. When prompted, click OK. 

Adding Computations 

The Computations tab lets you define calculations that you 
plan to use on the Columns tab of your financial report. 
Define the calculations that you plan to use in report 
columns. 
To add computations: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Computations`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Computations 
tab. 
2. Click Add computation. 
3. Select Set computations from the column drop-down 
list to add a computation for the entire column or click 

 Edit to add a computation for a specific account 
group. 
4. Select the Operation that you want to perform. 
5. Select a Variable type to determine how the report gets 
the Variable value used in the computation. 
• Account group: Sets the value to the total for the 
account group you select. 
• Account / Calculate amount: Sets the value to the 
amount of the account you select. 
• Constant: Sets the value to the number that you 
specify. 
6. Click Save.

otherwise disclosed outside of RealPage facilities, and may not be used in any way unless expressly authorized by RealPage.

Reports–Financial Report Writer Quick Steps 

RP Financial Suite Reports–Financial Report Writer Quick Steps 
Doc ID [195554] 
9/12/2024 

Specifying the Report Criteria 

Use the Filters tab to specify the report criteria. 
To set a report filter: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Filters`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Filters tab. 
2. Specify the As of date to set the reporting period. 
3. Select the Reporting book to set the main reporting 
book. 
4. Apply dimension filters.  

If you apply more than one filter, the report will contain 
the subset of data that meets all of the filter criteria. 

5. Select the Prompt check box for the criteria to let you 
define the criteria when the report is run. 

Defining the Report Format 

Use the Format tab to add report titles, define row and 
column formatting, and specify the page setup and 
orientation. 
To set the report format: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Format`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Format tab. 
2. Select the Reporting accounts for which you want to 
display output. 
3. Define how Numbers are displayed in the report. 
4. Specify how Dimensions are listed in rows and 
columns. 
5. Click the Page setup and columns tab. 
6. Enter the Page header titles and Page footer. 
7. Specify the Fonts and Page settings. 
8. Click the Rows & totals tab. 
9. Set Row formatting, Total formatting, and Currency 
options to determine how they should be displayed in 
printed reports. 
You can also recreate the appearance and layout of 
another financial report by copying the report. 

This option does not copy page settings (such as page size 
and orientation) or formatting options that differ by report 
(such as headers or column and row formats). 

1. In the Financial report writer, click the Format tab. 
2. On the General tab, select the Report whose 
formatting you want to copy. 
3. Click Copy formatting. 

Setting Report Permissions 

The Permissions tab identifies the report owner and 
restricts who can access the report. 

To add users or groups to the report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Permissions`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Permissions 
tab. 
2. Add users or groups to the Access list to grant access. 
3. Add users or groups to the Exclusion list to deny 
access. 

Previewing a Report 

The Next Steps tab allows you to preview the report to 
verify that it displays correctly. 
To preview your report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Next Steps`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Next Steps 
tab. 
2. Click the Preview button. 
3. Select the format in which you want to preview the 
report: 
• Live report (HTML): View the report in your 
browser. 
• Print version (PDF): View the report in print. 
• Excel: View the report in Excel. 
4. Edit the report as needed to refine the output. 

Adding a Report to Favorites 

The Next Steps tab allows you to add the report you just 
created to your “My Favorites” list. 
To add the report to your “My Favorites” list: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Next Steps`


1. Quickly access a report later on by adding it to your 
Favorites list. 
2. In the Financial report writer, click the Next steps 
tab. 
3. In the What’s next? section, click Add this report to 
your “my favorites” list in the reports center. 
4. Click Save. 

Adding a Report to a Dashboard 

The Next Steps tab allows you to add your financial report 
as a component on any dashboard that you own. 
To add the financial report to a dashboard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Next Steps`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Next steps 
tab. 

2. In the What’s next? section, click Add this report to a 
dashboard. 
3. Select the Dashboard. 
4. Type a Name. 
5. Click OK. 

Scheduling a Report 

The Next Steps tab allows you to schedule a report to run 
automatically on a recurring basis, such as weekly or 
monthly. 
To schedule a report to run automatically on a recurring 
basis. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Next Steps`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Next steps 
tab. 
2. In the What’s next? section, click Schedule this report 
to run periodically. 
3. Click Save and schedule. 
4. Set a Start date. 
5. In the Ending on drop-down list, select when the 
schedule should stop running: 
• Number of occurrences: Select this option to type 
the number of times that you want to run the report. 
• Never: Select this option to run the report 
indefinitely. 
• End date: Select this option to specify the date 
when you want to stop running the report. 
6. Select the Recurrence. 
7. Select one or more Delivery options. 

Adding a Report to a Report Group 

The Next Steps tab allows you to add a report group as an 
efficient and quick way to act upon multiple reports 
simultaneously. 
To add a report to a report group to include the report when 
performing bulk actions on a report group. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Financial Reports > Next Steps`


1. In the Financial report writer, click the Next steps 
tab. 
2. In the What’s next? section, click Include this report in 
a report group. 
3. Click Save and continue. 
4. Add the report to a report group. 
• Edit an existing report group, and then add the 
report as a member. 
• Create a new report group, and then add the report 
as a member.

Reports–Setting Up Quick Steps 

RealPage® Financial Suite Reports–Setting Up Quick Steps 
Doc ID [404478] 
8/30/2024 

About Setting Up Reports 

Use the Reports application to create reports online or 
process and store them offline. You can also save 
(memorize) reports to run over and over again, saving you 
time. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup`


Setting Up Accounting Reports 

To use the Reports application, begin by setting up reports 
in RealPage Accounting. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup`


Installing Account Groups from Account Groups 
Library 

To install an account group from the Account Groups 
library: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Account Groups`


1. On the Account groups page, click the Account 
groups library button to open the Account group 
library page. The page displays a list of system 
account groups that you can install. 
2. Locate the account group that you want to install, and 
then click the corresponding Install link. 

The system installs the account group using the name of 
the account group, without the “System_” prefix. For 
example, if you install “System_Amortization Expense,” 
the account group is installed as “Amortization 
Expense.” 

• To install all available account groups, click the 
Install all button. 
3. When the system completes the installation, click the 
Close button to close the confirmation window. 

Adding an Account Group 

To add an account group: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Account Groups`


1. Click the Add button. The Account group information 
page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Search & Find section on the 
Setup tab, click 
 Add next to Account groups. 
2. On the Account group information page, type a 
name for the new account group in the required Name 
field. 

Other fields in this section are optional. 

3. Select a group structure type from the Structure type 
field drop-down list. 
4. Select a calculation method from the Calculation 
method field drop-down list. 

Adding Statistical Accounts 

To add a statistical account: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Statistical Accounts`


1. Click the Add button. The Statistical accounts 
information page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Search & Find section on the 
Setup tab, click 
 Add next to Statistical 
accounts. 
2. On the Statistical accounts information page, type a 
number for the statistical account in the required 
Primary/sub account number field. 
3. Enter a title name for the statistical account in the 
required Title field. 

Other fields in this section are optional. 

4. Select dimension check boxes in the Required 
Dimensions section. 
5. Select a reporting account to use in the Reporting 
Account Mapping section. 

This section appears when your company uses account 
sets and has reporting accounts defined. 

6. Click Save. 

Adding a Reporting Account Set 

To add a reporting account set: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Reporting Accounts`


1. Click the Add button. The Reporting account set 
information page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Search & Find section on the 
Setup tab, click 
 Add next to Reporting 
accounts. 
2. On the Reporting account set information page, type 
a number for the reporting account set in the required 
Account set field. 

Other fields in this section are optional. 

3. In the Permissions section, in the first drop-down field, 
select Group or User. 
4. In the next drop-down field, select the desired group or 
user from the drop-down list, and then click the Add 
button. 
5. Select Allow or Deny to set the access rights for the 
user or group in the Access rights column. 

6. Click Save. 

Using Dimensions for Reporting 

A dimension is a category of data that you can organize 
and sort in meaningful ways. If you use dimensions for 
reporting, you can filter them by selecting the appropriate 
combinations in their respective drop-down boxes. 
To add a dimension for reporting: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Dimensions`


1. In the Dimensions section, select a dimension. The 
dimension list results page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The dimension information page 
appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Dimensions section on the Setup 
tab, click 
 Add next to dimension you want to 
add. 
3. Complete all fields for all tabs. 
4. Click Save. 

Setting Up a Dimension Group 

A dimension group is a name for a particular set of 
members in a dimension, or a set of members that meet 
certain criteria. 
To set up a dimension group: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Dimension Groups`


1. In the Dimension groups section, select a dimension 
group. The dimension group list results page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The dimension group information 
page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Dimension groups section on the 
Setup tab, click 
 Add next to dimension group 
you want to add. 
3. Complete all required fields. 
4. Click Save. 

Adding a Dimension Structure 

A dimension report structure provides a flexible way for you 
to organize dimension data that you want to see on the 
rows or columns of a financial report. You can add any 
number of structures for the dimensions you track. 
To add a dimension structure: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Dimension Structures`


1. In the Dimension structures section, select a dimension 
report structure. The dimension report structures list 
results page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The dimension report structure

Creating a Budget 

To add a budget: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Budgets`


1. In the More section, select Budgets. The Budgets list 
page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The Budget information page 
appears. 
• Alternatively, in the More section on the Setup tab, 
click 
 Add next to Budgets. 
3. Complete all required fields. 
4. Click Save. 

Using a Cover Letter 

To add a cover letter, you must first create a cover letter 
template. The cover letter template contains the text of your 
cover letter, and you create it using Microsoft Word. 

To create a cover letter template: 

1. Create a new document in Microsoft Word, and then 
write your cover letter template. 
2. For company-specific information in your cover letter 
template, substitute the corresponding merge field. You 
can copy and paste merge fields. For a list of merge 
fields, refer to the RP Accounting Report User Guide 
chapter titled Merge Field for Cover Letters. 
3. Save the cover letter template. 
To add a cover letter: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Cover Letters`


1. In the More section, select Cover letters. The Cover 
Letters list page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The Cover letter template page 
appears. 
• Alternatively, in the More section on the Setup tab, 
click 
 Add next to Cover letters. 
3. Complete all required fields. 
4. Click Save. 

Adding a Report Group 

A report group provides an efficient and quick way to act 
upon multiple reports simultaneously. 
To add a report group: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Report Groups`


1. In the More section, select Report groups. The Report 
groups list page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The Report group information 
page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the More section on the Setup tab, 
click 
 Add next to Report groups. 
3. Complete all required fields. 
4. Click Save. 

Running a Report Group 

There are two ways to run a report group, on demand or on 
a scheduled run time. 

To run a report group on demand: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Report Groups`


1. In the More section, select Report groups. The Report 
groups list page appears. 
2. On the Report groups list page, click the Run link next 
to the report group you want to run. The Storage 
options page opens. 
3. Complete all fields. 
4. Click the OK button. 
To schedule a report to run: 

1. In the More section, select Report groups. The Report 
groups list page appears. 
2. On the Report groups list page, click the Schedule 
link next to the report group you want to schedule. The 
Schedule report group page opens. 
3. Complete all required fields. 
4. Click Save. 

Defining a Reporting Period 

Reporting periods are used when you create reports and 
budgets, and when you open and close books. They let you 
limit the information in the report to specific time ranges. 
To add a reporting period: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Reporting Periods`


1. In the More section, select Reporting periods. The 
Reporting periods list page appears. 
2. Click the Add button. The Reporting period 
information page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the More section on the Setup tab, 
click 
 Add next to Reporting periods. 
3. Complete all required fields. 
4. Click Save. 

Using System Reporting Periods 

System reporting periods are out-of-the-box reporting 
periods. 
To change the status of a system reporting period: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Reporting Periods`


1. In the More section, select System Reporting 
Periods. The System reporting periods list page 
appears. 
2. For the reporting period that you want: 
• If the current status is Inactive, click the Activate 
link. 
• If the current status is Active, click the Inactivate 
link.

RP Financial Suite Reports–Custom Report Wizard Quick Steps 
Doc ID [407165] 
9/3/2024 

Using the Custom Report Wizard 

Use the Custom report wizard to create specialized 
reports from your company data. Unlike financial and 
standard reports, custom reports can include financial or 
non-financial data, or both, drawing on data from existing 
fields or your company’s custom fields. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
Custom Reports`


Selecting the Primary Data Source 

Choose a record or transaction as a starting point for your 
report. 
To create a custom report using the Custom Report Wizard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. On the Custom reports page, click the Add button. 
The Custom report wizard page appears. 
• Alternatively, in the Operational reports section on 
the All tab, click 
 Add next to Custom reports. 
2. On the Custom report wizard page, select a primary 
data source from the drop-down list. 
3. Click Next to proceed from Step 1 to Step 2. 

Defining the Columns 

Define the columns in your report using the following 
procedures. 
To define columns of a custom report using the Custom 
Report Wizard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. On the Custom report wizard Step 2 page, select the 
columns to include by selecting the corresponding 
check boxes. 
2. Click Next to proceed from Step 2 to Step 3. 
To create a formula for a calculated column: 

1. On the Custom report wizard Step 3 page, click the 
Add link. The Formula Editor box opens. 
2. In the Available Report Columns pane, select the 
column containing the data you want to include in the 
calculation. 
3. In the Operators column, select a basic math function 
to create a formula. 
4. Repeat Step 2, selecting another column containing 
data you want to include. 
5. When all columns are added, drag the column into the 
order you want to display for the report. 
6. In the Calculated column type drop-down list, select 
the formula format. 
7. In the Calculated column name field, enter a label for 
the column. 
8. Click Next to proceed from Step 3 to Step 4. 

To select the column sequence: 

1. On the Custom report wizard Step 4 page, select the 
 Move button to drag and drop the attached row. 
2. Click Next to proceed from Step 4 to Step 5. 
To add more column tools: 

1. On the Custom report wizard Step 5 page, expand 
both sections. 
2. From the top section, select any and all math function 
check boxes for each column. 
3. Review the bottom section for calculated columns. 
4. Click Next to proceed from Step 5 to Step 6. 
To sort the columns for priority: 

1. On the Custom report wizard Step 6 page, select the 
 Move button to drag and drop the attached row for 
priority. 
2. Click Next to proceed from Step 6 to Step 7. 

Filtering the Report 

You can use filters in your report to limit the data the 
system displays to the criteria that you choose. 
To select a filter for a custom report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. On the Custom report wizard Step 7 page, expand all 
sections. 
2. In the Columns column, click a drop-down list, and 
then select the column by which you want to filter. 
3. In the Operator column, select the operator you want 
to use to filter the column. 
4. In the Value column, enter the corresponding value. 
• Click the Add filter link below the columns to add 
more filters within the object. 
• Click the Delete last filter link to remove a filter 
field. 
5. Click Next to proceed from Step 7 to Step 8. 
To refine the filters: 

1. On the Custom report wizard Step 8 page, review the 
filters you added. 
2. In the Filter expression field, combine filter position 
numbers using logical operators and parentheses. 
3. Click Next to proceed from Step 8 to Step 9. 

Grouping the Data 

Grouping data allows you to set the level of detail you want 
the system to display in your report by selecting the 
appropriate grouping option, No Grouping or Grouping. 
No grouping displays a flat list of information, with the 
option to show a grand total at the bottom. Grouping 
arranges the information together and shows subtotals for 
grouped rows. 
To enable grouping of data: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. On the Custom report wizard Step 9 page, choose the 
level of detail you want to see in the custom report. 
2. Click Next to proceed from Step 9 to Step 10. 
To group data by column: 

This step appears only if the Grouping option is enabled. 
Otherwise continue to the next step. 

1. On the Custom report wizard Step 10 page, expand 
the object that contains the column by which you want 
to group the report. 
2. Select the column from the drop-down list. 
3. Repeat for all sections. 
4. Click Next to proceed from Step 10 to Step 11. 
To order the groups: 

1. On the Custom report wizard Step 11 page, in the 
Position column, select the button next to the column 
you want to move. 
• If a column has child columns, select the Include 
Children check box to enable the feature. 

2. Use the 
 Top, 
 Up, 
 Down, and 
Bottom arrows to change the sorting priority of the 
column. 
3. In the Sort column, use the corresponding drop-down 
list to select whether you want to sort your columns in 
ascending or descending order. 
4. Click Next to proceed from Step 11 to Step 12. 

Setting the Report Title 

You can set parameters for running the report, such as the 
reporting period and the title of the report. 
To set the report title and footer: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. On the Custom report wizard Step 12 page, select 
one of the Show details options, Yes or No. 
2. In the Report title 1 and Report title 2 fields, enter the 
first and second lines of the report title, respectively. 
3. In the Footer text field, add information you want to 
display at the bottom of the report pages. 
4. Click Next to proceed from Step 12 to Step 13. 

Defining the Chart Output 

You can choose to run a chart format to visually display 
your information. 
To define the chart output: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. On the Custom report wizard Step 13 page, complete 
all fields. 
2. Click Next to proceed from Step 13 to Step 14.

Adding a Runtime Prompt 

You can add additional prompts at runtime that are similar 
to filters. 
To add a runtime prompt: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. On the Custom report wizard Step 14 page, expand 
the section for the object that contains the field. 
2. Select the check box next to the field for which you 
want to add a prompt. Repeat as needed. 
3. Click Next to proceed from Step 14 to Step 15. 
To add a label or group to a prompt: 

1. On the Custom report wizard Step 15 page, click the 
Prompt label field and type the label you prefer. 
2. Click the Group field, and then type the name of the 
group you are creating. 
To use a prompt in Memorized Reports: 

• 
Use your selected prompts again in memorized reports 
by selecting the Enable when memorized check box. 
To change the display order of your runtime prompts: 

1. Select the button in the Position column for the 
parameter you want to move. 

2. Move the parameter by using the 
 Top, 
 Up, 

 Down, and 
 Bottom buttons. 
3. Click Next to proceed from Step 15 to Step 16. 

Saving the Report 

Save and add your report to the application menu. This 
makes it available to other users who have access to that 
application. 
To save your report: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Custom Reports`


1. On the Custom report wizard Step 16 page, in the 
Name field, type your preferred report name. 
2. Select the Add to menu check box. 
3. In the Application drop-down list, select the application 
to which you want to add the report. 
4. In the Description field, enter optional text to describe 
your report. 
5. In the Status drop-down list, select whether you want 
the report to be Active or Inactive. 
6. Click Save to save your report and add it to both the 
application menu you selected and to the list of reports.

#### Dashboard Permissions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide.pdf`, Page 12*

Dashboard Permissions 

Three levels of permissions affect a user’s access to dashboards. 

1. 
System-Level Dashboard Permissions: (on page 13) People who create and manage 

dashboards must have full system Dashboard permissions. Only administrators can assign 

system-level Dashboard permissions. 

2. 
Dashboard-Level Permissions: Each dashboard that a user creates has a set of properties 

that includes permissions. As part of creating a dashboard, the creator must assign 

permissions to the users and groups to allow them to access it. This process is discussed in 

detail in Assigning dashboard permissions (on page 31). 

3. 
Component Permissions: The people who are permitted to view another user’s dashboard 

must have system-level permissions to view its underlying data.  

For example, to be able to see a Current Revenue (to date) report on a dashboard, the user 

(the person viewing another user’s dashboard) must have system-level permissions to view 

Revenue. 

---



#### System-Level Dashboard Permissions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide.pdf`, Page 13*

Chapter 1: Setting Up the Dashboards Application 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide 

System-Level Dashboard Permissions 

Only the System Administrator can assign system dashboard permissions. System permissions are 

required to create and manage dashboards.  

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Company 
Dashboard 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

• 
List: This permission allows users to view the list of dashboards. 

• 
View: This permission allows users to see a dashboard’s contents. Users with View access 

cannot change dashboards in any way. 

• 
Add: This permission allows users to create new dashboards. 

• 
Edit: This permission allows users to change dashboard components. 

• 
Delete: This permission allows users to delete dashboards. A user can only delete a 

dashboard that he has created.  

Assign all five of these Dashboard permissions to users who are responsible for creating and 
managing dashboards for other users. As a rule, users who only view dashboards that others 
have created only need List and View permissions. 

For more information about system permissions, roles, and user types, see the User Types and 

Permissions (on page 110) topic in the help system or ask your system administrator for 

assistance.

#### Component Permissions

##### Changing Ownership of a Dashboard
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

Setting Up the Dashboards Application 

RealPage Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide

Component Permissions 

Dashboards have two types of components: general components and data-based components. 

• 
General components, like shortcuts, calendar, news, and events, automatically allow 

everyone to access them. 

• 
Data-based components, like reports and lists, extract data from other parts of the system 

for display in the dashboard component. 

The person viewing the dashboard must have permissions to view the data extracted for the 

report or list in order to see the component. If a user doesn’t have permission to view a 

component’s underlying data, he sees an error or a blank area instead of the component. If 

this occurs, have the system administrator check the user’s permissions to view the data that 

the component is accessing. 

• 
Lists of records: To access dashboards that include a list of records, the user must 

have permission to see the type of record displayed in the list. Lists of records can 

include accounts, vendors, A/P invoices, and A/R invoices. The Administrator is 

responsible for setting these system-level permissions. 

• 
Report: To access a report on a dashboard, the owner (creator) of the report must set 

the permissions to determine who is allowed to access the report. 

For example, if a user cannot view a component with vendor data, check the following: 

• 
Check the user’s Accounts Payable Vendors permissions to view and list vendor data. 

• 
Check each vendor record’s restriction level (on page 114) to ensure that the vendor’s 

Restrictions are set to Unrestricted vendor. 

• 
Ensure that the user’s dashboard viewer’s location and department have access to the 

vendors. 

Changing Ownership of a Dashboard 

When you have Full Administrator privileges, you can take ownership of someone else’s 

dashboard and assign the dashboard to someone else. This is particularly useful when a 

dashboard owner leaves the company. 

To change ownership of a dashboard: 

1. 
Select the Dashboards application and then select Dashboards.  

2. 
Select List All. 

3. 
Locate the dashboard and see if it is the default for the current owner. 

4. 
If it’s not their default dashboard, skip to the next step. If it is their default dashboard, you 

can’t change the owner until you assign a different dashboard as their default (locate one of 

their other dashboards, click Edit, and make it their new default). If it’s their only dashboard, 

create another one for them and make it their default. 

---

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide 

5. 
Next to the dashboard, click Edit. 

6. 
On the Dashboard properties page, click the Permissions tab. 

7. 
From Owner, select the new owner. 

8. 
Click Save.

Dashboard Home Page 

This section describes the features of dashboards. 

Dashboards consist of components that show snapshots of different parts of your business.

Moving and Rearranging Components 

To move components in a dashboard: 

1. 
Move your cursor to the top of a component.  

The cursor changes to 
 Move 

2. 
Drag and drop the component to the desired location. 

Performance cards stay together in groups. You can rearrange performance cards within 
its group, but you cannot separate the group. That is, you cannot move one or two 
performance cards above or below another type of component while leaving the rest of 
the performance cards in the original location. 

When you drop a performance card in a new location, the rest of the cards shift to the left 

to fill in the blank space. Performance cards wrap like words in a document, such that the 

leftmost card in the second row moves to the rightmost end of the top row.

Adding a Dashboard 

The fastest way to add a dashboard is to copy an existing dashboard that is similar to the one you 

want to create; but when you have no existing dashboards, you can create a new one. 

To add a new dashboard: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Dashboards.

Select Dashboards to open the My Dashboards list.

In the Title field, type the text that you want to appear at the top of the dashboard.

In the Description field, enter a note to remind yourself about the purpose of the 

dashboard.

In the Columns drop-down list, select 1, 2, or 3.

this column contains a wide component, then the setting gives the column a flexible width 

that presents as much detail as possible without the need for dashboard users to scroll. 

If you chose to have only one column, the Flexible-width column option does not appear.

your own by selecting Custom color.

select an existing group or select Create a new group.  

If you selected Create New Group, then enter a name for the new group and refresh your 

browser to see the new group in the Dashboards menu.

Assigning Dashboard Permissions 

When you create a new dashboard, or copy someone else’s dashboard, set up permissions for it 

so that other users can use it too. You can give access to your dashboard only to users who have 

accounts in RealPage Accounting. 

Dashboard Ownership 

The person who creates a dashboard is its owner. As owner, you can change and delete the 

dashboard and grant access to users and groups in the system. 

If you are unable to maintain the dashboard, then an Administrator with Full Administrator 
rights can reassign ownership (on page 14) of your dashboard to someone else. 

Granting an Individual Access to a Specific Dashboard

From the My Dashboards list, select a dashboard.

##### Changing Access Rights (Dashboards)
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide.pdf`, Page 36*

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide.pdf`, Page 36*

Working with Dashboards

•

For additional actions, select an option from the More actions drop-down list. The 

View audit trail (on page 116) option shows you changes to the record with the 
names and dates of the changes, while the Table size option allows you to select 
how many rows you want on the page. 

Changing Access Rights (Dashboards) 

After giving a user or a group permission to use your dashboard, you can later deny permission.  

You can allow a group to use your dashboard but deny use of the dashboard to selected 

individuals within the group. To set this up: 

Step 1: Set up permissions for the entire group.  

Step 2: Deny permission to select individuals: 

1. 
In the leftmost list, select User. 

2. 
In the list next to User, select a user from the group who will not have permission to use 

your dashboard. 

3. 
Click Add. 

4. 
In Access Rights for the user, select Deny. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Conflicting Access Rights 

Permissions establish a user’s access rights. When a user has access rights to a dashboard and the 

user belongs to a group that has access rights to the dashboard, conflicts between access rights 

can occur. This section explains what happens when those conflicts occur. 

A user’s access rights take priority over a group’s access rights: 

• 
If you deny access rights to a group but allow access rights to a user within the group, the 

user has permission to access the dashboard. 

• 
If you allow access rights to a group but deny access rights to a user within the group, the 

user does not have permission to access the dashboard. 

For a user belonging to more than one group, allowing access rights takes priority over denying 

access rights: 

• 
If a user belongs to two groups, and you deny access rights to one group but allow access 

rights to the other group, the user has permission to access the dashboard.

Dashboard Filters 

Using filters, you can clear information that you don’t need on a dashboard so that you can focus 

on the specifics that are most important to you. Set up filtering based on how you want to filter. 

You can filter by: 

• 
Date (As of date) 

• 
Dimensions (location and department) 

You can use filters with all financial reports, charts, and performance cards. You can prevent filters 

from applying to specific dashboard components. 

By adding filters to the top of the dashboard, you can create reports and other dashboard 

components once, and then let the user filter by a dimension and by time (As of date). For 

example, create a dashboard with filters for Location and As of date to allow users to filter the 

dashboard for a specific location by time. 

---


<!-- Page 38 -->
Working with Dashboards 

RealPage Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

How Filtering Works 

The filters that you select for your dashboard are available at the top of the dashboard, where 

users can filter the dashboard’s data on the fly. 

Currently, filters apply only to financial reports, financial charts, and performance cards. They 

don’t apply to standard reports and custom reports. 

Components That Can Be Filtered 

Components that can be filtered appear with the 
 Filter indicator. Filters apply automatically 
unless you select the option to prevent a component from being filtered. 


> **Navigation Path:** `When you select a report as a dashboard component, financial reports are listed with the prefix 
of Financials -. These reports are created using the Financial Report Writer and are listed in the 
General Ledger under General Ledger > All > Financial reporting.`


Components That Cannot Be Filtered 

Dashboard filters don’t apply to these components: 

• 
Standard reports, such as a Customer Aging report 

• 
Custom reports that were created with the Custom Report Writer 

• 
Non-report components 

This means that these reports are run: 

• 
As of the current date 

• 
Without any filters 

To make it clear that filters don’t apply, these components are displayed without a 
 Filter 
indicator. 

Consider wording the component title to make it clear that it isn’t filtered. For example, you might 
change “Customer Aging” to “Customer Aging as of today.” 

Filter Controls 

The filter controls appear at the top of the dashboard window, next to the 
 Add component 
button. Your filters appear along the top of the dashboard, to the left of the 
 Apply button. 
After you apply filters, the button text changes to say 
 Clear. 

This example shows a dashboard that has the As of date and Locations filters applied. 

---

Workflow 

Set up filters when you create or copy a dashboard. You can also use the 
 Settings button later 

to edit the dashboard’s properties and add or remove filters. Setting up filters is a two-step 

process: 

1. 
Set up the filters that you want to apply to most (or all) components on the dashboard. 

You can filter dashboard data by the dimensions that your system uses, typically 

Department and Location. You can also select the As of date filter to allow users to filter the 

dashboard by time. 

2. 
Exclude components from filtering. 

If you don’t want a particular component to be filtered when someone chooses a filter 

option at the top of the dashboard, you can exclude the component. This is useful if you 

have a component that displays fixed information, such as baseline data from a previous 

year or for a particular group of locations. See Excluding a Component from Filtering (on 

page 39). 

Setting Up Filters for a Dashboard 

To set up dashboard filters: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Dashboards. 

2. 
Select Dashboards. 

3. 
Locate the dashboard that you want to filter, and then click the View Components link. 

4. 
In the upper right, click the 
 Settings button.  

If the 
 Settings button does not appear, then you do not have permission to change the 
dashboard. You can only change the settings of a dashboard that you created.  

5. 
In the Dashboard properties box, click the Filters tab. 

6. 
On the Filters tab, select how you want to filter: 

• 
As of date: Get a historical perspective 

• 
Location: Get a perspective based on a property 

• 
Department: Get a perspective on department 

Depending on the dimensions that your company has enabled, additional filters may be 
available, including Vendor and Customer. 

7. 
Click Save.

Using Dashboard Filters 

When a dashboard creator has set up filters on a dashboard, you can use any of the filters that

To apply a filter to an entire dashboard: 

1. 
Choose one or more filters. 

• 
Date: If you enter a date earlier than As of today, components ignore everything that 

has happened since that date.  

To re-enter today’s date, type t (for today). 

• 
Department: Choose one department from the drop-down list. 

• 
Location: Choose one location from the locations drop-down list. 

2. 
Click the Apply button. Components update to reflect their filtered values. 

Some components may be excluded from filtering.  

To reset filtering: 

1. 
Click Clear all filters. Clearing does not update dashboard components; instead, it resets 

your dashboard filter choices: 

• 
Date: changes to As of today 

• 
Departments: changes to all departments 

• 
Locations: changes to all properties 

2. 
Click the Apply button. Components update to reflect their unfiltered values.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Financial Suite do not have the CSV for import option.

using:

Cloning an Existing Dashboard 

If you like someone else’s dashboard but want to customize it to meet your needs, clone their 

dashboard, save it under a new name, and then make your desired changes. 

You can change only the dashboards that you created. 

To clone a dashboard: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Dashboards. 

2. 
Select the Dashboards option. The My Dashboards list is displayed. 

3. 
Select a dashboard to clone, and then click View Components. If your company does not 

have dashboards yet, refer to Adding a Dashboard (on page 30) page. 

4. 
In the upper-right corner, click 
 Clone. 

5. 
In the Dashboard properties window, enter a new title. 

If you’re cloning an existing dashboard, don’t re-use the existing title. 

6. 
Click Save. The system returns to the original dashboard. 

Editing Your Cloned Dashboard 

To edit a cloned dashboard: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Dashboards. 

2. 
Select the Dashboards option. The My Dashboards list is displayed. 

3. 
Select the clone you created. 

To hide or show individual sections (components) of the dashboard, click the 

Collapse/Expand icon to the left of any component title. 

4. 
In the upper-right corner of the page, click 
 Settings. 

5. 
In the Dashboard properties window, change any field in the Appearance tab. 

You’re merely tinkering, so feel free to change anything and then see the result. 

6. 
Click Save.

Component Types 

A dashboard that you create is blank until you add a component to it. RealPage Financial Suite 

offers several types of components to choose from: 

• 
Action card: Shows tasks in the system that require your attention, such as invoices that are 

awaiting your approval or open budget variance analysis (BVA) periods that have been 

assigned to you. Action cards display on your home page dashboard. 

• 
Applications: Lists the RealPage Financial Suite applications available to you. 

• 
Calendar: Adds a calendar to your dashboard. 

• 
Charts/graphs: Shows any financial chart or memorized chart on a dashboard. 

• 
Entities: Adds a drop-down list with your available entities. 

• 
Main shortcuts: Lists convenient links that take you directly to a page without needing to 

navigate through several menus. 

• 
Message board: Shows messages from your system administrator. 

• 
New features: Lists recent updates to RealPage Financial Suite.  

• 
News and Events - RSS: Enables you to include content from popular news sources, such as 

the NY Times or CNN Money, by entering their RSS URL. 

• 
Report shortcuts: Lists convenient links that take you directly to a report. 

• 
Resources: Includes links to RealPage Financial Suite help and user guides. 

• 
Performance cards: Each performance card reports a single value. The foundation of each 

performance card is an account group, which you select. The account group determines the 

value that users see. 

• 
Record: Lists filtered, sorted records. For example, if you approve payments or expenses, 

then add a component that lists the ones that need your approval. Click to navigate and 

review the transactions without leaving the dashboard. 

• 
Report: Shows any memorized or financial report on a dashboard. 

• 
Report shortcuts: Lists shortcuts to the most popular reports in the main four RealPage 

Accounting applications: General ledger, Accounts receivable, Accounts payable, and Cash 

management. 

• 
Smartlinks: Add links to your dashboard. Two kinds of links are available: 

• 
Click: Shows links to web pages: when a user clicks a link, the page opens in a new 

window. 

• 
Fetch: Shows content from a web page directly in the dashboard component. 

View Components Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards > Dashboards > View Components`


This page appears when you click the View Components link of a dashboard from the My 

Dashboards list. The system opens the dashboard with controls to let you customize it.

Adding a Report to a Dashboard from a Dashboard

 Add > Report

To add a report to a dashboard: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Dashboards. 

2. 
Click Dashboards to open the My Dashboards list. 

3. 
Locate the dashboard to which you want to add a report. 

4. 
Click the View components link. 

5. 
In the upper-right corner, click the 
 Add button. The Component properties box opens. 

6. 
In the Component type drop-down list, select Report. 

7. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select Financial report or Memorized report. 

If Memorized report does not appear in the list, you have no memorized custom reports. 

8. 
From the Component drop-down list, select the report to add. 

What to do when you don’t see the report that you want to add  
Reports must be memorized before you can add them to a dashboard. Memorizing a 
report gives the report a name and retains the report settings, so you don’t have to select 
them each time you want to run or display the report.  
Financial reports do not need to be memorized. 

The system fills in the Component title field with the name of the selected report. You can 

change the title if needed. This is the text that appears in the report’s component box title, 

above the report. 

9. 
In the Rows field, select All rows. Select Enter # of rows if you do not want to show all rows 

in the dashboard component. If you selected Enter # of rows, then the # of rows field 

opens. Type the number of rows to display. 

The title occupies two rows. 

10. 
Select the Auto height check box to show all rows (no scrolling). This setting controls the 

vertical size of the component: 

• 
To show everything without the need to scroll vertically, select Auto height. 

• 
To set a fixed height and require scrolling for longer lists and reports, clear Auto 

height, and then enter a specific height. 

If you clear the Auto Height check box, then the Height field opens. In the Height field, 

type the limit on the vertical size of what shows on the dashboard (allow scrolling). 

11. 
In the Report view, select one of the following options: 

• 
Select Snapshot to have the system get the report when you initially open the 

dashboard and update it only when you refresh the report. To manually update the 

report, click the 
 Refresh button on the report component’s bar.

 Add button.

component.

Performance Cards 

Performance cards typically sit at the top of a dashboard. Each performance card reports a single 

value. RealPage Financial Suite offers two kinds of performance cards:  

• 
Financial 

• 
KPI 

The foundation of financial performance cards is an account group. The account group 

determines the value that users see.  

The foundation of a KPI performance card is a key performance indicator that you select when 

you create the performance card. 

You can add as many performance cards as you like to a dashboard. 

When you create performance cards, you can add them to a group so that they appear next to 

each other. You can also move grouped performance cards together as one unit. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Application

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a

In the Rounding drop-down list, select how much precision to show for the performance 

card value: 

• 
No rounding: Select to show all digits, up to two decimal places. 

• 
Whole number: Select to show all digits to the left of the decimal place. Example: if 

the value is 111,444,777.99, you see: 111,444,777 

• 
Thousands: Abbreviates the value with K. For values less than 10,000, it shows one 

decimal place. Examples:  

• 
If the value is 111,444,777.99, you see: 111,445K 

• 
If the value is 1,444.99, you see: 1,444.9 

• 
Millions: Abbreviates the value with M. For values less than 100,000,000, it shows up to 

one decimal place. For values less than 10,000,000, shows two decimal places. 

Examples: 

• 
If the value is 111,444,777.99, you see: 111M

Setting Up Mid-Period Comparisons 

Performance cards often show a number that is the result of comparing one reporting period to 

another period to determine whether an indicator is trending up or down. This article describes 

how to set up the comparisons.  

The system offers two types of comparisons: Period and Budget. You also have the option not to 

compare. 

The easiest way to build a performance card is to select a pre-defined reporting period and then 

select a pre-defined prior period in the Comparison section, but sometimes you must set up a 

comparison that starts in the middle of a reporting period. 

---


<!-- Page 84 -->
Working with Dashboard Components 

RealPage Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Comparing Two Periods Starting from the Middle of a Period 

To compare numbers from one entire period to another, select a period that is one period further 

back in time. 

If you’re comparing month-to-month Net Income, and it’s the middle of June, you don’t want to 

see a fraction of June’s net income compared to all of May’s. Instead, you’d set up to compare all 

of the prior month (May) to all of its prior period (April). 

Example: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select a prior period such as Prior Month, Prior 

Quarter, or Prior Year.  

2. 
In the Compare to drop-down list, select Period, and then select Prior period from the 

drop-down list next to Compare to.
