Creating Dashboard Groups 

When you have a dashboard open that is a member of a dashboard group, you can access the 

other dashboards in the group from the drop-down list that appears next to the dashboard title.  

If a group contains only one dashboard, the Dashboards menu shows the dashboard name as 

GroupName:DashboardName. 

To create a group of dashboards: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Dashboards. 

2. 
Select Dashboards to open the My Dashboards list. 

3. 
Open the first dashboard that you want to add to a group. 

4. 
On the Appearance tab, in Group, click in the Group drop-down list, and then select Create 

New Group.  

5. 
Type a name for the group. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Open another dashboard that you want to add to the group. 

8. 
On the Appearance tab, in Group, select the group that you created in step four.  

9. 
Click Save. 

10. 
Repeat steps 7-9 until you have added all of the desired dashboards to your new group. 

11. 
Refresh your browser. The new group name appears in place of the dashboard title. The 

selected dashboard is highlighted in the list and the other dashboards in the group appear 

in the drop-down list.

Renaming a Dashboard Group 

Renaming a dashboard group requires that you clear the group’s name from usage, and then 

create a new dashboard group.  

Workflow 

• 
Clear the group’s name from every dashboard, in effect, dissolving the dashboard group. 

• 
Create a new group with the desired name. 

• 
Reassign the dashboards to the new group. 

The following steps walk through the renaming process. 

To rename a dashboard group: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Dashboards. 

2. 
Select Dashboards to open the My Dashboards list. 

3. 
Find one of the dashboards in the group, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
In the Appearance tab, remove the group’s name from the Group drop-down box. You can 

do this by selecting Create New Group and leaving the New Group Name field blank, 

selecting a different group, or creating a new group and selecting it. 

5. 
Click Save.  

6. 
Repeat these steps for each dashboard in the group.

#### Roles and Permissions

##### Using Advanced Filters
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Dashboards User Guide.pdf`, Page 110*

Appendices

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 
that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 
permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 
When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 
can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 
permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 
groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 
A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 
Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 
to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

Using Advanced Filters 

To filter a list: 

1. 
Click the Advanced filters link. The Advanced filters box opens. 

2. 
Set up the first search condition.

Click the Apply button. 

If you want to generate an even more granular view, then continue adding filters. Click Add 

filter to add a row for another search condition. 

If you make a mistake or change your mind, then use the Delete last filter link to remove 

the last search condition (bottom row). 

Available Operators 

• 
equals 

• 
less than

greater than 

• 
less or equal

greater or equal 

• 
not equal to 

• 
contains 

• 
does not contain 

• 
starts with 

• 
ends with 

• 
includes 

• 
excludes 

• 
field equals null 

• 
field not equals null 

You can add as many filters as needed. Click the Add filter link to add additional rows to the 

Advanced Filters box. 

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns. 

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 

Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 

of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

%bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank,” like Metropolis Bank.

Filter Example 

To find an office property with an ID that begins with the letter M, break the search into two 

conditions.

Enter the first search condition: Find all property IDs that begin with the letter M. 

• 
Select the Property name column for the first search condition. 

• 
Select the Starts with operator. 

• 
Type the letter “M” in the third field. 

2. 
Enter the second search condition: Find all office properties. 

• 
Select the Property type column for the second search condition. 

• 
Select the Equals operator. 

• 
Type the word “Office” in the third field. 

When you apply the filter, the system displays a list of all items that meet both criteria. 

Filtering for Recent Records 

The system provides a set of standard views for quickly displaying list items that you recently 

modified or viewed. 

To filter or shorten the list to display only recent records: 

1. 
Click the down arrow beside the View menu, and then click Recently viewed, Recently 

modified, or All recently modified. The system displays only those records that you’ve 

recently viewed or modified. The list reflects your activity within this group of records. If you 

haven’t interacted with these records, then applying the recent activity will not return any 

records. 

2. 
To return to a view of all records, click the down arrow again, and then select All. 

The system makes the last view sticky, which means that the next time you open the list, 
you’ll see the last view that you displayed. 

Deleting a Filter 

To delete a filter: 

1. 
Click the Delete last filter link.

Account Groups 

Account groups are the fundamental building blocks of financial reporting in the system. 

Account groups simplify reporting by organizing accounts into re-usable structures (such as 

Assets and Expenses) that are separate from the reports, graphs, and performance cards that use 

them. These structures: 

• 
Roll-up and organize accounts. 

• 
Create the headings and subtotals in reports. 

General Ledger accounts are shown on financial statements only if they are included in an 
account group. Accounts can’t be added directly to a report. 

Although every company’s account groups will be different, your account groups will likely 

contain groupings related to assets, expenses, revenue, and more. To review your existing account 


> **Navigation Path:** `groups, go to General Ledger > All > Financial Report Structures > Account Groups.`


Vendors (Suppliers): Restrictions Tab 

This tab allows you to limit the use of this vendor. 

A vendor record can be available to all, available only at the top level, or available only to 

locations/location groups and departments/department groups that you select.

Dashboards Quick Steps 

RealPage® Financial Suites Dashboards Quick Steps 
Doc ID [404427] 
8/30/2024 

About Dashboards 

Use the Dashboards application to create and manage 
dashboards that help monitor important aspects of your 
business. 

Setting Up the Dashboards Application 

Before using the Dashboards application, an Administrator 
must set up the application by completing the installation of 
the Dashboards Library and assigning system-level 
Dashboard permissions. 

Installing the Dashboards LIbrary 

To install the system dashboard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards > 
Dashboards Library`


1. From the Applications menu, select Dashboards, and 
then select the Dashboards option on the All tab. 
2. Click the Dashboards library button. The Dashboards 
library page opens, 
3. Click the Install link next to the dashboard name that 
you want to install. 

Assigning Dashboard Permissions 

Three levels of permissions affect a user’s access to 
dashboards, system-level dashboard permissions, 
dashboard-level permissions, and component permissions. 
System permissions are required to create and manage 
dashboards. Only the System Administrator can assign 
system dashboard permissions. 
To assign dashboard-level permissions: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards > Edit > 
Permissions (tab)`


1. From the Applications menu, select Dashboards, and 
then select the Dashboards option on the All tab. 
2. Select Edit to access the dashboard properties, and 
then access the Permissions tab. 
3. Select User or Group, then in the next field, select a 
user or group from the drop-down list. 
4. Complete any additional fields, and then click Save. 

Assigning Component Permissions 

The person viewing the dashboard must have permissions 
to view the data extracted for the report or list in order to 
see the component. If a user doesn’t have permission to 
view a component’s underlying data, he sees an error or a 
blank area instead of the component. If this occurs, have 
the system administrator check the user’s permissions to 
view the data that the component is accessing. 

• 
Lists of records: To access dashboards that include a 
list of records, the user must have permission to see 

the type of record displayed in the list. Lists of records 
can include accounts, vendors, A/P invoices, and A/R 
invoices. The Administrator is responsible for setting 
these system-level permissions. 
• 
Report: To access a report on a dashboard, the owner 
(creator) of the report must set the permissions to 
determine who is allowed to access the report. 

Viewing a Dashboard 

You can view two types of dashboards, your default home 
dashboard or a dashboard created by someone else. 
To see your default home dashboard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards Home`


1. From the Applications menu, select Dashboards. 
2. Select Dashboards Home. Your default Dashboards 
Home page opens showing different components on it. 
To see a dashboard created by someone else: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards`


1. From the Applications menu, select Dashboards. 
2. If the dashboard you want appears in the list, select it. 
The My Dashboards list page opens with a list of 
different dashboards available to view.. 
3. Click the View link next to a dashboard you want to 
view. 

Adding a Component to the Dashboard 

To add a component to a dashboard that is not your default 
dashboard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards (list) > 
Add`


1. On a dashboard, in the upper-right corner, click 
Add. The Component properties box opens. 
2. In the Component type field, select a component type 
from the drop-down list. 
3. In the Component field, select a component from the 
drop-down list. 
4. In the Component title field, enter a name for the 
component. 
5. In the Height field, enter a height for the field in pixels. 
6. Select the Show Collapsed check box to display the 
component type section collapsed on the Company 
Home page. 
7. Click Save. The new component appears on the 
dashboard. 

After adding a component, you can drag it to the desired 
location on the dashboard. 

Editing and Deleting a Dashboard Component 

To edit a dashboard component: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards (list) > 
Add`


1. On the dashboard, in the upper-right corner of the 
desired component, click 
 Settings. The 
Component properties box opens. 
2. Edit any fields available. You can make several 
changes to see the result before you save the 
dashboard. 
3. Click Save. The changes you made appear on the 
dashboard. 
4. Review the edits you made. 
To delete a dashboard component: 

1. On the dashboard, in the upper-right corner of the 
desired component, click 
 Delete. A confirmation 
message appears. 
2. Click Ok. 

If you want to retrieve the component, you can either add 
it again, or clone the original dashboard. 

Moving and Rearranging Dashboard Components 

To move components in a dashboard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards (list) > 
Move`


1. Move your cursor to the top of a component. The cursor 

changes to 
 Move. 
2. Drag and drop the component to the desired location. 

Performance cards stay together in groups. You can 
rearrange performance cards within its group, but you 
cannot separate the group. That is, you cannot move 
one or two performance cards above or below another 
type of component while leaving the rest of the 
performance cards in the original location. 

When you drop a performance card in a new location, 
the rest of the cards shift to the left to fill in the blank 
space. Performance cards wrap like words in a 
document, such that the leftmost card in the second row 
moves to the rightmost end of the top row. 

Editing Your Cloned Dashboard 

To edit a cloned dashboard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards (list) > 
Move`


1. Click the Applications menu, and then select 
Dashboards. 
2. Select the Dashboards option. The My Dashboards 
list is displayed. 
3. Click the Edit link next to the clone you created.

## What’s Next?
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Dashboards Quick Steps.pdf`, Page 2*

Dashboards Quick Steps 

RealPage® Financial Suites Dashboards Quick Steps 
Doc ID [404427] 
8/30/2024 

To hide or show individual sections (components) of the 
dashboard, click the Collapse/Expand icon to the left of 
any component title. 

4. In the Dashboard properties window, change any field 
in the Appearance tab. 

Changes do not save until you click the Save button, so 
you can play with the layout to find your ideal settings.. 

5. Click Save. 

Cloning an Existing Dashboard 

If you like someone else’s dashboard but want to customize 
it to meet your needs, clone their dashboard, save it under 
a new name, and then make your desired changes. 

You can change only dashboards that you created. 

To clone a dashboard: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards (list) > 
View Components`


1. Click the Applications menu, and then select 
Dashboards. 
2. Select the Dashboards option. The My Dashboards 
list is displayed. 
3. Select a dashboard to clone, and then click View 
Components. If your company does not have 
dashboards yet, refer to Adding a Dashboard. 
4. In the upper-right corner, click 
 Clone Dashboard. 
5. In the Dashboard properties page, on the 
Appearance tab, enter a new title. 

If you’re cloning an existing dashboard, don’t re-use the 
existing title. 

6. Click Save. The system returns to the original 
dashboard. 

Refreshing the Data in a Dashboard 

Refreshing can be useful if data has changed since you 
opened the dashboard. 
To refresh one component: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Dashboards (menu) > Dashboards Home`


• 
Click 
 Refresh at the top of the component to 
refresh the data. 
To refresh the entire dashboard: 

• 
Refresh your browser window; for example, by 
pressing F5. 

For optimal response times, when refreshing the entire 
dashboard, the system retrieves the data as of 15 minutes 
ago. 

What’s Next? 

Now that you’ve learned the basics, you are ready to create 
your own dashboard.  
You can add as many dashboards as you like and control 
who can see them. For example, you might set up a 
dashboard for each role in your company. 
Group related dashboards for quick access. For example, 
you might set up a group of dashboards for your company: 
one for corporate oversight, one showing reports by 
department, and one showing employee metrics.

### Investor Tracking Overview
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 12*

Using Investor Tracking 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Investor Tracking Overview 

This application is an add-on product that requires an additional fee. After paying for the 

application, several configuration steps are required before you can use this application. See the 

Investor Tracking Setup Workflow (on page 86). 

After installing and enabling the Investor Tracking application and its permissions, the Investor 

Tracking application replaces the Reporting Portal application, and the Investor portal replaces 

the Owner portal. The system moves any documents that were stored in the Owner portal to the 

Investor portal. 

The Investor Tracking application helps you track contributions and distributions for investors and 

send the information to investors. Each investor has a portal where they can review the 

contributions that they have made and distributions that they received. Use this application to: 

• 
Create contributions. When you create a contribution, the system creates a contribution 

record and a companion invoice that appears in the A/R invoices list. 

• 
Create distributions. When you create a distribution, the system creates a distribution 

record and a companion invoice that appears in the A/P invoices list. 

• 
Calculate distributions. Have the system calculate distributions  

• 
Upload documents to share with investors. You can upload contribution and distribution 

records as you create them and you can also upload any other documents to share with the 

investors. 

• 
Generate reports. The Investor Tracking application offers three new reports, the Investors 

report, the Contributions Register, and the Distributions Register. In addition, you can create 

financial reports and graphs, and custom reports right from the Investor Tracking 

application.

After you add an investor, the system creates an investor portal for the investor. The system sends

To add an investor record: 

1. 
Open the Investor tracking menu. 

2. 
In the Search and Find section, click the 
 Add button next to Investor. 

Filling in the upper section of the page 

1. 
In the Investor ID field, type a unique code to assign to the investor record. 

2. 
In the Investor name field, type a name for the investor record, 

3. 
Fill in the address of the investor in the Address 1, Address 2, City, State/Territory, ZIP 

Code/Post code, and Country Code fields.  

4. 
In the Status field, leave the status set to Active.  

5. 
Fill in the electronic payment processing information in the ACH Bank Details section. 

6. 
Fill in the Routing number. 

7. 
Fill in the Account number. 

8. 
In the Account type field, select the type of account from the drop-down list. 

9. 
In the Account Classification drop-down list, select the account type, Business (CTX), 

Personal (PPD), or Business (CCD). 

Filling in the Contact List 

• 
Click a blank row, and then select a contact to associate with the Owner-Investor record. 

Filling In the Ownership List 

You can fill in this list manually, or you can import data into the list (on page 21). 

To fill in the list rows manually: 

1. 
Select the entity associated with the investor from the Entity drop-down list. 

2. 
In the Start date column, select the start date of the investor relationship. This field is 

required. 

3. 
In the End date column, select the end date of the investor relationship. 

4. 
In the Percentage ownership column, type the percentage of the property that the investor 

owns. This field is required. 

5. 
In the Initial Contribution column, type the amount that the investor contributed initially.

6. 
In the Initial Distribution column, type the amount that was paid out to the investor initially.

time.

investor over time. 

9.

When you create an Investor record, the system creates two additional records and 

associates them with the investor record.

Importing Investor Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Investor > Add/Edit/View`


You can import details about an investor’s investments into an investor’s record. 

Downloading the template 

To download the import template file for investors: 

1. 
Open the Investor Tracking menu. 

2. 
Click Investors. 

3. 
Click the Edit link to open the record that you want to import investor data into.  

4. 
In the Ownership section, click the Download entries form link. The system downloads the 

file to your browser’s default download location. 

Filling the Template with Data 

1. 
Open the template file in Excel, and fill in the required columns. 

• 
Entity: Type the location data of the investment property. 

• 
Start date: Type the date that investment in this property started. 

• 
Percent Ownership: Type the percentage of the property that the investment 

represents. 

2. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining columns: 

• 
End date: Type the date that investment in this property ended if any. 

• 
Initial Contribution: Type the amount that was initially invested in the property. 

• 
Initial Distribution: Type the amount that was initially distributed to the investor from 

the property. 

• 
Default Equity Account: Type the account to use as the equity account. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the File 

1. 
Open the investor record in which you want to import the investment data.  

2. 
Click the Choose file button. 

3. 
Find and select the file with the data that you saved as a CSV file.  

4. 
Click the Upload button. The system loads the data into the Ownership list. 

5. 
Click Save.

### Contacts List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 26*

Using Investor Tracking 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Contacts List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts`


The Contacts list displays all available contacts in your company, including the name and address 

of the contact. Contacts are used across your company in multiple ways: 

• 
To send event notifications  

• 
To determine ship-to/bill-to, and pay-to/return-to addresses in purchasing transactions  

• 
To determine tax on transactions 

Contacts aren ’t dimensions like vendors or customers. Instead, think of your contacts as a 
common, shared address book that is used across your company by many people for a variety of 
purposes. 

Use the Contacts list to add, edit, view, or delete the contacts in your company. Because contacts 

are flexible and can often be created at the time of need, there are a variety of ways you can add 

a contact. Most notably, contacts are created when new vendor, customer, user, or employee 

records are added to Performance Analytics. In each case, the Suggested contact name is created 

from specific fields, which may affect the consistency of your company naming conventions. Be 

sure to review the record for the specific fields when you create a new contact. 

Best Practices for Creating Contacts 

Because contacts are used and can be created by various records and applications in Performance 

Analytics, they can be set up inconsistently, which may be confusing in the future or even cause 

errors. To avoid these problems when setting up your contacts for the first time: 

• 
Use only supported characters. The Suggested contact name acts as a unique and 

permanent contact ID field in Performance Analytics. The supported values include: 

• 
Alphanumeric characters 

• 
Various punctuation (periods, hyphens, underscores, parentheses) 

Performance Analytics does not permit double spaces; using double spaces results in invalid 

contacts or contact records not appearing within drop-down menus. Furthermore, using 

other special characters not listed here (such as # or %) may also result in an invalid contact. 

• 
Establish a naming convention. The Suggested contact name is used in lists and 

drop-downs to identify your contacts. For this reason, we suggest using a naming 

convention that makes it easy to distinguish contacts in a list. 

For instance, you can use the company name of a vendor or customer, such as Example.com 

for the Suggested contact name. If the contact is an individual, you might choose a 

convention like Last Name, First Name or vice versa to keep your contacts consistent and 

easy to scan in lists and drop-downs. 

---



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 27*

Chapter 1: Using Investor Tracking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

How do users and contacts work together? 

A user ID and a password enable an individual to sign in to the company and access company 

information based on the user type. A contact is an individual who isn’t necessarily a user in the 

company, such as a vendor contact or customer contact. 

A contact can be made a user by adding the contact name to a user profile. For example, you 

could associate:  

• 
An employee contact with a user ID. 

• 
A customer contact with a user ID. 

• 
A vendor contact (for example a subcontractor) with a user ID. 

Associate an Existing Contact With a Customer, Vendor, Employee, or User 

Contact records hold the information you need to contact individuals or businesses. Alone, they 

are no more than a shared address book used for a variety of purposes. However, because one 

contact can be associated with many records, contacts become an easy way to manage contact 

information across many records, such as your customer, employee, vendor, and user records. 

Though you can create a new contact automatically when you create a customer, employee, 

vendor, or user, you may want to associate an existing contact with a record instead. 

Whatever the case, it’s important to note that contacts are associated with the records of 

individuals and businesses you interact with, not the other way around. For instance, if you want 

to associate the existing contact Jim West to the employee Jim West, you would go to the 

employee record to make this connection, not the contact record. 

Changing a contact in an existing record only affects transactions and other data records going 
forward. It won’t affect your historical data. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage contact records.

#### Adding a Contact
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 28*

Using Investor Tracking 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding a Contact 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > 
 Contact`


To create a contact quickly, you only need to assign it a unique Suggested contact name and a 

Print as name for documents. 

The Suggested contact name is the most important field in a contact record. It acts as a unique 

contact ID across the RealPage Financial Suite system, which means you can no longer edit the 

suggested contact name after you create the contact record. Furthermore, although you can 

change the printed name of a contact with the Print as field, the Suggested contact name is the 

name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists across RealPage Accounting. You can change 

the Suggested contact name of a contact (on page 33) in limited situations such as when a 

vendor’s name has changed. 

Additionally, when you create a new vendor, customer, employee, or user, a related contact is 

often created simultaneously based on specific fields in the record. See Creating a Contact from a 

Record (on page 34) to learn about which specific fields in each record create the related 

Suggested contact name. 

To create a more detailed contact record, fill in each tab on the Contact information page. 

Filling In Contact Information 

On the Contact information tab: 

1. 
Type the contact name. 

• 
This name isn’t necessarily the name that is used throughout your company because 

actual names aren’t always unique. For example, a name such as “Jose Hernandez” 

could be the same as a completely different contact in your company. 

• 
The system automatically suggests a unique Suggested contact name and Print as 

name based on the naming details you enter. 

2. 
Add the Primary email address, Primary phone number, and Company name for the 

contact.  

In the Property Management application, the system uses the primary email address that 
you enter here to fill in email addresses for emailing statements.  

3. 
Type a Suggested contact name if you want a different version than the one the system 

auto-populates. This name appears in lists and drop-down lists. 

After you save the contact, the Suggested contact name can’t be edited. 

4. 
Enter the Print as name if you want a different version to appear on printed documents than 

the one the system auto-populates.

Filling In Mailing Information 

On the Mailing information tab, add the mailing address for the contact. 

Filling In Additional Information 

On the Additional information tab, enter any secondary information you might have. This 

includes phone, URL, and taxable information. 

Marking a Contact to Be an Owner or Investor 

On the Reporting portal tab, select the This is an owner-Investor check box if you plan to include 

the contact as an owner or investor. This option enables the owners and investors to receive 

financial reports and other documents through the portal.  

Only contacts that are marked as an owner or investor will appear in the Contact drop-down list 
when you add a new Reporting Portal owner or investor (on page 16 ) record. Investor records are 
associated with the Investor Tracking application. Owner records, in this case, are associated 
with the Reporting portal application. They are not associated with the Owner records in the 

Condo and Co-op application and its Owner portal. 

Saving the Contact Record 

After providing the available information, click the Save button. 

To add another contact with the same information, click the Duplicate button. Everything is 

identical except for the Suggested contact name. Make any necessary changes, and then click the 

Save button. 

Viewing or Editing a Contact 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts > View/Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts > View or Edit`


After you save a new contact record, the Suggested contact name—which appears in drop-down 

lists and other lists—can’t be edited (see Changing the Suggested Contact Name (on page 33) for 

other options). However, you can make edits to the Print as field, which is separate from the 

Suggested contact name. While changes to this field don’t update the contact name that appears 

in your lists and drop-down lists, it does update the contact name as it appears on printed 

documents.  

To view or edit a contact: 

1. 
In the Contacts list, click the View or Edit link next to the contact record. 

The Contact information page opens. 

2. 
View or edit the information as needed. 

3. 
Click the Done or Save button.

Deleting or Inactivating a Contact

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts`


After you delete a contact, you can no longer restore it. If you are not sure whether to delete a 

contact, you can set its status to Inactive. Inactive contacts are hidden from the Contacts list and 

other system drop-down lists. 

You cannot delete a contact referenced in another area of the company. You must delete or 

remove the reference in those areas before deleting the contact. Common areas that refer to 

contact records include: 

• 
Customers  

• 
Vendors  

• 
Employees 

• 
Dimensions  

• 
Recurring transactions 

• 
Owners (Reporting Portal) or Investors (Investor Portal) 

You can configure the system to warn you when you are about to delete a contact. Click your 

username at the top of any page, select the My preferences option, and then select the Warn on 

delete check box in the On-screen messages section. 

Deleting a Contact 

1. 
In the Contacts list, select the Delete check box for each contact you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the Delete button. 

A confirmation box opens. 

3. 
Click OK to confirm. 

Inactivating a Contact 

1. 
In the Contacts list, click the Edit link next to the contact you want to inactivate. 

2. 
Set the Status of the contact to “Inactive.”  

3. 
Click Save.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts > Add/Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > > Search & Find > Contacts > Add/Edit`


When the Investor Tracking application is enabled, the Reporting portal application’s Owner 

portal is replaced with the Investor portal (on page 70). Investors can use the investor portal to 

access documents posted by the company and track their contributions and distributions. 

A Contact record must be flagged as an investor before you can give the contact access to the 

investor portal. 

You can only associate an email address with one investor. If you have multiple contact records 
with the same email address, then you can mark only one of those contacts as an investor. 

To mark a contact as an investor: 

1. 
On the Contact information page, click the Reporting portal tab. 

2. 
Select the This is an owner-investor check box. 

3. 
In the Send email notifications field, select when to notify the owner that a new document 

has been uploaded into their owner portal: 

• 
None: Does not send any email notifications. 

• 
Upon upload: Sends an email notification immediately after a document is uploaded. 

• 
Daily: Sends a daily email notification for all documents uploaded that day. The system 

sends the email overnight. 

4. 
Click Save. 

The contact will now be available in the Contact drop-down list when adding new investor 

records. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Add the contacts to the Investor record.  

All contacts that you list in the investor record can access the same Investor portal.

#### Changing the Suggested Contact Name
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 33*

Chapter 1: Using Investor Tracking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Changing the Suggested Contact Name 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts > Edit`


When you change the name of a vendor, customer, user, or employee, the Suggested contact 

name of the related contact doesn’t automatically update because it is a unique ID used across 

the system by various records. Unfortunately, you can’t change the Suggested contact name of a 

contact record after you create the record for the same reason. Instead, you’ll need to create and 

associate a new contact record with the appropriate record and then inactivate or delete the old 

contact record. 

For example, you create a vendor record and contact record simultaneously so that their names 

match. However, a few months later, you are required to change the name of your vendor and 

now the Suggested contact name of your associated contact record does not match the new 

name of the updated vendor record. First, you create a new contact record with the appropriate 

Suggested contact name, and then you associate that contact with your vendor record. 

Afterward, you can inactivate or delete the old contact record. 

To change the suggested contact name: 

1. 
Go to the record for which you want to change the related contact record, and then click the 

Edit link next to the record. For example, if you changed the name of a customer recently, 

go the Customers list in Accounts Payable, then click the Edit link next to the customer. 

2. 
On the Contact list tab, click Add to add a new contact to the record. 

3. 
Click the Contact drop-down list, and then choose the contact with the correct Suggested 

contact name, or click Add to add a new contact to which you can set the correct 

Suggested contact name. See Adding a Contact (on page 28) or Editing a Contact (on page 

29) for more information on your options. 

4. 
Set a Category for your new contact in the Contacts list. 

5. 
Select your new contact from the Primary contact drop-down list from above. Repeat as 

necessary for other required contact fields in the record. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Go to the Contacts list in Company. 

8. 
Inactivate or delete a contact record (on page 30) that no longer has the correct Suggested 

contact name.  

You can no longer restore a contact record after you delete it. If you are unsure, inactivate 
the record instead. 

---



#### Creating a Contact from a Record
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 34*

Using Investor Tracking 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Creating a Contact from a Record 

You can create new contacts as you create new vendor, customer, employee, or user records. The 

related contact, specifically the Suggested contact name, is created from specific fields 

depending on the kind of record you are creating. 

The Suggested contact name is a unique ID field that can’t be edited after creating the contact 
record. Be sure that the related field is correct before saving. See Changing the Suggested 
Contact Name (on page 33 ) for more details. 

Record Type 
Suggested Contact Name 

Vendor or Customer 
When you create a new related contact through a new vendor or 

customer record, the Suggested contact name is saved as Print as + V + 

Vendor ID for vendor records and Print as + C + Customer ID for 

customer records.  

For example, a vendor named Example.com with a vendor ID of 142 

would create a contact with the Suggested contact name of 

Example.com (V142). Similarly, a customer named Frank Smith with a 

customer ID of 1557 would create a contact with Frank Smith (C1557) as 

the Suggested contact name. 

Creating a new vendor or customer always automatically creates a new 

related contact unless you specifically select the Exclude from the 

company contact list check box when you create the record. You may 

want to use this option if you want to keep your contacts consistent with 

your company’s naming convention. 

Employee 
You must choose an existing contact or create a new contact using the 

Primary contact name field when you create a new employee record. 

If the employee is also a RealPage Accounting user, you must select the 

same primary contact name that you used for the employee’s user record. 

User 
When you create a new user, the system automatically creates a new 

contact based on the user ID if you do not select a contact in the Contact 

name field.  

For example, if the user ID of the new user is “jwilliams,” then the system 

assigns “jwilliams” as the related contact, unless you select a contact 

name when creating the user account. 

If the user is also an employee in RealPage Accounting, you must select 

the same contact name that you used in the user’s employee record to 

ensure that permissions work properly.

 Contributions.

5. 
In the G/L posting date field, type the date that you want the system to post the

6. 
In the Reference number field, type a number associated with the contribution. 

7. 
Type a description of this contribution in the Description field.

Deleting or Reversing a Contribution 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Daily Tasks > Contributions > Delete > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Daily Tasks > Contributions > Reverse`


You can delete a contribution until it has been paid. After payment is made, you can reverse the 

contribution instead. 

To delete a contribution: 

1. 
Open the Investor Tracking menu. 

2. 
In the Daily tasks section, click Contributions. 

3. 
Find the contribution record that you want to delete, and then click the Delete check box. 

4. 
Click the Delete button. 

When a contribution has been paid, a Reverse link appears instead of a Delete check box. 

To reverse a contribution: 

1. 
Open the Investor Tracking menu. 

2. 
In the Daily tasks section, click Contributions. 

3. 
Find the contribution record that you want to reverse , and then click the Reverse check box. 

4. 
Fill in the Transaction Reversal Date box with the date that you want to reverse the 

contribution in the Reverse the transaction on date field. 

5. 
Add a memo that explains the reversal in the Memo field.  

6. 
Click Submit.

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide

Uploading Contribution Records to the Portal 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Daily Tasks > Contributions > Select > Upload 
to Investor Portal`


After creating a new contribution, you may want to notify the investor by making the record 

available on the investor portal. 

To make a contribution record available on the portal: 

1. 
Open the Contributions list.  

2. 
Click the check boxes of the contributions that you want to upload to the portal to select 

them. 

3. 
Click the Upload to Investor Portal button. 

The system displays a confirmation message and uploads the contributions in PDF format 

into the Contributions folder of the associated investor(s) 

Contribution invoices are named with the invoice number and invoice date and uploaded 

into a Contributions folder in their portal.

Before You Begin 

Investor Tracking Is an Add-On 

The Investor Tracking application is an add-on product that your company has purchased. If the 

Investor Tracking application does not appear in your system, contact your system administrator 

to ask if your company has purchased the Investor Tracking add-on. 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions

#### Adding a Distribution
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 51*

Chapter 1: Using Investor Tracking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Adding a Distribution 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Daily Tasks > 
 Distributions`


To add a distribution record: 

1. 
Open the Investor Tracking menu. 

2. 
Click the 
 Distributions option. 

3. 
Fill in the Date field with the invoice date. 

4. 
In the Investor drop-down list, select the investor that you are creating a distribution for. 

5. 
In the Reference number field, type a number that refers to associated documentation or 

transactions related to this distribution.  

6. 
In the G/L posting date field, select the date that you want to post the distribution. 

7. 
In the Total distribution amount field, type the distribution amount. 

8. 
In the Description field, type a description of the distribution. 

9. 
You can optionally use the Attachments field to attach a document to the distribution. 

Filling In the Entries List 

1. 
Select the investment property in the Property drop-down list. 

2. 
Select the Account from which the distribution funds should be drawn from.  

3. 
Type the amount of the distribution in the Amount column. 

4. 
Select a department that is associated with the distribution if any. 

5. 
Type a memo if you want to add some information to the distribution invoice. 

6. 
Optionally, select a segment type and value to associate with the distribution.  

If the Segment type and Segment value fields do not appear, then your system may not 
have the segments feature enabled. 

To provide further details, click the Show details tab.  

• 
In the Segments section, continue defining segments that are relevant to the 

distribution.  

You can define up to four segments for a distribution record. 

• 
Fill in the fields such as the vendor associated with the distribution. 

Click the Hide details tab to close the section.

#### Deleting a Distribution
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 52*

Using Investor Tracking 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Finishing the Distribution 

When you are not ready to post the distribution, you can save it as a draft without affecting the 

G/L or any subledger. With the ability to save distributions in draft state, you can save your 

progress so far. Later on, you or another user can come back and post the distribution. Otherwise, 

you can post the distribution. 

When you finish entering or editing the distribution: 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the entry without posting it. Later, you 

or another user can review the entry and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the distribution. When you post a distribution record for an 

investor, the system creates an AP invoice. The invoice is automatically numbered using the 

distribution document sequence starting with D0001. The due date is set to 30 days from 

the invoice date. The distribution appears in the Distributions list with the invoice type set to 

“Distribution.” The system also adds the invoice to the A/P invoice list.  

Distribution invoices do not travel through the approval workflow. 

Deleting a Distribution 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Daily Tasks > Distributions > Delete`


You can delete a distribution that has been posted. After a distribution is paid, you can reverse it 

instead. 

To delete a distribution record: 

1. 
Open the Investor Tracking menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, click Distributions. 

3. 
Identify the record that you want to delete, and then click the Delete check box. 

4. 
Click the Delete button. 

5. 
Click OK to confirm the deletion.

Bulk Contribution List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Daily Tasks > Create Bulk Contributions`


Use the Bulk Contribution list to create multiple contributions at the same time. From this list, 

you can: 

• 
Manually add investor information for multiple investors and then create a bulk 

contribution.  

• 
Import investor data into the bulk contribution list so that you can then create a set of 

contribution records and A/R invoices at the same time. 

• 
Add more rows to the list by clicking the 
 Add button. 

• 
Delete a row from the list by clicking the 
 Delete button.  

Each line item will create one invoice.

#### Creating Bulk Contributions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 59*

Chapter 1: Using Investor Tracking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Creating Bulk Contributions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Daily Tasks > Create Bulk Contributions`


To create multiple contribution records and their A/R invoices: 

1. 
Open the Investor Tracking menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Create bulk contributions. The Bulk contribution page 

opens. 

3. 
In the Investor column, select the first investor to create a contribution for. 

4. 
Select or type today’s date. 

5. 
Select or type the date that you want the contribution to post to the general ledger.  

6. 
Type a description about the purpose or time frame for the contribution. 

7. 
Type a Reference number, a unique number associated with the contribution. 

8. 
In the Property column, select the investment property associated with the contribution. 

9. 
In the Account column, select the account to classify the contribution. 

10. 
Type the amount of the required contribution in the Amount column. 

11. 
Select a department that is associated with the contribution if any. 

12. 
Type a memo that you want to appear on the contribution’s A/R invoice. 

13. 
As an option, you can select a segment type and segment value to further classify the 

contribution. 

If the Segment type and Segment value fields do not appear, then your system does not 
have the segments feature enabled. 

14. 
Continue adding investors and contributions to the Bulk contribution list. 

15. 
When you have added all of the contributions, click the Create button. The Contributions 

list opens and shows the new contributions in the list.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

To access the Investor portals list, upload documents on the Upload documents page, view 

published documents, and delete investor portals, folders, and files, you must have the following 

permissions: 

Application 
Activities/Lists

Investor Tracking

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Uploading Reports and Documents to an Investor Portal 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Periodic Tasks > Upload Documents`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Periodic Tasks > Investor Portals > Upload`


There are multiple ways to upload financial reports and documents to an investor’s portal: 

• 
Attaching documents on the Upload document page. 

• 
Scheduling reports (or report groups) and storing them in the Investor Portal 

• 
Processing and storing reports (or report groups) in the Investor Portal 

Attaching Documents on the Upload Document Page 

To upload documents on the Upload document page: 

1. 
Open the Investor Tracking menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks section, select the Upload documents option. The Upload documents 

page opens.

### Calculate Distribution Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 76*

Using Investor Tracking 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Calculate Distribution Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Periodic Tasks > Calculate Distribution`


Use this page to have the system calculate the distribution of equity to investors and post the 

distributions.  

Distributions are funds paid to individuals as part of a real estate investment. Distributions are the 

means by which the company returns capital to their investors. The exact amount of distributions 

is dependent upon a number of factors including the rental income generated by the property 

and the operating expenses – property taxes, insurance, maintenance – incurred. 

The reserve amount is defined in the Entity’s Ownership Info tab. 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, the distribution amount is calculated by obtaining distribution 

account balance, subtracting the reserve account group balance from it, and then multiplying the 

remaining amount by the percentage ownership of the investor. 

The company pays periodic distributions to investors at regular intervals. Depending on the 

investment agreements, distributions can be paid, monthly, quarterly, or annually.  

This page presents filters in the upper part of the page, and the results of the filter in the Entries 

list in the lower part of the page. 

Use the filters and then click the Apply button to list calculated distributions. 

---

Application

Investor Tracking

user’s permissions. 

Calculating Distributions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Investor Tracking > All > Periodic Tasks > Calculate Distribution`


To calculate distributions: 

1. 
Filter for the investor that you want to calculate. 

2. 
You can also filter by entity or entity group in the Entity/entity group drop-down list. 

3. 
Click the Apply button. 

To clear the filter so that you can start over, click the Clear button. 

When you click the Apply button, the system fills in the list with the distribution calculations. 

The distribution calculation is: (Distribution account balance - the reserve account group 

balance) x percent ownership 

4.

5. 
Make changes to any of the available fields.

•

•

Investor Tracking Setup Workflow 

This section of the documentation discusses the three steps to prepare Investor Tracking for use: 

• 
Subscription: Enable the Investor Tracking application. 

• 
Permissions: Assign Investor Tracking permissions to the appropriate roles. 

• 
Configuration: Use the application’s configuration page to set up email notifications and 

custom folders for Investor Tracking. 

• 
Set up the investor distribution in the Entity record. (on page 92) 

After you install and enable the Investor Tracking application, the Investor Tracking 
application replaces the Reporting Portal application. If you had stored any files in the 
Reporting Portal, they are transferred to the Investor Portal. 

Subscribing to Investor Tracking 

To subscribe to Investor Tracking: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Subscriptions option. 

3. 
Find Investor Tracking. 

4. 
Click the Request Information button. The system sends a message to your account 

representative who will be notified to submit your order. 

You must have at least Limited Admin rights to request information about Investor 
Tracking. You must have Full Admin rights to enable the Investor Tracking application. 

5. 
After your purchase has been processed, you can enable the Investor Tracking module to 

use the application. 

To enable and configure the Investor Tracking application: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Subscriptions option. 

3. 
Find Investor Tracking. 

4. 
Enable the Investor Tracking module by clicking the toggle. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Configuring Investor Tracking (on page 90)

More Section 

This section describes how to use the menu options in the More section of the Setup tab. 

Cover Letters 

See the How to Get Here (on page 97) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

A cover letter is a document you can include in a group of reports. When you send the group of 

reports, you can use the cover letter to introduce the reports and describe what information they 

contain. In Performance Analytics, you can create a cover letter and include it in a memorized 

report group. 

For example, you can use a cover letter to introduce a package of reports sent to a client. 

The Cover letters page displays a list of default and custom cover letters available in your 

company. From this page, you can add, edit, view, and delete cover letters, or export the list of 

cover letters. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with cover letters: 

Application 
Activities/Lists

Cover Letters

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

In the More section, select Cover letters. 

Creating a Cover Letter Template 

To add a cover letter, you must first create a cover letter template. The cover letter template 

contains the text of your cover letter, and you create it using Microsoft Word. 

When you create your cover letter template, you can use merge fields in place of 

company-specific information, such as the company name, address, and reporting period dates. 

Using merge fields makes the template reusable and dynamic. When your memorized report 

group runs, it replaces the merge fields with the actual names, descriptions, and other specific 

information from your company or entity. For example, if you are an accountant, using merge 

fields for the company name and other company-specific information allows you to reuse the 

cover letter template for multiple client companies. 

For descriptions of the different merge fields, see Merge fields for cover letters (on page 98). 

To create a cover letter template: 

1. 
Create a new document in Microsoft Word, and then write your cover letter template. 

2. 
For company-specific information in your cover letter template, substitute the 

corresponding merge field. You can copy and paste merge fields. See the list of merge fields 

(on page 98). 

3. 
Save the cover letter template. 

---



#### Merge Fields for Cover Letters
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 98*

Setting Up Investor Tracking

Merge Fields for Cover Letters 

When you create your cover letter template, you will use merge fields in place of 

company-specific information, such as the company name, address, and reporting period dates. 

Using merge fields makes the template reusable and dynamic. When your memorized report 

group runs, it replaces the merge fields with the actual names, descriptions, and other specific 

information from your company or entity. For example, if you are an accountant, using merge 

fields for the company name and other company-specific information allows you to reuse the 

cover letter template for multiple client companies. 

The following lists the available merge fields you can use when creating cover letters: 

«CL_NAME»: Name of the cover letter template 

«CL_DESCRIPTION»: Description of the cover letter template 

«CL_ISDEFAULT»: Indicates that the cover letter template is the default 

«CL_COMPANY_TITLE»: The company ID that you enter when you sign in. 

For multi-entity shared companies, if you run the memorized report group at the entity level, the 
Company ID data merge fields will display entity information instead of top-level company 
information. 

«CL_COMPANY_NAME»: The name of the company 

«CL_COMPANY_COUNTRY»: The country for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALNAME»: The legal name of the company 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALCOUNTRY»: The country for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_FEDERALID»: The Federal ID for the company 

«CL_COMPANY_CONTACTNAME»: The contact name for the company 

«CL_COMPANY_CONTACTPHONE»: The contact phone number for the company 

«CL_COMPANY_CONTACTEMAIL»: The contact email address for the company 

«CL_COMPANY_ADDRESS1»: The first line for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_ADDRESS2»: The second line for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_CITY»: The city name for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_STATE»: The state or province name for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALADDRESS1»: The first line for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALADDRESS2»: The second line for the company’s legal address 

---


<!-- Page 99 -->
Chapter 2: Setting Up Investor Tracking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALCITY»: The city name for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALSTATE»: The state or province name for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_ZIPCODE»: The ZIP CODE or postal code for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALZIPCODE»: The ZIP CODE or postal code for the company’s legal address 

«CL_COMPANY_FAX»: The fax number for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_COUNTRYCODE»: The country code for the company’s address 

«CL_COMPANY_LEGALCOUNTRYCODE»: The country code for the company’s legal address 

«CL_MRG_NAME»: The name for the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_DESCRIPTION»: The description for the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_MEMBERS»: The member reports for the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_COVERLETTER»: The cover letter name for the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_PUBLICFLAG»: Indicates that the memorized report group is publicly available 

(available to other users who have permission to the memorize report groups feature) 

«CL_MRG_USERNAME»: Name of the user who created the memorized report group 

«CL_MRG_ASOFDATE»: As of date for the memorized report group 

«CL_RPI_NAME»: Name of the reporting period 

«CL_RPI_HEADER1»: The first line (Column Header 1) shown on the report. Example: “Quarter 

Ended” 

«CL_RPI_HEADER2»: The second line (Column Header 2) shown on the report. Example: 

“September 30, 2000” 

«CL_RPI_START_DATE»: The beginning date of the reporting period 

«CL_RPI_END_DATE»: The ending date of the reporting period 

«CL_RPI_BUDGETING»: Indicates that this reporting is displayed in the list of available reporting 

periods on the budgets page for inclusion in a budget 

«CL_RPI_STATUS»: The status of the reporting period (active or inactive)

Report Groups List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 105) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

A report group provides an efficient and quick way to act upon multiple reports simultaneously. 

For example, instead of having to run or schedule a set of reports one at a time, you can run a 

report group, which runs all of the member reports immediately or according to schedule. 

You can use the Report groups list to: 

• 
Add, edit, view, and delete report group information. 

• 
Run a report group on demand. 

• 
Schedule a date and time you want to run a report group. 

• 
View stored reports associated with a report group. 

• 
View operational reports associated with a report group. 

• 
View the status of a scheduled report group, including a log of executions and errors. 

Report groups that are public are available to any user with permissions to memorized report 
groups. If a report group is private, you can edit or run the report group only if you are the report 
owner or if you have full or limited administrator privileges. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Adding a Report Group 

Report Groups > Add 

See the How to Get Here (on page 105) topic for a list of ways to access the Report Groups list. 

To create a report group, fill in the report group information, add reports to the group, and set up 

any default parameters you want to apply to the report group at large. 

Filling In the Report Group Details 

1. 
Type a Name and Description for the report group. Names should contain letters and 

numbers and can contain single spaces or dashes. Do not use special characters in report 

group names. 

You can’t change the report group name after you’ve saved it. 

2. 
If you want to use a cover letter for the group, then select a Cover letter from the 

drop-down list and set a Cover letter reporting period. 

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to ask the user to select a reporting period at runtime. 

4. 
If you want the reports in this group to be numbered continuously, select the Sequential 

page numbering check box. For example, if the first report ends on page 3, then the next 

report starts on page 4, and so on for all of the reports in the group. 

---


<!-- Page 106 -->
Setting Up Investor Tracking 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
To make this report group available to other users who have permission for the memorized 

report groups feature, select the Public check box. 

6. 
You can add text to the footer that overrides any footer set in a group member. If you enter 

no footer here, then each report defaults to its own footer, if any. A footer can include up to 

400 characters. 

7. 
Select the Prompt on run check box to allow the user to create the footer text at runtime. 

By default, the user who creates the report group is listed as the Report owner. The 
report group can be edited and used by the report owner and any users with limited or full 
administrator privileges. If you mark the report group as Public, the report group is also 
available to other users who have permission to memorized report groups. 

8. 
In the Members list, click the Member drop-down line item, and then select a report to add 

to the group. Select all reports in the listed report groups to help you create complete 

owner reports in RealPage Accounting. 

OneSite reports are the last reports in the report output regardless of the order defined 
in the Members list. 

Setting Up Default Parameters (Optional) 

You can set up default parameters to save time when running or scheduling the report group. The 

system will automatically populate these parameters each time you run or schedule the report 

group; however, you can manually change the fields as needed. 

In the Default parameters section: 

1. 
In the As of date field, type the starting date from which to run the report.  

If you leave this field blank, then it will default to today’s date. 

2. 
In the Location/group drop-down list, select a specific location or location group for which 

you want to run the report. 

Report groups with Bank Reconciliation, Bank Reconciliation with Attachments, Bank 
Reconciliation Outstanding Items, Bank Reconciliation Adjusted Items, Delinquent and Prepaids, 
Security Deposits, and Rent Roll reports can be run on a location group and will generate 
individual reports per location. 

3. 
Select the Grouped by location/entity check box if you want to group the report data by 

location or entity. 

• 
Upon selecting the Grouped by location/entity check box, you can create a separate 

file per location. Select the Separate file per location/entity check box. 

• 
If the Separate file per location/entity check box is not enabled, the system creates 

the report group for each location and combines all reports into one file. 

---

Select the Create zipped file check box to zip the files together when created.

report group:

#### Running a Report Group On Demand
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 109*

Running a Report Group On Demand 

Report Groups > Run 

See the How to Get Here (on page 105) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can run a report group on demand instead of waiting for the report’s scheduled run time. 

Depending on the report group, certain conditions may apply: 

• 
If you run a report group with A/P Invoice Packages, the packages will include all invoices 

for the month (with attachments). 

• 
If you run a report group with Leasing & Rents reports or Bank Reconciliations on a location 

group, then the reports will be run as individual reports. 

• 
If you run a report group with Bank Reconciliations, then you will need to specify a location. 

If you have chosen to include Bank Reconciliations and you do not specify a location when 

running or scheduling the report, then the Bank Reconciliations will not be included in the 

report output. 

• 
If you run a report group with OneSite reports, the OneSite reports will be the last reports in 

the report group, regardless of the order defined in the Members list. 

• 
If you run a report group containing the Job Cost Open Invoices or Job Setup Summary 

report on a location group, then the report will include jobs for all locations in the location 

group.

any default parameters for the report, these fields will populate automatically; however, you can 

override them as needed.

If you leave this field blank, then it will default to today’s date. 

2. 
In the Location/group drop-down list, select a specific location or location group for which 

you want to run the report.

Viewing Stored Report Groups 

Reports run in the report group based on the As of date and/or Location/group you provide. 

When the reports are ready, you can view them in the My stored reports list (on page 319), 

available from the application in which you requested the report to be stored. 

If you have numerous entities, the location box can save you significant setup time. Create one 
generic report group without a location; when you run this generic report, you can specify the 
location you want. This saves you time you would otherwise spend setting up and maintaining 
multiple report groups per month per entity or location or editing each report location prior to 
the group’s scheduled run. 

You can also use the Run link to schedule an “off-cycle” run—that is, you can schedule the group

Scheduling a Report Group 

Report Groups > Schedule 

See the How to Get Here (on page 105) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can schedule any report group that you own. 

Depending on the report group, certain conditions may apply: 

• 
If you run a report group with A/P Invoice Packages, the packages will include all invoices 

for the month (with attachments). 

• 
If you run a report group with Leasing & Rents reports or Bank Reconciliations on a location 

group, then the reports will be run as individual reports. 

• 
If you run a report group with Bank Reconciliations, then you will need to specify a location. 

If you have chosen to include Bank Reconciliations and you do not specify a location when 

running or scheduling the report, then the Bank Reconciliations will not be included in the 

report output. 

• 
If you run a report group with OneSite reports, the OneSite reports will be the last reports in 

the report group, regardless of the order defined in the Members list. 

• 
If you run a report group containing the Job Cost Open Invoices or Job Setup Summary 

report on a location group, then the report will include jobs for all locations in the location 

group.

•

schedule. The Schedule report group page opens.

default parameters for the report group, then these fields will populate automatically; however, 

you can override them as needed.

you want to include in the report group. If you leave the field blank, the system runs the 

report for all departments. 

2. 
In the As of date field, type the starting date from which to run the report.  

If you leave this field blank, then it will default to today’s date. 

3. 
In the Location/group drop-down list, select a specific location or location group for which 

you want to run the report.

Scheduling the Report Group 

In the Schedule section: 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.   

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save. 

If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule Financial 

Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box to schedule reports 
and reports groups to run at that time.

Viewing the Status of a Scheduled Report Group 

Report Groups > (Status) 

See the How to Get Here (on page 105) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

If a report group is set to run on an automatic schedule, then you can view an execution log of 

previous runs and an error log for any failed attempts. 

To view the status of a scheduled report group: 

1. 
In the Report groups list, click one of the following links: 

• 
Status: This link appears if the schedule is ongoing. 

• 
Schedule completed with errors: This link appears if the report group has finished 

running for all scheduled occurrences, but one or more executions failed. 

If the report group was not scheduled to run or if it completed all scheduled runs 
successfully, then the status will display as Not scheduled or Schedule complete, 
respectively. Both of these statuses are read -only fields. 

The Schedule report group - Execution log page opens with the following information for 

each transaction log: 

• 
Log created on date: This is the date that the system generated the log. 

• 
Transaction date: This is the date that the run attempt occurred, as determined by the 

report group’s schedule. 

• 
Execution status: This displays whether the run attempt succeeded or failed. If it failed, 

then you can click the Failure link to open the Error log page (on page 122) with the 

details of any errors that occurred. 

2. 
When you have finished, click Done to return to the previous page or click Export to export 

the log to a CSV, Excel, Word, or PDF file.

members of a report group. Edit the report group to add and remove members.

A page footer is created in a client or entity, while an accountant’s footer

truncated in the report. For example, if a page footer has 380 characters, 
then the accountant ’s footer can print only 220 characters.

### Reporting Periods
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 131*

Chapter 2: Setting Up Investor Tracking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Reporting Periods 

See the How to Get Here (on page 133) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Reporting periods are used when you create reports and budgets, and when you open and close 

books. They let you limit the information on the report to specific time ranges. 

There are out-of-the-box (system) reporting periods that are most commonly used, such as: 

• 
Prior/Current/Next month 

• 
Prior/Current/Next quarter 

• 
Prior/Current/Next year 

• 
Current <month/quarter/year> to date 

Companies often work on unique schedules. If the out-of-the-box reporting periods don’t meet 

your needs, create additional ones. For information, see Adding Reporting Periods (on page 135). 

There are some system-based reporting periods, like Current month, that you can run repeatedly 

without modification. For some types of reports, that’s all you need. 

For other reports, you need to specify the period that the report spans. Date-driven reports that 

you create are used with specific calendar periods (for example, for budgeting or opening and 

closing books). For these reports, you need to create a matching reporting period. 

There are many reasons you might want a specific reporting period. For example, manually 

creating a reporting period makes sense for some companies that: 

• 
Run and report on a weekly basis 

• 
Don’t end periods at the end of the month 

• 
Work from a 28-day cycle instead of a calendar month 

• 
Need past or future reporting periods 

Reporting periods enable you to limit the data shown on reports based on the way your company 

works. 

---

Adding Reporting Periods 

 Reporting Periods

To add a reporting period: 

1. 
Click 
 Reporting Periods to create a new reporting period record. 

2. 
Type a Name for the reporting period. 

3. 
Type a Column header for the first column and, optionally, a Column header 2 for the 

second column. 

4. 
Type or select a Start date and an End date for the reporting period. 

5. 
Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

To make this reporting period available on the Budgets page, select the Use for budgeting 

check box. 

If you don’t see this check box, then make sure that you have permissions for budgeting. 

6. 
If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule Financial 

Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box to schedule 

reports and reports groups to run at that time. 

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists. 

8. 
Click Save.

Make changes as needed.

Click Save.

Use for budgeting 
Select this check box to allow this reporting period to be displayed in 

the list of available reporting periods on the budgets page for inclusion 

in a budget. 

The dates of periods selected for budgets cannot overlap. For example, 
you have two reporting periods: one includes January 1 to January 31, 
and another includes January 15 to February 15. If you select the 
first to be used for budgeting, you can’t select the second. 

Status 
This is the status of the reporting period. If you are no longer using the 

reporting period and do not want it to appear in lists, choose Inactive. 

This keeps the information in your system and suppresses it from lists 

without deleting it. If you want to see the inactive periods later, click the 

Show Inactive check box in the list. The default status is Active.

To customize the Investors report:

1. 
To run the report for one investor, select the investor from the Investor drop-down list.

To run the report for one location, select the desired location from the Location drop-down 

list. 

To run the report for all locations but have the system create a separate report for each 

location, clear the Location drop-down list, and then select the Individual report check box.
