RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

This applies to actuals only. 

• 
Display zero balance columns: Clearing this option automatically hides any columns that 

have only zero amounts. This can be particularly useful if you sometimes compare report 

data by time period or segment and you want to automatically hide any columns that don’t 

have data. 

• 
Do not display zero value calculation: Select this option to exclude zero-value calculations 

(0.00) in the report. This setting affects the Computation on actual and Computation on 

budget column types. 

Departments, Locations, and Other Segments 

The options for segments allow you to control how departments, locations, and other segments 

are listed in rows and columns. These options apply in either of the following situations: 

• 
If you change the detail level for rows to show segment detail 

• 
If you expand columns by segment or segment structure 

For example, you might expand an actual column so that it is split into multiple columns by 

location. 

The following lists the segment options. 

• 
Show departments: Choose whether to display departments by name only, by ID only, or by 

name and ID. 

• 
Show locations: Choose whether to display locations by name only, by ID only, or by name 

and ID. 

• 
Show other: Choose whether to display other segments by name only, by ID only, or by 

name and ID. 

• 
Sorting (alphabetically sort Department or Location Group): If you filter the report by a 

department or location group, the report automatically displays departments and locations 

in the order in which they are defined in the group. Select this option if you prefer to sort 

departments and locations alphabetically. 

If you don’t filter by a segment or location group, the report will always display 
departments and locations in alphabetical order.

Defining Report Headers and Footers 

Page Header 

By default, printed reports start with your company name, followed by the report title, and a 

subtitle that spells out the report’s “As of date” in words. Using the options in the Page header 

and Page footer sections, you have the option to: 

• 
Change the report title. 

• 
Include additional lines of header text and optionally change how and where the date is 

displayed. 

• 
Include your company logo in the header. 

• 
Include footer text, including dynamic information that specifies the page number and 

date/time when the report was printed. 

The list describes the header information that is included when the report is displayed in printable 

(PDF) format. As noted in the table, some header elements (such as the report title) also appear 

when the report is displayed in Excel or HTML format. 

• 
Logo options (displayed in PDF): Include your logo at the top of the report, aligned to the 

left, top, or center. 

If you have not uploaded your logo, you can do so on the 
Company information page. See 
Adding and Editing General Information for instructions. 

• 
Report title (displayed in PDF, HTML, Excel): Enter the title you want to display in the report. 

By default, the report uses the report name that you entered on the Report Info tab as the 

title. 

• 
Subtitle 1 and Subtitle 2 (displayed in PDF, Excel): For all new reports, Subtitle 1 displays as 

As of [As_of_Date_in_Word]. This displays the words “As of” followed by the date spelled 

out in words (as in “March 31, 2012”). You can enter your own text in either Subtitle 1 or 

Subtitle 2, and you can use the following variables to dynamically include the date either 

spelled out in words or numerically. 

• 
[As_of_Date_in_Word] 

• 
[As_of_Date] 

• 
Title comment (displayed in PDF, HTML, Excel): Enter an optional comment that will display 

aligned left, above the report body. 

• 
Company title: Display departments/locations as company title in individual reports 

(displayed in PDF). By default, your company name (as entered on the Company 

information page) is displayed at the top of the page header of printed reports and reports 

exported to Excel. However, if you’re splitting a report that compares data by department or 

location into multiple individual reports, you can choose to display the department or

Setting Other Options 

Page Settings 

By default, your report is set up to print in Portrait orientation on letter-size paper. The system 

will determine where columns break across pages, and the report may be more than one page 

wide. However, you can choose other options that allow you to control how the report prints 

across pages. 

The choices you make in the Page settings section determine how much control you have over the 

printed page. 

• 
Default page settings: This is the default setting. If you select this option, column size and 

breaks are determined automatically. However, you can change the report from Portrait 

orientation to Landscape to fit more columns across the page. 

• 
Fit to x page(s) wide: Select this option if you want to specify how many pages wide the 

report should be (for example, fitting it to one page wide), but still have the column width 

set automatically. 

• 
Page orientation: By default, pages are set to Portrait. Select Landscape from the 

drop-down list to change the orientation of the report pages. 

• 
Measurements: If you select Custom page size you can choose to see the measurements 

for margins and column widths as points or inches. 

• 
Custom page size, column widths, and column breaks: Select this option if you want more 

control over the printed report, including the ability to select a different page size, set 

column widths, and set the page margins. 

Column Options and Fonts 

You can use the Column options, breaks, and fonts section to control the look of particular 

columns on reports. Available options depend on your page settings selection. Some options 

apply only when the report is output as a PDF. 

• 
Hide filter details on column titles: Hide the details of filtered columns, such as the account 

group and segment structure display on the column header. This option applies to all 

outputs. It allows user to use the column filter to preset the column data without showing 

all details on the report presentation of column header. to hide column filter such as 

account group and segment structure display on the column header. This option applies to 

all outputs. It allows user to use the column filter to pre-set the column data without 

showing all details on the report presentation of column header. 

• 
Repeat segment name/ID as 1st column on reports more than 1 page wide: When a report 

is more than one page wide, enable this feature to ensure that the first column is repeated 

on each page, making it easier to follow the column information.

Controlling Rows and Total Lines in Printed Reports

Section Headings

Total Lines

line altogether.

Hide totals: Hides the total title and amount line. To suppress the totals for all lines, click the

the total.

Underline totals: Controls whether the total is underlined, and how many underlines are

Format Tab FAQs 

How do I control the width of the report? 

The width of the report is affected by the number of columns in the report, and the font sizes you 

selected. If you want to control how many pages wide your report is, you can have the system fit 

the report to a certain number of pages wide, or you can use column breaks to select how many 

columns are on each page. You can also fit more columns on a page by switching to landscape 

orientation. 

To control the width of the report, perform one of the following options: 

Fit the report to one page wide (or a selected number of pages). 

1. 
In the Page Settings section, select the Fit to x pages wide option. 

2. 
Specify how many pages wide the report should be. 

Select where page breaks fall. 

1. 
In the Page Settings section, set the custom page size, column breaks, margins, and column 

specific fonts. 

2. 
In the Column Options, Breaks, and Fonts section, locate the column after which you want 

the first column break. Any remaining columns will appear on the next page. 

If your report is more than two pages wide, set additional column breaks as needed. 

Set page orientation to landscape. 

• 
In the Page Settings section, select the Landscape option as the page orientation. 

How do I control page breaks? 

You can control where page breaks are in the report by inserting a page break at the end of a 

certain section. 

To insert a page break after a specific section: 

1. 
Go to the Rows section of the Format tab. 

2. 
Locate the section after which you want a page break. For example, if you want a page 

break after your Fixed Assets group, locate the row for that group. 

3. 
In the Row formatting column, select the check box for Page Break After.

Permissions Tab 

The Permissions tab identifies the report owner and specifies who can and can’t access this 

report. Users who don’t have access to a report won’t see it in the Financial reports list page, and 

it won’t appear in their Reports Center or dashboards. 

Assigning Report Access 

Depending on how your General Ledger was set up, the default permissions to financial reports 

may either grant or deny access to all users (the group called Group/Everyone). For example, if 

the default access privileges for financial reports are set up to deny access, you can selectively 

give access to users or user groups by adding them to the Access list. 

When a user or group is added to the Access list, even though the Exclusion list is set to 

Group/Everyone, the Access list takes precedence and any user or group specifically included in 

the Access list is granted access to the report. 

If access is granted to Group/Everyone but one user is added to the Exclusion list (even if that 

user is part of a group given access), that user can’t access the report. 

To set the report owner and permissions: 

1. 
If necessary, select the person who is responsible for the report as Report owner. 

By default, the person who creates the report is the report owner. However, if the report will 

be maintained by someone else, you can select that user from the list. 

2. 
Set permissions for the report by reviewing the Access list and Exclusion list. 

• 
To add a user or user group to either list, click the Add button. 

• 
To remove a user or user group from either list, select the user or group and click the 

Remove button. 

In addition to adding individual users, you can select groups of users. Learn more about adding 

user groups. 

Selecting Default Permissions 

A preference in the General Ledger determines whether financial reports are available to everyone 

by default. 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to General Ledger > Setup > Configuration.`


2. 
Scroll down to the Financial reports section and locate the option to Set default 

permissions to public.

Next Steps Tab 

When you’ve finished designing your report, it’s time to start using it. 

Although you can always run your report by going to the Financial reports list page or by going 

to the Reports Center, you can do more to highlight and use your report. 

Adding a Report to a Dashboard 

Dashboards give you an at-a-glance view of the areas of your business that matter most to you. 

From the Next steps tab, you quickly add your financial report as a component on any dashboard 

that you own. 

To use the Next steps tab to add the financial report to a dashboard: 

1. 
Click the Add this report to a dashboard link. 

2. 
Select the dashboard, give it a name and location, and enter other details as needed. 

Learn more about the options for report components. 

If you see a message that you don’t have any dashboards that you can add components to, but 
you know that you have dashboards, you probably aren’t the owner of those dashboards. In this 
case, you can still edit the dashboard from the Dashboards list and then add the component. 

Can I add this report to someone else’s dashboard? 

Yes, you can add this report to any dashboard that you can see on the Dashboards list, provided 

that you have permissions to edit dashboards. However, if you’re not the owner of the dashboard, 

you’ll need access the dashboard from the Dashboards list to add the component. 

Learn more about adding a component to a dashboard. 

Scheduling a Report 

You can schedule a report to run automatically on a recurring basis, such as weekly or monthly. 

When you schedule the report, you can set it up to be delivered by email or stored. 

To schedule a report from the Financial Report Writer: 

1. 
On the Next steps tab, click Schedule this report to run periodically. 

2. 
When prompted, click the Save and schedule button to save the report and proceed. 

3. 
On the Schedule financial report page, set up a schedule for the report and select how you 

want it to be delivered. 

Learn more about the options for scheduling a report (on page 168). 

In addition to having the report emailed to you, you can also have it stored. Learn how to access 

stored reports in the Reports Center.

Adding a Report to a Report Group 

A report group provides an efficient and quick way to act upon multiple reports simultaneously. 

For example, instead of having to run or schedule a set of reports one at a time, you can run a 

report group, which runs all member reports immediately or according to schedule. 

To include the report in a report group: 

1. 
On the Next steps tab, click Include this report in a report group. 

2. 
When prompted, click the Save and continue button to save the report and proceed to the 

Report groups list page. 

• 
To add the report to an existing report group, click the Edit link for the report group. 

Then add the report as a member. 

• 
If you don’t have any report groups, you can add one from the Report groups list. 


> **Navigation Path:** `You can access your report groups later on by going to Reports > Setup > More > Report`


Groups. 

Learn more about report groups (on page 104). 

Adding Budget Variance Analysis Notes to a Financial Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reports > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Reports > Edit`


If you want to see the budget variance analysis (BVA) notes in a financial report, then you can add 

it to the report as a column. 

To add the BVA notes column to a custom financial report: 

1. 
In the Financial reports list, click the Edit link next to the desired financial report. The 

Financial report writer opens. 

2. 
Click the Columns tab. 

3. 
Find where you want to insert the new column, and then click the drop-down arrow of the 

Column heading to display its submenu. 

4. 
Select Add column left or Add column right. The new column appears to the left or right of 

the selected column. 

5. 
In the Column type field, find the Budget section, and then select the Budget variance 

notes option. 

For information about column types, see Column types in online help or download the 
RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide
. 

---


<!-- Page 272 -->
Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

6. 
Select the Include variance amount, date, and user check box to display this information in 

the BVA note in the financial report. 

7. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the desired reporting period to include. 

For information about reporting periods, see Reporting periods in online help or download 
the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Reports User Guide
. 

8. 
If you selected a “Year to Date” reporting period, then you can select the Include prior 

period notes check box to include budget variance notes from a previous reporting period. 

For example, if you select this option and you run the report on March 31, then the report 

will display notes for January, February, and March. If you do not select this option and you 

run the report on March 31, then the report will display only YTD notes for March. 

9. 
In the Column heading 1 field, click the drop-down arrow to select a heading from the list. 

If the heading you want to use is not listed, select the Custom header option. A field is 
displayed that allows you to type a custom column heading. Click 
 Help for information 
about the column header. 

10. 
In the Column heading 2 field, click the drop-down arrow to select a heading from the list. 

If the heading that you want to use is not listed, select the Custom header option. A field 
is displayed that allows you to type a custom column heading. 

11. 
In the Column title field, the column header is pre-populated with the information in the 

Column type field. 

12. 
You can set the Expand by drop-down list to Location or Time period as needed. 

13. 
Select the Hide column check box when you want to hide this column from the financial 

report. 

14. 
When you run the report, the notes made during the budget variance analysis process 

appear in the column that you added, including the variance amount when the note was 

entered, the date the note was entered, and which user entered it.

KPIs in Financial Report Writer 

You can use the Financial Report Writer to enhance the way you look at financial data along with 

operational metrics. The Financial Report Writer can pull real-time metrics of your company’s 

financial and operation KPIs. For example, if you want to know capital expense for each unit 

(vacant units), you can display this by selecting predefined KPI groups in the Financial Report 

Writer. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use KPIs in financial reports.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

Use the Schedule financial report page to schedule a financial report to run automatically and 

routinely. You can schedule a financial report from the Financial reports list or from the Reports 

center. If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule 

Financial Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box to 

schedule reports and reports groups to run at that time. 

This page contains three sections: 

• 
Filters: Use this section to filter the scheduled report by specific criteria. 

• 
Schedule: Use this section to define the report schedule. 

• 
Delivery options: Use this section to choose how you want to deliver and store the report.

Financial Graphs 

Graphs help you visualize trends in your business, telling a story that goes beyond the numbers 

on a page. In addition to standard graphs that are included with applications, you can create any 

number of financial graphs. The graphs you create can be displayed on their own or added to a 

dashboard. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a

user’s permissions.

a) Use controls to select the graph data.

Preview and Refresh 

When you first create a graph, the preview is empty. Enter some basic graph information, and 

then click Refresh to start seeing the preview.

To create a financial graph: 

1. 
Enter a Name for the graph. 

2. 
Select the data you want to see in your graph. 

The data displayed by your graph is a combination of the data series (on page 307) you use 

to categorize values (for example, your columns or pie chart slices) and the accounting data 

you specify in Additional parameters. All graphs have at least a Primary data series. 

For some graph types, you can optionally include a Compare data series. 

Any data that isn’t selected as a data series is specified as Additional parameters. In the 

example above, reporting period is a data series but the main data that is being shown—in 

this case, revenue—is determined by the account group selected in Additional parameters. 

3. 
Select a graph type by clicking the corresponding icon. 

• 
The currently selected graph type appears in color. 

• 
Column graph is the default, but other graph types include pie, doughnut, line, 

column, bar, area, and waterfall. 

---


<!-- Page 306 -->
Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Hover over an icon to see name of the graph type. If the graph can be displayed only 

on-screen, “(HTML only)” is appended to the name, as in “Stacked column (HTML 

only).” 

4. 
Use Additional settings to refine your output. 

• 
Title, subtitle, and comment apply to PDF output only. 

• 
In most cases, you’ll want to leave the As of date blank to automatically use the 

current date, at the time the graph is displayed. You can override the date when the 

graph is viewed to see data from different time periods. 

• 
Select Hide zero numbers to remove data points that have no value. For example, if 

your graph compares revenue by customer, select this option to remove data points 

for customers with no associated revenue during the reporting period. 

5. 
Click to expand the Filters section and filter your report as needed. 

Filtering lets you select data based on segment, such as by location or department. You can: 

• 
Filter for a single segment member, such as a particular location. 

• 
Filter for multiple segment members, such as for a group of locations or a particular 

customer type.

#### Selecting Data for Financial Graphs
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 307*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Selecting Data for Financial Graphs 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Financial Reporting > 
 Financial Graphs`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Reports > Financial Statements > 
 Financial 
Graphs`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > 
 Financial Graphs`


When you create a financial graph, your choices for data series represent how you want to 

categorize the data. For example, a revenue graph can be broken down in multiple ways, such as 

by quarter, location, or customer. 

Primary vs. Compare Data Series 

Think of the Primary data series as the main way you want to categorize values, such as by 

reporting period, account group, segment, or segment structure (waterfall charts only). 

For some types of graphs, you have the option of showing a comparison within the primary data 

series. A Compare data series is available for all chart types except pie, doughnut, and waterfall. 

---


<!-- Page 308 -->
Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Data Series Options 

The way that data are displayed depends on the graph type. 

• 
Account groups: Categorizes data by one or more account groups. Example: Revenue vs. 

expense. 

• 
Reporting periods: Categorizes data by one or more reporting periods. Example: Four 

consecutive quarters. Although you can select individual reporting periods by moving them 

from Available to Selected, the quickest way to create a trend over time is to use the Period 

comparison options. 

• 
Budget comparison: Lets you compare Actual values against one or more budgets. 

This option is not available for pie, doughnut, or waterfall graphs. 

• 
Dimension: Categorizes data by the selected dimension. By default, the graph shows all 

members of each dimension. However, you can filter on a dimension group to show a 

subset of members. For example, suppose that you choose Locations as a data series. 

• 
By default, the graph shows all locations. 

• 
To restrict the list of locations, expand the Filters section. From the Location 

drop-down list, select a dimension group that represents the locations you want to 

include. 

• 
Dimension structure: In waterfall charts, categorizes data based on the substructures in a 

hierarchical dimension structure. 

This option is available only for waterfall graphs. 

Selecting a dimension structure, rather than a dimension, gives you the freedom to create 
intermediate columns based on how you want to organize and label the data.

Name 
Icon 
Primary data series

Pie

### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 319*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 320) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized—that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead.

### Storing Standard Reports and Charts
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 322*



#### Viewing a Stored Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 322*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

You can process and store the report or chart either before or after viewing it. 

Viewing a Stored Report 

After the system runs the report on the date that you selected, you can find the report in either 

the My stored reports list or the Reports center. 

To view a stored report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Open the application where you created the report. 

2. 
Select the My stored reports option located in the Reports column of the menu. 

The My stored reports list opens with a list of reports stored in the application. 

3. 
Find the report that you want to view and then verify the report date in the Run date/time 

column. Verifying the report date helps you avoid missing data. For example, if you 

scheduled the report to run two weeks ago, you would be missing the last two weeks of 

data. 

4. 
Click one of the following links to open your report in the format it was stored:  

• 
HTML: Opens the report in a new browser tab as a web page. 

• 
PDF: Opens a printable PDF version of the report that you can print and download. 

• 
CSV: Downloads a CSV file containing the report data. This is a good format to 

download if you want to import the data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Downloads the report as an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Opens a text version of the report in the web browser. 

• 
View Status: Opens the report in your configured cloud account. If there is no cloud 

link for the report, see Storing a Report in a Cloud Storage Location (on page 328). 

• 
Success: Opens the report in Reporting Portal. If there was an error processing the 

report, then the View status link appears in the column instead. See Viewing a Report 

Error Log for error details. 

If you have not yet processed the report offline, then click the Create offline link to process 
the report. 

---

Storing a Report in My Stored Reports 

You can generate reports on demand and store them in the My stored reports list for later 

access. 

To store a report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime (on page 249 ). 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand (on page 109 ). 

3. 
In the Delivery options section, select the Store report option. 

4. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report. 

If you ran the report on a location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, 
then the Location ID and Name is added to the end of the stored report name to easily 
identify which property the report is for.

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Saves reports in an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Saves the report as a text file.

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or 

Amazon S3. If you are a developer, you can also deliver the report to another application using 

HTTP. 

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets in RealPage Accounting. The targets that you 

define will be available as storage options for reports. 

To store a report in a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime (on page 249 ). 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand (on page 109 ). 

3. 
Select the Store in cloud check box. 

4. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the 

report.  

By default, you can choose from cloud-storage targets that either you ’ve defined or that 
others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, you can see all cloud 
targets. 

5. 
If you want to override the default path where the report is delivered in the cloud-storage 

target, then type a different path in the Path field. 

6. 
In the Report name field, type a name for the report.

### Memorized Reports
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 335*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 335*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Memorized Reports 

See the How to Get Here (on page 336) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Memorizing a report retains the report parameters so you don’t have to select them each time 

you want to run or display the report. When you memorize a report, you can assign it a unique 

name so you can add the report to dashboards or report groups or schedule it to run on a 

recurring basis. We recommend that you test run the report with the desired parameters to verify 

that the report output is correct before memorizing the report. 

A memorized report can be public or private. Public reports are available to all system users. 
Private reports are available only to the report owner and system administrators. 

Memorized Reports Locations 

Memorized reports appear in the Memorized reports list (on page 337) and in the Reports 

center. 

The Memorized reports list is accessible from most RealPage Financial Suite applications; 

however, it displays only the reports that were memorized in the application you access it from. 

For example, if you click the Memorized reports option in the Cash Management menu, then the 

list will include only reports memorized in Cash Management. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Memorizing a report requires that you have the permissions to do so. You must have permissions 

to access and run a report in order to memorize it. Permissions for users, groups, or roles are 

configured in the Company setup. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

How to Get Here

Reports > Memorized Reports`

Memorizing a Report or Chart 

To memorize a report or chart: 

1. 
Set up a report or chart with the filters and parameters that you want to save. 

2. 
Click the Memorize button. The Memorize report parameters box opens. 

3. 
In the Name field, type a name for the report or chart. 

If you plan to make the report or chart public, give it a name that is easily identifiable to 
others. 

4. 
Select the Public check box to make the report or chart available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to keep it private. Private reports and charts are 

visible only to the person who created them (owners), and administrators. 

5. 
Click OK.

Memorized Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 336) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Memorized reports list to view and manage reports that you saved in an application or 

that other users saved and then made public. From this list, you can:

• 
Edit memorized reports that you created. 

•

•

•

•

#### Editing a Memorized Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 338*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Editing a Memorized Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 336) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

You can edit a memorized report or chart only if you are the owner or a system administrator, 

even if the report or chart was made public. As the owner, you can change any parameter, 

including who owns it. The only field you cannot change is the report type.  

To edit a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, click the Edit link next to the report or chart that you want to 

change. The Edit memorized report page opens. The fields on this page correspond with 

the report’s type.  

2. 
Update the fields in the General information section as needed: 

• 
In the Report name and Report description fields, type a new name and description 

for the report, respectively. 

• 
In the Report owner drop-down list, select a different user to be the owner of the 

report. If you change the report’s owner, then you will no longer be able to edit this 

memorized report after you save the changes. However, you can continue to run the 

report if it’s still public.  

• 
Select the Public check box to make the report available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to make the report private; that is, 

available only to yourself and system administrators. 

Others can see private memorized reports by selecting the Include private check box 
in their Memorized reports list. 

3. 
Modify the other settings as needed. 

4. 
Click Save. 

---



#### Running a Memorized Report or Chart
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 339*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Running a Memorized Report or Chart 

See the How to Get Here (on page 336) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

To run a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, find the report or chart you want to view, and then click the 

Run link.  

2. 
In the Select report type drop-down list, select a format for the report or chart output:  

• 
HTML: Saves the report as an HTML file so you can view it in your web browser. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report as a comma-separated value (CSV) file so you can import the 

data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Saves the report as an Excel file so you can manipulate the data further. 

• 
Text: Saves the report as a basic text file.  

Charts are only available in Printable and HTML format. 

3. 
Click OK to run the report. 

• 
If you selected Printable, HTML, or Text, then the report opens in a new window. 

• 
If you selected CSV or Excel, then the system saves the report in your local Downloads 

folder. 

You can also run a memorized report from the Reports center.

#### Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 340*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here (on page 336) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report (on page 347) page 

opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report (on page 347) page opens. 

---


<!-- Page 341 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups (on page 249), then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or 

more G/L account groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use. 

---


<!-- Page 342 -->
Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.   

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save.

### Custom Reports
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 354*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Custom Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > Custom Reports`


In addition to standard and financial reports, you can build custom reports. Create custom reports 

to get insight and answers from the unique information stored in your system. Financial reports 

are based on account groupings such as assets and liabilities, while custom reports and 

dimension structures are based on records and fields either grouped together or separately. 

For example, you can create a custom report that displays vendor contact information. You can 

control which vendors you want to display, such as active vendors in certain regions, and select 

the details to include about the vendors. You can then sort and display the results to highlight 

what is most important to you. 

With a custom report, you can: 

• 
Report on fields from almost any record or transaction in the system, and any related data. 

• 
Customize the report for your needs. 

• 
Run the reports, export them in another format, or add them to dashboards. 

Before you can export a report or add it to a group, you need to memorize the report (on 
page 335 ).  

Creating Custom Reports 

Custom reports are created with the custom report wizard, which walks you through the steps to 

create a report. Only users who have permission to Customization Services can add and edit 

reports by going to the Custom Reports list on the Customization services menu. 

You can run the custom report from the Reports application. 

Adding a Custom Report to an Application’s Menu 

If you use a custom report on a regular basis, you can add the custom report to an application’s 

menu. For example, a report with payables-related data can be added to the Accounts Payable 

menu. After adding a custom report to the A/P menu, you can run the custom report by clicking 

the Custom Reports menu option, which displays a list of all of the custom reports that you have 

added to the Accounts Payable menu. 

The Custom Reports option displays on menus only after you (or someone else) has added at 

least one custom report to the application’s menu. The Custom Reports option does not appear 

on a menu if no one has added any custom reports to the application’s menu.

#### Selecting the Primary Data Source
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 358*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Custom Report Wizard 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > 
 Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > 
 Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > New Report > Custom Report > 
Create with Custom Report Wizard`


Use the Custom report wizard to create specialized reports from your company data. Unlike 

financial and standard reports, custom reports can include financial or non-financial data, or both, 

drawing on data from existing fields or your company’s custom fields. 

Selecting the Primary Data Source 

Choose a record or transaction as a starting point for your report. 

Records 

A record is any piece of information in your company. The records available for selection are 

based on your user permissions; you cannot select a record you don’t have access to. When a 

record is selected, other related information is available for inclusion in your report. 

For example, if you select Customer as your primary data source, you can include column 

information from the Contact, Parent customer, or Customer type records. 

Transactions 

You can select a transaction type as your primary data source, such as A/P invoice, A/R 

adjustment, or Deposits. These options include all header information in the transaction record. If 

you want to include the header information plus any amounts and line-item details from the 

transaction, then select the data source option labeled “detail,” such as A/P invoice detail, A/R 

adjustment detail, or Deposits details. This allows you to access transaction amounts and use the 

custom report writer to add calculated columns later in the process. 

For example, to list all invoices with line items over $10,000, you can start by choosing the data 

source A/P invoice detail. Your report can include columns of information from A/P invoice 

details and related data. 

When you run a custom report for User Permission Activity, this custom report only shows 
permissions which have been explicitly activated by an administrator. There are other 
permissions which are switched on by other applications, called derived permissions. To see a 
complete list of your permissions, run a User Permissions report. 

---



#### Defining Columns
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 359*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Defining Columns 

Define the columns in your report using the following procedures. 

Add Columns 

Select the data that you want to add to your report. Each check box represents one column in the 

report. 

It is better to include more information than you need at this point in creating your report. In 
later steps, you can refine which data to display. 

The following icons are used to help you identify information you want to use in your report: 

• 
: identifies a linked field. When you run the report, you can see more information by 

clicking the link. 

• 
: identifies a custom field. 

Viewing custom fields is dependent on your permissions. If you include custom fields in your 
report and then deploy the report to an application, the custom fields might or might not 
be visible to other users, depending on their permission levels. 

• 
: identifies an expandable subsection of the primary data source. If a subsection is also a 

data source, when you expand it, the system displays the data source’s subsections with 

additional data, possibly even additional subsections, that you can include as columns in 

your report. 

For multi-entity companies: Click Created at entity information below a transaction or object, 
and then select what you want to track. For anything created at the top level, the report will 
show a blank entry. 

---


<!-- Page 360 -->
Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Add Calculated Columns 

The custom report writer also allows you to create column calculations based on the columns you 

selected. 

For example, you can calculate an employee’s commission by multiplying their commission rate 

by the total number of sales invoices attributed to that employee. When you run the report, the 

system displays the calculation in the report in a column with the name you assigned. 

You can add calculations by creating a formula uses columns of information from your data 

source. This lets you perform operations on other columns in your data source and then show 

results in your report. 

The formulas created follow the mathematical order or operations. Keep the following order of 

operations in mind when you create a formula: 

• 
Calculations inside parentheses are performed first. 

• 
All multiplications and divisions are performed next, working from left to right. 

• 
Lastly, all additions and subtractions are performed, working from left to right. 

To create a formula for a calculated column: 

Calculations can only be applied to columns containing numbers. 

1. 
Click the Add button. 

The system opens the Formula Editor box. Use this editor to create a formula from any of 

the information in your primary data source. You can add multiple columns and operator, 

depending on the calculation you want to display. 

2. 
In the Available Report Columns pane, select the column containing the data you want to 

include in the calculation. For example, select AP Invoice Detail Total Due. 

---


<!-- Page 361 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

The system adds an expression in the Formula pane. 

3. 
Use the basic math operators (addition +, subtraction -, multiplication *, and division /) and 

parentheses to create a formula. For example, click the subtraction operator under the 

Operators column. 

4. 
In the Available Report Columns pane, select the column containing the date included in 

the calculation. For example, select AP Invoice Detail Transaction amount. 

The system displays an expression for the transaction in the Formula pane. 

5. 
In the Calculated column type drop-down list, select the formula format. 

6. 
In the Calculated column name field, enter a label for the column.

#### Filtering the Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 362*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Select the Column Sequence 

1. 
Drag columns into the order that you want the system to display them in your report. 

2. 
Optionally, use the text box to rename columns in the report. 

Add Column Totals 

Select the check boxes next to the columns for which you want to display a summary. You can 

only perform mathematical summaries, such as count, sum, average, std deviation, variance, 

largest, and smallest, on numeric data fields. Text fields are limited to count summaries. 

In a report without grouping, the system displays the calculations at the bottom of the report for 

the entire table. In a report with grouping, the system displays the calculations for each subgroup 

and for the entire table. 

Sort the Columns and Set the Priority 

1. 
Click the drop-down list next to each column title. 

2. 
Select whether you want to sort the column in Ascending or Descending order, or None. 

You can assign an ascending or descending order to a maximum of four columns. 

3. 
Drag and drop the columns in the list to change the sorting priority. 

The column in the first position will be sorted first, the next column down will be sorted 

within the first, and so on. 

Filtering the Report 

You can use filters in your report to limit the data the system displays to the criteria that you 

choose. 

Select a Filter 

You set the first group of filters when you select the columns from your primary data source. 

Other information related to your primary data source are available to use as filters as well and 

are listed under the first group of filters as expandable objects. 

1. 
Expand the object that has the column or field you want to filter. 

2. 
In the Columns column, click a drop-down list, and then select the column by which you 

want to filter. 

3. 
In the Operator column, select the operator you want to use to filter the column. 

See the list of available operators (on page 370). 

4. 
In the Value column, enter the corresponding value. 

This can be a number or a string of text depending on the chosen operator. If you choose 

Includes or Excludes, the value could be a comma delimited list of numbers or text strings. 

---


<!-- Page 363 -->
Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

5. 
Click the Add filter link below the columns to add more filters in the object. 

6. 
Click the Delete last filter link to remove a filter field. 

Refine the Filters 

By default, all filter conditions are combined with an AND logic. In this step, you can apply more 

advanced logic using OR conditions and group filters. 

1. 
Review the filters you added in the previous step. 

The system displays filter position numbers, which you can use to create your advanced 

filter statement. 

2. 
In the Filter expression field, combine filter position numbers using logical operators and 

parentheses. 

For example, you want to filter a report to display transactions for customer accounts within 

the 2010-3010 range or the 6010-7010 range, and the total paid amount is greater than 0.

#### Grouping Data
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 364*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Grouping Data 

Enable Grouping 

Set the level of detail you want the system to display in your report by selecting the appropriate 

grouping option. 

• 
No grouping: Select this format if you want to display a flat list of information, with the 

option to show a grand total at the bottom. For example, you can use this format to display 

a list of employees with their contact information, or a list of invoices with their total dollar 

value. 

• 
Grouping: Select this format if you want to arrange the information together and show 

subtotals for grouped rows. By default, the report shows subtotals based on the groups you 

select in succeeding steps. The system automatically includes totals by group. For example, 

you can use this format to display invoice subtotals by customer and invoice totals for all 

customers. 

Group Data by Columns 

You can only group data by columns if you enable the Grouping option in the previous step. 

1. 
Expand the object that contains the column by which you want to group the report. 

2. 
Select the column from the drop-down list. 

When you select multiple columns, the system creates subgroups in the report. 

Grouping the data by more than three columns could distort the data. As a best practice, 
only group by three or less columns. 

Order the Groups 

You can set which groups take priority when sorted. The system sorts the items first by the first 

column, and then by the second column, and so on, creating multiple levels of summary 

information. 

1. 
In the Position column, select the button next to the column you want to move. 

2. 
If a column has child columns, select the Include Children check box to enable the feature. 

3. 
Use the 
 Top, 
 Up, 
 Down, and 
 Bottom arrows to change the sorting priority 

of the column. 

4. 
In the Sort column, use the corresponding drop-down list to select whether you want to 

sort your columns in ascending or descending order. 

Group Totals 

In a report with grouping, the system displays the calculations for each subgroup and for the 

entire table. Select the desired column totals in the Add more totals step. For more information, 

see Defining columns (on page 359).

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 365*

Setting the Report Date and Title 

You can set parameters for running the report, such as the reporting period and the title of the 

report. 

1. 
Select a reporting period or a range of dates. 

• 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select monthly, quarterly, or annual options 

that include next, current, and past periods. You can modify this time period by adding 

an As of date value. 

• 
In Start date and End date fields, select an exact date range for the report. 

2. 
Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

If your company is comprised of multiple entities with multiple base currencies, set the 

location and department. 

• 
Select the Location and Department for which you want to run the report. 

• 
In the Show for drop-down list, select whether you want to display All locations, This 

location, or Child locations, regardless of the location you selected in the Location 

field. 

If you enabled the “p” in the As of Date field of the Filters section on the Schedule 

Financial Report page, select the Run as of the last day of the prior month check box 
to schedule reports and reports groups to run at that time. 

3. 
In the Show details field, select whether you want to hide or display the detail lines that 

make up the calculated amounts. Hiding the detail gives you a high-level breakdown of the 

data, showing just subtotal and total calculations. 

4. 
Set the report title and footer. 

• 
In the Report title 1 and Report title 2 fields, enter the first and second lines of the 

report title, respectively. 

• 
In the Footer text field, add information you want to display at the bottom of the 

report pages. 

Titles and footers can use letters, numbers, spaces, and most punctuation. The system 

does not support wild cards and variables.

Defining the Chart Output 

You can choose to run a chart format to visually display your information.

Adding Prompts 

The additional prompts you can add at runtime are similar to filters, in that they filter the data 

according to the criteria you set. Unlike filters, these prompts are set up as fields that the user 

specifies at the time they run the report. For example, if you want the user running the report to 

specify the A/R status regarding the invoice from which the item comes, you can add a prompt 

for the A/R Account Label object, and then select the Status field. 

To select a runtime prompt: 

1. 
Expand the section for the object that contains the field. 

2. 
Select the check box next to the field for which you want to add a prompt. 

3. 
Repeat the steps to add more prompts. 

You can select up to six runtime prompts. 

If you run the report from the Custom reports list, the system ignores the filters and runs the 

report without any prompts. To ensure that all your filters and prompts are applied, run the 

custom report from the application in which you saved it. Learn more about saving a report to a 

menu (on page 369).

Labeling and Grouping Prompts 

You only need to label and organize prompts if you chose to include additional prompts in the 

previous step of the custom report writer. 

This page allows you to control how a prompt field will be labeled, how multiple fields will be 

grouped, and whether it will have a prompt at runtime. 

Change the Prompt Label 

By default, the name of the field is provided as the Prompt Label. 

To change the Prompt Label, click the Prompt label field and type the label you prefer. 

Group Prompts 

The Group field allows you to present your prompts in groups when you run the report. 

For example, if you want to group several fields together in a section titled A/R Parameters, for

On a report with several prompts, grouping fields with meaningful labels can save time for the 

person running the report.

Saving the Report 

The final step of the custom report writer allows you to save your report and add your report to 

an application menu. This makes it available to other users who have access to that application. 

Save and Deploy Your Report to an Application Menu 

1. 
In the Name field, type your preferred report name. 

2. 
Select the Add to menu check box. 

To access your report only through the Custom reports list, leave the Add to menu check 
box clear. However, we recommend that you add your custom report to an application 
menu. If you run the report from the Custom reports list, the system omits filters and 
prompts. When you run the report from the application menu, the report presents all 
prompts and filters. 

3. 
In the Application drop-down list, select the application to which you want to add the 

report. 

4. 
In the Description field, enter optional text to describe your report. 

5. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether you want the report to be Active or Inactive. 

New reports are set to Active by default. 

6. 
Click the Save button at the top of the page to save your report.  

Your report is saved and added to both the application menu you selected and to the list of 

reports. 

Make the Custom Report Available in Other Places 

One of the advantages of custom reports is that you can schedule them to run at different times 

with the same settings and make them available in dashboards and report groups. To take 

advantage of this feature: 

• 
Memorize the report so it can be run again with the same settings. 

• 
Add a memorized report to a dashboard or report group. 

• 
Schedule a memorized report.

##### Operator Definitions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 370*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Operator Definitions 

The following operators are available for use when filtering: 

• 
Equals: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column matches the text or 

number in the Value field. 

• 
Less than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is less 

than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

greater than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Less or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

less than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen 

column is greater than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Not equal to: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column does not match 

the text or number in the Value field. 

• 
Contains: Displays all records in which a character or group of characters in the chosen 

column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The characters must 

match in the same order. For example, “ox” typed in the Value field may return records for 

Oxygen Inc., Boxing Agency, and Clorox, if those were values in the chosen column. 

• 
Does not contain: Displays all records in which no character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. 

• 
Starts with: Displays all records in which the first character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you have an item ID scheme that 

uses initial letters to identify the product type, you can select the item ID column and set the 

Value field to these letters to display all records for that product type. 

• 
Ends with: Displays all records in which the last character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you tag the end of the item ID for 

all custom order items with the letters “CO,” you can select the item ID column and set the 

value to CO to display all records for custom order items. 

• 
Includes: Displays all records that match items in a comma delimited list in the Value field. 

• 
Excludes: Displays all records that do not match items in a comma delimited list in the 

Value field. 

• 
Field equals null: Displays all records that have a null or empty field. 

• 
Field not equals null: Displays all records that do not have a null or empty field. 

---



#### Running a Custom Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 371*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns. 

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 

Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 

of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

% bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank,” like Metropolis Bank. 

Running a Custom Report 

When a custom report is created, the report designer has the option to add (or “deploy”) the 

report to an application, such as General Ledger, Accounts Payable, or Accounts Receivable. 

Deploying the report to an application makes the report available from the application menu and 

from the Report Center. 

To run a report from the Reports center page, go to Running a Report from Reports Center. 

To run a custom report from an application menu: 

1. 
Go to the application whose report you want to run, and then click the corresponding link 

for the custom report that you want to run. 

2. 
Set the filters as needed. 

3. 
Do one of the following options: 

• 
Click View to display the report in HTML. 

• 
Click Print to display the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
Click the Export drop-down list, select your preferred format, and then click Go.

#### Copying a Custom Report from One Company or Entity to Another

Copying a Custom Report from One Company or Entity to Another 

If you’re using the Custom report wizard and have a report that you want to copy from one 

company to another, you can create a custom package document to transfer your custom report. 

You must have administrator -level privileges to access the Platform Services (or Customization 
Services) application. 

Creating a Report Definition Package 

1. 
Sign into the company whose report definition you want to copy. 

2. 
In the Applications menu, select Platform Services (or Customization Services), and then 

select the Custom reports option. The Custom reports page opens. 

3. 
Locate the report that you want to copy, and then click the corresponding View link. The 

Custom report wizard opens. 

4. 
In the Step drop-down list, select Save and add to menu. 

5. 
Click the Export def button. The system downloads the report to your local drive as an XML 

file. 

Preparing the Package 

Modify the package to prepare it for importing to the second company or entity. 

1. 
Open a text edit and paste the following XML wrapper text into a new file: 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 

<customErpPackage 
xmlns:xsi=“http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance”> 

<packageDescription> 

<name>INSERT NAME HERE</name> 

<description>INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE</description> 

<author>AUTHOR NAME</author> 

</packageDescription> 


> **Navigation Path:** `<customReports>`


<!-- Paste the contents of the file here--> 


> **Navigation Path:** `</customReports>`


</customErpPackage> 

1. 
Do not close the file. 

---


<!-- Page 376 -->
Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding the Definition to the XML File 

1. 
Using a text editor, open the report XML file you downloaded to your local drive. 

2. 
Copy the entire contents of the file. 

3. 
Go back to the XML wrapper file you created in the previous procedure. 

4. 
Paste the report code into the XML wrapper file in the space after the text <!--Paste the 

contents of the file here-->. 

5. 
Delete the following text: 

<!--Paste the contents of the file here--> 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 

Only delete the second instance of <?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?>. 
This is included in the report XML. The first instance at the top of the file should remain. 

6. 
Inside the XML wrapper section, replace the following with your own information: 

• 
INSERT NAME HERE 

• 
INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE 

• 
AUTHOR NAME 

7. 
Save the file with a new name. 

The new file should look similar to the following. The actual report definition was edited for 

this example.

##### Property Report Groups
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide.pdf`, Page 389*

Chapter 3: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Investor Tracking User Guide 

Property Report Groups 

Instead of running reports one at a time, you can create a group of reports that run at the same 

time. Create property report packages using the Property Report Groups menu option in 

Investor Tracking.  

Property report groups can include owner statements and any memorized reports. Property 

report groups are created for one property that you choose when you are setting it up. To 

complete the package, you can add a cover letter to the group that introduces the reports. 

Workflow 

• 
Create a property report group. 

• 
Run the report group. 

• 
Send the resulting report package to the Investor Portal. 

Running the Report Group 

You can run a property report group as needed, or you can run the report group on a schedule. 

Unlike individual reports, report groups aren’t added to or run from application menus. You must 

access and run report groups from the Reports Center. 

Sending the Package of Reports 

After generating the package of reports, you can send it to the investor portal. To send the 

package of reports generated by a property report group to investors, see Running a Property 

Report Group (on page 394). When you select the investors in storage options, the system 

uploads the reports to a system-generated property-specific folder in the investors portal. 

You can instead choose to store the reports and send them to the investor portals later. See 

Uploading Reports and Documents to an Investor Portal (on page 67).

Select Store in cloud to store the reports in a secure, cloud-based location such as 

Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or Amazon S3.  

• 
Select Store in Reporting Portal to send the report to the investors’ portal. To do this: 

• 
Type the name for the report group in the Report name field. 

• 
In the Report type drop-down list, select Printable to save the report as a 

printable PDF file. Select Excel to save the reports in an Excel file. 

• 
In the Investor list, select the investors where you want to send the reports to 

their portals.  

2. 
Click OK. 

If you choose to store the report, you can upload the reports to the investor portal later. 
See Uploading Reports and Documents to an Investor Portal (on page 67 ).

### RealPage Financial Suite
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

Introduction 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The RealPage Financial Suite integrates a traditional back-office accounting system with general 

ledger, cash management, accounts receivable, and accounts payable applications with new and 

updated applications that let you save valuable time by streamlining and automating your daily 

processes and workflow. Some applications described in the documentation are optional and can 

be purchased through RealPage sales. RealPage Financial Suite is composed of RealPage 

Accounting core applications, optional applications, and add-on applications.  

The RealPage Accounting suite contains these core accounting applications: 

• 
Accounts Payable: Use the Accounts Payable application to manage vendor records, pay 

vendors, create custom terms, adjust accounts with credit and debit memos, and create and 

print A/P reports. 

• 
Accounts Receivable: Use the Accounts Receivable application to manage the full A/R cycle, 

manage customer records, receivables transactions, and generate reports, create and send 

invoices, apply penalties and adjust accounts, make deposits, and deliver statements. 

• 
Company: Use the Company application to manage your company setup and to set up user 

accounts. Administrators can define security and global settings, grant permissions to users, 

and manage subscriptions to applications and services. 

• 
Dashboard: Use Dashboards to get real-time snapshots of information. 

• 
General Ledger: Use the General Ledger application to post journal entries, design and run 

reports, create budgets, and more. The General Ledger is the central ledger for the 

company. 

• 
Cash Management: Use the Cash Management application to manage your cash accounts, 

including checking accounts, savings institutions, and credit cards. 

• 
Reporting Portal: Use the Reporting Portal application to set up owner portals for owners 

and investors so you can upload financial reports and other documents for them in a central 

location. 

• 
Reports: Use customizable reports to get real-time snapshots of information. 

• 
Platform (Customization) Services: Administrators use the Platform Services (or 

Customization Services) application to customize and extend the RealPage Accounting 

system. 

• 
Multi-entity: Administrators use the Multi-entity application to set up and run multi-entity 

shared companies. 

• 
Forecasting & Planning: Use this application to create and refine budgets, and to associate 

properties with a budget when publishing it. 

---

Chapter 1: Introduction
