These applications are part of RealPage Accounting core applications, but are optional as not all 

of our clients need them: 

• 
Global Consolidations: This application is used by multi-currency companies. 

• 
Taxes: This application is used by companies who are required to collect and report value 

added taxes (VAT) to the United Kingdom’s tax authority, HM Revenue & Customs. 

The RealPage Financial Suite contains RealPage Accounting applications, plus additional 

applications that you can purchase to extend and enhance the functionality of the suite. 

• 
Job Cost and Reserves: Use this application to manage costs for property improvements 

and new developments. 

If your company does not subscribe to Job Cost, then use the standalone Replacement 

Reserves application to track replacement and repair expenses and request 
reimbursements from lenders. 

• 
Spend Management: Use this application to set up a budget and bring visibility to 

spending, to analyze the impact of sourcing strategies, assess business savings, and review 

compliance with preferred suppliers and contracts. 

• 
Commercial Property Management: Use this application to set up your properties, 

locations, floors, and units and then configure and manage billing, including straight line 

rent billing, and percentage rent billing. Manage the billing and payment cycle, including 

inter-entity billing, collecting fees, and recovering expenses. 

• 
Condo and Co-op: Use this application to set up condominiums and co-operatives and then 

manage owners, bill dues and other charges, and manage unit maintenance.  

• 
Financial Close Management: Use this application to simplify your month-end and year-end 

close processes by reconciling work papers into one package that you can download and 

open in Excel. 

• 
Fixed Assets: Use this application to manage your assets, including depreciation and asset 

disposal.  

• 
Investor Tracking: Use this application to track contributions from and distributions to 

investors. Using this application, you can invoice contributions, calculate and pay out 

distributions, and run reports of these activities.  

• 
Procore Integration: Integrate Job Cost with the Procore construction management 

platform to synchronize job information, job budgets, and cost totals between the two 

systems.  

To purchase any of the add-ons, contact your RealPage Account Representative.

Logging In Through Unified Platform

In your web browser, access the RealPage home URL (https://www.realpage.com/home). The 

login page opens. 

2.

• 
To save your user name to the login page, select the Remember me check box. 

3.

4.

5. 
Click Login. 

6. 
If your company does not use multi-factor authentication, skip to step 9. If your company 

uses RealPage multi-factor authentication, follow the instructions on the screen to verify 

your identity by providing the authentication code. You must have multi-factor 

authentication set up in your Unified Platform profile.

Forgot Password Link 

If you forget your RealPage Unified Platform password, click the Forgot Password? link on the 

login page, answer your security questions, and create a new password. If you cannot answer your 

security questions, contact your Administrator to set a temporary password for your account. 

This information applies if you are logging on to RealPage Unified Platform directly, as shown 
below. If you are using a third-party identity service provider to log on to the RealPage Unified 
Platform, then this information does not apply to you, and you must use your provider’s 
password change procedure. 

To reset your password from the RealPage Unified Platform log on page: 

1. 
Click the Forgot Password? link. 

2. 
Answer your security questions, and then click Continue. 

3. 
Type a new password. The password must meet the following criteria: 

• 
8–20 characters (The default is eight, but your company can change it.) 

• 
One uppercase letter 

• 
One lowercase letter 

• 
One number 

• 
One special character, such as !@&#$% 

4. 
Retype the new password, and then click Change Password. 

5. 
After a message displays indicating that you changed your password successfully, log on 

again. 

• 
Click Next. 

• 
Type the new password. 

• 
Click Login.

Header 

The header at the top of each RealPage Financial Suite page contains a number of key system 

features. Some options appear only if your company has installed Spend Management or enabled 

Full Service Spend Management. 

a) Level Menu: Click the

with the selected entity’s data. 

b) 
 Shopping Cart: Click this button to open the shopping cart associated with Spend 

Management’s Storefront application. This icon appears only if your company has installed 

the Spend Management application. 

c) 
 Help: Click this button to open the RealPage Financial Suite help system and access 

other learning resources. 

d) 
 Notifications: Click this button to view your notifications. Notifications come from 

RealPage and from RealPage applications. 

e) User Name: Click your name to access your preferences (on page 42) or log out of the 

system. 

f) 
 Home: Click this button to return to the Home page.

h) 
 Favorites: Click this option to access your favorite menu options anywhere in the system. 

i) 
Search Menu: Type the name of any menu option in this field to view a list of matching 

menu options across the RealPage Financial Suite. Select an option to open the 

corresponding page. 

j) 
 Bookmarks: Click this button to view your bookmarks and access bookmarked pages. 

k) Full Service Exception Queue: Click this button to view invoices in the exception queue. This 

option appears only if your company has installed Spend Management and enabled Full 

Service Spend Management. The number represents the number of invoices in the 

exception queue.  

The exception queue is associated with Accounts Payable and Spend Management.

### Levels
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 25*

Chapter 2: Navigation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Levels 

The Financial Suite lets you work at either the top level—where anything you create is shared 

across all entities—or at an individual entity level, where your additions apply only to that specific 

entity. 

Be mindful of where you are working when you create new records. Items created at the top level 

are available to every entity, while items created within an entity belong only to that entity and 

are considered private. 

Many property management companies (PMCs) create a bank account at the entity level so that it 

can only be accessed for that entity. Typically, PMCs also create one bank account at the top level 

that all entities can use. 

Some records can only be created at the top level, such as G/L accounts, prepaid journal entries, 
vendor, and customer records. 

The (Level) menu appears above the menu selector.  

---



#### Selecting Levels
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 26*

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide

Selecting Levels 

You can work at the top level or an entity’s level. By default, when you open the Financial Suite, 

you are working at the top level. 

To go to an entity’s level: 

1. 
Click the (Level) menu in the top header. A drop-down list of entities opens. 

2. 
Select an entity.  

A new browser tab opens for the selected entity.  

---


<!-- Page 27 -->
Chapter 2: Navigation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

a) 
This is the Top-level tab where the RealPage Financial Suite system continues to run 

with access to all entities. Top level access remains active in the original tab. You can 

freely switch back and forth between tabs, working in either tab. 

b) 
This is an entity’s tab. When you are working in an entity, the system displays the 

entity’s name in its assigned color, and the color also appears in the lines of the 

header. 

Any changes you make in an individual entity affects only that entity. For example: 

If you create a location at the entity level, then the location is associated only with the entity 

and is considered private. If you were to switch to the top level tab and view the Locations 

list, the location does not appear in the list unless the Include private check box is selected. 

(The Include private check box is selected by default.) 

When you view the Locations list at the entity level, the list includes only the location 

records that belong to the selected entity. 

3. 
When you have finished working with the selected entity, close the entity’s tab to return to 

the original tab, where the top level continues to be active. 

You can also click the All entities option, and then select a different entity to open.

Financial Suite Home Page 

Wherever you are in the system, you can always return to the Home page by clicking the 

Home button. The Home page is your dashboard for the system. Click the title bar of any section 

on the Home page to collapse or expand the section. 

If you prefer, you can choose a page other than the Home page to have the system display when 

you open the application. See Setting Up Display Preferences (on page 51). 

The Home page includes the following sections: 

a) (Dashboard): Click the Add action card button to add or remove action cards from your 

Financial Suite Home page. Action cards can display the number of invoices, purchase 

orders, or payments that are awaiting your approval, budget variance analysis (BVA) periods 

that are still open, service tickets that have been assigned to you, or payments that have 

been submitted in the last 30 days. When your company subscribes to the AI Finance Agent 

application, the action cards can include AI agent-related activities, like the number of 

invoices processed by the AI agent, missing expenses, automated accruals, and bank 

reconciliations. 

b) Important Updates & Information: RealPage adds news about the latest content from 

RealPage Financial Suite to keep you informed. Check this section for continuously updated 

news; it provides easy access to the latest RealPage Financial Suite release notes and 

demonstrations. 

---

which industry experts demonstrate the latest features and applications of the RealPage

d) Entities: This section lists all the entities set up for your company. Each entity represents a 

separate tax identification or a separately secured, fully balancing set of books. 

This section appears only for multi-entity shared companies.

Finance Agent Action Cards 

The AI Finance Agent offers additional action cards that you can add to the Financial Suite Home 

Page. These action cards provide a snapshot of tasks that the Finance Agent has completed and 

that now require your action. These are the Finance Agent action cards: 

• 
Bank Reconciliation 

• 
AI Invoice Queue Count 

• 
Missing Expenses - Current Month 

• 
Missing Expenses - Prior Month 

• 
Automated Accruals - Current Month 

• 
Automated Accruals - Prior Month 

Prerequisites 

Before the Finance Agent action cards can appear on the Home page, you must have the 

following: 

• 
Your company must subscribe to the AI Finance Agent application. 

• 
You must have permissions to view each type of data. For example, to view the AI invoice 

queue count, you must have the View permission for A/P invoices and the Run permission 

for the AI Invoice Queue. 

AI Finance Agent Action Cards 

Clicking a number in an action card opens the task list associated with the action. 

AI Invoice Queue Count: This card displays the number of invoices that have been AI-processed 

and that are in queue.  

• 
Click the number to open the AI-Invoice Queue list where you can view, edit, review, and 

archive AI-processed invoices. You can also upload and scan invoices from this list.

reconciliations, and the number of reconciliations that are pending approval. 

• 
Click the Open number to open the Pending Bank Reconciliations list. 

• 
Click the Pending approval number to open the Approve Bank Reconciliations list where 

you can view and approve or decline reconciliations. 

Missing Expenses - Current Month: The categories that appear on this action card are 

determined by the four vendor types that have the most missing expenses for the current month. 

The rest of the categories are combined in the Other category.  

•

list opens filtered for Landscaping vendors.

### To Do List on the Financial Suite Home Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 41*

Chapter 2: Navigation 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

To Do List on the Financial Suite Home Page 

The To Do list on the Financial Suite Home page shows tasks that the AI Finance Agent has 

started and that are waiting for you to complete the final steps. Clicking the View button opens a 

corresponding list of transactions that have been processed by AI. 

Prerequisites 

• 
Your company must subscribe to the AI Finance Agent. 

• 
The tasks that appear depend on your permissions. 

AI Finance Agent Tasks 

Tasks that may appear in the To Do List include:  

• 
Pending Reconciliation - Bank Rec: This task appears when a bank reconciliation is pending 

your approval. Select the View button to open the Approve Reconciliations list. 

• 
Approval Needed - Invoice Approvals: This task appears when invoices require your 

approval. Select the View button to open the Approval workbench. 

• 
Invoice Entry - AI Invoice: This task appears when the AI agent has received and processed 

invoices and place them in the queue. Click the View button to open the AI-Invoice Queue 

list. 

• 
Review Needed - Missing Expenses: This task appears when the AI agent has identified 

missing expenses and has placed them in the list for your review. Select the View button to 

open the Missing Expenses list. 

• 
Review Needed - Accruals: This task appears when the AI agent has calculated accruals that

User Preferences 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide

My Preferences Page 

(User Name) > My Preferences 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


Use the Preferences page to adjust your individual user preferences to better suit how you work 

in RealPage Financial Suite. You can also adjust some of the default security preferences set by 

your company administrator. For example, if your administrator sets a maximum interval of six 

hours before you are automatically signed out but you only need to be in the system for two 

hours, you can change that interval. 

The Preferences page contains the following sections: 

• 
General information: Use this section to add and modify your contact information, 

including the name and email address used to identify you in the system. The system 

automatically updates this information in your contact record. Your phone number and 

address are optional. 

• 
Security preferences: Use this section to create a password security question, adjust system 

timeouts, and change your password. 

• 
Email notifications: Use this section to add signature information for sending email 

notifications and select the types of notifications you want to receive. 

• 
On-screen messages: Use this section to select display preferences for on-screen messages 

and warnings. 

• 
Display: Use this section to personalize your system display. 

• 
Check preferences: Use this section to upload a digital signature for checks. 

• 
General preferences: Use this section to set your time zone, date and time format, 

language, and bookmarks. 

• 
Approval delegates: Use this section to reroute approval requests to a specific delegate in 

your absence. 

• 
Mobile app preferences for service requests: Use this section to set your display 

preferences for service requests. 

The options on this page may vary based on your user type. For example, external users cannot 
change their passwords from this page.

#### Setting Inactivity and Session Timeouts
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 57*

Chapter 3: User Preferences 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Setting Inactivity and Session Timeouts 

(User Name) > My Preferences  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


To protect company security, you can set timeouts for when the system should automatically sign 

you out. The system measures two kinds of activity: 

• 
Inactivity duration: Set the amount of time your system can remain inactive (when you 

aren’t using it) before it signs you out. The maximum amount of time that you can set is 

limited by the maximum amount of inactivity hours set for your entire organization, which is 

six hours or less. 

• 
Session duration: Set the amount of time that you can be in the system if you’re actively 

using it. The maximum amount of time you can set is limited by the maximum number of 

hours set for your entire organization, which is 12 hours or less. 

For example, say you set a six-hour session duration and a two-hour inactivity duration. If you 

continuously work in the system, then the system signs you out after six hours. If you work two 

hours in the system, and then leave it idle for two hours, then you’ll be automatically signed out 

at the end of the two idle hours, regardless of your overall session duration time. 

To set your timeout preferences: 

1. 
On the Preferences page, find the Security preferences section. 

2. 
In the Timeout section, below Inactivity duration signout, select the number of Hours and 

Minutes that RealPage Financial Suite remains active until it times out due to inactivity. The 

system signs you out when you are inactive for the duration that you set. 

3. 
In the Session duration signout section, select the number of Hours and Minutes to allow a 

session to last. When this time expires, the system requires you to log in again. 

The maximum amount of time that you can set in these fields is dictated by the maximum 
timeout settings that your administrator defined for the entire company on the Company 

information page. 

4. 
Click Save. 

---

When the system sends an email on your behalf, it appends your email signature to the end of

Setting Up Email Notification Preferences

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


You can adjust your notification preferences to choose which events you want the system to 

notify you about. 

To set your email notification preferences: 

1. 
On the Preferences page, find the Email notifications section. 

2. 
When you use the Process & store option to store reports, the Stored reports are 

generated and available check box determines whether the system sends you an email 

message with the report as an attachment. If you want to receive stored reports by email, 

then select the Stored reports are generated and available check box.

Intercompany Ticketing 

Use this section to choose your email notification preference for intercompany service tickets. 

When a service ticket is created, the system sends an email to: 

• 
The user who submitted the ticket (to notify them that it was successfully submitted) 

• 
The user or users who are assigned as the reviewer (to notify them that a ticket requires 

their approval) 

• 
The user or users who are assigned to the ticket (to notify them that they are assigned to 

resolve and close the ticket) 

You can select your personal notification preference for these emails: 

• 
None: Do not receive any notifications for service tickets. 

• 
Individual: Receive a separate email each time a service ticket is created. 

• 
Consolidated: Consolidate notifications into a single email for all service tickets created that 

day. 

If you are the user who submitted the service ticket, then you will receive a separate email for 
each ticket you submit, regardless of your notification preference. 

Approval Request Notifications 

If you approve a lot of transactions, then you receive a lot of approval notifications. To mitigate 

this, you can consolidate approval notifications into a single, daily email. 

1. 
Select a notification preference for each transaction type: 

• 
None: Do not receive any notifications. 

• 
Individual: Receive an email each time a transaction of this type is approved. 

• 
Consolidated: Reduce your incoming email by grouping related approved transaction 

notifications into one email. 

Your list of transaction types is determined by the applications that your company has 

installed. Items that have an asterisk (*) appear only if you have installed one of the 

additional RealPage Financial Suite applications, such as Spend Management or Job Cost 

and Reserves: 

• 
A/P invoice 

• 
Purchase order* 

• 
Service contracts* 

• 
Subcontracts* 

• 
Job cost change order* 

• 
Journal entry 

• 
Payment

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

• 
Expense report 

2. 
In the Consolidated notification time section, set the date to begin receiving consolidated 

notifications in the Start date/time field, and then specify the time in the adjacent fields. 

3. 
If your company has enabled approvals for bank reconciliations, then by default, you will 

receive email notifications under the following circumstances: 

• 
A new bank reconciliation was submitted to you for approval. 

• 
A bank reconciliation that you submitted was approved or declined. 

If you do not want to receive any notifications related to these approvals, then select the 

Exclude from bank reconciliation approval notifications check box. 

This applies only if you have permission to submit and/or approve bank reconciliations to 
receive these types of notifications. 

Approval Confirmations 

You can opt to receive notifications when certain transactions are approved.

None: Select this option if you don’t want to receive an email when a purchase order

Personalizing the Page Defaults 

In the Personalize page defaults section, you can set the number of items you want to appear in 

page elements, such as lists, drop-down lists, transaction rows, and more. 

1. 
In the List screens drop-down list, select the number of lines to display in pages that 

provide lists of records. The system default is 20 lines. 

You can change this number to accommodate your monitor’s resolution and line speed. The 

greater the number, the more lines you can see without clicking Next. However, if you have 

a slow Internet connection, increasing the line number may increase the time it takes to 

download the additional data. 

2. 
In the Selection list pop-ups drop-down list, select the number of lines to display in pop-up 

selection pages in the event that there are more items than the drop-down list displays. The 

system default is 15 lines. 

3. 
In the Drop-down lists drop-down list, select the number of list items to display in 

drop-down menu lists. 

Keep in mind that the larger the number, the longer the list of data the system needs to 

load in the background. Long lists can slow down the page refresh rate. You can set up to 

5000 items in a drop-down list. The default is 1000. If you have more than 5000 items, the 

system displays the list in a separate window instead. 

4. 
In the Transaction rows drop-down list, select the number of rows displayed when adding a 

new transaction on multi-line edit pages (pages used for entering bills, invoices, expense 

reports, adjustments, and so on). For example, if you set the default to two rows and add a 

new expense report, then the system displays two empty rows on the Add expense report 

page. 

5. 
In the Fast entry row drop-down list, set the number of blank lines (up to a maximum of six) 

used for splitting the transaction across two or more account-department-location

Personalizing the Interactive Behavior 

In the Personalize interactive behavior section, you can define how you want the system to interact 

with your input. 

1. 
Select the Automatically insert a decimal point in numbers check box if you want the 

system to place a decimal point before the last two numbers entered. Clear this check box if 

you want the system to place a decimal point at the end of the number entered, and then 

add two zeros. 

For example, if you type 1056 and do not select this check box, 1056 is interpreted as 

1,056.00. If you select this check box, 1056 is interpreted as 10.56. The system formats the 

number when you tab out of a field on any transaction page. 

2. 
Select the Display type-ahead suggestions as you type check box to allow the system to 

anticipate and display suggestions as you type. The type-ahead feature anticipates what you 

will type next by displaying the word it thinks you will type, so you don’t have to type the 

entire word. For example, say you have one vendor named Franklin. As you enter the first 

characters “Fr,” the system supplies “Franklin.” The system locally caches all of your vendor 

names so that it can suggest the correct name. 

While this speeds data entry, it also adds time to page downloads. If you enter a lot of 
data, then you should enable this feature. However, if pages take an excessively long time 
to load, then you can disable this feature. 

3. 
Select the Display all line item fields per line item check box if you want to see a line item 

and all of its details on one long line. Unless you have a specific reason for enabling this 

option, we recommend that you use the default details area on pages, such as Journal Entry 

and Sales Order entry, to contain infrequently used fields. 

4. 
Select the Always show the details area when selecting line items check box to always 

show the details area when selecting line items. Unless you always need to see the details, 

we recommend that you use the expand and collapse feature on the pages to control the 

display of the details area. 

5. 
Select the Use Enter (not Tab) to move between fields check box to use the ENTER key to 

move from field to field. Clear the check box if you want to use the TAB key to move from

#### Setting Up Check Preferences
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 68*

User Preferences 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up Check Preferences 

The system can use a digital signature that you upload to the system on printed checks so that 

the digital signature appears on the printed checks. The system uses the signature of the person 

who selects the invoices to pay, and not the person who prints the checks. 

Create the desired digital signature as a GIF or JPG and then upload it to either the bank account 

record or to your user preferences. You can set up signatures in the system in two places:  

• 
On the bank account record. You can upload a signature associated with a checking 

account in the Cash Management application. 

• 
In your user preferences. The signature that you upload with the My preferences option is 

associated with your company user ID.  

When signatures are set up in both places, the system uses the signature that is set up in your 

user preferences, not the one set up in the bank account record. The user who selects invoices on 

the Pay A/P invoices page is the one whose signature goes on the check; it is not the user who 

prints the actual check. 

If you do not upload a signature file in your preferences, then the system uses the signatures 

associated with the checking account instead. 

If a digital signature is not set up in either location, then the check prints with a blank signature 

line. 

For information on creating a signature file, see Creating a Digital Check Signature (on page 57). 

---



#### Creating a Digital Check Signature
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 69*

Chapter 3: User Preferences 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Creating a Digital Check Signature 

The signature file must be 3.0” wide x 0.36” high, 150 dpi, and saved as a GIF or JPG file no larger 

than 10K. If you have a scanner and a little experience in computer graphics, you can create the 

signature yourself. If not, ask a local desktop-publishing service to scan your signature and resize 

it for you. 

1. 
Sign your name in a 3.0” wide by 0.36” high frame. 

2. 
Scan the signature. Use 150 dpi resolution. 

3. 
Save the file as a 16-bit color GIF or JPG file. The file size can’t exceed 10K. 

4. 
Open the file in a graphics program and verify that it appears correctly. 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

Don’t be concerned if your graphics program tells you that the size of the image is greater than 

3.0” wide by 0.36” high. However, be sure to maintain the correct aspect ratio of 3.0” wide by 

0.36” high. Otherwise, the system enlarges or reduces the image to fit the bounding box, so the 

image appears distorted both on your printed checks and through the check delivery service. 

Good Digital Signatures 

The most effective signature fills the box, leaving little white space. 

If your signature does not fill the box, it appears distorted on your printed checks or through the 

RealPage Check Delivery service. 

Good: The signature fills the box. 

Too small: The signature leaves too much white space. 

Unclear: The signature is too small and too far to the left.

Uploading Your Signature 

(User Name) > My Preferences  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


To upload a signature: 

1. 
On the Preferences page, find the Check preferences section. 

2. 
Click the Upload signature button.  

The Upload signature image box opens. 

3. 
Click the Choose files button and select the file with your signature image. After a moment, 

a preview of your signature appears. 

If you don’t like it, or if you are replacing an existing signature, click the Remove signature 

button and choose another signature image. 

4.

To adjust printer offsets, see Aligning Your Printer to Print Checks (on page 58). 

Aligning Your Printer to Print Checks 

(User Name) > My Preferences 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


This topic assists you in adjusting printer offsets to align your check PDFs with your printer. The 

adjustments are applied to any printer on which you print a PDF check image. The adjustment 

process does not affect the printing of non-RealPage PDFs or RealPage PDFs other than checks. 

The adjustments you make are unique to you as a user. Other users may have different PDF 

offsets. Thus, if you must have two sets of adjustment parameters for two printers, you need to 

have two users with different adjustment parameters. 

Measure the distance of the crosshairs from the top and left edges of the sheet of paper. Use a 

ruler that has a decimal scale. If the measurements are not exactly 1”, then click the adjustment 

controls on your Preferences page until the relative position of the printed image is exactly 1” 

from the top and left edges of the sheet of paper. 

---


<!-- Page 71 -->
Chapter 3: User Preferences 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

The illustration below shows the controls. Click the horizontal arrows to move the image left or 

right; click the vertical ones to move the image up or down. 

Each click moves the image by 0.05.” Thus, if your image is offset to the right by 0.10”, click the 

horizontal offset left arrow 
 two times. If the image is offset downward by 0.15,” click the up 

arrow 
 three times. 

To offset the PDF image: 

1. 
On the Preferences page, find the Check preferences section. 

2. 
Click the Verify your printer alignment for RealPage checks link at the bottom of the 

section, and then print the page to the printer that you normally use to print checks. 

3. 
Measure the crosshairs horizontally and vertically. The intersection must be exactly 1” from 

the top edge and 1” from the left edge of your sheet of paper. 

4. 
If the measurements are not exactly 1”, then use the Printing offsets controls on the 

Preferences page to adjust the relative position of how your printer prints the PDF on the 

page. 

5. 
Print the test page again. If the crosshairs are not exactly 1” × 1”, repeat the adjustment 

process until they are.

### Managing Lists
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 108*

Lists 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Managing Lists 

Lists provide access to like records. After you create a record, you can access it from its list. Most 

lists allow you to add, edit, view, and delete the records in it. You can also export the list to an 

XML file or a PDF file. After exporting a list, you can import the list into an external application like 

Excel, and then print the list from that application. 

Some lists allow you to access related information. For example, from the customers list, you can 

also access the customers A/R ledger and view a breakdown of the total amount that the 

customer owes. 

Since the list page is where you perform most of your work, the system provides several features 

to let you filter and sort lists and create and manage custom views of your data. 

• 
Sorting (on page 97): Sort the list alphabetically by the data in the desired column. 

• 
Filtering (on page 98): Filter lists so that you see only the data that you need. 

• 
Views (on page 118): Create a custom view to determine which columns appear in your lists, 

and apply a filter so that the list appears just the way you want it. 

Lists and Links 

Each list is unique and can offer links to let you navigate into an associated record to see more 

detailed data. For example, some invoice lists have a Preview link that, when clicked, opens the 

invoice in PDF format in a browser window. Another type of list may have a link to the customer 

record or the vendor record. 

Many reports present figures as links that, when clicked, open the associated record. This example 

shows links in the Debit and Credit columns of a journal entry. When you click a link, the system 

navigates to more information, allowing you to delve into the details. 

---



#### Sorting Lists
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 109*

Chapter 5: Lists 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Sorting Lists 

You can display a list by a column’s ascending or descending values by clicking the column name. 

An arrow to the right of the column name indicates the sort direction. The arrow points 
 up for 

ascending order and 
 down for descending order. Only one column can control the list’s sort 

order at a time. 

In this example, the system sorts the list by the data in the Entity ID column. The sort arrow 

appears on the column that the system is sorting on. 

To reverse the sort order, click the column name again. The sort order reverses, and the arrow 

flips direction to indicate that the sort is reversed. 

To sort on a different column, click the desired column name. 

---



#### Filtering Lists
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 110*

Lists 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Filtering Lists 

Using Column Filters 

Column filters are text boxes that appear at the top of each column. Filters let you find items in a 

list that match the text that you enter. 

To apply a column filter: 

• 
Type the text that you want to find in the column filter, and then press ENTER. 

The system searches for matches, and then displays the matches in the list. 

If a text box does not appear at the top of a column, the column is not searchable. 

---


<!-- Page 111 -->
Chapter 5: Lists 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Using the Wild Card Character 

• 
Use the % symbol as a wild card or placeholder. For example, typing “san%” in the City 

column’s filter would find both San Francisco and Santa Diego. 

• 
Placing the % in front of text tells the system to find these letters in the middle of text in a 

field. 

• 
Placing % at the end of a word tells the system to find the word and any letters that follow 

the word. 

• 
Use % to filter text columns only. The % symbol does not work on non-text columns such as 

date columns or amount columns. 

• 
For best success, anticipate differences and adapt your filter to account for them. 

To find records that contain a specific value: 

• 
Type the first part of the value. 

If you are looking for a contact in a city that starts with “San,” then you can filter the Contact 

list by typing “san” in the City filter field, then and pressing ENTER. The system searches for 

contacts with a city that begins with San, such as San Jose, San Francisco, and Santa Fe. 

• 
If you know only part of the text that you want to find, type “%” and then type the text that 

you have. 

For example, if you are looking for a contact with the letters “Will” in the name, but you do 

not have the full, correct name of the business, type “%will%” in the Contact name filter of 

the Contacts list, and then press ENTER. The system searches for matches, retrieving all 

contacts that contain the letters “will” in the Contact name field. 

Example 

Your company uses this standard format for naming invoice summaries: Invoices: Month Year. 

When you want to find all June summaries, type “%June” in the filter above the Summary column, 

and then press ENTER to apply the filter. Placing the % in front of June tells the system that the 

word “June” appears in the middle of the text string. Placing % at the end of the word “June” tells 

the system to find the word June and any word with letters that follow the word “June,” such as 

“Juneteenth.” 

---


<!-- Page 112 -->
Lists 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Searches for Units 

You can search for a unit by entering any part of the unit ID. The system will find matches for any 

part of the unit ID string. For example, if the units in your property are configured with an 

alphanumeric pattern such as A-10, A-11, A12, B-20, B-21, B-22, then you can enter any part of 

the string, such as “22,” and the system will find B-22.  

The string does not have to start with the entered value to match. Typing “A” finds a list of units 

on the A floor as in our example or all units that have “A” in the unit ID. 

Displaying One-Time Items 

Some quick-entry records are set for one-time use. For example, you may have a seasonal 

customer, such as a Halloween supply store, or customers who pay only once and are not likely to 

purchase again. 

Create the customer record so that you can record the cash receipt, but because you don’t need 

to see that customer in your customer list regularly, flag the customer as Exclude from the 

company contact list. One-time customers aren’t included in the list unless you specify them to be 

included. 

To include one-time items in the list, select the Include One-Time check box. The system displays 

the one-time items along with regular items and adds a One-Time column to show which items 

are one-time records. 

Example 

You may have a customer who purchases from you only once a year, and you do not want to see 

the customer’s name in the list all the time. You still need to create a Customer record so that you 

can record the cash receipt, but since you do not need to see the customer in your Customers list 

regularly, edit the Customer record, and select the One-Time Use check box. 

---


<!-- Page 113 -->
Chapter 5: Lists 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Including Inactive Records in Search Results 

Almost every kind of record in the system has a Status field with choices of Active and Inactive. 

The Include Inactive check box appears at the top of many lists and allows the system to include 

the inactive records in search results. 

• 
Select the Include Inactive check box to include items set to a status of Inactive in the 

search. The system refreshes the list and adds a Status column to indicate which items are 

active and which are inactive. 

• 
Clear the Include Inactive check box to prevent inactive items from appearing in the list. 

A list can contain items that are inactive but still present because they link to transaction data. For 

example, you may have a vendor who no longer carries items you need to purchase. In the vendor 

record, you flag the vendor as Inactive. Inactive vendors aren’t included in the list unless you 

select Include Inactive. 

One-time use customers do not appear in the Company application’s Contacts list unless you 
select the Include one-time check box.

##### Operator Definitions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 117*

Chapter 5: Lists 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Operator Definitions 

The following operators are available for use when filtering: 

• 
Equals: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column matches the text or 

number in the Value field. 

• 
Less than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is less 

than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

greater than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Less or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

less than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen 

column is greater than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Not equal to: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column does not match 

the text or number in the Value field. 

• 
Contains: Displays all records in which a character or group of characters in the chosen 

column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The characters must 

match in the same order. For example, “ox” typed in the Value field may return records for 

Oxygen Inc., Boxing Agency, and Clorox, if those were values in the chosen column. 

• 
Does not contain: Displays all records in which no character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. 

• 
Starts with: Displays all records in which the first character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you have an item ID scheme that 

uses initial letters to identify the product type, you can select the item ID column and set the 

Value field to these letters to display all records for that product type. 

• 
Ends with: Displays all records in which the last character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you tag the end of the item ID for 

all custom order items with the letters “CO,” you can select the item ID column and set the 

value to CO to display all records for custom order items. 

• 
Includes: Displays all records that match items in a comma delimited list in the Value field. 

• 
Excludes: Displays all records that do not match items in a comma delimited list in the 

Value field. 

• 
Field equals null: Displays all records that have a null or empty field. 

• 
Field not equals null: Displays all records that do not have a null or empty field. 

---


<!-- Page 118 -->
Lists 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns. 

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 

Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 

of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

% bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank,” like Metropolis Bank.

Displaying a Hierarchical View 

Some lists, such as the Locations list, can display a hierarchical structure of parent-child 

relationships using icons and indentations. 

Use the Display Hierarchy check box to view the list to help you identify locations that are 

subsidiaries of parent records. 

Parent records can have up to five levels of child records, allowing you to view and act on the 

records as needed. You can still sort and search for records as you would in any view. 

If the parent record is not visible because of permission restrictions, or if you filtered the list in a 

way that the parent is not visible, the system still shows the child as indented and colored to 

indicate that it is a child in a relationship. 

To toggle between flat view and hierarchical view of a list: 

• 
To switch to a flat view, clear the Display hierarchy check box on the white bar above the 

list. Clearing the check box causes all items to be displayed by their unique ID, whether they 

have relationships to other items. 

• 
To return to the hierarchical view, select the Display hierarchy check box. 

The default for a list that has hierarchical items is to display the hierarchical view. 
Hierarchical items include Locations, departments, vendors, and customers.

Exporting from Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

To export a list of records from the system: 

1. 
Select the Include inactive check box to include items with an Inactive status in the data 

export results or clear the Include inactive check box to exclude inactive items. 

Some lists do not offer an option to filter by active/inactive status. 

2. 
Select the Include private check box to include items that are associated with an entity or 

clear the Include private check box to exclude these items. 

Some lists do not offer an option to include and exclude private items. 

3. 
Click the Export button. 

4. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again.

Finding Transactions in a Specific State 

List views of transactions provide a hub for viewing and accessing all transactions of a specific 

type, for example, bills or invoices. 

There are two ways to locate transactions in a specific state: 

• 
Filter for the transaction state on the fly: In the transaction list view, type the state in the 

State column, then click Go. The list displays only those transactions in that state. 

• 
Create a permanent custom view that filters for the transaction state: Create the view (on 

page 122) and set the filter to State = <state>, where <state> equals the state you are 

seeking, such as Draft, Posted, Paid, Reversed, and so forth. This custom view is always 

available from the transaction list.

find an item in a long list that you want to add to a drop-down list. 

1. 
Click the down arrow to display the field-level commands. 

2. 
Click Find. The system displays a search form that lists all of the available values for the field. 

Each search form is unique to the type of information that you want to find, but all search 

forms have these common commands. 

• 
Clear all filters: Remove all text from the search fields from previous searches. Clearing 

a search returns all of the items of this type. 

• 
Cancel: Exit the search form without adding a new value to the drop-down list or text 

box. 

• 
Select: Add the item to the drop-down list.

Using Field-Level Controls in Drop-Down Lists 

The system offers two kinds of drop-down lists – those with field-level controls at the top and 

those without. This example shows the field-level controls. 

Field Level Options 

The most common field level options are Add, View, and Find. 

• 
Add: If you cannot find the record that you need, you can add a new record right from 

where you need it. Clicking Add opens a new blank record for the same type of object. For 

example, if you are selecting G/L accounts, then clicking Add opens a new blank record so 

that you can create a new account. 

• 
View: Use the View command when you want to verify that you are selecting the correct 

record. Select the item that you want to view, and then click the View command to open the 

record. 

• 
Find: Use this option when you have looked through the drop-down list and don’t find the 

record that you need, but you believe that it exists. Click the Find option. The system opens 

a box in which you can type the text to search for the desired record. If you don’t find it, you 

can click Cancel and then click the Add option to add a new record. 

You must be at the top level to create new customer, vendor, and G/L account records.

Exporting from a Workbench 

To export from a workbench: 

1. 
Right-click any data in the workbench to display the export controls menu. 

2. 
Click the Export button, and then select the file format that you want the system to use to 

export the data. 

• 
CSV Export: This format makes it easy to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in the CSV format with any spreadsheet program. After 

selecting this option, the system exports the list as a CSV file. 

• 
Excel Export (.xlsx): After selecting this option, the system exports the list in Excel’s 

native format. 

• 
Excel Export (.xml): After selecting this option, the system exports the list in XML 

format. 

The location of the exported file depends on your browser’s default download functionality. 

All three of these export formats export the entire list, including these links: 

• 
Actions: Exports the HTML code for editing, viewing, approving, and declining the 

transaction. 

• 
Add approver: Click to add another approver for the transaction. 

• 
Send back: Send the transaction back to the requester. 

• 
Status: Click to view the transaction’s approval history. 

Additional Menu Items 

• 
Select Copy to copy the data in the selected cell to the clipboard. You can paste the copied 

data into a text file or another application. 

• 
Select Copy with headers to copy the data in the selected cell and the cell’s column header 

to the clipboard. 

The Paste command is not for use in the Workbench at this time.

Managing Transactions 

This section discusses the basics of working with transactions in RealPage Financial Suite. 

Adding, Editing, and Viewing Transactions 

You can manage transactions and other records from various lists throughout RealPage Financial 

Suite. Adding, editing, or viewing transactions opens the corresponding transaction information 

page in Add, Edit, or View mode, respectively: 

• 
Add: Opens a new, blank record to create a new transaction. 

• 
Edit: Opens an existing record to edit the details of the transaction. 

• 
View: Opens an existing record in read-only mode to view the details of the transaction. 

In some cases, certain features and settings may only appear in View or Edit mode after you 
create and save the transaction. 

Adding New Transactions 

You can add a new transaction multiple ways: 

• 
Click the 
 Add button next to the menu option. 

• 
Click the Add button on the main transaction list. 

• 
Click the Save & new option from the More actions button while creating a new transaction. 

• 
Click the Duplicate button while viewing or editing an existing transaction. 

Viewing and Editing Transactions 

To view or edit an existing transaction, go to the main transaction list, and then click the View or 

Edit link next to the transaction. 

---



#### Creating a Recurring Transaction from an Existing Transaction
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 159*

Chapter 7: Transactions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Creating a Recurring Transaction from an Existing Transaction 

You can create a recurring transaction that is based on an existing transaction. 

To create a recurring transaction: 

1. 
Find the transaction that you want to make a recurring transaction. 

2. 
Click the Edit link next to the transaction. 

3. 
Click the More actions button, and then select Create recurring transaction. 

4. 
Change any information as needed. 

5. 
Click the Schedule tab. 

6. 
In Start Date, click the Calendar, and then select the first date on which you want this 

invoice to be generated. 

7. 
In Repeats, select the frequency in which the transaction is to recur: 

• 
To have the invoice occur only once, select None. You may want to select none if you 

are setting up an invoice for an item that might be recurring such as a 30-day trial for 

a new service. Later you can choose to change the schedule if the service becomes an 

ongoing expense. 

• 
To have the invoice occur at regular intervals, select Days, Weeks, End of month, 

Months, or Years, and then type the number of intervals in the adjacent text box. 

For instance, if an invoice only occurs every other month, select Months and type 2. If 

you select a time period but do not type a number, the system will default to 1. 

For weeks, months, and years, the invoice will recur at the next interval on the same 

day as the start date. For instance, if you set an invoice to start on the 15th of the 

month and recur monthly, the system generates the invoice each month on the 15th.  

• 
To make an invoice with a month’s interval generate at the end of the month, select 

End of Month. 

8. 
Click Save. 

---



#### Reversing a Transaction
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 160*

Transactions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reversing a Transaction 

Occasionally, you may need to reverse a transaction, maybe because it is a duplicate, or because 

you paid a bill that you didn’t want to pay right now. Whatever the reason, you have the option of 

reversing many types of transactions. 

Reversing a journal entry is a little different from reversing other transaction types. See 
Reversing a Journal Entry (on page 150 ). 

If you reverse a transaction such as an invoice, and then discover that it shouldn’t have been 

reversed, you can’t undo the reversal, but you can recreate the transaction as needed. 

To reverse a transaction: 

1. 
Open the transaction list for any transaction that can be reversed, locate the transaction that 

you want to reverse, and click the Reverse link. For example, say you want to reverse an A/R 

adjustment.  

• 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu. 

• 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select Adjustments. 

• 
Find the adjustment that you want to reverse, and then click the Reverse link. The 

Transaction reversal date page opens. 

2. 
On the Transaction reversal date page, enter the following: 

• 
Reversal date: Select the date for reversing the transaction. This date is usually the 

original transaction date or a later date. 

• 
Memo: We recommend that you enter the reason for the reversal to maintain an audit 

trail. 

3. 
Click Submit. The system returns you to the transaction list and displays two line items for 

this transaction. (The transaction is not zeroed out, so there is an audit trail). 

• 
One line item is the original transaction, where the Reverse link now is labeled 

Reversed. 

• 
The other line item added by the system is the reverse of that transaction, which 

produces a net effect of zero for that transaction. This transaction is labeled Reversal. 

After you click Submit, you can’t undo the reversal. 

---

#### Reversing a Journal Entry
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 162*

Transactions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reversing a Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry > View 
Transactions > Reverse`


You can reverse any journal entry that was entered by you or another user that hasn’t already 

been reversed, as long as it is in an open period. You can reverse statistical journal entries, 

adjusting G/L journal entries, and adjusting statistical journal entries in the same way. To reverse a 

different type of journal entry, start from the corresponding journal entry list in the General 

Ledger menu. 

This example reverses a G/L journal entry.  

To reverse an entry: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
Select Journal entry.  

3. 
Click the View transactions link in the row of the desired journal. 

4. 
In the list of transactions, locate the transaction that you want to reverse, and then select 

the check box in the Select column.  

See our tips for finding journal entries. 

If you don’t see the option to reverse, another application might have created the entry, 
such as Accounts Payable. To undo other types of transactions, you must go to the 
application in which the transaction was created and void or reverse it there. 

5. 
Click the Reverse button.  

• 
Accept the default Reverse date, or type another date. You can reverse the transaction 

as of another date in the past or future. 

• 
Type a description so that you leave an appropriate audit trail. 

• 
In the Reference number field, the word “Reversed” appears, followed by the original 

transaction number. If the number does not appear, type the original transaction 

number if you have it. 

6. 
Click the Reverse button. 

After you reverse a journal entry, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create 
another journal entry to replace it. 

When you reverse a journal entry, the General Ledger: 

• 
Adds a Reversed on link below the Date field. This shows the date on which the 

transaction was reversed. 

---



#### Other Ways to Reverse a Transaction
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 163*



#### Reclassifying a Transaction
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 163*

• 
Creates an identical transaction that is the inverse of the original transaction, which 

zeros out the original transaction. 

• 
You now have two transactions for audit purposes. 

To see the date on which you reversed this transaction, click the Reversed on link. Click it 

again to see the Reversed from date. 

Other Ways to Reverse a Transaction 

You can reverse a transaction from several places in RealPage Financial Suite, including: 

• 
Check register: Select Void to void the payment. The system reverses the A/P invoice. 

• 
Receipt register: Reverse the receipt of payment. 

• 
Bank register: Reverse a receipt of payment, or void payment to automatically reverse an 

A/P invoice. 

• 
A/R Adjustments List 

If the transaction was created in a closed period, you can: 

• 
Open the closed period to reverse the transaction with the original date. 

• 
Reverse the transaction in the current open period. 

The transaction must be partially or fully paid, unless you specifically configured your application 

for reversal of unpaid transactions, such as A/P invoices, A/R invoices, expenses, or adjustments. 

If the transaction state is Selected, remove the transaction from the selected state, and then 
reverse the transaction. 

If the transaction state is Partially paid or Paid, reverse the payment first, and then reverse the 
transaction. 

Reclassifying a Transaction 

To reclassify a transaction: 

1. 
In the transactions list, click Edit beside a paid or partially paid transaction. The transaction 

opens in edit mode. 

2. 
Click Reclassify at the top of the page. 

3. 
Add, remove, or delete dimensions as needed. 

Transactions must be paid or partially paid before you can reclassify them.

Printing a Transaction 

After you create a transaction, you can print a copy of it. You can print from the transaction page 

itself, such as from the A/P invoice or A/R invoice pages, or from the transaction list page. 

To print a transaction: 

• 
From a transaction list: Locate the appropriate transaction and, at the end of the row, click 

Print. 

• 
From a transaction page: Click the Print button at the top of the page. 

The system generates a PDF of the transaction, which you can view, print, or save to add as an 

email attachment as needed. 

After you apply a credit adjustment to an invoice, the invoice is updated to show that the 
amount due is reduced by the amount of the credit. However, if you send the customer an 
updated invoice, the invoice does not show why the amount due was reduced. You can send the 
customer an A/R statement to show which adjustments were applied to which invoices. Learn 
more about printing or emailing A/R statements . 

Printing PDF Documents from Chrome 

PDF reports appear in a box. Make sure you allow pop ups in your browser (the PDF appears in a 

box). 

To set Chrome to allow pop-up boxes, go to Settings > Show advanced settings > Content 

settings > Pop-ups. 

If you download a PDF but the files aren’t saved or you see the error Failed - Forbidden, disable 

the native Chrome PDF Viewer: 

1. 
Open Google Chrome. 

2. 
In the address bar, enter chrome://plug-ins to see the list of plug-ins that are installed. 

3. 
Locate Chrome PDF viewer in the list and put a check mark beside Disable. 

4. 
Return to the RealPage Financial Suite, and then download the PDF file.

Editing Customer Contact Information in a Transaction 

If you notice that the customer contact information is incorrect on a transaction, or perhaps the 

transaction uses the wrong contact entirely, then you can edit or change the contact on the 

transaction’s page. 

If you notice the error during the creation of the transaction, change the contact in the 

transaction, but keep in mind that editing customer contact information only affects the current 

transaction being created and future transactions. 

If you already saved and posted the transaction, editing or changing a contact becomes more 

complicated. Depending on the type of transaction and the state of the transaction, you may have 

to reverse the transaction before you can make any changes to the transaction record, including 

changes to the associated contact record that apply to the existing transaction. 

See one of the following for more detailed information and step-by-step instructions. 

• 
Editing Contact Information from a Transaction During Creation (on page 155) 

• 
Editing Contact Information in an Existing Transaction (on page 156) 

• 
Changing a Contact in an Existing Transaction (on page 157) 

Editing Contact Information from a Transaction During Creation 

When you edit contact information used in a transaction, you only edit the information for that 

transaction and future transactions. If you want the same changes to apply to existing 

transactions, you must manually update the contact information in that record as well. 

To edit contact information during the creation of a transaction: 

1. 
In the new transaction record, click the drop-down arrow in the contact field and highlight 

the contact you want to edit, and then click View. 

2. 
In the Contact Information box, click Edit. 

3. 
Make any necessary changes to the contact record. The Suggested contact name is a 

unique ID used across the system by various records. It can’t be changed after creation. The 

Print as name is the text that appears on printed documents and transactions. 

4. 
Click Save.

Editing Contact Information in an Existing Transaction 

To edit the contact information used in an existing transaction, you may have to reverse the 

transaction and recreate it. Whether you can edit or reverse a transaction depends on the 

transaction type, the state of the transaction, and your permissions. 

You can only edit information in transactions that are still open. If the transaction is part of a 
closed period, you must open the books to make any changes. 

To edit contact information in an existing transaction: 

1. 
Go to the transaction and click Edit. If you can’t edit the transaction, you must first Reverse 

a transaction, and then Edit it. 

You can only edit transactions from where they were created. For instance, if you create a 
vendor invoice in Purchasing, you cannot edit the corresponding A/P invoice in Accounts 
Payable. Instead, you must edit the vendor invoice from the vendor invoice list in 
Purchasing. 

2. 
In the contact field you want to edit, click the drop-down arrow and highlight the contact, 

then click View. 

3. 
In the Contact Information window, click Edit. 

4. 
Make any necessary changes to the contact record. The Suggested contact name is a 

unique ID used across the system by various records. It can’t be changed after creation. The 

Print as name is the text that appears on printed documents and transactions. 

5. 
Click Save.

Multi-Currency Controls in A/R Transactions 

When Multi-currency management is enabled, multi-currency controls appear for currency type, 

exchange rate type, transaction amount, base amount, and the exchange rate date. 

In the Accounts Receivable application, transactions with multi-currency controls include invoices, 

recurring invoices, and adjustments. In addition, you can associate a default currency with a 

customer in their customer records. 

In the Accounts Payable application in vendor records, you can assign a default currency to use 

for transactions with each vendor. 

Enabling Multi-Currency Management 

When Multi-currency management is enabled, multi-currency controls appear for currency type, 

exchange rate type, transaction amount, base amount, and the exchange rate date. 

To enable multi-currency management: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
In the Account settings section, find the Multi-currency management section. 

4. 
Select the Enable check box. 

5. 
In Rounding account, select the account that you want to use for to keep debits and credits 

in balance. 

The system automatically uses this rounding account to keep debits and credits in balance 

if: 

• 
Journal entries are imported from a spreadsheet, and 

• 
Rounding of base currency amounts during import causes a minor difference between 

debits and credits, requiring a correcting entry (typically, a debit or credit of a penny) 

to the rounding account. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

You may need to close and restart RealPage Financial Suite to make the changes take effect. 

What’s Next? 

To select the currencies you want to make available in your company, see Adding a Transaction 

Currency (on page 161). You may also want to: 

• 
Enable electronic payments 

• 
Enable a vendor to receive electronic payments

#### Messages in Printed Documents
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 174*

Transactions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide

Messages in Printed Documents 

As there are several places in RealPage Financial Suite where you can define a custom message to 

print on a document, sometimes there is confusion over why and when certain messages appear 

in printed output. This topic describes where message fields are, and when they appear in a 

printed document. 

About Formatting Printed Output 

There are two options for formatting printed output in the system: 

• 
Custom document templates: These are Microsoft Word files that use merge fields 

supported by the system to create a customized, branded print format for your transaction 

documents. These allow you to share the information you want how you want. 

• 
Default print templates: These are hard-coded, auto-assigned templates that the system 

uses for output when there is no custom document template assigned to a transaction or 

related record. The only things you can customize in the default templates are the logo and 

the message text. 

RealPage recommends that you use custom document templates for your printed output. 

When Messages Appear in Printed Documents 

The system follows these rules when printing messages in documents: 

• 
When no custom document template is defined, any message text that exists in a message 

field will print in the document. 

• 
When a custom document template is defined, the message text will only print in the 

document if the custom document template includes the message merge field. 

In scenarios where the message will print, you can override the message text with different text or 

delete the message text in a transaction prior to printing.

### Audit Trails
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 177*



#### Viewing Audit Trails

#### Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 177*

Chapter 7: Transactions

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail 

You can export data from the audit trail to a file in one of three formats, Microsoft Excel, CSV, or 

PDF. 

1. 
Open the audit trail. 

2. 
Click the audit trail’s More actions button, and then select the format to which you want to 

export: 

• 
Export to CSV 

• 
Export to Excel 

• 
Export to PDF 

If the audit trail table is lengthy, you can change the size of the list. From the More actions 
drop-down list, select Table size, and then select the number of rows that you want to be 
able to view. 

---

#### Displaying All Fields of a Line Item
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 188*



#### Best Practices for Creating Names and IDs
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 188*

Data Entry 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Tips for Entering Line Items 

This section provides helpful tips for entering line items. 

Displaying All Fields of a Line Item 

You can configure your personal preferences to display every possible field at the line-item level. 

Unless you have a real need for this, we don’t recommend it as a best practice because the line 

items become extremely long. 

To display all fields at the line-item level: 

1. 
Click your sign-in name at the top of any page, and then select My preferences.  

The My preferences page opens. 

2. 
Find the Display section, and then find the Personalize interactive behavior subsection. 

3. 
Select the Display all line item fields per line item check box. 

4. 
Select the Always show the details area when selecting line items check box. 

5. 
Click the Save button to save the changes. 

You may have to sign out and sign back in to see the effect of these changes. 

Best Practices for Creating Names and IDs 

Special Characters 

Most applications have best practices for names and IDs. In some cases, even if a name is allowed 

when you create a transaction or record, if that transaction or record interacts with another 

application—or even another area of the same application—the system might not be able to find 

and load it. 

Best practice: We recommend that you create a name or ID using only the following characters. 

Use 

• 
Letters 

• 
Numbers 

• 
A single space 

• 
A single dash 

• 
Underscores 

• 
Periods 

Don’t use 

• 
Special characters such as exclamation marks (!), at signs (@), equal signs (=), and any other 

character not specifically listed in the Use column. 

---


<!-- Page 189 -->
Chapter 8: Data Entry 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

• 
Double spaces 

• 
Double dashes 

• 
Leading spaces 

• 
Trailing spaces 

You can use some special characters in names, but if you use only the ones in the Use column, you 
can be sure that the name or ID won’t cause problems elsewhere. 

When a name is rendered, double spaces often appear the same as single spaces, which can 

cause difficulty in name recognition. For example, if an application displays an error that an item 

with a double space doesn’t exist, but you know that it does, check the name in the appropriate 

list to make sure that no extra or hidden characters are part of the name or ID. 

Leading Zeros 

We recommend against using leading zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can cause 

errors when you import information into your company from Excel because Excel removes the 

leading zero. Use a character as a prefix to your ID. 

• 
Correct: C0001 

• 
Incorrect: 00C43 

Other Considerations 

When creating names and IDs, or configuring sequencing for applications, consider not only the 

impact of the naming scheme in different areas of the system but also the impact in outside 

applications such as importing and exporting files to Excel, Word, and CSV. Reports might sort 

differently than you expect if you use special characters or leading spaces. Some applications strip 

out leading zeros and spaces while others ignore them. 

Learn any limitations of third-party applications that you commonly use to help create your 

naming strategy.

Setting Default Line-Item Values 

Setting default values is a time-saver when you need to fill in a long list of line items. 

To set a default value for a line-item field: 

1. 
In the Entries section of a transaction’s page, click the Show defaults link. 

The area expands to display all fields for which you can set defaults. The type of fields that 

appear here depend on your company setup. For example, if you’ve enabled standard 

dimensions, or created and deployed user-defined dimensions, multi-currency processing 

fields, or revenue-recognition fields, then you can set default values for them here. 

2. 
Click the drop-down arrow for any field that frequently uses the same value, and then select 

that value. 

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button above the first line item. 

The value that you selected appears on every line or in the line-item detail of every line, 

depending on where the field is located. 

You can override the default value by selecting a different value or typing over the text. 

4. 
Optionally, click the Hide defaults link to hide the defaults section after you have applied 

them to the list. 

Example 

In this example, the user chooses to set up a default value for the Location column in the Entries 

list. 

a) Select the location that you want the system to complete for you. 

b) Click the Apply defaults button. 

c) The system completes the Location column with your selected location.

Editing the Line-Item Display 

If you are an administrator, the system enables you to customize field placement on the line-item

your company uses some dimensions more frequently, you can display the frequently used 

dimensions, including user-defined dimensions, at the line level, and move the less frequently 

used dimensions to the line-item detail.

### Attachments Overview
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 194*

Attachments 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Attachments Overview 

Attachments are bundles of one or more files that you associate with a transaction or record, such 

as a letter of credit, an invoice, or a photo. For example, if you have a contract signed by a 

customer, you can attach the contract to the customer record. You can attach as many files or 

combinations of file types as you need and bundle them into a single attachment record. 

To attach a document, you first need to create an electronic version of it. If it is a paper copy, scan 

the document, and then save it as one of the supported file types:  

• 
Word 

• 
PDF 

• 
Excel 

• 
Text 

• 
JPG 

• 
PNG 

Attaching Files to Transaction Records 

The Enable single scan upload setting in your user preferences changes the way that the system 

treats attachments. These differences are described below: 

When scanning is disabled: 

• 
You can select one attachment record to associate with a transaction, but the attachment 

record can contain multiple files as needed. 

• 
You can create folders for storing attachments from the transaction record. 

• 
You can access the attachment folders from the transaction record. 

When scanning is enabled: 

• 
You can add multiple attachments to a transaction record. 

• 
You can scan a document to attach it directly to the transaction record. 

• 
You cannot create or access attachment folders. 

For instructions on enabling the Enable single scan upload option, see Enabling the Scanning 

Feature (on page 197). 

---
