Managing Attachments 

This section discusses how to add and manage attachments in RealPage Financial Suite. An 

attachment is a bundle of one or more supporting documents, such as bills, spreadsheets, tax 

forms, images, and so on, that provides tangible, historical, and auditable information in support 

of a transaction or financial record. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

To view and manage attachments, you must have permissions for both attachments and 

attachment folders. 

You cannot restrict access to attachment folders by an individual user. When a user has 
permission to view attachments and attachment folders, they can view all attachments and 
folders in the system. 

These permissions are required to work with attachments.

#### Adding an Attachment to the System
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 196*

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide

Adding an Attachment to the System 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Storage > 
 Attachments`


You can create an attachment record in the Attachments list to upload one or more files into a 

single attachment and store it in RealPage Financial Suite. Any attachment records you create will 

be available in Attachment drop-down lists throughout RealPage Financial Suite; for example, 

when you are entering a new transaction or record and you want to attach supporting 

documents. 

To add an attachment, you need at least one attachment folder in which to store the attachment. 

Your company may have created an initial folder for you. If no folder currently exists, you can 

quickly create one while you are adding an attachment.  

To add a new attachment record in the system: 

1. 
In the Attachments list, click the Add button. 

The Select attachments page opens. 

2. 
Type a unique ID for the attachment record. If your company is configured to auto-number, 

then the system automatically displays an ID for the attachment. 

3. 
Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

4. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

5. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment. 

6. 
In the Attach files section: 

• 
Click the Choose files button, select the file(s) you want to attach, and then click the 

Open button. Alternatively, you can drag and drop files directly from your file explorer 

into the browser window. 

• 
If you have Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-Op, and you 

purchased the portal add-on, then the Display on portal check box also appears. 

Select the check box for any attachment that you want the tenant or owner to be able 

to access on their portal.

Deleting or Removing an Attachment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Storage > Attachments > Edit`


If you accidentally added the wrong attachment to a record, you can remove it from the system. 

Although you can delete some attachments from the Attachments list, you cannot delete an 

attachment that is currently attached to a record. Instead, go to the original record and delete the 

attachment there. 

Deleting an Attachment from the Attachments List 

To delete an attachment from the Attachments list: 

1. 
Select the Delete check box next to one or more attachment records. 

2. 
Click the Delete button. 

A confirmation box opens. 

3. 
Click OK to proceed. 

You cannot delete attachments that are already associated with a transaction or record.

Removing an Attachment from a Transaction or Record 

To remove an attachment from a specific transaction or record: 

1. 
Edit the record with the attachment you want to delete. For example, to remove an 

attachment from an A/P invoice, go to the A/P invoices list, and then edit the appropriate 

A/P invoice. 

2. 
Find the attachment. This will be located in a different place depending on whether you’ve 

enabled scanning in your user preferences: 

• 
If scanning is enabled, find the Documents section, and then click the 
 Delete icon 

next to the attachment files you want to remove. 

• 
If scanning is not enabled, find the Attachment(s) field, and then clear the selected 

attachment. 

You can enable or disable scanning using the Enable single scan upload check box on the 

Preferences page. This setting is located in the Display section under Personalize 

interactive behavior. 

3. 
Click Save to save the transaction or record.

#### Scanning Troubleshooting Checklist
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 212*

Scanning 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Naming Scanned A/P Invoices 

The file number for a single scan is a combination of the A/P invoice number and the date. The 

file number for multiple scans is a combination of the A/P invoice number and the date, plus a 

version number appended to the end. For example: 

• 
First scan: 846566-09-26-17 

• 
Second scan: 846566-09-26-17-1 

• 
Third scan: 846566-09-26-17-2 

Scanning Troubleshooting Checklist 

If you are having trouble scanning documents or connecting to Dynamsoft’s scanning service, the 

following checklists can help you identify the source of the problem. 

Scanner Checklist 

1. 
Confirm that the scanner is turned on and receiving power. Verify that all of the scanner’s 

cables are connected properly to the back of the scanner, the computer’s USB port, and the 

wall outlet. If the scanner’s power cable is plugged into a power strip or surge protector, try 

connecting the scanner directly to a wall outlet to verify that the power strip or surge 

protector is not causing the problem. If your scanner uses a wireless connection rather than 

a USB connection, make sure that your Wi-Fi is on and that your printer or scanner is 

connected to your wireless network. If the scanner still does not have power after checking 

the scanner’s cable and Wi-Fi connections, contact your scanner’s manufacturer. 

2. 
Update or reinstall the scanner’s drivers. Verify that the latest drivers are installed for the 

operating system used on your computer. 

3. 
Make sure that all trays for your scanner are loaded in the correct position with the 

correct paper type. Scanners that say they’re out of paper even though the paper is loaded 

correctly in the tray may have another paper source, especially if the scanner is part of a 

printer with multiple paper sources. 

4. 
Check for paper jams. Look up your scanner’s make and model online for instructions on 

opening your device and removing any jammed paper. 

5. 
Restart the scanner. Sometimes, you may only need to unplug and reconnect your device 

to get it to function correctly.

#### Standard vs. User-Defined Dimensions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 217*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Standard vs. User-Defined Dimensions 

You have a set of standard dimensions right out of the box, ready to be enabled. You can use 

them as is or repurpose them as needed. 

If you need a unique dimension, defined to reflect your individual business needs, you can create 

a user-defined dimension. For example, if you are a software company with various product lines, 

you might create a user-defined dimension called Line of Business. The values you could add are 

Direct Customers, Channel Partner, and OEM. Your dimension becomes available throughout the 

company wherever dimensions are displayed and is used the same way as any standard 

dimension. 

Additional fees may apply for some dimensions, including user-defined dimensions. Contact your 
account representative for more information. 

Territories can be optionally set up in Accounts Receivable, enhancing filtering in certain A/R 
reports. However, territory isn ’t a dimension and can’t be used for tagging transactions. Learn 
more about Territories and Territory Groups . 

Types of Dimensions 

Mix and match standard and user-defined dimensions to report on all aspects of your business. 

• 
Standard dimensions: These dimensions are provided when your company is set up. They 

are commonly useful and can be repurposed as needed. Standard dimensions include 

Location, Department, Customer, Employee, and Vendor. 

• 
User-defined dimensions: These are dimensions you can create to organize and sort 

categories of data unique to your business activities. 

Additional subscription fees may apply when creating user-defined dimensions.

Dimension Examples

only. In multi-entity shared companies, location groups also include entities.

### Dimension Relationships
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 220*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension Relationships 

If you create transactions where the value of one dimension is based on the value of another, you 

can create a relationship between the two dimensions to auto-populate the related value. For 

example, if you always use the same location for a specific customer, you can create a relationship 

between the Customer and Location dimensions to set the Location value to auto-populate every 

time you create a transaction against that customer. 

Specifically, dimension relationships are useful for: 

• 
Auto-populating dimension values: For example, you can select a customer and the system 

auto-populates the related location. 

• 
Filtering and validating dimensions: For example, you can select a specific location and the 

system displays only a subset of departments. 

• 
Cascading dimensions: For example, select a specific customer, and the system populates 

the related location, and the project, which is dependent on the selected location and 

department. 

Creating relationships between dimensions automates and speeds up data entry and lowers the 

incidence of data-entry errors. You can create relationships between: 

• 
User-defined dimensions 

• 
Standard dimensions 

• 
User-defined dimensions and standard dimensions 

In fact, you can create relationships between dimensions that enable many values on one or 

either side of the relationship. These are typically called one-to-many, or many-to-many 

relationships. 

To create relationships between dimensions, you must be subscribed to Platform Services and 
have Administrator permissions. 

You can’t export or import an application package that contains standard -to-standard 
dimension relationships. Import or export the package first, and then manually create the 
relationships.

Selecting the Base Dimension 

To create a relationship between two dimensions, you select the base dimension, the dimension 

whose value will determine the value of the second dimension. For example, Customer and 

Location can be set up in a relationship in which the value of customer, the base dimension, 

determines the value of location in transactions involving that customer. 

To select the base dimension: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Platform Services, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select the Objects option. The Objects list is displayed. 

3. 
Locate the base dimension, and then click the corresponding Edit link. 

For example, if you want to create a relationship that specifies the value for location every 

time you use a specific customer, click Edit beside Customer, which is the base dimension in 

this example. 

4. 
In the Status options section, select the Auto-Fill Related Objects check box. 

---


<!-- Page 222 -->
Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
Leave Enable Override of Auto-Filled Objects unselected if you want a fixed relationship. 

In a fixed relationship case, enabling override defeats the purpose of creating the 
relationship because the user can pick any value from the drop-down list. Conversely, if you 
want to default to a suggested value, but also want to leave the user free to select 
another value as appropriate, enable override. Remember, if you’ve set up priority for 
possible conflict between multiple dimension relationships, enabling override won’t be 
respected. 

The option to override auto-populated dimension fields works only for newer pages, such as 
in Cash Management. 

6. 
Click Save to return to the object list.

#### Creating a Relationship Between Two Dimensions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 223*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Creating a Relationship Between Two Dimensions 

After editing the base dimension to enable auto-population of related objects, you’re ready to 

create the relationships between the two dimensions. 

To create a relationship between two dimensions: 

1. 
In the Object definitions list, locate the base dimension, and then click the corresponding 

link in the Object column. In this example, click Customer. 

The system opens the Object definition page. 

2. 
At the top of the page, click the Relationships link, or scroll down to the Relationships 

section. 

3. 
Click the New relationship link. 

The system opens the New relationship page for the selected dimension. 

4. 
Select the dimension with which you want to create the relationship. You can select either a 

standard or user-defined dimension. In this example, select Location. 

5. 
Click the Next button. 

The system opens the next page which defines the relationship you just created. For 

example, Customer: New relationship with location page. 

---


<!-- Page 224 -->
Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

6. 
Select the Relationship type. Each type is described here and on the page itself. 

Many-to-Many is the most common relationship type. 

Dimension relationships are reciprocal. In other words, creating a relationship from 

customer to location is the same as creating a relationship from location to customer. What 

distinguishes relationships is the relationship type. The relationship type determines the 

drop-down list that you create in the related object. For example, in the relationship 

between customer and location, if you pick a one-to-one relationship, in the customer 

record, you can pick just one value for the location. 

• 
One Customer to One Location 

Each customer can be related to, at most, one location 

Each location can be related to, at most, one customer 

• 
One Customer to Many Locations 

Each customer can be related to many locations 

Each location can be related to, at most, one customer 

• 
Many Customers to One Location 

Each customer can be related to, at most, one location 

Each location can be related to many customers 

• 
Many Customers to Many Locations 

Each customer can be related to many locations 

Each location can be related to many customers 

Auto-fill doesn’t work in many-to-many relationships. 

7. 
Click Save to confirm the relationship. 

The system returns you to the Object definition page for the dimension.

Creating a Naming Convention for Related-Dimension Display (optional) 

When you create a relationship, the system automatically creates a naming convention that will

Selecting the Related Dimension Value 

After you create a relationship between two dimensions, you are ready to select the related 

dimension value. For example, in the relationship of location to customer, you would select a 

specific customer and the specific location to be used each time a user creates a transaction with 

that customer. If you created a relationship that can have more than one value for the related

#### Testing the Dimension Relationship
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 228*



#### Setting the Value that Wins in a Transaction with Overlapping Relationships
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 228*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Testing the Dimension Relationship 

After creating a dimension relationship, you can easily test it in any transaction that uses the two 

dimensions. For example, if you created a customer/location relationship, you could test the 

relation by creating a transaction against that customer. The system automatically completes the 

location dimension with the value that you selected for the customer. In addition, because you 

didn’t enable override when you created the relationship, the user can view the location value but 

can’t change it. 

The user can view this value but can’t override it. 

Setting the Value that Wins in a Transaction with Overlapping Relationships 

If you have transactions with overlapping dimension relationships—that is, the base dimensions 

are different and the related dimension is the same, but with different values—you can set the 

priority for which related dimension value wins. For example, if you have two relationships where 

the two base dimensions are Customer and Department, and the related dimension is Location, 

you can configure the priority-order setting so that Location takes it value from the 

Customer/Location or the Department/Location relationship whenever the two relationships 

overlap in a transaction. 

To prioritize related dimensions: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. The General ledger setup page appears. 

3. 
Scroll down to the Dimension relationships table. 

4. 
In the Priority Order column for the appropriate related dimension, drag the handle of the 

dimension that should take precedence to the top of the list. 

---



#### Filtering and Restricting Values in Transactions With Overlapping Relationships
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 229*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Filtering and Restricting Values in Transactions With Overlapping Relationships 

Unlike simple relationships in which the single value of one dimension is set by the single value of 

another, many-to-many relationships can have multiple values on both sides of the relationship. 

You can filter for and populate lists of values to transactions that include many-to-many 

dimension relationships. The system is smart enough to handle overlapping relationships in the 

same transaction. 

Here’s how the system populates the values list for such relationships in a transaction: 

• 
If there are common values between the multiple relationships, the system populates the 

overlapping values to the related-dimension list. 

Example relationships: 

• 
Customer and Location 

• 
Department and Location 

• 
If no common values exist, the system populates the combined values to the related 

dimension list. 

Example relationships: 

• 
Customer and Location 

• 
Department and Location 

---


<!-- Page 230 -->
Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To restrict the list of values that appears for a many-to-many relationship: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, click the appropriate dimension, such as Customer. 

3. 
Scroll to the desired item in the dimension’s list, and then click the Edit link.  

4. 
On the dimension page, scroll to the bottom, and, in the related dimension field, enter or 

select an appropriate value. 

5. 
Continue adding values until the list is complete.

Dimensions 

This section discusses the different dimensions. 

A dimension is a category of data that you can organize and sort in meaningful ways. RealPage 

Financial Suite provides the following pre-defined dimensions: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

In addition, RealPage Financial Suite enables you to define new dimensions to suit your needs. 

These user-defined dimensions enable you to organize and sort categories of data unique to your 

business. For example, if you are a software company with various product lines, you might create 

a user-defined dimension called Line of business. The values you could add are Direct customers, 

Channel partner, and OEM. 

Dimensions enable you to collect, sort, analyze, and report on data within one category, or 

between categories, so you can identify key factors such as: 

• 
Your most profitable or most costly customers. 

• 
The return on investment of a location or department. 

• 
Whether and to what degree a new product or product line is successful. 

• 
Which way a particular aspect of your business is trending. 

RealPage Financial Suite dimensions give you fine control over data definition and data hierarchy. 

With dimensions, you can customize financial reports around specific business activities, get 

greater visibility into how the business is doing, and make faster, more meaningful business 

decisions. 

Additional fees may apply for user-defined dimensions. Contact your RealPage account 

representative for more information.

Use the Vendors (Suppliers) list to add and manage vendor records. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add a vendor. 

• 
View or edit a vendor’s details. 

• 
View the A/P ledger for the vendor. 

• 
View the total amount due to a vendor. 

• 
Delete a vendor record. 

• 
Export vendor information. 

If you are working in a multi-entity, multi-base currency company, then a View due link appears in 
the Total due column instead of an amount. Click this link to open the Vendor totals box to see 
the total amount due for each entity.

#### Adding Vendor (Supplier) Records
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 236*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding Vendor (Supplier) Records 

See the How to Get Here (on page 222) topic for a list of ways to access the Vendors list. 

Adding Vendor Records 

Add vendor records when you want to pay A/P invoices.  

When you add a vendor, you can type key descriptive information about that vendor and select 

the payment method that the vendor prefers, such as by check, credit card, or ACH (electronic 

payment). 

If you enabled the Single Scan Upload feature in your preferences and have previously 
downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the software 
when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, purchase order, service 
contract, or document. When this occurs, download the new software; there is no need to 
uninstall the previous version. 

To add a basic vendor record: 

1. 
In the ID field, type a unique identifier for the vendor record. 

Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, V0001 for a vendor ID. 

When you save the record, the system converts the vendor ID to all uppercase to prevent 

duplication. You can prevent this conversion by clearing the Set IDs to uppercase check 

box. For information, see Disabling Vendor ID Capitalization. 

After creating a vendor ID, you can only change it with the Customer Utility Tool. Most users 

do not have access to the tool as it requires administrator privileges. Contact your system 

administrator if you need to change a vendor ID. 

2. 
In the Name field, type the vendor’s name. The system completes the Print as field in the 

Primary Contact section. 

3. 
Select the One-time use check box to designate the vendor as a one-time or occasional use 

vendor that you don’t want to include in your standard vendor lists. An example of a 

one-time use of a vendor record is when you issue a customer’s deposit refund. 

These vendors won’t appear in the Vendors (Suppliers) list unless you select the Include 

one-time option at the top of the list. 

4. 
Select the Corporate vendor check box as needed. When you add an invoice for a corporate 

vendor, the system marks the invoice as a corporate invoice and prevents it from appearing 

in Site Experience. Also, corporate vendors do not appear in Site Experience. 

5. 
Select the This vendor is an owner check box when the vendor is also the owner of the 

company. 

---


<!-- Page 237 -->
Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

6. 
In the Status list, select the Active option if you want vendors to have A/P invoices entered 

and payments issued. You can also select the Inactive option to prevent A/P invoices from 

being entered and payment issued. 

You can inactivate multiple vendors at a time using the Customer Utility Tool’s Inactivate 

Vendors option. 

7. 
Select the appropriate Storefront supplier code. This code is the vendor’s code for use with 

the Storefront application associated with Spend Management.  

If your company does not use Spend Management, then this option does not appear. 

8. 
Select the Require PO – Spend check box option when your company requires that you 

create a manual or online purchase order before creating an online A/P invoice on behalf of 

the vendor. If a purchase order is not available to match with the A/P invoice, then the user 

cannot submit the A/P invoice for the vendor. 

The Require PO – Spend check box appears only when your company has purchased and 
installed Spend Management. 

9. 
Select the Send Offline Purchase Orders to Vendor check box. When enabled, when the 

user adds or edits a purchase order in the Submitted or Partially Approved state, the option 

Send purchase order to vendor appears.  

To use this feature, the vendor’s subscription type must also be set to Invoice Submission 

Service, and a Storefront Supplier Code must be defined for the vendor. 

If this option is ever disabled, the system continues to show the Send purchase order to 

vendor option on historical purchase orders.  

10. 
Select Keep active to prevent the vendor from being automatically changed to Inactive.  

Use this option for vendors that should remain available, even if they meet conditions that 

would normally make them inactive. For example, companies that use the AI Finance Agent 

may have rules that automatically inactivate vendor records based on configured criteria. 

When Keep active is selected, the vendor stays active and can continue to be used. 

11. 
Select the Exclude from Full Service check box to prevent the vendor from syncing with 

Invoice processing full service. You can enable syncing again at any time. 

12. 
Select the Exclude from Auto Request Storefront Account check box to prevent the system 

from sending an automatic request for the vendor for a Storefront account.  

13. 
Select the Preferred vendor check box to identify this vendor as one your company prefers 

or recommends using. This setting helps users distinguish preferred vendors from other 

vendors in the vendor list. 

---


<!-- Page 238 -->
Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

14. 
Select the Do not itemize invoices check box if you do not want the AI Agent to itemize this 

vendor’s invoices when its invoices are scanned. The system will define only one line item 

for the total amount of each invoice when the AI Agent scans this vendor’s invoices. This 

setting is useful when, after scanning in an invoice, you find that you have to delete line 

items after the AI Agent has broken out charge details into multiple line items.  

If you do not select this check box, the AI Agent creates a line item for each charge it finds 

in invoices when it scans invoices.  

15. 
Select the OneSite resident check box if the vendor is a resident in a OneSite-managed 

property. 

16. 
Select the Sync to external systems check box to allow RealPage Accounting to sync the 

vendor record with Procore or other external systems. 

This field appears only if you have configured the Procore integration in Job Cost & 
Reserves. 

17. 
Select the RequirePO check box when the vendor requires a purchase order. The A/P 

invoice must be matched to a purchase order before you save and post it. 

This field does not apply to actions performed in the RealPage Financial Suite system. The 

RequirePO check box appears only when your system is integrated with OPSTechnology. 
When the RequirePO check box is selected, it causes the OPS system to validate the 
purchase order record in OPS. 

Filling In the Tax Information Section 

The fields in this section vary based on the country where the vendor is located.  

1. 
In the Country field, type the country where the vendor is located.  

2. 
In the Tax ID field, type the company’s tax identification number or the individual’s Social 

Security Number.  

If the vendor is located in the United Kingdom, then the fields reflect UK tax requirements: 

1. 
In the Company name as registered field, type the company name as it is registered with 

the tax jurisdiction. 

2. 
In the Address field, type the address of the vendor’s tax jurisdiction. 

3. 
In the VAT reg no field, type the vendor’s VAT registration number.  

4. 
In the Date tax number last validated field, type the date that the tax number was last 

validated.  

Filling In the Primary Contact Section 

1. 
Fill in the name and address of the primary contact for the vendor. 

---

In the Print as field of the Primary contact section, verify that the name appears the way you

joint checks, then fill in the names of the two required signers. This field is required. 

3. 
In the Primary phone field, type the phone number of the primary contact. 

4. 
In the Mobile field, type the cell phone number of the primary contact. 

5. 
In the Pager field, type the pager number of the primary contact. 

6.

In the Remittance attachment section, select the desired format, PDF or Excel. The

#### Deleting or Inactivating a Vendor
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 241*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Deleting or Inactivating a Vendor 

See the How to Get Here (on page 222) topic for a list of ways to access the Vendors list. 

Deleting a Vendor 

If you haven’t used a vendor for any transactions in the system, you can permanently delete the 

vendor record. 

• 
In the Vendors list, select the Delete check box next to one or more vendor(s), and then 

click Delete to remove the vendor(s). 

Inactivating a Vendor 

Vendors that have already been used can’t be deleted. However, you can make a vendor inactive, 

effectively removing that vendor from drop-down menus and lists throughout the company. 

To make a vendor inactive: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click the Vendors option. The Vendors list opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the vendor record you want to make inactive. 

4. 
Change the Status for the vendor to Inactive. 

You can remove unused or duplicate vendors.

Vendor (Supplier) Information Page 

See the How to Get Here (on page 222) topic for a list of ways to access the Vendors (Suppliers) 

list. 

Use this page to add and edit vendor records. A vendor record has six tabs: 

• 
Vendor (Supplier): This tab has two sections, the Summary section, and the Primary contact 

section. Use the Summary section to determine how the vendor is handled in the system, 

and the Primary contact section to record all of the contact details for the primary contact of 

the vendor. 

• 
Additional information: This tab has five sections: Vendor details, Billing details, Email 

template options, Vendor merge, and CA DE 542. Use this tab to record details about the 

vendor and billing, select email templates to associate with a transaction type, view details 

about vendor merges, and indicate when a California form DE 542 is required and note the 

date the form was sent. 

• 
Contact list: This tab has two sections, Pay to/Return to and Contact list. Use this tab to 

define the contact to whom to direct payments and to list all contacts associated with this 

vendor. 

• 
Payment information: This tab has three sections: Payment details, Payment services, and 

Vendor account number. Use this tab to define how and when to pay this vendor. 

• 
Restrictions: This tab has one section. Use this tab to restrict access to this vendor. This tab 

appears only when your system has multiple entities. 

• 
Insurance/License: This tab has three sections for three insurance policies and licenses. Use 

this tab to maintain details about insurance and licenses that cover this vendor.

Fields 

ID 
The system provides two mutually exclusive ways to add vendor IDs. You 

can type your own unique ID, or you can have the system automatically 

add them from a present numbering scheme. Set up automatic 

numbering for vendors, 

This ID can’t be overwritten after the vendor is created. 

Best practices for creating identifiers 

An ID enables your company to keep track of a specific type of 

information, such as G/L account, department, location, transaction, 

vendor, and customer. You can create IDs by adding them on the fly or 

by having the system automatically add them from a preset numbering 

scheme. 

Whichever method you choose, we recommend against using leading 

zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can cause errors when you 

import information into your company from Excel because Excel 

removes the leading zeros. 

Best practice: Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, C0001 

for a customer ID. 

Workaround: If you must use leading zeros in IDs, then convert the 

column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file 

content. Excel won’t remove the leading zeros when you save the file. 

Remember to do this every time you use a template to import 

information that requires IDs.

The name of the vendor as it will appear on lists and menus across your 

company.

### Customers List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 261*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Customers List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 247) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Use the Customers list to view and manage customer records. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add new customers. 

• 
Edit or view existing customer details. 

• 
Import customer records. 

• 
Export the list of customers. 

• 
Open a customer’s A/R ledger. 

• 
View the total amount that a customer owes to an entity. 

By default, the Customers list uses icons and indentation to show how parent and child customers 

are related. This hierarchical view is helpful when you have customers that belong to the same 

parent customer, such as when you are doing business with subsidiaries or divisions of the same 

company and need to separately track their contact and billing information. 

The list also provides access to related information, including: 

a) Customer’s A/R ledger: Click the customer’s name to open the customer’s A/R ledger. 

b) Customer totals box: Click the amount in the Total due column to open the Customer 

totals box and view the individual amounts due from the customer.  

If you are working in a multi-entity, multi-currency company, then a View due link appears in 
place of an amount in the Total due column. Click this link to open the Customer totals box 
to see the total amount due for each entity. 

---



#### Adding Customers
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 262*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding Customers 

See the How to Get Here (on page 247) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

The Customer information page has multiple tabs that contain basic information about the 

customer, such as company name, address, and phone numbers. 

To add a customer: 

1. 
From the top level, click the Applications menu, and then select Accounts Receivable. 

2. 
Select 
 Add next to Customers. 

Filling In the Customer Section 

To fill in the customer’s company and contact information. 

1. 
In the ID field, type a unique identifier for the customer. 

After creating and saving a customer record, you can only change the Customer ID with the 
Customer Utility Tool . Most users do not have access to the Customer Utility tool. 
Contact your system administrator if you need to change a Customer ID. 

2. 
In the Name field, type the name of the company as it should appear in lists and menus. 

3. 
Select the One-time use check box to designate the customer as a one-time or occasional 

use customer that you don’t want to include in your standard customer lists. 

These customers won’t appear in the Customers list unless you select the Include 

one-time check box at the top of the list. 

4. 
Select the Status of the customer record, either Active or Inactive. Inactive customers do not 

appear in any system lists or drop-down lists. 

Filling In the Tax Information Section 

The Tax information section appears when you use the international version of the RealPage 
Financial Suite.  

1. 
Select the country where the customer files taxes in the Country drop-down list. 

2. 
In the VAT reg no field, type the customer’s VAT registration number so that you can track 

VAT taxes. 

Filling In the Primary Contact Section 

1. 
Type the name, address, and contact information for the person who is your primary contact 

associated with the company. 

2. 
In the Print as field, type the name of the company as it will appear on payments and 

notices. 

---


<!-- Page 263 -->
Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

When you create a new customer, the system automatically creates a related contact record 

for you. The Print as field is used in coordination with the Customer ID to create the 

suggested contact name, which is the unique contact ID used throughout the system that 

can’t be edited after creation. This is also the name that appears in all lists and drop-down 

lists. See Contacts for more detailed information. 

Duplicate information is shared between the Customer tab and the Contact list tab. 

Therefore, if you change the data in the Customer tab, the changes are reflected in the 

Contact list tab and vice versa (provided you have not selected the Exclude from the 

company contact list check box). 

3. 
Open the Additional information tab. 

Filling In the Additional Information Tab 

Enter accounting details for this customer: 

1. 
Select the customer’s type in the Type ID drop-down list. 

2. 
In the Sales rep drop-down list, select the user who is responsible for this customer’s 

account. 

3. 
If this customer account is a subsidiary of another customer, click the Parent drop down list, 

and then select the name of the parent company. 

4. 
To use a G/L group other than the default, select it in G/L group drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Territory ID drop-down list, select the sales territory to which you assigned the 

customer. You can also add a territory by clicking the Add link in the drop-down list. 

6. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, add an attachment to associate with the customer 

record. See Adding attachments to a record. Learn more about who can add attachments in 

Permissions for attachments. If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your 

file in the Attachments (on page 185) box to attach the file to this record. 

Filling In the Invoicing Details Section 

1. 
In the Term drop-down list, select the credit terms to extend to the customer. The selected 

term becomes the default term whenever you perform transactions related to the customer. 

You can also add a new term by clicking the Add link and filling in the A/R Terms 

Information box. 

2. 
In the Default revenue account drop-down list, select the G/L account that you want the 

system to use for revenue transactions. When you select an account, the system completes 

the G/L account field with the selected account in revenue transactions, but you can change 

it. 

If your system is an international system, the A/R account drop-down list appears instead.  

---


<!-- Page 264 -->
Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To use an alternative A/R account to override the default G/L A/R account, select it in the 

A/R account drop-down list. The system populates the A/R override account you select 
here to every invoice or adjustment transaction that includes this customer. See 
Overriding the G/L account in A/R transactions for more information.  
In Accounts Receivable, this feature applies to invoices and adjustments only. It doesn ’t 
apply to recurring invoices, manual deposits, quick check entry, quick invoice entry, or 
advances. 

3. 
In the Shipping method drop-down list, select how you will ship goods to the customer. 

You can also add a new shipping method by clicking the Add link and filling in the Shipping 

method information box. 

4. 
If the customer is a reseller of your products and services, type the customer’s resale 

number in the Resale number field. 

5. 
Select the Taxable check box if regular purchases from this customer are taxable. 

6. 
In the Tax group drop-down list, select the contact tax group to associate with the 

customer. 

This setting applies only when the customer is international. The contact tax group helps 
the system determine which tax maps and tax details to use to calculate tax for this 
customer for applicable documents in the Accounts Receivable application. 

7. 
In the Tax ID field, type the government tax ID number for the customer. (US only) 

8. 
To define a credit limit for this customer, type the amount of credit you are willing to extend 

to the customer in the Credit limit field. 

9. 
To prevent anyone from entering invoices for this customer, select the On Hold check box. 

10. 
In the Statement/Invoice delivery section, select how you want to deliver the customer’s 

statement: 

• 
Print: Mail the customer a printed copy of his invoice. 

• 
Email: Send a copy of the invoice through email. 

• 
Both: Mail the printed copy and send a copy of the A/R invoice through email. 

11. 
In the Default invoice message drop-down list, select the message that you want to include 

in this customer’s invoices. You can also add a standard message by clicking the Add link 

and then filling in the Customer Messages box. 

12. 
In the Comments field, make note of anything that others may need to know about this 

customer. 

13. 
The Currency field appears if your system is configured for multiple currencies. Select the 

currency that the customer uses.

Selected locations or departments will be able to view this customer. See Using the 

multi-select box (on page 171) for help on selecting locations and departments. 

When setting up location groups or department groups, keep in mind that restrictions can 
be based on groups that contain specific locations or departments, but can ’t be based on 
groups that filter dynamically based on the value of certain fields (such as locations where 
the status equals “Active ”). Location groups and department groups that contain dynamic 
filtering won’t appear on the Restrictions tab for you to select. 

Viewing or Editing a Customer 

See the How to Get Here (on page 247) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

The Customers menu item appears on both the All and Setup tabs of Accounts Receivable. Both 
menu options open the same Customers list, and the lists ’ settings are exactly the same. 

To view or edit customer details: 

1. 
In the Customers list, click the View or Edit next to the customer record. 

The Customer information page opens. 

2. 
View or edit the record as needed, and then click Done or Save. 

Deleting or Inactivating a Customer 

See the How to Get Here (on page 247) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

If you haven’t used a customer for any transactions in your company, you can click the Delete link 

in the Customers list to remove the customer. 

Customers that have already been used can’t be deleted. However, you can make that customer 

inactive, effectively removing the customer from drop-down menus and lists throughout the 

company. 

To make a customer inactive: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, and then select Accounts receivable. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab. 

3. 
Select Customers. The Customers list appears. 

4. 
Locate the customer that you want to make inactive and click Edit next to the Customer ID. 

5. 
On the Customer tab, change the Status for the customer to Inactive.  

After you’ve inactivated a customer, you can still access the customer’s record by selecting 

Include inactive at the top of the Customers list. 

6. 
Click the Save button.

Customer Information Page 

See the How to Get Here (on page 247) topic for a list of ways to access the Customers list. 

Use the Customer information page to add and change customer details. From this page, you 

can: 

• 
View or edit customer details. 

• 
Duplicate the customer record. 

• 
Print the customer details. 

• 
Export the customer details in XML format. 

• 
View the audit trail. 

Each customer record has four tabs: 

• 
Customer: This tab contains general information about the customer, such as their unique 

identifier, name, status, primary contact information. 

• 
Additional information: This tab contains additional information about the customer, such 

as their customer type, sales rep, parent company, invoicing details, transaction printing 

options, and email template. 

• 
Contact list: This tab contains the customer’s billing and shipping information. 

• 
Restrictions: This tab allows you to control who can view and edit the customer record. 

Fields 

Customers List Columns 

Customer ID 
This column contains a unique identifier assigned to the customer.

#### Importing Employees
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 276*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Employees 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Employees`


You can import employees’ data by uploading a CSV file. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file containing 

data. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Employees > Template`


1. 
Download the most recent Employees template from the Import data list. When you get 

your templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been tailored to your 

specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses.  

2. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

3. 
Fill in the required columns in the template using the correct formatting as explained in the 

template. See Filling in Import Templates. 

• 
EMPLOYEE_ID: Type a unique identifier for the employee. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type the employee’s contact name of up to 40 characters. 

• 
PRINT_AS: Type the employee name as you want it to appear on documents. 

4. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. Refer to the Employees Data Template for 

a full list of columns. 

After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 

mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common Errors 

and Best Practices. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

6. 
On the Company menu, click Import data. 

7. 
In the Set Up Company Master List section, find the Employees row, and then click the 

Import link. The Employees import box opens. 

---


<!-- Page 277 -->
Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

8. 
To import the CSV file with employee data: 

• 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file you want to import. 

• 
In the Date format field, select the desired date format. 

When you select a date format here, the system attempts to import your file using the 

selected date format. If the system can’t import your file with the selected date format, 

it attempts to discover the date format used in your file and import the data using that 

date format. 

• 
In the File encoding drop-down list, leave this option set to Auto detect unless you’re 

unable to import your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to 

select a different type of file encoding. 

• 
Select the Process Offline check box to import offline. 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much 

processing the system must do on the uploaded data. If you’re not sure how much 

time your upload will take, select Process Offline. When the system completes the 

process, it sends an email to the address you provide in the Email results to this 

address field. The system also sends you any errors that may have occurred in the 

process. If you prefer to wait until the upload process is complete, do not select the 

Process Offline check box. 

• 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. 

This is the email address where the system sends import results and errors. You can 

enter multiple email addresses, separated by a semicolon (;) or comma (,). RealPage 

highly recommends entering an email address. 

9. 
Click the Import button. 

10. 
Resolve any errors.

#### Adding an Employee
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 279*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Adding an Employee 

See the How to Get Here (on page 263) topic for a list of ways to access this page. 

A basic employee record contains an employee ID and a primary contact name that is used to 

reference the employee throughout the system. 

To add an employee, complete the following fields on the Employee information page: 

1. 
In the Employee ID field, type a unique identifier for the employee. An employee ID can 

consist of numbers, letters, or both. 

You can create employee IDs by adding them manually or by creating a document 

numbering sequence to automatically generate them from a preset numbering scheme. 

As a best practice, do not use leading zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can 

cause errors when you import information into your company from Excel because Excel 

removes the leading zeros. 

If you must use leading zeros in your ID, be sure to convert the column of ID numbers to 

text format in Excel before importing the file content so that Excel does not remove the 

leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you use a template to 

import information that requires IDs. 

2. 
In the Primary contact name drop-down list, select the contact name that is used to 

reference the employee throughout the system and in printed output. If needed, create a 

new contact. 

The Status drop-down list defaults to Active. Do not change this value to Inactive unless you 

no longer want the employee to appear in Employee drop-down lists throughout the 

system. 

---

Departments 

Although departments are optional, they are useful for filtering and categorizing data in many 

areas of the system. For example, you may want to generate financial reports and graphs based 

on departments. Additionally, many companies set up transaction approvals to be routed to the 

department manager. 

You can create a hierarchy of departments to reflect how departments are organized in your 

company. The hierarchy is established by defining parent and child relationships between 

departments. For example, you could have a parent department called West Coast Division that 

contains several child departments including Engineering, which itself has two additional child 

departments, Software Engineering and Hardware Engineering. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with department dimensions: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Departments 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing department records. You may have additional 

options based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Departments`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Company, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, select Departments. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > Departments`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Forecasting & Planning, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, select Departments.

Importing Departments 

You can import departments by uploading a CSV file. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Departments > Template`


1. 
Download the most recent Departments template from the Import data list. When you get 

your templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been tailored to your 

specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses. See Downloading a 

Template from the Import Data Page. 

2. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

3. 
Fill in the import template starting with the required columns in the template: 

• 
DEPT_ID: Type a unique identifier for the department. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
DEPT_NAME: Type a department name of up to 40 characters.

In the Set Up Company Master List section, find the Departments row, and then click the 

Import link.

Importing the Data 

To import the CSV file with department data: 

• 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file you want to import. 

• 
In the Date format field, select the desired date format. 

When you select a date format here, the system attempts to import your file using the 

selected date format. If the system can’t import your file with the selected date format, 

it attempts to discover the date format used in your file and import the data using that 

date format. 

• 
In the File encoding drop-down list, leave this option set to Auto detect unless you’re 

unable to import your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to 

select a different type of file encoding. 

• 
Select the Process Offline check box to import offline. 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much 

processing the system must do on the uploaded data. If you’re not sure how much 

time your upload will take, select Process Offline. When the system completes the 

process, it sends an email to the address you provide in the Email results to this 

address field. The system also sends you any errors that may have occurred in the 

process. If you prefer to wait until the upload process is complete, do not select the 

Process Offline check box. 

• 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. 

• 
This is the email address where the system sends import results and errors. You can 

enter multiple email addresses, separated by a semicolon (;) or comma (,). RealPage 

highly recommends entering an email address. 

• 
Click the Import button. 

• 
Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors.

Adding and Editing Departments 

See the How to Get Here (on page 273) topic for a list of ways to access the Departments list. 

All you need to create a department is to assign an ID and name for it. 

To add a department: 

1. 
Enter an ID and a Name. See Best Practices for Creating Identifiers. 

You cannot change the Department ID after creating and saving the department record. 
However, the administrator can change the Department ID using the Customer Utility Tool . 
Contact your system administrator if you need to change a department ID. 

2. 
If the department belongs to a hierarchy of departments, select its Parent department from 

the drop-down list. 

3. 
Click the Manager drop-down list to select a manager from the list of employees. If no 


> **Navigation Path:** `names appear in this list, you need to add them by clicking Reports > All > Dimensions >`


Employees. 

If you want department managers to approve their employees’ purchase requests, you must 

select a manager. Otherwise, you can leave this blank. 

4. 
Select the status from the Status drop-down list. The default status is Active. If you no 

longer use the department and do not want it to appear in lists, select Inactive. The 

department information remains in your system, but the system will not display it in any 

department lists. You can view these inactive departments by selecting the Include Inactive 

check box on top of the list. 

5. 
Type a Department title in the Reporting section. 

To save time, you can run a financial report or other General Ledger report for a group of 

entities/locations or departments and have the system automatically split the report into 

multiple individual reports. In this case, the report header for the “individual report” displays 

the name of the department, entity, or location, plus any title text you enter here, instead of 

the company name. 

For example, a location title might provide additional information that you want to display 

on reports, such as the address and manager name. 

San Jose office 

111 Post Street 

Managed by: Karla Grace 

You can enter up to five lines, with a maximum of 50 characters per line. 

6. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

new. The system saves the record and opens a new blank record.

Locations 

You can create a hierarchy of locations to reflect how locations are organized in your company. 

The hierarchy is established by defining parent and child relationships between locations.  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have limited or full Administrator privileges to work with locations. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with locations: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Company 
Locations 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

---



#### How to Get Here
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 295*



#### Importing Locations
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 295*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing location records. You may have additional options 

based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Locations`


1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, select Locations. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > Locations`


1. 
Open the Forecasting & Planning menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, select Locations. 

Importing Locations 

You can import locations by uploading a CSV file. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file containing 

data. 

Downloading the Template 

When you download templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been 

tailored to your specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses.  

1. 
Open the Company menu.  

2. 
Click the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Locations row, and then click the 

Template link. 

The system either downloads the Locations.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling In the Locations Template 

Add your data using the correct formatting as explained in the template.  

1. 
Open the template in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

---


<!-- Page 296 -->
Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type a unique identifier for the location. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
LOCATION_NAME: Type a location name of up to 40 characters. 

• 
START_DATE: Type the start date related to the location.  

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type a contact name. This column is required if the contact is 

specified. 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. 

4. 
After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 

mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common errors, 

Best practices. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format [File > Export > CSV (Comma delimited file)]. 

6. 
Import the location data’s CSV file (Company > All > Import Data > Locations > Import). 

7. 
In the Date format field, unless your dates are already in MM/DD/YYYY format, select a date 

format that you want to use. The system supports 24 date formats.  

8. 
In the File encoding field, leave the setting as auto detect unless you are unable to import 

your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of 

file encoding. 

9. 
Select the Process offline check box if you are importing a large quantity of data or if you 

are unsure how much time your import will take. Some imports can take considerable time, 

depending on their size and how much processing the system must do on the imported 

data. The Process offline feature allows the system to process the data when system activity 

is lighter. If you prefer to wait until the import process is complete, do not select the 

Process offline check box. 

10. 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. When the system 

completes the import process, it sends an email to the address with either a message about 

the success or failure of the import, including any errors that occurred in the process. 

11. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row in the file that starts with a # symbol. 

12. 
Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors. 

---

Locations List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 283) topic for a list of ways to access the Locations list. 

Use the Locations list to view a list of the locations in your company. You can sort and filter the 

locations list to see just the group of locations you want using the standard filters, group filters, 

and custom views. 

From the Locations list, you can: 

• 
Add a new location record. 

• 
Edit and view a location’s details. 

• 
Display the hierarchy of locations. 

• 
Delete a location. 

• 
Export the list of locations. 

If you have long lists of locations in external data files, you can upload them in CSV format on the 

Import data page. On the Locations row, click the Import link. 

List Tools 

For information about filters, sorts, and views, see Managing lists (on page 96). 

For information about field-level controls, see Using controls in drop-down lists (on page 115). 

Adding and Editing Locations 

See the How to Get Here (on page 283) topic for a list of ways to access the Locations list. 

To add a location: 

1. 
Type the ID and Name of the location as you want it to appear in the system. 

After saving the record you cannot change the location ID.  

If you must change the ID, contact your system administrator and have them run the 

RealPage Accounting Customer Utility tool to change the Location ID/Property ID. 

2. 
If the location belongs to a hierarchy of locations, then select its Parent location. 

• 
For example, suppose that your West Coast Division contains several locations 

including California, Nevada, and Utah. When you define California, Nevada, and Utah, 

select West Coast Division as the parent. 

• 
If you have a multi-entity company that also uses multiple base currencies, then you 

must assign each location to an entity so that the system knows which base currency 

to use for that location. In this case, you can’t change the Parent location. 

You can change the parent of a location only when your system uses one base 
currency. 

---


<!-- Page 298 -->
Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
Type the location’s Tax ID. 

• 
For US companies with domestic-only business, type the location’s state tax ID for 

reference purposes. 

• 
If the location tracks VAT, then type the location’s VAT registration ID. 

4. 
In the Manager drop-down list, select or add the employee who manages this location. This 

field is useful if you route purchasing approvals to the manager of a requesting employee’s 

location. 

5. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists. 

Filling In the Contacts Section 

Unlike contact records that refer to an individual (such as an employee), contact records for 

locations contain information about the location. At a minimum, enter a main contact that 

specifies the location name, address, and other details as they should appear on A/R invoices, A/P 

invoices, and other forms. If the location uses a different address for receiving goods and services, 

then create or select a Ship to contact record.  

1. 
In the Location drop-down list, add or select the main location contact. The location’s 

contact record must contain the company name, address, and other details as you want 

them to appear on A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and other forms. 

2. 
Add or select the Ship to contact record. 

Filling In the Reporting Section 

Enter the information that you want to appear in reports. You can enter up to five lines, with a 

maximum of 50 characters per line. 

To save time, you can run a financial report or other general ledger report for a group of 

entities/locations or departments and have the system automatically split the report into multiple 

individual reports. In this case, the report header for the “individual report” displays the name of 

the department, entity, or location, plus any title text you enter in the Location title field, instead 

of the company name. 

For example, a location title might provide additional information that you want to display in 

reports, such as the address and manager name. You can enter up to five lines, with a maximum 

of 50 characters per line. For more information, see Individual Reports for Each Department 

Location or Entity. 

The Reporting section appears only when the Enable additional header titles option is selected on 
the General ledger application’s configuration page.  

---

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Filling In the Dates of Operation Section 

1. 
In the Start date field, type the date that the building became operational. This information 

is for record-keeping purposes only and is not used anywhere else in the system. 

2. 
In the End date field, type the date when the location was taken out of operation. This 

information is for record-keeping purposes only and is not used anywhere else in the 

system. 

Filling In the Tax Code Groups Section 

The system uses tax codes for automatic tax charging. Assigning tax codes to locations is the last 

step in setting up this feature.  

Select the Federal, Provincial/State, City, County, or other applicable tax code from the 

drop-down lists. Your company configures the tax code group names, so your company’s tax 

code group names may vary.  

Defining the Location’s Management Reporting Codes 

Management reporting codes let you capture location attributes for filtering reports. Location 

management reporting code descriptions are the same as the entity reporting codes. 

1. 
Click the Management reporting codes tab. 

2. 
Assign reporting codes as needed. 

3. 
Click the Save button. You can also save this record and create another one. Click the More 

actions button, and then select Save & new. Another blank location information record 

opens. 

To edit a location: 

1. 
In the Dimensions section of an application’s menu, click the Locations option. The 

Locations list opens. 

2. 
Locate the location you want to edit and click Edit next to it. The Location information page 

opens. 

3. 
Change any information about the location as you want it to appear in the system. 

4. 
Click Save.

Inactivating a Location 

See the How to Get Here (on page 283) topic for a list of ways to access the Locations list. 

Making a location inactive does not make its associated accounts and transactions inactive. 

Transactions and accounts of inactive locations continue to appear in lists.  

To make a location inactive: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the All tab of the menu. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, click Locations. The Locations list opens. 

3. 
Find the location that you want to inactivate, and then click the Edit link. The Location 

information page opens. 

4. 
In the Status drop-down list, click Inactive. 

5. 
Click Save. 

The system continues to include transactions of the location in invoices, adjustments, and 

advances lists. In addition, accounts associated with the location continue to appear in lists. 

However, bank account records cannot be viewed. If you want to view the bank account of 

an inactive location, you must reactivate the location first.

### Classes
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 306*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Classes 

Just like any other standard dimension, classes are tags with a set of values which you can 

associate with transactions to create and filter reports. However, unlike other dimensions, classes 

aren’t linked to any specific information in other areas of the system like vendors, customers, or 

employees are. For example, you can rename vendor dimension to something more meaningful 

like “Supplier,” but because the vendor dimension is used for a specific purpose across many 

applications, you can’t repurpose the vendor dimension. 

Classes, instead, can be both renamed and repurposed to track anything you want. For example, if 

your business requires you to track the industry of all of your customers, you could rename Class 

to Industry, add a few custom fields, and then build reports off your new Industry dimension. 

As with all dimensions, associate only one class per detail transaction line. You can co-mingle 

multiple class groupings, depending on which transactions you choose to use with class. For 

example, you can use a class to track loan types on loan invoice transactions and use a class to 

track cost transactions on internal projects.

About Dimension Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Setup > Dimension Groups`


In addition to the default dimensions for departments and locations, your company can use other 

standard dimensions that are available out-of-the-box, as well as user-defined dimensions that 

you create for your own unique tracking requirements. These dimensions let you filter or display 

information in multiple ways, for instance by showing data from only certain locations or projects. 

A dimension group is a name for a particular set of members in a dimension, or a set of members 

that meet certain criteria. For example, you might create customer groups for a particular set of 

customers, customers located in a particular state, or customers with the greatest open balance. 

Finding Each Type of Dimension Group

Availability depends on the dimensions that are set up for your company and your own

#### Where Dimension Groups Can and Can’t Be Used
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 315*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Where Dimension Groups Can and Can’t Be Used 

The following describes where you can and cannot use dimension group filters: 

Financial Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Financial reports allow filtering by dimension groups in Applications > General Ledger > All >`



> **Navigation Path:** `Financial Reporting > Financial Reports.`


When you define a report, you can specify the filters as part of the report definition, or you can 

prompt the user to filter the report at runtime. 

Financial Graphs 


> **Navigation Path:** `Financial graphs allow filtering by dimension groups in Applications > General Ledger > All >`


Financial Reporting > Financial Graphs. 

When you define a graph, you can specify the filters as part of the graph definition, or you can 

prompt the user to filter the graph at runtime. 

Standard General Ledger Reports 

Standard G/L reports listed on the G/L menu, such as the Journals or Trial Balance report, allow 

filtering by dimension groups. 

When you run a G/L report, you can select the filters to use, or you can create a pre-filtered report 

by memorizing the report with your selected filters. 

Dashboards 

Dashboards allow filtering by dimension groups, but filtering is limited to components for 

performance cards, financial reports and graphs, and standard G/L reports. You can also pre-filter 

dashboard components for a dimension group. See Dashboard filtering. 

Other Reports 

Currently, reports outside of the G/L do not support dimension groups: 

• 
Standard reports outside of the G/L 

• 
Custom reports created with the Custom Report Writer

### Dimension Groups in Reports and Dashboards
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 316*



#### How Dimension Groups Are Used in Financial Reports
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 316*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension Groups in Reports and Dashboards 

Defining a dimension group gives you additional control over what appears in reports and 

dashboards. In general, any dimension group that you create will appear as additional filter 

choices. 

With a dimension group, you can: 

• 
Filter for a particular set of members, such as specific customers, vendors, or locations. 

• 
Filter to show data from members that meet certain criteria, such as items of the same type 

or locations with the same parent location. 

• 
Take advantage of dimension count to post to statistical journal entries automatically. 

How Dimension Groups Are Used in Financial Reports 

In financial reports, dimension groups can be used in several ways: 

• 
Filtering for multiple dimension members, or for members that meet certain criteria 

• 
Controlling the order in which the members appear in report columns and rows 

• 
As the basis for report structures 

Dimension report structures (on page 328) enable dimensions to be used on the rows or columns 

of financial reports. The following graphic shows a simple location report structure named South, 

which contains a location group entitled Southern offices.

Setting Up Dimension Groups 

The way that you set up dimension groups for your company depends on your business and how 

you plan to use the groups. 

For example, if your company performs services from multiple locations, you can set up 

dimension groups that help you filter reports by location, customer, and employee. In each type 

of dimension group, you can define multiple groups for different purposes, such as groups that 

filter customers by type, amount due, country, or even a combination of criteria.

your permissions.

Adding or Editing a Group 

1.

If you’re editing an existing group, click the corresponding Edit link for the group. 

2. 
Enter an ID and Name for the dimension group. 

When displayed elsewhere in the system, the dimension group will be listed with the ID and 
name together (ID--Name), as in NAOPS--North America Operations. You can no longer 
change IDs after creating the group, but you can edit names at a later time. 

3. 
Enter a Description that can help identify what this group includes or how it is used. 

4.
