• 
Specific members: Select if you want to hand pick the locations, departments, 

customers, vendors, or employees to include in the group. 

• 
All members: Select if you want to filter based on criteria of your choice. For example, 

you might define a Direct Customers group which includes all members but then 

filters the results to only customers where the Customer Type field is equal to Direct. 

Learn more about determining what’s in the group (on page 308). 

5. 
Define how you want to sort dimension members when displayed in reports. 

The display order for members is controlled by the selected Group type. Learn how to select 

and order members (on page 309). 

• 
Specific members: The system displays the members in the order they appear in the 

Members list. 

• 
All members: In Sort order, select between Ascending and Descending. In Sorting 

field, select the field by which you want to sort the members. By default, the system 

sorts the members in ascending order based on ID. In Max matches, you can limit the 

number of members the system displays or leave it blank to show all members. 

6. 
Select the Dimension structure check box to automatically create a dimension structure (on 

page 328) that enables the group to be used on the rows or columns of financial reports. 


> **Navigation Path:** `You can find your dimension structures by going to Reports > Setup > Dimension`


Structures. 

If you don’t create a dimension structure for the group, you can use the group for filtering 

only. 

7. 
If you are a user with administrative privileges and you are creating a location group, then 

you have the option to make the location group public or private. If you are not an 

administrative user, then any location group that you create will automatically be private. 

See Making a Location Group Public or Private (on page 320) for more information.

#### Filtering Groups
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 323*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Filtering Groups 

Use filters on dimension groups to affect what appears in reports. This page describes a few 

examples of how you can apply filters to dimension groups. You can: 

• 
Filter with field values. 

• 
Filter for employees, locations, or departments managed by the current user. 

• 
Combine multiple filters. 

• 
Create dimension groups that contain both active and inactive members (on page 312). 

Filtering with Field Values 

You can add filters that select dimension members based on the value of certain fields. For 

example, you might want to select customers of a certain type or vendors that have a payment 

priority of urgent. 

1. 
Select the field you want to filter on. 

2. 
Choose the operation and value you want to filter for. 

The options you’ll see depend on the field you choose. 

By default, if you add more than one filter, members are included only if they match all 

criteria. However, you can change this behavior using the options in the Filter conditions 

section. 

Filtering for Employees, Locations, or Departments Managed by the Current User 

Dimension groups can automatically show managers only the information that’s relevant to them. 

For example, you can set up an Employee dimension group called My employees, which 

dynamically filters for employees managed by the current user. Similarly, groups can be used to 

filter for departments or locations managed by the current user. 

The current user is the user who is currently logged into the system. 

When you set the filter to current user, you limit the user to see only the group—such as 

employees or locations—that is associated with the user. For example, if you set a filter where the 

field is Manager and the operator is current user, when the manager runs the report, he or she will 

only see his or her own employees. To create a group that filters for the current user: 

1. 
Create a new group of type Department or Location. 

2. 
Define the group by giving it a name that users will recognize. 

For example — My department. 

3. 
In the Filters section, select a field that is connected to an employee who is a user in the 

system. For Department or Location dimension groups, you can select the Manager field. 

---



#### Creating a Dimension Group Filter for Both Active and Inactive Members
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 324*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Not all contact fields are connected to a user. For this reason, filtering for the current 
user is restricted to the Manager field. 

4. 
Set the Operator to is current user. 

Combining Multiple Filters 

If you have multiple filters, the default behavior is to match only members that meet all of the 

criteria. However, you can change how this works using the Filter conditions section. 

Filter Conditions 

All (AND) 
Include members that match all criteria (the default). 

Any (OR) 
Include members that match any criteria. 

Expression 
Uses an expression that you define to apply the filters. 

For example, the following expression matches members that either meet criteria 1 

and 2, or that meet criteria 3. 

(1 AND 2) OR 3 

If you want to select one of something, such as departments where the manager is either Jim, 
Sue, or Terri, create several filters and use the Any (OR) filter condition. 

Creating a Dimension Group Filter for Both Active and Inactive Members 

If you want to include inactive dimensions in reports, you can create a dimension group that 

filters for both active and inactive members. To do this: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the Dimension groups section, select the dimension type to filter (for example, 

departments or locations.) 

3. 
Select the dimension group to filter, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
In the Filters section, create two filters: 

• 
Status equals active  

• 
Status equals inactive

Deleting a Dimension Group 

You cannot delete dimension groups that are used for reporting. 

To delete a dimension group: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the Dimension groups section, select the dimension type. 

3. 
Locate the dimension group to delete, and then click the corresponding Delete link. 

If you are unable to delete a dimension group, check whether the group is currently used to filter 
one or more reports, graphs, or dashboards (on page 304 ) or is part of a dimension structure 
(on page 328 ). 

For example, if you have a location group that you use to filter financial reports, remove the filter 
from the financial reports, save your changes, and then try deleting the location group again.

### Location Groups
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 327*

Location Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Groups > Location`


In RealPage Financial Suite, you can create a location group so that you can generate reports for 

more than one property at a time. A property can be a member of more than one location group. 

For example, you can have one location group for all of your Texas properties, and another 

location group that contains all properties. 

There are a number of ways to use a location group: 

• 
All active properties 

• 
Specific properties 

• 
Reporting all location groups for specific members 

• 
Reporting the locations in a location group 

• 
By manager 

• 
Where the manager is the current user 

• 
With the same parent property 

• 
With a particular base currency 

It’s also possible to create a location group that includes only your company’s entities, thereby 

representing an “entity group” in reporting. See Creating Entity Groups (on page 320) for more 

information. 

For companies using OpsTechnology with RealPage Accounting, OpsTechnology does not 
recognize location groups. When you restrict a vendor to a location group in RealPage 
Accounting, the system sends this information to OpsTechnology as a list of locations rather 
than the location group.

Adding a Location Group

 Location`


To add a location group: 

1.

 Add button next to Location.

3.

name together (ID--Name), as in NAOPS--North America Operations. IDs can’t be changed

throughout the system.

location group. This information is only for your benefit; the system does not use this 

information anywhere else. 

7.

• 
All members: Select this option if you want to filter which locations are included in the 

group based on the criteria of your choice. For example, you might define a “US 

Locations” group which includes all members but then filters the results to only 

locations in the United States. 

• 
Specific members: Select this option if you want to choose specific locations to 

include in the group. 

Tip: To include all active members of a group (such as all customers), select All 

members as the group type. Then, in the Filters section, set the Field to “Status, ”

Dimension Group (on page 308 ) for more information.

In the Sort order drop-down list, select whether you want to sort the members of the

members of the location group.

group.

In a multi-entity environment, how do I select entity-specific members?

Set Up Filter Conditions 

Use this section to set up filters for the location group. With filters, you can: 

• 
Create field/value tests that will determine which locations are included in the group. 

• 
Create an expression with conditions that determine members of the group. 

To set up filters: 

1. 
In the Field drop-down list, select the field that you want to use for a condition’s test. 

2. 
In the Operator drop-down list, select the comparison operator. 

3. 
In the Value drop-down list, type the value to compare. 

4. 
Continue adding rows to the list as needed, especially if you are building conditions for an 

expression: 

• 
Click 
 Add to add another row.  

• 
Click 
 Delete to delete a row. 

---

Because an expression uses the row numbers in the Filters list, you must write the 
expression last. 

5. 
In the Filter conditions field, select the logic that the system should use when filtering 

locations: 

• 
All (AND): All tests must result in a True state to include a member in the group. 

• 
Any (OR): At least one test must result in a True state to include a member in the 

group. 

• 
Expression: Select to type a Boolean expression in the Condition box below it. 

For example, say you’ve defined three field/value tests in the Filters list: 

• 
Country is the US 

• 
Base currency is USD. 

• 
Location Contact Name starts with “Ed.” 

In this case, you can set filter conditions as follows: 

• 
Select All (AND) to include a location only when all of these tests are true. 

• 
Select OR to include any location in which at least one of these tests is true. 

• 
Select Expression if you want to set up a more complex combination. When you select 

Expression, type the condition logic in the Condition field that appears below. Use the 

row numbers of the Filters list in the expression.

Example of a Condition 

You want the system to find properties with an amount between $150 and $999. 

Each row is a condition. 

Row 1: 

Field = Status 

Operator = equals 

Value = Active 

Row 2:  

Field = First tax month 

Operator = equals 

Value = January 

Expression Examples 

(1 AND 2) OR (2 AND 3) 

If the first two expressions both evaluate to true OR if the second and third expressions both 

evaluate to true, then the location is included in the group.  

(1 AND 3) OR 2 

If the first and third conditions both evaluate to true or the second condition evaluates to true, 

then the location is included in the group.

actually creating a location group with the location records that represent your company’s

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Groups > 
 Location`


Users with full or limited administrative privileges can choose whether to make a location group 

public or private. Public location groups can be viewed and edited by all users. Private location 

groups can be viewed and edited only by the following types of users:

Users with full or limited administrative privileges 

• 
Users with the Administrator role 

• 
Users with the Location Group Admin role

Dimension Report Structures 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Structures`


Dimension report structures provide a flexible way for you to organize dimension data that you 

want to see on the rows or columns of a financial report. For example, instead of showing all 

locations on a report, you might want to select a Location structure that is named for a particular 

region and includes a subset of locations. 

You can add any number of structures for the dimensions you track. 

The list of standard dimension structures may include: 

• 
Customer 

• 
Department 

• 
Employee 

• 
Location 

• 
Vendor 

If you have additional dimension structures listed in the Dimension structure submenu, they are 

custom structures and are not discussed in this document. 

Creating a dimension structure from a group enables you to add the group to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. 

A dimension structure can only be used for filtering reports if you don’t select the Dimension 

Structure check box when you are creating a dimension group. 

Viewing the Available Dimension Report Structures

financial reports (on page 328).

### Dimension Structures Overview
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 339*

Dimension Structures Overview 

Dimension structures are structures that represent dimensional data that you intend to use on the 

rows or columns of financial reports. 

a) Dimension structure on report rows 

b) Dimension structure on report columns 

For example, you might create dimension structures that show: 

• 
Selected departments 

• 
Locations by region 

You can create any number of dimension structures to represent the different ways you want to 

segment your data. For instance, you might create multiple customer structures that enable you 

to analyze your Customers by type, Customers by sales territory, and so on. After they’re created, 

the re-usable dimension structures can be used across the rows or columns of any number of 

financial reports. 

In the following example, two different dimension structures are added to the rows of a report: 

• 
One hierarchical structure that breaks down customers by industry. 

• 
A flat structure that lists individual items 

When added to the rows of a report, each dimension structure has: 

• 
a heading 

• 
rows for the individual members or substructures in the dimension structure 

• 
a total row

children. 

• 
By default, amounts for dimension members don’t include amounts from children. For 

example, amounts for departments don’t include any child departments, locations 

don’t include sub locations, and so on. 

• 
In some cases, rolled up reporting might make sense. For example, suppose that your 

projects are typically organized into child projects. By selecting Roll Up Child 

Amounts, you can ensure that when Project A is included on a report, the amounts 

reported all of the child projects.

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 347*

How the System Handles Hierarchical Dimensions 

Dimensions are often hierarchical. For example, a department can have one or more child 

departments up to several levels deep.  

When a report filter includes a member of a dimension, data from any members that belong to it 

will also be included. This means that a department group that matches the Engineering 

department will automatically include data from any sub departments (like Development, Quality 

Assurance, and Documentation.) 

When filtering financial reports by department or location, you can decide to exclude sub 

departments or sub locations by clearing the Include Subs option under the filter field. 

Dimension Structures Created from Dimension Groups 

Dimension structures are built from dimension groups, which can contain particular members 

(such as one or more locations) or members that meet certain criteria (such as customers of a 

particular type). Learn more about dimension groups (on page 355). 

The following graphic shows a simple location structure named South, which contains a location 

group that includes a company’s southern offices as its members. 

a) Dimension groups are custom groupings that are meaningful to your company. 

b) Dimension report structures can contain one or more dimension groups. 

c) The dimension report structure is what enables you to add the dimension to the report. 

Dimension groups and dimension structures work together to provide power and flexibility in 

reporting. 

---



#### Examples
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 348*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Dimension groups enable you to dynamically filter data at the time you run a report, and 

can be used for standard reports, such as an A/R Ledger, as well as financial reports. 

• 
In addition to creating groups that include particular members, one of the most 

powerful ways to use dimension groups is to select members based on filter criteria. 

For example, a dimension group can filter for customers of the same type, items from 

the same product line, or locations with the same parent location. 

• 
Dimension groups are also used outside of financial reports. For example, you might 

have a dimension group that is used only to filter the A/R Ledger for customers with 

an outstanding balance greater than $500. 

• 
Dimension structures are created specifically for the purpose of adding dimensions to the 

rows or columns of financial reports. 

• 
Depending on how you assemble the groups in structures, you can achieve different 

results on reports. Groups can be assembled into structures that display dimension 

members (such as locations or customers) in a flat list or can be used to create 

multi-level hierarchical structures. 

• 
As with account groups, dimension structures enable you to choose what text you 

want to appear on heading and total lines, for example enabling you to display 

Customers by Industry in the heading row and Total Customers in the total row. 

Examples 

This section provides step-by-step instructions for creating specific types of dimension structures 

that you might need for your financial reports. 

Learn how to create structures that represent: 

A Single Member (Such as a Single Location) 

In some cases, you might want to display a single dimension member, such as a particular 

location or department, by itself in a column or row. 

To create this type of structure, you create a dimension group that contains a single member and 

then select the option to create a dimension structure of the same name. 

To create this type of structure: 

1. 
Create a new dimension group, such as a new Location group. 

• 
For example, to create a new location group, go to the Reports application, click the 

Setup tab, and then select Location in the Dimension groups section. 

• 
Click the Add button to create a new group. 

2. 
Type an ID for the group. When you press the TAB key, the system prefills this ID as the 

name. 

3. 
For the Group type, select Specific members. 

---


<!-- Page 349 -->
Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

4. 
Click in the Members section, and then add the member. For example, you might add a 

downtown location. 

5. 
Select the Dimension structure option to request that we automatically create a dimension 

structure with the same name. 

When you save your new dimension group, the corresponding dimension structure is 

created at the same time. That way, the dimension group will be ready to be used on 

financial reports. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Verify the dimension structure and make any optional changes. 

• 
Display the dimension structure list. For example, to display your Location structures, 

go to the General Ledger menu and, under Report Structure, select Dimension 

Structures > Location. 

• 
Click the Edit link next to the structure you want to edit. 

• 
Verify how the structure will appear on reports by reviewing the Display on report as

Multi-Entity Shared > Multi-Entity Report Structures 

You can create report structures both at the top level and at the entity level of a multi-entity 

shared company. 

In practice, many companies create and manage the majority of account groups and dimension 

structures at the top level of the company. These report structures are then automatically shared 

by all entities, and available for use in financial reports, graphs, and performance cards. 

Best Practices 

To determine whether to create a report structure at the top level or entity level, consider who 

needs to access the structure.

If a report structure should be available to all entities, create it at the top level. Account 

groups and dimension structures created at the top level automatically appear in the 

corresponding lists in each entity. 

Report structures created at the top level can be edited only at the top level.

level. These report structures can then be used within that entity, along with any report 

structures that were inherited from the top level.

revenue per customer.

### Dimension Counts Workflow
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 356*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dimension Counts Workflow 

Setting up dimension count is a multi-step process and requires admin privileges. 

1. 
Create specific statistical accounts to track updates. 

2. 
Configure dimension groups for the counts you want to track. 

3. 
Enable dimension counts and create dimension count rules to provide granularity. 

Step 1. Create a statistical account 

Each dimension count must be posted to a separate statistical account. 

For example, you might create a statistical account for customers located in New York. Based on 

the rule you define for the dimension group; the count of New York customers is tracked 

automatically. When a new customer from New York is added, the statistical account is increased 

by 1. When a New York customer is made inactive (meaning they are no longer a customer), the 

statistical account is decreased by 1. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level statistical accounts are available. You can ’t select 
statistical accounts that are private to subsidiary entities.

See Statistical accounts in online help or download the RealPage Accounting General Ledger User 

Guide. 

Step 2. Configure dimension groups 

A “dimension group” is a name for a particular set of members in a dimension, or a set of 

members that meet certain criteria. For example, you might create customer groups for a 

particular set of customers, customers located in a particular state, or customers with the greatest 

open balance. A dimension group lets you define the rule for updating dimension count. 

For each count to automate, create an appropriate dimension group. There’s a separate 

dimension group list for each type of dimension, and access is controlled by your permissions. 

Some dimension groups, such as customers and vendors, can be accessed from multiple menus. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level dimension groups are available. You can’t select 
dimension groups that are private to subsidiary entities. 

For example, if you want to be able to show only how many of your customers are in New York, 

create a customer group that includes only customers whose main address is in New York. 

If you spell out the state name in the Customer record, set the value to New York. You could also 

add a second filter to include the customer if the value for the State/province equals NY. In this 

case, you would set the filter conditions to Any (OR). Any customer whose record showed the 

state as NY or New York would be included in the group. 

To learn how to create dimension groups, refer to Dimension groups (on page 301). 

---


<!-- Page 357 -->
Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Step 3. Create dimension count rules 

Dimension count rules are the foundation of automating statistical account counts. It is these 

rules that allow the finer granularity necessary for insight and analysis. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Create at least one dimension count rule. Each row in General Ledger Setup > Dimension count is`


a separate rule that creates a statistical journal entry when the rule values are met. 

There is no functional limit to the number of dimension count rules you can create, so you can 

automate the process for everything that matches the corporate requirements. 

To learn about creating rules, refer to Dimension count rules (on page 351) and Creating 

Dimension Count Rules (on page 352). 

Step 4. Select the statistical journal 

Select or create the statistical journal into which transactions are posted when a dimension count 

rule is matched. This can be a new statistical journal or an existing one. One statistical journal is 

used for all dimension count transactions. This journal helps you organize dimension counts for 

your audit log, to understand how the counts are updated. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level statistical journals are available. You can ’t select 
statistical journals that are private to subsidiary entities.

Establish a Base Count 

When you enable dimension count, only new updates are included in statistical account updates. 

The existing dimension objects are not included, even if they match the dimension count criteria. 

Enter a manual journal entry to the statistical account to establish a beginning balance as a 

starting point. 

To learn how to enter a manual journal entry, refer to Statistical journal entries. 

Best practice: If you’ve already set up a dimension count rule, don’t disable the dimension. 

Disabling the dimension can cause unexpected behavior. 

---



### Automated Dimension Count Posting
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 358*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Automated Dimension Count Posting 

Statistical accounts are often used to track the number of dimension members. For example, it’s 

common to track the number of active customers. This information can be reported on by itself or 

used to compute metrics such as the recurring revenue per customer. 

You can: 

• 
Automate counts for any enabled dimension. As you add or remove dimension members, 

the count is automatically updated. 

• 
Set up rules that define what you want to count. For example, in addition to tracking the 

number of active customers, you might set up a separate statistical account for tracking 

different customer types. 

About Dimension Counts 

There are many reasons for automating the dimension count to a statistical account. It saves time 

and effort—especially when you are tracking many dimensions and can increase insight into your 

business. 

Manual vs. Automated Posting 

Your company might already use multiple spreadsheets to track changes for various things like 

new, lost, and long-time customers. With the dimension count posting feature, the system 

updates dimension counts automatically, reducing the need for manual spreadsheets that are 

time-consuming and sometimes error prone. 

You can still post changes manually—for example, when establishing a base count—but 

automating the count eliminates data-entry work by reducing the steps needed to update the 

count accurately and immediately. 

Use in Metrics 

Finely tuned metrics increase insight into your business and provide greater detail when you are 

making business decisions. By providing a way to automate counts, dimension count gives you 

flexibility to ensure that your metrics are appropriate and accurate. 

To increase the granularity of business metrics, analysis, or reporting, different posting rules 

update different statistic counts. You can use the values in computational reports and 

performance cards to increase insight into how your company is doing. 

Dimension counts use a separate dimension group for each dimension rule you create. There is 

no limit to the number of things that can be tracked automatically. 

---


<!-- Page 359 -->
Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Setup Overview 

A dimension must be enabled for dimension counts to work. For example, to use the 
Locations 
dimension count, the Location dimension must be active. If you don’t see a particular dimension 
count, verify that the dimension is enabled in Dimension settings. 

The dimension count setup process requires admin privileges and requires setting up a statistical 

account for each dimension count and then defining the rules for posting. Creating a dimension 

count rule is a one-time process. After that, dimension count changes are automatic and don’t 

need any further action. 

For example, you might create a rule to update the count of active customers based in Vermont 

who have a high credit limit. Any time a customer moves into that group, the dimension count 

rule creates a statistical journal entry to increase the count. If a customer moves out of the group, 

then the same dimension count rule creates an entry to decrease the count. 

Best practice: If you’ve already set up a dimension count rule, then don’t disable the dimension. 
Disabling the dimension can cause unexpected behavior. 

For step-by-step setup instructions, refer to Set up dimension count (on page 350). 

Functionality of Automated Posting 

1. 
Create statistical accounts and dimension groups for dimension count to use. 

2. 
Establish the initial base value of the count, such as the customer count as of the date you 

begin automated posting. 

3. 
As you create the dimension count rules, the system automatically monitors increases and 

decreases and posts journal entries to the statistical journal. 

Establishing a Base Count 

When you enable dimension count, only new updates are included in statistical account updates. 

The existing dimension objects are not included, even if they match the dimension count criteria. 

Enter a manual journal entry to the statistical account to establish a beginning balance as a 

starting point. This step is optional, but if you don’t establish a base count, then the count starts 

at zero and only new changes are recorded. There is no historical starting point. 

In many cases, the company could be maintaining a spreadsheet with the information you want to 

track. After a base count is included in the statistical account, you might be able to get rid of 

these spreadsheets and let the system track and count for you. 

---


<!-- Page 360 -->
Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Functionality of Dimension Count Updates 

After a dimension count is set up, the system automatically posts entries when you create and 

save a new object or delete an object that matches the rule. You can’t create an automated post 

for a previous period. 

For example, if you created a customer record on 12/2/2019, then the customer count is 

increased for the date of 12/2/2019, the date that the record was created. Because the count 

update is automated, the transaction date is not configurable in the dimension count rules. 

Adding Counts to the Previous Period 

Continuing the example, suppose that this customer signed the deal on 11/26/2019. In this case, 

you want the customer count to be posted and counted for the month of November, even 

though the customer record wasn’t created until December, but the system would post the record 

for December. You can’t edit any of the system-posted record counts. This preserves the business 

rule audit trail. However, you can manually adjust the count to November by both increasing the 

count with 11/26/2019 and decreasing the count with 12/2/2019 accordingly. 

As you create new dimension count rules, newly created objects that match the rules are posted 

to the journal and added to the statistical account. Existing objects that match the dimension 

count rules are not added, only new objects are. Deleting a rule doesn’t remove the object from 

the statistical account count, but new count changes aren’t updated automatically. 

Editing a Dimension Record That Is Used by Dimension Count 

When you make a change to a record that is used by dimension count, the appropriate journal 

entry is updated at that time. Record changes are made the same way you change any other 

record for that dimension. 

For example, suppose you have a vendor who is included in the dimension group for California 

vendors and is part of a dimension count rule. If this vendor moved to another state, you would 

change the vendor record to reflect the new address. When you change the record, the 

appropriate changes are made by dimension count: the count of California vendors is decreased 

by one. If there is a dimension group/rule for the new state, then that count is increased by one. 

There is one exception to this: employee records and location. 

Special Case: Changing an Employee Location in a Multi-Entity Company 

For multi-entity companies, the employee record requires a location. This tells the system which 

entity the employee belongs with. If you change the location of an employee from one entity to 

another, then the record is changed correctly. But because the dimension count gets the location 

from the employee record, dimension count handles the change a bit differently, and that affects 

how the count is changed. 

---


<!-- Page 361 -->
Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Best practice: To ensure that the count is correct for both the original and the new location, many 

companies find that the following steps are helpful. 

1. 
Make the employee inactive to remove the count from original location. 

2. 
While the employee is still inactive, change the employee location. 

3. 
Set the employee record back to active. 

Alternatively, you can make statistical journal entries manually to reduce the original employee by 

location count by one and add the employee by location count by one. 

The following examples show some of the possible uses of dimension count. 

Customer Retention Rate 

Automate the count of new customers you acquired for a period, how many existing customers 

stayed, and how many customers left. Count by total customers or filter further, such as by 

location or salesperson. 

Suppose you started out with 365 customers for a period. Over the period you added ten new 

customers but lost three. Rather than just reporting that you now have 372 customers, dimension 

count automates the count, making it available for reports. 

Customer Count by Customer Type 

Using dimension count makes it easy to automatically track by customers of a certain type or 

industry—anything from direct and retail sales, by ZIP Code range, state, or country. Knowing how 

many customers of different types can help your company make business decisions. 

Employee Retention 

One of the most important assets a company has is its employees. You need to know not just how 

many employees the company has at a certain period, but how many are new, how many have 

left, and even how long the average employee stays with the company. You can break it down 

even further and see which locations or departments have higher or lower attrition rates at a 

glance. Dimension count can automate that information for inclusion in reports. 

---

Setting Up a Dimension Count

Automate Dimension Count Changes 

Dimension count rules automatically post a journal transaction and update the count to a 

statistical journal based on the dimension groups you specify, any time you create a dimension 

member record, such as customer or item, which matches the rule. 

To make sure that counts are always current, dimension count posts a transaction based on the 

system date when the dimension member record is saved or deleted. 

A dimension must be enabled for dimension counts to work. For example, to use the Locations 
dimension count, the Location dimension must be active. If you don’t see a particular dimension 
count, verify that the dimension is enabled in the Dimension settings section of General ledger 
configuration.

> **Navigation Path:** `Setup > Configuration.`


You can configure dimensions to automatically post statistical journal entries whenever their 

counts change, based on the criteria you select. 

You can configure dimensions so that the system automatically updates count changes to a 

statistical account using dimension groups and dimension count rules. You can post and track 

dimension count changes automatically, providing more granular metrics to measure your 

business. Better metrics information means better insight.

Dimension Count Rules 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Advanced GL Section > Dimension Count List`


Dimension count rules enable automation of object count updates to statistical accounts. This 

gives you a simple way to track exactly the specifics that you want. For example, automate counts 

for only direct customers, only departments with offices in London, or vendors active in the 

Northeast. These types of counts are often used for averaging and analysis. 

Configuration 

You configure the dimensions you want the system to track and define the statistical journal 

where the system is to track the dimension counts. 

• 
Define the “rules” that control the count of what you’re tracking. (You select the dimensions 

that you want the system to count and the account that the rules apply to.) 

• 
Select the statistical account to use for each dimension count rule. 

Results 

Based on your configuration of the dimension count rules, the system creates statistical journal 

entries and automatically updates dimension counts to a statistical account. As your dimension 

count changes, the increase or decrease is automatically posted to the statistical account.

Creating Dimension Count Rules 

To create dimension count rules: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select General Ledger, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

The system opens the General ledger setup page. 

3. 
Under the Advanced G/L options section, go to the Dimension count list. 

4. 
Under the Dimensions column, click the drop-down list for a line item, and then select a 

dimension. The system displays all available standard and user-defined dimensions in the 

drop-down list. 

For multi-entity companies: In multi-entity companies, you can set a dimension group filter 
to create the dimensions at either the top or entity level so you can further filter the 
dimension records to find all the dimensions, based on where they were created. 

5. 
Under the Account column, select or create the statistical account to associate with this 

dimension count rule. Only the top-level statistical accounts are available. 

The statistical account you select is the account into which any matching dimension count 

rules are updated. For example, if you select a statistical account for customers in California, 

that statistical account is updated any time a customer that matches the rule is added or 

removed. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level statistical accounts are available. You can ’t 
select statistical accounts that are private to subsidiary entities.

6. 
Under the Active dimension group column, select the dimension group to match the 

dimension object. 

A “dimension group” is a name for a particular set of members in a dimension, or a set of 

members that meet certain criteria. For example, you might create customer groups for a 

particular set of customers, customers located in a particular state, or even customers with 

the greatest open balance. 

When creating a dimension group for dimension count, you can use a broad set of criteria 

for the group or use filtering to ensure that your update counts match specific needs, such 

as items groups whose average cost is higher or lower than a certain amount. 

If you don’t see a particular dimension group in a menu, ask your administrator to give you 
permission to the dimension group. There are separate permissions for each application 
from which you can access the dimension group list. 

For multi-entity companies: Only top-level dimension groups are available. You can’t select 
dimension groups that are private to subsidiary entities.

#### Viewing Count Changes
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 365*

7.

posted to the statistical journal used to contain dimension count posting. 

8. 
Under the Posting location column, select or create a location to associate with the 

dimension count rule. 

For multi-entity companies: Select a posting entity. Posting entities are required for 
multi-entity companies, because the dimensions are set up at the top level in multi-entity 
companies. Essentially, you need to assign one entity (location) for each transaction rule. 
This ensures that a member of the entity can be responsible for the transaction. 

9. 
Repeat this process for each object to be included in a dimension count. 

You can create multiple dimension count rules. However, the total of all dimension count

description.

11. 
Click the Save button. 

Viewing Count Changes

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select General Ledger, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Click Statistical Accounts. 

The system displays a list of your statistical accounts. 

3. 
Locate the statistical account that you want to view, and then click the corresponding link 

under the Account number column. 

The system displays a General Ledger report where you can see the count of increases and 

decreases change as you add or delete objects matching the dimension count rule. 

4. 
Click the Customize button to refine the report. 

• 
Select the date range and any other item for the report that you want to change or 

include. 

• 
Click the View button. 

The system displays report to show the changes. 

5. 
Save, print, or take any other available action for your report.

### Dimension FAQs
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 367*

Chapter 11: Working with Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Dimension FAQs 

How do I create a group for all members of a dimension? 

You can easily create a dimension group that includes all active members of a dimension. 

When creating the dimension group, select the following options: 

1. 
Select All members as the group type. 

2. 
Change the sort order as needed. 

3. 
In the Filters list, filter for all Active members. 

• 
For the Field, select Status. 

• 
For the Operator, select equals. 

• 
For the Value, select Active. 

What do the filter operators mean? 

Depending on the type of field you select, matching can work differently. 

• 
For numerical fields, equals, greater than, and less than are often used to filter based on 

whether the amount is equal to, above, or below the number you enter. 

• 
In general, non-number fields ask you to select a specific record from a list (for example, a 

specific department name or manager). For these types of fields, equals, not equal to, is 

empty, and is not empty are the most useful operators. 

• 
If you want to match records that contain a certain word (for example, project names that 

contain the word design), use the contains operator. Instead of choosing a record from a list, 

enter the word in the Value field. 

What date is used when filter for amounts? 

Some fields, such as amount due and item price, contain data that can change over time. For the 

purposes of filtering reports, amount-based filters are always applied using the most current data, 

even if the as of date for the report is in the past. 

For example, suppose that you create a revenue report that filters for items with the highest price. 

When you run the report, the filter will be applied based on the current price of the items, even if 

the report is being run for a prior reporting period. 

Are filters applied to all members of the dimension, or just the members in the 
Members list? 

The filters operate differently depending on whether you select any specific members in the 

Members list. 

• 
If you use the Members list to select specific dimension members, such as particular 

departments or customers, the filters will be applied only to those specific members. 

---



#### Pages With Limited Dimensions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 368*

Working with Dimensions 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
To apply filters to all members of a dimension (for example, selecting all your locations 

where the Status equals Active) do not select any specific members in the Members list. 

Example: Suppose that you have a location group that has three members—California, New York, 

and Oregon (an inactive location)—and you then add a filter for locations where the Status equals 

Active. In this case, when you use the location group to filter reports, the report will include data 

only for California and New York and will not include the inactive location. 

How are hierarchical dimensions handled? 

Dimensions are often hierarchical. For example, a department can have one or more child 

departments, up to several levels deep. 

When a report filter includes a member of a dimension, data from any members that belong to it 

will also be included. This means that a department group that matches the Engineering 

department will automatically include data from any sub departments (like Development, Quality 

Assurance, and Documentation.) 

When filtering financial reports by department or location, you can decide to exclude sub 
departments or sub locations by deselecting the Include Subs option under the filter field. 

How do I include inactive dimensions in reports? 

Create a dimension group that is filtered to include both inactive and active members. Then use 

that dimension group to filter financial reports. 

See the help for the specific dimension. For example, for department, see the details on making a 

dimension inactive. 

Pages With Limited Dimensions 

In some situations, dimension use is limited to specific dimensions, as listed below. 

Accounts Receivable 

• 
Quick Invoice Entry page: Department, Location 

Accounts Payable 

Apply Payments (Overpayments): Department, Location 

Bill Backs: Department, Location 

• 
Quick Check Entry: Department, Location 

• 
Quick A/P Invoice Entry: Department, Location

What Happens After Implementing Dimensions 

After you implement the standard dimensions, you want to use, and create any unique 

dimensions you might need, the system propagates your dimensions everywhere that you want to 

access them: 

• 
Transactions: On the transaction entry pages, you can select the dimensions that you want 

to propagate to the general ledger. By selecting dimensions in various transactions such as 

A/P or A/R invoices, you organize and prepare your operational and financial information to 

be sliced and diced any way that you need to gain insight into your business. 

• 
Reports: Dimensions are a core component of reporting to help you meet the needs of your 

changing business and instantly track performance by different business drivers as your 

strategies and operations change. Using dimensions in reporting, you can create almost 

limitless ways of viewing your information and capturing key metrics. 

What Happens After Inactivating a Dimension Value 

When you inactivate a dimension value, it no longer appears in your drop-down lists. This helps 

prevent the creation of new transactions using that dimension value. However, your dimension 

value still exists within the company, so inactivating a dimension value will not affect your 

financial reporting because the dimension value still rolls up to the top-level of the dimension 

hierarchy at the time the report is run. 

For instance, your California location dimension has a Northern California and Southern California 

child dimension associated with it. Your Southern California location closes in June, so you 

inactivate the dimension value. Users can no longer create transactions against that dimension 

value. However, at the end of the year, you still need to see how you did at that location while it 

was open. You can’t run a report on Southern California because it is inactivated, but you can run 

a report on California for the year. The system automatically rolls up all transactions including the 

Southern California location and displays in your California report.

in balance.

if: 

•

•

debits and credits, requiring a correcting entry (typically, a debit or credit of a penny) 

to the rounding account.

Click the Save button.

Configuring Your Company as a Multi-Entity Organization 

To configure the use of multiple entities: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Subscriptions. 

3. 
Find Multi-entity console, and then click the switch to enable the package. 

4. 
Click the Configure link. 

Configuring Multiple Base Currencies 

1. 
In the Entity preferences section, select the Enable multiple base currencies check box to 

allow each entity to select their own base currency. 

For example, you might select this option if you have an entity that operates in US dollars 

(USD) and another that operates in Euros (EUR). If all of your entities use the same base 

currency, leave this check box cleared. 

When you enable multiple base currencies: 

• 
You can’t enable the top level as an operating entity. 

• 
G/L accounts are shared across entities. 

Multiple base currencies aren’t required for transacting in multiple currencies. For 
instance, if all entities have US dollars as their base currency, they can still transact in 
other currencies (such as paying an A/P invoice in Yen), by enabling multi-currency 
management in General Ledger. 

The Value Approval Currency Setup section appears when Multiple base currencies is 

enabled. 

2. 
In Value approval currency setup, if you enabled multiple base currencies, you can set a 

value approval currency for purchase transactions and expense reports. The system 

translates the transaction currency into the value approval currency to evaluate the approval 

thresholds and determine who needs to provide approval. 

To set a value approval currency, select a currency from the drop-down menu. Only 

currencies enabled in your system are available for selection.

Creating a New Entity for Your Corporate Office 

The Enable top level as a transaction operating entity feature was removed and can’t be enabled. 
Instead of making the top level an operating entity, create a new entity for your corporate office. 

• 
In Top-level entity setup, if you do enable the top level as a transaction operating entity 

(not recommended), you must fill in additional information about the top level. 

• 
ID: The ID defaults to the name of your current company. You can change the ID as 

needed. 

• 
Federal ID: If you are printing 1099s on an entity-by-entity basis, the system uses this 

ID for the top-level entity 1099 form. 

• 
Receivables account: This is the G/L account used for tracking inter-entity receivables 

due to the top level. 

• 
Payables account: This is the G/L account used for inter-entity payables owed by the 

top level. 

Filling In the 1099 Section 

• 
Select the Issue a separate 1099 per entity check box to print 1099s with entity-level 

information, rather than top-level company information. This means that: 

• 
1099s will print the legal name, address, and tax ID of the entity, even if the top-level 

company prints them. 

• 
If two entities pay the same vendor, the payments from each appear on separate 1099 

forms. 

Clear this check box if you want the top-level company to print a single set of 1099s across 

all entities and all vendors. In this case the forms print with the company legal name, 

address, and tax ID of the top-level entity, even if a subordinate entity made the payment.

Filling In the Entity Restrictions Section 

By default, bank accounts created at the top level are shared by all entities. However, you can 

restrict access by location, location group, departments, and department groups. For example, 

you might want to restrict a bank account (checking or savings) to a certain department and 

location so that other locations and departments can’t use the account to prevent them from 

paying A/P invoices out of the wrong account. 

When setting up location groups or department groups, keep in mind that restrictions can be 

based on groups that contain specific locations or departments, but can’t be based on groups 

that filter dynamically based on the value of certain fields (such as locations where the status is 

set to Active). Location groups and department groups that contain dynamic filtering won’t 

appear on the Restrictions tab for you to select. 

When you enable Entity restrictions for Customers and Vendors, a new menu item appears in the 

Setup section called Customer Visibility or Vendor (Supplier) Visibility. For bank accounts, a new 

Restrictions tab becomes available. 

1. 
Select the Customers check box to prevent some entities from being able to see and access 

selected customers. Clear the check box to allow all entities to access all customers. If you 

select this option, you can use the Customer Visibility page to specify which locations and 

departments can transact with a customer. 

Customer records must be created at the top level. 

2. 
Select the Vendors check box to restrict access to vendors. Clear the check box to allow all 

entities to access all vendors. 

Vendors must be created at the top level. 

Do not use field-level controls to add vendor records if your company uses the vendor 
approval feature. 

3. 
Select the Bank accounts check box to restrict a bank account to a specific location or 

department. If you select this option, you can use the Restrictions tab on the Bank account 

information page to specify which locations and departments have access to the account. 

• 
You can restrict bank accounts that are checking or savings accounts. 

• 
If the bank account was created at the entity level, then it is already restricted to the 

entity, and no Restrictions tab appears on the bank account record.

Filling In the Inter-Entity Transactions Section 

When you have a multi-entity company, you often have transactions that affect multiple entities, 

which means that you need to account for the inter-entity “due to” and “due from.” For example, 

one entity might pay an A/P invoice on behalf of another entity. 

You use this section of the Configure Multi-Entity page to control how the system records 

transactions that involve two or more entities: 

• 
For non-journal entries: If you enter a subledger transaction (such as an A/P invoice, A/R 

invoice, or advance), offsetting journal entries are automatically recorded for the inter-entity 

payables and receivables in the affected entities. 

If you don’t want to automatically record these entries for you, you can choose manual 

balancing only. See the manual balancing only options below for more information. 

• 
For journal entries: If you create a journal entry that involves two or more entities, the 

system doesn’t automatically create any additional line items for the inter-entity payables 

and receivables. If you want the system to automatically create the offsetting entries in the 

affected entities, you must select the option to Enable auto-balancing for GL/Journal 

Entries. 

Filling In the Manual Balancing Only Section 

1. 
Select the Credits check box to turn off the automatic recording of inter-entity payables and 

receivables, but only for credits, adjustments, and prepayments. Although you can still 

continue to create credits, prepayments, and adjustments that involve multiple entities, 

you’ll be required to track who owes money to whom separately. 

Your company won’t automatically track the inter-entity payables and receivables by 

creating offsetting journal entries in the affected entities.  

2. 
Select the All subledger transactions check box if you do not want the system to track 

inter-entity payables and receivables for any transaction. For example, although one entity 

can still pay an A/P invoice on behalf of another entity, the system won’t track the 

inter-entity payables and receivables by creating offsetting journal entries in the affected 

entities. 

Selecting this option also disables the ability to auto-balance G/L journal entries. 

By default, when you enter a manual journal entry that involves two or more entities, the 

additional offsetting transactions are not automatically added into the journals of each 

affected entity. This means that you must enter all balancing line items manually. 

3. 
Select the Enable auto-balancing for G/L Journal Entries check box to have the system 

record the inter-entity payables and receivables for you automatically. 

With this option, auto-balancing occurs only by entity. To auto-balance journal entries for 

other dimensions, you must do it manually. 

---


<!-- Page 382 -->
Configuring Currency 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

This option becomes unavailable if you enabled auto-balancing in the General Ledger 
configuration, which auto-balances journal entries across all selected dimensions. 

4. 
In the Enforce journal entry balancing by section, select Location or Entity. 

This option applies only if you don’t enable auto-balancing for GL/Journal entries. In this 

case, you can choose whether line items manually entered by users must balance by 

location or entity. 

If you enable auto-balancing for journal entries, it occurs at the entity level. If you don’t 

select auto-balancing, then you can choose to enforce the balancing at the location or 

entity level. 

Best practice: Unless you have a clear business requirement to balance by location, a best 

practice is to balance by entity. Balancing by entity includes all journal entries for the entity 

and includes line items for all locations in the entity but balancing by location includes only 

line items specific to the location and can cause some line items not to be included. 

5. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal you want to use when you post inter-entity 

credit invoices to A/P or A/R. 

IET journal entries are combined with source transactions to simplify the reviewing of all 

transactions and ease reconciliations. 

6. 
Select the Limit A/P credits to the entity owners check box to apply credits to A/P invoices 

of the owning entity only. 

In a multi-entity company, the system applies the credit to the owning entity first and then 

applies credit from the oldest to the newest bills. If you enable your company to limit credits 

to only the owning entity, then credits are applied to the bills of the owning entity and no 

others; any remaining credit is reserved for more bills owned by that entity. 

7. 
Select the Limit A/R credits to the entity owners check box to apply credits to the owning 

entity first. Next, the system applies credit from the oldest to the newest invoices. If you 

enable your company to limit credits to only the owning entity, then credits are applied to 

the invoices of the owning entity and no others; any remaining credit is reserved for more 

invoices owned by that entity.

With this option, auto-balancing occurs only by entity. To auto-balance 

journal entries for other dimensions, you must do it manually. 

Enforce journal entry 

balancing by  

This option applies only if you don’t enable auto-balancing for 

GL/Journal entries. In this case, you can choose whether line items 

manually entered by users must balance by location or entity. 

If you enable auto-balancing for journal entries, it occurs at the entity 

level. If you don’t select auto-balancing, then you can choose to enforce 

the balancing at the location or entity level. 

Best practice: Unless you have a clear business requirement to balance 

by location, a best practice is to balance by entity. Balancing by entity 

includes all journal entries for the entity and includes line items for all 

locations in the entity but balancing by location includes only line items 

specific to the location and can cause some line items not to be 

included. 

Journal 
In the Journal drop-down list, select a single journal to use when 

posting inter-entity credit bills or invoices to AP or AR, respectively.

<!-- Page 385 -->
Chapter 12: Configuring Currency 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

Limit A/P credits to 

the entity owners 

Select to apply credits to A/P invoices of the owning entity only. 

In a multi-entity company, the system applies the credit to the owning 

entity first and then applies credit from the oldest to the newest A/P 

invoices. If you enable your company to limit credits to only the owning 

entity, then credits are applied to the A/P invoices of the owning entity 

and no others; any remaining credit is reserved for more A/P invoices 

owned by that entity. 

Limit A/R credits to 

the entity owners 

In a multi-entity company, the system applies credit to the owning entity 

first, and then applies credit from the oldest to the newest invoices. If 

you enable your company to limit credits to only the owning entity, then 

credits are applied to the invoices of the owning entity and no others; 

any remaining credit is reserved for more invoices owned by that entity. 

Inter-Entity Account Mapping Section 

Inter-entity account 

mapping plan 

Select the inter-entity account mapping plan you want to use: Basic or 

Advanced. 

Basic 
With the Basic inter-entity account mapping plan, when mapping 

entities to accounts for posting inter-entity transactions (IETs), the plan 

defines a common receivable account and payable account that will be 

used for all transactions involving that entity. Because it’s unnecessary to 

separately settle balances among entities involved, one inter-entity 

receivable (IER) and one inter-entity payable (IEP) account is defined per 

entity. A single set of inter-entity receivable and payable accounts can 

be shared across multiple entities or settled directly through cash or 

investments as needed. 

Advanced 
With the Advanced mapping plan, relationships are mapped between 

pairs of entities. This allows for greater granularity in tracking who owes 

whom, so you can settle between each entity pairing individually, if 

necessary. Any combination of IER and IEP accounts can be used, based 

on the accounts you defined in your previous IET account setup. This 

plan enables mapping each entity to a combination of directional 

accounts tracking IER and IEP, using separate or common IER and IEP 

accounts.

Base Currency

Enabling multi-currency management (on page 160). 

Several of the core accounting settings on the Company information record’s Accounting tab 

were set during your initial company setup and cannot be changed. Base currency is one of these. 

You can only change the base currency before transactions are created in your company. 

Changing the base currency can have major impacts on your financials. 

Instead, you can add transaction currencies. Learn about Adding a transaction currency (on page

For companies that use multiple base currencies, you assign a base currency to an entity when 

you create the entity. Any properties and locations that are associated with the entity use its base 

currency. When you have locations that require a different base currency, create a new entity for 

those locations. 

Entities created prior to activating the Multiple base currencies setting will retain the system 
default base currency.

### Exchange Rates and Exchange Rate Types
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 398*

Exchange Rates 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Exchange Rates and Exchange Rate Types 

You can use a separate exchange rate type for each currency exchange, and you can use one type 

of exchange rate for some transactions but not others. 

Exchange Rates 

An exchange rate enables you to specify: 

• 
The currency you’re converting from 

• 
The currency you’re converting to (usually your organization’s base currency) 

• 
The conversion rate 

• 
The date when the conversion rate takes effect 

Exchange Rate Types 

An exchange rate type enables you to create a group to contain one or more custom-defined 

exchange rates under one name. 

For example, if your company transacts in both Euros and Yen and you want to convert from 

those currencies to your base currency, which is USD, you could have one exchange rate type that 

includes both these currencies. You can then select the exchange rate type whenever you create a 

transaction that includes either Euros or Yen. 

Custom Exchange Rate Types 

A custom exchange rate type enables your organization to process foreign currency transactions, 

such as foreign currency A/R invoices and A/P invoices, using exchange rates specific to your 

business requirements. You can use a custom exchange rate type for global consolidation, or to 

override the standard daily rate type. 

You can get the latest exchange rates from any number of sources, such as the Wall Street 

Journal, American Express, newspapers, or other financial services Websites. This helps you select 

a rate that is most appropriate for your business. 

Example 

Your base currency is US dollars, but your organization also conducts business in Euros and Yen. 

You might use two different exchange rates:  

• 
A monthly type for smaller transactions. A monthly type fluctuates less but is less accurate. 

• 
A daily type for larger transactions. A daily type fluctuates more but is more accurate. 

When you go to the Accounts Payable invoice page to associate an exchange rate type with an 

A/P invoice, you can select either the monthly exchange rate type or the daily exchange rate type. 

Either rate type will apply to both Euros and Yen. 

---


<!-- Page 399 -->
Chapter 14: Exchange Rates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

How to Select an Exchange Rate Type 

Generally speaking, use the RealPage Daily Rate when: 

• 
You exchange currencies or perform revaluation frequently and need the most up-to-date 

rate type. 

• 
You do not want to maintain or manage the exchange rate type you use. 

Use your own custom-defined exchange rate type if you want an exchange rate type that 

fluctuates less frequently and requires less revaluation on your part, such as when: 

• 
You only report weekly or monthly. 

• 
You enter all your A/P invoices at the end of the month. 

---



### RealPage Daily Rate
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 400*

Exchange Rates 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

RealPage Daily Rate 

RealPage gets the daily exchange rate once a day from Oanda.com, an exchange rate provider. 

Oanda uses an algorithm to calculate the daily exchange rate for that day and provides it to 

RealPage for transactions using the RealPage Daily Rate. The rate that RealPage takes is based on 

the average ask rate. Because the algorithm uses rates from the entire day, the RealPage Daily 

Rate uses the rate from the previous day. 

After Oanda updates their daily rates at 22:00 ET, it takes about an hour for the daily rate to be 

updated across the system. 

Configuration 

By default, the RealPage Daily Rate is ready to use and is calculated and maintained automatically. 

When to Use the RealPage Daily Rate 

Use the RealPage Daily Rate when you exchange currencies or perform revaluation frequently and 

need the most up-to-date rate type. 

Overriding the RealPage Daily Rate Type 

Set an exchange rate type as the system-wide default when you use multiple exchange rate types, 

but you use a particular one most frequently.  

You can override the default exchange rate type as needed.

#### How to Read Paths
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide.pdf`, Page 407*

Chapter 15: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 

How to Read Paths 

If you have ever been puzzled over a path in the documentation, this topic describes what it all 

means. 

Application Menus and Tabs 

Most paths begin with the Applications menu. This menu is located in the upper-left corner next 

to the Home button. When you select an application, the name of the Applications menu 

changes to the application that you selected. 

Menus have two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab is available to all users, but the Setup tab is 

restricted to users with full or limited administrator privileges. 

The Company application has two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab contains setup options for 
global features and is available to all users with the appropriate permissions. The Setup tab is 
restricted to administrators only. 

Simple Paths 

This is an example of a simple path: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry`


The first three parts in a path are standard; they translate to “Click the Applications menu (a), 

select the name of the application (b), and then select the menu tab (c).” 

---


<!-- Page 408 -->
Help and Support 

RealPage Financial Suite Getting Started User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The next steps in the path—the menu section (d) and the menu option (e)—direct you to a 

specific list or page in the application. 

a) Click the Applications menu.  

b) Select the application. 

c) Select the menu tab. 

d) Find the menu section or subsection, if any. 

e) Click the menu option.  

If you see the 
 icon in a path, then you can click the  icon in front of the menu option to add 
a new blank record. 

Paths with Multiple Options 

Some paths offer multiple choices. The choices are separated with a “/” symbol.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable > Setup > Taxes > Authorities > 
View/Edit`


In this example, Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable means that the same option is available 

in two applications’ menus, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. Likewise, View/Edit 

means that you can select either the View or the Edit link to get to the page that you need.

Use the following tools and strategies that can help you be
more efficient in using the RealPage Financial Suite.

Changing Your Password

For increased security, your company might require you to
change your password periodically.

1. Click your sign-in name at the top of any page, and then select
My preferences.
2. In the Security preferences section, click Change password.
3. Enter your current password.
4. Enter a new password. It must be at least eight characters and
follow password quality requirements.
5. Re-enter your new password to confirm.
6. Click Save.

Creating an Email Signature

Add an email signature for the system to automatically
generate in your outgoing email.

1. Click your sign-in name at the top of any page, and then select
My preferences.
2. In the Email notifications section, enter your name, title, and
contact information in the My email signature field.
3. Click Save.

Setting Up Personal Timeout Preferences

Set timeouts for when the system should automatically sign you
out.

1. Click your sign-in name at the top of any page, and then select
My preferences.
2. In the Security preferences section, under Inactivity duration
signout, select the number of hours and minutes your system
can remain inactive before it signs you out.
3. In the Session duration signout drop-down list, select the
maximum number of hours and minutes that you can work in the
system, regardless of whether it is active or not, before it signs
you out.
4. Click Save.

Uploading a Digital Check Signature

Add a digital signature that appears on both online and printed
checks.

1. Click your sign-in name at the top of any page, and then select
My preferences.
2. In the Check preferences section, click Upload signature.

3. Click Choose files, and then select your signature file in GIF
format.
4. Click Open.

Color Code Levels

Set a color for each entity that appears in a band across the top
of your console.

1. Click the Level drop-down list at the top of the page.
2. Click the dot for the entity that you want to color code.
3. Select the desired color.

Using Bookmarks

Create bookmarks to let you quickly access frequently used
tasks and views.

1. Go to a page that you want to bookmark.

2. Click 
 Bookmark, and then select Bookmark this page.
3. Type a name for the bookmark.
4. Click Save.

Filtering Lists

Set filter criteria using the boxes on top of each column to
customize your lists.

1. Select the Include private check box to show all items to
include records created at the entity level.
2. If applicable, select the Include inactive check box to display
inactive items.
3. If applicable, select the Display hierarchy check box to show
relationships for parent-child records.
4. In the filter field of a column, enter the value by which you want
to filter the list.

▪
Enter the first few characters of the value.
▪
Add % if you only know a part of the text that you want to
filter by. For example, %palm%.

The % symbol only works for text columns. It does not apply
to date or amount columns.

5. Press ENTER.

Using Advanced Filters

Apply standard operators to a list's columns to display specific
items.

1. On a list page, click Advanced filters.
2. Select a field by which you want to filter.
3. Select an operator.

4. Enter the value.

To filter check boxes, select the Equals operator, and then enter
True for selected check boxes or False for unselected boxes.

5. Add more filters as needed.
6. Click Apply.

Creating Custom Views

Create a new view to display list items according to your
preferences.

1. On a list page, click the Manage views menu, and then select
Create New View.
2. Select the columns to include in the view.
3. In the Step drop-down list, click Select column sequence.
4. Drag the columns to arrange them in the desired order.
5. Edit the text to change the text at the top of a view's column.
6. In the Step drop-down list, click Select Filters.
7. Set up the filter conditions.
8. In the Step drop-down list, click Sort Results.
9. Drag the rows to set the order in which the system sorts the
view results.
10. Set included columns to ascending or descending order.
11. In the Step drop-down list, click Save Advanced Options.
12. Enter a Name and Description.
13. Select Deploy to make the view available to others.
14. Click Save.

Adjusting the Table Size

Change the number of rows that you want the system to
display on the page.

The Table size command only affects a table on the page and does
not affect list pages.

1. On the page with the table that you want to change, click the
More actions drop-down menu.
2. Click Table size, and then select the number of rows that you
want to display.

Adding a Menu Item to Favorites

Access your most frequently used menu items by adding them
to your Favorites list.

1. Click the Application drop-down menu.
2. Pause on the menu item that you want to add to your favorites.
3. Click the star next to the menu item.
