Using the Selection Box

Select items to include in an action when performing a task.

1. Click Select or Edit to open the selection box.

2. In the left pane, click 
 Add next to the items that you want to
include in the Selected items pane.
3. Click Add all to add all items from the Available items pane to
the Selected items pane.
4. Click Done.

Adding an Attachment to a Record

Attach electronic files to a record to serve as supporting
documents. Use this method when an Attachments drop-down
list is available.

1. Open the record to which you want to attach a file.
2. Click the Attachment drop-down menu.
To attach an existing record, select the file from the list.

▪
Click Show unattached to display files that have not yet
been attached to a record.
▪
Click Show all to view the list of all available files.
▪
Click Find to search for a specific attachment.
To add a new attachment, click Add, and then upload your
file.

3. Click Save.

Adding an Attachment in the Documents Section

Attach electronic files to a record to serve as supporting
documents. Use this method when you have enabled single
scan in your preferences. The Documents section appears in
place of the Attachments field if you enabled single scan in
Preferences.
You can either upload a document from your computer or scan
a document if you have a scanner attached to your computer.
To upload a document:

1. Click the Choose file button.
2. Browse to the document that you want to associate with this
record.
3. Select the document, and then click the Open button.
4. Click the Attach button.

To scan a document:

1. In the File name field, type a name for the document that you
want to associate with the record.
2. Click the Scan button.
3. In the Select Source box, select the scanner that is attached to
your computer.
4. Click the Select button.

5. Follow the on-screen instructions to scan the document.

Exporting a List of Records

Export a list to a different file format so that you can open it in a
different application.

1. On a list page, filter the list or apply a view to display only the
information you need.
2. Click the Export drop-down list, and then select your preferred
format. The file downloads to your default browser download
location.
3. Open the file using the appropriate external application.

Viewing Audit Trails

View an audit trail to track the changes made to a record.

1. On a record's page, click the More actions drop-down menu.
2. Select View audit trail.

Adding a Record or Transaction

Use any of the following options to open a new entry page for a
record or transaction.

▪
To quickly add an entry from anywhere in the application, click

 Add next to any item on the menu tab.
▪
To add an entry right after creating a new record or
transaction, click Save and New.

On some pages, the Save and New option is available through
the More actions button. Depending on the transaction, you
may also see Post & New, Draft & New, or Submit & New.

▪
To add a record using field values from your current record,
click Duplicate.

Setting Default Line Item Values

Set default values to help quicken the line item entry process.

1. Click Show defaults to display all fields where you can set
default values.
2. Click the drop-down menu for a field for which you want to set a
default, and then select the value.
3. Click Apply defaults.

Reversing a Transaction

Use the Transaction Reversal box if you accidentally created
a duplicate record or if you want to reverse a payment for an
invoice.

You cannot undo a reversal. Recreate a transaction if you reverse
one by mistake.

1. Go to the list page for the transaction that you want to reverse.
2. Locate the transaction, and then click Reverse on the far right
side of the row.
3. In Memo, enter a reason for reversal.
4. Set the Reversal date.
5. Click Submit.

Printing a Transaction

Print a copy of a transaction.

1. Perform one of the following to generate a PDF copy of the
transaction.

▪
Go to the list page of the transaction that you want to print,
locate the transaction, and then click Print.
▪
Open the transaction page, and then click Print.
The PDF opens on the browser tab. If you do not have
Adobe Reader installed as a browser add-on, then the
system saves the file in your browser's default download
location or opens in your PDF-associated application.

2. Print the file using the Adobe Acrobat print feature.

#### Company Information Page

##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Company Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company`


The Company information page controls various options throughout the RealPage Accounting 

system. Review each tab available at the company level to understand the impact that each 

option has on the various applications throughout the system: 

• 
General information 

• 
Security 

• 
Accounting 

• 
Schedules 

• 
CSV import 

• 
Property management 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to set up your company’s information. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Administration 
Company info 
View, Edit 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

#### General Information Tab
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 19*



##### Adding or Editing General Information
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 19*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

General Information Tab 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company > General Information`


The General information tab displays basic information and settings for your company. 

The sections on this tab include: 

• 
Company information 

• 
Global settings 

• 
Display 

• 
Printed logos and text 

• 
Tax code groups 

Adding or Editing General Information 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company > General Information > Edit`


Enter your company’s details and define basic settings on the General information tab. The only 

two required fields on this tab are Name and Email address. The main contact email is for the 

main financial contact at your company. 

Company Information Section 

Use the Company information section to enter your company’s information the way it should 

appear on outgoing documents, such as sales quotes and invoices.  

1. 
In the Name field, type your company’s name. 

2. 
In the Tax ID field, type the company’s federal tax ID number. The system uses this for Form 

1099 and Form 1098. If applicable, enter the VAT registration number. 

3. 
In the Transmitter control code field, type the TCC code that is assigned to your business 

by the Internal Revenue Service.  

4. 
Select the company’s country of operation from the Operating country drop-down list. 

5. 
Type the company’s Address and City along with RealPage and OneSite system information: 

• 
OneSite URL (for OneSite drill-ability): Type the URL to access the OneSite database, 

for example, “training.onesite.realpage.com.” This has the RealPage Accounting data. 

• 
OneSite PMCID (For this Company ID): Type the company ID as it appears in OneSite. 

This is the OneSite PMC ID. 

6. 
Select the Use ISO country codes check box to enter your country designation so that it 

aligns with ISO 3166-1 standard country codes. Using ISO country codes helps separate US 

and foreign addresses when computing sales tax. 

---


<!-- Page 20 -->
Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

7. 
In the Main contact section, type the name, phone, email address, and fax number for the 

person in your company in charge of financial data. RealPage Accounting uses this contact 

when sending out important communications regarding feature releases or product issues. 

8. 
In the Legal address section, type the name and address of your company as it should 

appear on tax forms. This address is used in cases where your company has been legally 

established in a state or province different from the one in which your company is physically 

located. 

Global Settings Section 

1. 
In the Language drop-down list, select the language for your company. 

2. 
In the Time zone drop-down list, select the time zone for your company. For companies 

spread across multiple time zones, this is usually the main office. 

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select the format setting you prefer. The system uses this 

format when a date appears on a document. 

4. 
In the Time format drop-down list, select either a 12-hour or 24-hour format. 

5. 
If your company prints PDF versions of reports or statements that include any non-Latin 

characters, select “UTF-8 enabled” in the PDF format drop-down list. 

• 
Enabling UTF-8 also changes the format of your PDFs. As a result, we recommend you 

only enable UTF-8 if you are printing non-Latin characters (for example, written 

Chinese, Hebrew, or Japanese). 

• 
Even if you enable UTF-8, RealPage Accounting does not support non-Latin characters 

in checks, 1099 forms, any customized forms you may have created using RealPage 

Accounting’s custom documents feature, or any customized forms RealPage 

Accounting may have created on your behalf. 

• 
You can enable or disable this feature at any time. If you print reports with non-Latin 

characters only occasionally, you can enable UTF-8 only when you print these reports. 

6. 
In the Attachment sequence type drop-down list, select a sequence to let the company 

automatically assign a number to attachments. Attachments that users add to transactions 

and other documents are automatically numbered, saving time for the user. 

The system automatically generates a unique number for each new attachment you create. 

Learn more about document sequences (on page 258). 

7. 
Select a Permission type option: 

• 
User-based: Select this option to set permissions for each individual user separately. 

This permission type is easier to maintain and configure if you only have a few 

employees. 

---


<!-- Page 21 -->
Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Role-based: Select this option to adjust user permissions in bulk through user roles. 

This permission type is better if you have large groups of employees with similar 

permissions, or if you experience high turnover in certain positions. 

8. 
In the Scheduled jobs drop-down list, select On to turn on all scheduled jobs. This controls 

all scheduled jobs, including all recurring transactions, scheduled or offline reports, and 

renewal templates. Scheduled jobs are run daily, on or after 12:00 am PT. 

9. 
Select the Set IDs to uppercase check box to display all IDs in uppercase format. 

Display Section 

Use the Display section to customize the order in which the menu items appear on the menu, 

change entity colors, and upload a logo to replace the RealPage Accounting logo for your login 

and company pages.  

To change the application order: 

1. 
Click and hold 
 Rearrange next to the menu item you want to move, and then drag it to 

the desired location. 

2. 
Rearrange the menu items to get your preferred order. 

To assign entity colors: 

---


<!-- Page 22 -->
Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

1. 
Click the drop-down arrow for the entity whose color you want to change. 

2. 
Select from the available colors or click the See custom colors link to pick a custom color. 

To replace the logo: 

1. 
Click the Upload logo button. 

The system displays the Upload a Logo box. 

2. 
Click Browse and select a GIF, JPG, or PNG image. 

3. 
Click Upload. The system replaces the RealPage Accounting logo with your logo. 

Printed Logos and Text Section 

This section lets you add a company logo to system-generated documents. You can add logos in 

printed documents, XSL custom documents, and email templates. 

To upload a logo: 

1. 
Click the applicable Upload logo button: 

• 
In printed documents: The logo must be 216 x 43 pixels. This will appear on invoices, 

statements, Spend Management documents, and financial reports. 

• 
In XSL custom documents: The logo must be 300 x 300 pixels. This will appear on all 

XSL custom documents. 

• 
In email templates: The logo must be 300 x 300 pixels. This will appear in emails sent 

using a template that includes a logo. 

The Upload a Logo box opens. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button. 

3. 
Select a GIF, JPG, or PNG image, and then click the Open button. 

4. 
Click the Upload button. 

5. 
In the Marketing field, type marketing text to display in the top section on a customer 

invoice near the transaction header. 

---


<!-- Page 23 -->
Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

6. 
In the Message field, type marketing text to display in the lower section of a customer 

invoice.  

Tax Code Groups Section 

Type the tax code groups to which your company belongs. 

What’s Next? 

The Company Information page has additional tabs with configurable information for Security, 

Accounting, and Schedules. Continue setting up your company configuration by selecting 

another tab. 

• 
Security Tab (on page 10) 

• 
Accounting Tab (on page 15) 

• 
Schedules Tab (on page 17) 

• 
CSV Import Tab (on page 19) 

The Property Management tab is for informational purposes only, and appears only when your 
company has purchased the RealPage Commercial Property Management application.

#### Security Tab
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*



##### Adding or Editing Security Settings
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Security Tab 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company > Security`


Your company security is of the utmost important to RealPage. For this reason, we recommend 

that only administrators make changes to your company security features and settings on the 

Security tab. 

Adding or Editing Security Settings 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company > Security`


Sign-In Settings Section 

1. 
Define the timeout settings: 

• 
Default inactivity duration: Select the default amount of time users can remain active 

before they are automatically logged out of the system. The Maximum hours let you 

define a maximum amount of time to extend the default inactivity. 

• 
Default session duration: Select the default amount of time users can stay in the 

system before they are automatically logged out, regardless of their activity. The 

Maximum hours let you define a maximum amount of time to extend the default 

session duration. 

2. 
Each user must have a password. Complete the options for each password: 

• 
Change duration: Click the drop-down arrow and select the frequency at which users 

must change their passwords. You can require users to change their passwords every 

week, once a year, or somewhere in-between. Your choice depends on your work 

environment, number of employees, employee rotation, organizational policy, and so 

on. You can easily change this frequency at any time.

##### Enforcing IP Address Filters
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 27*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Enforcing IP Address Filters 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company > Security`


1. 
When you enforce IP address filters, any login that doesn’t come from the list of allowed IP 

addresses is denied, preventing login attempts from unknown locations. Your options 

include: 

• 
None: Users can sign on from anywhere. 

• 
Enforce at company level: All users can only sign on from a specified range of IP 

addresses for your company. 

• 
Enforce at company level and override at user level: Users can sign on either from 

the company range of specified IP addresses or from any of the IP addresses specified 

in their user IP address filters. 

• 
Enforce at user level: Users can only sign on from any of their individual, specified IP 

addresses. 

If IP address filtering is turned on and a user is unable to log into RealPage Accounting, click 

 Edit under the IP filter drop-down list and make sure that the user’s IP address appears 
in the list of allowed IP addresses. 

2. 
To add approved IP addresses, click 
 Edit under the IP filter drop-down list. 

3. 
In the IP Address Filter Information box, click Add. Add an IP address or IP address range. 

To enter a single address (rather than a range), type the same IP address in the Start IP 

address and End IP address fields.  

• 
Company-level: Type only the IP address or address range. Do not select a user name. 

• 
User-level: Select the user name, and enter the IP address or address range. 

You can add more than one IP address filter per user. For example, if your CFO signs in 
from two different locations, add two records to your IP address list —one record 
for each IP address—and select the CFO’s user name for both records. 

4. 
Save your changes. 

If you enable IP filtering without creating the appropriate filters, a user can access your 
RealPage Accounting company regardless of their IP address. For example, if you choose 

Enforce at company level, but you do not create a filter for the company range, then the 
system does not enforce IP address filtering because it does not have an IP address range 
to check. The effect is the same as if you set IP address filtering to “None.”

#### Schedules Tab
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 31*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Schedules Tab 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company > Schedules`


Use the Schedules tab to define the company work week and office holidays. 

Week Schedule Section 

In the Week schedule section, you can specify your company’s workdays and weekends. This gives 

you flexibility to control whether people can submit hours for time worked on these days and, if 

they can, to apply a different pay rate.  

Select the days to include as workdays and weekends by selecting the check boxes. The system 

defaults to a work week of Monday through Friday, and a weekend of Saturday and Sunday. 

Holiday Schedule Section 

The Holiday schedule section is intended primarily for service organizations that want to control 

whether their consultants or employees can work on company or office holidays. 

A holiday schedule consists of a related group of individual holidays. By creating a holiday 

schedule, you can configure the system automatically to: 

• 
Reject any time sheets submitted with time worked on one of the designated holidays.  

• 
Apply a different pay scale for hourly workers who are allowed to work on holidays. 

Holiday schedules are ideal for organizations with multiple offices or multiple corporate entities. 

These organizations can create a different holiday schedule for each related group of 

holidays—for example, “India Holidays” or “Chinese Holidays” —and so better incorporate labor 

costs into project financial planning.  

If you have no need or desire to control whether your people work on a company holiday, you 

can leave this section blank.

Enforce IP address 

filters 

IP filter 

When you enforce IP address filters, any login that doesn’t come from the 

list of allowed IP addresses is denied. This adds an extra level of security by 

preventing login attempts from unknown locations. Depending on the type 

of security you want to use, you can choose to specify ranges of known IP 

addresses for your company, allowed IP addresses for each user, or a 

combination of both. 

You can enforce IP address access in four ways: 

• 
None: Users can log in from anywhere. 

• 
Enforce at company level: All users in the company are restricted to 

logging in from the range or ranges of IP addresses that you specify.  

• 
Enforce at company level and override at user level: Users can log 

in either from the company range of IP addresses or from one or 

more IP addresses specified in their IP address filters. For example, 

you can specify that everyone log in from the office, but that your 

CFO be able to log in either from the office or from home. In this 

case, the CFO needs two filters, one for the office and one for home. 

• 
Enforce at user level: Each user must have an IP address filter with a 

specific address. Anyone without an explicit IP address filter cannot 

log in, even if there is a company range for the office and the user 

logs in from the office. 

• 
If IP address filtering is turned on and a user is unable to log into 

RealPage Accounting, click the pencil icon to the right of the 

drop-down menu and make sure that the user’s IP address appears 

in the list of allowed IP addresses.

#### My Preferences Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 44*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

My Preferences Page 

(User Name) > My Preferences 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


Use the Preferences page to adjust your individual user preferences to better suit how you work 

in RealPage Accounting. You can also adjust some of the default security preferences set by your 

company administrator. For example, if your administrator sets a maximum interval of six hours 

before you are automatically signed out but you only need to be in the system for two hours, you 

can change that interval. 

The Preferences page contains the following sections: 

• 
General information: Use this section to add and modify your contact information, 

including the name and email address used to identify you in the system. The system 

automatically updates this information in your contact record. Your phone number and 

address are optional. 

• 
Security preferences: Use this section to create a password security question, adjust system 

timeouts, and change your password. 

• 
Email notifications: Use this section to add signature information for sending email 

notifications and select the types of notifications you want to receive. 

• 
On-screen messages: Use this section to select display preferences for on-screen messages 

and warnings. 

• 
Display: Use this section to personalize your system display. 

• 
Check preferences: Use this section to upload a digital signature for checks. 

• 
General preferences: Use this section to set your time zone, date and time format, 

language, and bookmarks. 

• 
Approval delegates: Use this section to reroute approval requests to a specific delegate in 

your absence. 

• 
Mobile app preferences for service requests: Use this section to set your display 

preferences for service requests. 

The options on this page may vary based on your user type. For example, external users cannot 
change their passwords from this page. 

Changing Another User’s Preferences (Administrators Only) 

If you are an administrator, you can set your own preferences or change another user’s 

preferences (on page 47). 

By editing a user’s preferences, you can control settings such as the user’s start page, menu order, 

session timeouts, and check signature.

##### Setting Inactivity and Session Timeouts
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Setting Inactivity and Session Timeouts 

(User Name) > My Preferences  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


To protect company security, you can set timeouts for when the system should automatically sign 

you out. The system measures two kinds of activity: 

• 
Inactivity duration: Set the amount of time your system can remain inactive (when you 

aren’t using it) before it signs you out. The maximum amount of time that you can set is 

limited by the maximum amount of inactivity hours set for your entire organization, which is 

six hours or less. 

• 
Session duration: Set the amount of time that you can be in the system if you’re actively 

using it. The maximum amount of time you can set is limited by the maximum number of 

hours set for your entire organization, which is 12 hours or less. 

For example, say you set a six-hour session duration and a two-hour inactivity duration. If you 

continuously work in the system, then the system signs you out after six hours. If you work two 

hours in the system, and then leave it idle for two hours, then you’ll be automatically signed out 

at the end of the two idle hours, regardless of your overall session duration time. 

To set your timeout preferences: 

1. 
On the Preferences page, find the Security preferences section. 

2. 
In the Timeout section, below Inactivity duration signout, select the number of Hours and 

Minutes that RealPage Accounting remains active until it times out due to inactivity. The 

system signs you out when you are inactive for the duration that you set. 

3. 
In the Session duration signout section, select the number of Hours and Minutes to allow a 

session to last. When this time expires, the system requires you to log in again. 

The maximum amount of time that you can set in these fields is dictated by the maximum 
timeout settings that your administrator defined for the entire company on the Company 

information page. 

4. 
Click Save.

Intercompany Ticketing 

Use this section to choose your email notification preference for intercompany service tickets. 

When a service ticket is created, the system sends an email to: 

• 
The user who submitted the ticket (to notify them that it was successfully submitted) 

• 
The user or users who are assigned as the reviewer (to notify them that a ticket requires 

their approval) 

• 
The user or users who are assigned to the ticket (to notify them that they are assigned to 

resolve and close the ticket) 

You can select your personal notification preference for these emails: 

• 
None: Do not receive any notifications for service tickets. 

• 
Individual: Receive a separate email each time a service ticket is created. 

• 
Consolidated: Consolidate notifications into a single email for all service tickets created that 

day. 

If you are the user who submitted the service ticket, then you will receive a separate email for 
each ticket you submit, regardless of your notification preference. 

Approval Request Notifications 

If you approve a lot of transactions, then you receive a lot of approval notifications. To mitigate 

this, you can consolidate approval notifications into a single, daily email. 

1. 
Select a notification preference for each transaction type: 

• 
None: Do not receive any notifications. 

• 
Individual: Receive an email each time a transaction of this type is approved. 

• 
Consolidated: Reduce your incoming email by grouping related approved transaction 

notifications into one email. 

Your list of transaction types is determined by the applications that your company has 

installed. Items that have an asterisk (*) appear only if you have installed one of the 

additional RealPage Financial Suite applications, such as Spend Management or Job Cost 

and Reserves: 

• 
A/P invoice 

• 
Purchase order* 

• 
Service contracts* 

• 
Subcontracts* 

• 
Job cost change order* 

• 
Journal entry 

• 
Payment 

• 
Expense report

Setting Up Check Preferences 

The system can use a digital signature that you upload to the system on printed checks so that 

the digital signature appears on the printed checks. The system uses the signature of the person 

who selects the invoices to pay, and not the person who prints the checks. 

Create the desired digital signature as a GIF or JPG and then upload it to either the bank account 

record or to your user preferences. You can set up signatures in the system in two places:  

• 
On the bank account record. You can upload a signature associated with a checking 

account in the Cash Management application. 

• 
In your user preferences. The signature that you upload with the My preferences option is 

associated with your company user ID.  

When signatures are set up in both places, the system uses the signature that is set up in your 

user preferences, not the one set up in the bank account record. The user who selects invoices on 

the Pay A/P invoices page is the one whose signature goes on the check; it is not the user who 

prints the actual check. 

If you do not upload a signature file in your preferences, then the system uses the signatures 

associated with the checking account instead. 

If a digital signature is not set up in either location, then the check prints with a blank signature 

line. 

For information on creating a signature file, see Creating a Digital Check Signature (on page 42).

##### Creating a Digital Check Signature
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 57*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Creating a Digital Check Signature 

The signature file must be 3.0” wide x 0.36” high, 150 dpi, and saved as a GIF or JPG file no larger 

than 10K. If you have a scanner and a little experience in computer graphics, you can create the 

signature yourself. If not, ask a local desktop-publishing service to scan your signature and resize 

it for you. 

1. 
Sign your name in a 3.0” wide by 0.36” high frame. 

2. 
Scan the signature. Use 150 dpi resolution. 

3. 
Save the file as a 16-bit color GIF or JPG file. The file size can’t exceed 10K. 

4. 
Open the file in a graphics program and verify that it appears correctly. 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

Don’t be concerned if your graphics program tells you that the size of the image is greater than 

3.0” wide by 0.36” high. However, be sure to maintain the correct aspect ratio of 3.0” wide by 

0.36” high. Otherwise, the system enlarges or reduces the image to fit the bounding box, so the 

image appears distorted both on your printed checks and through the check delivery service. 

Good Digital Signatures 

The most effective signature fills the box, leaving little white space. 

If your signature does not fill the box, it appears distorted on your printed checks or through the 

RealPage Check Delivery service. 

Good: The signature fills the box. 

Too small: The signature leaves too much white space. 

Unclear: The signature is too small and too far to the left. 

---

To adjust printer offsets, see Aligning Your Printer to Print Checks (on page 44). 

Aligning Your Printer to Print Checks 

(User Name) > My Preferences 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


This topic assists you in adjusting printer offsets to align your check PDFs with your printer. The 

adjustments are applied to any printer on which you print a PDF check image. The adjustment 

process does not affect the printing of non-RealPage PDFs or RealPage PDFs other than checks. 

The adjustments you make are unique to you as a user. Other users may have different PDF 

offsets. Thus, if you must have two sets of adjustment parameters for two printers, you need to 

have two users with different adjustment parameters. 

Measure the distance of the crosshairs from the top and left edges of the sheet of paper. Use a 

ruler that has a decimal scale. If the measurements are not exactly 1”, then click the adjustment 

controls on your Preferences page until the relative position of the printed image is exactly 1” 

from the top and left edges of the sheet of paper. 

---


<!-- Page 59 -->
Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

The illustration below shows the controls. Click the horizontal arrows to move the image left or 

right; click the vertical ones to move the image up or down. 

Each click moves the image by 0.05.” Thus, if your image is offset to the right by 0.10”, click the 

horizontal offset left arrow 
 two times. If the image is offset downward by 0.15,” click the up 

arrow 
 three times. 

To offset the PDF image: 

1. 
On the Preferences page, find the Check preferences section. 

2. 
Click the Verify your printer alignment for RealPage checks link at the bottom of the 

section, and then print the page to the printer that you normally use to print checks. 

3. 
Measure the crosshairs horizontally and vertically. The intersection must be exactly 1” from 

the top edge and 1” from the left edge of your sheet of paper. 

4. 
If the measurements are not exactly 1”, then use the Printing offsets controls on the 

Preferences page to adjust the relative position of how your printer prints the PDF on the 

page. 

5. 
Print the test page again. If the crosshairs are not exactly 1” × 1”, repeat the adjustment 

process until they are.

using other formats. For example, say you set your date format to MM/DD/YY. January 1, 

2020 displays as 1/1/2020. However, you can enter the date of January 1, 2020 as 1-1-2020, 

and it still displays as 1/1/2020. You can change the date format at any time. For example, if 

you want a particular date format to print a single report, change it here, print the report, 

and then change it back again.

In the Display option after posting a converted transaction section, choose an option:

List the converted from transactions

List the converted to transactions

##### Configuring A/P Thresholds
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 75*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Configuring A/P Thresholds 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Accounts Payable > 
Thresholds`


Use the Thresholds section to configure how the system responds when these events occur:  

• 
When posting in the future 

• 
When a credit limit is exceeded 

• 
When the vendor is on hold 

To configure A/P thresholds: 

1. 
In the If posting in future period section, select the system response if a user attempts to set 

a future period date as the General Ledger posting date. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message requesting the user to 

select a date within the current period. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

Do nothing is the default. 

The subledgers share the same posting periods as the general ledger. 

2. 
In the If credit limit is exceeded section, select the desired system response to an attempt to 

enter an invoice that exceeds the credit limit with a vendor. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message showing the total due for 

the vendor and your set credit limit. The transaction can’t be created as entered. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

Do nothing is the default. 

3. 
In the If vendor is on hold section, select the desired system response to an attempt to enter 

an A/P invoice from a vendor with an On Hold status: 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message that the vendor is 

currently on hold. The transaction can’t be created. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

4. 
Don’t allow transactions to be created is the default. 

---



##### Enabling A/P Functionality
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 76*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Enabling A/P Functionality 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Accounts Payable > Enable 
Functionality`


Use the Enable Functionality section to enable or disable Accounts Payable features. 

To customize A/P functionality: 

1. 
Selecting the Enable accounts payable G/L account override in invoice and adjustment 

entry option enables you to override the default G/L account as you create a transaction. 

You can override: 

• 
An entire A/P invoice or adjustment 

• 
One or more specific line-items in an A/P invoice or adjustment 

• 
All transactions involving a specific vendor 

To use this feature, you must also flag the override accounts and grant permissions. See 

Flagging an account as an override account. 

2.

Filling In the Enable Independent Release and Processing of Payments for Line Items in 
the Same A/P Invoice Section 

1. 
In the Release to pay section, select the desired option to enable independent release and 

processing of payment for line items in the same A/P invoice: 

• 
Select Don’t enable to show all line items. 

• 
Select Enable and show all, including items yet to be released for payment. 

• 
Select Enable and show only items released for payment. 

The ability to release only specific line items of an A/P invoice for payment gives you tighter 

control over your cash outflows. Pay only certain line items of an invoice, and pay others as 

you want. The invoice remains partially paid in the system until every line item has been 

paid. This is especially helpful for companies that have multiple entities – for example, if one 

entity has funds available to make a payment but another entity does not. For example, if 

you enter a multi-line invoice that has some items due immediately and others due in 30 

days, use this feature to release for payment only those items that are due immediately. 

Then return to this invoice in a month and release for payment the line items that were due 

in 30 days. This gives you greater control over your cash outflows and ensures that only 

those items you are ready to pay are selected for payment.

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 80*

Configuring A/P Screen Settings 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Accounts Payable > Screen 
Settings`


Use the Screen settings section to configure how the Accounts Payable application handles G/L 

posting date overrides, how it displays the memo line on A/P invoices and adjustments, and 

whether you want the system to auto-complete vendor information in the next A/P invoice or 

adjustment. 

To configure A/P screen settings: 

1. 
In the Enable override of G/L posting date during entry section, in the G/L posting date 

section, select Yes to allow users to override the posting date of A/P invoices or adjustments 

during transaction entry. This enables you to have one date for the transaction and a 

separate date for when the transaction posts to the G/L. 

The G/L Posting Date is also available via the XML Gateway. If you use different posting and 
transaction dates and you automatically export multiple transactions into your company, 
this enables you to retain those separate dates when the data enters the system. 

2. 
In the Auto-populate with G/L posting date section, select Yes to have the system complete 

the transaction with the G/L for A/P invoices and adjustments. This option is only available 

when Enable override of G/L posting date during entry is set to Yes. 

Setting this to No causes the G/L posting date to be blank when creating A/P invoices in 
Accounts payable. 

3. 
In the Display as section, in the Display each A/P invoice or adjustment memo line as a 

section, select how you want the memo box to appear on the A/P invoice or adjustment line 

item: 

• 
Single line with pop-up text area 

• 
Double line text area 

• 
Triple line text area 

4. 
Select the Auto-populate vendor information to the next invoice/adjustment during 

multi-invoice/adjustment entry check box to enable the system to complete information 

from the previous A/P invoice or adjustment to save data-entry time. This feature is most 

useful when entering multiple A/P invoices or adjustments for the same vendor. 

5. 
Select the Make A/P invoices memo as required check box to require users who are 

entering A/P invoices to fill in the Memo fields. When the user tries to post the transaction 

without text in the Memo field, the system displays an error message.

Spend Management Tab 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Spend Management`


Use the Spend management tab on the Central configuration page to configure frequently used 

Spend Management settings. This tab contains the following sections, depending on the features 

that your company has chosen to enable: 

• 
Thresholds: Use this section to enable tolerance rules for A/P invoices. Tolerance rules allow 

for A/P invoices that do not match the budgeted amount to be approved if they do not 

exceed a certain amount. 

• 
Enable functionality: Use this section to enable the logging of the receipt of goods to a 

journal, allow change orders to be performed, require attachments from site users, or enable 

the Storefront feature. 

• 
Journals: If you enable the receipt of goods functionality, use this section to set up journals 

for logging the receipt of goods. This section only appears if the Enable Receipt of Goods 

check box is selected. 

• 
G/L accounts: If you implement Job Cost, use this section to choose the account for 

retainage on contracts. 

• 
Document sequencing: Use this section to set up prefixes for document numbers for 

orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. Using prefixes for different documents allows for 

easier identification of the document type. For example, you can set up service contracts 

with a prefix of “SC-” so that you can easily identify a document numbered “SC-3001” as a 

service contract.

•

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Select this option to display a message 

showing the total due for the customer and the set credit limit. The transaction can’t

•

##### Enabling A/R Functionality
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 93*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Enabling A/R Functionality 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Accounts Receivable > Enable 
Functionality`


Use the Enable functionality section to enable or disable Accounts Receivable features. 

To enable A/R functionality: 

1. 
Select the Enable accounts receivable G/L account override in invoice and adjustment 

entry check box when you want to override the default G/L account as you create a 

transaction. 

To make use of this option, you also need to: 

• 
Configure one or more G/L accounts as override accounts. 

• 
Provide permissions for selected users to override the default G/L account in invoice 

and adjustment transaction, as well as for any invoice or adjustment transactions 

involving specific customers, as needed. 

To tag an account, go to General Ledger, select the account, and designate it as either a 

Payables account or a Receivables account as appropriate. The system adds the account to 

the filtered list of override accounts that you can select from in specific pages, such as 

transaction pages and vendor and customer pages. 

Payables account: the system adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts 

available as override accounts on A/P invoice, adjustment, and vendor pages. 

Receivables account: the system adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts 

available as override accounts on A/R invoice, adjustment, and customer pages. 

You can enable override of the default A/R G/L account for: 

• 
An entire invoice or adjustment 

• 
One or more specific line-items in an invoice or adjustment 

• 
All transactions involving a specific customer 

2. 
Select the Enable account labels check box to provide restricted access to G/L accounts and 

a means of textually naming them.  

This setting determines whether Account labels will be required or not (On or Off). Account 

labels are a good way to restrict access to G/L accounts. If an Account label is not set up for 

a particular G/L account, that account can’t be accessed. Also, Account labels provide a 

plain-English equivalent for G/L account numbers, which can be helpful for users. When 

enabled, you can: 

• 
Associate an account number with an intuitive name that is easy to recognize and 

select from a drop-down list. 

• 
Create subtotal lines in invoices, such as for sales tax.  

---


<!-- Page 94 -->
Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Categorize different products/expenses/services. 

• 
Restrict access to only those G/L accounts that do have labels. 

After you enable account labels, two additional options appear in this section: 

Display tax and subtotals fields for invoices: Select this option if you’re going to create an 
account label for use in tax subtotals. (US taxes only) 

Enable Advanced Tax schedules: This option is not supported. 

3. 
Select the Enable allocation in invoice entry check box to allow users to allocate charges to 

different accounts on a single line item of an invoice. 

This option can only be enabled here if you’ve enabled it in G/L configuration. 

4. 
Select the Enable the system to automatically apply discounts check box. 

When you record the receipt of a payment for an invoice with an associated term discount, 

the system automatically selects the Apply discount check box in the transaction and 

applies the term discount. 

Leave this option unselected if you want to manually apply the discount. 

5. 
Select the Turn off automatic payment suggestions check box to limit the system to using 

the payment amount you enter to populate the Amount Received fields on the Select 

Invoices for Payment page. 

By default, the system applies the payment to the invoices starting with the oldest invoice. 

• 
If the amount of the payment is sufficient to fully pay that invoice, the system 

automatically selects the Receive Full check box for that invoice, applies the remainder 

to the next invoice, and so on until the entire payment amount is used up. 

• 
If any amount is left over because the payment amount is greater than the total of the 

invoices, the system displays the overpayment amount in the Amount Overpaid field. 

If you usually overwrite the amounts proposed by the system, and no longer want the 
system to propose those amounts, select this check box to disable this feature. 

6. 
Select the Enable reclassification for invoices and adjustments check box to allow users 

with proper permissions to edit accounting information on both partially and fully paid 

invoices and adjustments. 

7. 
Select the Enable reversal of unpaid invoices check box to prevents the deletion of unpaid 

invoices. Instead, you must reverse unpaid invoices, which maintains an audit trail. 

Selecting Enable reversal of unpaid invoices changes the following pages: 

• 
Accounts Receivable: for Invoices, Delete becomes Reverse. 

• 
Permissions: for Invoices, Delete becomes a read-only selection. 

---


<!-- Page 95 -->
Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

When this check box is enabled, you cannot delete invoices. 

8. 
Select the Enable creating, editing, and deleting foreign currency invoices check box. If 

your company uses multiple currencies, you can use multiple currencies in your invoice 

entry process. 

Depending on your configuration, this check box may also be named Enable creating 

foreign-currency advances, and enable creating, editing, and deleting foreign-currency 

invoices, and adjustments. 

Even after you enable multi-currency transactions in General ledger setup, you must 
enable multi-currency in each application. This gives you the option to configure your 
company so that users can make multi-currency transactions in one application but not 
another. For example, enable them in Accounts payable but not Accounts receivable. 

9. 
Select the Payment dates must be greater than their invoice dates check box to enforce a 

rule that the payment date must be on or after the invoice date. 

10. 
Select the Display tax and subtotals for invoices check box to enable the system to display 

tax and subtotal fields on invoices. 

This feature is available only if you’ve enabled account labels in the Enable Functionality 

section. 

11. 
Skip the Use Advanced tax schedules check box. The Advanced Tax feature is not 

supported. 

12. 
Select the Enable inter-company bill back check box. This option enables the system to 

automatically create a bill on one entity’s books when an invoice is created in a second 

entity in multi-entity, single-currency companies.  

This feature is available only for multi-entity shared companies. 

13. 
Select the Enable bank account selection in A/R invoice check box to allow users to select a 

bank account when creating an A/R invoice. When paying the invoice, the system allows you 

to pay from the bank account that you select in the invoice. When paying the invoice, you 

can filter on the bank account so that you can select from invoices that were marked to be 

paid with that bank account.  

After you select this option, you cannot disable it. 

14. 
Select the Enforce entity/property currency and base currency check box when your 

company manages multiple currencies, and you want to restrict users to using only two 

currencies in transactions: their designated property’s currency and the entity’s base 

currency. 

15. 
Click the Save button.

##### Configuring A/R Screen Settings
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 97*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Configuring A/R Screen Settings 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Accounts Receivable > Screen 
Settings`


Use the Screen Settings section to configure how the Accounts Receivable application handles G/L 

posting date overrides, how it displays the memo line on invoices and adjustments, and whether 

you want the system to auto-complete G/L posting dates and customer information. 

To configure A/R screen settings: 

1. 
Under Enable override of G/L posting date during entry: 

In G/L posting date, select Yes to have the system allow you to override the posting date of 

invoices or adjustments during transaction entry. This enables you to have one date for the 

date of actual transaction and a different date for the date the transaction actually posts to 

the G/L. 

The G/L Posting Date is also available via the XML Gateway. If you use different posting and 
transaction dates and you automatically export multiple transactions into your company, 
this enables you to retain those separate dates when the data enters the system. 

2. 
In the Auto-populate with G/L posting date section: 

Select Yes if you want to have the system automatically complete the transaction posting 

date with the G/L posting date for invoices and adjustments. This option is only available 

when Enable override of G/L posting date during entry is set to Yes. 

Setting this to No causes the G/L posting date to be blank when creating invoices in 
Accounts Receivable. 

3. 
In the Display each invoice or adjustment memo line as a section, select how you want the 

memo box to appear on the invoice or adjustment line item: 

• 
Single line with pop-up text area 

• 
Double line text area 

• 
Triple line text area 

4. 
Select the Auto-populate customer information check box to have the system complete 

information from the previous invoice to save data-entry time. This feature is most useful 

when entering multiple invoices from the same customer. 

5. 
Click the Save button.

Cash Management Tab

Use the Cash management tab to configure and define settings for the Cash Management 

application. This tab contains the following sections, depending on the features that your 

company has chosen to enable. 

• 
Accounting: This section defines the journal to use for posting miscellaneous cash receipts 

and the default account for undeposited funds.

Third party payments: This section configures third-party payment services in RealPage 

Accounting. 

Configuring Cash Management 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Cash Management`


To configure the Cash Management application, complete the following sections on the Cash 

management tab, and then click the Save button. 

Accounting Section 

1. 
In the Transaction summary posting drop-down list, select when the transaction summary 

automatically posts. 

• 
Daily: Select this option to post a single summary to the General Ledger for each 

transaction day. 

• 
Monthly: Select this option to create a single summary at the end of each month, 

regardless of the transaction date within that period. 

 We recommend the daily posting option because it provides the most granular reporting. 

2. 
In the Journal for other cash receipts drop-down list, select the journal to which you want 

to post customer payments. 

For dual-method reporting companies, the options include journals defined as both accrual 
and cash-based. 

3. 
Select the Account labels check box to restrict access to G/L accounts by requiring account 

labels. If an account label is not set up for a particular G/L account, that account cannot be 

accessed. Account labels are created in A/P and A/R, and they provide a plain-English 

equivalent for G/L account numbers, which can be helpful for users. 

4. 
In the If posting in future period field, select what happens if someone tries to set a future 

period date as the General Ledger posting date. 

---


<!-- Page 102 -->
Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

5. 
In the Default exchange rate type drop-down list, select the exchange rate required to 

process foreign currency transactions. 

6. 
In the Default undeposited funds account drop-down list, select the account into which 

you usually record undeposited funds for it to appear as the default when users make 

deposits and record other receipts. 

7. 
Select the Disable journal entry from bank reconciliation check box to remove the journal 

entry links from the Reconcile bank account page. 

8. 
If you want to be able to pay entity A/P invoices from the top level, select the Enable 

alternate G/L for bank account check box. After saving this change, edit the entity records 

and select an alternate bank account. After configuring this feature, you can use the Pay by 

entity option where you can select an alternate bank account.  

After you enable this feature, it cannot be disabled. 

9. 
Select the Enable foreign electronic payment formats check box to allow sending different 

types of electronic payment files, including ACH, EFT, and BACS. 

After you enable this feature, it cannot be disabled. 

10. 
Select the Show recent credits applied to invoices on check/payment remittance check 

box to display recent credits applied to invoices in the last 30 days at the end of the check 

and grouped by vendor. This information includes the invoice date, invoice number, invoice 

amount, and credits applied. These are included in the Print payment copies and 

Remittance email sent after successful payments via check and ACH payment methods. The 

system also includes invoices paid at the entity level using credits. 

When printing multiple checks for multiple vendors, recent credits are displayed only once 
per vendor. 

11. 
Select the Use the current date as check print date check box to print the current date on 

the check instead of the payment date. 

12. 
Select the Use current date as the payment date for ACH check box to automatically 

update the payment date to the current date when you generate a payment file from the 

ACH file generation page. 

13. 
Select the Use current date as the payment request date for check payments check box to 

set the payment date as the current date when you choose to print the checks on days 

other than the selected date. 

14. 
Select the Automatically confirm checks when they are printed check box to automatically 

confirm checks while they are being printed. The system will run an offline process to 

confirm the checks when you start a new check run or print the check from the Print checks 

page. You will receive an email notification when the process is complete.  

---


<!-- Page 103 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Allowing the system to auto -confirm checks saves time and prevents printed checks from 
sitting unconfirmed. 

15. 
Select the Advance posting date when subledger is closed check box to allow users to 

make end-of-month payments even if the Cash Management subledger is closed. When this 

option is activated, the system automatically advances any cash management transactions 

(deposits, funds transfers, bulk funds transfers, payments, manual payments, or other 

receipts) to the first of the next month if the books are already closed for the period you’re 

posting them to. 

Banking Section 

1. 
In the Default bank account drop-down list, select the bank into which you usually make 

deposits and record other receipts for it to appear as the default when users perform these 

transactions. 

For multi-entity organizations, you can set a default payment method and bank account on 
an entity-by-entity basis on the Additional information tab of the Entity information page

2. 
In the Currency to use on blank check stock field, select whether you want to print the 

Bank account or Country currency on blank check stocks. 

3. 
If your company uses standard ACH payments, then select the Include invoice ACH details 

check box to add ACH details when printing checks. If your company uses multiple 

currencies, then select the Include invoice electronic payments details check box to add 

electronic payment details when printing checks. 

4. 
When payment files are uploaded directly to a bank’s SFTP site, they are automatically 

confirmed in RealPage Accounting. However, you can disable this feature by selecting the

Site View Tab 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Site View`


Use the Site view tab to configure and define settings for Spend Management Site Experience. 

This tab contains two sections:

Grid layout: Use this section to customize which columns appear in the entries grid when 

you are entering line items for A/P invoices and purchase orders in Spend Management Site 

Experience. 

• 
Dimension setup: Use this section to enable additional dimensions in the entries grid when 

you are entering line items for A/P invoices and purchase orders in Spend Management Site 

Experience. 

Customizing Fields in the Entries Grid in the Site View 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Central Configuration > Site View`


You can customize which fields appear in the entries grid when you enter line items for A/P 

invoices and purchase orders in Spend Management Site Experience. 

To customize the entries grid: 

1. 
In the Company application menu, select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Configuration section, select the Central configuration option. 

The Central configuration page opens. 

3. 
Select the Site view tab. 

4. 
The Grid layouts section contains a list of fields associated with A/P invoice and purchase 

order line items. By default, all of these fields are included in the entries grid in Spend 

Management Site Experience. Clear the check box next to any fields that you want to hide 

from the entries grid. 

5. 
Click the Save button to save the changes.

 Workbench page or when you create an invoice from a scanned document on the

Fields 

This page describes the settings used to configure applications on the Central configuration 

page.

Accounts Payable 

Central Configuration Page - Accounts Payable Tab - Thresholds Section 

If posting in future 

period 

Select the system response if a user attempts to set a future period date 

as the general ledger posting date for the A/P invoice.  

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to 

proceed.  

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message 

requesting the user to select a date within the current period.  

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without 

any alert or action on the part of the system. This is the default.  

The subledgers share the same posting periods as the general ledger. 

If credit limit is 

exceeded 

Select the system response to an attempt to enter an A/P invoice that 

exceeds the company’s credit limit with a vendor. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to 

proceed.  

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message 

showing the total due for the vendor and your set credit limit. 

The transaction can’t be created as entered.  

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without 

any alert or action on the part of the system. This is the default. 

If vendor is on hold 
Select the system response to an attempt to enter an A/P invoice from a 

vendor with an On Hold status.  

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to 

proceed.  

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message that 

the vendor is currently on hold. The transaction can’t be created. 

This is the default. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without 

any alert or action on the part of the system.

If the amount of the payment is sufficient to fully pay that invoice, the 

system automatically selects the Receive Full check box for that invoice, 

applies the remainder to the next invoice, and so on until the entire 

payment amount is used up.

the total of the invoices, the system displays the overpayment amount 

in the Amount Overpaid field.

#### Company Setup Wizard
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 134*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 134*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Company Setup Wizard 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company Setup Wizard`


The Company setup wizard takes you through the steps to set up a new company in RealPage 

Accounting so that it is ready for live use. The wizard includes steps to: 

• 
Import and activate entities 

• 
Set up a master chart of accounts 

• 
Enter or upload bank accounts 

• 
Import a master vendor list 

• 
Validate configuration options 

You can download CSV templates to populate your accounting data and then import it back into 

the system, or you can manually enter data into the provided lists. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

You must have Administrator privileges to access the Company setup wizard. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to complete the Company setup wizard: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Company setup wizard 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

##### Importing and Activating Entities
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 135*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Importing and Activating Entities 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company Setup Wizard > Step 1 - Activate Entities`


Use the Activate entities page in the Company setup wizard to activate entities that are in the 

Ordered state. This status indicates that the entity is newly added to the accounting system 

through Unified Provisioning. You can also import and activate entities in bulk by downloading 

the provided template and uploading a list of entities back into the system. 

Activating Existing Entities 

To activate existing entities that are still in the Ordered state: 

1. 
Select the Activate check box next to the desired entity or entities. 

2. 
Edit or fill in the following information for each entity as needed: 

• 
In the Property type drop-down list, select a property type to associate with the entity. 

• 
In the Federal ID field, type the entity’s federal tax ID. This field appears only if you 

configure the multi-entity console to issue a separate 1099 per entity. 

• 
In the Address 1, Address 2, City/town, State, Zip code/Post code, and Country fields, 

fill in the entity’s address information.  

3. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Importing New Entities 

To import new entities in bulk: 

1. 
Click the Download entity template link to download the entity template. 

Alternatively, click the Import new entities button, and then click the Download entities 

template button in the Upload new entities box. 

2. 
Populate data into the spreadsheet. 

3. 
Save the spreadsheet in CSV format. 

4. 
In the wizard, click the Choose file button to upload the CSV file back into the system. 

5. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step. 

What’s Next? 

Setting Up a Master Chart of Accounts (on page 122) 

---



##### Setting Up a Master Chart of Accounts
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 136*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Setting Up a Master Chart of Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company Setup Wizard > Step 2 - Set Master Chart of 
Accounts`


Use the Set master chart of accounts page in the Company setup wizard to set up a chart of 

accounts for your company. The system pre-populates default, industry-standard chart options. 

You can add, edit, or remove accounts from this default chart as needed.  

Do not click the Finish button until you complete the remaining steps in the wizard. Doing this 
saves and activates your entities in Step 1, after which you will not be able to replace the 
default chart of accounts. 

1. 
Under Chart option, choose the type of properties to use for the chart of accounts: 

• 
Conventional: Derives accounts from conventional properties. 

• 
Affordable: Derives accounts from affordable properties. 

A standard chart of accounts appears. The system pre-populates the Title, Category, and 

the first four digits of the Account number. However, you can modify these fields according 

to your business needs. 

2. 
Fill in or edit the required information for each account: 

• 
Type an Account number for the account. 

• 
Type a name for the account in the Title field. 

• 
Select a Category from the drop-down list to associate with the account. Categories 

are permanently pre-assigned to account groups, which are used in financial reports 

and graphs that are supplied in the RealPage Accounting system. 

3. 
The remaining fields automatically populate with information and cannot be changed: 

• 
Account type: Specifies whether the account is a balance sheet or income statement 

account. 

• 
Balance sheet accounts are a snapshot of the current state of a company’s assets, 

liabilities, and equity at a specific time. 

• 
Income statement accounts, also known as profit and loss statement accounts, 

are cumulative for the selected period. 

• 
Period end closing type: Specifies whether the account is a closing or non-closing 

account. 

• 
Instead of manually closing accounts at year end, you can set them to be closing 

accounts and then specify the account in which to close that period. 

• 
Income statement accounts should be closing accounts; balance sheet accounts 

should be non-closing accounts. 

---



##### Entering or Uploading Bank Accounts
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 137*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Close into account: Specifies the account into which closing accounts are closed at the 

end of each period. 

For all income statement accounts, the close-into account will typically be Retained 

Earnings. The system then zeros closing-type accounts into retained earnings at 

year-end. 

• 
Normal balance: Specifies whether the normal balance, from an accounting 

standpoint, is debit or credit. For example, expense accounts are normally debit, while 

sales accounts are normally credit. 

4. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

What’s Next? 

Entering or Uploading Bank Accounts (on page 123) 

Entering or Uploading Bank Accounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company Setup Wizard > Step 3 - Enter/Upload Bank 
Accounts`


Use the Enter/Upload bank accounts page in the Company setup wizard to manually enter bank 

accounts for your company or upload them in bulk using a template. 

To manually enter bank account data: 

1. 
In the Location ID drop-down list, select the default location/entity for G/L posting.  

2. 
Select the Private check box if you want to restrict the bank account so that it is only 

available for the selected location/entity to use. Clear the check box if the bank account is 

shared across multiple locations/entities. 

3. 
In the Account category drop-down list, select a category for the bank account. 

4. 
In the Account number field, type the account number for the bank account. The account 

number is a 10-digit number printed at the bottom of the check.  

5. 
In the Routing number field, type the routing number for the bank account. The routing 

number is 9-digit number printed at the bottom of the check.  

6. 
In the Bank name field, type the bank name. If you have more than one account at this 

bank, then include a description in the name.  

7. 
In the Account type drop-down list, select whether the bank account is a checking or 

savings account. 

8. 
In the G/L account drop-down list, select a G/L account. The G/L account references the 

balance sheet cash account that is tied to your operating system. Bank accounts do not 

need individual G/L codes unless the bank accounts are shared by multiple 

locations/entities.  

---

Importing a Master Vendor List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company Setup Wizard > Import Master Vendor List`


Use the Import master vendor list page in the Company setup wizard to manually enter a master 

vendor list for your company or bulk upload vendors using a template. 

By default, vendors can be used by all entities in a multi-entity shared environment; however, if 

needed, you can restrict them to a particular entity or department. Additional vendor 

configuration options are available in the Accounts Payable application. 

To manually set up vendors: 

1. 
If you do not want the system to automatically assign sequential vendor IDs: 

• 
Clear the Auto assign vendor ID check box. The Vendor ID field appears. 

• 
Type a unique identifier for each vendor record in the Vendor ID field. 

Otherwise, skip this step. 

2. 
In the Vendor name field, type the vendor’s name. 

3. 
In the Print as field, type the vendor’s name the way that you want it to appear on checks. 

4. 
In the Address 1, Address 2, City, State, and Zip code/Post code fields, type address where 

the vendor does business. 

5. 
In the Tax ID field, type the federal tax ID for the vendor. 

6. 
In the Email address field, type the email address of the primary contact for the vendor. 

7. 
In the Phone field, type the phone number of the primary contact for the vendor. 

8. 
In the Country drop-down list, select the country where the vendor does business.

Validating Configuration Options 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company Setup Wizard > Step 5 - Validate 
Configuration Options`


Each module in the RealPage Accounting system is preconfigured according to industry best 

practices. You can adjust these settings in the module configurations. 

The Validate configuration options page in the Company setup wizard displays the settings that 

are most commonly changed. Review and update the following settings as needed: 

1. 
Select the Memo required check box to require users to provide a description on all A/P 

transactions. 

2. 
Select the Enable reversal of unpaid invoices check box to force invoices to be reversed 

instead of deleted. 

3. 
In the Accounts payable account drop-down list, select the default G/L account to use for 

offsetting A/P transactions. 

4. 
In the Discounts account drop-down list, select the default G/L account to use based on 

payment terms.  

What’s Next? 

Click the Finish button to finalize and save your configurations in each step of the Company 

setup wizard.

Approval Setup Wizard 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approval Setup Wizard`


The Approval setup wizard takes you through the steps to set up transaction approval policies 

and workflows for your company and streamlines the approval setup process. It also allows you to 

set up spend policies to compare transactions against your budget. 

The wizard includes the following steps: 

• 
Define user roles 

• 
Set up approval policies 

• 
Set up spend policies 

• 
Set up workflows 

• 
Preview workflows 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

You must have Administrator privileges to access the Approval setup wizard. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to complete the Approval setup wizard: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Approval Setup Wizard 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 146*

Defining User Roles 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approval Setup Wizard > Step 1 - Define User Roles`


The Define user roles page lists all user roles in RealPage Accounting that have any permissions 

for Accounts Payable or Spend Management. You can add additional roles required for your 

business needs. 

By default, any new roles that you create on the Define user roles page are assigned the 

following permissions:

To add a new role: 

1. 
Click the Add roles button. 

The Add roles box opens. 

2. 
In the Name field, type a name for the new role; for example, “Expense Report Reviewer”. 

3. 
In the Description field, type a description of the role’s intended purpose; for example, “This 

role evaluates expense reports and approves or declines them.” 

4. 
Click the Save role button to save the role and continue adding more roles. 

5. 
When you are finished adding roles, click the Finished adding roles button to close the Add 

roles box and return to the wizard.

##### Setting Up Approval Policies
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 147*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Setting Up Approval Policies 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approval Setup Wizard > Step 2 - Set Up Approval 
Policies`


Approval policies define the system logic for determining whether or not a transaction requires 

approval and, if so, who should be assigned to approve it. Each approval policy consists of the 

following settings: 

• 
Policy type: This tells the system which transactions to look for when routing transactions to 

the designated approver or approvers.  

• 
Approval routing and limits: This tells the system which user(s) or role(s) to send the 

transactions to for approval and sets the levels of approval that the transaction must 

progress through in the approval queue. 

Use the Set up approval policy page in the Approval setup wizard to view and edit default 

policies or create additional policies required for your business needs. 

Adding Approval Policies 

To add a new approval policy: 

1. 
Click the Add approval policy button. 

The Approval policy manager box opens. 

2. 
Follow the instructions for adding approval policies (on page 319) in the Approval policy 

manager. 

3. 
When you are finished, click Save to save the policy settings and return to the wizard. 

The approval policy is added to the list with the configured Policy type and Policy name. 

Viewing and Editing Approval Policies 

To view or edit an existing approval policy: 

1. 
Click the Edit or View link in the Options column. 

The Approval policy manager box opens in Edit or View mode, depending on your 

selection. 

2. 
If you are in Edit mode, modify the policy settings as needed, and then click Save. 

What’s Next? 

Setting Up Spend Policies (on page 134) 

---



##### Setting Up Spend Policies
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 148*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Setting Up Spend Policies 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approval Setup Wizard > Step 3 - Setup Spend Policies`


Spend policies allow you to set up and tie rules for spending to budgets in the general ledger 

(G/L). When new transactions are entered, the transaction amount is compared to the budget for 

the period that is set up in the Budget check section on the Approval configuration (on page 295) 

page (monthly, annual, or year-to-date). 

Use the Setup spend policies page in the Approval setup wizard to view and existing spend 

policies or create additional policies required for your business needs. 

If you do not create policies based on budget comparison, proceed to the next step in the wizard. 

Adding Spend Policies 

To add a new spend policy: 

1. 
Click the Add spend policy button. 

The Spend policy manager box opens. 

2. 
Follow the instructions for adding new spend policies (on page 334) in the Spend policy 

manager. 

3. 
When you are finished, click Save to save the policy settings and return to the wizard. 

The spend policy is added to the list with the configured Policy type and Policy name. 

Viewing and Editing Spend Policies 

To view or edit an existing spend policy: 

1. 
Click the Edit or View link in the Options column. 

The Approval policy manager box opens in Edit or View mode, depending on your 

selection. 

2. 
If you are in Edit mode, modify the policy settings as needed, and then click Save. 

What’s Next? 

Setting Up Approval Workflows (on page 134)
