##### Setting Up Approval Workflows
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 149*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Setting Up Approval Workflows 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approval Setup Wizard > Step 4 - Setup Workflows`


Approval workflows associate approval policies with specific properties. Use the Setup workflows 

page in the Approval setup wizard to view and edit default workflows or create additional 

workflows required for your business needs. 

Adding Approval Workflows 

To add a new approval workflow: 

1. 
Click the Add workflow button. 

The Workflow wizard box opens. 

2. 
Follow the instructions for adding approval workflows (on page 339) in the Workflow 

wizard. 

3. 
When you are finished, click Save to save the workflow settings and return to the main 

wizard. 

The approval workflow is added to the list with the information that you configured: 

• 
Workflow name: The name of the workflow. 

• 
Policies: The number of approval policies associated with the workflow. 

• 
Transaction objects: The transaction types to which the workflow applies.  

Viewing and Editing Approval Workflows 

To view or edit an existing approval workflow: 

1. 
Click the Edit or View link in the Options column. 

The Workflow wizard box opens in Edit or View mode, depending on your selection. 

2. 
If you are in Edit mode, modify the policy settings as needed, and then click Save. 

What’s Next? 

Previewing Workflows (on page 135)

##### Previewing Workflows
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 150*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Previewing Workflows 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approval Setup Wizard > Step 5 - Preview Workflows`


The final step in the Approval setup wizard is to preview and verify the approval paths of your 

company’s workflows. Select a transaction type on the Preview workflows page, and then fill in 

the required transaction details to preview the approval workflow settings and see how the 

system will route approvals for these types of transactions. 

To preview approval workflows: 

1. 
Select the desired transaction type from the Transaction drop-down list. 

The remaining fields change based on your selection. 

2. 
Fill in the transaction details as needed to preview how the system routes approvals for 

transactions with these settings. Depending on your selection in step 1, you must configure 

a variation of the following fields:  

• 
Vendor ID: Select the desired vendor record to associate with the transaction. 

• 
G/L account: Select the desired G/L account to associate with the transaction.  

• 
WIP account: Select the desired WIP account to associate with the transaction. 

• 
Location ID: Select the desired location record to associate with the transaction. 

• 
Transaction amount: Type the desired transaction amount. 

• 
Job: Select the desired job to associate with the transaction.  

3. 
Click the Preview workflow button. 

4. 
Review the following columns to verify that the approval routing settings are correct: 

• 
Approval type: This is the approval policy type; for example, User, Tiered Amount, 

Accounting Reviewer, etc. 

• 
Policy name: This is the approval policy name. Click this link to open the Approval 

policy manager box and view the details of your approval policy. 

• 
Workflow name: This is the approval workflow name. Click this link to open the 

Workflow wizard box and view the details of your approval workflow. 

• 
Approver: This is the role (or user) to which the system will route the transaction for 

approval. Click this link to view the details of the user role. 

If the approval policy is set up with multiple levels of approval, such as when you have a 

Tiered amount policy type that requires increasing transaction amounts to progress 
through multiple levels of authority, then the list displays each approver in a separate row, 
ordered from lowest to highest approver level. 

5. 
 Click Done when you are finished previewing approval paths.

recommend that you import those charts as a reference point and use them throughout the steps

Importing 1099 Opening Balances

Set 1099 opening balances for 1099 vendors to ensure that annual reports are correct. 

To import 1099 opening balances manually: 

1. 
In the Year field, type the year for which you are importing 1099 opening balances. 

2. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select the 1099 vendor. 

3. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the entity to which the opening balance applies. 

4. 
In the Form 1099 type column, select the 1099 form type that the vendor receives: MISC, 

NEC, DIV, INT, R, S, PATR, or G. 

5. 
In the Form 1099 box column, select the Form 1099 box. 

6. 
In the Amount column, type the opening YTD balance for the 1099 vendor. 

7. 
Click the Create 1099s balances button to set the opening balances for the 1099 vendors. 

To import 1099 opening balances from a template: 

1. 
Click the Download 1099 template link to download the CSV template. 

2. 
Populate data into the spreadsheet. 

3. 
Save the spreadsheet in CSV format. 

4. 
In the wizard, click the Choose file button to upload the CSV file back into the system. 

5. 
Click the Create 1099s balances button to set the opening balances for the 1099 vendors.

Importing Open A/P Invoices (on page 142)

##### Importing Open A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 156*

Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Importing Open A/P Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Data Import Wizard > Step 3 - Open A/P Invoices`


A/P invoices that were generated in a previous accounting software with an open action should 

be imported to ensure that there isn’t a duplicate entry on the general ledger. 

To import open A/P invoices manually: 

1. 
If you imported a legacy or historical chart of accounts (on page 141), then select the Use 

map check box to import open A/P invoices according to that chart of accounts map. 

Otherwise, leave this check box blank.  

2. 
Select the 1099 check box if the vendor for the transaction is 1099 eligible. Otherwise, leave 

this check box blank. 

3. 
In the Vendor ID drop-down list, select the vendor that is the source of the A/P invoice. 

4. 
In the Invoice date field, select the transaction date for the A/P invoice. 

5. 
In the Due date field, select that date that the payment is due.  

6. 
In the Invoice number field, type the invoice number. 

7. 
In the Invoice amount field, type the amount that is due for the invoice. 

8. 
In the Invoice description field, type any information that you want to store with the A/P 

invoice. This information prints on the Vendor Ledger report but does not print on the check 

or remittance stub. 

9. 
Optionally, in the Reference (optional) field, type a reference number such as a purchase 

order or account number that may be useful in searches or reports on this A/P invoice. This 

number shows on the G/L Details report but does not print on the check or check 

remittance stub. 

10. 
In the Location ID field, select the location associated with the A/P invoice.  

11. 
If you selected the Use map check box in step 1, then type the account number of the 

Legacy account to which you are assigning the expense. If you did not select the Use map 

check box, then select the RealPage account to which you are assigning the expense.  

12. 
In the Amount field, type the amount of the transaction.  

13. 
In the Memo field, type any information regarding the transaction that may be of use in the 

future. 

14. 
Optionally, select the department related to the A/P invoice from the Department 

(optional) drop-down list. 

15. 
Optionally, select the unit related to the A/P invoice in the Unit Number (optional) 

drop-down list.

time. If you select this option, then the Journal field defaults to the CONV--Historical 

Conversion journal. 

• 
Regular journals: Select this option to import account balances from other types of 

journals; for example, when you already use RealPage Accounting and you need to 

consolidate balances from another journal.  

3. 
In the Beginning balance date or Journal date field, type or select the date that you want to 

post to the journal. 

4. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal to which you are importing balances. 

5. 
Select one or more entities from the Locations drop-down list. 

6. 
If you selected the Regular journals option, type a Description for the journal activity. 

7. 
Click the Apply button. 

A list of accounts and entities appears. 

If you selected the Use map check box in step 1, the first column displays the legacy or 
historical accounts that you mapped to system G/L accounts on the Chart of accounts 

map wizard page. 

8. 
Type the beginning balances for accounts and entities into the list as needed. 

If you are importing beginning balances in bulk for multiple entities, click the Download 

beginning balance journals template link to download a CSV template. Populate the 

spreadsheet with the data, save it as a CSV file, and then click the Choose file button to 

upload it back into the system.

Importing External and Historical Journal Entries Using the Data Import Wizard 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Data Import Wizard > Step 6 - External and Historical 
Journals`


Use this procedure to import journal entries when you are using the Data Import wizard to 

import. If you are importing them independently of the Data Import wizard, follow the 

instructions in Importing Journal Entries. 

You can either create journal entries manually or you can import multiple journal entries at the 

same time (import journal entries in bulk). 

To create journal entries manually: 

1. 
If you imported a legacy or historical chart of accounts (on page 141), then select the Use 

map check box to import journal entries according to that chart of accounts map. 

Otherwise, leave this check box blank.  

2. 
Select a journal from the Journal drop-down list for which you are importing journal entries. 

3. 
Type a Description for the journal entry. 

4. 
In the Posting date field, type or select the date that you want to post the journal entry to 

the journal. 

5. 
Optionally, in the Reference no. field, type your own number by which you can reference 

the transaction. 

6. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the entity associated with the transaction. 

7. 
In the Department drop-down list, select the department associated with the transaction. 

8. 
If you selected the Use map check box in step 1, then type the account number of the 

Legacy account associated with the journal entry. If you did not select the Use map check 

box, then select the RealPage account associated with the journal entry. 

9. 
In the Debit field, type the debit amount of the transaction.  

10.

Property Transfer Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > Property Transfer`


Use the Property transfer page to export all of an entity’s activity when you are transferring the 

entity to another PMC. This includes the following data: 

• 
Opening balances 

• 
Monthly activity 

• 
Bank accounts 

• 
Budgets 

• 
Vendors 

• 
1099 opening balances 

• 
Open invoices 

• 
G/L accounts 

The system exports files in the same format required to import data so that you don’t have to 

gather the information from multiple places. You can use the Import tab to import files back into 

the system in a new entity. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

##### Transferring Entity Data to Another Property
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 167*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Transferring Entity Data to Another Property 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > Property Transfer`


The Property transfer page supports transferring an entity’s data between property management 

companies (PMCs).  

This process involves two parties: 

• 
Current PMC (Exporting PMC): Generates and reviews the entity data files. 

• 
New PMC (Importing PMC): Sets up the entity in their system and imports the files. 

The exporting PMC generates files on the Export tab, reviews them, and then sends the finalized 

files to the importing PMC. The importing PMC sets up the entity in their instance of RealPage 

Accounting and completes the transfer using the Import tab. 

Exporting an Entity’s Data (Current PMC) 

To export data for a property transfer: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Configuration section, click the Property transfer menu option. 

The Property transfer page opens on the Export tab. 

3. 
In the Beginning balance date field, type or select the date that the entity’s beginning 

balances were posted to the General Ledger.  

4. 
In the End date field, type or select the date through which you want to export the entity’s 

monthly activity. This date can be up to two years apart from the Beginning balance date. 

5. 
In the Property drop-down list, select the entity whose data you want to export. This is the 

entity that you are transferring to another PMC. 

6. 
In the Budget period drop-down list, select whether you want to export budgets for the 

prior year, current year, or next year. 

7. 
Select the types of files you want to generate: 

• 
Opening balances: Generate a file containing the entity’s opening balances. The file 

will contain opening balances starting from one day before the Beginning balance 

date that you entered. For example, if you entered 1/1/26 as the beginning balance 

date, the file will include opening balances as of 12/31/25. 

If the entity uses a dual accounting method, the system generates separate files for 
both Accrual and Cash. 

• 
Monthly activity: Generate one or more files containing entity activity from the 

Beginning balance date to the End date. You can choose the Net change option to 

export a single file containing the monthly net change for each account or the 

---


<!-- Page 168 -->
Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Transaction detail option to export separate files containing the transaction details for 

each month. 

If the entity uses a dual accounting method, the system generates separate files for 
both Accrual and Cash. For example, say you set the date range from 11/1/25 to 
12/31/25. If you choose the Net change option, the system generates one cash file 
and one accrual file containing the monthly net change for the whole date range. If you 
choose the Transaction detail option, the system generates cash and accrual files 
for each month within the date range (Cash file for Nov 2025, Accrual file for Nov 
2025, Cash file for Dec 2025, Accrual file for Dec 2025). 

• 
Bank accounts: Generate a file containing all of the entity’s checking and savings 

accounts. 

• 
Budgets: Generate a file containing the entity’s budgets for each reporting period 

based on the Budget period that you selected. Budgets exported as balance sheet 

accounts will be the end of period. 

• 
Vendors: Generate a file containing all of the entity’s active vendors, including their 

address and 1099 information.  

• 
1099 opening balances: Generate a file containing the entity’s current balances for 

1099 vendors. 

• 
Open invoices: Select this option to generate a file containing all of the entity’s open 

invoices, including the invoice details. 

• 
G/L accounts: Select this option to generate a file containing all of the entity’s G/L 

accounts. 

8. 
Type the email address that you want to deliver the files to. The system sends separate 

emails for each of the files you selected above. 

9. 
Click the Generate files button in the upper-right corner. 

10. 
After generating the files: 

• 
Review the exported files to confirm completeness and accuracy. 

• 
Send the files to the receiving PMC using your company’s approved method (for 

example, secure email or file transfer). 

These files are required for the importing PMC to complete the transfer. 

Importing an Entity’s Data (New PMC) 

Before you begin, ensure that you have received the required export files from the transferring 

PMC.  

You can import files individually or in any combination. For example, you might import vendors 

and bank accounts first, and then import balances and activity later. Complete only the fields 

required for the files that you are importing. 

---


<!-- Page 169 -->
Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

To import data for a property transfer: 

1. 
Click the Import tab on the Property transfer page. 

2. 
Complete the following common fields: 

• 
Original entity ID: Type the entity ID from the transferring PMC. 

• 
New entity ID: Select the entity you created to receive the transferred data. 

• 
Email results to: Type the email address to notify when the import is complete. 

3. 
Complete the following fields only if they apply to the files you are importing: 

• 
Chart map: Select an existing chart of accounts map as a reference point if you are 

importing opening balances or monthly activity based on a legacy or historical chart of 

accounts. 

• 
Journal: Select the journal to use when importing opening balances and monthly 

activity. 

• 
Beginning balance date: Select the beginning balance date to use when importing 

opening balances and monthly activity.  

• 
1099 year: Type the year to use when importing 1099 opening balances. 

4. 
In the Import files section, upload the files you received from the transferring PMC. You can 

upload one or multiple file types: 

• 
Opening balances 

• 
Monthly activity 

• 
Budgets 

• 
Bank accounts 

• 
Vendors 

• 
Open invoices 

• 
1099 opening balances 

5. 
Click the Import data button. 

---

##### Adding an External Chart Map
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 175*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding an External Chart Map 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > 
 External Chart Maps`


To add an external chart map: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Configuration section, click the 
 Add button next to the External chart maps menu 

option. 

The External chart map page opens on a new, blank page. 

3. 
Type a name for the external chart map. 

4. 
Optionally, type a description of the external chart map. 

5. 
Add or import the chart of accounts used in a previous or additional accounting system. See 

the sections below for instructions. 

Manually Adding an External Chart of Accounts 

To manually add an external chart of accounts: 

1. 
Type the legacy account number in the Legacy account field. 

2. 
Type the legacy account name in the Legacy description field. 

3. 
In the RealPage account drop-down list, select the G/L account to map to the legacy 

account. 

4. 
Click Save to save the external chart map. 

Importing an External Chart of Accounts 

To import an external chart of accounts: 

1. 
Click the Download external chart of accounts template link. 

2. 
Open the downloaded CSV file and fill in the following information for each legacy account: 

• 
Legacy account: Type the legacy account number. 

• 
Legacy description: Type the legacy account name. 

• 
RealPage account: Type the G/L account to map to the legacy account. 

3. 
Save the CSV file. 

4. 
Return to the External chart map page, and then click the Choose file button below Import 

external chart of accounts (CSV). 

5. 
Select the CSV file to upload the chart of accounts into the system.

#### Service Ticket Configuration Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 179*

Chapter 1: Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Service Ticket Configuration Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > Service Ticket Configuration`


Use the Service ticket configuration page to configure intercompany ticketing for your 

organization. Having a ticketing system allows your company’s users to create and submit internal 

service tickets for tasks that need to be completed by your team members. Tickets can be created 

in the Company application in RealPage Accounting or in Spend Management Site Experience. 

You can customize ticket categories to fit your business’s needs, such as: 

• 
Requesting a check to be reissued. 

• 
Adding a bank account for a new property. 

• 
Setting up a vendor for online shopping. 

• 
Posting accrual or reclass journal entries. 

After a ticket is approved, assignees can claim and complete tickets through the Intercompany 

ticketing workbench. The Service Ticket report allows you to monitor open and closed tickets. 

---

Configuring Service Tickets 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > Service Ticket Configuration`


The Service ticket configuration page has two sections to help you configure your company’s 

ticketing system: 

• 
Service ticket settings: Use this section to enable or disable settings for service tickets, such 

as priority levels. 

• 
Ticket categories: Use this section to set up what types of tickets users can submit, who has 

to approve them, and who has to complete them. 

Configuring Service Ticket Settings 

In the Service ticket settings section, enable the following settings as needed: 

• 
Enable reviewer approval: Displays a Reviewer column in the Ticket categories section so 

you can assign a reviewer to ticket categories. If a reviewer is defined for a ticket category, 

then the reviewer must approve any tickets submitted under that category before the ticket 

can be assigned to someone. The reviewer can be an individual user or user role. 

• 
Enable need by date: Displays a Need by date field when users are creating and submitting 

a service request. This is a required field; it is the date the user needs the service request to 

be completed by. 

• 
Enable priorities: Displays a grid to set up priority levels for service tickets. Type a name for 

each priority level in the Priority column—for example, “High,” “Medium,” “Low,” etc. When 

users create a service ticket, they will be required to select a Priority for their request. 

If you enable priorities, you must define at least one Priority. 

• 
Enable accruals: Enables the Accrual ticket category so users can submit requests to post 

journal entries for accruals. 

• 
Enable reclasses: Enables the Reclass ticket category so users can submit requests to post 

journal entries for reclassifications. 

Optionally, you can define one or more Unrestricted users. Unrestricted users are able to select 

any action in the Intercompany ticketing workbench regardless of whether the ticket is in their 

queue. They can approve, claim, and close tickets submitted by anyone even if they were not 

directly assigned to it. 

Configuring Ticket Categories 

In the Ticket categories section, define the types of tickets your users can submit: 

1. 
Type a descriptive label for the Service ticket category. For example, if the category is for 

requesting a check to be reissued, you could label it “Reissue check”. 

---


<!-- Page 182 -->
Configuration

If you enabled accruals or reclasses, then a ticket category will be created for you 
automatically. 

2. 
In the Reviewer drop-down list, select the user or user role required to approve tickets 

submitted under that category. The system will route tickets to the reviewer for approval 

before being assigned to someone. 

This field appears only if you enabled reviewer approval in the 
Service ticket settings section. 

3. 
In the Assigned to drop-down list, select the user or user role to assign to tickets submitted 

under that category. 

4. 
Select the Attachment required check box to require users to include an attachment when 

they submit tickets under that category. 

5. 
Leave the Status as “Active”. 

6. 
Optionally, type any Special instructions you want to include on all tickets of a specific 

category, such as what information is required to process the request in a timely and 

accurate manner. Special instructions appear when adding, viewing, or editing the ticket. 

7. 
Continue adding additional categories as needed. Use the 
 Add and 
 Delete icons to 

add and delete rows.

#### Ledger Sentry Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 186*

Ledger Sentry 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Ledger Sentry Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry`


The Ledger sentry page allows you to set controls and alerts for various actions taken in the 

RealPage Accounting system, providing more control and visibility into daily operations. For 

example, you could create a rule to prevent users from posting invoices more than 30 days in the 

future or prevent them from posting a payment if the vendor’s bank balance cannot absorb the 

amount. You could also set up an alert to notify a group of people when certain user actions 

occur, such as if a user books a manual journal entry to a specific system journal.  

This page has four sections: 

• 
Segment rule set (on page 174): Use this section to add or import segment rules to help 

your company capture more information about specific properties or G/L accounts. 

Segment rules require users to define specific segments when creating journal entries or 

A/P invoices. 

• 
Dimension rule set (on page 179): Use this section to add or import dimension rules to help 

your company capture more information about specific properties or G/L accounts. 

Dimension rules require users to define specific dimensions when creating transactions. 

• 
General rule set (on page 186): Use this section to set up general rules to warn or prevent 

users from taking specific actions. 

• 
Alerts and notifications (on page 188): Use this section to set up alerts and notifications to 

notify a group of people within your organization when transactions meet a specific 

threshold, such as when an invoice has been awaiting approval for X number of days, when 

a bank balance has fallen below X amount, or when an invoice is past due. 

The Ledger sentry is a top-level feature only.

#### Segment Rule Set
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 188*

Ledger Sentry 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Segment Rule Set 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > More > Segment Rule Set`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry > Segment Rule Set`


Segment requirements help your company capture more information about specific properties 

and G/L accounts. Segment rules enable you to specify when a segment type is required when a 

user enters a transaction. The system applies segment rules when a user creates a journal entry or 

an A/P invoice. 

There are two kinds of segment rules: Property and Account. 

• 
A property segment rule associates a property with one or more segments. When a user 

creates a transaction with the property, the user must select the segments that are defined 

in the rule. 

• 
An account segment rule associates a G/L account with one or more segments. When a 

user creates a transaction with the G/L account, the user must select the segments that are 

defined in the rule. 

When you create a rule, you must require at least one segment. You can require up to four 

segments in a rule. 

Segment Rule Components 

A segment rule is made up of the type (account or property), the name of the account or 

property, and the list of required segments. 

Rule Type: Account  
Account # 
Segments required: 1, 2, 3 

Rule Type: Property  
Name of property Segments required: 1 

Every time a user creates an A/P invoice or journal entry associated with one of the properties or 

accounts that have rules, the system requires the user to select the segments required by the rule. 

If the user tries to save the A/P invoice or journal entry without selecting the required segment 

values, then the system displays an error.

#### Dimension Rule Set
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 193*

Chapter 2: Ledger Sentry 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Dimension Rule Set 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry > Dimension Rule Set`


Dimension rules help your company capture more information about specific properties and G/L 

accounts by requiring users to define dimensions when they enter new transactions. The system 

applies dimension rules to all transactions in any application where the dimension is enabled. 

There are two types of dimension rules: Property and Account. 

• 
A property dimension rule associates a property with one or more dimensions. When a user 

enters a transaction for the property, they must also select any dimensions defined in the 

dimension rule. 

• 
An account dimension rule associates a G/L account with one or more dimensions. When a 

user enters a transaction for the G/L account, they must also select any dimensions defined 

in the dimension rule. 

When you create a dimension rule, you must require at least one dimension. You can require up 

to four dimensions in a dimension rule. 

Dimension Rule Components 

A dimension rule has three parts:  

• 
The rule type 

• 
The property or account ID 

• 
The required dimensions. 

Together, the dimension rules make up your company’s dimension rule set. 

When a user creates a transaction for one of the properties or accounts associated with a 

dimension rule, the system requires the user to select the dimensions defined in the rule. If the 

user tries to save the transaction without selecting values for the required dimension fields, then 

the system displays one of the following error messages: 

• 
Location {location ID} requires {dimension name} Dimension in Line #{line number it applies 

to} 

• 
Account {account number} requires {dimension name} Dimension in Line #{line number it 

applies to}

#### General Rule Set
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 200*



##### Setting Up General Rules
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 200*

Ledger Sentry 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

General Rule Set 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry > General Rule Set`


General rules allow you to warn or prevent users from performing an action when specific criteria 

exist. This includes when: 

• 
An invoice date is more than 30 days in the future. 

• 
A void or reversal date is more than 30 days in the future. 

• 
A payment amount is more than the available bank balance. 

• 
Credits are available for a vendor but have not been applied. 

If you select the Warn option, then the system will display a warning message when the user 

takes an action that triggers the rule. The user can bypass the warning at their own discretion. If 

you select the Prevent option, then the system will restrict the user from taking the action 

altogether. 

Setting Up General Rules 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry > General Rule Set`


To set general rules: 

1. 
On the Ledger sentry page, find the General rule set section. 

2. 
Select an option for each condition. 

If invoice date is more than 30 days in the future 

• 
Prevent: Prevent users from entering an invoice date that is more than 30 days in the 

future. The user will receive an error message stating, “You cannot enter an invoice 

date more than 30 days from today.” 

• 
Warn: Warn the user if they enter an invoice date that is more than 30 days in the 

future. The user will receive a warning message stating, “The invoice is more than 30 

days from today.” 

• 
Do nothing: Do not prevent or warn users. 

This rule applies to RealPage Accounting core applications and Spend Management Site 
View.  

If void or reversal date is more than 30 days in the future 

• 
Prevent: Prevent users from voiding or reversing a transaction if the void or reversal 

date is more than 30 days in the future. The user will receive an error message stating, 

“You cannot enter a void date that is more than 30 days from today” or “You cannot 

enter a reversal date that is more than 30 days from today.” 

---


<!-- Page 201 -->
Chapter 2: Ledger Sentry 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Warn: Warn the user if they enter a void or reversal date that is more than 30 days in 

the future. The user will receive a warning message stating, “The void date is more 

than 30 days from today” or “The reversal date is more than 30 days from today.” 

• 
Do nothing: Do not prevent or warn users. 

This rule applies to RealPage Accounting core applications and Spend Management Site 
View.  

If payment amount is more than the available bank balance 

• 
Prevent: Prevent users from submitting a payment request if the payment amount is 

greater than the available bank balance. The user will receive an error message stating, 

“Enter a payment amount that is less than the current bank balance, then try again.” 

• 
Warn: Warn the user if they submit a payment request with a payment amount that is 

greater than the available bank balance. The user will receive a warning message 

stating, “Enter a payment amount that is less than the current bank balance, then try 

again. Click OK to continue the payment.” 

• 
Do nothing: Do not prevent or warn users. 

3. 
If you want to notify users when credits are available for a vendor that have not been 

applied, then select the Notify when credits available are not applied check box. 

4. 
Click Save.

#### Alerts and Notifications
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 202*

Ledger Sentry 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Alerts and Notifications 

You can set up alerts and notifications based on thresholds to notify a group of people in your 

organization when transactions cross that threshold. This includes when: 

• 
A manual journal entry is over XX amount. 

• 
A bank account balance is less than XX dollars. 

• 
An A/P invoice, purchase order, service contract, or subcontract is pending approval for 

more than XX days. 

• 
An A/P invoice is past due. 

• 
A contract is expiring in the next XX days. 

• 
Vendor insurance has expired. 

• 
Vendor insurance is expiring in XX days. 

• 
Petty cash card transactions have been not been submitted in XX days. 

When this occurs, the system will send an email to all users with the selected user role. You can 

assign only one user role per notification rule. 

Default Notification Rules 

The following notification rules are predefined for you using default system roles; however, you 

can edit them or set up additional rules as needed. Add users to these roles if you want them to 

receive notifications.

Setting Up Alerts and Notifications

when new transactions cross that threshold. 

To set up alerts and notifications:

On the Ledger sentry page, find the Alerts and notifications section. 

2. 
In the Rule item column, select the rule type:

If manual journal entry is over XX amount: When you select this option, the system 

will send a single email for each journal entry that meets the criteria. 

• 
If bank account balance is less than XX dollars: When you select this option, the 

system will send a daily email with all bank accounts whose balance is below the 

defined amount. 

• 
If A/P invoice is pending approval for more than XX days: When you select this 

option, the system will send a daily email with all A/P invoices that meet the criteria. 

This option appears only if you have enabled A/P invoice approvals. 

• 
If purchase order is pending approval for more than XX days: When you select this 

option, the system will send a daily email with all purchase orders that meet the 

criteria. This option appears only if you have enabled purchase order approvals. 

• 
If service contract is pending approval for more than XX days: When you select this 

option, the system will send a daily email with all service contracts that meet the 

criteria. This option appears only if you have enabled service contract approvals. 

• 
If subcontract is pending approval for more than XX days: When you select this 

option, the system will send a daily email with all subcontracts that meet the criteria. 

This option appears only if you have enabled subcontract approvals. 

• 
If A/P invoice is past due: When you select this option, the system will send a daily 

email with all A/P invoices that are past due. 

• 
If contracts are expiring in the next XX days: When you select this option, the system 

will send a daily email with all service contracts or subcontracts that meet the criteria. 

• 
If vendor insurance is expired: When you select this option, the system will send an 

email once a week on Thursday with a list of vendors whose insurance has expired. 

• 
If vendor insurance is expiring in XX days: When you select this option, the system 

will send a daily email with a list of vendors whose insurance meets the criteria. 

• 
If petty cash card charges pending submission for XX days: When you select this 

option, the system will send a daily email with a list of petty cash card transactions that 

meet the criteria.

#### Intercompany Ticketing Workbench Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 216*

Ticket Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Intercompany Ticketing Workbench Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ticket Workbench`


The Intercompany ticketing workbench allows team members to complete service requests 

submitted by other users in your organization. Reviewers can approve or decline tickets directly 

from the workbench. If a ticket is approved, the user assigned to the ticket category can complete 

and close the ticket. If a ticket is assigned to a user role, then anyone with that user role can claim 

the ticket to assign themselves to the task. 

Tickets require approval only when approval is enabled for the ticket category. If a ticket doesn’t 
require approval, then the system routes it directly to the assignee user or user role. 

The workbench has two views: 

• 
My tickets: Displays only the tickets that have been assigned directly to you or to your user 

role. 

• 
View all: Displays all open tickets in your company. 

You can filter the workbench and then save it as a custom workbench view using the Save view as 

button. If you want to export the list of tickets to an Excel report, then click the Export to Excel 

button. 

---

##### Filtering the Intercompany Ticketing Workbench
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 218*

Ticket Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Filtering the Intercompany Ticketing Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ticket Workbench`


You can apply filters to target specific service tickets and then save the filters as a preset 

workbench view. 

Filtering the Workbench 

To filter the workbench: 

1. 
Define one or more filter options: 

• 
Submitted from date / Submitted to date: Type or select a date range by which to 

filter tickets. This is based on the date that the tickets were submitted. 

• 
Service ticket number: Type the number of a specific service ticket. 

• 
Status: Select one or more ticket statuses: 

• 
Submitted: The ticket is submitted, but hasn’t been assigned to a user. 

• 
In review: The ticket is submitted and pending approval. 

• 
Working: The ticket is assigned to a user and work is in progress. 

• 
Declined: The ticket was declined and closed. 

• 
Closed: The ticket was closed and marked as complete. 

• 
No action: The ticket was closed with no action taken. 

• 
Submitted by: Select the user who submitted the ticket. 

• 
Assigned to: Select a user or user role to filter by the tickets assigned to them. 

• 
Property: Select one or more properties to view tickets submitted for those properties. 

2. 
Click the Apply button to apply the filters. 

A list of tickets matching the filter criteria appears. 

Saving a Custom View 

To save your workbench filters as a custom view: 

1. 
Apply the desired filters, and then click the Save view as button. 

The Save view as box opens. 

2. 
Type a View name. This is the name that will appear in the Apply view drop-down list. 

3. 
Select the Default check box if you want to make the view the default view when you open 

the workbench. Only one custom view can be set as the default; selecting this option will 

override the current default view. 

Applying a Custom View 

To apply a custom workbench view, select the custom view from the Apply view drop-down list. 

The workbench automatically applies any filters saved in the custom view. 

---



##### Approving or Declining Service Tickets
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 219*

Chapter 3: Ticket Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Editing or Deleting a Custom View 

You can update a custom view to set it as the default view or delete it entirely.  

To update a custom view: 

1. 
Select the custom view from the Apply view drop-down list. 

2. 
Click the Update view button. 

The Save view as box opens. 

3. 
Select the Default check box to set the view as the default view in the workbench, or click 

the Delete the button to delete the view. 

Approving or Declining Service Tickets 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Setup > Ticket Workbench > Approve/Decline`


If you are assigned as a Reviewer for a service ticket category, then any tickets submitted under 

that category will require approval before they can be claimed by or assigned to another user. 

You can approve or decline tickets directly from the Intercompany ticketing workbench. 

Approving a Service Ticket 

There are two ways to approve tickets: 

• 
Click the Approve link in the Actions column. 

• 
Click the View link to open the ticket details, and then click the Approve button on the My 

service tickets page. 

The Status of the ticket will change from In review to Submitted. At this point, the user assigned to 

the ticket can view and complete the request or, if a user role was assigned to the ticket, someone 

with that user role can claim the ticket. 

Declining a Service Ticket 

There are two ways to decline tickets: 

• 
Click the Decline link in the Actions column. 

• 
Click the View link to open the ticket details, and then click the Decline button on the My 

service tickets page. 

The Decline service ticket box opens so you can enter your reason for declining the request. Type 

the Reason, and then click Decline. The Status of the ticket will change from In review to Declined. 

The user who submitted the ticket will be able to see the status change in the My service tickets 

list and can view the ticket details to see the reason it was declined. 

---



##### Claiming a Service Ticket
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 220*



##### Closing a Service Ticket
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 220*

Ticket Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Claiming a Service Ticket 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Setup > Ticket Workbench > Claim`


If a user role is assigned to a ticket category, then anyone with that user role can view the service 

tickets submitted under that category. After a user claims a ticket, they are assigned to complete 

it. If a user is directly assigned to a ticket, then they do not need to claim it. 

To claim a service ticket: 

1. 
Click the Claim link in the Actions column. 

Alternatively, click the View link to open the ticket details, and then click the Claim button. 

2. 
Click OK to confirm. 

The Status of the ticket changes from Submitted to Working, and the system assigns the 

ticket to you to complete. 

What’s Next? 

Closing a Service Ticket (on page 206) 

Closing a Service Ticket 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Setup > Ticket Workbench > Complete`


If a user role is assigned to a ticket category, then anyone with that user role can view the service 

tickets submitted under that category. After a user claims a ticket, they are assigned to complete 

it. If a user is directly assigned to a ticket, then they do not need to claim it. 

When you’ve completed a service request, you can close the ticket and mark it as completed. 

If you want to close a service ticket that you submitted, then see Closing Your Own Service 
Ticket (on page 584 ). 

To close a service ticket: 

1. 
Click the Complete link in the Actions column. Alternatively, click the View link to open the 

ticket details, and then click the Complete button. 

The Close service ticket box opens. 

2. 
Select a Close as option: 

• 
Complete: The request was completed. 

• 
No action: No action was taken. 

3. 
In the Close comment field, type the reason for closing the ticket. 

---


<!-- Page 221 -->
Chapter 3: Ticket Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

4. 
If the ticket is a request to post an accrual or reclassification journal entry, then confirm the 

journal entry so it can be posted to the General Ledger. Scroll to the bottom of the Close 

service ticket box and complete the following fields: 

• 
Post: Select this check box next to each line item that you want to post. You can select 

the check box at the top of the column to select all line items. 

• 
Accrual account: Select the G/L account you want to post the accrual for. This field 

appears only for accrual journal entries. 

• 
Posting date: Type or select a G/L posting date for each line item. If you select 

different posting dates for different line items, the system will create separate G/L 

journal entries. 

5. 
When you are ready to close the ticket, click the Close ticket button. This will trigger the 

following actions: 

• 
The ticket is removed from the workbench. 

• 
If the ticket was a request to post an accrual or reclassification journal entry, then the 

journal entry automatically posts to the General Ledger. 

• 
The status of the ticket changes from Working to Closed or No action. The user who 

submitted the ticket can view the ticket details to see the close comments. This 

information will also be available in the Service Ticket report. 

---



##### Reassigning a Service Ticket to Another User
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 222*

Ticket Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Reassigning a Service Ticket to Another User 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Setup > Ticket Workbench > Reassign`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Service Tickets > My Service Tickets > Edit > Reassign`


If you have the Reassign permission for Service tickets (on page 166), then you can reassign 

service tickets to another user or user role. The Reassign option appears in two locations: 

• 
In the Actions column on the Intercompany ticketing workbench page (link) 

• 
On the My service tickets page when viewing a ticket (button) 

You can’t reassign a ticket after it ’s been closed. 

Reassigning a Service Ticket 

To reassign a service ticket: 

1. 
On the Intercompany ticketing workbench page, click the Reassign link next to a ticket.

### Close Calendar
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 229*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Close Calendar 

This section explains how to use the Close calendar page. 

In This Chapter 

Close Calendar Page .......................................................................................................................... 216

#### Close Calendar Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 230*

Close Calendar 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Close Calendar Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Close Calendar`


Use the Close calendar in RealPage Accounting to automate your month-end close process by 

scheduling reports and close tasks on specific days throughout the year. From this page, you can 

automate the following tasks: 

• 
Closing books for General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and Cash 

Management 

• 
Opening Budget Variance Analysis periods 

• 
Running report groups 

• 
Generating Financial Close Management work papers 

• 
Generating Financial Close Management checklists 

• 
Posting depreciation for fixed assets 

• 
Sending messages 

When you are scheduling close tasks through the calendar, keep in mind that the system executes 

all tasks at 2:00 a.m. CST. For example, if you’re closing your A/P books on the 25th of the month, 

but you still want to allow activity throughout the day, then make sure you schedule the task for 

closing your A/P books on the 26th of the month. 

The Close calendar page has three sections: 

a) Filters: Filter the list of scheduled tasks by a specific month and year. If a task’s As of date 

falls within the selected month and year, then it appears in the list. 

b) Imports: Download a CSV template to import groups of close tasks into the system. 

c) Tasks: Manually enter and edit close tasks. By default, this list displays tasks for the current 

month and year and sorts them by date in descending order. 

---

Before You Begin

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Filtering Close Calendar Tasks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Close Calendar`


By default, the Close calendar displays all close tasks scheduled for the current month of the 

current year. However, you can filter the list by an alternate month and year or clear the filters to 

view all tasks scheduled through the calendar. 

Filtering Close Tasks 

To filter tasks: 

1. 
Select the Year and Month from the drop-down lists.

2.

• 
Task 

•

• 
Notify when complete 

3.

The page refreshes with a list of tasks whose As of date falls within the selected date range. 

Clearing Filters 

To clear or reset all filters, click the Clear button. The filters are set to blank values, and the page 

refreshes to display all previous and future tasks scheduled in the Close calendar.

##### Importing Close Calendar Tasks
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 232*

Close Calendar 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Importing Close Calendar Tasks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Close Calendar`


You can import multiple tasks into the Close calendar using a CSV template. Importing tasks is a 

two-step process: 

• 
Download and fill in the template. 

• 
Upload the template back into the system. 

We recommend downloading a new blank template whenever you import information into 

RealPage Accounting. This is important because the template can be updated at any time, 

especially when a new version of RealPage Accounting is released. An older template might not 

work. 

Downloading the Import Template 

To download the import template for close calendar tasks: 

1. 
On the Close calendar page, click the Download entries form link. 

The system either downloads the CloseCalendarTemplate.xls file or prompts you to open or 

save the file, depending on your browser’s settings. 

2. 
Open the file and fill in the fields required for each task (on page 219): 

• 
Task: Type the name of the task. Valid values include: 

• 
Close Books - GL 

• 
Close Books - AP 

• 
Close Books - AR 

• 
Close Books - CM 

• 
Open Budget Variance Analysis Periods 

• 
Run Report Group 

• 
Generate FCM Work Papers 

• 
Generate FCM Checklist 

• 
Post Depreciation for Fixed Assets 

• 
Send Message 

• 
As of date: Type the date on which to run the task. You can use any valid date format 

(on page 221). 

• 
Location/Location group: Type the location or location group ID to which the task 

applies. 

• 
Notify when complete: Type the user ID or role ID to notify when the task is complete. 

• 
For period: Type the reporting period to which the task applies. 

---


<!-- Page 233 -->
Chapter 4: Close Calendar 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
If the task is Close books, then type the name of the reporting period as it 

appears in the Reporting periods list. 

• 
If the task is Open budget variance analysis periods, Generate FCM work 

papers, or Generate FCM close checklist, then the valid values are “Current 

Period” or “Previous Period”. 

• 
Message: Type the message text to include in the email. 

• 
Report group: Type the name of a report group as it appears in the Report groups list. 

• 
Report group as of date: Type the As of date from which to run the report. 

• 
Budget variance analysis: Type the name of the BVA configuration as it appears in the 

Budget variance analysis configuration list. This will determine the rules that the 

system uses when evaluating budget variances. 

• 
FCM work paper - Preliminary: Type the name of the preliminary FCM work paper you 

want to generate. 

• 
FCM work paper - Final: Type the name of the final FCM work paper you want to 

generate. 

• 
FCM checklist: Type the name of the close or monthly checklist that you want to 

generate and assign tasks for. 

• 
Depreciation date: Type the depreciation date for the fixed assets. You can use any 

valid date format (on page 221). 

• 
Posting date for depreciation: Type the G/L posting date for the depreciation journal 

entries: You can use any valid date format. 

• 
Months to include for depreciation: Type 1 or 2 to specify which months to include in 

the depreciation entries. 

• 
1: Posts only the depreciation for the month specified in the depreciation date. 

• 
2: Includes depreciation for previous months for any fixed assets that have not 

yet been depreciated. 

3. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

Importing Data From the Template 

To import the template back into the system: 

1. 
On the Close calendar page, click the Choose file button, and then select your file. 

2. 
Click the Upload button. 

The Close calendar refreshes with the new tasks.

##### Manually Entering Close Calendar Tasks
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 236*

Close Calendar

Formatting Dates

When you select a date format here, the system attempts to import your file using the selected 

date format. If the system can’t import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to 

discover the date format used in your file and import the data using that date format. 

Manually Entering Close Calendar Tasks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Close Calendar`


You can schedule and edit individual close tasks by manually entering new rows in the Close 

calendar and completing the required fields. To import tasks in bulk, see Importing Close 

Calendar Tasks (on page 218).  

Adding and Scheduling Tasks 

Click the 
 Add icon to add a new task. RealPage Accounting allows you to automate the 

following month-end close tasks: 

• 
Close books (GL, AP, AR, CM) (on page 223): Closes the books for General Ledger, Accounts 

Payable, Accounts Receivable, or Cash Management. If you are closing G/L books, then the 

system will automatically generate KPIs. 

• 
Open budget variance analysis periods (on page 225): Generates the budget variance 

analysis (BVA) periods for each location or location group and adds them to the Budget 

variance analysis locations by period list. The system sends an email to users assigned to 

those periods based on the locations they have access to. 

• 
Run report group (on page 226): Generates the report group based on the default 

parameters set up in the report group and stores it in the My stored reports list in the 

Reports application. 

---


<!-- Page 237 -->
Chapter 4: Close Calendar 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Generate FCM work papers (on page 228): Generates a preliminary or final work paper 

package and adds them to the Work papers list.  

• 
For preliminary work papers, the system automatically includes every report set up in 

the work paper configuration. 

• 
For final work papers, the system automatically includes custom worksheets from 

previous months and retrieves any attachments from those custom worksheets. 

• 
Generate FCM checklist (on page 229): Generates the close checklist or monthly checklist 

tasks and adds them to the Close workbench and Close console. The system sends an email 

to the users assigned to those tasks. 

• 
Post depreciation for fixed assets (on page 231): Posts depreciation journal entries for fixed 

assets to the General Ledger and adds them to the Depreciation batches list. 

• 
Send message (on page 232): Sends a message to a specific user or group of users. 

Each task requires a different set of fields. The Notify when complete field is optional for all 
tasks; when notifications are enabled, the system sends an email to the selected user (or user 
role) when the task is complete. 

Editing Tasks 

You can edit a task up to its As of date. For example, if a task is set up to run as of March 24th, 

then you can still edit that task on March 23rd until midnight. Afterwards, the fields for that task 

will be set to read only. 

The system provides an audit trail (on page 234) for each task so you can track changes made to 

it before the As of date. 

Deleting Tasks 

To delete a task, click the 
 Delete icon next to the task row. This action cannot be undone. 

Completed tasks cannot be deleted. 

---



##### Closing Books
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 238*

Close Calendar 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Closing Books 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Close Calendar`


Create a Close books task to automate the process for closing out your General Ledger, Accounts 

Payable, Accounts Receivable, or Cash Management books. 

To create the task: 

1. 
Click the 
 Add icon to add a new row. 

2. 
In the Task drop-down list, select the Close books task for the books you want to close: 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Close books - GL > General Ledger`



> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Close books - AP > Accounts Payable`


• 
Close books - AR > Accounts Receivable 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Close books - CM > Cash Management`


3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date on which to close the books. 

When you are scheduling close tasks through the calendar, keep in mind that the system 
executes all tasks at 2:00 a.m. CST. For example, if you ’re closing your A/P books on the 
25th of the month, but you still want to allow activity throughout the day, then make sure 
you schedule the task for closing your A/P books on the 26th of the month. 

4. 
In the Location/Location group drop-down list, select the location or location group to 

which the task applies. 

5. 
Optionally, in the Notify when complete drop-down list, select the user or user role to 

notify when the task is complete. 

Make sure you consider each user’s entity restrictions. For example, if you are closing 
books for XYZ Company and the Notify role includes Dana, Kim, and Charlie—but Dana and 
Kim do not have access to XYZ Company—then you should send an email only to Charlie. 

6. 
In the For period drop-down list, select the reporting period to which the task applies. 

7. 
Click Save. 

Run Workflow 

On the As of date, the system executes the Close books task as follows: 

1. 
Close the books. 

2. 
Generate KPIs (General Ledger books only). 

3. 
Send an email notification to the selected user(s). 

4. 
Log the Last run date in the Close calendar.

#### AI Invoice Approvals
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 257*

Chapter 5: AI Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

AI Invoice Approvals 

Some vendors, due to their nature of their work, frequently submit invoices with roughly the same 

amounts. Your company may come to expect a certain number of invoices from that vendor 

within a specific time frame. 

If approvals are enabled for A/P invoices, then each time an invoice is processed, it is routed 

through an approval workflow. AI approvals in RealPage Accounting streamline the approval 

process for A/P invoices by calculating an AI match percentage based on the number of invoices 

you usually receive from a vendor within a specified period. You can set up auto-approvals for 

invoices that are above a specific confidence percentage and below a specific dollar amount. 

Where to View the AI Match Percentage 

To view the AI match percentage, go to the Approval workbench page in RealPage Accounting 

or Spend Management Site Experience and select the A/P invoice view. The confidence level 

appears next to each invoice; hover over the field to view the criteria from which the percentage 

was calculated. 

---


<!-- Page 258 -->
AI Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

The AI match percentage also appears when you view the invoice. 

How the AI Match Percentage Is Calculated 

The confidence percentage is calculated when a new invoice is submitted and then recalculated 

each time the invoice is approved in the approval workflow. The calculation works as follows: 

• 
If the number of invoices within the last XX days equals or exceeds the number defined, 

then the system assigns 50% to the match level. If the number of invoices within the last XX 

days is less than the number defined, then the system assigns 25% to the match level. 

• 
If the invoice is within the invoice variance amount, then the system assigns 25% to the 

match level. 

• 
If a purchase order (PO) is matched to the invoice, then the system assigns 25% to the 

match level. 

---



#### Configuring AI Invoice Approvals
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 259*

Chapter 5: AI Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Configuring AI Invoice Approvals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > AI Invoice Approvals`


Use the AI invoice approval feature to let the system automatically review and approve A/P 

invoices. When you submit a new invoice, the system calculates a confidence percentage for the 

invoice. For an A/P invoice to be approved, it must pass the confidence percentage (AI match) 

that is above a specific threshold and must fall below a specified dollar amount. 

To set up AI Invoice approvals feature for use, you configure the match threshold and the dollar 

amount.  

To configure AI approvals for A/P invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration menu option.  

4. 
Find the AI invoice approvals section. 

5. 
Set the criteria for the system to use to calculate the confidence percentage for an invoice. 

• 
For XX number of days, type the number of days to use in the calculation. 

• 
For Count of invoices posted within XX days, type the number of invoices that the 

vendor needs to have submitted within the time period. 

• 
For Total invoice amount variance percent, type the variance percentage that the new 

invoice must fall within when compared to the average of previous invoices. 

6. 
Select the Calculate check box to have the system calculate the AI Match confidence level 

for new invoices.  

Any invoices submitted before this option is enabled will not have an AI match percentage. 

When you submit a new invoice, the system calculates a confidence percentage for the 

invoice. Each time the invoice is approved in the approval workflow, it recalculates the 

confidence level as a percentage. The calculation works as follows: 

---


<!-- Page 260 -->
AI Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
If the number of invoices within the last XX days equals or exceeds the number 

defined, then the system assigns 50% to the match level. If the number of invoices 

within the last XX days is less than the number defined, then the system assigns 25% 

to the match level. 

• 
If the invoice is within the invoice variance amount, then the system assigns 25% to 

the match level. 

• 
If a purchase order (PO) is matched to the invoice, then the system assigns 25% to the 

match level. 

The default criteria for AI invoice approvals are 90 days, three invoices, and 10% variance. 

7. 
Optionally, select the Auto approve check box to enable automatic approvals based on 

specific thresholds: 

• 
In the first field, type the percent threshold required to auto-approve invoices. For 

example, 90 means the invoice must have at least a 90% AI match percentage. 

• 
In the second field, type the amount threshold required to auto-approve invoices. For 

example, 350 means the invoice amount must be equal to or below $350.00. 

The Auto approve check box appears only if your company subscribes to the Finance Agent. 

You can set up alerts and notifications (on page 188) based on thresholds to notify a group 

of people in your organization when invoices are submitted that cross that threshold. The 

system provides several predefined roles and criteria by default. You can add or edit rules as 

needed to adjust them. 

8. 
Click Save.

#### AI-Invoice Scanning
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 261*

Chapter 5: AI Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

AI-Invoice Scanning 

The AI-Invoice feature automates the process of bringing A/P invoices into the system, creating 

A/P invoice records by reading and extracting key information from the invoice document.  

How It Works 

The AI agent receives invoices when you scan, upload, or email invoices to the system. You can 

scan or upload invoices directly into the Financial Suite or set up an email address for vendors 

and employees to send invoices for AI processing. 

The AI agent scans the document and extracts all relevant information, including the invoice 

number, date, amount, vendor, property, and line-item descriptions.  

To find a vendor in the system that matches the vendor on the invoice, the agent first looks for a 

vendor record with a matching Vendor name. If it doesn’t find a match, then it will look for a 

matching Print as name instead. If it still doesn’t find a match, it will check for a matching vendor 

address. 

After the AI agent processes an invoice, the result is an A/P invoice record. You can view the 

invoice records that the agent created in the AI-invoice queue list. 

Configuration 

Before you can use the AI-Invoice Scanning agent, you must enable the AI-Invoice Scanning 

function and configure its settings. See Configuring AI-Invoice Scanning (on page 248) for more 

information. 

Agent Processing Results 

After configuring AI-invoice scanning, use the following pages to track the progress of invoices 

that have been processed by the AI-Invoice scanning agent: 

• 
AI-Invoice Queue: This page displays a list of all invoices successfully processed by the 

AI-Invoice feature.  

• 
AI-Invoice Upload Audit: This page provides an additional view for administrators to 

monitor which email addresses the invoices are submitted from, what time they’re 

submitted, and who submitted them. 

To monitor the scanned invoice progress, you can add an action card to your Home page for AI 

invoice queue count. To add an action card, see Adding a Finance Agent Action Card to the 

Home Page. 

When the AI Agent Fails to Match an Invoice to a Property 

When an invoice is sent into the AI-Invoice queue and the AI Finance Agent cannot identify the 

property, the AI agent creates invoice but does not assign a property to it. The AI agent places the 

invoice in the AI-Invoice Queue list where the submitter can access it.  

---

grant a user access to these invoices, assign the user the View Invoices with No Property Defined 

permission.

#### AI Contract Scanning
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 264*

AI Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

AI Contract Scanning 

The AI contract scanning feature allows you to define keywords that the AI agent uses to 

automatically identify and extract contract clauses—such as management agreements and vendor 

contracts—so that you don’t have to read through the full document to find the information.  

Configuration 

By configuring keywords on the AI Configuration page, you enable the system to scan uploaded 

contracts and pull out any clauses that contain those terms. This streamlines clause management 

by ensuring that key sections of a contract are captured without manual review. 

After configuring this feature, the extracted data is available in the Contract record, and in the 

Contract Activity report. All information that the AI agent extracted can be edited. 

To use this feature, the contract must be uploaded as a PDF attachment to the contract 
record. 

How It Works 

After you define the keywords, you upload a PDF of a contract into the system. The AI agent 

analyzes the document, locates matching clauses, and extracts them into the system for further 

review or processing. 

---



##### Adding Clauses and Keywords to AI Contract Screening
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 265*

Chapter 5: AI Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

The Clauses tab on the Contract information page displays a list of clauses that you defined on 

the AI configuration page. When a new contract is uploaded, the system automatically scans the 

contract and extracts information surrounding the keywords defined for each clause. 

Adding Clauses and Keywords to AI Contract Screening

#### Document Numbering List
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 272*

Settings 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Document Numbering List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Document Numbering`


The system offers an automatic document numbering feature used to assign unique identifiers to 

new records. 

The system uses numbering plans to assign sequential identifiers, typically when creating new 

records or transactions. The numbering plans, or document sequences, can be composed of 

numbers, letters, and punctuation such as hyphens.  

For instance, in Accounts Receivable, document sequences can be applied to invoices. If you want 

an invoice number to be preceded by the “INV-” prefix, the system will assign a sequential 

number to each new invoice using the prefix that you define (e.g., INV-001, INV-002), making it 

easy to track and organize invoices efficiently. 

Document sequencing is available only for these select transactions and records: 

• 
A/P credit adjustments, A/P debit adjustments, vendor records, and transfer payments in 

Accounts Payable. 

• 
Intercompany billing, A/R invoices, recurring A/R invoices, A/R debit adjustments, A/R credit 

adjustments, and customer records in Accounts Receivable. 

• 
Leases and amenity reservations in Commercial Property Management. 

• 
Ownership records, portal communications, and amenity reservations in Condo and Co-op. 

• 
Purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts in Spend Management. 

This targeted use of sequencing ensures clarity and consistency where it’s most critical, without 

applying it universally across the system. 

Document sequencing is a two-step process. First, you configure the document number 

sequence, or numbering format, and then you assign the document sequence to the type of 

record or transaction.  

You create and manage document sequences from this list. You assign a document sequence to a 

transaction or record from the appropriate application’s configuration page. For example, to 


> **Navigation Path:** `assign a document sequence to A/R invoices, go to Accounts Receivable > Setup >`


Configuration, and then find the Document Sequencing section. 

After a document sequence is configured and assigned, the system automatically creates a 

sequential ID to each new transaction or record, ensuring a smooth and consistent flow of unique 

identifiers. 

By auto-generating IDs instead of having users enter unique IDs for new customers, vendors, and 

other records, the system saves time, adds consistency to the document numbering process, and 

avoids duplication.

#### Document Sequence Information Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 275*

Chapter 6: Settings

Document Sequence Information Page 

On the Document Sequence Information page, you add new sequences. Each sequence stores all 

the information on how to number a transaction or record. 

You choose where to use a specific sequence on the configuration page for Accounts Payable and 

Accounts Receivable. The configuration pages are on the Subscriptions option at the Company > 

Setup menu. Click the application, and then select Configure. For example, you can create a 

numbering sequence for invoices and then update the configuration for Accounts Receivable to 

use the numbering sequence for new invoices. 

After you configure an application for document numbering sequences, use caution when 
changing them. This is especially true when you delete sequences or reset the starting number. 

Best practice for adding a document ID sequence 

We recommend against using leading zeros as part of an ID sequence. IDs with leading zeros can 

cause errors when you import information into your company from Excel because Excel removes 

the leading zero. Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, C0001 for a customer ID.  

If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the column of ID numbers to text format in Excel 

before importing the file content. Excel won’t remove the leading zeros when you save the file. 

Remember to do this every time you use a template to import information that requires IDs.

Type the title the system prints on PDFs of invoice-type documents. In other

We recommend against using leading zeros as part of an ID. IDs with 

leading zeros can cause errors when you import information into your 

company from Excel because Excel removes the leading zero. Use a 

character as a prefix to your ID; for example, C0001 for a customer ID. 

Next number 
Type the number that the system uses for the next document in this 

sequence. The document numbering administrator can use this number for 

troubleshooting. For example, it might otherwise be time consuming for the 

administrator to locate the last invoice to check the number. 

You can reset this number. However, be careful when editing this number 

after you have created documents that already use this sequence. If you

Status

sequence to appear on lists–but you do want to keep it for future 

use–choose Inactive. For example, you create sequences that are relevant 

only to calendar quarters for expense reports such as EXPRPT-1847-2004Q1. 

You may want to make this sequence inactive at the beginning of Q2 when 

the sequence EXPRPT-1847-2001Q2 begins. You may still view inactive 

sequences by clicking the Show Inactive check box in the Document

Email Templates List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Email Templates`


Email templates are an efficient way to automate sending one or more document attachments 

with a standard message to multiple customers and vendors. You can create a variety of email 

templates that can be used for different situations, from sending monthly invoices to sending a 

unique message with your transaction documents during the holiday season. 

You can also customize an email template by adding merge fields to populate your email with 

dynamic data from RealPage Accounting, such as primary and secondary customer email 

addresses, customer name, and more. You can even use HTML markup to create and format the 

message itself. 

The email template process, from creation to delivery, involves: 

• 
Creating an email template. You can use plain text, HTML markup, and merge fields to 

create and customize your email template.  

• 
Assigning the email template to a customer, vendor, or transaction definition after you 

create and save your email template. Every time a user in your company sends an email to a 

particular customer or vendor or for a specific transaction definition, the system 

automatically uses the assigned email template.  

• 
Emailing documents in bulk or one at a time using your assigned email template. You can 

also override the assigned email template at delivery. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to use email templates. 

Application 
Activities/Lists

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

##### Adding an Email Template
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 284*

Settings 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding an Email Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Email Templates`


You can create and customize email templates using text, HTML markup, and merge fields that 

auto-populate when an email is generated based on the email template. Custom fields are not 

supported in email templates. 

To create an email template, click 
 Add next to Email templates. The system opens a blank 

Email template page. 

Filling in Basic Information 

1. 
In the Name field, enter a label that helps you identify the template in drop-down lists. For 

example, if you are creating a template to send a monthly sales invoice, you could name it 

“Sales Invoice-Monthly.”  

2. 
In the Description field, enter text to help describe the template. 

3. 
In the Object name drop-down list, select the type of transaction used for the email 

template. 

4. 
Select the Attachments check box to include all attachments associated with the sales 

transaction in the email. 

5. 
In the Status drop-down list, the default selection is “Active.” If, for any reason, you want to 

make the template inactive, select “Inactive.” 

Filling In Email Addresses 

You can use either or both of the following methods, as needed. 

• 
In the Reply-to and Reply-to name fields, enter an email address and corresponding name 

that the recipient can reply to. This corresponds to the From email address the user sees in 

the Print/Email box when they send an email from a transaction. 

• 
In the Contact lookup drop-down list, select, copy, and paste contact merge fields which 

are automatically replaced with addresses associated with each customer and transaction 

during email generation. For example, if you plan to use this template for multiple emails to 

different recipients, you can enter a contact merge field in the To field. The merge field is 

replaced with your customer’s information when the email is generated.  

Use commas to enter multiple addresses in a single field. 

Filling In the Message Content 

1. 
In the Doc element lookup and Company element lookup drop-down lists, select, copy, 

and paste merge fields which are automatically replaced with transaction information and 

values in the subject line or message content when you generate an email. 

2. 
In the Subject field, enter text that you want to appear in the subject line of each email.
