format the message.  

4. 
If the ENTER key fails to create separate lines in your message, turn of the Enable tab on 

Enter key feature under the Personalize interactive behavior section in Company > All > 

Configuration > My Preferences. If you prefer to leave this option selected, you can create 

separate lines in your email template by manually adding the HTML markup <br> at the 

end of each line.  

5. 
Select the Include logo check box to add your company’s logo to the template, and then 

select your preferred vertical and horizontal logo positions. 

Saving the Email Template 

After completing the necessary fields, click the Save button. You can then assign the template to a 

customer, vendor, or transaction definition.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Email Templates`

##### Customizing the Email Template Message at Delivery
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 286*

Settings 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Customizing the Email Template Message at Delivery 

In some cases, you may have a standard email template that you use each month but want to 

customize it to point out something specific about a month’s billing to a specific customer or 

vendor. However, since email templates are primarily used to efficiently email standard messages 

with key information and document attachments to multiple customers or vendors at once, there 

is no way to change the email message directly when the invoice is being delivered.  

Instead, to send a more personalized message to a specific customer, you can choose between 

two options. 

Option 1 

This solution is recommended for sending customized messages to one or two customers. 

1. 
Create a new email template for that specific customer or vendor. 

2. 
Override the assigned email template when you send the email to your customer or vendor. 

After you finish using the customized template, you can set its status to Inactive to prevent 

others from using it. 

Option 2 

This option is recommended for sending customized messages to many customers or vendors. 

1. 
Type your custom message to your customer or vendor in the Message/Description field of 

the desired transaction.  

By adding the appropriate merge field to your email template, you reference the 

Message/Description specific to the individual transaction. When you send the email using this 

email template, your notes about the specific transaction are included. 

1. 
Include the appropriate merge field in your email template ({!SODOCUMENT.MESSAGE!} or 

{!CONTRACT.DESCRIPTION!}).  

2. 
Override the assigned email template when you send the email to your customer or vendor. 

---

Contact Tax Groups List

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Taxes > Setup > Tax Groups > Contact Tax Groups`


If your company calculates value added taxes (VAT), tax groups offer flexibility in assigning the 

way that transactions involving customers, vendors, and their contacts are taxed. For example, you 

have tax groups that represent different state, provincial, or local taxes. Suppose the Los Angeles 

sales tax is 8% but the San Francisco tax is only 7%. Create two tax groups, one for Los Angeles 

and another for San Francisco. You can then apply one tax schedule to all members in the San 

Francisco group, and another to the members of the Los Angeles group. 

The items on this page vary slightly depending on whether your company is an enterprise or a 
multi-entity shared company. When you edit an item that was created in an entity, your changes 
apply to that entity. After you save your changes, you return to the top level. 

From the Contact tax groups list, you can add, edit, view, or delete a contact tax group. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to contact tax groups. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to contact tax groups.

##### Creating Account Label Tax Groups
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 296*

Settings 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Tax Code Configuration Workflow 

Follow these steps to configure automatic tax charging:  

1. 
Assign permissions for tax codes (on page 281). 

2. 
Create account label tax groups (on page 282) for each tax jurisdiction. 

3. 
Define the tax code groups for the company (on page 283). 

4. 
Create A/R account labels for each tax group (on page 283) to charge your customer. 

5. 
Add tax codes for each tax (on page 284) you need to charge.  

6. 
Check existing A/R account labels (on page 285) for taxes and configure them as needed. 

7. 
Associate each entity with the appropriate tax code groups (on page 285). 

8. 
If a property has leases that are tax exempt, mark the leases. 

Creating Account Label Tax Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > 
 Account Label Tax Groups`


To create an account label tax group: 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select 
 Add next to Account label tax groups. 

3. 
In the Name field, type the name of one type of tax that you want to charge your 

customers. 

4. 
Click the More actions button, and then select Save & New. 

5. 
Repeat steps three and four until you have created all of the tax groups that you will need. 

6. 
Click Save or Cancel to exit the page.

job cost change order approval workflow.

Spend Management application.

Filling In the Journal Entry Approvals Section 

1.

and workflow selection when creating a journal entry.

them. For instructions on using the selection box, see Using the Multi-Select Box.

journal entries to post without going through the approval process.

entries that are created by recurring transactions for approval. Clear the check box to

##### Defining a Default Approver
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 317*

Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Defining a Default Approver 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


You can define a default approver for any transaction type (journal entries, A/P invoices, purchase 

orders, service contracts, subcontracts, job cost change orders, and A/P payments) if you enable 

approvals for that transaction type on the Approval configuration page. A default approver is a 

user that the system automatically assigns to review and approve a transaction when it detects a 

“gap” in the approval configuration. What constitutes a gap differs depending on the transaction 

type: 

• 
If the transaction is a journal entry, A/P invoice, purchase order, service contract, 

subcontract, or job cost change order, the default approver is automatically assigned if the 

user role that was set up as the approver is not assigned to any users, if there is an inactive 

user in the role, or if no one with that role has access to the transaction’s entity. 

• 
If the transaction is an A/P payment, the default approver is automatically assigned if a 

location is not assigned to a workflow for the payment method(s) selected from the 

Payment method drop-down list. 

How It Works 

The process for default approvers works as follows: 

1. 
A new transaction is submitted for approval. 

2. 
The system checks if there is a gap at any point in the workflow. 

3. 
If a gap is detected, a warning message appears at the top of the page to alert the person 

submitting the transaction. Warning messages appear in both RealPage Accounting and 

Spend Management Site Experience. 

4. 
The system notifies the default approver and routes the transaction to them for approval. If 

you are an admin user, a record of this action appears on the Approval history page. 

Defining a Default Approver for Journal Entries, A/P Invoices, Purchase Orders, Service 
Contracts, Subcontracts, and Job Cost Change Orders 

To define a default approver for one of these transaction types: 

1. 
On the Approval configuration page, locate the section for the desired transaction type: 

• 
Journal entry approvals 

• 
A/P invoice approvals 

• 
Purchase orders 

• 
Service contract 

• 
Subcontract 

• 
Job cost 

---


<!-- Page 318 -->
Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

2. 
Select the Enable approval check box to enable approvals for those transactions. 

The Approver assigned if a user is inactive or a user is not present in a role drop-down 

field appears. 

3. 
Select a user or role from the drop-down list to set as the default approver. 

Make sure the default approver does not have any entity restrictions . 

4. 
Click Save to save this configuration. 

When you save the configuration, the system auto-generates a default policy and a default 

workflow for the transaction type in the Approval policy manager and Approval workflow 

lists. Only admin users with the appropriate right can view default policies and workflows. 

Defining a Default Approver for A/P Payments 

To define a default approver for A/P payments: 

1. 
On the Approval configuration page, locate the A/P payments section. 

2. 
Select the Enable payment approval check box to enable approvals for A/P payments. 

The Default approver if no workflow is assigned for the following payment methods 

drop-down list appears. 

3. 
Select a user or role from the drop-down list to set as the default approver. 

Make sure the default approver does not have any entity restrictions . 

4. 
Select one or more payment methods from the Payment method drop-down list. 

The default approver receives A/P payments for approval if a location is not assigned to a 

workflow for the selected payment method(s). 

5. 
Click Save to save this configuration. 

When you save the configuration, the system auto-generates a default policy and default 

workflow for A/P payments in the Approval policy manager and Approval workflow lists. 

Only admin users with the appropriate right can view default policies and workflows.

##### Disabling Auto-Approvals for Transactions
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 320*

Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Disabling Auto-Approvals for Transactions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


You can disable auto-approvals for A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, and A/P 

payments. Auto-approving can occur when: 

• 
A user enters the transaction and is assigned to the first level of approval for that 

transaction. 

• 
A role requires more than one Required approver. 

• 
A transaction requires approval from multiple approval policies, and some of the same roles 

are defined for these policies. When a user who is assigned a specific role approves the 

transaction for that role, the system auto-approves transactions for that role in other 

policies and does not require a second approval from that role. 

To prevent the system from automatically approving transactions in any of the above scenarios, 

select the Disable auto approve check box for that transaction type on the Approval 

configuration page. When auto-approve is disabled, the system will require approval at each step 

in the approval workflow (on page 338). 

If an approval workflow applies to more than one of these transaction types, but you’ve disabled 
auto-approve for only one of the transaction types, then the system will auto-approve for one 
but not the other. 

Disabling Auto-Approvals  

To disable auto-approvals for A/P invoices, purchase orders, or service contracts: 

1. 
On the Approval configuration page, find the section that corresponds with the transaction 
type: 

• 
A/P invoice approvals 

• 
Purchase orders 

• 
Service contract  

2. 
Select the Disable auto approve check box. 

3. 
Click Save. 

Example: Approval Policy with Multiple Required Approvers 

XYZ Company has created an approval policy to route A/P invoices through three levels of 

approval: 

1. 
Property Manager 

2. 
Regional Manager 

3. 
Accounting Clerk 

---


<!-- Page 321 -->
Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Two of these levels—the Property Manager and Accounting Clerk—require two different users 

with that role to approve an invoice before it can move to the next level.  

Someone enters an A/P invoice that triggers the approval workflow. The following users have the 

Property Manager role and receive a notification that an invoice is pending approval: 

• 
Charlie 

• 
Dana 

• 
Kim 

The first Property Manager to approve the invoice is Charlie. The second is Kim. 

The invoice moves to the second level and is approved by a Regional Manager. 

The invoice moves to the third level and requires approval by two Accounting Clerks. The 

following users have the Accounting Clerk role and receive a notification that an invoice is 

pending approval: 

• 
Charlie 

• 
Kiran 

• 
Lee 

• 
Quinn 

• 
Sasha  

Normally, because Charlie has already approved the invoice at the first level, the system would 

auto-approve the invoice for him at the third level. However, the company has opted to Disable 

auto approve for A/P invoices, so the invoice still requires approval from two Accounting Clerks. 

---



##### Automatically Advancing A/P Invoices and Purchase Orders to the Next Approver After XX Days
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 322*

Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Automatically Advancing A/P Invoices and Purchase Orders to the Next Approver After 
XX Days 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


You can configure approvals so that A/P invoices and purchase orders automatically advance to 

the next approver if they are not approved within a set number of days. This prevents transactions 

from getting held up in the approval workflow. The system will continue skipping approvers until 

the invoice or purchase order reaches the final approver. The last person will not be skipped to 

ensure that at least one person reviews the transaction before it gets posted. 

To enable this feature: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval configuration menu option. 

The Approval configuration page opens. 

3. 
In the A/P invoice approvals and/or Purchase orders section, select the Advance to next 

approver after XX days if the approver has not approved it check box. 

4. 
Type the number of days that the system should wait before advancing the invoice or 

purchase order to the next approver. For example, if you set the threshold to 4 days, then 

the invoice or purchase order will move to the next approver if it is not approved within four 

days. 

5. 
Click the Save button at the top of the page. 

Returning an Invoice or Purchase Order to an Approver Who Was Skipped 

You can send an A/P invoice or purchase order back the previous approver even if that approver 

was automatically skipped. See Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver (on page 

372).

#### Approval Policy Manager List
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 332*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 332*

Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Approval Policy Manager List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`


The Approval policy manager list is a central location where you can manage your system’s 

approval policies. When new transactions are entered, the system compares them against the 

policies to determine the approval’s route. If the details of the transaction (amount, vendor, G/L 

account, etc.) match a policy, then the system assigns the approver(s) set in that policy. You can 

apply approval policies to journal entries, A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, 

subcontracts, job cost change orders, A/P payments, and purchase order change orders.  

Use this list to view and manage the existing approval policies. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add new approval policies. 

• 
Edit existing approval policy details. 

• 
View existing approval policy details. 

• 
Export the list of approval policies. 

• 
Use the list controls to sort, search, and create custom views of the list. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Accounting auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver. Default policies and workflows are visible only to admin 
users. The system uses these default policies and workflows only under certain conditions; see 
Defining a default approver (on page 302 ) for more information. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage approval policies. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Work Flow Approvals 
Setup 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

##### Adding Approval Policies
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 333*

Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding Approval Policies 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > 
 Approval Policy Manager`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > 
 Approval Policy Manager`


To add an approval policy: 

1. 
In the Policy type drop-down list, select the approval policy type. The available types 

include: 

User: Use this policy type to send all transactions to a specific user or role. You can combine 

this policy with one or more other policies that are based on other criteria in the approval 

workflow. 

Amount: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are based on 

the amount of the transaction or change order. The system sends transactions of the 

amount you enter (or higher) to the selected approvers. Amount policies recognize the 

approver level of the person submitting the transaction or entering the change order; the 

system auto-approves (on page 328) transactions up to the submitter’s level in the approval 

hierarchy. 

Tiered amount: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are 

based on the amount of the transaction or change order. Each approver has a limit to the 

amount he or she can approve. When a transaction or change order comes in that is over an 

approver’s limit, each approver must approve it to move the transaction to the next level. 

Tiered amount policies recognize the approver level of the person submitting the 

transaction or entering the change order; the system auto-approves (on page 328) 

transactions up to the submitter’s level in the approval hierarchy. 

Vendor: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that include a specific 

vendor. The system sends all transactions for the selected vendor to the designated 

approver or approvers. 

Vendor type: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that include a 

specific vendor type. The system sends all transactions for the selected vendor type to the 

designated approver or approvers. 

G/L account: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with 

a specific G/L account, such as Travel and Entertainment. The system sends all transactions 

tagged with a G/L account or G/L account range to the selected approver or approvers. 

Job: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with a specific 

job. 

Job type: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with a 

specific job type. 

---


<!-- Page 334 -->
Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

If you do not see Job and Job type policy types, your company may not have enabled the Job 

Cost application. 

Cost code: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions with a specific cost 

code. 

Accounting reviewer: Use this policy type to collect all A/P invoices and put them in an A/P 

invoice approval queue. The invoices must be approved before they can be posted. After 

creating this policy type, apply the policy to a workflow, and then assign the workflow to the 

desired properties. 

Journal type: Use this policy type to collect all journal entries for a journal, and then put 

them in a journal entry approval queue. The journal entries must be approved before they 

can post to the General Ledger. After creating this policy type, apply the policy to a 

workflow, and then assign the workflow to the desired properties. 

Payment method: Use this policy type to have the system check for A/P payments made 

through a specific payment method. The system sends all payments for the selected 

payment method to the designated approver or approvers. 

Bank account: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are 

associated with a specific bank account. The system sends all transactions for the selected 

bank account to the designated approver or approvers. 

2. 
In the Policy name drop-down list, type a name that describes the policy’s purpose. 

Filling in the Approval Routing and Limits Section 

The Approval routing and limits columns differ depending on the policy type. 

Follow the instructions for the policy type you selected: 

User 

To create an approval policy that sends all approvals to the same person or role: 

1. 
In the Role/user column, select the role or user that you want to approve all transactions 

that require approvals. 

2. 
In the Require approvers drop-down list, select the highest level of approval required for 

transactions. 

3. 
Click Save. 

Amount 

To create a policy based on the amount of the transaction: 

1. 
In the Role/user drop-down list, select the role or user that you want to approve all 

transactions that meet the amount threshold. 

---


<!-- Page 335 -->
Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

2. 
In the Amount from text field, type the lowest amount of a cost that requires transactions 

to be approved. 

3. 
In the Amount to text field, type the highest amount that these approvers are authorized to 

approve. 

4. 
In the Require approvers drop-down list, select the highest level of approval required for 

transactions. 

5. 
Click Save. 

When you create an Amount policy for a job cost change order (JC) or purchase order change 
order (POCO), the approval policy is triggered by the change amount, not the total amount of the 
transaction. 

Tiered amount 

This type is most often used with increasing costs. Typically, the higher the amount of the 

transaction, the higher the approver’s rank is. 

To create a policy based on the amount of the expense, with tiers of amounts: 

1. 
In the Role/user drop-down list, select the role or user that you want to approve all 

transactions that meet the amount threshold. The first role or user should be a low-level 

approver. 

2. 
In the Amount from and Amount to text fields, type the lowest amount range that requires 

approval. 

3. 
Click the 
 Add icon to add another row. 

4. 
Repeat the three steps to add additional tiers, increasing the user or role and amounts with 

each row, or tier. 

5. 
Click Save. 

When you create a Tiered amount policy for a job cost change order (JC) or purchase order 
change order (POCO), the approval policy is triggered by the change amount, not the total 
amount of the transaction. 

Vendors 

To create a policy for one vendor:  

1. 
In the Role/user drop-down list, select a role or a specific user who you want to approve 

vendor records. 

2. 
In the Vendor from drop-down list, select a vendor name that you always want to undergo 

approval. The system fills in the Vendor to field with the same name.  

3. 
In the Require approvers drop-down list, select the levels of approval that the vendor must 

go through (1-4). 

---


<!-- Page 336 -->
Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

4. 
Click Save. 

To create an approval policy for a range of vendors: 

1. 
In the Role/user drop-down list, select a role or a specific user who you want to approve 

vendor records. 

2. 
In the Vendor from drop-down list, select the beginning vendor in the list of vendors. 

3. 
In the Vendor to drop-down list, select the ending vendor in the range of vendors. 

4. 
In the Require approvers drop-down list, select the levels of approval that the vendor must 

go through (1-4). 

5. 
Click Save. 

Vendor types 

To create a policy based on vendor type: 

1. 
In the Role/user drop-down list, select a role or a specific user who you want to approve 

vendor records. 

2. 
In the Vendor type drop-down list, select the type of vendor that should always go through 

approval. 

3. 
In the Require approvers drop-down list, select the levels of approval that the vendor must 

go through (1-4). 

4. 
Click Save. 

G/L account 

To send all transactions through approval when they are tagged with a specific G/L account: 

1. 
In the Role/user drop-down list, select the role or user that you want to approve all 

transactions that are tagged with a specific G/L account. 

2. 
In the G/L account from drop-down list, select the G/L account that is to flag transactions 

for approval.  

For example, choose 6700.016--Miscellaneous as the G/L account to ensure that anything 

tagged as Miscellaneous goes through an approval process. 

The system fills in the G/L account to with the same G/L account.  

3. 
In the Require approvers drop-down list, select the highest level of approval required for 

transactions. 

4. 
Click Save. 

To approve all transactions that are tagged within a range of G/L accounts: 

---


<!-- Page 337 -->
Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

1. 
In the Role/user drop-down list, select the role or user that you want to approve 

transactions based on a range of G/L accounts. 

2.

##### Auto-Approving Transaction Amounts Through the Submitter Level
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 343*

Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Auto-Approving Transaction Amounts Through the Submitter Level 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`


If an approval policy is based on the amount of a transaction (the policy type is set to Amount or 

Tiered amount), then RealPage Accounting will automatically approve transactions up to the 

submitter’s level of approval. This means that if the user who submitted the transaction is higher 

in the approval hierarchy, the system auto-approves the lower levels. For example, a CFO who 

enters a transaction in a multi-level approval workflow does not need approval from approvers at 

lower levels, such as a Property Manager or Regional Manager. 

Example 1: Amount Policy 

XYZ Company has set up an Amount policy to require approval for transactions over $500.00. The 

policy designates four (4) levels of approval—Property Manager, Regional Manager, Asset 

Manager, and CFO—for four (4) different amount ranges. The image below illustrates this policy. 

A user with the Regional Manager role is entering a new A/P invoice. The system can 

auto-approve invoices up to the Regional Manager’s amount range. For example: 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $600.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice instead of routing it to the Property Manager because the Regional Manager is 

higher in the approval hierarchy than the Property Manager. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $2,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice instead of routing it to the Regional Manager role because the Regional Manager is 

the one who submitted the transaction. 

---


<!-- Page 344 -->
Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $3,000.00, then the Asset Manager must 

approve the invoice because the amount is above the Regional Manager’s approval limit. 

Example 2: Tiered Amount Policy 

In an alternate scenario, XYZ Company has set up a Tiered amount policy to require approval for 

transactions over $500.00. The policy designates four (4) levels of approval—Property Manager, 

Regional Manager, Asset Manager, and CFO—for four (4) different amount ranges. Unlike the 

Amount policy, the Tiered amount policy does not route transactions directly to the approver 

assigned to the amount range. Instead, the transaction must be approved in tiers, starting from 

the lowest level and progressing to the highest level required for the transaction amount. 

A user with the Regional Manager role is entering a new A/P invoice. The system can 

auto-approve invoices up to the Regional Manager’s amount range. For example: 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $600.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for the Property Manager tier because the Regional Manager is higher in the 

approval hierarchy than the Property Manager. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $2,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for both the Property Manager and Regional Manager tiers. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $3,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for the Property Manager and Regional Manager tiers; however, the Asset Manager 

must still approve the invoice.

##### Adding Approval Workflows
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 354*

Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding Approval Workflows 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Approval Workflow`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > 
 Approval Workflow`


You can only add a new approval workflow from the workflow list view. If you do not see the 
Add 
button, click the Flipview button. 

To add an approval workflow: 

1. 
In the Name field, type a name that describes the purpose of the workflow; for example, 

“Job Approvals”. Workflow names cannot exceed 60 characters and cannot include any 

special characters except en dashes (–) or underscores (_). 

2. 
In the Transaction section, select the check box for each type of transaction this workflow is 

going to contain. Only the transactions for which approvals are enabled appear in this list.  

• 
Account payable invoice (AP) 

• 
Purchase order (PO) 

• 
Job cost transaction (JCT) 

• 
Job cost change order (JC) 

• 
Service contract (SC) 

• 
Subcontract (SUB) 

• 
eInvoice (EI) / oInvoice (OI) 

• 
Journal entry (JE) 

• 
Corporate invoice (CI) 

• 
Payment (PYMT) 

• 
Purchase order change order (POCO) 

The following workflow types apply to A/P invoices: 

• 
Distribution (D): This option appears only if the Investor Tracking application is 

enabled and A/P invoice approvals are enabled. If selected, then invoices created from 

a distribution will go through the approval workflow before being posted. 

• 
Petty cash reimbursement (PCR): This option appears only if Debit cards for petty 

cash is enabled and A/P invoice approvals are enabled. If selected, then invoices 

created from a card transaction will go through the approval workflow before being 

posted. 

You can apply a workflow to multiple types of transactions or create a separate workflow if 
you want to apply different policies to different types. However, you cannot combine the 

Journal entry, Payment, or Purchase order change order selections with other transaction 
types. 

---


<!-- Page 355 -->
Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Selecting the Policies 

1. 
In the Policy name column, select the first policy to add to the workflow. The system 

completes the policy type column. Click the link to view the policy’s details. 

2. 
Click the Override check box if you want the policy to be an override. 

When selected, this policy is the only policy that is followed when the criterion is met. All 

other policies are discarded, and the policy will be the only approval required by the 

selected properties. 

The system applies the approval policies in the order they appear in the workflow’s Policies 
list. 

Selecting the Properties 

Click the Select button and choose the properties that you want to use this approval workflow. 

For help, see Using the Multi-Select Box. 

If workflows are not assigned to a property, they are visible for all properties. The workflows that 
are not assigned to a property are available for selection if you choose to assign a workflow while 
entering a transaction. 

Defining Conditions 

You can set up conditions to determine whether transactions require approval. The system applies 

the workflow policies to a new transaction only when the conditions are met. 

This section is optional. 

1. 
Select the Enable conditions check box to enable conditions for the approval workflow. 

A blank list appears for you to choose the criteria that you want to apply to the workflow. 

2. 
Select the Filter condition: 

• 
All (AND): Select to run the approval workflow when all conditions are met. 

• 
Any (OR): Select to run the approval workflow when any condition is met. 

• 
Expression: Select when you want to write an expression, a combination of AND and 

OR logic that determines whether to run the approval workflow. 

3. 
In the Policy type column, select a policy type that you want to use for a condition’s test. 

The following policy types are available to use in a workflow condition: 

• 
G/L account 

• 
G/L account group 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Vendor type 

• 
Amount 

---


<!-- Page 356 -->
Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Job 

• 
Job type 

• 
Journal type 

• 
Department 

When Payment is the selected transaction, then the policy type drop-down list also 

includes: 

• 
Payment method 

• 
Bank account 

The following options are not approval policy types but can be used when defining 

conditions for approval workflows:  

• 
Submitter 

• 
Submitter role 

Submitter conditions set criteria for approval workflows based on the user (or user role) who 

submitted the transaction. For more information, see Submitter Conditions in Approval 

Workflows (on page 348). 

4. 
In the Operator column, select the logical expression that you want to use to evaluate the 

condition: 

• 
Equal to (IN): The condition is true when the policy type is equal to (or in the range of) 

the From and To criteria. 

• 
Not equal to (NOT IN): The condition is true when the policy type is not equal to (or 

not in the range of) the From and To criteria. 

• 
Within: The condition is true when the G/L account defined in the policy is in the 

selected account group in the From drop-down list. This operator is available only with 

the G/L account group policy type. 

5. 
In the From and To columns, select the criterion or range of criteria. 

Example of a Condition 

If the amount is between $150 and $999, then the condition is true. 

6. 
Continue adding new conditions to the list as needed, especially if you are building 

conditions for an expression.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Click 
 Add to add another row. 
Click 
 Delete to delete a row. 

7. 
If you selected Expression, type an expression to combine AND and OR logic for your 

conditions: 

Because an expression uses the row numbers in the conditions list, you write the 
expression last. 

Expression Examples 

(1 AND 2) OR (2 AND 3) 

If the first two conditions both evaluate to true OR if the second and third conditions both 

evaluate to true, then the approval workflow runs. 

(1 AND 3) OR 2 

If the first and third conditions both evaluate to true or if the second condition evaluates to 

true, then the approval workflow runs. 

8. 
Click the Save button to save the workflow.

##### Defining Approval Workflow Conditions
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 360*

Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Defining Approval Workflow Conditions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > 
 Approval Workflow`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > 
 Approval Workflow`


You can set up conditions to determine whether or not transactions require approval. When a 

new transaction is entered, the system first evaluates whether these conditions are met; only then 

does it apply the workflow policies to the transaction. If the conditions are not met, then the 

system does not apply the workflow policies to the transaction. 

To define workflow conditions, go to the Conditions section on the Workflow wizard page: 

1. 
Select the Enable conditions check box to enable conditions for the approval workflow. 

A blank list appears for you to choose the criteria that you want to apply to the workflow. 

2. 
Select the Filter condition: 

• 
All (AND): Select to run the approval workflow when all conditions are met. 

• 
Any (OR): Select to run the approval workflow when any condition is met. 

• 
Expression: Select when you want to write an expression, a combination of AND and 

OR logic that determines whether to run the approval workflow. 

3. 
In the Policy type column, select a policy type that you want to use for a condition’s test. 

The following policy types are available to use in a workflow condition: 

• 
G/L account 

• 
G/L account group 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Vendor type 

• 
Amount 

• 
Job 

• 
Job type 

• 
Journal type 

• 
Department 

When Payment is the selected transaction, then the policy type drop-down list also 

includes: 

• 
Payment method 

• 
Bank account 

The following options are not approval policy types but can be used when defining 

conditions for approval workflows:  

• 
Submitter 

---


<!-- Page 361 -->
Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Submitter role 

Submitter conditions set criteria for approval workflows based on the user (or user role) who 

submitted the transaction. For more information, see Submitter Conditions in Approval 

Workflows (on page 348). 

4. 
In the Operator column, select the logical expression that you want to use to evaluate the 

condition: 

• 
Equal to (IN): The condition is true when the policy type is equal to (or in the range of) 

the From and To criteria. 

• 
Not equal to (NOT IN): The condition is true when the policy type is not equal to (or 

not in the range of) the From and To criteria. 

• 
Within: The condition is true when the G/L account defined in the policy is in the 

selected account group in the From drop-down list. This operator is available only with 

the G/L account group policy type. 

5. 
In the From and To columns, select the criterion or range of criteria. 

Example of a Condition 

If the amount is between $150 and $999, then the condition is true. 

6. 
Continue adding new conditions to the list as needed, especially if you are building 

conditions for an expression. 

Click 
 Add to add another row. 
Click 
 Delete to delete a row. 

---


<!-- Page 362 -->
Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

7. 
If you selected Expression, type an expression to combine AND and OR logic for your 

conditions: 

Because an expression uses the row numbers in the conditions list, you write the 
expression last. 

Expression Examples 

(1 AND 2) OR (2 AND 3) 

If the first two conditions both evaluate to true OR if the second and third conditions both 

evaluate to true, then the approval workflow runs. 

(1 AND 3) OR 2 

If the first and third conditions both evaluate to true or if the second condition evaluates to 

true, then the approval workflow runs.

##### Submitter Conditions in Approval Workflows
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 363*

Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Submitter Conditions in Approval Workflows 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > 
 Approval Workflow`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > 
 Approval Workflow`


You can set up submitter conditions for approval workflows based on the user (or user role) who 

submitted the transaction. These conditions can be used to: 

• 
Apply the workflow only when a specific user or user role—such as a President or 

CFO—enters a transaction.  

• 
Apply the workflow to every user except a specific user or group of users. 

To define submitter conditions, set the Policy type of the condition (on page 346 ) to 
“Submitter ” or “Submitter role ”. 

Example 1 

The approval workflow should apply only when Kim Johnson enters a transaction. 

Set up the condition as follows: 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

• 
From: Kim Johnson 

• 
To: Kim Johnson 

If you are specifying a single user, make sure to set the From and To fields to the same user. 

Example 2 

The approval workflow should apply only when Kim Johnson or Alex Garcia enters a transaction. 

Set up the condition as follows: 

Row 1 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

---


<!-- Page 364 -->
Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
From: Kim Johnson 

• 
To: Kim Johnson 

Row 2 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

• 
From: Alex Garcia 

• 
To: Alex Garcia 

If you are specifying multiple users or roles, make sure to set the Filter condition to “Any (OR)”. 
This tells the system that the condition is met if Kim Johnson or Alex Garcia enter a 
transaction. 

Example 3 

The approval workflow should apply to every user who enters a transaction except the CFO. 

Set up the condition as follows: 

• 
Policy type: Submitter Role 

• 
Operator: Not equal to (NOT IN) 

• 
From: CFO 

---

type. Click the link to review the policy details. 

Override 
Select the check box if this policy is to override any other policies. 

Properties Section 

Property 
Select one or more properties to which this workflow should apply. 

When you submit a new transaction, the selected properties are the first 

criteria that the system uses to look up workflow rules. If the system 

finds a workflow, then the transaction is compared to the policies (and, if 

enabled, conditions) to determine which approvers to assign to the 

transaction. 

Conditions Section 

Enable conditions

Filter conditions

• 
All (AND): The workflow applies when all conditions in this 

section are met. 

• 
Any (OR): The workflow applies when any condition in this 

section is met. 

• 
Expression: The workflow applies when conditions are met 

according to the written expression. An expression is a 

combination of AND and OR logic used to string multiple 

conditions together. Because an expression uses the row 

numbers from the conditions list, you write the expression after 

you define your conditions.

##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 370*

Approvals

Approval Workbench - View All 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Subscriptions 

Your company must subscribe to the Company application and at least one of the following 

applications. Choose the appropriate application for the type of approval workflow that you need. 

• 
Accounts Payable: Subscribe to the Accounts Payable application to use the approval 

process with A/P invoices, A/P payments, and expense reports. Approvals of new and 

changed vendors also requires you to subscribe to the Accounts Payable application. 

• 
Spend Management: Subscribe to the Spend Management application to use the approval 

process with purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. 

• 
General Ledger: Subscribe to the General Ledger application to use the approval process 

with journal entries. 

• 
Job Cost & Reserves: Subscribe to the Job Cost & Reserves application to use the approval 

process with job cost change orders.

Journal entry

Approving and Declining Transactions 

See the How to Get Here (on page 358) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench.  

This page has two views, View All and My Approvals. You must be in the Approval Workbench - 

My Approvals view to approve and decline transactions. If you are on the Approvals Workbench 

- View All view, click the My Approvals button to change to the My Approvals view.  

From the My Approvals view, you can approve or decline transactions individually or in bulk. If 

you are reviewing A/P invoices, then you can use the Review and approve button to quickly 

approve or decline invoices back-to-back (on page 367). 

When you approve a transaction, the system looks up the next approver. If the next approver 
previously approved the transaction, then the system sets the status of the transaction to 
Approved. 

Approving One Transaction 

To approve one transaction: 

1. 
Click the Approve link. 

The Approve [transaction type] box opens. 

2. 
Optionally, in the Comments box, type a comment. 

3. 
Click the Approve button. 

Approving Multiple Transactions 

This method does not allow you to enter a comment about why you are approving these 
transactions. 

To approve multiple transactions:

From the Approval Workbench - My Approvals page, select the check box for each 

transaction that you want to approve, and then click the Approve button.

1. 
Click the Decline link. 

The Decline [transaction name] box opens. 

2. 
In the Reason box, type an explanation for why you declined the transaction.

##### Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 381*

Chapter 7: Approvals

•

You also have the option to close and delete declined purchase orders to remove them from your

Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices 

See the How to Get Here (on page 358) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

When the Approval workbench is filtered by A/P invoices, an additional button appears in the 

upper-right corner labeled Review & approve. This button allows you to quickly open and review 

invoices in the order they appear in the approval queue.  

To review and approve A/P invoices: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Approval workbench. 

3. 
Select the A/P invoice option. Set any other filters as needed. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. The system filters the list so that it shows only A/P invoices. 

5. 
Click the Review & approve button. The A/P invoice page opens. If the A/P invoice has an 

attachment and you have enabled the image viewer, the attachment displays in a separate 

window. If not, the invoice image will show on the same page as the invoice. 

If the Review & approve button does not appear, there are no A/P invoices in queue to 
approve. 

6. 
Review the A/P invoice. You can also edit the invoice at the same time. 

7. 
Click one of the buttons: 

• 
Approve & next: Approve the current A/P invoice, and then have the system display 

the next A/P invoice to evaluate. If you made any changes to the invoice, your changes 

are saved and the invoice is routed to the next person for approval. 

• 
Approve & next > Next: Skip the current A/P invoice and display the next A/P invoice 

in your queue. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

---



##### Exporting Transactions to Excel
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 382*

Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Decline & next: Decline the A/P invoice, and then display the next A/P invoice to 

evaluate. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Add approver: Add someone who you think should approve the A/P invoice. Any 

changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Send back: Send the invoice back to the previous approver. Any changes you made to 

the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Done: Close the approval queue. 

8. 
Click the Done button to exit the review and approval process. 

When an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through approvals, and then gets posted, 
RealPage Accounting sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status from 

Pending to Approved. This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the 
invoice. We also send updates to OpsMerchant when the eInvoice is paid or voided, along 
with the payment details. 

Exporting Transactions to Excel 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Workbench`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench`


You can export transaction data from the Approval workbench or Spend management 

workbench to an Excel file. The data included in the file depends on the columns that you have 

enabled in the workbench. 

To export data using the Export to Excel button: 

1. 
Click the Export to Excel button in the upper-right corner of the approval queue. 

The Excel file downloads with any column data configured in the workbench. 

2. 
In the Save as box, name the Excel file, and determine a file location for the exported file. 

3. 
Click Save.

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 383*

Chapter 7: Approvals

Saving a Custom Workbench View 

You can save your workbench filters and selections as a view for settings that you use regularly. 

After saving a view, you can save it as your default view, or load it from the Apply view 

drop-down list.  

Creating a View 

To save your workbench settings as a view: 

1. 
In the workbench, set up the filters that you want to save. 

• 
Select a transaction type. 

• 
Select a date, property, or vendor that you frequently access. 

2. 
Click the Save view as button. 

3. 
Type a name for these selections, such as “A/P invoices for Alpha Properties.” 

4. 
If you want the view to be applied whenever you open the workbench, select the Default 

check box. You can also apply the view as needed by selecting it in the Apply view 

drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

You can also manage the views of the Approvals workbench in the Accounts Payable application 
by using the Approval Workbench Views option. 

Updating Views 

1. 
In the workbench, select the view that you want to change from the Apply view drop-down 

list. 

2. 
Make the desired changes to the filters and settings. 

3. 
Click the Update View button.

Approvals

Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver 

See the How to Get Here (on page 358) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

Some transactions require approvals from multiple levels. If a transaction pending your approval 

was approved by someone else, you can send the transaction back to that approver instead of 

declining the transaction outright. 

To send a transaction back to the previous approver: 

1. 
On the Approval workbench - My approvals page, click the Send back link in the Send 

back column next to the transaction. 

The Send back box opens. 

2. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

3. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transaction no 

longer appears in your queue. 

Sending Back Multiple Transactions 

To send back multiple transactions to the previous approver: 

1. 
From the Approval workbench - My approvals page, select the check box next to each 

transaction that you want to send back to the previous approver. 

2. 
Click the Send back link in the Send back column next to any of the transactions that you 

selected. 

The Send back box opens. 

3. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

4. 
Select the additional approver from the Additional approver drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transactions no 

longer appear in your queue. 

Viewing an Attachment for a Transaction 

See the How to Get Here (on page 358) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

To view an attachment for a transaction in the approval queue: 

1. 
Click the 
 icon in the Actions column next to the transaction. 

2. 
Click the Open button to open the file. You may have to open the file in a separate program 

to view its contents.

1.

information. 

Including Declined Transactions in the Approval Workbench 

See the How to Get Here (on page 358) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Declined transactions are not included in the approval workbench by default. 

To include declined transactions:

Filter (on page 359) the Approval workbench as needed. 

2. 
Select the Include declined check box to include declined transactions. 

3. 
If you want to make this the default setting, then you can save a new custom view (on page 

368) in the workbench and set it as the Default view.

#### Approval History List
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 407*

Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Approval History List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 394) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Use this page to review a transaction’s approval history. This page displays when you click a status 

in the Approval workbench. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Accounting auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver (on page 302 ). Default policies and workflows are visible 
only to admin users, including any events or actions logged in the approval history. 

Columns 

• 
Policy type: This column shows the policy type that the system used to approve the item. 

• 
Policy name: This column shows the policy name that the system used to approve the item. 

Click the link to view policy details. 

• 
Workflow name: This column shows the name of the workflow that the system used in the 

transaction. Click the link to view workflow details. 

• 
Approver role/user: This column contains a link to information about the person who 

decided on the approval. Click to view the role assignment details. You can find out who is 

assigned to a particular role with this link. 

• 
Approved/Declined by: This column contains the user name of the person who made the 

approval decisions. 

• 
Event date: This column contains the date that the transaction last underwent an approval 

event. (It was submitted for approval or partially approved.) 

• 
Comments: This column contains the comments the approver made along with his decision. 

• 
State: This column contains the status of the approval. 

• 
Action type: This column contains the approval status of the transaction. 

• 
Action comments: This column contains the comments associated with the action in the 

state. 

• 
Submitted by: This column contains the name of the user who submitted the transaction. 

“Console member” appears when the user accesses RealPage Accounting through the 
console rather than by logging in directly.

Viewing Approval Policy Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here (on page 394) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of an approval policy that was used to decide on a transaction. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 359) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all button to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction in the approval queue. 

4. 
Click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history list opens. See Approval History List (on page 393) for more 

information. 

5. 
Click the text in the Policy name column to open the Approval policy manager, allowing 

you to review the policy details. 

6. 
Click the Close button to return to the Approval history box. You can also click Print to 

print the approval policy details. 

Viewing Workflow Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here (on page 394) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of an approval workflow that was used to route a transaction. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 359) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all button to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction in the approval queue. 

4. 
Click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history list opens. See Approval history list (on page 393) for more 

information. 

5. 
Click the link in the Workflow name column to display the Approval workflow details. 

6. 
Click Close to return to the Approval history box. You can also click Print to print the 

approval workflow details. 

Viewing Approver Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here (on page 394) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of a user or user role that approved a transaction.

Approvals

Approval Aging Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Aging Report`

The Approval Aging Report provides details of approvals based on the length of time transactions 

have been waiting for approval. From this report, you can see a snapshot of outstanding payments 

based on vendor, transaction type, job, and location. 

Approval Aging Report (Summary) 

Approval Aging Report (Detail)

the text in the Current state column. You can also click the value in the Amount or Total column 

to review the transaction details.

##### Approval Aging Report Options
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 413*

Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Approval Aging Report Options 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Aging Report`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Aging Report`


Viewing a Monthly Report 

To run a report using default settings: 

1. 
When the report settings screen appears, click the View button.  

The system opens a report showing all results for the default reporting period. 

2. 
To refine the report, click the Customize button to return to the main report screen, and 

then follow the steps in customizing and running this report. 

Customizing and Running the Report 

To see every result for a particular category, do not make selections from any of the data entry 
boxes. You can run this report without entering any search information. However, the report may 
take a long time to run and may return too many results to be useful.  

Before running the report, you can select the types of items to include and specify how you want 

the report to appear. 

To customize and run the report: 

1. 
In the Time period section, create your own reporting period. 

• 
Select Today if you want to generate the report for the current date. 

• 
Select Selected date if you want to generate the report for a different date, and then 

select your preferred date. 

2. 
In the Filters section, include or exclude specific types of objects in the report. As a general 

rule, set more filters to get fewer and more precise results. 

• 
In the Transaction type drop-down list, select to return results only for a specific 

transaction type. 

• 
In the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists, select a range of vendors for 

which you want to return results. 

• 
In the Location drop-down list, select to return results only for a specific location. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to generate an individual report for each 

location. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to require a location before running the report. 

• 
In the Show for drop-down list, select whether you want to display results for all 

locations, parent locations, or child locations. 

---


<!-- Page 414 -->
Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Select the Hide declined transactions check box to hide declined transactions from 

the report.  

3. 
In the Format section, specify the sort order and change the page layout of the report. 

• 
In the Sort by drop-down list, select the category by which you want to sort the report. 

• 
In the Page orientation drop-down list, select either Portrait or Landscape. 

• 
In Dates to display, click Select/Edit to choose the dates that you want to include in 

the report.  

The Dates to display option does not appear when the selected transaction type is 

Expense report. 

4. 
In the Titles section, enter titles, subtitles, and footers to display on print versions of the 

report. 

• 
In Report title 1, type the main title that you want to display in large type at the top of 

the page, directly under your company name. 

• 
In Report title 2, type the subtitle that you want to display in smaller type, directly 

under the main title. 

• 
In Footer text, type the footer text that you want to display at the bottom center of 

the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title and subtitle, and footer.  

5. 
Click the View button to generate the report. 

You can easily use trial-and-error to get the precise results you want. To refine the report further, 

click Customize to return to the report setup page.  

---



##### Approval Aging Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 415*

Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Approval Aging Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Aging Report`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Aging Report`


You can click any link to navigate into details. 

Depending on your report configuration, the Approval Aging report may contain the following 

columns: 

• 
Vendor: The name of the vendor on the transaction 

• 
Order no: The transaction’s order number, such as the purchase order number 

• 
PO created date: The date that the purchase order was created 

• 
Employee: The name of the employee who submitted the expense report 

• 
Expense report name: The name of the expense report 

• 
Date filed: The date that the employee submitted the expense report for approval 

• 
Current state: The status of the approval, whether “Submitted,” “Declined,” or “Partially 

approved” 

• 
Next approver: The next approver in line to approve the transaction 

• 
Days aged: The number of days since the transaction entered the approval workflow 

• 
0-7: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are between zero 

and seven days old 

• 
8-14: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are between eight 

and 14 days old 

• 
15-21: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are between 15 

and 21 days old 

• 
22-28: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are between 22 

and 28 days old 

• 
29-: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are older than 29 

days old 

• 
Total: The total amount of money owed to the vendor based on the purchase order or other 

transaction. Click the link to open the Purchase order information page, A/P invoice page, 

or Job cost change order page. 

•

Use the Approval History Audit report to review your company’s transaction approval history,

those policies. You can filter the report by single or multiple transaction types, including A/P 

invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, subcontracts, payments, and expense reports. You 

can also filter by specific transaction numbers, statuses, vendors, or locations.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

##### Customizing and Running the Approval History Audit Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 418*

Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Customizing and Running the Approval History Audit Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval History Audit Report`


To customize and run the Approval History Audit report: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval history audit report option. 

The report configuration page opens. 

Defining the Report Period 

In the Time period section, define the time period for the report. You can either select the 

Reporting period and As of date or select a date range to identify the report’s coverage period 

but not both. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See Specifying 

Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

To run a report for a reporting period: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the reporting period. 

2. 
In the As of date field, select the date to begin the report coverage.  

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want to be able to choose the reporting period 

and As of date when you run the report. 

To run a report for a date range: 

Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s period of coverage. 

Filtering the Report 

Optionally, in the Filters section, select any filters you want to apply to the report: 

• 
Transaction type: Select one or more transaction types. 

• 
Transaction number: Type one or more transaction numbers. To filter by specific transaction 

numbers, the Transaction type filter must be set to a single transaction type. If you are 

entering multiple transaction numbers, insert a comma between each number (for example, 

INV-0003, INV-0023). 

• 
From vendor/To vendor: Select a range of vendor IDs. 

• 
Vendor type: Select a vendor type. 

• 
Location: Select a location or location group. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you want to generate one report per location. 

If you select this option, then you must click the Process & store button at the end. 

---


<!-- Page 419 -->
Chapter 7: Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to prompt users to select a location before 

running the report. 

• 
Status: Select one or more transaction approval statuses. 

Labeling the Report 

In the Titles section, define the report title, subtitle, and footer text: 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type a title for the report. The system assigns a report name by 

default, but you can customize it as needed. The report title displays in large typeface at the 

top of the page directly beneath your company’s name.  

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, type the text that you want to appear below the title of the report. 

This subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In the Footer text field, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the PDF version of the report (click Print to get the 
PDF version). You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each field. 

Running the Report 

When you have finished configuring the report, click one of the following buttons: 

• 
View: Runs and displays the report directly in your browser.  

• 
Print: Exports the report to a printable PDF file. 

• 
Process & store: Allows you to process and store the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Add to dashboard: Adds the report to one of your custom dashboards. 

• 
Memorize: Memorizes the report and stores it in the Memorized reports list. 

• 
Export: Exports the report to a Word, CSV, Excel, or Text file. 

What’s Next?  

After you run the report, you can email the report to others. Use trial and error to get the precise 

results you want by filling in the desired fields and then clicking View to run the report. If you 

want to refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 

process as needed.

#### Attachments List
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 424*

Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Attachments List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Attachments`


The Attachments list displays a list of all attachments uploaded to RealPage Accounting. An 

attachment is a bundle of one or more supporting documents, such as bills, spreadsheets, tax 

forms, images, and so on, that provides tangible, historical, and auditable information in support 

of a transaction or financial record. Attachments stored in this list will appear in any 

Attachment(s) drop-down field throughout the system. This allows you to quickly attach 

supporting documents when creating new transactions and records; for example, A/P invoices, 

purchase orders, service contracts, or journal entries. 

There are multiple ways to store new attachments in the Attachments list: 

• 
Click the Add button in the Attachments list. 

• 
Click the Add link in the Attachment(s) drop-down field when creating a transaction or 

record (if scanning is disabled). 

• 
Attach or Scan documents when creating a transaction or record (if scanning is enabled). 

When Scanning is Enabled 

If you have selected the Enable single scan upload check box in your user preferences (on page 

37), then a section labeled Documents will appear on the transaction information page instead of 

the Attachment(s) drop-down list. From this section, you can scan individual documents or attach 

files from your local drive. The system automatically stores any scanned or attached documents as 

a new attachment record in the Attachments list. 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 425*

Chapter 8: Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

While scanning is enabled, you cannot attach or scan a file that is already stored in the system. 
To do this, you must disable scanning in your user preferences. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

To view and manage attachments, you must have permissions for both attachments and 

attachment folders. 

You cannot restrict access to attachment folders by an individual user. When a user has 
permission to view attachments and attachment folders, they can view all attachments and 
folders in the system. 

These permissions are required to work with attachments.

#### Attachments Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 426*

Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Attachments Overview 

Attachments are bundles of one or more files that you associate with a transaction or record, such 

as a letter of credit, an invoice, or a photo. For example, if you have a contract signed by a 

customer, you can attach the contract to the customer record. You can attach as many files or 

combinations of file types as you need and bundle them into a single attachment record. 

To attach a document, you first need to create an electronic version of it. If it is a paper copy, scan 

the document, and then save it as one of the supported file types:  

• 
Word 

• 
PDF 

• 
Excel 

• 
Text 

• 
JPG 

• 
PNG 

Attaching Files to Transaction Records 

The Enable single scan upload setting in your user preferences changes the way that the system 

treats attachments. These differences are described below: 

When scanning is disabled: 

• 
You can select one attachment record to associate with a transaction, but the attachment 

record can contain multiple files as needed. 

• 
You can create folders for storing attachments from the transaction record. 

• 
You can access the attachment folders from the transaction record. 

When scanning is enabled: 

• 
You can add multiple attachments to a transaction record. 

• 
You can scan a document to attach it directly to the transaction record. 

• 
You cannot create or access attachment folders. 

For instructions on enabling the Enable single scan upload option, see Enabling the Scanning 

Feature. 

---



##### Adding an Attachment to the System
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 427*

Chapter 8: Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding an Attachment to the System 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Storage > 
 Attachments`


You can create an attachment record in the Attachments list to upload one or more files into a 

single attachment and store it in RealPage Accounting. Any attachment records you create will be 

available in Attachment drop-down lists throughout RealPage Accounting; for example, when you 

are entering a new transaction or record and you want to attach supporting documents. 

To add an attachment, you need at least one attachment folder (on page 424) in which to store 

the attachment. Your company may have created an initial folder for you. If no folder currently 

exists, you can quickly create one while you are adding an attachment.  

To add a new attachment record in the system: 

1. 
In the Attachments list, click the Add button. 

The Select attachments page opens. 

2. 
Type a unique ID for the attachment record. If your company is configured to auto-number, 

then the system automatically displays an ID for the attachment. 

3. 
Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

4. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

5. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment. 

6. 
In the Attach files section: 

• 
Click the Choose files button, select the file(s) you want to attach, and then click the 

Open button. Alternatively, you can drag and drop files directly from your file explorer 

into the browser window. 

• 
If you have Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-Op, and you 
purchased the portal add-on, then the Display on portal check box also appears. 
Select the check box for any attachment that you want the tenant or owner to be able 
to access on their portal. 

7. 
Attach additional files as needed. 

8. 
Click the Save button. 

---

Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

5. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

6. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment. 

7. 
In the Attach files section:

• 
If you have Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-Op, and you 

purchased the portal add-on, then the Display on portal check box also appears. 

Select the check box for any attachment that you want the tenant or owner to be able 

to access on their portal.

Adding a New Attachment to a Record When Scanning is Enabled 

To add a new attachment to a record when scanning is enabled: 

1. 
Add a new record or edit an existing record to open the information page. 

2. 
Find the Documents section. 

3. 
Click the Choose file button, select the file you want to attach, and then click the Attach 

button to upload it to the record. The file appears in the list of attachments. 

Alternatively, you can scan documents into the record. See Scanning a Document into a 

Record for more information. 

4. 
Continue attaching files as needed. 

5. 
Save the record. 

When you save the record, the system stores the attached files in a new attachment record 

in the Attachments list.

Adding an Existing Attachment to a Record

attachment there.

enabled scanning in your user preferences:

 Delete icon 

next to the attachment files you want to remove.

attachment.

Attachment folders help you organize and group attachments stored in RealPage Accounting. For 

example, if your company has many projects, you could make an attachment folder for each 

project. Then, when you add an attachment to a project transaction or record, you can store the 

attachment in the folder associated with the correct project, making your attachments easy to find 

and maintain. 

The items you can see on this page vary slightly depending on whether your company is an 

enterprise or a multi-entity shared company. If your company is a multi-entity shared company at 

the top level, you initially see only the items that were created at the top level. To see items 

created in the entities, select the Include private check box. Also, when you edit an item that was 

created in an entity, your changes apply to that entity. After you save your changes, you are 

returned to the top level. 

You can add attachment folders from the Attachment folders list or create folders when you are 

attaching files to a record (if scanning is disabled). However, if you are setting up a 

comprehensive folder system with naming conventions, we recommend that you create the 

hierarchy for your attachment folders from the Attachment folders list before you begin adding 

and storing attachments.
