#### Cloud Storage
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 443*

Chapter 8: Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Cloud Storage 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Cloud Storage`


You can deliver RealPage Accounting data to cloud storage sites, such as HTTP, Dropbox, Box, 

Google Drive, Amazon S3, SharePoint, OneDrive, and SFTP. The option to store data on an off-site 

location currently applies to reports that you schedule, standard and custom reports that you 

process and store, and files sent by Data Delivery Service (DDS). 

Cloud Storage Targets 

You can use the Cloud-storage targets list to: 

• 
Define cloud storage locations, known as “targets,” where you plan to store your company 

data. For example, if you plan to deliver financial reports to a folder on Google Drive, you 

first need to define a cloud-storage target for the Google Drive location. 

• 
Define the cloud storage destination that DDS uses when sending exported object files. 

• 
Review and troubleshoot any existing cloud storage targets, with the option to easily correct 

problems and resend any undelivered reports. 

Cloud Storage Privacy 

In most cases, any files you upload into the target will inherit the target’s public or private settings 

specified in the third-party target (Google Drive, Box, Dropbox, and so on). For instance, if you 

have a public folder called “Monthly Reports” in your Box account that you share with another 

user, and the folder is set to public, then the other user can see the files stored in this folder. In 

contrast, if the folder is instead set to private, then only you, the target owner, would have access 

to these files. 

However, in the case of an Amazon S3 target, you have the option to restrict file access to the 

bucket owner only or to authenticated users who have permissions to read the Amazon S3 

account. 

The Private check box located in the header section of a target doesn’t dictate whether the files 

themselves are private or public. Privacy of files is controlled by the bucket’s permissions set in 

the third-party target, with the exception of Amazon S3 targets. Instead, this option specifies 

whether the target owner alone can see this target in a list when choosing target destinations, or 

if it is available to all RealPage Accounting users who can set up reports and DDS jobs to deliver 

to a target.

#### Cloud Storage Targets List
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 445*

Chapter 8: Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Cloud Storage Targets List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Cloud Storage`


The Cloud-storage targets list defines one or more cloud-storage targets that you can use to 

deliver reports. When you set up delivery or storage for a particular report, you can pick from one 

of the cloud-storage targets that you previously added to the list. 

In addition to defining cloud-storage targets, the Cloud-storage targets list serves as the central 

place for status monitoring and troubleshooting. If any reports weren’t successfully delivered, 

then you can easily correct the problem and redeliver the reports, all from a single page. 

List Columns 

For each cloud storage target, the list displays the: 

• 
Name of each cloud-storage target. 

• 
Storage type, such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, Amazon S3, Microsoft, or HTTP. 

• 
Status of the last delivery, including whether there were any delivery errors. 

• 
Date and time of the last delivery. 

From the list, you can easily edit a particular target, correct any errors, and redeliver any 

undelivered reports that are waiting in the queue. 

Administrative Tasks 

For each cloud-storage target, you can see whether the target is signed in and whether the last 

delivery was successful. We recommend that you review the status of your cloud-storage targets 

list on a regular basis and check for the following issues: 

• 
If the State field in an individual target record indicates that the target is Signed-out, 

re-establish the connection by signing in again (on page 436). 

• 
If the Last delivery column indicates that there was a Delivery error, correct the problem 

and redeliver any failed reports (on page 438).

##### Adding a Cloud-Storage Target
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 446*

Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding a Cloud-Storage Target 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Cloud Storage`


You can define as many cloud-storage targets as you need. Multiple targets can be set up for 

different cloud-storage sites, or for the same cloud-storage site. For example, you can define one 

Dropbox target for an external client, another Dropbox target for internal reports, and a third as a 

DDS delivery destination. 

Procedures 

To add a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application. 

2. 
On the All tab, select the Cloud storage menu option. 

The Cloud-storage targets list opens. 

3. 
In the Storage type drop-down list, select one of the options: 

• 
HTTP: Uploads files to a web server using an HTTP or HTTPS endpoint. Use when your 

organization provides a URL-based service for receiving files. 

• 
Dropbox: Connects to a Dropbox account to store files in designated folders. Use for 

simple, cloud-based file sharing and collaboration. 

• 
Google Drive: Saves files to a Google Drive account. Useful for teams that manage and 

share documents within the Google Workspace ecosystem. 

• 
Box: Stores files in a Box account. Commonly used by organizations with enterprise 

content management and security requirements. 

• 
Amazon S3: Uploads files to an Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) bucket. Best for 

scalable, high-volume cloud storage managed through AWS. 

• 
Microsoft: Saves files to SharePoint or OneDrive. Ideal for organizations using 

Microsoft 365 for document management and collaboration. 

• 
SFTP: Transfers files to a secure server using Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP). 

Typically used for automated, secure file exchanges with external systems or vendors. 

4. 
In the Name field, type a name for the cloud-storage target. This is the same name that 

displays when you set up cloud delivery for a particular report. 

5. 
Verify the assigned Owner.  

• 
If you are an administrator, you have the option to make another user the owner. 

Otherwise, you are automatically the owner. 

• 
If the cloud-storage target is marked as Private, only the owner or administrators can 

edit its information. 

6. 
In the Email address field, type the email addresses that you want to notify with the status 

of the report delivery. 

---


<!-- Page 447 -->
Chapter 8: Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

7. 
Select the Private check box if you want the target to be used only by the owner and 

administrators. Other users can’t see private targets in the Cloud-storage targets list and 

can’t choose them for report delivery. 

8. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists. 

9. 
Complete the Storage type details section based on your selected storage type. See the 

corresponding section below for instructions. 

HTTP 

If you are a developer of RealPage Accounting, you can have the report delivered to another 

application using HTTP. When you select HTTP as the storage type, the address or URL that you 

specify receives reports in the form of a post call. 

Using the HTTP option, the system sends DDS files and offline reports using HTTP post requests. 

You include the company title parameter as an HTTP request body field. In this case, you will get 

the company ID along with the DDS or report file. 

To set up an HTTP target: 

1. 
Type the complete Address/URL where you want the system to send the post call, starting 

with “http” or “https”. 

2. 
If the URL requires authentication, type the HTTP user name and HTTP password. 

3. 
Click the Save button. 

Dropbox, Google Drive, or Box 

If you selected Dropbox, Google Drive, or Box, type the storage Path. The path represents the 

folder location in your account where reports will be stored. 

For these storage types, you need to establish a connection to your cloud-storage account (on 
page 436 ) after setting up the target. 

Amazon S3 

If you selected Amazon S3: 

1. 
In the Bucket field, type the name of the bucket you created in your Amazon S3 account (on 

page 435). This is the top-level container where reports should be stored. 

2. 
Optionally, in the Path field, type the folder location within the bucket where reports should 

be delivered. If you don’t enter a path, the system delivers all reports to the top-level 

bucket. 

3. 
Select the Encrypt check box to apply server-side encryption (AES-256) to files stored in 

Amazon S3. 

4. 
In the Restrict file access to drop-down list, select one of the options: 

---


<!-- Page 448 -->
Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Bucket owner only: Files are private and accessible only to the bucket owner or 

administrators. 

• 
Authenticated users: Files are accessible to users who have permission to access the 

S3 account. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Microsoft 

If you selected Microsoft: 

1. 
In the Destination field, select where you want to store reports: 

• 
SharePoint: Store files in a SharePoint site. 

• 
OneDrive: Store files in your OneDrive account directly on your local machine. 

2. 
In the Host field, type the SharePoint or OneDrive domain; for example, 

customer.sharepoint.com or customer-my.sharepoint.com. 

3. 
In the Site path field, type the site or team path as it appears in the URL; for example, 

sites/YourSiteName or teams/YourTeamName. 

4. 
In the Drive name field, type the document library or the main folder where files are stored, 

such as Documents, Shared Documents, or Site Assets). 

5. 
Optionally, in the Path field, type the folder location within the document library; for 

example, Reports or Reports/Quarterly. If you do not specify a path, reports are saved to the 

top level of the document library. 

6. 
Click Save. 

After you save the cloud-storage target, use the Sign in button to sign in to your Microsoft 
account (on page 436 ). 

SFTP 

Use SFTP to securely deliver reports to an external server provided by your organization or a third 

party. 

If you selected SFTP: 

1. 
In the Host field, type the server address provided by your administrator or service provider. 

This is typically a domain name (for example, sftp.company.com) or an IP address. 

2. 
In the Port field, type the port number used to connect to the server. 

• 
The default SFTP port is 22. 

• 
If a different port is required, your administrator will provide it. 

3. 
Type the SFTP username and password used to access the server. These credentials are 
provided by your organization’s IT team or the external service you are sending files to. 

4. 
Click Save.

##### Setting Up an Amazon S3 Account for Cloud Storage
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 449*

Chapter 8: Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Setting Up an Amazon S3 Account for Cloud Storage 

Before you can deliver data to Amazon S3, you need to create a bucket in your Amazon S3 

account and edit the bucket policy to grant access privileges to RealPage Accounting. 

1. 
On the Amazon Web Services site, create a bucket in your S3 account: 

• 
Type a Bucket name. 

• 
Select the AWS region where the bucket should reside. 

2. 
Add a bucket policy: 

• 
Go to the information page for the bucket you created. 

• 
Open the Bucket policy editor and paste the script below. 

{ 

“Version”: “2012-10-17”, 

“Statement”: [ 

{ 

“Sid”: “AddPerm”, 

“Effect”: “Allow”, 

“Principal”: { 

“AWS”: “arn:aws:iam::533618318345:user/ia-app-CloudStorage-S3” 

}, 

“Action”: “s3:PutObject”, 

“Resource”: “arn:aws:s3:::bucket_name/*” 

} 

] 

} 

3. 
Save your changes. 

You can now add a cloud-storage target (on page 431) that uses Amazon S3.

##### Redelivering Failed Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 452*

Storage 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Redelivering Failed Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All Cloud storage`


Report delivery can fail when the system is unable to connect to the storage destination or when 

the destination configuration is invalid. Common causes include expired or missing sign-in 

credentials, incorrect host or path values, unavailable or inactive services, insufficient storage 

space, or temporary connectivity issues. 

Procedures 

To redeliver failed reports after a delivery error: 

1. 
In the Cloud-Storage Targets list, locate the target with the delivery error, and then click the 

corresponding Edit or View link. 

2. 
Review the error message associated with the failed report to determine the cause, update 

the storage configuration or resolve the issue as needed, and then retry delivery. 

In addition to the error message, you will see the total number of reports that are waiting 
to be delivered. 

3. 
Click the Retry button.

scheduled report.

or your sign-in credentials weren’t recognized.

storage, then try again.

This upload failed to complete because the URL

in the Address/URL field.

##### Importing Locations
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 459*

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing location records. You may have additional options 

based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Locations`


1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, select Locations. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > Locations`


1. 
Open the Forecasting & Planning menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, select Locations. 

Importing Locations 

You can import locations by uploading a CSV file. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file containing 

data. 

Downloading the Template 

When you download templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been 

tailored to your specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses.  

1. 
Open the Company menu.  

2. 
Click the Import data option. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the Locations row, and then click the 

Template link. 

The system either downloads the Locations.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

Filling In the Locations Template 

Add your data using the correct formatting as explained in the template.  

1. 
Open the template in Excel. 

2. 
Fill in the required columns in the template: 

---


<!-- Page 460 -->
Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type a unique identifier for the location. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
LOCATION_NAME: Type a location name of up to 40 characters. 

• 
START_DATE: Type the start date related to the location.  

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type a contact name. This column is required if the contact is 

specified. 

3. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. 

4. 
After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 

mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common errors, 

Best practices. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format [File > Export > CSV (Comma delimited file)]. 

6. 
Import the location data’s CSV file (Company > All > Import Data > Locations > Import). 

7. 
In the Date format field, unless your dates are already in MM/DD/YYYY format, select a date 

format that you want to use. The system supports 24 date formats.  

8. 
In the File encoding field, leave the setting as auto detect unless you are unable to import 

your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of 

file encoding. 

9. 
Select the Process offline check box if you are importing a large quantity of data or if you 

are unsure how much time your import will take. Some imports can take considerable time, 

depending on their size and how much processing the system must do on the imported 

data. The Process offline feature allows the system to process the data when system activity 

is lighter. If you prefer to wait until the import process is complete, do not select the 

Process offline check box. 

10. 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. When the system 

completes the import process, it sends an email to the address with either a message about 

the success or failure of the import, including any errors that occurred in the process. 

11. 
Click the Import button. 

The system does not import the data of any row in the file that starts with a # symbol. 

12. 
Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors.

Locations List

•

•

•

##### Adding and Editing Locations
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 462*

Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding and Editing Locations 

See the How to Get Here (on page 444) topic for a list of ways to access the Locations list. 

To add a location: 

1. 
Type the ID and Name of the location as you want it to appear in the system. 

After saving the record you cannot change the location ID.  

If you must change the ID, contact your system administrator and have them run the 

RealPage Accounting Customer Utility tool to change the Location ID/Property ID. 

2. 
If the location belongs to a hierarchy of locations, then select its Parent location. 

• 
For example, suppose that your West Coast Division contains several locations 

including California, Nevada, and Utah. When you define California, Nevada, and Utah, 

select West Coast Division as the parent. 

• 
If you have a multi-entity company that also uses multiple base currencies, then you 

must assign each location to an entity so that the system knows which base currency 

to use for that location. In this case, you can’t change the Parent location. 

You can change the parent of a location only when your system uses one base 
currency. 

3. 
Type the location’s Tax ID. 

• 
For US companies with domestic-only business, type the location’s state tax ID for 

reference purposes. 

• 
If the location tracks VAT, then type the location’s VAT registration ID. 

4. 
In the Manager drop-down list, select or add the employee who manages this location. This 

field is useful if you route purchasing approvals to the manager of a requesting employee’s 

location. 

5. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists. 

Filling In the Contacts Section 

Unlike contact records that refer to an individual (such as an employee), contact records for 

locations contain information about the location. At a minimum, enter a main contact that 

specifies the location name, address, and other details as they should appear on A/R invoices, A/P 

invoices, and other forms. If the location uses a different address for receiving goods and services, 

then create or select a Ship to contact record.  

1. 
In the Location drop-down list, add or select the main location contact. The location’s 

contact record must contain the company name, address, and other details as you want 

them to appear on A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and other forms. 

2. 
Add or select the Ship to contact record. 

---


<!-- Page 463 -->
Chapter 9: Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Filling In the Reporting Section 

Enter the information that you want to appear in reports. You can enter up to five lines, with a 

maximum of 50 characters per line. 

To save time, you can run a financial report or other general ledger report for a group of 

entities/locations or departments and have the system automatically split the report into multiple 

individual reports. In this case, the report header for the “individual report” displays the name of 

the department, entity, or location, plus any title text you enter in the Location title field, instead 

of the company name. 

For example, a location title might provide additional information that you want to display in 

reports, such as the address and manager name. You can enter up to five lines, with a maximum 

of 50 characters per line. For more information, see Individual Reports for Each Department 

Location or Entity. 

The Reporting section appears only when the Enable additional header titles option is selected on 
the General ledger application’s configuration page.  

Filling In the Dates of Operation Section 

1. 
In the Start date field, type the date that the building became operational. This information 

is for record-keeping purposes only and is not used anywhere else in the system. 

2. 
In the End date field, type the date when the location was taken out of operation. This 

information is for record-keeping purposes only and is not used anywhere else in the 

system. 

Filling In the Tax Code Groups Section 

The system uses tax codes for automatic tax charging. Assigning tax codes to locations is the last 

step in setting up this feature.  

Select the Federal, Provincial/State, City, County, or other applicable tax code from the 

drop-down lists. Your company configures the tax code group names, so your company’s tax 

code group names may vary.  

Defining the Location’s Management Reporting Codes 

Management reporting codes let you capture location attributes for filtering reports. Location 

management reporting code descriptions are the same as the entity reporting codes. 

1. 
Click the Management reporting codes tab. 

2. 
Assign reporting codes as needed. 

3. 
Click the Save button. You can also save this record and create another one. Click the More 

actions button, and then select Save & new. Another blank location information record 

opens.

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 466*

Dimensions

Inactivating a Location 

See the How to Get Here (on page 444) topic for a list of ways to access the Locations list. 

Making a location inactive does not make its associated accounts and transactions inactive. 

Transactions and accounts of inactive locations continue to appear in lists.  

To make a location inactive: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the All tab of the menu. 

2. 
In the Dimensions section, click Locations. The Locations list opens. 

3. 
Find the location that you want to inactivate, and then click the Edit link. The Location 

information page opens. 

4. 
In the Status drop-down list, click Inactive. 

5. 
Click Save. 

The system continues to include transactions of the location in invoices, adjustments, and 

advances lists. In addition, accounts associated with the location continue to appear in lists. 

However, bank account records cannot be viewed. If you want to view the bank account of 

an inactive location, you must reactivate the location first.

Departments 

Although departments are optional, they are useful for filtering and categorizing data in many 

areas of the system. For example, you may want to generate financial reports and graphs based 

on departments. Additionally, many companies set up transaction approvals to be routed to the 

department manager. 

You can create a hierarchy of departments to reflect how departments are organized in your 

company. The hierarchy is established by defining parent and child relationships between 

departments. For example, you could have a parent department called West Coast Division that 

contains several child departments including Engineering, which itself has two additional child 

departments, Software Engineering and Hardware Engineering. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

Importing the Data 

To import the CSV file with department data: 

• 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file you want to import. 

• 
In the Date format field, select the desired date format. 

When you select a date format here, the system attempts to import your file using the 

selected date format. If the system can’t import your file with the selected date format, 

it attempts to discover the date format used in your file and import the data using that 

date format. 

• 
In the File encoding drop-down list, leave this option set to Auto detect unless you’re 

unable to import your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to 

select a different type of file encoding.

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much 

processing the system must do on the uploaded data. If you’re not sure how much 

time your upload will take, select Process Offline. When the system completes the 

process, it sends an email to the address you provide in the Email results to this 

address field. The system also sends you any errors that may have occurred in the 

process. If you prefer to wait until the upload process is complete, do not select the 

Process Offline check box. 

• 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. 

• 
This is the email address where the system sends import results and errors. You can 

enter multiple email addresses, separated by a semicolon (;) or comma (,). RealPage 

highly recommends entering an email address.

Click the Import button.

Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors.

##### Importing Employees
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 481*

Chapter 9: Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Importing Employees 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Employees`


You can import employees’ data by uploading a CSV file. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file containing 

data. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > 
Employees > Template`


1. 
Download the most recent Employees template from the Import data list. When you get 

your templates from the Import data list, you get templates that have been tailored to your 

specific company, including the dimensions that your company uses.  

2. 
Open the template file in Excel. 

3. 
Fill in the required columns in the template using the correct formatting as explained in the 

template. See Filling in Import Templates. 

• 
EMPLOYEE_ID: Type a unique identifier for the employee. The identifier can be 

alphanumeric and up to 20 characters. 

• 
CONTACT_NAME: Type the employee’s contact name of up to 40 characters. 

• 
PRINT_AS: Type the employee name as you want it to appear on documents. 

4. 
Optionally, add data into the remaining columns. Refer to the Employees Data Template for 

a full list of columns. 

After you’ve added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in 

mind. This helps eliminate anything that might make your import fail. See Common Errors 

and Best Practices. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

6. 
On the Company menu, click Import data. 

7. 
In the Set Up Company Master List section, find the Employees row, and then click the 

Import link. The Employees import box opens. 

8. 
To import the CSV file with employee data: 

---


<!-- Page 482 -->
Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file you want to import. 

• 
In the Date format field, select the desired date format. 

When you select a date format here, the system attempts to import your file using the 

selected date format. If the system can’t import your file with the selected date format, 

it attempts to discover the date format used in your file and import the data using that 

date format. 

• 
In the File encoding drop-down list, leave this option set to Auto detect unless you’re 

unable to import your file. Depending on your operating system, you may need to 

select a different type of file encoding. 

• 
Select the Process Offline check box to import offline. 

Some imports can take considerable time, depending on their size and how much 

processing the system must do on the uploaded data. If you’re not sure how much 

time your upload will take, select Process Offline. When the system completes the 

process, it sends an email to the address you provide in the Email results to this 

address field. The system also sends you any errors that may have occurred in the 

process. If you prefer to wait until the upload process is complete, do not select the 

Process Offline check box. 

• 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address. 

This is the email address where the system sends import results and errors. You can 

enter multiple email addresses, separated by a semicolon (;) or comma (,). RealPage 

highly recommends entering an email address. 

9. 
Click the Import button. 

10. 
Resolve any errors. See Resolving errors.

##### Adding an Employee
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 484*

Dimensions 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding an Employee 

See the How to Get Here (on page 466) topic for a list of ways to access this page. 

A basic employee record contains an employee ID and a primary contact name that is used to 

reference the employee throughout the system. 

To add an employee, complete the following fields on the Employee information page: 

1. 
In the Employee ID field, type a unique identifier for the employee. An employee ID can 

consist of numbers, letters, or both. 

You can create employee IDs by adding them manually or by creating a document 

numbering sequence (on page 258) to automatically generate them from a preset 

numbering scheme. 

As a best practice, do not use leading zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can 

cause errors when you import information into your company from Excel because Excel 

removes the leading zeros. 

If you must use leading zeros in your ID, be sure to convert the column of ID numbers to 

text format in Excel before importing the file content so that Excel does not remove the 

leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you use a template to 

import information that requires IDs. 

2. 
In the Primary contact name drop-down list, select the contact name that is used to 

reference the employee throughout the system and in printed output. If needed, create a 

new contact (on page 636). 

The Status drop-down list defaults to Active. Do not change this value to Inactive unless you 

no longer want the employee to appear in Employee drop-down lists throughout the 

system.

Importing Accounting Units Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Units > Template/Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Template/Import`


The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

This procedure assists you with importing units data to use with the core RealPage Accounting 

applications. You can use import template to create new unit records, update existing units, or 

both. When importing, the system does not remove existing data when a column is blank in the 

import template. 

Importing unit data for use with Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-op requires 
the use of different templates and import links. To import data into unit records for one of these 
applications, see Importing Unit Data (on page 479 ).

Open the file in Excel.

•

•

•

•

•

•

•

Adding an Entity

 Entities`


You must have individual permissions for each tab in the entity record (on page 486) to add or 

edit information on that tab. If you don’t have permission for the tab—but you do have

apply when adding entities, importing entities, editing entities, or updating entities via import. 

Filling In the Entity Information Tab 

In the Entity section: 

1. 
Type a unique ID for the entity, up to 20 alphanumeric characters. This is typically an 

abbreviation of the full entity name.  

You cannot change the ID after saving the entity record. 

2. 
Type a Name for the entity, up to 40 characters using any combination of letters, numbers, 

and special characters. 

3. 
If the property name on your invoices is slightly different than your entity name in RealPage 

Accounting, update the Property name field with the name that appears on your invoices. 

During the AI invoice process, the system checks to see if the name on the invoice is the 

same as either the entity name or the property name. 

4. 
In the Tax solution drop-down list, select a tax solution for the entity. 

This field appears only when your company has subscribed to the Taxes application. 

5. 
In the Federal ID field, type the entity’s federal tax ID. 

This field appears only if you configure the multi-entity console to issue a separate 1099 
form per entity. 

6. 
In the Operating country drop-down list, select the country where this tax entity’s office is 

located. 

7. 
In the Tax ID field, type the entity’s state tax ID (for US companies with domestic-only 

businesses) or VAT registration number (if the entity pays VAT taxes). 

8. 
In the Manager drop-down list, select the contact record of the employee who manages 

this entity. Assigning an entity manager is useful if you plan to route purchasing approvals 

to the manager of the entity to which the requesting employee belongs. 

9. 
In the Status drop-down list, select the applicable status: 

• 
Active: This is the default status and indicates that the entity is in use. 

• 
Inactive: This status prevents the entity from appearing in lists throughout the system. 

---


<!-- Page 503 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Ordered: This status indicates that the entity is newly added to RealPage Accounting 

through Unified Provisioning. When an entity is in Ordered status, complete the 

required information, set up multi-entity preferences, and then change the status to 

Active.  

When setting up user accounts and choosing the entities that the user can access, 

Ordered entities appear in the list of available entities along with Active entities. Make 
sure that you choose only Active entities. 

Active and Ordered entities are included in the default view of the Entities list, but Inactive 

entities are not. To view inactive entities, select the Include inactive check box in the Entities 

list. 

10. 
In the Color drop-down list, select a color to assign to the entity. Click the See custom 

colors link to choose a custom color. 

11. 
If you are subscribed to Full Service Spend Management, then you can select the Exclude 

from Full Service check box to prevent the entity from syncing to RealPage Invoice 

Processing. Clear this check box to allow the entity to sync again. 

12. 
If AI-Invoice scanning (on page 248) is enabled but you don’t want the system to 

automatically set the entity on AI invoices, then select the Exclude from AI Invoice check 

box. You can use this setting for entities that represent your property management 

company or funds so that the system doesn’t code the wrong property on an AI invoice. 

13.

top level or the entity level. 

• 
The entity will not appear in the Group by entity list. 

• 
Payments that are manually imported for the entity at the top level or entity level 

cannot be processed. 

You can create a custom view of the Entities list that includes the Do not pay field as an 
additional column.

Do not pay (filter from Schedule Payment Selection) check box. Payments for the entity 

will not be picked up when the automatic payment schedule runs. Payment schedules 

appear in the Schedule payments selection list. 

In the Contacts section:

5. 
If journal entry approvals are enabled for your company and your system is configured to

Advance posting date check box appears on entity records. Select this check box if you 

want to have the system advance the posting date of journal entries that are submitted in a 

closed period. The system advances the posting date to the next open period. 

When you select the Advance posting date check box, the End of month day drop-down 

list appears. Select the day of the month that you want the system to use to determine the 

next open period’s posting date. 

The advance posting date feature is set up for each entity so that the entities can run on 

their own accounting schedules based on their business needs.  

---


<!-- Page 505 -->
Chapter 11: Entities 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

The advance posting date feature can be used to mimic the OneSite feature that allows you 

to close a month out early, in a sense. In OneSite, the posting date is driven by the Leasing 

& Rents period ending date. Transactions that are recorded after the period ends are 

considered to be in the dead zone. After you close the period and before you advance the 

property into the new fiscal period, dead zone transactions post on the first day of the new 

fiscal period.  

In contrast, in RealPage Accounting, you enable the Advance posting date check box and 

then identify the End of month day to have the system advance postings to the first day of 

the next month. This creates a dead zone between the End of month day and the next 

month. Dead zone transactions post on the first day of the next month.  

You can also use this feature if your end of month day is on a different day than the last day 

of the month. For example, when the end of month day is set to the 15th, then anything 

entered from 5/1 – 5/15 posts in May. Anything entered from 5/15 – 5/31 posts on June 1. 

In the Reporting section: 

1. 
In the Print entity name as field, type the name of the entity as it should appear on reports 

and invoices that are printed for the entity. This name applies only when you switch to the 

entity. When you generate reports or invoices, the system uses the name from the Name 

field. 

2. 
In the Entity title field, type the text that you want to appear in the report header instead of 

the company name. For example, a location title can provide additional information that you 

want to display on reports. Enter up to five lines with a maximum of 50 characters per line. 

In the Calendar section: 

1. 
In the Week begins on drop-down list, select the first day of each week. This enables the 

system to provide accurate data for reports that begin on the first day of a week. 

2. 
In the Workdays and Weekends fields, select workdays and weekends to control whether 

employees can submit hours for time worked on these days, and if they can, to apply a 

different pay rate. 

In the Dates of operation section: 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date when the entity became operational. 

2. 
In the End date field, type or select the date when the entity was taken out of operation. 

In the Tax code groups section: 

• 
Select the tax code groups to which the entity belongs in the applicable drop-down lists.  

Only Commercial Property Management and Condo and Co-op use tax codes at this time.

If your company has multiple entities, an additional link labeled Set up inter-entity account

when one entity pays for an A/P invoice on behalf of another entity, are tracked separately from 

regular accounts receivable and accounts payable transactions.

specify a default payable and receivable account to use for recording inter-entity balances.

##### Updating Entity Information in Bulk via Import
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 514*

Updating Entity Information in Bulk via Import 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up Company Master List > Entities 
> Template / Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Import`


You can update entity information in bulk using the Import feature. The only field that is required 

when updating information in bulk is the Entity ID. Any additional information that you enter into 

the CSV file either adds to or updates existing information. Fields that are left blank do not 

change or overwrite existing information in the entity record. 

You must have individual permissions for each tab in the entity record (on page 486 ) to add or 
edit information on that tab. If you don’t have permission for the tab—but you do have 
permissions for entities —then the information on the tab will be read-only. These tab 
permissions apply when adding entities, importing entities, editing entities, or updating entities 
via import. 

Download the Entities Template from the Import Data Page 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information. This is important because: 

• 
Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by RealPage Accounting at any time, especially when a new 

version of RealPage Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not 

work. 

To download the Entities template from the Import data page: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import data menu option. The Import data page opens. 

3. 
In the Set up company master list section, find the row labeled Entities, and then click the 
Template link. 

In addition to standard columns, the system dynamically appends columns for any 
dimensions you’ve enabled and any custom fields and custom objects you’ve created so 
that you can import that information as well. 

4. 
Populate the template with any entity information that you want to add or update. Leave 
the cell blank if you do not want to update that field in the existing entity record. 

You must enter the Entity ID; all other fields are optional. 

5. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

6. 
Close the CSV file.

the entity records. 

To import the CSV file: 

1. 
On the Import data page, click the Import link in the row labeled Entities. The Entities box 

opens. 

You can also import directly from the Entities list (on page 486 ) itself. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button. 

Deleting an Entity 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Delete`


You can’t delete an entity if any records or transactions are associated with it. If you added any 

records to the entity, then delete them before you delete the entity. Additionally, be sure to 

update any top-level records that refer to the entity. For example, if you restricted a user to the 

entity, edit the user’s record and remove the entity. 

To delete an entity: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Entities option. 

3. 
In the Entities list, locate the entity that you want to delete, and then click the 

corresponding Delete link. 

A confirmation box opens. 

4. 
Click OK.

##### Switching to an Entity
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 516*

Entities 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Switching to an Entity 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Switch to Entity`


You can navigate to another entity from the top level. 

To access another entity in your organization, you can switch to that entity at any time from the 

top-level company without having to log in or out again. There are three ways to switch to 

another entity: 

• 
From the Header: Click the Top level drop-down list (your company name in the top 

header), and then click the entity you want to access. 

• 
From the Entities List: Find the entity you want to access in the list, and then click the 

Switch to entity link next to it.  

The entity opens in a new browser tab. The name of the entity displays under your company 

name in the top header in the color assigned to that entity. 

Companies that use multiple currencies create additional entities, called “elimination entities,” 
to perform consolidations. These entities serve only to contain the amounts eliminated due to 
inter-entity transfers. You cannot access elimination entities, nor can you open these entities 
at the entity level.

#### Currency and Entities
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 517*

Chapter 11: Entities 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Currency and Entities 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Multi Entity Console > Configure`


The entity record determines the base currency. The base currency is the currency that you use in 

your company. Transaction currency is the currency that is used in a transaction.  

Typically, all entities in a company use the same base currency.  

Multiple base currencies aren’t required for transacting in multiple currencies. For instance, if all 

entities have US dollars as their base currency, they can still transact in other currencies (such as 

paying an A/P invoice in Yen), by enabling multi-currency management in General Ledger. See 

Enabling Multi-Currency Management. 

However, if an entity needs to use a different base currency, then you need to enable multiple 

base currencies on your system.  

After enabling multiple base currencies, you cannot revert the system. 

To configure multiple base currencies, see Configuring Multiple Base Currencies for a Multi-Entity 

Company. 

---

•

Setting Up a Property Alias 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Edit > Property Name`


You can create an alias for a property name to help the system’s AI recognize the property on 

scanned invoices—even if the name differs slightly from the official record. This improves invoice 

automation and reduces manual review. 

Creating a Property Name Alias 

An alias can be a nickname, a commonly used abbreviation, or an alternate spelling of the 

property. 

To create an alias for a property: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Entities. 

3. 
Find the entity record associated with the property, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
Type the alias (such as the commonly used name or abbreviation) in the Property Name 

field. 

Tip: Use consistent naming conventions and include a common variation that vendors 
might use. If no alias is created and the invoice name doesn’t match, the system may not 
recognize the property, leading to processing delays. 

5. 
Click Save. 

During AI invoice processing, the system checks the name on the invoice to see if it matches 

either the entity name or the property name (alias).

Making an Entity Inactive 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Edit`


If you want to hide an entity without deleting it, then you can make the entity inactive. By making 

an entity inactive, you can keep the entity but make sure it doesn’t appear in reports. Inactive 

entities don’t appear in lists or reports unless you choose to show inactive entities. 

To make an entity inactive:

Restricting Payments for Specific Entities 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Add/Edit`


You can mark entities as Do not pay so that payments made for those entities can’t be processed. 

Restricting Users from Making Payments on Invoices 

To restrict users from making payments on invoices for an entity: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Entities menu option. The Entities list opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the entity. The Entity information page opens. 

4. 
On the Entity information tab, in the Entity section, select the Do not pay (filter from Pay

Invoices submitted for the entity will not appear on the Pay A/P invoices page at the

•

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 521*

Disabling Automatic Payments 

To prevent the system from automatically processing payments that have been scheduled for an 

entity: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Entities menu option. The Entities list opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the entity. The Entity information page opens. 

4. 
On the Entity information tab, in the Entity section, select the Do not pay (filter from 

Schedule Payment Selection) check box. When you save this setting, payments for the 

entity will not be picked up when the automatic payment schedule runs. Payment schedules 

appear in the Schedule payments selection list. 

Automatically Advancing the Posting Date 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Add/Edit`


When you want the system to advance the G/L posting date after a set day of the month, you can 

set up the feature by entity.  

This procedure affects journal entries, subledger transactions, and external transactions. 

To set up an entity to use the advance posting date feature: 

1. 
Open the desired entity record. 

2. 
In the Accounting section, select the Advance posting date check box. 

3. 
In the End of month day field, select the day of the month after which you want to advance 

the posting dates. This is the day of the month to advance entered journal entries. 

4. 
Save the entity record. 

When you submit a journal entry and the G/L posting date is after the entity’s end of month 

day, then the system automatically advances the posting date to the first of the next month. 

To set up advance posting for check dates: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Configuration menu option. 

The Configure cash management page opens. 

3. 
In the Accounting section, select the Use the current date as check print date check box. 

4. 
Select the Use current date as the payment request date for check payments check box. 

5. 
Click Save.

##### Requesting or Removing Vendor Account Numbers
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 526*

Entities 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Requesting or Removing Vendor Account Numbers 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Edit > Spend Management > Generate 
Account Number/Remove Account Number`


If you have enabled the Storefront feature, then an additional section will appear on the Spend 

management tab of the Entity information page with a list of all of the online vendors that have 

been matched to Storefront. From this section, you can request or remove account numbers for 

your selected vendors. 

To enable Storefront, select the Enable online shopping check box on the Configure Spend 

Management page, and then configure the corresponding settings. 

Before You Begin 

You must have permission to request account numbers for online vendors. Before you request or 

remove a vendor account number, make sure you enter a billing and shipping address for the 

entity.  

To add billing and shipping addresses: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Entities menu option. 

3. 
In the Entities list, click the Edit link next to the entity. The Entity information page opens 

on the Entity information tab. 

4. 
In the Contacts section, select the contact records that contain information about the entity: 

• 
Entity: Select the primary contact that contains the entity’s location name, address, 

and other details as they should appear on invoices, bills, and other forms. 

• 
Ship to: If the entity uses a different address for receiving goods and services, then 

select the contact record that contains the shipping address. 

Make sure to fill in the Address, City, State/Territory, and Zip code/Postal code fields in 
both of the contact records; you won’t be able to generate or remove vendor account 
numbers if any of these fields are missing. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Requesting Vendor Account Numbers  

To request account numbers for one or more online vendors: 

1. 
In the Entities list, click the Edit link next to the entity. The Entity information page opens. 

2. 
Click the Spend Management tab. 

3. 
Select the check boxes next to the vendors for which you want to request account numbers. 

4. 
Click the Generate account number button. 

---


<!-- Page 527 -->
Chapter 11: Entities 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

The system sends a request to the selected vendors. You can monitor the status of each 

account number request in the Status column: 

• 
Requested: The request was sent to the vendor. 

• 
Pending: The vendor has accepted the request but has not yet assigned an account 

number to the entity.  

• 
Done: The vendor has assigned an account number to the entity, which appears in the 

Account number column. 

• 
Declined: The vendor has declined the request. 

Removing Vendor Account Numbers 

To remove account numbers for one or more online vendors: 

1. 
In the Entities list, click the Edit link next to the entity. 

The Entity information page opens. 

2. 
Click the Spend Management tab. 

3. 
Select the check boxes next to the vendors for which you want to remove account numbers. 

4. 
Click the Remove account number button. 

The system removes the account numbers for the selected vendors.

##### Associating Standard Vendors with an Entity
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 528*

Entities 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Associating Standard Vendors with an Entity 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Edit > Finance Agent`


To enable the AI Finance Agent to perform automated actions—such as automatic invoice 

approvals, accruals, payments, and detecting missing expenses—each entity must be assigned its 

standard vendors. These vendor assignments give the AI agent the context it needs to recognize 

routine activity and apply automation accurately across financial workflows. 

If you prefer to limit the automated actions for this entity, you can do that here.  

Prerequisites 

• 
Your company must be subscribed to the AI Finance Agent module. 

• 
You must have the Entity tab permission, Standard vendors, to access the Finance Agent tab 

of an entity record. 

Procedure 

To associate standard vendors with an entity: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Entities menu option. 

3. 
Find the entity to which you want to adjust standard vendors, and click the Edit link. 

4. 
Click the Finance Agent tab. 

5. 
Click the first blank row in the Standard vendors list, and then select a vendor from the list. 

Only vendors that have one invoice per month can be standard vendors. See Setting Up 
Standard Vendor Types to have the AI agent set standard vendors for you. 

6. 
You can exclude this entity’s standard vendors from being processed by the AI Agent for 

any of these activities. Select the activities to exclude: 

• 
Exclude from automated invoice approvals 

• 
Exclude from automated accruals 

• 
Exclude from automated payments 

• 
Exclude from missing expenses 

7. 
Click Save.

#### Import Data Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 546*

Import Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


Use the Import data page to: 

• 
Add accounting data to a new company. 

• 
Quickly clear some or all records from an existing company. 

• 
Choose parts of your existing accounting package you want to import, or upload long lists, 

so you don’t have to enter the data manually. 

About the Import Data Page 

If you are using the Import data page to add accounting data or other information to an 

otherwise empty company, follow the sections in their pre-defined order. The following sections 

are in the Import data page: 

• 
Set Up Company Master List: Use this section to set up your chart of accounts, statistical 

accounts, account groups, group members, departments, locations, allocations, employees, 

and territories (see Setting Up the Company Master List (on page 542)). 

• 
Set Up General Ledger Transactions: Use this section to set up journals, account beginning 

balances, reporting periods, and budgets (see Setting Up General Ledger Transactions (on 

page 546)). 

• 
Set Up A/P Master List, Open Invoices, and Adjustments: Use this section to set up the 

Accounts Payable application, A/P invoices, adjustments, and assets (see Setting Up A/P 

Master List, Open Invoices, and Adjustments (on page 550)). 

• 
Set Up A/R Master List, Open Invoices, and Adjustments: Use this section to set up the 

Accounts Receivable application, A/R invoices, customer lists, and adjustments (see Setting 

Up A/R Master List, Open Invoices, and Adjustments (on page 555)). 

• 
Set Up Cash Management: Use this section to set up your bank accounts, credit cards, 

credit card transactions, and other receipts (see Setting Up Cash Management (on page 

558)). 

• 
Property Management: Use this section to set up your property, leases, locations, 

measurements, expenses, and tenant information 

This section displays if you have Commercial Property Management installed. 

• 
Condo and Co-op: Use this section to set up your property, owners, owner information, 

measurements, tasks, billing, and more. 

This section displays if you have Condo and Co-op installed. 

• 
Set Up Job Cost: Use this section to set up your jobs, draw model details, job cost history, 

job cost and replacement reserve draws, and external commitments (see Setting Up Job 

Cost (on page 559)). 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 547*

Chapter 12: Import Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Set Up Spend Management: Use this section to set up catalog mapping and saved items 

(see Setting Up Spend Management (on page 560)). 

Understanding the Actions Within the Sections 

Each predefined section has one or more actions to help you customize your accounting 

application and direct you to the next step in the process flow. The following diagram describes 

the different actions in each section of the Import data page. 

These actions are per row in each section of the checklist and can differ depending on what data 
is being requested on the row. 

a) Status: A check mark in this column indicates a completed step. 

b) Type: This is accounting function or record type. 

c) Create: Click this link to add a new record. 

d) Import: Click this link to import information from a CSV file. 

e) Template: Click this link to download an XLS template that provides all standard and custom 

fields and descriptions of requirements for each field. 

f) 
View: Click this link to view a list of existing records. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions

Creating a New Budget and Giving It a Unique Budget ID 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All >

Before you can upload a budget spreadsheet, you must first create the budget. Clicking Add in 

the Budgets list lets you create a new budget and give it a budget ID. 

1. 
In the Budget ID field, type a unique ID for the budget, such as “Board-approved” or 

“Current Budget.” The budget ID identifies the budget when you are adding budget data or 

including a budget in a report. Before naming your budgets, review the information in Plan 

Your Budgets. 

A best practice is to give the budget an ID that doesn’t reference a particular fiscal year or 

date. Then you can append new time periods to your existing budget. 

2.

3.

• 
If this is your first budget, select the Create a new budget option. 

• 
If you are using an existing budget as a basis for a new budget, select the Create a 

budget from existing budget and reporting period range option, and then choose 

the budget from the drop-down list. 

4. 
Select the Default Budget check box if this budget will be the default for financial reports. 

5. 
Click the Save button.

reporting periods are high-level categories that you would expect to see in a balance sheet.

##### Importing Data During Company Setup
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 552*

Import Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Importing Data During Company Setup 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


Whether you are importing data into a company for the first time or updating existing data, 

importing data into your system is a two-step process: first, you download and populate a 

template, and second, you import the data from the template. 

It’s best to complete the setup in the order listed in the Import data page. 

Download the Import Template 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information. This is important because: 

• 
Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by RealPage Accounting at any time, especially when a new 

version of RealPage Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not 

work. 

To download a template from the Import data page: 

1. 
Click the Template link for the data type you want to import. For example, click Template 

on the Account groups row to download a template that enables you to import or update 

account groups. 

In addition to standard columns, the system dynamically appends columns for any 
dimensions you’ve enabled and any custom fields and custom objects you’ve created so 
that you can import that information as well. 

2. 
Populate the template with your company’s information. 

3. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

4. 
Close out the CSV file. 

Import Data From the Template 

When you have populated your selected template, import the file. 

To import the table of data into your system: 

1. 
On the Import data page, locate the item for which you downloaded the template. For 

example, if you downloaded an Account Groups template, locate the Account groups row, 

and then click the corresponding Import link. The system displays an import page. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

---



##### Importing Journals
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 553*

Chapter 12: Import Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button. 

Importing Journals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


The system can automatically import default journals based on your company’s accounting 

method. 

Importing Default Journals 

To import default journals: 

1. 
Open the Company application. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
In the Set up General Ledger transactions section, find Journal, and then click the Default 

link. 

The Create default journals box opens. Journals will be imported based on the accounting 

method you have selected  

4. 
Click the Create button. 

The system begins importing the default journals. The journals that are imported depend on 

which accounting method your company uses: single-book (either Accrual or Cash) or 

dual-book (Accrual and cash). See below for a list of journals imported for each method.  

• 
If the import is successful, then the Import success notification box will appear with a 

confirmation message. 

• 
If the import is unsuccessful, then the Import error notification box will appear with 

an error message. You will receive an email notification with an explanation of the 

error(s). There will also be a link to download a CSV file with the error details. 

5. 
Click Done to close the box. 

Default Journals for Single-Book Companies

##### About Account Beginning Balances
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 555*



##### Importing Tax Configurations
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 555*

Chapter 12: Import Data 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

About Account Beginning Balances 

Before you can establish the beginning balances for the G/L, you must create journals and then 

set their Balance as of date. Typically, this date is the next day after you close your old accounting 

system and start a new set of books, but it can be another date. If you do not select a date, then 

this field defaults to today’s date.  

Be careful when entering the beginning date. If you are uploading historical transactions, then 

make sure that your starting balances contain these uploaded transactions and then set the 

Balance as of date to that date. Use a template to import beginning balances into one journal 

with one file. If you intend to import multiple journals with one file, see Importing General Ledger 

Journal Entries for more information. 

Because G/L transactions contain fields for both department and location, you may enter as many 

unique G/L transaction department/location combinations as you wish. 

After Importing 

After importing account beginning balances, you should: 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Populate your account group ranges from the Account groups page. (General Ledger > All`


> Account Groups) 

• 
Create a financial report to test your data from the Financial reports page. (General Ledger 


> **Navigation Path:** `> All > Financial Reports)`


• 
Create a trial balance to make certain that your starting balances have been set up correctly 


> **Navigation Path:** `from the Trial balance report page. (General Ledger > All > Trial Balance Report)`


Be sure to properly format your Trial Balance report so that it includes all relevant accounts. You 
can make sure the relevant accounts are included on the Account groups page. If the correct 
accounts are not included, this can throw off your balance sheet artificially. 

Importing Tax Configurations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Authorities > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Details > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Schedules > Import`


Importing the following tax data is not supported at this time: 

• 
Tax authorities 

• 
Tax details  

• 
Tax schedules

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 579*

Chapter 13: Segments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Segments Overview 

Segments are custom classifications that help you organize, sort, and report on your company 

information in meaningful ways. Think of a segment as a tag with a set of values that you can 

associate with transactions and G/L entries. For example, you might add a custom segment to 

report on your expense types, employees, or special projects. 

When you enter a new transaction, you can assign a segment to that transaction and then tag it 

with one or more segment values. Segmenting transactions is optional; however, it can be useful 

for identifying transactions and analyzing data in your reports. 

You can define up to 15 segments for your company. An additional segment, called 

Intercompany segment, is available by default. Because it’s a system segment, it cannot be 

modified. 

Enabling Segments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > Setup > Configuration > Enable Segments`


To enable segments: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Configuration option. The General Ledger setup page opens. 

3. 
In the Advanced G/L options section, select the Enable segments check box. 

4. 
Click the Save button. 

Reports That Use Segments 

The reports you can run to see your assigned segments include: 

• 
General Ledger Report 

• 
Trial Balance Report 

• 
Financial Reports 

• 
Budget Report 

• 
Segment Activity Report 

---

##### Adding Segments
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 582*

Segments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding Segments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Segments`



> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > 
 Segments`


Use this page to add segment types and their values to the system. After adding the segments to 

the system, you can use them to classify your transactions by assigning segment types and their 

values as you create and edit transactions. You can add up to 15 segments. 

Segments do not appear on the menu unless segments have been enabled on the 
General Ledger 


> **Navigation Path:** `Setup page. Go to General Ledger > Setup > Configuration > Advanced GL Options > Enable`


Segments. 

To add a segment: 

1. 
In the Type field, type a two-character alphabetical code to identify the segment. This is the 

code that appears in Segment type drop-down lists when users tag a transaction with a 

segment. 

2. 
In the Name field, type a name for the segment. This name appears in reports. 

3. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists. By default, the 

status is Active. 

4. 
In the Segment values section, type the values to associate with the segment type.  

Alternatively, you can import the segment values (on page 571) from a CSV template. 

5. 
Click the Save button.

##### Importing Segments
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 583*

Chapter 13: Segments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Importing Segments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Segments > Template/Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Forecasting & Planning > Setup > Segments > Import`


Downloading the Template 

1. 
On the Import data page, find the Segments row, and click the Template link. 

2. 
Open the downloaded file and fill it with segment data: 

• 
Type: Type a two-character alphabetical code for the segment. 

• 
Name: Type a name that describes the segment. This name appears in reports. 

• 
Segment value: Leave this column blank. 

• 
Status: Type the status of the segment, either “Active” or “Inactive.” 

You can include up to 15 segment types and values in the import file. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the Segments 

1. 
In the Segments list, click the Import link. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

4. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in 

the background. The system sends you an email when it completes the upload. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, enter your email address to receive a message with 

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete. 

7. 
Click the Import button.

##### Creating a Service Ticket
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 593*

Chapter 14: Service Tickets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Creating a Service Ticket 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Service Tickets > 
 My Service Tickets`


To create a service ticket: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Service tickets section, select the 
 My service tickets menu option. 

The My service tickets page opens. 

3. 
Select a category for the request from the Category drop-down list. 

4. 
Optionally, select a location from the Location drop-down list. 

If you select a location, then only users who have access to that entity will be able to view 
and act on the service ticket. 

5. 
If applicable, type or select the Need by date. 

6. 
If applicable, select a Priority level. 

7. 
Type additional information or comments for your request in the Description field. 

Note any additional instructions in the Special instructions section. These are instructions 
that correspond with the ticket category you selected. 

8. 
If required, select, upload, or scan at least one attachment as a supporting document. This 

will look different depending on whether scanning is enabled for your company. See 

Managing Attachments for more information. 

9. 
If you are submitting a service request to post a journal entry for an accrual or 

reclassification, then you will see an additional section labeled Accrual or Reclass to enter 

the line items for that journal entry. When your ticket is approved, the system automatically 

posts the journal entry for the accrual or reclassification. See below for instructions on 

entering line items. 

10. 
Click Save to submit the ticket. You will receive an email confirmation when the ticket is 

successfully submitted. 

•

#### About Contracts
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 611*

Chapter 15: Contracts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

About Contracts 

A contract is an agreement between a vendor and your company. You can use contract records in 

RealPage Financial Suite as a repository for information about a job.  

In the Contracts list, you can find two kinds of contracts, offline and online. 

• 
An offline contract is one that is created in RealPage Financial Suite.  

• 
An online contract is one that is created in Vendor Marketplace’s Bids & Contracts. 

In addition to these two kinds of contracts, the Contracts list contains transactions associated 

with a contract, including subcontracts, purchase orders, and service contracts. 

• 
Service contracts are for recurring or scheduled services. 

• 
Purchase orders are for products or services that do not have a set monthly amount. 

• 
Subcontracts are for specific jobs that are defined in the Job Cost application. 

A contract record can be associated with only one of these transactions. 

If your company does not subscribe to the Spend Management application, then the Contracts list 

is for reference purposes only. You can create contract records, and you can view both online and 

offline contracts, but you will not be able to associate purchase orders, subcontracts, or service 

contracts with your contracts. 

Contract Setup 

• 
Before you begin creating contracts, create the various contract types that your company 

needs in the Contract Types list. 

• 
If you want the system to review contract documents and pull out key clause information for 

display, then set up the clauses and keywords to look for on the AI Configuration page. See 

Company > AI Configuration > AI Contract Screening. The purpose of this feature is to 

have the system read the text of a contract and extract the desired clauses from it, making 

the clause information more visible to users.  

Contract Usage Workflow 

• 
Create a service contract, subcontract, or purchase order. 

• 
When the vendor or contracted party sends an invoice to your company, create the invoice 

• 
Match the invoice with the service contract, subcontract, or purchase order. 

• 
When the contract is completed, pay the vendor. When this is a contract for a recurring 

service, create a recurring invoice.  

---

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 612*

Creating a Purchase Order from a Contract 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Bids and Contracts >
