> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contracts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Contracts > Create > 
Purchase Order`


When you create a purchase order from a contract, the system completes some of the fields using 

information from the contract, such as Item Description, SKU, Qty, and Price. If taxes and 

shipping are defined in the contract, then they appear as separate line items in the Entries list. 

To create a purchase order associated with a contract: 

1. 
Select the Contracts option. 

2. 
Select the check box of the contract on which to base a new purchase order. 

3. 
Click the Create button, and then select Purchase order. 

4. 
In the Create type section, select the Purchase order option. 

5. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the date of the purchase 

order. 

6. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Encumbrance date field, and then select the date of the 

encumbrance. 

7. 
Select a vendor from the Vendor drop-down list. 

If the vendor that you need is not available in the drop-down list, click the Add link and then 
add a new vendor record.  

8. 
Select the Use Company address for bill to check box if you want to use the vendor’s 

company address to send bills to. When you select this option, the Bill to field is not 

available. 

9. 
If you want to select a specific contact to send bills to, select the contact in the Bill to 

drop-down list. If the Bill to list is not available, then clear the Use Company address for bill 

to check box. 

10. 
In the Ship to drop-down list, select the contact record with the address where you want to 

ship goods or deliver services. 

11. 
Click the Saved items link if you want to view an offline shopping list of frequently used 

items for the vendor you entered on the purchase order. Select and apply items from this 

list to quickly populate them as line entries in the purchase order.  

---

When you access the Saved items list from the Purchase order information page, only the 
items that are saved for the vendor that you entered on the purchase order appear in the 
list. If you do not see the item(s) that you are looking for, you can add them to the list for 
the future.  

12. 
If this is a blanket purchase order, select the Blanket check box, and then select the 

appropriate option: 

• 
Blanket PO validated on item quantities 

• 
Blanket PO validated on dollar value only 

13. 
Click the Calendar button in the Expiry date field to select the date that the blanket 

purchase order expires. This option appears only when the Blanket option is selected. 

14. 
Select the Line entry type. If you implement the Job Cost application and this purchase 

order should be entered as a job cost, select the Job Cost option. Otherwise, select 

Standard. The system adjusts the entries list based on your selection. 

15. 
Type a description of the purchase in the Description field. 

16.

the vendor and property on the purchase order.

1.

When you have scanning disabled in your preferences, use the Attachments field to add 

documents to a record.

##### Setting Up the Contract Expiration Alert
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 624*

Contracts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Setting Up the Contract Expiration Alert 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry > Alerts and Notifications`


A contract expiration alert helps you stay ahead of upcoming contract deadlines by sending a 

reminder as an email notification before the contract’s expiration date or due date arrives. You 

can set up this alert to give you enough time to review terms, renew the agreement, or take any 

required action before the contract lapses. By setting up this notification, you can proactively 

manage contract timelines and avoid missed renewals or service interruptions. 

Prerequisite 

Before you begin, set up a role to use for contract expiration notifications. The users assigned to 

this role will receive a reminder by email when a contract is about to expire.  

To set up the contract expiration notification: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and select the Ledger sentry option. 

2. 
In the Ledger sentry page, find the Alerts and notifications section. 

Click the 
 Add button to add a row for the new alert if needed. 

3. 
In the Rule item column, select If contracts are expiring in the next XX days. 

4. 
In the Criteria column, type the number of days before contract expiration to have the 

system notify the users. The contract expiration is based on the End date that you defined in 

the contract record.  

5. 
In the Notify column, select the contract expiration role that you set up. 

6. 
Click Save. 

---

The content of the Contract information page varies depending on whether the record is a 

service contract, a subcontract, or a purchase order, and whether the contract is online (created in 

Bids and Contracts) or offline (created in RealPage Financial Suite). 

• 
The top section of a record contains information about the contract. 

• 
The Bids and contract attachments section lists the files attached to the contract record 

when the contract is an online contract. 

• 
The Create type section is where you select the type of record that you want to create and 

associate with the open record: a purchase order, service contract, or subcontract. 

• 
The (Date) section reflects the type of record that you chose in the Create type section, a 

service contract, subcontract, or purchase order. 

• 
The Documents or Attachment sections allow you to attach a file to the record. The 

Attachments section and drop-down list appears when you do not have scanning enabled. 

The Documents section appears when scanning is enabled. The scanner setting is available 

in My Preferences. 

If the AI contract screening feature is configured, whenever you attach a document to a 

contract record, the system reviews the document for clauses and keywords in the 

document, and then displays the clause information prominently in the contract record. 

• 
When you create a transaction, you can add items in a purchase order, or the job tasks in a 

service contract or subcontract. After you save the transaction, the list does not appear 

when viewing the contract. You must open the transaction to view the list of items. 

After you save the record, additional links appear on the record. The links vary depending on the 

record type and whether your system uses the approval workflow for service contracts, purchase 

orders, and subcontracts:

Subcontracts have a link to the parent contract in the Date section of the record. The 

Contract ID number is a link to the parent contract. 

• 
Records that traveled through the approval workflow have an Approval history link. Clicking 

the link opens the Approval history box so that you can review the record’s progress 

through the approval workflow. 

• 
Records that have been matched with A/P invoices have a Matched invoices link. Clicking 

the link opens the Matched invoices box where you can access the A/P invoice that is

### Contacts
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 647*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Contacts 

This section explains how to add and manage contacts in the Contacts list. 

In This Chapter 

Contacts List .......................................................................................................................................... 634 

C H A P T E R 16 

---



#### Contacts List
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 648*

Contacts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Contacts List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts`


The Contacts list displays all available contacts in your company, including the name and address 

of the contact. Contacts are used across your company in multiple ways: 

• 
To send event notifications  

• 
To determine ship-to/bill-to, and pay-to/return-to addresses in purchasing transactions  

• 
To determine tax on transactions 

Contacts aren ’t dimensions like vendors or customers. Instead, think of your contacts as a 
common, shared address book that is used across your company by many people for a variety of 
purposes. 

Use the Contacts list to add, edit, view, or delete the contacts in your company. Because contacts 

are flexible and can often be created at the time of need, there are a variety of ways you can add 

a contact. Most notably, contacts are created when new vendor, customer, user, or employee 

records are added to RealPage Accounting. In each case, the Suggested contact name is created 

from specific fields, which may affect the consistency of your company naming conventions. Be 

sure to review the record for the specific fields when you create a new contact. 

Best Practices for Creating Contacts 

Because contacts are used and can be created by various records and applications in RealPage 

Accounting, they can be set up inconsistently, which may be confusing in the future or even cause 

errors. To avoid these problems when setting up your contacts for the first time: 

• 
Use only supported characters. The Suggested contact name acts as a unique and 

permanent contact ID field in RealPage Accounting. The supported values include: 

• 
Alphanumeric characters 

• 
Various punctuation (periods, hyphens, underscores, parentheses) 

RealPage Accounting does not permit double spaces; using double spaces results in invalid 

contacts or contact records not appearing within drop-down menus. Furthermore, using 

other special characters not listed here (such as # or %) may also result in an invalid contact. 

• 
Establish a naming convention. The Suggested contact name is used in lists and 

drop-downs to identify your contacts. For this reason, we suggest using a naming 

convention that makes it easy to distinguish contacts in a list. 

For instance, you can use the company name of a vendor or customer, such as Example.com 

for the Suggested contact name. If the contact is an individual, you might choose a 

convention like Last Name, First Name or vice versa to keep your contacts consistent and 

easy to scan in lists and drop-downs. 

---


<!-- Page 649 -->
Chapter 16: Contacts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

How do users and contacts work together? 

A user ID and a password enable an individual to sign in to the company and access company 

information based on the user type. A contact is an individual who isn’t necessarily a user in the 

company, such as a vendor contact or customer contact. 

A contact can be made a user by adding the contact name to a user profile. For example, you 

could associate:  

• 
An employee contact with a user ID. 

• 
A customer contact with a user ID. 

• 
A vendor contact (for example a subcontractor) with a user ID. 

Associate an Existing Contact With a Customer, Vendor, Employee, or User 

Contact records hold the information you need to contact individuals or businesses. Alone, they 

are no more than a shared address book used for a variety of purposes. However, because one 

contact can be associated with many records, contacts become an easy way to manage contact 

information across many records, such as your customer, employee, vendor, and user records. 

Though you can create a new contact automatically when you create a customer, employee, 

vendor, or user, you may want to associate an existing contact with a record instead. 

Whatever the case, it’s important to note that contacts are associated with the records of 

individuals and businesses you interact with, not the other way around. For instance, if you want 

to associate the existing contact Jim West to the employee Jim West, you would go to the 

employee record to make this connection, not the contact record. 

Changing a contact in an existing record only affects transactions and other data records going 
forward. It won’t affect your historical data. 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 650*



##### Adding a Contact
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 650*

Contacts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage contact records. 

Application 
Activities/Lists Permissions 

Administration 
Users 
List, View, Edit, Add, Delete, Permissions, Groups 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Adding a Contact 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Contacts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > 
 Contact`


To create a contact quickly, you only need to assign it a unique Suggested contact name and a 

Print as name for documents. 

The Suggested contact name is the most important field in a contact record. It acts as a unique 

contact ID across the RealPage Financial Suite system, which means you can no longer edit the 

suggested contact name after you create the contact record. Furthermore, although you can 

change the printed name of a contact with the Print as field, the Suggested contact name is the 

name that appears in all lists and drop-down lists across RealPage Accounting. You can change 

the Suggested contact name of a contact (on page 641) in limited situations such as when a 

vendor’s name has changed. 

Additionally, when you create a new vendor, customer, employee, or user, a related contact is 

often created simultaneously based on specific fields in the record. See Creating a Contact from a 

Record (on page 643) to learn about which specific fields in each record create the related 

Suggested contact name. 

To create a more detailed contact record, fill in each tab on the Contact information page. 

Filling In Contact Information 

On the Contact information tab: 

1. 
Type the contact name. 

---


<!-- Page 651 -->
Chapter 16: Contacts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
This name isn’t necessarily the name that is used throughout your company because 

actual names aren’t always unique. For example, a name such as “Jose Hernandez” 

could be the same as a completely different contact in your company. 

• 
The system automatically suggests a unique Suggested contact name and Print as 

name based on the naming details you enter. 

2. 
Add the Primary email address, Primary phone number, and Company name for the 

contact.  

In the Property Management application, the system uses the primary email address that 
you enter here to fill in email addresses for emailing statements.  

3. 
Type a Suggested contact name if you want a different version than the one the system 

auto-populates. This name appears in lists and drop-down lists. 

After you save the contact, the Suggested contact name can’t be edited. 

4. 
Enter the Print as name if you want a different version to appear on printed documents than 

the one the system auto-populates. 

Filling In Mailing Information 

On the Mailing information tab, add the mailing address for the contact. 

Filling In Additional Information 

On the Additional information tab, enter any secondary information you might have. This 

includes phone, URL, and taxable information. 

Marking a Contact to Be an Owner or Investor 

On the Reporting portal tab, select the This is an owner-Investor check box if you plan to include 

the contact as an owner or investor. This option enables the owners and investors to receive 

financial reports and other documents through the portal.  

Only contacts that are marked as an owner or investor will appear in the Contact drop-down list 
when you add a new Reporting Portal owner or investor record. Investor records are associated 
with the Investor Tracking application. Owner records, in this case, are associated with the 

Reporting portal application. They are not associated with the Owner records in the Condo and 

Co-op application and its Owner portal. 

Saving the Contact Record 

After providing the available information, click the Save button. 

To add another contact with the same information, click the Duplicate button. Everything is 

identical except for the Suggested contact name. Make any necessary changes, and then click the 

Save button.

##### Changing the Suggested Contact Name
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 656*

Contacts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Changing the Suggested Contact Name 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contacts > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Search & Find > Contacts > Edit`


When you change the name of a vendor, customer, user, or employee, the Suggested contact 

name of the related contact doesn’t automatically update because it is a unique ID used across 

the system by various records. Unfortunately, you can’t change the Suggested contact name of a 

contact record after you create the record for the same reason. Instead, you’ll need to create and 

associate a new contact record with the appropriate record and then inactivate or delete the old 

contact record. 

For example, you create a vendor record and contact record simultaneously so that their names 

match. However, a few months later, you are required to change the name of your vendor and 

now the Suggested contact name of your associated contact record does not match the new 

name of the updated vendor record. First, you create a new contact record with the appropriate 

Suggested contact name, and then you associate that contact with your vendor record. 

Afterward, you can inactivate or delete the old contact record. 

To change the suggested contact name: 

1. 
Go to the record for which you want to change the related contact record, and then click the 

Edit link next to the record. For example, if you changed the name of a customer recently, 

go the Customers list in Accounts Payable, then click the Edit link next to the customer. 

2. 
On the Contact list tab, click Add to add a new contact to the record. 

3. 
Click the Contact drop-down list, and then choose the contact with the correct Suggested 

contact name, or click Add to add a new contact to which you can set the correct 

Suggested contact name. See Adding a Contact (on page 636) or Editing a Contact (on 

page 638) for more information on your options. 

4. 
Set a Category for your new contact in the Contacts list. 

5. 
Select your new contact from the Primary contact drop-down list from above. Repeat as 

necessary for other required contact fields in the record. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Go to the Contacts list in Company. 

8. 
Inactivate or delete a contact record (on page 638) that no longer has the correct 

Suggested contact name.  

You can no longer restore a contact record after you delete it. If you are unsure, inactivate 
the record instead.

##### Creating a Contact from a Record
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 657*

Chapter 16: Contacts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Creating a Contact from a Record 

You can create new contacts as you create new vendor, customer, employee, or user records. The 

related contact, specifically the Suggested contact name, is created from specific fields 

depending on the kind of record you are creating. 

The Suggested contact name is a unique ID field that can’t be edited after creating the contact 
record. Be sure that the related field is correct before saving. See Changing the Suggested 
Contact Name (on page 641 ) for more details. 

Record Type 
Suggested Contact Name 

Vendor or Customer 
When you create a new related contact through a new vendor or 

customer record, the Suggested contact name is saved as Print as + V + 

Vendor ID for vendor records and Print as + C + Customer ID for 

customer records.  

For example, a vendor named Example.com with a vendor ID of 142 

would create a contact with the Suggested contact name of 

Example.com (V142). Similarly, a customer named Frank Smith with a 

customer ID of 1557 would create a contact with Frank Smith (C1557) as 

the Suggested contact name. 

Creating a new vendor or customer always automatically creates a new 

related contact unless you specifically select the Exclude from the 

company contact list check box when you create the record. You may 

want to use this option if you want to keep your contacts consistent with 

your company’s naming convention. 

Employee 
You must choose an existing contact or create a new contact using the 

Primary contact name field when you create a new employee record. 

If the employee is also a RealPage Accounting user, you must select the 

same primary contact name that you used for the employee’s user record. 

User 
When you create a new user, the system automatically creates a new 

contact based on the user ID if you do not select a contact in the Contact 

name field.  

For example, if the user ID of the new user is “jwilliams,” then the system 

assigns “jwilliams” as the related contact, unless you select a contact 

name when creating the user account. 

If the user is also an employee in RealPage Accounting, you must select 

the same contact name that you used in the user’s employee record to 

ensure that permissions work properly.

##### Adding a Transaction Currency
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 665*

Chapter 17: More 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding a Transaction Currency 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Multi-currency > Transaction Currencies > Add`


To add a currency: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Multi-currency section, select the Transaction currencies menu option. The 

Transaction currencies list opens. 

If you do not see the Transaction currencies option in the menu, check to make sure that 
multi-currency management is enabled for your company. See Enabling Multi-Currency 
Management for more information. 

3. 
Click the Add button. 

Filling In the Currency Section 

In the Currency section, click the Currency code drop-down list, and then select the currency you 

want. The system completes the Currency name and ISO-4217 numeric code fields. 

Filling In the Format Section 

1. 
In the Currency format drop-down list, select the nationality of the currency. 

The remaining fields automatically populate with the selected country’s standard format 

settings. You can edit these fields as needed. 

2. 
In the Currency unit drop-down list, select the major unit of currency, such as dollars, 

pounds, or yen. 

3. 
In the Currency subunit drop-down list, select the sub-unit of currency, such as cents, 

pence, or centavos. 

4. 
In the Currency symbol drop-down list, select the standard currency symbol. 

5. 
In the Thousand separator drop-down list, select the symbol that separates numbers into 

thousands—usually a comma. 

6. 
In the Decimal separator drop-down list, select the symbol that separates decimals— 

usually a period. 

7. 
In the Alignment drop-down list, select “Left” or “Right” to align the monetary units. This 

controls whether the currency symbol displays to the left or to the right of the number. 

Under Currency sample, the system displays a preview of how the currency will appear with the 
current settings.

Company Messages List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Company Messages`


The Company messages page lets you enter short announcements or reminders to share with 

users in the company. For example, you can remind employees to submit their weekly timesheets 

by Friday or announce the next company holiday. 

Where do company messages appear? 

Company messages appear on the Message board. The Message board is located on right side 

of the Home page. You can also add the Message board to any dashboard. 

The Message board displays only five messages at a time, sorted by priority, and then by date. 

Each posted message displays the date the message was posted followed by the subject of the 

message. Under the subject line, the first 100 characters of the message appears, followed by the 

name of the user who posted the message. 

To display the details for a specific message, click the View link. The Company message 

information page displays the subject, who posted the message, the post date, last updated date, 

valid until date, view level, priority, message text, and the current status.

Adding a Company Message 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Company Messages`


To add a company message: 

1. 
Type the Subject of the message. It appears next to the date on the Message board. 

2. 
In the Valid until field, select or enter the date on which the message expires. The message 

expires at midnight on the date you specify. 

Even after expiration, messages remain in the system until deleted. RealPage recommends 

that you periodically delete unnecessary expired messages from the system, even if they are 

set to inactive. 

3. 
In the View level drop-down list, select the types of users that can see the message. Only 

users with the selected user type can view the message. 

• 
All Users: This includes Employee, Product Manager, Platform, and Payment Approver 

user types. 

• 
Business Users: This includes Business user types. 

• 
Administrators: This includes Business user types with some or all Admin privileges. 

4. 
In the Priority drop-down list, select “Urgent,” “High,” or “Normal.” The message list and 

message board are sorted by priority, and then by last update.  

5. 
Type the Message text. You can type a maximum of 4000 characters, but RealPage 

recommends that you keep the messages short, limiting the message length to 100 

characters or less.

User Permissions Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > User Permissions Report`


When run at the top level, the User Permissions report lists all of the user permissions for the top 

level and for every entity underneath it.  

This report allows administrators to view users and roles so they can audit and maintain the user 

base without looking up each team member individually. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the User Permissions report: 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

General ledger 
User Permissions Report 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

User Permissions Report Options 

View a full report 

If you want to see every result for a particular category, do not make selections from any of the 

data entry boxes. You can run this report without entering any search information. If you do that, 

however, the report may take a long time to run and may return too many results to be useful.  

To run a full report: 

1. 
When the report settings screen appears, click the View button.  

The system opens a report showing all results for the default reporting period.  

2. 
To refine the report, click the Customize button to return to the main report screen, and 

follow the steps in customizing and running this report. 

Customize and run 

Before running the report, you can select the types of items to include as well as specify how you 

want the report to appear. 

---


<!-- Page 676 -->
More 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

To customize and run a report: 

1. 
Set the filters to get the specific data you want. 

• 
Using filters, you can include or exclude specific types of data in the report. 

• 
As a general rule, to get fewer and more precise results in your report, set more filters. 

2. 
Format the report. 

Format options vary from report to report. You can set the layout of the report and arrange 

how to group and display the data contained in the report. 

3. 
Enter a title, subtitle, and footer for your report. 

You can use trial-and-error to get the precise results you want. Fill in the desired boxes, and then 

click the View button to see the report in your browser. If after viewing the results, you want to 

refine the report further, click the Customize button to return to the report setup page. Repeat 

this process until you’re satisfied.  

Filters 

Use the filters to focus the results of your report. Filters enable you to include or exclude specific 

types of objects in the report, such as location, role, or user. You can set any combination of 

filters. To get fewer and more precise results in your report, you can set more filters. 

Format 

Use this section to specify the sort order and to change the page layout of the report. 

Titles 

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the print versions of this report. Export to Excel or .CSV, 

or click the Print button for a .PDF version. 

To add a title, subtitle, and footer to the report:  

1. 
In Report title 1, type the main report title.  

• 
This title displays in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company 

name.  

• 
You can type over any default name that the system may have automatically supplied 

in this box. 

2. 
In Report title 2, type the subtitle.  

This subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the footer. Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title and subtitle, and footer.  

---

KPI Setup Page

A KPI setup record tells the system which KPI data to collect for a property type. 

Use this page to create a KPI setup for each property type, and then add the entities and locations 

of that type to the setup. 

This page has four sections: 

• 
Summary: This section displays the type and description of the property for which the KPIs 

are being defined. 

• 
Mapped account groups to generate financial KPIs: This section lists the KPI and the 

account group to which it is mapped. This section is not editable here; to edit a mapping, 

see Mapping Financial KPIs to Account Groups (on page 669). 

• 
Mapped entities/locations: This section lists the mapped entities and locations for which 

you can generate KPIs. For more information, see Mapping Entities and Locations. 

• 
KPI: This section lists the KPIs that will be generated based on this KPI setup.

Key Performance Indicators List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > More > View KPIs`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Key Performance Indicators > Create`


RealPage Accounting calculates and captures key performance indicators (KPIs) on a monthly 

basis, combining the financial results of subsidiary companies into the financial results of the 

parent company.  

You can either use the standard financial KPI set or create a custom set of KPIs for a property 

type. The standard financial set of KPIs includes: 

• 
A/R balance 

• 
Net operating income 

• 
Net cash flow 

• 
Total operating expense 

• 
Total revenue 

• 
Unit turnover 

• 
Rental income 

• 
Rental losses 

• 
Move in fees 

• 
Other income 

• 
Payroll and related 

• 
Administrative 

• 
Marketing 

• 
Utilities 

• 
Operating and maintenance 

• 
Taxes 

• 
Insurance 

You can’t create a custom KPI in RealPage Accounting; however, you can enter the information in 
a statistical account and then use that information in a calculation for a financial report.

 Add button next to the View KPIs menu option.

focus advances to the next row.

fields, custom fields, and descriptions of the required data for each field.

 KPIs Setup`


•

• 
YEAR: Type the year of the KPI data. 

3. 
Optionally, add data in the remaining columns of the template. Refer to the data template 

for KPIs for the names and valid values of the remaining columns.  

4. 
Save the template as a CSV file. 

5. 
On the Import data page, click the corresponding Import link for Key performance 

indicators. The system opens the Key Performance Indicators box. 

6. 
Import your file into the system. See Importing the CSV file for more information.

Generating KPI Data 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > More > Generate KPIs`


Filter and format the data before you generate KPIs.  

Filtering KPI Data 

Use the Filters section to filter the KPI data that the system generates. 

1. 
In the Type drop-down list, select the desired property type for which you want to retrieve 

KPI data. 

2. 
In the Calculate from and Calculate to drop-down lists, select a range of months for which 

you want to retrieve KPI data. 

You cannot manually calculate KPIs for the current month. 

3. 
In the Year field, type the year to retrieve KPI data starting with a specific year. 

4. 
In the Location field, click the Select button to select the location(s) for which you want to 

retrieve KPI data. For more information, see Using the Multi-Select Box. 

5. 
Select the Calculate operational KPIs or Calculate financial KPIs check boxes to generate 

operational KPIs, financial KPIs, or both. 

The option to calculate operational KPIs applies only to Affordable, Conventional, 
Multifamily, Senior Living, and Student Living property types. 

Formatting KPI Data 

Use the Format section to organize the KPI data. 

1. 
In the Sort by drop-down list, select how you want to sort the list of locations in the 

resulting KPI data. 

• 
Location: Sort locations alphabetically by [Location ID] - [Location name]. 

• 
Prior closed period: Sort locations by the date in the Prior closed period field of the 

location. 

2. 
Click the Apply filters button to populate a list of locations that match the filter settings, or 

select the Clear filters button to reset the filters if you want to start over. 

The list of locations includes the following columns: 

• 
Select: Use this check box to select the locations for which to generate KPIs. If a 

location’s check box is not selectable, the location is not eligible for KPI generation. 

The reason it is not eligible is provided in the KPI status column. 

• 
Location: The location is formatted as [Location ID] – [Location Name].

Customizing and Running a Service Ticket Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Reports > Service Ticket Report`


To customize and run the Service Ticket report: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select Company, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, select the Service ticket report option. 

The report parameters page opens. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can use one of the predefined reporting periods available from the Reporting period and As 

of date fields, or create your own reporting period using the Start date and End date fields. You 

can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both.  

In the Time period section, do one of the following: 

• 
Use the Reporting period drop-down list to select the desired reporting period, and then 

type a date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button and select a date. These 

periods are relative to the As of date. All periods begin on the first day of the period—that 

is, the first day of the month/quarter/year you select. For example, select Prior month as the 

reporting period, and then select a vendor to limit the report to a list of invoices from that 

vendor. 

• 
Type a specific Start date and/or a specific End date or click the 
 Calendar button in 

each field and select the desired date(s). 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

• 
Select Prompt on run to have the system prompt you for this information at runtime. 

If you don’t specify a reporting period and you don’t select Prompt on run, then the generated 
report uses the current month to date. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Optionally, you can filter the report by location, ticket status, and ticket category. 

In the Filters section, select one or more filters: 

• 
Select a location or location group from the Location drop-down list. 

---


<!-- Page 700 -->
Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Select one or more ticket statuses from the Status drop-down list. 

• 
Select one or more ticket categories from the Category drop-down list. 

Filling In the Format Section 

Choose a page layout option for the report, either Portrait or Landscape. 

Filling In the Titles Section 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the PDF version of the report (click Print to get the PDF version). 

1. 
By default, the system completes the Report title 1 field with the system-assigned report 

name. This title displays in large type at the top of the page directly under your company 

name. You can leave the title as the default, or change it by typing over the default name in 

Report title 1.  

2. 
In Report title 2, type the text that you want to appear under the title of the report. This 

subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. Footer text 

displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

Running the Report 

When you are finished customizing the report, choose a report output: 

• 
To view the report in your browser, click View. 

• 
To view the report in a printable format, click Print. 

• 
To process and store the report, click Process & store. 

• 
To add the report to a dashboard, click Add to dashboard. 

• 
To memorize the report, click Memorize. 

• 
To export the report to an Excel or CSV file, click Export, and then select Excel or CSV.

#### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 703*

Chapter 18: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 690) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized—that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead.

#### Storing Standard Reports and Charts
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 706*



##### Viewing a Stored Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 706*

Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

You can process and store the report or chart either before or after viewing it. 

Viewing a Stored Report 

After the system runs the report on the date that you selected, you can find the report in either 

the My stored reports list or the Reports center. 

To view a stored report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Open the application where you created the report. 

2. 
Select the My stored reports option located in the Reports column of the menu. 

The My stored reports list opens with a list of reports stored in the application. 

3. 
Find the report that you want to view and then verify the report date in the Run date/time 

column. Verifying the report date helps you avoid missing data. For example, if you 

scheduled the report to run two weeks ago, you would be missing the last two weeks of 

data. 

4. 
Click one of the following links to open your report in the format it was stored:  

• 
HTML: Opens the report in a new browser tab as a web page. 

• 
PDF: Opens a printable PDF version of the report that you can print and download. 

• 
CSV: Downloads a CSV file containing the report data. This is a good format to 

download if you want to import the data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Downloads the report as an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Opens a text version of the report in the web browser. 

• 
View Status: Opens the report in your configured cloud account. If there is no cloud 

link for the report, see Storing a Report in a Cloud Storage Location (on page 697). 

• 
Success: Opens the report in Reporting Portal. If there was an error processing the 

report, then the View status link appears in the column instead. See Viewing a Report 

Error Log for error details. 

If you have not yet processed the report offline, then click the Create offline link to process 
the report.

##### Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 711*

Chapter 18: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Only the Printable and Excel options are available for report groups. When storing report 
groups as an Excel file, each report appears on a separate tab. 

6.

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or 

Amazon S3. If you are a developer, you can also deliver the report to another application using 

HTTP. 

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets (on page 431) in RealPage Accounting. The 

targets that you define will be available as storage options for reports. 

To store a report in a cloud-storage target: 

1. 
Locate the report, and then select the option to process or run it. 

• 
Financial reports: Click the Process & store link. 

• 
Report groups: Click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Display the report, and then click the Process & store button. 

The Storage options page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule section, type or select the date on which to run the report in the Run report 

on field. 

Additional fields may appear if you have set up financial reports to prompt for filters at 
runtime. See Prompting for Filters at Runtime . 

If you are running a report group, a different set of fields will appear. See Running a Report 
Group on Demand. 

3. 
Select the Store in cloud check box. 

4. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the 

report.  

By default, you can choose from cloud-storage targets that either you ’ve defined or that 
others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, you can see all cloud 
targets.

#### Memorized Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 719*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 719*

Chapter 18: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Memorized Reports 

See the How to Get Here (on page 705) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Memorizing a report retains the report parameters so you don’t have to select them each time 

you want to run or display the report. When you memorize a report, you can assign it a unique 

name so you can add the report to dashboards or report groups or schedule it to run on a 

recurring basis. We recommend that you test run the report with the desired parameters to verify 

that the report output is correct before memorizing the report. 

A memorized report can be public or private. Public reports are available to all system users. 
Private reports are available only to the report owner and system administrators. 

Memorized Reports Locations 

Memorized reports appear in the Memorized reports list (on page 707) and in the Reports 

center. 

The Memorized reports list is accessible from most RealPage Financial Suite applications; 

however, it displays only the reports that were memorized in the application you access it from. 

For example, if you click the Memorized reports option in the Cash Management menu, then the 

list will include only reports memorized in Cash Management. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Memorizing a report requires that you have the permissions to do so. You must have permissions 

to access and run a report in order to memorize it. Permissions for users, groups, or roles are 

configured in the Company setup. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

---

How to Get Here

Reports > Memorized Reports`

Memorizing a Report or Chart 

To memorize a report or chart: 

1. 
Set up a report or chart with the filters and parameters that you want to save. 

2. 
Click the Memorize button. The Memorize report parameters box opens. 

3. 
In the Name field, type a name for the report or chart. 

If you plan to make the report or chart public, give it a name that is easily identifiable to 
others. 

4. 
Select the Public check box to make the report or chart available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to keep it private. Private reports and charts are 

visible only to the person who created them (owners), and administrators. 

5. 
Click OK.

Memorized Reports List

##### Editing a Memorized Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 722*

Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Editing a Memorized Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 705) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

You can edit a memorized report or chart only if you are the owner or a system administrator, 

even if the report or chart was made public. As the owner, you can change any parameter, 

including who owns it. The only field you cannot change is the report type.  

To edit a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, click the Edit link next to the report or chart that you want to 

change. The Edit memorized report page opens. The fields on this page correspond with 

the report’s type.  

2. 
Update the fields in the General information section as needed: 

• 
In the Report name and Report description fields, type a new name and description 

for the report, respectively. 

• 
In the Report owner drop-down list, select a different user to be the owner of the 

report. If you change the report’s owner, then you will no longer be able to edit this 

memorized report after you save the changes. However, you can continue to run the 

report if it’s still public.  

• 
Select the Public check box to make the report available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to make the report private; that is, 

available only to yourself and system administrators. 

Others can see private memorized reports by selecting the Include private check box 
in their Memorized reports list. 

3. 
Modify the other settings as needed. 

4. 
Click Save. 

---



##### Running a Memorized Report or Chart
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 723*



##### Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 723*

Chapter 18: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Running a Memorized Report or Chart 

See the How to Get Here (on page 705) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

To run a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, find the report or chart you want to view, and then click the 

Run link.  

2. 
In the Select report type drop-down list, select a format for the report or chart output:  

• 
HTML: Saves the report as an HTML file so you can view it in your web browser. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report as a comma-separated value (CSV) file so you can import the 

data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Saves the report as an Excel file so you can manipulate the data further. 

• 
Text: Saves the report as a basic text file.  

Charts are only available in Printable and HTML format. 

3. 
Click OK to run the report. 

• 
If you selected Printable, HTML, or Text, then the report opens in a new window. 

• 
If you selected CSV or Excel, then the system saves the report in your local Downloads 

folder. 

You can also run a memorized report from the Reports center. 

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here (on page 705) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

---


<!-- Page 724 -->
Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report (on page 715) page 

opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report (on page 715) page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use. 

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 

---


<!-- Page 725 -->
Chapter 18: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

• 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send 

the report results, and then click Save. 

Storing and Delivering the Report 

1. 
Select one or more delivery options for the report: 

• 
Email: Sends the report in an email. 

• 
Store report: Stores the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Store in cloud: Stores the report in a cloud-storage target. 

• 
Store in Reporting Portal: Stores the report in the selected owner portal(s). 

2. 
Fill in the fields corresponding with each section. 

Email 

1. 
In the To field, type the email address to which you want to send the report.

Select the CC me check box if you want the system to send a copy of the email message to 

your inbox.

In the Subject field, type the subject of the email message.

• 
HTML: Sends the report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Sends the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Sends the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file.

#### Users List

##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 740*

Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Users List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users`


Each RealPage Accounting user must have a unique user record. Users are individuals who have 

access to some part of the system; however, that access can vary widely from user to user. 

Normally, users are employees, but they can also be people from outside your company, such as 

accountants, attorneys, bankers, vendors, customers, or auditors. 

The Users list is where administrators manage users. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add and edit users. 

• 
Manage user permissions and roles. 

• 
View a list of a user’s group memberships. 

• 
Adjust a user’s preferences. 

• 
Access a user’s dashboards. 

• 
Delete users. 

• 
Export a list of users. 

If your company has migrated to Unified Platform, then all user management must be handled in 
Unified Platform. You will not be able to add or update users, user groups, or user roles in 
RealPage Accounting. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with user accounts: 

Application 
Activities/Lists Permissions 

Administration 
Users 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete, Permissions, Groups, 

Impersonate 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

---



##### Adding Users
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 741*

Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding Users 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > 
 Users`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users > Add`


Any user that wants to sign in must have a unique user record. The User information page 

enables administrators to create and edit users.  

For each user, you can: 

• 
Specify their user ID and contact information. 

• 
Reset a user’s password. 

• 
Inactivate a user, which effectively removes them from the system. 

• 
Select other access options, such as making them a full or limited administrator and 

enabling additional sign-in verification steps. 

Prerequisites 

• 
To add a user, you need full or limited Admin privileges and must also have access in the 

Company application to list, view, add, and edit users. To add another user with Admin 

privileges, you need full Admin privileges. 

• 
To add a user at the top level of a multi-entity shared company, you can’t be restricted to 

particular entities or departments. If you don’t see an Add button in the Users list, verify 

that nothing is specified on the User entities and User departments tabs of your user 

record. 

• 
Any time you add or edit a user (including resetting a user’s password), be prepared to 

enter your administrator password. This verification protects a user’s information from 

unsanctioned or unlawful access. 

• 
If you are creating a user that is also an employee, customer, or vendor, add them to the 

Customers, Vendors, or Employees list first, and then add them as a user. This enables you 

to select their existing contact record on the User information page, and also ensures that 

their user record is linked to their function as a customer, vendor, or employee. 

Add Basic User Information 

Fill in the User information tab: 

1. 
In the User ID field, type a unique ID for the new user. 

You can’t edit this field after you save the user record. 

2. 
Type the user’s Last name and First name. 

3. 
Type the user’s Email address. This field is required for verification purposes whenever the 

user initiates or requests a password reset. 

---


<!-- Page 742 -->
Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

This email address must match the primary email address of the associated contact 
name. 

4. 
In the Contact name drop-down list, select the user’s name if the user already exists in the 

system. Otherwise, the system automatically creates a contact name with the user record. 

A user ID combined with a password provides access to the company while a contact name 
can be a person who is not necessarily a user in the company, such as a vendor or customer 
contact. 

5. 
In the User name field, type a name to identify the person in the Users list. 

6. 
In the Report to drop-down list, select the person to whom the user directly reports. 

7. 
Select the level of Admin privileges. A user with administrator privileges is given the highest 

possible level of system access, including the ability to configure and subscribe to 

applications, create users, and assign permissions to users. 

• 
Off: Select this option if you do not want the user to be an administrator. 

• 
Limited: Select this option to give the user administrator privileges except the ability 

to create full administrators or access all features in Platform Services. 

• 
Full: Select this option to give the user permissions for appropriate tasks, such as 

creating users, subscribing to applications or modules, payment information, and so 

on. 

8. 
Select the user Status. 

• 
Active: This is the default status, which allows the user to log in and access the system. 

• 
Lockedout: This status prevents the user from logging in to the system. Administrators 

can change a user’s status to Lockedout if the user exceeds the allowable number of 

login attempts. 

• 
Inactive: This status retains the user information in your system but hides the user 

from lists. If you wish to see inactive users, select the Include inactive check box in the 

list. 

New users can be created only with a status of Active or Lockedout. You can edit a user 
after creation to change its status to Inactive. 

9. 
Select the RealPage contact check box if the user is a RealPage employee. 

10. 
Select the Site user check box if the user accesses the Spend Management site. 

11. 
Select the Budget variance analysis user check box to allow the user to use the Budget 

Variance Analysis feature. If you select this option, an additional tab labeled Budget 

variance analysis appears in the user record. 

12. 
Select the Keep password until admin resets it check box to exempt the user from adhering 

to the company password change duration setting. 

---


<!-- Page 743 -->
Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

This setting should be used only in situations where software automatically logs into the 
Web Services API. 

13. 
Select the Owner document approval level required for this user. 

Assign Role-Based Permissions 

When you enable the role-based permissions feature, the system automatically creates and 

assigns a role for each existing user. You can keep the assigned role, remove it, or select another 

role. System-generated roles are denoted by “::SYS::” in the name. 

If your company has not enabled the role-based permissions feature, the system opens the User 

applications subscriptions page after you click Save. On this page, you can choose applications 

you want the user to access, and control which functional areas the user has permission to use in 

the selected application. If a user is a member of a group that already has the required role 

assigned to it, then you do not need to assign it here. 

To assign a role to a user: 

1. 
On the Roles information tab, click the drop-down arrow on a line item under the Role 

name column, and then select a role that you want to assign to the new user. 

2. 
Add other roles that you want to assign. 

3. 
Click the Save button. 

Add Entity Restrictions 

Top level users are restricted to the entities listed on this tab. These restrictions determine which 

entities you can switch to or use as a dimension on a transaction, and how much data you can see 

in reports, transactions, and other data records. 

• 
Users without any listed restrictions have access to all entities in the multi-entity company. 

• 
Users restricted to a single entity sign in to the system at the top level. They can switch to 

the entity as needed. 

• 
Users restricted to two or more entities only have access to entities listed on this tab. 

Entity restrictions also restrict the data a user might see in a report or transaction. It also 
restricts their ability to create transactions and other data that asks them to choose specific 
entities. 

To include entity restrictions: 

1. 
On the User entities tab, click the drop-down arrow on a line item under the 

Entity/locations groups column, and then select an entity or location group to which you 

want to restrict the user. The entities that you select are the only entities and locations that 

the user can view. 

---


<!-- Page 744 -->
Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
You can select location groups containing entities, locations, and both entities and 

locations. 

• 
If you are restricted to only locations in a location group, then logging in will display 

the top level. The records that are created will always be at the top level, not the entity 

level. 

• 
You cannot select a location group that has locations with no parent entity tagged. 

• 
You cannot select a location group without sublocations. 

Entities that appear in the list include both active and ordered entities. Be sure to select 
only entities that are active. 

2. 
Add entity or location groups as required. 

3. 
Click the Save button. 

Add User Department Restrictions 

Any user of a multi-entity company, whether at the top level or at the entity level, can be 

restricted to work with and see specific departments only, which may affect what data they can 

see in reports, transactions, and other data records. 

• 
Users without any listed restrictions have access to all departments in the multi-entity 

company. 

• 
Users with one or more departments in their restriction list are able to see those specific 

departments only. 

If a user has specified department restrictions, they may experience different results when 
running reports because the report data is limited to their department restrictions. The 
restrictions may also affect their ability to view or create transactions or other data records 
that include departments that are not in their restriction list. 

To add department restrictions: 

1. 
On the User departments tab, click the drop-down arrow on a line item under the 

Department column, and then select the department to which you want to restrict the user. 

2. 
Add department restrictions as required. 

3. 
Click the Save button. 

Add User Territory Restrictions 

Any user of a multi-entity company, whether at the top level or at the entity level, can be 

restricted to work with and see specific territories only, which may affect what data they can see in 

reports, transactions, and other data records. 

Because customers can be assigned to specific territories, restricting a user by territory 
impacts which customers they can see and use in transactions and reports. 

---


<!-- Page 745 -->
Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

• 
Users without any listed restrictions have access to all territories in the multi-entity 

company. 

• 
Users with one or more territories in their restriction list are only able to see those specific 

territories and customers associated with those territories. 

If a user has specified territory restrictions, they may experience different results when running 

reports because the report data is limited to their territory restrictions. The restrictions may also 

affect their ability to view or create transactions or other data records that include territories that 

are not in their restriction list. 

To add territory restrictions: 

1. 
On the User territories tab, click the drop-down arrow on a line item under the Territory 

column, and then select a territory to which you want to restrict the user. 

2. 
Add territory restrictions as required. 

3. 
Click the Save button. 

Set Up Budget Variance Analysis 

If you marked the user as a Budget variance analysis user, then fill in the Budget variance 

analysis tab: 

1. 
In the Notify when complete drop-down list, select the role or user group to notify when 

the user completes a budget variance analysis. 

When a user is marked as a Site user and a Budget variance analysis user, the Notify when 

complete field is required.  

2. 
Select the Omit from data ready notifications check box to prevent the system from 

notifying the user when data is ready for analysis. 

3. 
Select the Edit comments made by other users check box if you want the user to be able to 

edit comments made by other users. 

4. 
In the Restricted accounts/account groups section, select the accounts or account groups 

that the users cannot access. For example, Payroll is typically included in this list. 

If no accounts or account groups are selected, then the users can access and make notes on 

all accounts, account groups, and groups of account groups.  

5. 
Click Save. 

Assign a OneSite name 

On the Remote authentication tab, type a OneSite sign on name to link the user’s OneSite 

sign-in name to the RealPage Accounting user record. 

Enter Audit Details 

On the Audit tab, type the name of the user who amended the record.

Making an Employee a User 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup

#### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 751*

Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

---



##### Assigning Permissions for a New Feature
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 752*

Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Assigning Permissions for a New Feature 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users > Subscriptions > Permissions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > Permissions`


When RealPage adds a new feature, it often comes with new permissions that you must enable 

before users can use the new feature. 

To add permissions for a new feature: 

• 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

If using Role-based permissions 

1. 
Select Roles. 

2. 
Find the role that you want to change. 

3. 
Click the Subscriptions link.  

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions window opens. 

5.

##### Restricting Users From Editing Specific Tabs in Entity Records
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 753*

Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Restricting Users From Editing Specific Tabs in Entity Records 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > (Company) Permissions`


You can limit the tabs on which users can add or edit information in entity records (on page 486). 

Each tab is tied to an individual user permission. By disabling permissions for a tab, you disable 

the user from editing information on that tab. These restrictions apply when the user is: 

• 
Adding a new entity 

• 
Importing entities 

• 
Editing an entity 

• 
Updating an entity via import 

As long as the user has permissions to manage entities, they will still be able to view disabled 
tabs in read-only mode. For example, if you do not give the user permission to the 
Inter-entity 

setup tab, then they can view the Inter-entity setup tab but they can’t make any changes. 

To enable or disable entity tab permissions: 

1. 
In the Company application, select the Setup tab, and then click the Roles menu option. 

The Roles list opens. 

2. 
Click the Subscriptions link next to the role whose permissions you want to edit. 

The Roles subscriptions page opens. 

3. 
Click the Permissions link next to the Company application. 

The Company permissions page opens. 

4. 
Find the Entity tabs permission, and then select or clear the check boxes to enable or 

disable tabs, respectively. 

The Custom permission applies to any custom tabs created to include custom fields .  

5. 
Click Save.

<!-- Page 757 -->
Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Entity/Location 

groups 

Top-level users are restricted to the entities listed on this tab. These 

restrictions determine which entities you can switch to, use as a dimension 

on a transaction, and how much data you can see in reports, transactions, 

and other data records. 

Even though this tab appears on entity-level users, there is no further 

restriction that can be applied. 

• 
Users without any listed restrictions have access to all entities in the 

multi-entity company. They login to the top level and can slide-in to 

any entity. 

• 
Users restricted to a single entity automatically switch to the entity 

at login, and cannot access the top level after that. 

• 
Users restricted to two or more entities only have access to entities 

listed on this tab. They login to the top-level and can switch to one 

of their specified entities. 

In addition to where a user can navigate, entity restrictions also restrict the 

data a user might see in a report or transaction. It also restricts their ability 

to create transactions and other data that asks them to choose specific 

entities. 

Effects on running reports: Because RealPage takes the security of your 

financial data very seriously, users with entity restrictions can only see data 

on reports related to their specified entities. If any entity is not included in 

their restrictions list, then they cannot see report data related to those 

transactions which include those other entities as dimensions. 

Effects on viewing and creating data: Users with entity restrictions can only 

see transactions and other data related to their specified entities. If a 

transaction or some other record has data that includes an entity not on the 

user restriction list, then the user won’t be able to view that data. This also 

prevents users from creating new data or transactions that include an entity 

not listed in their restrictions tab, because the entity won’t even appear in 

the drop-down menu for selection.

#### Web Services Users
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 761*

Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Web Services Users 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Web Services Users`


Web Services users exchange information programmatically with RealPage Accounting via Web 

Services API calls. 

About Web Services Users 

Web Services users are like standard users in terms of how you set them up. They can have the 

same user types and Admin privileges as a standard user, but there are a few key differences, 

including: 

• 
Access to the RealPage Accounting API through Web Services only 

Web Services users are automatically limited to the API through Web Services access only, 

meaning they can’t sign on to your company through the UI. 

• 
Password remains until the Admin resets it 

Because many integrations rely on a Web Services user to execute certain functions, Web 

Services users’ passwords do not automatically expire. With Web Services users, an Admin is 

required to manually reset the password using the UI. Keep in mind that if you reset a Web 

Services user’s password, you may break an existing integration until you can update the 

password the integration uses. 

• 
Cannot have single sign-on (SSO) or multi-factor authentication (MFA) 

Because Web Services users are programmatic and do not log into the UI, both SSO and 

MFA are automatically disabled for them. 

A Web Services user ID does not grant you access to use Web Services itself. A Web Services 

sender ID is an additional credential which is required to send requests to a Web Services 

endpoint. You can obtain a sender ID by contacting your RealPage Accounting account 

representative. 

To view the details of an individual Web Services user, click the corresponding View link for that 

user. 

---
