Adding a Web Services User 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > 
 Web Services Users`


If you have an external application or integration that needs a unique user to exchange 

information with RealPage Accounting via Web Services API calls, then add a user for them here. 

Standard users can make Web Services requests to the API. However, as a security precaution, 
you should not provide a standard user’s credentials to any external application or integration 
that needs to make Web Services requests to your company via the API. Instead, you should 
create a separate Web Services user and provide those credentials. This also allows you to 
separately control the permissions to that application or integration on your own.

User Entities Tab 

This tab appears when the system is set up for a multi-entity company. 

Entity/Location 

Groups 

Top-level users are restricted to the entities listed on this tab. These 

restrictions determine which entities you can slide-in to, use as a 

dimension on a transaction, and how much data you can see in reports, 

transactions, and other data records. 

Even though this tab appears on entity-level users, there is no further 

restriction that can be applied. 

• 
Users without any listed restrictions have access to all entities in 

the multi-entity company. They login to the top level and can 

slide-in to any entity. 

• 
Users restricted to a single entity sign in at the top level and can 

slide in to the entity as needed. 

• 
Users restricted to two or more entities only have access to 

entities listed on this tab. They login to the top-level and can 

slide-in to one of their specified entities. 

In addition to where a user can navigate, entity restrictions also restrict 

the data a user might see in a report or transaction. It also restricts their 

ability to create transactions and other data that asks them to choose 

specific entities. 

Effects on running reports: Because RealPage takes the security of your 

financial data very seriously, users with entity restrictions can only see 

data on reports related to their specified entities. If any entity is not 

included in their restrictions list, then they cannot see report data 

related to those transactions which include those other entities as 

dimensions. 

Effects on viewing and creating data: Users with entity restrictions can 

only see transactions and other data related to their specified entities. If 

a transaction or some other record has data that includes an entity not 

on the user restriction list, then the user won’t be able to view that data. 

This also prevents users from creating new data or transactions that 

include an entity not listed in their restrictions tab, because the entity 

won’t even appear in the drop-down menu for selection. 

User Departments Tab 

This tab appears when the system is set up for a multi-entity company. 

---


<!-- Page 773 -->
Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Department 
Any user of a multi-entity company, whether at the top-level or at the 

entity-level, can be restricted to work with and see specific departments 

only, which may affect what data they can see in reports, transactions, 

and other data records. 

• 
Users without any listed restrictions have access to all 

departments in the multi-entity company. 

• 
Users with one or more departments included on their 

Department restrictions list are only able to see those specific 

departments. 

If a user has specified department restrictions, they may experience 

different results than expected when running reports because the report 

data they can see is limited to their department restrictions. They also 

won’t be able to view or create transactions or other data records that 

include a department other than the ones specified on their department 

restrictions tab. 

User Territories Tab 

This tab appears when the system is set up for a multi-entity company. 

Territory 
Any user of a multi-entity company, whether at the top-level or at the 

entity-level, can be restricted to work with and see specific territories 

only, which may affect what data they can see in reports, transactions, 

and other data records. 

Since customers can be assigned to specific territories, restricting a user 

by territory impacts which customers they can see and use in 

transactions and reports. 

• 
Users without any listed restrictions have access to all territories 

in the multi-entity company. 

• 
Users with one or more territories included on their Territory 

restrictions list are only able to see those specific territories, and, 

if you assign customers to territories, those customers 

associated with the territory. 

If a user has specified department restrictions, they may experience 

different results than expected when running reports because the report 

data they can see is limited to their territory restrictions. They also won’t 

be able to view or create transactions or other data records that include 

a customer associated with a territory other than the ones specified on 

their Territory restrictions tab.

External Users 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > External users`


An external user is one who accesses the company through a console company rather than 

signing on to the company directly. The External users list displays all external user records for 

the company. You can view and edit external user information from the list of external users. 

The External users list columns include: 

• 
Company ID: This column displays the ID of the company from which the external user is 

accessing your company. 

• 
Default user: This column indicates the default user associated with a particular external 

authorization.  

• 
User ID: This column displays the automatically generated external User ID. 

• 
User name: This column displays the external user’s name taken from the user’s record in 

the parent console. 

• 
Admin privileges: This column displays whether the external user has Full, Limited, or no 

administrator privileges. 

If your company has migrated to Unified Platform, then all user management must be handled in 
Unified Platform. You will not be able to add or update users, user groups, or user roles in 
RealPage Accounting. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

You must have Administrator level privileges to access the Administration application. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with external user accounts: 

Application 
Activities/Lists Permissions 

Administration 
Users 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete, Permissions, Groups 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

#### External Authorizations
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 780*

Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

External Authorizations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > External Authorizations`


An external authorization record allows another RealPage Accounting company to access your 

company externally for a specified time or until you disable the access. 

About external authorizations 

External authorization types include: 

• 
Consolidation: This is used by the Consolidation application in a multi-entity distributed 

environment. The subsidiary entity adds the external authorization record for the parent 

entity.  

• 
Practice: This is used by a console to link to a client or entity. The RealPage Accounting 

provisioning team creates this type of external authorization record for each applicable 

client or entity. A client or entity can disable this authorization record as applicable.  

• 
Services: This is used by a RealPage Accounting services provider company to perform 

services in another RealPage Accounting company. The company that wants the services 

creates this type of external authorization record for the RealPage Accounting services 

provider company. 

• 
Support: This is used by RealPage Accounting Support and Platform Services portals only. 

The system automatically creates a Support external authorization in every company and 

associates an “RealPage Accounting” external user with it. If you create and deploy a portal 

in Platform Services, the system creates a Support external authorization and associates a 

“portaluser” external user with it. 

An external authorization record is in effect until its Access field is set to “Disabled” or, for 

Services or Customer Support only, the expiration date has not been exceeded. 

---

Application 
Activities/Lists

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Adding an External Authorization 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > 
 External Authorizations`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > External Authorizations > Add`


You can only add an external authorization record for a parent consolidating company or for a 

service provider. The system automatically adds an external user for each company to which you 

give external authorization. 

To add an external authorization: 

1. 
In the Company ID field, type the ID of the company to which you are authorizing access.  

2. 
In the Access type drop-down list, select “Services” to give access to an external service 

provider, or select “Consolidation” to give access to your parent consolidating company. 

3. 
In the Description field, enter text to describe the need for the external authorization. 

4. 
In the Expiration date field, select or enter the date the external authorization record 

terminates. This field only applies if you select “Services” as the access type. 

The expiration date cannot exceed a date that is beyond the number of days the service 
provider company has specified as the maximum duration for service authorizations. If you 
enter a date that is beyond the service provider’s maximum duration, you receive an error 
message stating that the expiration date must be less than or equal to X days from today, 
where X is the number of days set by the external service provider.  

5. 
Click the Save button.

Editing an External Authorization

also edit the expiration date to extend or shorten the duration of the external authorization. 

To edit an external authorization:

Make the required changes.

Deleting or Disabling an External Authorization 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > External Authorizations`


You can only delete an external authorization record for a parent consolidating company. 

However, you can set the Access field to Disabled to prevent the external company from 

accessing your company but retain the external authorization for historical purposes. 

Deleting an External Authorization 

To delete an external authorization: 

1. 
In the External authorizations list, locate the record that you want to delete, and then click 

the corresponding Delete link. 

The system opens a delete confirmation box. 

2. 
Depending on your user preferences, you may have to confirm the delete by clicking OK. 

Disabling an External Authorization 

When an external authorization is disabled, no users associated with the external company 

associated with the external authorization can access your company externally. You can re-enable 

access later as desired.  

To disable an external authorization: 

1. 
In the External authorizations list, locate the record that you want to disable, and then click 
corresponding Edit link.  

The system opens the External authorization information page. 

2. 
In the Access drop-down list, select Disabled. 

3. 
Click Save.

#### User Groups
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 787*

Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

User Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Groups`


A user group is simply a group of users. However, used with role, dashboard, and financial report 

permissions, a user group becomes an efficient tool to manage many users and their permissions 

at once.  

To set overall permissions for a user group, you can assign a role to the user group, and every 

member of that group automatically inherits those permissions. For example, the Accounts 

Payable user group has the “A/P clerk” role, permitting users in that user group to report on and 

add invoices. To save time, you can also specify who can access a financial report or dashboard by 

user group rather than by individual user. If you move a user from one user group to another, 

then that user automatically inherits the permissions of their new user group. 

If your company has migrated to Unified Platform, then all user management must be handled in 
Unified Platform. You will not be able to add or update users, user groups, or user roles in 
RealPage Accounting. 

About the User Groups List 

From the User groups list, you can: 

• 
See the list of user groups for your company. 

• 
Edit user groups. 

• 
Click the Members link to add or remove members from the group. 

• 
Click the Roles assigned link to see the roles assigned to a user group. 

• 
Click Details to view the User Group Hierarchy report. This is useful if you have hierarchical 

user groups. 

How User Groups Streamline Permissions 

When you assign a user to a group, the user automatically inherits that group’s level of access. 

That means he or she has permission to access the same features and functions that every other 

group member has. This applies to: 

• 
Financial reports 

• 
Dashboards 

• 
Role-based permissions 

• 
Client company/entity access (for multi-entity console companies) 

Also, when you remove a user from one group and add that user to another group, that user’s 

access and permissions change accordingly.  

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 788*

Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Assigning Permissions Based On User Groups 

There are four areas of RealPage Accounting where you can save time by granting permissions to 

user groups, rather than individual users.  

• 
Roles: Assign roles to user groups (if you’re using role-based permissions). For example, you 

might set up an Accounts Payable user group with five members and then assign that group 

to the role of “A/P clerk.”  

• 
Financial reports: Grant or deny access to a specific report by user group.  

• 
Dashboards: Grant or deny access to a specific dashboard by user group.  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to work with user groups.

Application

Administration 
Users

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

On the User group information tab, fill in the required information. 

• 
In the Name field, enter a label to help identify the user group. 

After saving the user group, you can no longer change the name. 

• 
In the Description field, enter text to describe the user group.  

2. 
On the Roles information tab, assign roles to the group if your company uses role-based 

permissions. Roles can be assigned to both users and user groups. If a user is assigned more 

than one role (for example, if individually assigned roles and is also part of a group that has 

a role), the user gets the total permissions from all assigned roles. 

• 
Under Role name, click the drop-down arrow on a line item, and then select or add a 

role. System-generated roles are denoted by “::SYS::” 

User groups can also be used to efficiently assign permissions in other areas, such as dashboards 

and financial reports.  

• 
Roles: Assign roles to user groups (if you’re using role-based permissions). For example, you 

might set up an Accounts Payable user group with five members, and then assign that 

group to the role of “AP clerk.” 

• 
Financial reports: Grant or deny access to a particular report by user group. 

• 
Dashboards: Grant or deny access to a particular dashboard by user group.

This page is available only if your company is set to Role-based permissions on the Company 

information page. If your company has been migrated to Unified Platform, all user management 
must be handled in Unified Platform. You won’t be able to add or update a user or a user’s roles in 
RealPage Accounting after the migration has taken place. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

• 
You must have full administrator privileges to manage roles. 

• 
If your company has been migrated to Unified Platform, then your user roles must be 

handled in Unified Platform instead of RealPage Accounting. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage roles: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Administration 
Users

Groups, Impersonate 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a

##### Importing and Updating Multiple Roles
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 798*

Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

To switch back to your original user role, click the Switch back to my role button in the 

upper-right corner of the page. 

Importing and Updating Multiple Roles 

If you have multiple roles to add or update in your company, defining or updating roles one at a 

time can make for a tedious, time-intensive task. You can streamline the process and speed up 

implementations by importing new roles and updates that are ready to use into the company. 

You can use an exportable CSV file that contains role information directly based on any standard 

or custom list view. You can edit the resulting file, and then import your changes back into your 

company. The system processes your changes, and then validates each role. 

A CSV import works well for: 

• 
Updating information for multiple roles at once: Using a CSV import, you can update 

selected data for multiple roles. For example, if you export the Roles list with the Role name 

field included, you can modify the names in a spreadsheet application, and then import your 

changes. 

• 
Adding new roles to your existing Roles list: Using a CSV import, you can quickly add new 

roles without having to create the roles one at a time. Any spreadsheet row that contains a 

unique role name is added as a new record, provided all required information exists. 

Recommended precautions: 

• 
Make a backup of your role information before you make changes. Save a copy of the CSV 

for Import spreadsheet so that you have a record of the list before the update process. 

• 
Before making large-scale changes, test the update process. Try creating a few test roles, 

and then update just those records. 

• 
When you export the CSV for Import file, be sure to include the Role name column. This 

identifies the record that you are updating. 

Column order isn’t important; for example, the role name doesn’t need to be first. The header row 
identifies the contents of each column. 

Export the Roles list in “CSV for Import” format 

Before starting this process, it’s recommended that you create a custom view of your Roles list 

that includes the roles and columns you want to update. That way, when you export the list, you’ll 

have a spreadsheet that’s tailored to the information you want to change. 

1. 
On the Roles page, click the All drop-down menu, and then select the list view that includes 

the data you want to export. If you don’t select a view before exporting the Roles list, then 

your export file will include the list of roles and columns that you currently see in the list. 

2. 
In the Export drop-down list, select “CSV for Import.” 

---


<!-- Page 799 -->
Chapter 19: Users 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Update the CSV file 

The most important thing to remember when updating role records through CSV import is that 

changes you make in the spreadsheet affect your role records.  

• 
If you update spreadsheet data for a role, the information you specify overwrites the data in 

the existing role record.  

• 
If you remove data from the spreadsheet, the corresponding information is removed from 

the role records. 

Only overwrite existing data with blank data if you intend to remove that data from your list. For 
example, if you export the Role for user on field, which describes the type of company for which 
this role was created, and then clear the data in the Role type column of your spreadsheet, 
existing company types will be deleted when you import the file. 

1. 
Open the downloaded CSV for import file in a spreadsheet application. 

2. 
Update the spreadsheet.  

• 
You can update information for existing roles. For example, you might edit role names 

or descriptions.  

• 
You can also add new roles. If the role name that you specify doesn’t already exist, the 

system creates a new role record. 

3. 
Save the spreadsheet in .CSV format. 

Import your changes 

1. 
On the Roles page, click the Import button. 

The system opens the Import company information box. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then browse to locate the updated CSV for import file. 

3. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select your preferred format. 

4. 
In the File encoding drop-down list, select the applicable option. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box to complete the import process offline. 

6. 
In Email results to this address, specify the email address where results should be sent. If 

any records fail to import, you’ll be notified by email. 

7. 
Click the Import button. 

---

#### About Inter-Entity Account Mapping Plans
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 830*

Inter-Entity Account Mapping 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

About Inter-Entity Account Mapping Plans 

In a multi-entity shared environment, entities represent a separate tax identification or a 

separately secured, fully balancing set of books. Entities typically represent divisions, franchises, 

affiliates, associations, locations, chapters, self-balancing funds or subsidiaries managed by a 

common entity (central headquarters) using centralized payables and receivables and a common 

chart of accounts. 

Inter-entity transactions, such as those created when one entity pays a bill on behalf of another 

entity, are tracked separately from regular accounts receivable and accounts payable transactions. 

For each entity you define, you can specify the payable and receivable accounts to be used for 

inter-entity transactions. 

You can set up inter-entity transaction (IET) accounts for all your entities, and the relationships 

between these entities, on one central page. The inter-entity account mapping plan you choose 

enables you to select the type of plan you want to use to map your entities and define the IET 

accounts to be used between them. 

---



#### Inter-Entity Account Mapping Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 831*

Chapter 20: Inter-Entity Account Mapping 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Inter-Entity Account Mapping Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Inter-Entity Account Mapping > Edit`


You can use the Inter-entity account mapping page as the central location for defining 

inter-entity accounts (payable and receivable accounts) for entities and relationships between 

them. 

Depending on your company’s configuration, the page displays a Basic or Advanced mapping 

plan. 

Basic Mapping Plan 

Advanced Mapping Plan 

---



##### Mapping Example
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 832*

Inter-Entity Account Mapping 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Mapping Example 

Basic Mapping 

The company in this example has three entities: 100-US, 200-UK, and 300-AUS. 

• 
Select one inter-entity receivable (IER) account and one inter-entity payable (IEP) account 

per entity.  

For example, the US entity uses IER 1901 and IEP 2901 to transact lETs with UK and AUS 

entities. The inter-entity balance will not be separated among UK and AUS. 

Advanced Mapping 

The company in this example has five entities: 100-US. 200-UK, 300-AUS, 400-CAN, and 500-MEX. 

With the Advanced inter-entity mapping selected, you can map relationships between pairs of 

entities as needed. 

 To set up inter-entity maps for transactions between two entities, Entities A and B: 

• 
Select inter-entity receivable (IER) and inter-entity payable (IEP) accounts. 

For example, in the table below, the inter-entity balance is recorded in: 

• 
IER 1911 and IEP 2911 for the US entity when transacting with the UK. 

• 
IER 1921 and IEP 2921 for the UK entity when transacting with the US.  

In this case, when Entity A (the US entity) bills down to Entity B (the UK entity), IER 1911 is 

booked for Entity A and IEP 2921 is booked for Entity B. 

For each pair of entities, you can define specific inter-entity IER and IEP accounts to 
separate out inter -entity balances across different entity pairs. 

---



##### Importing Inter-Entity Account Mapping
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 833*

Chapter 20: Inter-Entity Account Mapping 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Importing Inter-Entity Account Mapping 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Inter-Entity Account Mapping > Edit`


You can use the import feature to: 

• 
Map accounts to entities or entity pairs in bulk. 

• 
Update account mapping in bulk. 

To import mapping information: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Inter-entity account mapping menu option. The Inter-entity account mapping 

page opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit button in the upper-right corner of the page. 

4. 
Click the Export template button. 

The system downloads the mapping template to your local drive as iet_config.csv. 

5. 
Open the file using a spreadsheet application. 

6. 
Enter the required information by filling in the columns with inter-entity receivable (IER) and 

inter-entity payable (IEP) accounts. These accounts will be used to post transactions for the 

pair of entities. 

7. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

8. 
Return to the Inter-entity account mapping page. 

9. 
Click the Import button. The Inter-entity account mapping import box opens. 

10. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you filled with data.  

11. 
In the Date format drop-down list, select a format that matches the date format in your CSV 

file. 

12. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 
Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 
encoding. 

13. 
Select the Process offline check box to move on to other tasks while a large file uploads in

a list of data import errors or to get notified when the upload is complete.

Click the Import button.

with the new information. 

16. 
Click Save.

Subscriptions Page

The Subscriptions page contains a list of applications, integrations, and custom packages that 

you can configure for a company in the RealPage Financial Suite to increase financial efficiency in 

your organization, drive growth, and allow you to integrate with external applications that you are 

already using. 

Only administrators can subscribe to, cancel, or configure applications. 

Applications Tab 

The following list provides a description of available applications and integrations. 

Applications and 

Integrations 

Description 

Accounts Payable 
Manage and track your vendors, bills, adjustments, and payments; and 

set up automatic processes, such as approval routing and recurring 

billing. 

Accounts Receivable 
Manage and track your customer invoices, adjustments, and payment 

receipts; and set up automatic processes, such as recurring invoicing. 

Bank Feeds 
Connect to bank feeds. 

Cash Management 
Manage and track your accounts, including banks, savings institutions, 

and charge card accounts; and record transactions, such as fund 

transfers, payment receipts, and deposits.  

Cloud Services 
Prepare and vile VAT and GST returns. 

Company 
As an administrator, manage all aspects of your applications and users, 

including subscribing to and configuring applications, adding users and 

permissions, and more. As a user, set your system and personal 

preferences, such as email signature, receiving notifications, page 

display and interactive behavior, time zone, and date format. 

Condo and Co-op 
Manage dues, violation billing, and collection fees for homeowner 

associations and cooperatives. Through the Owner Portal, homeowners 

can submit service requests, review statements, make payments, and 

view messages and documents shared by their property manager. 

Consolidation 
Roll up multiple subsidiary financials into a parent company to generate 

a set of consolidated financials securely and in real time. For 

multi-currency companies, consolidate financials from subsidiaries into 

one currency.

Services 

Create new fields, email notifications, rules, warnings, and reports that

Management

accelerate the close process. Financial information is consolidated from 

other RealPage systems in the process and a workflow for approvals can 

be applied.

reporting with a fully integrated module for multiple asset books.

Create, monitor, and manage a budget or forecast; review the current 

performance of the budget against last year and current year budgets 

and actuals; search and modify the budgets on the fly and compare the 

budget values with previous years’ budgets and actuals.

Management 

Enable invoice processing from RealPage. Paperless invoice processing 

saves the time and expense of managing paper invoices. Includes the 

ability to manage centralized exception queues and upload invoices for

Create and maintain multiple journals and G/L and statistical accounts, 

and create and maintain budgets, all in GAAP compliance.

processes.

property improvements. From capital improvement projects to 

renovations to new construction, Job Costs manages every phase of a 

project through completion. This includes generating documentation 

packages for job draw requests and reimbursement requests for 

property repair and replacement expenses.

Create new fields, email notifications, rules, warnings, and reports that 

help extend RealPage Accounting and customize it to suit your business 

needs.

both platform and customization services or access to customization

services only. See Customization Services above.  

Property 

Management 

Business service designed to assist owners in the supervision of 

commercial properties. Essentially, the property manager takes care of 

details related to the upkeep of the buildings on the property, qualifies 

potential tenants, oversees leasing of sections of the property, and 

collects rentals on behalf of the owner. The process of managing 

commercial properties may involve overseeing any type of property 

from retail space to multi-storied office buildings. 

Replacement 

Reserves 

Manage the property replacement reserve process from invoice entry to 

creating the draw package for your lenders. You can set limits per

purchase orders, receiving and invoice matching. Take greater control 

and visibility of your spending through the use of Spend Inquiry.

amount of time spent on activities and calculate billable hours. Resource 

management allows you to manage profiles, contact information, and 

other information about your employees.

time you sign in.

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 844*

Subscriptions

Adding or Deleting Custom Packages 

A custom package is a group of related activities that enhances and automates the things you 

routinely do. For example, a custom report that provides unique insights into your business. When 

an activity is installed, the setting is turned on.  

To add or remove a custom package: 

1. 
On the Subscriptions page, go to the Custom packages tab. 

2. 
Locate the package that you want to add or remove, and then click the toggle button. 

The system opens an Alert box.  

3. 
Click the Ok button to confirm the action, or click the Close button to cancel. 

Canceling a Subscription 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions`


You can cancel a subscription if you changed your business direction or reorganized your 

company. However, you cannot cancel your subscription to core applications Company, General 

Ledger, and Cash Management. These core applications are available for configuration. 

To cancel a subscription to an application: 

1. 
On the Applications tab, locate the application that you want to unsubscribe from, and then 

click the toggle button. 

The system opens a box with a description of the application.  

2. 
Click the Cancel subscription button. 

3. 
Click Yes to confirm that you want to cancel your subscription.

User Access Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > History and Reports > User Access Report`


The Access Log lists all users who attempted to access your company, including those currently 

signed in. 

Generally, only administrators have permission to view the Access Log. By default, the log lists all 

logins, by all users, for all time. However, you can reduce this list by filtering by user, time, 

including the time of day. 

The log is organized first by user, and then by login date and time. The log shows how long the 

user was signed in and how the user signed out along with the user’s IP address. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to run the Access Log.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 737) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 737) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

##### Access Log Report Options
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 847*

Chapter 22: History and Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Access Log Report Options 

Running a Monthly Report 

To run a report using default settings: 

1. 
When the report settings screen appears, click the View button.  

The system opens a report showing all results for the default reporting period.  

2. 
To refine the report, click the Customize button to return to the main report screen, and 

then follow the steps in customizing and running this report. 

Customizing and Running the Report 

To see every result for a particular category, do not make selections from any of the data entry 
boxes. You can run this report without entering any search information. However, the report may 
take a long time to run and may return too many results to be useful.  

Before running the report, you can select the types of items to include and specify how you want 

the report to appear. 

To customize and run the report: 

1. 
In the Time period section, create your own reporting period. 

• 
In the Start date and End date fields, select or enter specific dates at which to start 

and end the audit. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to require a time period before running the 

report. 

• 
In the Start time and End time drop-down lists, select the specific hour, minute, and 

second at which to start and end the audit. 

2. 
In the Filters section, include or exclude specific types of objects in the report. As a general 

rule, set more filters to get fewer and more precise results. 

• 
In the User ID drop-down list, select a specific user ID to return results on the actions 

taken only by the selected user.  

3. 
In the Format section, specify the sort order and change the page layout of the report. 

• 
In the Sort by drop-down list, select the category by which you want the sort the 

report. 

• 
In the Page orientation drop-down list, select either “Portrait” or “Landscape.” 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 848*

History and Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

4. 
In the Titles section, enter titles, subtitles, and footers to display on print versions of the 

report. 

• 
In Report title 1, type the main title that you want to display in large type at the top of 

the page, directly under your company name. 

• 
In Report title 2, type the subtitle that you want to display in smaller type, directly 

under the main title. 

• 
In Footer text, type the footer text that you want to display at the bottom center of 

the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title and subtitle, and footer.  

5. 
Click the View button to generate the report. 

You can easily use trial-and-error to get the precise results you want. To refine the report further, 

click the Customize button to return to the report setup page.  

For complex financial reports you plan to run regularly, select a reporting period and save the 
report after setting it up. The next time you are ready to run the report, change only the date 
before running the report.  

Access Log Report Columns 

The default Access Log columns include: 

• 
User ID: This column displays the ID associated with a user. 

• 
User name: This column displays the name of the user. 

• 
Login time: This column displays the date and time at which the user logged in to the 

company. 

• 
Login result: This column displays whether the login was successful or unsuccessful. 

• 
Logout time: This column displays the date and time at which the user logged out of the 

company. 

• 
Activity: This column displays how much time the user spent actively using applications. 

• 
Logout type: This column displays the reason the user was logged out. 

• 
Source IP: This column displays the IP address from which the user logged in and out.

#### Audit Event Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 850*

History and Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Audit Event Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Audit Event Report`


The Audit Log is useful for tracking changes to standard transactions and records. The report lists 

all users who have added, edited, or deleted an object, with the date and time at which the 

change occurred.  

To run an audit log, you must: 

• 
Have the audit log package installed.  

• 
Be a limited or full administrator. 

The report is organized first by user, and then by object, object ID, action, and access time. By 

default, the list contains all logins by all users for all time. However, you can reduce this list by 

filtering by date, as well as by user.  

There are updated and expanded audit capabilities with the release of the audit trail. For more 
information, see Viewing Audit Trails. 

For a multi-entity shared company, the audit event report is available at the entity level. 

An audit event report shows changes to transactions and records in your company. To report on 
changes to user permissions, you can create an audit trail report. 

Installing the Audit Log Package 

The audit log is an optional package that you can install in your company. If you already have the 

audit log package installed, it appears in the list of Customization Packages in either the 

Customization Services or Platform Services menu (depending on your company’s subscriptions). 

To install the Audit Log Package: 

1. 
Request the audit log package from RealPage Accounting customer support.  

Submit a support case, requesting the audit log package. You will be sent the audit log 

package in the form of an XML file. 

2. 
Using Customization Services or Platform Services, install the audit log package.  

• 
From the Customization packages list, click the Add button to add a new package. 

• 
Browse to the location of the XML package. 

• 
Select the package, and then click the Import button. 

---

Email Delivery Log 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > History and Reports > Email Delivery History`


Use the Email delivery log to check whether any emails that were sent encountered errors. The 

log displays a list of emails that failed to be sent to one or more recipients. Click View to view the 

details of an error. 

For example, suppose that you email invoices to multiple customers. By checking the Email 

delivery log, you can see whether any invoices encountered errors. By viewing the details of a 

particular error, you can see which recipients couldn’t be reached, giving you the opportunity to 

go back and correct the errors. 

The Email delivery log captures only errors that are encountered at the time the emails are 
sent. Sometimes, email errors are returned some period of time after the email is sent. For 
example, a particular email domain might return an error several hours after the original email 
was sent. These errors are not captured in the log. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to view the email delivery log. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to view the email delivery log.

Viewing the Log of Email Delivery Errors 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > History and Reports > Email Delivery History`


When you view the Email delivery log, you see a list of emails that failed to be sent to one or 

more recipients. 

By default, administrators automatically have access to the Email delivery log, but access can 
be granted to other users by changing their permissions to the Company application. 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the History and reports section, select the Email delivery history menu option. 

The Email delivery log opens. 

3. 
Review the list of errors in the log: 

• 
Error: Emails with this status weren’t delivered to any recipients. 

• 
Warning: Emails with this status were sent to at least one recipient, but other 

recipients couldn’t be reached. 

Each record in the log represents one email, each of which may have had multiple recipients.

4. 
Click the View link next to an item to examine a particular error. 

A separate Email delivery log page opens. The left side of the record displays the email 

errors that were encountered. The Result details field lists each email address that was 

rejected. The right side of the record displays a copy of the email that was sent.

##### Resending Failed Emails
*Source: `RP Accounting Company User Guide.pdf`, Page 856*

History and Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Viewing All Emails 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > History and Reports > Email Delivery History > 
Show All Emails`


By default, the Email delivery log displays only failed emails. However, you can use the Show all 

emails button to display all sent emails. 

To view all emails sent within the company: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the History and reports section, select the Email delivery history menu option. 

3. 
Click the Show all emails button located in the upper-right corner of the page. This button 

acts as a toggle between displaying all errors and showing all emails. Click the Show errors 

only button to return to the original view. 

Troubleshooting Incorrect Email Addresses 

The majority of emails are sent to either customers, vendors, or employees. When you send an 

email, the email address is typically pulled from the contact record for that customer, vendor, or 

employee. You also have the option to manually enter one or more email addresses at the time 

that you send the email. 

If the email address for a customer, vendor, or employee is incorrect, then it’s best to correct the 

error in their contact record.  

Resending Failed Emails 

After correcting any incorrect email addresses, try resending the failed documents. To do this, 

return to the page where you originally sent the email. The Accounts Receivable, Accounts 

Payable, and Spend Management applications have email functions where you can send invoices, 

statements, payment notifications, and other documents. 

For automatic payment notifications to vendors or employees, you can resend a payment 

notification that failed by emailing a copy of the payment. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Account maintenance section, select Print payment copies. 

3. 
Use the filters to narrow your search. You can filter for a specific range of dates, or for a 

particular customer, vendor, or employee. 

4. 
Resend the email.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

A/P batch 

A group of A/P transactions—such as invoices or 

credits—entered and posted together. 

A/P configuration 

The collection of settings that define how A/P 

functions behave, including approval rules, 

numbering formats, tolerances, and posting 

options. 

A/P workflow 

The routing and approval structure that 

determines how invoices move through review 

and approval before posting. 

A/R Batch 

A group of A/R transactions—such as charges, 

receipts, or adjustments—entered and posted 

together. 

Account balance 

The total amount recorded in a G/L account for a 

given period, including beginning balance, 

activity, and ending balance. 

Account grouping 

A structure used in financial reports to organize 

G/L accounts into meaningful categories such as 

assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses. 

Predefined or custom groupings of G/L accounts 

used for reporting, dashboards, and financial 

analysis. 

Account type 

A classification that determines how an account 

behaves in financial statements (Asset, Liability, 

Equity, Revenue, Expense). 

Accounting period 

Transactions are recorded and separated into 

different reporting periods such as months, 

quarters, and years. The use of reporting periods 

lets you compare past and present performance. 

Accounting reviewer 

A designated role responsible for reviewing and 

approving accounting-related transactions 

before they are posted. 

Accounts 

An account keeps track of what your company 

owns, owes, spends, or receives. Separate 

accounts let you keep separate records for each 

type of asset, liability, equity, revenue, and 

expense. 

Each account can contain several subaccounts, 

which helps organize and manage your finances. 

Each account tracks the activity of its category. 

For example, the Receivables account tracks 

money coming in and the Payables account 

tracks money going out. Each of these accounts 

typically has many subaccounts. For example, the 

Receivables account may have a subaccount for 

each property: 

1201.001 - Accounts Receivable - Fair Haven 

1201.002 - Accounts Receivable - Coconut Grove 

Glossary of Terms

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Each account has a beginning balance. You 

record the increases and decreases for a period, 

and at the end of the period, you have the 

resulting ending balance. 

Accrual accounting 

The accrual method of accounting recognizes 

income in the period earned, and expenses in 

the period incurred. The accrual method is a 

better measure of profit and loss. 

Accrued Expenses report 

A report showing expenses that have been 

incurred but not yet paid, used during close to 

validate balances. 

Accumulated depreciation account 

The G/L account credited when depreciation is 

posted. It offsets the asset’s cost on the balance 

sheet. 

Action card 

A dashboard component that provides quick 

access buttons for common tasks or navigation 

shortcuts. 

Actuals 

Financial results of activity in the general ledger 

and used as the baseline for forecasts and 

budgets. 

Adjustment 

A manual increase or decrease to a customer’s or 

vendor’s balance, used to correct errors or apply 

special credits/charges. 

Adjustment codes 

Predefined codes used to categorize manual 

increases or decreases to a customer’s balance. 

Aging buckets 

Time based categories (e.g., 0–30, 31–60 days) 

used to group outstanding receivables or 

payables for reporting. 

Aging report 

A report that groups outstanding balances (A/P 

or A/R) by how long they have been unpaid (e.g., 

0–30, 31–60 days). 

Allocation 

A process that distributes amounts from one 

account or entity to others based on predefined 

rules or percentages. 

Allocation (Expense Reports) 

A method of distributing an expense across 

multiple projects, tasks, or locations. 

Approval levels 

The hierarchy of users or roles authorized to 

approve invoices based on amount, vendor, or 

other criteria.  

The number of approvers required for a role 

(1–4) when that role is assigned to an approval 

policy. 

Approval policy 

A rule that determines which users or roles are 

authorized to approve a transaction based on 

criteria such as amount, vendor, G/L account, 

job, or payment method.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Approval policy manager 

The page in the Company application used to 

create, edit, and organize approval policies. 

Approval queue 

The list of transactions awaiting approval, 

displayed in the Approval Workbench. 

Approval workbench 

An approval workbench is where users review, 

approve, and decline pending transactions. 

Approval workflow 

The routing process that determines who must 

review and approve a transaction before it can 

be posted or paid. A collection of approval 

policies are applied to specific transaction types 

and properties. 

Approver 

An approver is a person responsible for deciding 

to approve or decline a transaction. There are 

three types of approvers: 

• 
General approvers can approve or decline 

only transactions assigned to them or their 

role. 

• 
Unrestricted approvers can approve or 

decline any transaction. 

• 
Delegate approvers can approve or decline 

transactions assigned to another approver. 

Approver permissions 

The system permissions required to create 

approval policies or approve transactions. 

Asset account 

The G/L account representing the asset’s cost. 

Used when posting depreciation and disposal 

entries. 

Asset Activity report 

A report showing additions, disposals, transfers, 

and depreciation activity for selected assets. 

Asset class 

A category of assets that share the same 

depreciation rules and G/L account structure. 

Determines how depreciation is calculated and 

posted. 

Asset Disposal report 

A report showing assets that have been disposed 

of, including gain/loss calculations. 

Asset List report 

A report showing basic asset details such as cost, 

location, class, and placed in service date. 

Asset Reconciliation report 

A report comparing fixed asset balances to G/L 

balances to identify discrepancies. 

Assets 

The tangible and intangible items used in the 

operation of a business. Tangible assets include 

buildings, equipment, and vehicles. Intangible 

assets include the company’s bank account 

balance and A/R invoices representing future 

income from customers. Assets are tracked 

through acquisition, depreciation, transfer, and 

disposal.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Assumptions 

User defined variables—such as inflation rates, 

occupancy targets, or expense growth—that 

drive forecast calculations. 

Attachments 

An attachment is a bundle of one or more 

supporting documents, such as spreadsheets, 

scanned images, or word processor documents. 

Audit trail 

A system record showing changes made to 

transactions or records, including who made the 

change and when. 

Bank account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on the bank account used. 

Bank accounts 

Financial accounts set up in the system for 

issuing payments, recording deposits, 

withdrawals, and performing reconciliations. 

Bank feed 

An automated connection that imports bank 

transactions into reconciliation for matching and 

reconciliation. 

Bank reconciliation 

The process of matching bank activity to general 

ledger transactions to ensure the bank balance 

and book balance agree. 

Bank register 

A chronological list of all transactions recorded 

in a bank account within the system. 

Baseline forecast 

The initial forecast generated from actuals and 

default assumptions before adjustments or 

scenario modeling. 

Batch 

A group of journal entries entered and posted 

together as a single unit. 

Batch report 

A report that displays all transactions included in 

a specific batch, such as A/P invoices or journal 

entries. 

Beginning balance 

The starting balance of a G/L account at the 

beginning of a fiscal period. 

Billable time 

Hours worked on a project that can be invoiced 

to a customer. The Billable Time page allows 

users to generate invoices for approved billable 

hours. 

Book balance 

The balance of a bank account according to the 

general ledger. It can also be the balance from 

the general ledger of a default general ledger 

account set on the bank account. 

Bookmarks / favorites 

User-defined shortcuts to frequently accessed 

pages or modules. 

Books closed 

The state indicating that the accounting period 

has been finalized for a property.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Budget 

A financial plan for a future period that outlines 

expected revenue, expenses, and cash flow. In 

Job Cost, a budget is an estimate of expected 

costs for a job. 

Budget version 

A saved iteration of a budget or forecast, 

allowing comparison between drafts, scenarios, 

or approval stages. 

BVA 

Budget Variance Analysis is an analysis of the 

difference between the amount that you 

budgeted for and the actual amount that you 

spent. 

Calculation model 

The logic used to compute forecasted values, 

such as percentage growth, fixed amounts, or 

driver based formulas. 

Cash accounting 

The cash method of accounting recognizes 

revenue in the same reporting period as the cash 

is received, and expenses in the period in which 

cash payments are made. 

Cash flow forecast 

A projection of expected cash inflows and 

outflows over a defined period. 

Certification / skill 

A credential, license, or skill tracked for an 

employee. Users can add, edit, or delete 

certifications and skills in their profile. 

Charge 

A receivable posted to a customer or tenant 

account for rent, fees, utilities, or other billable 

items. 

Charge schedule 

A configuration that defines when recurring 

charges generate, such as monthly rent cycles. 

Chart of accounts (COA) 

The structured list of G/L accounts used to 

categorize financial transactions. 

Check layout 

The format and design used when printing 

checks, including alignment, fields, and MICR line 

settings. 

Check run 

A batch process that selects, reviews, and prints 

multiple vendor payments at once. 

Child location 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, properties are 

called locations. Subproperties are called child 

locations. 

An entity represents the corporate office of one 

or more locations, responsible for locations’ 

taxes. Every location is associated with an entity. 

An entity can be responsible for one location or 

a large group of locations and child locations.  

A company can be composed of one entity or 

multiple entities. See also Multi-entity companies 

(on page 859).

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Cleared transaction 

A payment or deposit that has been matched to 

bank activity during reconciliation. 

Cloned dashboard 

A duplicate of an existing dashboard that can be 

edited independently. 

Close account 

A close account is a G/L account used to track 

job completion. 

Close checklist 

A list of tasks required to complete the financial 

close for a period. Can be generated 

automatically or manually. 

Close console 

A centralized page for managing close activities, 

including generating checklists, opening/closing 

books, and viewing charts. 

Close workbench 

A workspace that displays close tasks, checklists, 

and work paper actions for selected properties. 

Closing period 

The process of finalizing a fiscal period so no 

additional transactions can be posted. 

Coding 

Assigning G/L accounts, properties, entities, and 

other classifications to an invoice or credit. 

Commitment 

A commitment, or purchase order, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount. 

Component 

An individual element displayed on a dashboard, 

such as a chart, list, report, performance card, 

calendar, or smartlink. 

Component controls 

The actions available on each dashboard 

component, such as edit, delete, expand, 

collapse, or move. 

Component group 

A collection of dashboard components grouped 

together for organization or layout purposes. 

Component permissions 

Permissions required to view the underlying data 

of a dashboard component. Users must have 

access to the data source (e.g., A/P invoices, G/L 

accounts) to see the component. 

Concession 

A concession is a negative charge awarded to 

the customer as a short-term incentive. Examples 

of concessions include waived fees, reduced rent, 

nuisance discounts, and renovation credits.  

Console page 

A dashboard style page showing close status, 

charts, and tools for generating checklists and 

managing books.

Glossary of Terms

Consolidation 

Combining financial data from multiple entities 

into a single set of financial statements. 

Contra accounts 

A contra account is an account which offsets and 

reduces or offsets the balance of another 

account. You can have contra accounts for both 

assets and liabilities. 

A contra asset account has a credit balance and 

offsets and decreases the debit balance of the 

related asset account. An example of a 

contra-asset account is Accumulated 

Depreciation Autos & Vehicles account, which 

reduces the Automobiles & Vehicles account to 

arrive at the net value. 

A contra-liability account has a debit balance 

and offsets and decreases the credit balance of 

the related liability account. 

Cost code 

A cost code is a way to track a specific cost 

based on nature or function. 

Cost code policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific cost code. 

Cost coding 

Cost coding is a method of grouping individual 

costs based on their nature, function, or work 

phase. 

Credit memo 

A credit memo increases the overall amount you 

owe a vendor. It is typically a vendor-issued 

document that reduces the amount owed on an 

invoice. 

Custom field 

A user-defined field added to records or 

transactions to capture additional data not 

included in standard RealPage fields. 

Custom field wizard 

The guided tool used to create new custom 

fields, define field types, and configure visibility. 

Custom report 

A user built report that pulls data from Financial 

Suite records, transactions, and custom fields, 

allowing flexible filtering, grouping, and 

calculations. 

Custom report wizard 

A step-by-step tool for building custom reports, 

including selecting data sources, defining 

columns, adding filters, grouping, and setting 

prompts. 

Custom view 

A personalized list view that displays selected 

columns, filters, and sorting for any application’s 

list pages. 

Customer / tenant ledger 

A detailed record of all charges, payments, 

adjustments, and balances for a specific 

customer or tenant. 

Dashboard 

A workspace where users can pin frequently 

used reports for quick access, and display

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

business insights using components such as 

charts, KPIs, lists, and reports. 

Dashboard library 

A collection of prebuilt dashboards available for 

installation, typically provided when a company 

is created using a QuickStart template. 

Data import wizard 

A tool used to import data such as vendors, 

customers, G/L accounts, or transactions into the 

Financial Suite. 

Data mapping 

The process of aligning fields in your import file 

with the corresponding fields in the Financial 

Suite so the system knows where each value 

belongs. 

Data source (primary data source) 

The record or transaction type selected as the 

foundation for a report (e.g., Customer, A/P 

Invoice Detail, G/L entry). 

Data template 

A predefined spreadsheet or CSV layout 

provided by RealPage that specifies the required 

columns and formatting for a successful import. 

Debit memo 

A debit memo decreases the overall amount you 

owe that vendor. 

For example, if you receive a credit memo from a 

vendor, enter it as a debit memo to reduce the 

amount you owe that vendor. 

Debits and credits 

In common use, credit generally has positive 

associations; in accounting, credit is associated 

with decreases in asset, expense, and equity 

accounts. 

Debits increase balances in asset and expense 

accounts and decrease balances in liability 

accounts, revenue accounts, and capital 

accounts. 

Credits increase balances in liability, revenue, 

and capital accounts, and decrease balances in 

asset and expense accounts. 

Debit accounts are asset and expense accounts 

that usually have debit balances; the total debits 

usually exceed the total credits in each debit 

account. 

Credit accounts are revenue (income, gains) 

accounts and liability accounts that usually have 

credit balances. 

Declining balance (100/150/200) 

A depreciation method that accelerates 

depreciation by applying a percentage to the 

asset’s remaining book value. 

Default dashboard 

The dashboard automatically displayed when a 

user logs in. 

Default settings 

Predefined values that automatically populate 

fields when creating records, such as default G/L 

accounts or payment terms (A/P), or default 

charge codes or payment application rules (A/R).

Delegate 

The approver who assumes your responsibility 

for approving transactions while you are out of 

the office. Any approvals that have been 

delegated while you are out of the office remain 

with your delegate, even if you turn off the 

out-of-office notification before the delegate has 

approved or declined the transaction. 

Deposit 

Funds received and recorded in a bank account, 

often grouped into a deposit batch for posting. 

Deposit batch 

A group of deposits entered and posted 

together. 

Depreciation batch 

A batch of depreciation journal entries generated 

for a period. Can be posted, viewed, or deleted. 

Depreciation expense account 

The G/L account debited when depreciation is 

posted. 

Depreciation journal entry 

The G/L entry created when depreciation is 

posted, debiting expense and crediting 

accumulated depreciation. 

Depreciation schedule 

The system generated schedule showing 

depreciation amounts for each period over the 

asset’s useful life. 

Depreciation schedules (financial vs. 
tax) 

Separate schedules that allow different 

depreciation rules for GAAP and tax reporting. 

Detail data source

and line item information for transactions (e.g., 

A/P Invoice Detail). 

Detail ledger 

A record showing all transactions posted to a 

specific G/L account. 

Detail report 

A report that includes line item or transaction 

level information rather than summarized totals. 

Dimension report structures 

Dimension report structures are named 

structures that you can create for the purpose of 

adding custom analysis to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. You can add dimension 

structures for any dimension that you have in 

your company. 

Disbursement 

Any outgoing cash transaction, such as checks, 

ACH payments, or manual payments. 

Document template 

A customizable Word-based template used for 

printed documents such as invoices, statements, 

sales orders, and purchase orders.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Document type 

The category of document associated with a 

report, such as invoices, statements, or purchase 

orders. 

Draft asset 

An asset imported from an external system that 

has not yet been activated. 

Draft expense report 

An expense report that has been created but not 

yet submitted for approval. 

Draw 

In Job Cost & Reserves, a draw summarizes 

invoiced costs by combining job activity into 

predetermined categories. After it’s summarized, 

you can provide the draw to the funding sources 

of the job. 

Draw model 

A draw model is an agreement between a lender 

and your company that lists the budgeted items 

approved for funds. 

Driver 

A variable that influences forecasted values (e.g., 

occupancy, rent growth, utility usage). 

Due date 

The date by which a vendor invoice must be 

paid. 

eInvoice 

A system-generated A/P invoice created by 

Spend Management Storefront. 

Entity 

An entity record contains a property’s or 

location’s accounting and legal details, such as 

the business name and address as they should 

appear on A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and tax 

forms. An entity contains the accounting 

information of a location/property or property 

management company. 

In a multi-entity environment, entities are 

distinct—but nearly identical—companies or 

business units that are fully owned by a 

corporate or headquarters entity. Entities can 

represent divisions managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized 

payables and receivables and a common chart of 

accounts. 

Exception 

A transaction that does not match bank activity 

during reconciliation and requires review or 

correction. 

Expense report 

A form used to record reimbursable expenses. 

Users can add receipts, allocate expenses, and 

submit for approval. 

FAS 

A final account statement (FAS) is a document 

that provides a detailed record of a transaction’s 

activity. 

Filter 

Criteria applied to limit which records appear in 

a report.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Final work paper package 

The completed, approved set of work papers for 

a period, locked after approval. 

Fiscal calendar 

The structure of accounting periods and fiscal 

years used for reporting and posting. 

Forecast 

A forward looking projection of financial 

performance based on actuals, assumptions, and 

drivers. 

Forecast cycle 

The defined period for creating, reviewing, and 

finalizing forecasts (monthly, quarterly, annually). 

Funding source 

A funding source is a lender for a job. 

G/L account (general ledger account) 

A financial account used to categorize 

transactions for reporting and posting. A G/L 

account is associated with each charge or 

payment. 

G/L account group 

A predefined group of G/L accounts that can be 

selected instead of individual account ranges. 

G/L account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific G/L account or 

account range. 

G/L group 

A collection of G/L accounts grouped for 

reporting, allocations, or approval routing. 

Global (top level) setup 

Configuration performed at the top level that 

applies to all entities in the portfolio. 

Home page 

The landing page provides quick access to 

dashboards, tasks, and frequently used modules. 

Import log 

A system-generated record that shows which 

rows were imported successfully and which 

failed, including error messages. 

Initial posting date 

Revaluation reports help you manage 

unrecognized gains and losses from the 

fluctuation in exchange rates. Set the initial 

posting date on this report as the end of the 

month. 

Injection (smart rules / smart events) 

A dynamic value inserted into a rule or event 

action, such as a field value, date, or user 

information. 

Interim financing 

Interim financing, or construction loan, is a 

deployment of capital for short-term 

development, such as the acquisition and 

renovation of properties. This capital is typically 

provided by a lender.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

When the project is complete, owners pay the 

construction loan and replace it with permanent 

financing. 

In-transit item 

A transaction recorded in the system but not yet 

reflected on the bank statement (e.g., 

outstanding checks, deposits in transit). 

Invoice (A/P) 

A vendor’s bill for goods or services received. 

Invoice (A/R) 

A document generated to bill a customer for 

charges owed. In A/R, invoices may be created 

manually or automatically. 

Invoice entry 

The process of entering vendor invoices into the 

A/P module for approval and posting. 

Invoice matching 

The process of comparing an invoice to purchase 

orders, receipts, or expected amounts before 

approval. 

Invoice numbering rules 

Settings that determine how invoice numbers are 

validated, formatted, or restricted. 

Job 

A job is a method of tracking the work and 

expenses related to construction at a property. 

Jobs are used for job costing and approval 

routing. 

Job policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific job. 

Job type 

A classification of jobs used for approval policies 

and reporting. 

Job type policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a job type. 

Journal entry 

A journal entry documents the movement of 

money. When you add a journal entry, you enter 

an accounting transaction into the records. Every 

journal entry must include at least two equal and 

offsetting entries. This is because every 

transaction involves a change in at least two 

places in the accounting records, and the total of 

all debits and credits must balance. 

Key performance indicator (KPI) 

A measurable metric used to evaluate financial 

or operational performance (e.g., NOI, occupancy 

rate). KPIs can be displayed on performance 

cards on a dashboard to show financial or 

operational performance. 

Late fee 

A charge applied when a customer fails to pay by 

the due date, based on configured rules. 

Late fee rules 

Configuration that determines when late fees 

apply, how they are calculated, and which charge 

codes they use.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Ledger 

The complete set of financial accounts used to 

record all transactions for an entity or portfolio. 

Line item 

An individual revenue or expense entry within a 

transaction such as an invoice, purchase order, 

budget or forecast. 

Loan schedule 

A loan schedule is a list of all payments 

previously paid (historical purposes only) or due 

to the lender for the loan. 

Lookup values 

Reference lists—such as vendors, charge codes, 

or account types—that must exist in the system 

before certain imports can succeed. 

Manual entry 

A bank transaction entered directly into the 

system rather than imported through a bank 

feed or processed by AI. 

Manual journal entry 

A journal entry created directly by a user rather 

than generated by a subsystem such as A/P or 

A/R. 

Matching 

The process of pairing bank activity with 

corresponding G/L transactions during 

reconciliation.  

M-console 

The M-console is the management console used 

by administrators to create and manage multiple 

RealPage Accounting Suite environments. 

M-console access is different from RealPage 

Accounting Suite system access. To access the 

M-console, you must have a separate account in 

the M-console. 

Most implementations of RealPage Accounting 

Suite do not need the M-console. 

Memorized report 

A saved version of a report with preset filters, 

parameters, and formatting for quick reuse. 

Merge field 

A placeholder inserted into a Word document 

template that pulls data from the Financial Suite 

when the document is generated. 

Monthly checklist 

A checklist used for monthly close activities. 

Multi year forecast 

A projection that spans multiple fiscal years, 

often used for long term planning. 

Multi-entity companies 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, a parent property 

is called a location, and a subproperty is called a 

child location. A location must have an entity 

associated with it. The entity handles the 

accounting and tax activities for its location and 

any child locations. 

In a multi-entity shared corporation, entities 

represent a separate tax identification or a 

separately secured, fully balancing set of books. 

Entities typically represent properties, or 

locations, which are managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Performance card 

A dashboard component that displays KPIs, 

trends, or financial metrics in a compact visual 

format. 

Period activity 

The total debits and credits posted to an account 

within a specific accounting period. 

Period close 

The workflow used to review, adjust, and finalize 

financial activity before closing an accounting 

period. 

Periodic tasks 

Recurring A/P activities performed on a regular 

schedule, such as check runs, recurring invoice 

generation, or reconciliation. 

Permission 

The rights required to view and work with data 

and access pages. 

A permission allows you to access a single 

function. When RealPage adds a new feature to a 

product, the feature often comes with new 

permissions that you must enable before users 

can use the new feature. The word “Right” and 

the word “Permission” refer to the same thing. 

When you use the Unified Platform, they are 

referred to as rights. When you set up access to 

functions in the Financial Suite, they are referred 

to as permissions.  

Permit 

A permit is a category that organizes job 

attachments by type or function. 

Placed in service date 

The date the asset begins being used. 

Depreciation starts based on this date. 

PO 

An abbreviation for purchase order (on page 

862). 

Policy type 

The category of rule used to determine approval 

routing (User, Amount, Tiered Amount, Vendor, 

Vendor Type, G/L Account, Job, Job Type, Cost 

Code, Accounting Reviewer, Journal Type, 

Payment Method, Bank Account). 

Positive Pay 

Positive pay is an automated service that the 

bank offers to help detect fraud by matching a 

company’s check with the check presented for 

payment.  

You can use the RealPage Financial Suite Positive 

Pay feature to generate a Positive Pay file and 

transmit the list of checks to the bank for review. 

The bank compares the amount, check number, 

and account number to ensure that they match. 

Non-matching checks are flagged and sent back 

to the check issuer for review. 

You can also configure the system to submit 

Positive Pay files on a schedule. When a schedule 

is configured, the system generates the Positive 

Pay files containing a list of checks on the 

scheduled dates and automatically sends them 

to the bank. 

Posting 

The action that finalizes a transaction and 

records it in the general ledger.

Prompts

PTO (paid time off)

application. 

PTO approvals

decline PTO requests. 

PTO request

time off. 

PTO types 

Administrator-defined categories of PTO, such as 

vacation, sick leave, or personal time. 

Punchout vendor 

Punchout refers to a digital system in which a 

vendor allows customers to browse his product 

catalogs online and then purchase goods or 

services within the client’s e-procurement 

system. 

Purchase order 

A purchase order, or commitment, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount.

QuickStart template 

A predefined setup template that provides 

dashboards, account groups, and structural 

configuration during company creation. 

Receipt 

A recorded payment from a customer. In the 

Financial Suite, “receipt” and “payment” are often 

used interchangeably. 

Reclassification (asset) 

Changing the G/L account or asset class 

associated with an asset. 

Reconciliation date 

The date through which the bank account is 

being reconciled. 

Reconciliation workbench 

The tool used to match bank activity with G/L 

transactions and complete bank reconciliations. 

You can match, review, and clear bank 

transactions during the reconciliation process. 

Record 

Any data object in the Financial Suite, such as 

Customer, Vendor, G/L Account, or Invoice. 

Recurring charge (property 
management) 

A charge that is automatically generated on a 

schedule (e.g., monthly rent or recurring fees). 

Also called recurring invoice. 

Recurring invoice (accounting) 

An invoice template that automatically generates 

new invoices on a set schedule. 

Recurring journal entry 

A journal entry template that automatically 

generates entries on a defined schedule. 

Refresh 

The action that reloads a page’s data to reflect 

the most recent system updates. 

REIT 

Real Estate Investment Trust 

REMIC 

Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit 

Report audience 

A report audience is an audience assigned to a 

report in order to designate who the report is 

intended to be viewed by or addressed to. By 

assigning a report audience to a report, you can 

filter the list of reports by audience type later. 

Report center 

The central hub where users browse, run, create, 

and manage reports. 

Report column 

A vertical section in a report that displays one 

specific type of information, such as dates, 

amounts, or statuses.
