Reporting portal 

The centralized location for running, 

customizing, and exporting reports. 

Required fields (importing) 

Columns that must be present and populated in 

your import file for the system to accept the 

data. 

Revaluate 

An adjustment to a country’s official exchange 

rate relative to the base amount. 

Revenue account 

The G/L account associated with a charge code, 

used to classify revenue in financial reporting. 

Reversal 

A journal entry created to negate a previous 

entry, often used for accruals. 

Rights 

A right allows you to access a single function. 

When RealPage adds a new feature to a product, 

the feature often comes with new rights that you 

must enable before users can use the new 

feature. The word “Right” and the word 

“Permission” refer to the same thing. When you 

use the Unified Platform, they are referred to as 

rights. When you set up access to functions in 

the Financial Suite, they are referred to as 

permissions.  

Role 

A group of users who share permissions and 

responsibilities; roles can be assigned as 

approvers. Roles are assigned to users to control 

access to modules and actions. 

RPA 

An abbreviation for RealPage Accounting. 

Segments 

A component used to categorize financial data 

(e.g., entity, department, account). 

You can use segments to organize, sort, and 

report on your company information in 

meaningful ways. It is a type of tag with a set of 

values, which you can associate with transactions 

and G/L entries. 

Sequences 

Document sequences refer to the system’s 

automatic document numbering feature used to 

assign unique identifiers to new records. This 

helps ensure consistency and avoids duplication. 

Automatic numbering, also known as document 

sequencing, is available only for select 

transactions and records in RealPage 

Accounting. Document sequencing uses 

pre-defined numbering plans to assign 

sequential identifiers to new records or 

transactions, such as customer records or A/R 

invoices. Document sequencing is a two-step 

process. First, you configure the numbering 

scheme, then you assign the scheme to the type 

of record or transaction.  

Service charge 

A bank fee recorded during reconciliation to 

adjust the book balance. 

Setup 

The Setup tab appears at the top of most menu 

panes. Click it to display the menu items 

available to you based on your subscriptions, 

user permissions, and admin privileges. If the

Site Experience 

The Site Experience is a scaled-down version of 

Spend Management in a simplified interface. 

While the Spend Management application in the 

RealPage Financial Suite offers more robust 

functionality, most users can accomplish their 

procurement-to-payment processes from the 

Site Experience. 

The Site View option opens Site Experience. The 

Site View menu option is available in the Spend 

Management, General Ledger, and Accounts 

Payable application menus. 

Smart event 

An automation that triggers an action—such as 

sending an email, making an API call, or posting 

an HTTP request—when conditions are met. 

Smart rule 

A rule that triggers warnings or errors to guide 

user behavior when certain conditions are met. 

Smartlink 

A dashboard component that provides a 

clickable link to another page, report, or 

application. 

Source entity 

The paying entity. The entity that is the source of 

the money in a transaction between two or more 

entities. 

Splits 

A line within a transaction that records the 

account and amount of money involved is called 

a split. 

Spread method (budgeting) 

The rule used to distribute annual amounts 

across months (e.g., evenly, seasonally, 

driver-based). 

Staff expenses 

Expense reports created on behalf of staff 

members by administrators or managers. 

Staff timesheets 

Timesheets created or managed by supervisors 

for their staff. 

Standard report 

A pre-built Financial Suite report that cannot be 

modified but can be exported or memorized. 

Statement 

A statement, or Statement of Account, is 

essentially a report. It’s a snapshot that includes 

all open and unapplied transactions at the time 

the snapshot was taken—usually at the end of a 

period. 

Statement balance 

The ending balance shown on the bank 

statement for the reconciliation period. 

Straight line depreciation 

A depreciation method that spreads the asset’s 

cost evenly over its useful life.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Subledger 

A subledger is a ledger containing all of one kind 

of transaction. For example, a subledger may 

contain all accounts receivable transactions, or 

accounts payable transactions, or fixed asset 

transactions. All transactions in all subledgers roll 

up into the general ledger. 

Submitted (timesheet status) 

Indicates that a timesheet has been submitted 

and is awaiting approval. 

Sum of years digits (SYD) 

An accelerated depreciation method that applies 

a decreasing fraction of the asset’s cost each 

year. 

Summary 

Summaries are collections of the same type of 

transactions, grouped together for processing. 

Until you or the system creates a new summary, 

no line items appear in the Summaries list. 

Summaries can be either open or closed. When 

summaries are open in Accounts Receivable, you 

can add invoices, adjustments, and deposits. In 

designing an accounts receivable process, the 

system administrator can give access to the 

pages involved with managing invoices but not 

opening or closing summaries. 

Summary report 

A high level report that aggregates data without 

showing line item detail. 

Suspense account 

A temporary account used to hold transactions 

that require review or correction. 

System journal 

A system journal is a journal that is used by the 

system. Users can designate a journal as a 

system journal. Users cannot add journal entries 

to system journals, and system journals are 

excluded from appearing in manual journals 

drop-down lists. 

Target (budgeting) 

A predefined financial goal used to guide 

budgeting or forecasting (e.g., NOI target, 

expense cap). 

Task (Financial Close Management) 

An individual close activity, such as reconciling a 

subledger or reviewing a report. 

Task (Time & Resources application) 

A specific activity within a project. Tasks must be 

created before they can be selected on 

timesheets. 

Template version (importing) 

The specific RealPage-approved layout for an 

import file. Using an outdated version can cause 

errors. 

Tenant / customer 

The individual or organization responsible for 

paying charges recorded in A/R. 

Three-way tie 

A reconciliation requirement ensuring that the 

bank balance, book balance, and cleared balance 

all match.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Tiered amount policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions 

through multiple approval tiers based on 

increasing amount ranges. 

TIH 

Trust Interest Holder 

Time approvals 

The list where approvers review and approve or 

decline submitted timesheets. 

Timesheet 

A weekly record of hours worked on projects and 

tasks. Users can add comments, submit for 

approval, and track status. 

Timesheet periods 

Defined weekly or biweekly periods used for 

time entry. Administrators open and close 

periods as needed. 

Tolerance percentage 

The allowable variance between an invoice and 

the expected amount before manual approval is 

required. 

Transaction date 

The date the A/R activity occurred, which 

determines how it appears in aging and 

reporting. 

Transaction detail 

Line-level information associated with a 

transaction, such as invoice items or journal 

entry lines. 

Transaction type 

The category of transaction, such as invoices, 

journal entries, or payments. 

Transactions 

A transaction represents money flowing from 

one account to another. Whenever you spend or 

receive money, or transfer money from one 

account to another, it is represented as a 

transaction. 

In double-entry accounting, transactions always 

involve at least two accounts—a source account 

and a destination account. 

Transfer 

A movement of funds between two bank 

accounts within the system. 

Transfer (asset transfer) 

Moving an asset from one location, entity, or 

department to another. 

Trial balance 

A report showing all G/L accounts with 

beginning balances, period activity, and ending 

balances. 

Unapplied payment 

A payment that has been received but not yet 

applied to specific charges. 

Unapplied payment handling 

Rules that determine how payments are stored 

when they cannot be matched to specific 

charges.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 

Unapproving (Expense report) 

The action of reversing an approval so the report 

can be edited. 

Unapproving (Expense report) 

The action of reversing an approval so the report 

can be edited. 

Uncleared transaction 

A transaction recorded in the system that has 

not yet been matched to bank activity. 

Unit 

A unit is a rentable space on a property. 

Unposted batch 

A batch of journal entries that has been created 

but not yet posted to the general ledger. 

Unrestricted user 

A user who can do a task, such as approve work 

papers on behalf of others, regardless of 

property restrictions. 

An unrestricted user can see all transactions that 

are waiting to be approved. Unrestricted users 

can act on these transactions even when the 

approvals are not assigned to them. 

Useful life (periods) 

The number of periods over which the asset will 

depreciate. 

User 

An individual system account assigned roles, 

permissions, and approval responsibilities. 

Variance (Financial Close 
Management) 

A difference between expected and actual 

balances in work papers, requiring review and 

resolution. 

Variance (Forecasting and Budgeting) 

The difference between actual results and 

budgeted or forecasted values. 

Vendor 

A supplier of goods or services who receives 

payment through the A/P process. 

Vendor categories / vendor types 

Classifications used to group vendors for 

reporting, workflow, or payment processing. 

Vendor defaults 

Preset values applied automatically when 

creating invoices for a vendor, such as G/L 

accounts or payment terms. 

Vendor import 

A file upload that creates or updates vendor 

records, including addresses, payment terms, 

and tax information. 

Vendor policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific vendor or vendor 

range. 

Vendor type 

A classification of vendors used for approval 

routing or reporting.

Vendor type policy

approval based on the vendor’s classification. 

Version control (budgeting) 

The system of tracking changes across multiple 

budget or forecast versions. 

Views (manage views) 

Saved list configurations that define which 

columns appear and how data is sorted or 

filtered. 

WHFIT 

Widely Held Fixed Investment Trust 

WIP account 

A WIP account, or work in process account, is a 

G/L account used to track jobs that are in active 

development. 

Work breakdown structure (WBS) 

A work breakdown structure (WBS) is a system 

that organizes a large project into manageable 

sections. In Job Cost, a job, or project, is 

separated into cost codes that help organize the 

job and track progress. 

Work in process account 

A work in process account, or WIP account, is a 

G/L account used to track jobs that are in active 

development. 

Work paper 

A work paper is an accounting document that 

reconciles all subaccounts of an accounting 

category for auditing purposes. Work papers can 

also be used for preparing financial statements. 

Work paper package 

A compiled set of work papers, attachments, and 

supporting documents for a period.

About Company

The Company application allows system and accounting
administrators to set up and manage their company, users, and
roles in RealPage Accounting. Administrators can define
security settings and global settings, grant permissions to
users, and manage subscriptions to applications and services.
Users can then use the application to edit their personal
preferences—including their email signature, email
notifications, page design, time zone, and date format.

Adding a User

Create user accounts in RealPage Accounting for employees
and external users, such as accountants, attorneys, bankers,
vendors, customers, or auditors.

1. In Company, click the Setup tab.

2. Select 
 Users.
3. On the User information tab, enter general information about
the user and set their Admin privileges.
4. On the Roles information tab, assign role-based permissions
to the user.
5. On the User entities tab, add entity restrictions.
6. On the User departments tab, add department restrictions.
7. On the User territories tab, add territory restrictions.
8. On the Remote authentication tab, type a OneSite sign-in
name to link the user's OneSite sign-in name to their user
record in RealPage Accounting.
9. On the Audit tab, type the name of the user who amended the
record.
10. Click Save.

Adding a Role

Create user roles for various job functions and assign specific
permissions to each role. You can then assign the roles to
users and user groups.

1. In Company, click the Setup tab.

2. Select 
 Roles.
3. Type a Name and Description for the role.
4. Click Save. The Role subscriptions page opens.
5. Select an application or module.
6. Click Permissions.
7. Select the permissions you want to assign to the role.
8. Click Save to save the permissions.
9. Repeat this process for each application or module as needed.
10. Click Save again to save the role.
11. Close Close.

Updating Permissions in a Role

Grant permissions to roles to determine what actions users with
the role can perform in the system.

1. In Company, click the Setup tab.
2. Select Users.
3. Click View permissions & roles next to the user.
4. Click the Roles tab.
5. Click View.

If there are multiple roles, click the View link next to the role you
want to add the new permissions to.

6. Click Permissions next to the application or module.
7. Select the permissions you want to enable.
8. Click Save to save the permissions.
9. Click Save again to save the role.
10. Click Close.

Assigning a Role to a User

Assign roles to users to determine their system permissions.

1. In Company, click the Setup tab.
2. Select Users.
3. Click Edit next to the user.
4. Click the Roles information tab.
5. Select a Role name.
6. Click Save.

Managing Company Subscriptions

If you are an administrator, you can subscribe to applications,
integrations, and custom packages for your company.
Subscribing to an Application

1. In Company, click the Setup tab.
2. Click Subscriptions.
3. On the Applications tab, toggle any applications or integrations
you want to subscribe to.
4. Click Subscribe.
5. Configure the application as required.
6. Click Save.

Canceling a Subscription

1. In Company, click the Setup tab.
2. Click Subscriptions.
3. On the Applications tab, toggle any applications or integrations
you want to unsubscribe from.
4. Click Cancel subscription.
5. Click Yes to confirm.

Adding an Entity

Set up entities to represent divisions, franchises, affiliates,
associations, locations, chapters, self-balancing funds, or
subsidiaries managed by your corporate headquarters.

1. In Company, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Entities.
3. On the Entity information tab:

▪
Fill in information about the entity, such as a Name and ID.
▪
Select contacts to associate with the entity.
▪
Select the entity's first fiscal month and first tax month.
▪
Specify reporting titles for the entity.
▪
Set the entity's work days and weekends.
▪
Set the entity's dates of operation.
▪
Assign federal, state, and local tax code groups.

4. On the Inter-entity setup tab, define the accounts to use for
tracking inter-entity payable and receivable balances.
5. On the Management reporting codes tab, assign reporting
codes that describe the entity.
6. On the Additional information tab, select the customer and
vendor records that represent the entity.
7. Complete the remainder of the entity record as needed.
8. Click Save.
9. Optionally, you can Edit the entity to:

▪
Override account titles (Entity information tab).
▪
Map inter-entity accounts (Entity information tab).
▪
Define Spend Management activation and deactivation
dates (Spend Management tab).
▪
Override Site View subledger A/P close dates (Spend
Management tab).
▪
Request Storefront vendor account numbers in bulk
(Spend Management tab).
▪
Add entity-level holiday schedules (Holiday schedules
tab).

Adding a Contact

Set up company contacts to store contact information for
individuals or businesses.

1. In Company, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Contacts.
3. Fill in the contact information on each tab:

▪
Contact information
▪
Mailing information
▪
Additional information

4. Click Save.

Adding Segments

Add segments to organize, sort, and report on your company
information in meaningful ways.

1. In Company, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Segments.
3. In the Type field, type a two-character alphabetical code for the
segment.
4. Type a Name for the segment as it should appear in reports.
5. Set the Status to "Active".
6. Enter values for the segment type.
7. Click Save.

Adding and Importing Units

Add or import units to define and report on specific property
units, such as apartments.
Adding Units

1. In Company, click the All tab.

2. Select 
 Units.
3. Select the Entity/location where the unit is located.
4. In the Unit field, type a unique name or number for the unit.
5. Set the Status to "Active".
6. Fill in the address and floor plan details for the unit.
7. Click Save.

Importing Units from L&R

1. In Company, click the All tab.
2. Select Units.
3. Click Import from L&R.
4. Select the Entity/location where the unit is located.
5. Type the Confirmation email you want to notify.
6. Click Apply filters.
7. Select the entities or locations you want to import unit data for.
8. Click Import.

Changing a RealPage Accounting Term

Change the terminology in RealPage Accounting to suit your
business needs.

1. In Company, click the All tab.
2. Select Terminology.
3. Click Edit next to a term.
4. Select the Language.
5. Type a new Singular name and Plural name; for example,
"Client" and "Clients".
6. Repeat for other languages as needed.
7. Click Save.

Uploading a Logo

Add logos to the application or to printed documents.

1. In Company, click the All tab.
2. In the Configuration section, select Company.
3. Click Edit.
4. On the General information tab, find the Display section.
5. Click Upload logo.
6. Click Choose files.
7. Select a PNG, JPG, or GIF image file.
8. In the Printed logos and text section, repeat the procedure for
the system to use your logo in additional locations:

▪
Printed documents
▪
XSL custom documents
▪
Email templates

9. Click Save.

Setting Timeout Durations

Set default timeout durations for all users. Users can adjust
these settings in their user preferences.

1. In Company, click the All tab.
2. In the Configuration section, select Company.
3. Click Edit.
4. Click the Security tab.
5. In the Sign-in settings section, fill in the desired timeout values:

▪
Default inactivity duration: Select the default amount of
time users can remain active before they are automatically
logged out of the system.
▪
Default session duration: Select the default amount of
time users can stay in the system before they are
automatically logged out, regardless of their activity.

6. Click Save.

Unlocking a User

Unlock a user that has been locked out of their account. You
must have administrator privileges.

1. In Company, click the Setup tab.
2. Select Users.
3. Click Edit next to the user.
4. Change the Status from Lockedout to Active.
5. Click Save.

Setting a Password Policy

Set a system-wide password policy.

1. In Company, click the All tab.
2. In the Configuration section, select Company.
3. Click Edit.
4. Click the Security tab.
5. Configure the Sign-in settings section:

▪
Change duration: Select the frequency at which users
must change their passwords.
▪
Minimum length characters: Select the minimum number
of characters required in a password.
▪
Prevent reuse of previous passwords: Select the
number of recent passwords that cannot be reused when
resetting a password.
▪
Maximum sign-in attempts per day: Select the maximum
number of sign-in attempts allowed in a 24-hour period
before the user is locked out.
▪
Maximum reset attempts per day: Select the maximum
number of password resets allowed in a 24-hour period.
▪
Enforce IP address filters IP filter: Select an option to
enforce IP address filters and prevent login attempts from
unknown locations.

6. Click Save.

Resetting a Password

Reset a user's forgotten password. You must have
administrator privileges.

1. In Company, click the Setup tab.
2. Select Users.
3. Click Edit next to the user.
4. On the User information tab, click Reset password.
The system sends a password reset email to the address in the
user record. The email address has a link that allows the user to
change their password.

### Configuring Service Tickets
*Source: `RP Accounting Company QS.pdf`, Page 3*



### Submitting Service Tickets
*Source: `RP Accounting Company QS.pdf`, Page 3*



### Reviewing and Closing Service Tickets
*Source: `RP Accounting Company QS.pdf`, Page 3*

Configuring Service Tickets

Set up an internal ticketing system so users in your company
can submit service requests to your team members.

1. On the All tab, select Service ticket configuration.
2. Configure the service ticket settings:

▪
Enable reviewer approval to require approval on specific
ticket categories.
▪
Enable a need by date to require users to specify when the
task should be completed.
▪
Enable priorities to define priority levels for tickets.

3. Define your ticket categories:

▪
Type a name for the category.
▪
Select a reviewer to approve tickets, if applicable.
▪
Select the user or user role to assign to the ticket category.
▪
Select whether tickets in this category should require
attachments.

4. Click Save.

Submitting Service Tickets

Submit a service ticket for a task that needs to be completed by
another team member, such as reissuing a check, adding a
bank account, or setting up a vendor.

1. On the All tab, select 
 My service tickets.
2. Select a Category.
3. Optionally, select a Location to restrict the ticket to users who
have access to that entity.
4. Type or select a Need by date.
5. Select the Priority level.
6. Type your request in the Description field.
7. Select, upload, or scan at least one attachment, if required.
8. Click Save to submit the ticket.

Reviewing and Closing Service Tickets

Approve, decline, claim, and complete service tickets assigned
to you in the Intercompany ticketing workbench.

1. On the All tab, select Ticket workbench.
2. Apply the desired filters.
3. Select an Action:

▪
Approve: Approve the ticket.
▪
Decline: Enter the Reason for declining the ticket.
▪
Claim: Claim the ticket.
▪
Complete: Close the ticket and type any Close
comments.

User Accounts for Service Providers 

There are two kinds of user accounts that you can create for a service provider in the RealPage 

Accounting system. 

• 
A Web Service XML user accesses the web services API to create integrations with 

third-party applications.  

• 
An Admin user has access to the Company. The Admin subscribes the applications, creates 

users, and assigns and edits permissions. 

When the service provider is ready to integrate with RealPage: 

• 
Decide which type of user account to create based on the needs of the service provider.  

• 
Create either a Web Service XML account or an Admin account for the service provider.  

• 
Create an account group, if needed. 

Creating a Web Service User 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Admin > Web Services Users`


To create a web service user account: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Admin tab. 

2. 
Select the Web services users option.

Roles 

A role is a collection of permissions that allow a user to perform a typical set of tasks. After 

creating a role for each type of user, it is easy to assign the role to users while creating user 

accounts. This best practice applies to Web service and Admin users too. 

Creating a Role 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Admin > Roles`


To create a role: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Admin tab. 

2. 
Select the Roles option.  

3. 
Click the Add button to create a new role.  

4. 
Type a Name for the role, and then click Save. 

---


<!-- Page 13 -->
Chapter 1: Setting Up a Service Provider 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Service Provider Setup User Guide 

A new window appears where you can select Application/Module permissions. 

5. 
To define permissions for the role, click the Permissions link of each application. For service 

providers that connect through APIs, be sure to assign permissions in both General Ledger 

and Accounts Payable applications.  

6. 
Select the boxes of the permissions to grant. Each check box that you select gives the user 

access to perform a specific activity, or to run a process or report. 

Clear the check boxes of permissions that you want to prevent the user from accessing. 

All 

All 

---


<!-- Page 14 -->
Setting Up a Service Provider

For example, to grant all permissions to the General Ledger, click the All option. To grant 

permissions to General Ledger reports, scroll down to the Reports section, and then select 

the All option to select all General Ledger reports.  

7. 
After granting all permissions, click Save.  

The system returns to the Application/Module list, allowing you to select another 

application. You can also click Save to save all selections, and then exit the permission 

assignment area.

## Introduction to Time & Resources
*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 9*

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 

Introduction to Time & Resources 

Use the Time & Resources application to configure projects and tasks, add and manage job positions, log time 

and expenses, submit requests for paid time off (PTO), and approve staff timesheets and PTO. You can also track 

certifications and skills in this application. 

To use this application, your company must have a subscription to the application. It must be configured with 

projects and tasks before you can use the application to track time and expenses.  

Your user account or your role must have permissions to use Time & Resources features. 

If you cannot find the Time & Resources application in the drop-down list of applications, contact your system 

administrator.

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide

My Timesheets 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > My Timesheets`


Use the My Timesheets list to add and manage your timesheets. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add a new timesheet. 

• 
Edit an existing timesheet. 

• 
View the details of a timesheet. 

• 
Delete a timesheet. 

• 
Export the list of timesheets as a file. 

Statuses include: 

• 
Saved: You have saved the timesheet, but it has not been submitted yet. 

• 
Submitted: You have submitted the timesheet for approval. 

• 
Approved: Your timesheet has been approved. 

• 
Declined: Your timesheet has been declined. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with your timesheets: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Time & Resources 
My Timesheet 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

Before you can start creating timesheets, make sure that your system has the projects (on page 

101), tasks (on page 106), and PTO types that you will need to include in your timesheet. Make 

sure that the current time period has an open period, allowing you to create a timesheet for it.  

Adding Your Timesheet 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > 
 My Timesheets`


To add a timesheet: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu. 

2. 
Click the 
 Add button next to My Timesheets. 

3. 
In the Period drop-down list, select the period for the timesheet. 

4. 
In the Project/PTO column, select a project that you worked on.  

5. 
In the Task column, select the task that you spent time working on. 

6. 
In the Location column, select the location associated with the task. 

7. 
Fill in the hours for each day that you worked on the project and task. 

8. 
Click the 
 Comment button to add a comment for each entry. 

9. 
Continue adding rows for each project and task combination, filling in the hours that you 

worked each day, and then adding comments. 

10. 
Click Submit. After you have submitted your timesheet for approval, you can no longer 

change the entries. 

If your timesheet is declined, the system sends you an email message.

My Timesheet Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > My Timesheets > Add/Edit/View`


This page is composed of two sections: 

• 
The top section contains the period of time that the timesheet covers and the timesheet 

approval information when your system has timesheet approvals enabled. 

• 
The second section is where you enter the projects, tasks, and time that you spent on each 

task during the week. Employees who are allocated to work for more than one location 

should also select the location where you worked in the Location column.  

Use this page to create your timesheet for a period of time.  

• 
Select the time period that you want to enter time for from the Period drop-down list. 

After selecting the time period in the Period drop-down list, you can use this page to 

document how you spent time during the period on projects and tasks.  

For each row, you select a project (or PTO), a task, a location, and then enter the hours 

spent.  

• 
You can add a comment to each task. For example, you can use the comment to add details 

about the subtasks that you worked on during this period. 

Deleting a Timesheet Row 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > My Timesheets > Edit >  Delete`


You can delete a row from your timesheet. You cannot delete a row if the timesheet has been 

submitted for approval. 

To delete a row: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu. 

2. 
Click My Timesheets. 

3. 
Click the Edit link of the timesheet with the row that you want to delete. 

4. 
Click the 
 Delete button at the end of the row. 

5. 
Click the Save button.

Time Approvals List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Time Approvals`


Use this list to review employee timesheets and approve or decline them.  

You can approve and decline timesheets one at a time by clicking the Approve or Decline link. 

You can approve or decline multiple timesheets at the same time by selecting the check boxes in 

the Select column, and then clicking the Approve or Decline button. 

You can set up when to receive notifications about timesheet approvals in your email notification 

preferences. 

You can also: 

• 
Click the linked text in the Period column to examine an employee’s timesheet’s details.  

• 
Export the list as a PDF, Word, Excel, or CSV file. 

Before You Begin 

You must have administrator privileges to access the Company application’s Setup tab. 

Your system’s timesheet approvals feature can be configured in one of two ways. Either a 

manager must have direct reports, or the manager must be assigned to the Time Entry Approver 

role. 

• 
Direct reports: When your system is set up for timesheet approvals based on the Manager 

/Report to setting, then your system must be configured so that every employee user 

record is assigned to the manager who they report to. (There is no Manager setting. A 

manager is made to be a manager by having people set up to report to them.) 

You can set up an employee’s user record to report to a manager by going to Company > 


> **Navigation Path:** `Setup > Users > Edit > Report to to set up user records (employees) to report to a specific`


user (manager). 

• 
Approver Role: When the system is configured so that approvals require managers to be 

assigned to a role, all managers’ user records must be assigned to the Time Entry Approver

Roles Information > Time Entry Approver.

Approving Timesheets 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Time Approvals > Approve`


To approve someone’s timesheets, you must be the person’s manager, or you must be assigned 

to the Approver role, depending on how your system is configured. See Before You Begin (on 

page 23) for details. 

To approve a timesheet: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu. 

2. 
Select the Time Approvals option. 

3. 
Find the desired timesheet that you want to approve.  

4. 
Click Approve.  

The user’s timesheet status changes from Submitted to Approved in the Status column of 

the user’s timesheet. You can view the timesheet in the Staff Timesheets list.

My Expenses List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > My 
Expenses`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Daily Tasks > My Expenses`


This list displays expense reports that you created, or that someone created for you. The most 

recently submitted expenses appear at the top of the list. 

Use this list to add, view, edit, and delete expense reports. You can use the list tools to add and 

manage list views, and sort and filter the list. 

Importing expenses is available in the Staff Expenses list. (on page 76) 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with expense reports. The My Expenses permission allows 

you to add and manage expenses and to create expense reports. Staff expenses permissions allow 

you to access expense reports created by your employees, or on behalf of your employees.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Dependencies 

To submit an expense report, the system must have: 

• 
A user record that represents the employee. 

• 
A vendor record that represents the employee.

Setting Default Values 

Selecting default values is one method of speeding up data entry. Use this section to choose the 

values that you want the system to complete for you in the Entries list. (optional)  

After choosing the values and applying them, the system completes the fields in the Entries list 

with the values that you selected. After the system completes the fields, you can change any of 

the values, such as when one row requires a different value than the others. 

To set up default values: 

1. 
Click the Show defaults link to expand the area. 

2. 
For each field that you want to prefill, choose the value that you enter most frequently or 

choose a value that is a standard value for the list of line items in this invoice.

The Status column shows where the expense report is in the approval process.

• 
Approved: The expense report has been approved.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again.

#### Creating Invoices from an Approved Expense Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*

Using the Time & Resources Application 

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Creating Invoices from an Approved Expense Report 

Your system administrator can configure the system to create reimbursement invoices 

automatically after an expense report is approved. If the system is not configured this way, then 

you must create the A/P invoices for each approved expense report manually. 

After it’s configured, users only need to pay the A/P invoices to reimburse the employee, 

property, or P-Card vendor. 

To configure the system to create reimbursement invoices automatically, see Configuring expense 

reports in the online help or in the Accounts Payable Setup User Guide. 

How the Create Reimbursement Invoice Feature Works 

When an expense report is approved, the system automatically creates an invoice or invoices 

based on the information in the expense report. The reimbursement type determines how many 

invoices that the system creates.  

• 
If the expense report contains several items, but only one reimbursement type, then the 

system creates only one invoice for all expenses.  

• 
If the expense report contains expenses of all three reimbursement types, then the system 

creates one invoice for each reimbursement type (Employee, Property, and P-card vendor).

Payment Status 
This is the payment status of the invoices that the system created from 

this report. The system determines payment status of the invoices that 

were created by the report. The system displays a null or blank value 

until the expense report is approved. After the expense report is 

approved, the status changes to Pending.  

Possible values include: 

• 
Null value: This means that the expense report has not yet been 

approved. 

• 
Pending: The expense report has been approved but not yet 

paid. 

• 
Partially Paid: The expense report has been partially paid.  

• 
Paid: The expense report has been fully paid.

Requesting Paid Time Off (PTO) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Daily Tasks > 
 PTO Request`


To request time off: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, click the 
 Add button next to the PTO Request 

option. 

3. 
On the PTO request page, in the From date field, type the date that you want the time off 

to begin. 

4. 
In the To date field, type the date that you want the time off to end. 

5. 
In the PTO type drop-down list, select the reason for the time off, such as Company 

Holiday, Sick Time, or Vacation. 

If the PTO request is for a date range, the system fills in the Total Hours field and the 

number of hours cannot be changed. 

If the PTO request is for one day, the system fills in 8 hours, but you can change the number 

of hours. 

6. 
In the Comment field, type a note for the approver to see that explains your time off 

request further, if needed. 

7. 
Click the Submit button to submit the request into the approval queue.  

You can also click the Save button if you do not want to submit the request to the queue at 

this time. 

When your PTO request is approved, the system sends you an email message and locks the 

vacation row on the timesheet. 

Deleting PTO Requests 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Daily Tasks > PTO Requests > Delete`


You can delete time-off requests.  

To delete a time-off request: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, click the PTO Requests option. 

3. 
Find the PTO request that you want to delete, and then click the Delete link. 

4. 
Click OK to confirm the deletion.

#### Creating an Invoice for Billable Time
*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 74*

Using the Time & Resources Application 

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Creating an Invoice for Billable Time 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Periodic Tasks > Billable Time > (select) > 
Create Invoice`


You can create A/P and A/R invoices from the Billable time list. After the system creates the 

invoices, it removes the billable time record from the list and sends an email to the address that 

you specified in the Send completion notification to field. It also locks the record in the 

timesheet so that it cannot be edited. 

To create the invoices: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section, click the Billable time list. 

3. 
Select the lines for which you want to create invoices. Three fields appear at the top of the 

page. 

4. 
Fill in the Invoice date, G/L posting date, and Send completion notification to fields. 

5. 
In the Invoice date field, type the date that you want to appear on the A/P and A/R invoices. 

6. 
In the G/L posting date field, select the date that you want the two invoices to be posted on 

the general ledger. 

7. 
In the Send completion notification to field, type the email address of the person who you 

want to notify when the time has been billed. 

8. 
Click the Create invoice button.  

You can view the invoices in the A/P invoices and A/R invoices lists.

Importing Staff Expenses

Importing Draft Expenses 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > Staff 
Expenses > Import`


You can import expenses from the Staff expenses page or from the Import data page. This 

procedure describes importing from the Import data page.  

When you add expense data to the import file, add the User ID of the user who incurred the 

expense and the amount. You can also specify the expense report name to associate an expense 

with a specific expense report.  

After importing the CSV file, these expenses appear in users’ My expenses lists. The system sends 

an email message to each user who had expenses in the imported file. The user must add 

additional information, attach any required receipts and invoices, and then submit the expenses 

for approval. 

To import expenses: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Expense Reports - 

Draft row, and then select Template. The template for draft expenses downloads to your 

browser’s default download location.  

Preparing the Data for Importing 

1. 
Export the unapproved, draft expenses data from your other system. 

2. 
Open the downloaded template in Microsoft Excel or your favorite spreadsheet application. 

3. 
Fill in the template with the unapproved expense data that you want to import. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this.  

4. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
USER_ID: Type the ID of the user who the expense is being submitted for. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the draft expense. 

---


<!-- Page 84 -->
Using the Time & Resources Application 

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns. Many of the valid values differ by company 

because your company configures expenses in your system depending on your business 

needs. See Configuring Expense Reports. 

• 
EXP_REPORT_NAME: Type the expense report name. 

• 
DATE_FILED: Type the date that the expenses were filed. The default value is today’s 

date. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the expense. 

• 
DATE: Type the date. The default value is today’s date. 

• 
EXPENSE_CATEGORY: Type the category of the expense.  

• 
REIMBURSEMENT_TYPE: Type who or what will be reimbursed: Employees, Property, 

or P-card vendor. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique identifier of the location associated with the expense.  

• 
MEMO: Type a note about the expense.  

• 
UNIT: Type the unit number associated with this expense.  

• 
CORPORATE_EXP_REPORT: Type “true” if this is a corporate expense report or type 

“false” if not. Corporate expense reports do not appear in Site View. 

• 
DEPARTMENTID: Type the unique identifier of the department that is associated with 

the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_1: Type the segment type associated with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_1: Type the segment value of segment 1 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_2: Type a second segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_2: Type the segment value of segment 2 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_3: Type the third segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_3: Type the segment value of segment 3 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_4: Type the fourth segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_4: Type the segment value of segment 4 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_5: Type the fifth segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_5: Type the segment value of segment 5 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_CUSTOMERID: Type the unique identifier of the customer that 

is associated with the expense report item. 

---


<!-- Page 85 -->

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_VENDORID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor that is 

associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_EMPLOYEEID: Type the unique identifier of the employee that 

is associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_PROJECTID: Type the unique identifier of the project that is 

associated with the expense report item. 

• 
STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_CLASSID: Type the unique identifier of the class that is 

associated with the expense report item. 

6. 
Save the file as a CSV-formatted file. 

Importing the File 

1. 
When you are ready to import the file, click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV 

formatted file. 

2. 
In the Date format field, type the date format that you used for the expenses in the CSV file. 

3. 
Leave the File encoding field as auto detect. 

4. 
In the Import as section, select Draft if the staff expenses have not been approved. 

5. 
Select the Process offline check box if your file contains such a large number of expenses 

that you want the system to process the data offline so as not to degrade system 

performance. 

6. 
In the Email results to this address field, type your email address to have the system notify 

you when the import is complete. If the import generates errors, the error report is sent to 

this email address. 

7. 
Click the Import button. The system groups all imported expense reports by User ID. 

The system sends an email to the users who have had expenses imported on their behalf. 

The user must review and update the expense report and then submit it for approval.

When you import expenses that have already been approved, the system marks the expenses with 

an Approved status. The system creates invoices for the posted expenses. After importing the CSV 

file, these expenses appear in users’ My expenses lists, and posted expense reports appear in the 

Staff expenses list.  

When importing approved expenses, the system automatically posts expenses because expenses 

from P-card vendors have already been approved once.

Select Import data.

to your browser’s default download location.

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this.

• 
DATE_FILED: Type the date that the expenses were filed. The default value is today’s 

date. 

• 
DATE: Type the date. The default value is today’s date. 

• 
EXPENSE_CATEGORY: Type the category of the expense.  

• 
REIMBURSEMENT_TYPE: Type who or what will be reimbursed: Employees, Property, 

or P-card vendor.

*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 89*

Creating an Expense Report for Someone Else 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > 
 Staff 
Expenses`


The process of creating an expense report for someone else is the same as creating your personal 

expense report except that you specify the name of the user for whom you are creating it. You 

can create an expense report for anyone. 

To create an expense report on behalf of another user: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click 
 Staff expenses. The Staff expense report page opens. 

3. 
In the User drop-down list, select the user for whom you are creating an expense report. 

4. 
The system completes the Date filed field with today’s date. This is the date that the 

expense report is to be filed. You can change the date by typing or selecting a different 

date. 

The system assigns a unique identifier to the expense report after you submit it. It appears 

in the Expense report number field the next time that you open the expense report. 

5. 
In the Expense report name field, type a name for the report. 

6. 
Select the Corporate expense report check box if you do not want the corporate expense 

report to appear in Site View.  

7. 
In the Description field, type more details about the expense report, such as the reason or 

purpose of the expenses. 

Setting Default Values 

Selecting default values is one method of speeding up data entry. Use this section to choose the 

values that you want the system to complete for you in the Entries list. (optional)  

After choosing the values and applying them, the system completes the fields in the Entries list 

with the values that you selected. After the system completes the fields, you can change any of 

the values, such as when one row requires a different value than the others. 

To set up default values: 

1. 
Click the Show defaults link to expand the area. 

2. 
For each field that you want to prefill, choose the value that you enter most frequently or 

choose a value that is a standard value for the list of line items in this invoice. 

---


<!-- Page 90 -->
Using the Time & Resources Application 

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button. The system completes the column or columns with your 

default values. Learn more about Setting default line items. 

Next, you can either enter expenses manually, or use a template to speed up the expense entry 

process. 

Using an Allocation Template to Fill In the Expense Entries List 

You can create allocation templates on the Accounts Payable Setup tab using the Templates 

option. 

1. 
Click the Apply Template button. 

2. 
Select the desired template to use for expenses. 

3. 
Type the amount of the expense. 

4. 
Select the expense category. 

5. 
Select the reimbursement type. 

6. 
Click the Apply button. 

Save Template

Saving the Template 

You can fill in the desired values and then save them as a template without leaving the page. 

1. 
Click the Save Template button. 

2. 
Type a name for the template. 

3. 
Type a description such as the purpose of the template. 

4. 
Select the template type. 

5. 
Type a memo that will help you remember why you created this template. 

6. 
Click Save. You can access and edit templates saved this way on the Accounts Payable 

Setup tab by selecting the Templates option. 

Filling In the Expenses Section Manually 

1. 
In the Date column, type or select the date that the expense was incurred. This field is 

required. 

2. 
In the Location column, select the location associated with the expense. This field is 

required. 

3. 
In the Expense category column, select the appropriate category for the expense. Examples 

of employee expenses include Airfare, Hotel, Meals, and Gasoline. Examples of property 

expenses include Office supplies and Employee recognition. This field is required.

In the Amount column, type the amount of the expense. This field is required.

box opens where you can enter the miles driven.  

• 
When the Rate field is available, type the rate at which your company reimburses for 

mileage. If the Rate field is not available, it is configured to use the IRS rate.

Click Save. The system inserts the calculated amount in the Amount field, and inserts a

Duplicating Another User’s Expense Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > Staff 
Expenses > View/Edit > Duplicate`


If you have appropriate permissions, you can duplicate one user’s expense report and then 

customize it to create a similar expense report for another user. 

To duplicate an expense report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select Staff expenses. 

3. 
Click the View or Edit link of the expense report that you want to copy. 

4. 
Click the Duplicate button. 

5. 
Edit the report to make it unique: 

• 
Select the user for whom you are creating an expense report. 

• 
Name the expense report with a unique name. 

• 
Change the dates to match the dates that expenses were incurred. 

• 
Adjust the amount of each expense to match the receipts that you have. 

• 
Attach the receipts. 

6. 
When you have completed your changes, click the Draft button to save your changes 

without submitting the expense report for approval or click the Submit button to save your 

changes, and then submit your expense report for approval.

#### Editing an Approved Expense Report (Reopen)
*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 95*

Chapter 2: Using the Time & Resources Application 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 

Editing an Approved Expense Report (Reopen) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Staff Expenses > View > Reopen`


After an expense report is approved, the expense report and the invoice(s) tied to it cannot be 

edited. If you need to make a change to either the expense report or the invoice, then you can 

reopen the expense report. 

When you reopen an expense report, the system deletes the A/P invoices that are associated with 

it and changes its status to Draft. After it’s reopened, you can change all fields in the expense 

report. Edit the expense report to correct the errors, and then resubmit it. 

After invoices are paid, you cannot change any fields in the expense report that are tied to 

invoices.  

Reopening an expense report requires the Reopen permission. You can only reopen an expense 

report from the Staff Expenses list. 

To reopen an expense report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Expense reports section of the menu, select Staff Expenses. The Staff Expenses list 

opens. 

3. 
Click the View link of the expense report that you want to reopen. 

4. 
Click the Reopen button. The expense report opens to allow you to make changes.  

5. 
Edit the expense report to correct the errors. 

6. 
Click the Draft button to save it without submitting it, or click the Submit button to 

resubmit the changed expense report for approval with its changes. 

---

## Setting Up Time & Resources
*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 103*

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 

Setting Up Time & Resources 

This chapter describes the menu options that appear on the Setup tab of the Time & Resources menu. You must 

have administrator permissions to access the Setup tab of the menu. 

Before you start using this application to record time and expenses, a few setup steps are needed. First, create 

projects and task types so employees have something to track their time against. Then, configure the PTO types 

available to your team, and define any certification or skill categories you want to track. You’ll also want to set up 

billing preferences for time and expenses, and enable the approval feature for time approvals and PTO requests, 

assigning approvers and backup approvers.

### Configuring Time & Resources
*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 104*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 104*

Setting Up Time & Resources 

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring Time & Resources 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > Setup > Configuration`


To configure the Time & Resources application: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
Type the billable rate per hour in the Billable rate per hour field. 

4. 
Select the entity to bill for employee expenses in the Billing entity. 

5. 
In the A/P invoice expense account drop-down list, select the expense account to use for 

employee expenses. 

6. 
Select the Create A/R invoice check box to have the system create an A/R invoice for time 

and expenses automatically. 

7. 
In the A/R invoice revenue account drop-down list, select the revenue account to use for 

A/R invoices. 

8. 
To turn on the timesheet approval feature, select the Enable time approvals check box. 

9. 
Select who you want to approve the timesheets: 

• 
Manager/Report to  

• 
Time entry approver role 

10. 
Select the default approver for the system to use when there are no users assigned to the 

Time Entry Approver role. 

11. 
To turn on the PTO approval feature, select the Enable PTO approvals check box. 

12. 
Select the default approver to use if no user has the PTO approval permission. 

13. 
In the Unrestricted section, select one or more users to serve as a backup approver when no 

other user is available to approve items. 

14. 
Click Save. 

Before You Begin 

You must have administrator level permissions to configure the Time & Resources settings. 

---

Continue selecting roles as needed.

To delete a row, click the

Click the first blank row. 

2. 
Select a task to associate it with this project. 

3. 
Continue selecting tasks that are related to the project. 

• 
To add more rows, click the 
 Add button.  

• 
To delete a row, click the 
 Delete button. 

Saving the Project

*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 135*

Application

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Customizing and Running the Employee Time Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Reports > Employee Time`


To customize and run the report: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, select Employee time. 

Setting the Coverage Period 

You can use one of the pre-defined reporting periods available from the Reporting Period and As 

of Date boxes, or enter the Start date and End date you want the report to cover. You can specify 

either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both. 

Setting Up Filters 

Filters enable you to include or exclude specific types of data in the report, such as vendor and 

location. As a general rule, to get fewer and more precise results in your report, set more filters. 

To customize your report results, change the filters as follows: 

1. 
To include time for all employees, leave the Employee drop-down list blank. To show time 

for one employee, select the employee’s name in the Employee drop-down list. 

2. 
To include time spent on a specific project type, select the desired project type from the 

Project type drop-down list. You can select multiple project types.  

3. 
To include time spent on a specific project, select the desired project from the Project 

drop-down list. You can select more than one project. 

4. 
To filter the report for employees that work for a specific location, select the location in the 

Location drop-down list. You can also select a location group. 

Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per location. 

---


<!-- Page 136 -->
Time & Resources Reports 

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

 Individual Report
Process & Store

Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a location 

before it will run the report. 

Filling In the Format Section 

Use this section to select the report type, the page orientation, or group the data of the report. 

To format this report: 

1. 
Select the report type. To create a brief report, select Summary. To create a detailed report, 

select Detail. 

2. 
To change the page layout, in the Page Orientation section, and then click either Portrait or 

Landscape. Portrait is the default layout. 

3. 
If you selected the Detail report type, then you can choose how you want to group the data. 

Select None, Employee, Project, or Period. 

Filling In the Titles Section 

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the print versions of this report. You can export the 

report to Excel or CSV, or click Print for a PDF version. 

To add a title, subtitle, and footer to the report: 

1. 
Enter the title in the Report Title 1 box. 

This title appears in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that may automatically appear in this box. 

2. 
Enter the subtitle in the Report Title 2 box. 

This subtitle appears in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Enter the footer text in the Footer Text box. Footer text appears at the bottom center of the 

report. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report. 

You can view, process, memorize, export, or customize the report or add it to the dashboard 

by clicking one of the buttons at the top of the page.  

Use trial and error to get the precise results you want. Fill in the desired fields, and click 

View to see the report. To refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report 

setup page. Repeat this process until you’re satisfied.

report, and then type a description of the report.

#### Customizing and Running the Billable Time Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Time & Resources User Guide.pdf`, Page 140*

Time & Resources Reports 

RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide

Customizing and Running the Billable Time Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Reports > Billable Time`


To customize and run the report: 

1. 
Open the Time & Resources menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, select Billable time. 

Setting the Coverage Period 

You can use one of the predefined reporting periods available from the Reporting period and As 

of date fields, or create your own reporting period using the Start date and End date fields. You 

can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both.  

In the Time period section, do one of the following: 

• 
Use the Reporting period drop-down list to select the desired reporting period, and then 

type a date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button and select a date. These 

periods are relative to the As of date. All periods begin on the first day of the period—that 

is, the first day of the month/quarter/year you select. For example, select Prior month as the 

reporting period, and then select a vendor to limit the report to a list of invoices from that 

vendor. 

• 
Type a specific Start date and/or a specific End date or click the 
 Calendar button in 

each field and select the desired date(s). 

• 
Select Prompt on run to have the system prompt you for this information at runtime. 

Prompt on run

Setting Up Filters 

Filters enable you to include or exclude specific types of data in the report, such as vendor and 

location. As a general rule, to get fewer and more precise results in your report, set more filters. 

To customize your report results, change the filters as follows: 

1. 
To include time for all employees, leave the Employee drop-down list blank. To show time 

for one employee, select the employee’s name in the Employee drop-down list. 

2. 
To include time spent on a specific project type, select the desired project type from the 

Project type drop-down list. You can select multiple project types.  

---


<!-- Page 141 -->
Chapter 4: Time & Resources Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Time & Resources User Guide 

3. 
To include time spent on a specific project, select the desired project from the Project 

drop-down list. You can select more than one project. 

4. 
To filter the report for employees that work for a specific location, select the location in the 

Location drop-down list. You can also select a location group. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per 

location. 

 Individual Report
Process & Store

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a 

location before it will run the report. 

Filling In the Format Section 

Use this section to select the report type, the page orientation, or group the data of the report. 

To format this report: 

1. 
Select how you want to group the data. Select None, Employee, or Project. 

2. 
To change the page layout, in the Page Orientation section, and then click either Portrait or 

Landscape. Portrait is the default layout. 

Filling In the Titles Section 

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the print versions of this report. You can export the 

report to Excel or CSV, or click Print for a PDF version. 

To add a title, subtitle, and footer to the report: 

1. 
Enter the title in the Report Title 1 box. 

This title appears in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that may automatically appear in this box. 

2. 
Enter the subtitle in the Report Title 2 box. 

This subtitle appears in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Enter the footer text in the Footer Text box. Footer text appears at the bottom center of the 

report. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report.  

You can view, process, memorize, export, or customize the report or add it to the dashboard 

by clicking one of the buttons at the top of the page.

## Introduction to Value Added Taxes
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 7*

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

Introduction to Value Added Taxes 

The RealPage Financial Suite offers the Taxes application to manage tax-related settings and track tax transactions 

for your system. 

The Taxes application is designed for companies that do business with countries that collect Value-Added Tax 

(VAT), such as the United Kingdom (UK).  

RealPage provides pre-installed tax solutions upon request. You need a tax solution for each tax jurisdiction that 

your company does business in. 

With the pre-installed United Kingdom tax solution, you can use your RealPage Financial Suite system to conduct 

business between the United Kingdom and European Union (EU). 

In This Chapter

C H A P T E R 1

### About Value-Added Tax (VAT)
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 8*

Introduction to Value Added Taxes 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

About Value-Added Tax (VAT) 

Value added taxes (VAT) are collected at multiple points during the production of a finished 

product.  

Register Your Company 

In order to exchange goods and services with companies in a VAT country, you must register your 

company with the tax authority, and then account for the VAT. Goods and services traded under 

VAT rules can be from the UK, the European Union (EU), Australia, and other countries. At this 

time, RealPage Financial Suite supports VAT rules of the United Kingdom. After registering your 

company, the UK government provides your business with a VAT registration number.  

HOW VAT Works 

Generally speaking, you collect VAT on sales, and you pay VAT on purchases.  

Whenever you sell something, you collect and account for the VAT. When you submit your taxes, 

the government uses the tax submission to reimburse the previous buyer in the chain. In this way, 

the VAT is ultimately paid by the consumer. 

VAT collection is based on invoicing. As the seller, you must account for invoiced amounts at the 

VAT rate, and then reclaim the VAT at the same time that you submit VAT tax reports. 

Property Management and VAT 

The landlord of a commercial property can opt in or out of taxes for VAT purposes, and must opt 

in or out of taxes on each building of a property. When the landlord opts to tax, then rental 

payments are subject to VAT. Commercial property owners charge VAT at 20% on leases. 

Residential leases are exempt from VAT in the UK. However, landlords of residential properties 

can claim VAT for renovations and other building works. 

---



### VAT and RealPage Financial Suite
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 9*

Chapter 1: Introduction to Value Added Taxes 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

RealPage Financial Suite helps with VAT collection when your company creates invoices, and 

assists with tax submissions directly to the HMRC, the UK tax authority. 

Before you can use the RealPage Financial Suite with VAT, you must enable the VAT module and 

then configure your system to be able to collect and submit VAT. 

As a supplier of property to your commercial tenants, you must calculate the taxes on rent, and 

then capture the transactions for accounting, auditing, and reporting purposes. The Taxes 

application helps your company comply with these requirements by calculating, capturing, and 

submitting VAT tax information following the rules of the HMRC. 

Entities 

Entities in the RealPage Financial Suite are a property’s tax entity. Each entity must have a unique 

VAT number.  

As an entity does business with tenants and suppliers, you provide your entity’s VAT number. 

Supported Accounting Methods 

The Taxes application supports the Accrual only or Accrual and cash accounting methods. 

RealPage Financial Suite Transactions That Support VAT Collection

transactions:

### Configuration Overview
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

Configuration 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Configuration Overview 

The Taxes application of RealPage Accounting allows you to record, report, and file taxes 

electronically to HM Revenue & Customs. Before use, the Taxes application requires some 

configuration.  

The tasks that are required depend on which tax solutions you plan to use. Use the workflow (on 

page 15) to ensure that you complete all of the configuration tasks so that the system can capture 

the taxes correctly for each tax solution that your organization uses. Many of these tasks are 

performed by an administrator or the implementation team. 

Tax Solutions 

If your company chooses to collect and submit VAT, then RealPage pre-installs a tax solution on 

your system. The tax solution determines how tax is calculated, captured, and reported for your 

tax jurisdiction. 

You can review the tax solution by opening the Taxes application, Setup tab, and then select the 

Tax solution option. 

After reviewing the tax solution, configure your system (on page 13) to use VAT.  

After your system is configured for VAT, then you can create transactions that track VAT values.  

Check out the VAT quick tour (on page 38) to see how the RealPage Financial Suite helps you 

enter invoices and journal entries.

Enabling Multi-Currency Management in General Ledger 

Enable the multi-currency subscription on the General Ledger Setup page. 

To enable multi-currency management in the General Ledger application: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click Configuration. 

3. 
In the Accounting settings section, find the Multi-currency management section. 

4. 
Select the Enable multi-currency subscription check box.  

When you select this option, multi-currency options are turned on in other applications, and 

options for managing currencies show up in the Company application.  

These applications support multi-currency:  

• 
General Ledger 

• 
Accounts Receivable 

• 
Accounts Payable 

• 
Spend Management 

5. 
In the Rounding account drop-down list, select a G/L account that the system can use for 

recording gains and losses resulting from importing journal entries.  

The system uses the rounding account to keep debits and credits in balance when journal 

entries are imported form a spreadsheet and when rounding the base currency amounts 

during import causes a minor difference between debits and credits. This requires a 

correcting entry, typically of a penny, to the rounding account. 

6. 
Click Save. 

Exchange Rates 

You can only use the RealPage Daily Rate to convert the currency of transactions of less than 20 

years in the past.

information.

Type the information you need in any of the other boxes in the Format section, and then 

click Save.

Configuration 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide

Enabling the Multi-Entity Console 

To enable the Multi Entity Console: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Select Subscriptions. 

3. 
When the Subscriptions page opens, click the Multi Entity Console switch. 

Enabling Multiple Base Currencies (VAT) 

To enable multiple base currencies: 

1. 
From the Multi entity console, click the Configure link. 

2. 
Find the Entity Preferences section, and then select the Enable multiple base currencies 

check box. 

For example, you might select this option if you have an entity that operates in US dollars 

(USD) and another that operates in Euros (EUR). 

If all your entities use the same base currency, leave this check box cleared. 

If you enable multiple base currencies: 

• 
You can’t enable the top level as an operating entity. 

• 
G/L accounts are shared across entities. 

Multiple base currencies aren’t required for transacting in multiple currencies. For instance, 

if all entities have US dollars as their base currency, they can still transact in other currencies 

(such as paying a bill in Yen), by enabling multi-currency management in the General 

Ledger. 

When you enable multiple base currencies, the Value Approval currency setup section 

appears. A value approval currency enables the system to translate the transaction currency 

into a common currency used to evaluate transaction approval thresholds and determine 

whether a transaction requires approval. 

As you enable multiple base currencies, you can set a value approval currency for purchase 

orders. The value approval currency is the main currency used in your company. 

3. 
To set a value approval currency, in the Value approval currency drop-down list, select a 

currency. Only the currencies that you enable in the RealPage Financial Suite system are 

available for selection. 

4. 
Click Save.

Register Your Property for VAT With the Tax Authority 

If your property is mixed use, register the property for VAT, but flag the leases of non-VAT units 

so that they will not be charged VAT.

Where to Get Electronic Payment Information for Your Bank 

When you decide to issue standard electronic payments, you must first inform your bank. The 

bank will in turn send you details about how it wants to format your electronic payments. This 

information is often in a document called a specification sheet. When you receive this information 

from your bank, you then enter that information on the Electronic Payment Bank Configurations 

page. 

The field names used on the Electronic Payment Bank Configuration page reflect the 

terminology of the payment service, making it easy to map the information on your bank’s 

specification sheet to the bank configuration record. 

If you select ACH, then ACH terminology is used.  

If you select EFT - Standard 005, then EFT related terminology is used.  

If you select BACS, then the terminology is related to BACS.

fields in the Defaults section and then select Apply Defaults, the system fills in all line items with 

the default values that you set up. See Setting default line items for more information. 

To set up default values: 

1. 
Click Show defaults. The Defaults section expands to show the fields for which you can set 

defaults. The Show defaults link changes to Hide defaults. 

2. 
Set up the default values for each field that you want the system to fill. 

Typically, you want to fill in default values for only one or two fields. For example, if you 

want the memo field to contain the same text for each line item, then type the desired text 

in the Memo field.  

In the Defaults section, click the drop-down list beside the desired field that you want the 

system to fill, and then choose a value.  

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button. The system completes the fields with the default values that 

you set up.

Entering Line Items in an A/R Invoice (A/R Sales Invoice) 

For the invoice to be posted, you must specify at least:

detail level in line items to enter additional information. 

To enter information for the charges in this invoice: 

1.
