If your company uses multiple currencies, then the Transaction Amount field is displayed 

instead of the Amount field. Type the amount of the line item, expressed in the currency 

that you used for the transaction. The system then calculates the Base Amount in your 

company’s base currency according to the exchange rate from the Currency section. 

3. 
Select the Multiple taxes on line check box to specify taxes for multiple jurisdictions for the 

line item. 

The Tax detail section opens. 

• 
Select the appropriate Tax detail, and then press the TAB key to move to the 

Transaction tax field. The system calculates the transaction tax based on the 

pre-defined tax rate. Check the value and make changes as needed. 

• 
On the next row, select the next applicable tax detail. You can adjust the figure in the 

Transaction tax field as needed.

Adding an A/R Adjustment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > 
 Adjustments`


This section provides the fast track to getting an adjustment entered. For a description of every 

field, see field-by-field descriptions. 

Credit Adjustments 

When you provide a credit to a customer, to record a simple decrease in the amount the 

customer owes, such as a credit for shipping costs, a return, or poor quality or service, you can 

enter the credited amount to show a decrease in your customer’s overall debt to you. You can 

then apply the decrease to one or more invoices at your convenience. 

This article describes how to create a credit adjustment for recording a simple decrease and 

answers questions about recording decreases when there are additional considerations, such as 

an associated project. 

A credit adjustment decreases the overall amount the customer owes you. For instance, if a 

customer makes a return, you create a credit adjustment for that customer to decrease the 

amount the customer owes you. 

Debit Adjustments 

A debit memo increases the overall amount the customer owes you. For instance, if you forgot to 

charge the customer for shipping or some other service, you can create an adjustment rather than 

a whole new invoice.

Multi-Entity, Multi-Currency Companies 

If your company is a multi-entity, multi-currency company, you can make adjustments at the top 

level or in the entities. When creating a top-level adjustment, you must select the base currency 

and location. However, when you make adjustments at the entity level, the system already knows 

the location and the base currency. In either case, you must select a transaction currency if you 

are entering a foreign currency adjustment. 

If you’re a multi-currency company, enter the currency details in the Currency section: 

1. 
In the Transaction currency drop-down list, select the currency that was used in the 

transaction. If the currency is not your company’s base currency, continue with the next two 

steps. 

2. 
In the Base currency drop-down list, select the currency used by your entity. 

3. 
Click Exchange rate type, and then select RealPage Daily Rate which is the system-supplied 

default exchange rate type, unless you’ve defined a different one. 

If you know what the exchange rate for this transaction is or have contracted with the 

customer on a set exchange rate, you can type it in Exchange rate to override system 

calculations. 

4. 
In Exchange rate date, type or select a date. The default value is the current date, but you 

can override this. For example, you may want to change it to the date the transaction was 

issued or the date you intend to pay the transaction. (If you override the Date, the exchange 

rate date updates automatically.) 

Fill In the Line Items in the Entries Section 

Set Up Default Values for All Line Items (Optional) 

In the Entries section, you can add values directly to each line item where needed or click the 

Show defaults link to set up default values that the system will use to complete each line item. 

To set up a value as a default for each existing and new line item: 

1. 
Click Show defaults. 

2. 
In each drop-down list that you want the system to complete, choose a value.  

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button to save the selections.  

Keep in mind that you can override any default value on any line item.

 If your company has enabled account labels, this column is called Account label. Select the

about Segments.

Finding Draft or Posted Transactions 

Lists of transactions let you view and access all transactions of a specific type, such as invoices or 

adjustments. 

There are two ways to locate and view items in the draft and posted state. 

• 
Filter for Draft or Posted Transactions on the Fly 

From a list view, type either “Draft” or “Posted” in the State column. 

The system filters the list, displaying only those items with a state matching the text that you 

typed. 

• 
Create a Permanent Custom View That Filters for Draft or Posted Transactions 

Create a view.

Paid). 

When you save the view, you can select it from the All menu whenever you go to the list.

to show only posted transactions.

Adding a New Attachment to a Record 

This topic describes how to attach a file to a record when the file is not yet stored in the system. 

To attach a file to a record when the file is already in the system, see Adding an Existing 

Attachment to a Record. 

The steps for attaching documents to transactions and records are different depending on 

whether the Enable single scan upload option is enabled or disabled in your user preferences. 

Adding a New Attachment to a Record When Scanning is Disabled  

To add a new attachment to a record when scanning is disabled: 

1. 
Add a new record or edit an existing record to open the information page. 

2. 
Click the Attachments drop-down list, and then click the Add link. 

The Select attachments page opens. 

3. 
Type a unique ID for the attachment record. If your company is configured to auto-number, 

then the system automatically displays an ID for the attachment. 

4. 
Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

5. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

6. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment.

Configuration Differences that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
When your system is configured to use multiple currencies, additional currency fields appear 

in this record. See the multi-currency systems section on the General Ledger configuration 

page. 

• 
When the Intercompany billing option is enabled (Accounts Receivable configuration), the 

A/R Invoice Dimensions section appears. 

• 
When your system is integrated with OpsTechnology, it allows RealPage Accounting to 

receive eInvoices. 

• 
Accounts Payable configuration:  

• 
When the Enable bank account selection in A/P invoice option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Bank account field to appear on the A/P invoice 

record. 

• 
When the Enable invoice entry control validation option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Total invoice amount field to appear on the A/P 

invoice record. 

• 
When Spend management is enabled, then the Match Order button appears, allowing you 

to match a purchase order to the A/P invoice. Additional fields appear on the record such as 

QTY, Price, Extended Price, UOM, and Account code description. 

• 
When Job Cost is enabled, then the Line Entry Type section appears. When you select 

Include Job cost, the system adds Job cost-specific columns in the Invoice Entries list such 

as Job name, Cost code, and Job unit.  

• 
When scanning is enabled, the Attachments field is replaced with the Documents section, 

affecting the way that you attach documents.  

• 
If the Please complete one-time setup scanner prompt appears, follow the 

instructions in Downloading the Scanning Software. If you do not plan to scan 

supporting documents at this time, you can skip the download by clicking the X in 

upper-right corner of the box.

To create an A/P invoice: 

1. 
In the Date field, type the date of the invoice, or leave it set to today’s date.  

Any date entered here is automatically filled in the G/L posting date field (and to the 

Exchange rate date field if you’re a multi-currency company). You can change either date as 

needed; for example, if you want to create the adjustment today, but post it on a different 

date. 

2. 
In the G/L posting date field, type the date that you want the A/P invoice to post on the 

general ledger.  

3. 
In the Total invoice amount field, type the amount of the invoice.  

This field appears only when the Enable invoice entry control validation check box is 

selected on the configuration page of Accounts Payable. When enabled, this is a required 

field.  

4. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select an existing vendor or add a new vendor, as required. 

The system completes the Pay to and Return to fields automatically based on the vendor 

record that you select. This is a required field. 

To add a new vendor, you must be at the top level. You can use the field-level controls to 

add a new vendor, view a vendor’s record, or find a vendor’s record. 

The system fills in the Pay to field automatically. If you need to change the Pay to contact, 

you can do that here. In the Pay to drop-down list, select the name of the person to whom 

the payment should be sent. 

The system fills in the Return to field automatically. If you need to change the Return to 

contact, you can do that here. In the Return to drop-down list, select the name of the 

person to whom returns should be addressed.  

5. 
To fill in the A/P invoice form with data from the last A/P invoice from this vendor, click the 

Populate from last A/P invoice button.

In the Invoice number field, type the invoice number. This is a required field.

Saving the A/P Invoice 

When entering the transaction information, save it as a draft or post it. The system validates 

transactions only when they are posted. For example, required departments or locations are not 

validated until posting. 

•

subledger or G/L. Later, you or another user can review and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the transaction. 

System Checks for Budget Exceeded  

If you try to post an A/P invoice that exceeds the default budget, and your company uses the A/P 

invoice approval process with the budget exceeded feature, the system displays a warning. The 

system may also prevent you from posting the A/P invoice. If you want to be able to bypass this 

budget check, ask your system administrator to grant you the desired bypass permission. Bypass 

permissions are available for A/P invoices and purchase orders. 

When the budget exceeded feature is enabled, the system checks the A/P invoice amount against 

the budgeted number for the G/L account. When the amount exceeds the budget, then the 

system either displays a warning or prevents you from saving the A/P invoice, depending on how 

your company configured the feature. When preventing an A/P invoice from being posted, the 

system also displays a warning to let you know why you cannot post. 

To enable or disable the budget exceeded feature, see Setting a system action when an A/P 

invoice or purchase order exceeds the budget.

System Checks for Attachments 

Your company may require that you attach a document to support the A/P invoice before you can 

save it as a draft, post, or submit it. If you need to save an A/P invoice without an attachment, 

contact your system administrator and ask them to remove the Require attachment permission 

from your role or account. 

What’s Next? 

When your company uses approvals, A/P invoices first go through the payment approval 

workflow. After payments are approved, you can make the payments.  

Go to the Pay A/P invoices page to select the invoice for payment. When you select Add to 

outbox or Pay now: 

• 
The invoice becomes a payment request. 

• 
The system notifies approvers that a payment is waiting for their approval. 

• 
You can view the status of the payment request in the Payment request list. 

• 
When an approver approves the invoice, the system pays the invoice. 

• 
If the payment method is Check, the system allows the payment to be included in a check 

run.

Finishing the Adjustment 

When you finish entering the adjustment, save it as a draft or post it.  

Selecting Draft saves the adjustment as a draft without affecting the General Ledger or any 

subledger. With the ability to save A/P invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments in draft state, you 

can save your progress so far. Later on, you or another user can come back and post the 

transaction. 

Selecting Post saves the adjustment and has the system validate the transaction when it is posted. 

For example, required departments or locations are not validated until posting. 

• 
Select Draft to save your progress on the transaction. The system saves the entry, but 

doesn’t post it. 

• 
Select Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction. The system saves the entry, but 

doesn’t post it, and opens a new adjustment.  

• 
Select Draft & Continue to save your progress on the transaction and continue working on 

it. 

• 
Select Post to save your transaction and post it to the General Ledger. 

• 
Select Post & new to post the transaction. The system validates the transaction and posts it 

to the General Ledger. 

Adding a Journal Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find 
 Journal Entry`


When you add a transaction to a journal, you have the option of saving it as a draft or posting it 

right away. Transactions that are saved as a draft do not have to be complete—you or another 

user can review them later, make changes, and then post them. When you post a journal 

transaction, the entire transaction must balance, and all required information must be entered. 

You can substantiate a transaction by associating it with a supporting attachment. You can also 

use the transaction allocations to automatically distribute amounts across departments and 

locations. 

You can add a journal entry directly or add it from the General Ledger workbench. This topic 

describes how to add a journal entry directly. 

This topic describes how to add a standard journal entry. If you want to create a statistical journal 

entry, see Creating statistical journal entries. 

To add a new journal entry: 

Enter general information about the transaction. The top part of the page is where you enter the 

transaction date, description, and other basic information.

In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal where you want to add the new journal 

entry.

advance the posting date of the journal entry to the next open period.

Finishing the Journal Entry 

When you finish entering or editing the journal entry:

a new journal entry.

 Add button next to Customer 

adjustments.

In the Customer drop-down list, select the customer to whom this adjustment applies.

In the Attachments drop-down list, add an attachment if needed.

 Calendar button, 

and then select the desired date to have the system fill in the date.

should be sent.

this adjustment.

### Submitting VAT Taxes Workflow
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 106*

Using RealPage Financial Suite with VAT Taxes 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Submitting VAT Taxes Workflow 

To use your system with VAT taxes there are a few differences in the way you must manage 

information. 

1. 
Data entry. During data entry, the user selects a tax rate for each line item in a transaction. 

Interaction with VAT taxes occurs in the following places in the system: 

• 
Multi-currency invoices and postings 

• 
Multi-currency payments 

• 
Journal entries 

• 
Journal entries from OneSite that use VAT 

• 
Viewing tax records 

• 
Submitting taxes 

• 
Viewing submitted returns 

• 
Reconciling transactions  

The system calculates VAT based on the selected tax rate and collects the information for 

later submission to the tax authority.  

2. 
View your tax records (on page 107). 

3. 
Submit VAT tax returns to HMRC online (on page 107) or offline (on page 109). 

4. 
Verify and review your submitted tax returns (on page 111). 

5. 
Use these reports to monitor tax transactions and submissions: 

• 
Tax Transactions (on page 132) 

• 
Tax Submissions (on page 128) 

---

Submitting Taxes Offline 

You can submit your VAT taxes offline rather than working through the HMRC website.

Download the tax file. 

5. 
Download your tax form from HMRC and fill it in offline with the data from the tax file that 

you downloaded from RealPage’s Taxes application. Submit the taxes offline.

3 - Total VAT Due

(link) 

This is the total amount of deductible VAT charged on your business

period.

(link) 

This is the total value of all your business sales and other specific

VAT (link)

not include any VAT.

obligation period. 

8 - Total Goods 

Supplied Ex VAT 

(link) 

This is the total value of all exported goods and related costs, excluding 

any VAT, to EU member states. Related costs include freight and 

insurance.

period. 

9 - Total Acquisitions 

Ex VAT (link) 

This is the total value of all purchased goods from VAT-registered 

suppliers in EU member states and directly related costs, such as freight 

and insurance, where these form part of the invoice or contract price. 

This figure does not include any VAT. 

Click the link to view the list of imported goods for this tax obligation 

period.

### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 137*

Chapter 5: Reports 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 138) topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized, that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead.

### Storing Standard Reports and Charts
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 140*



#### Viewing a Stored Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 140*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

Viewing a Stored Report 

After the system runs the report on the date that you selected, you can find the report in either 

the My stored reports list or the Reports center. 

To view a stored report in the My stored reports list: 

1. 
Open the application where you created the report. 

2. 
On the All tab of the menu, find and select the My stored reports option. 

The My stored reports list opens with a list of reports stored in the application. 

3. 
Find the report that you want to view and then verify the report date in the Run date/time 

column. Verifying the report date helps you avoid missing data. For example, if you 

scheduled the report to run two weeks ago, you would be missing the last two weeks of 

data. 

4. 
Click one of the following links to open your report in the format it was stored:  

• 
HTML: Opens the report in a new browser tab as a web page. 

• 
PDF: Opens a printable PDF version of the report that you can print and download. 

• 
CSV: Downloads a CSV file containing the report data. This is a good format to 

download if you want to import the data into another application. 

• 
Excel: Downloads the report as an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Opens a text version of the report in the web browser. 

• 
Cloud: Opens the report in your configured cloud account. If there is no cloud link for 

the report, see Storing a Report in a Cloud Storage Location (on page 145). 

• 
Success: Opens the report in Reporting Portal. If there was an error processing the 

report, then the View status link appears in the column instead. See Viewing a Report 

Error Log for error details.

### Memorized Reports
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 152*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 152*



#### How to Get Here
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 152*

Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Memorized Reports 

See the How to Get Here (on page 152) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Memorizing a report retains the report parameters so you don’t have to select them each time 

you want to run or display the report. When you memorize a report, you can assign it a unique 

name so you can add the report to dashboards or report groups or schedule it to run on a 

recurring basis. We recommend that you test run the report with the desired parameters to verify 

that the report output is correct before memorizing the report. 

Memorized Reports Locations 

Memorized reports appear in the Memorized reports list (on page 154) and in the Reports 

center. 

The Memorized reports list is accessible from most RealPage Financial Suite applications; 

however, it displays only the reports that were memorized in the application you access it from. 

For example, if you click the Memorized reports option in the Cash Management menu, then the 

list will include only reports memorized in Cash Management. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Memorizing a report requires that you have the permissions to do so. You must have permissions 

to access and run a report in order to memorize it. Permissions for users, groups, or roles are 

configured in the Company setup. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 189) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 188) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

How to Get Here 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Reports Center > Memorized`


1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
Select Reports Center. 

3. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

---

Chapter 5: Reports

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide

2.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Property Management/Condo and Co-op > All > Reports > Custom 
Reports > Memorized Reports`


1. 
Open the desired application. 

2. 
In the Reports column, find the Custom Reports section, and then select Memorized reports. 

Memorizing a Report or Chart 

To memorize a report or chart: 

1. 
Set up a report or chart with the filters and parameters that you want to save. 

2. 
Click the Memorize button. The Memorize report parameters box opens. 

3. 
In the Name field, type a name for the report or chart. 

4. 
Select the Public check box to make the report or chart available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to keep it private. Private reports and charts are 

visible only to the person who created them (owners), and administrators. 

5. 
Click OK.

Memorized Reports List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 152) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Memorized reports list to view and manage reports that you saved in an application or 

that other users saved and then made public. From this list, you can: 

• 
Run memorized reports. 

• 
Edit memorized reports that you created. 

• 
Process large reports in the background and store them in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Schedule reports so that they run at a future date. 

• 
Delete memorized reports. 

• 
Export the list of memorized reports.

Editing a Memorized Report 

See the How to Get Here (on page 152) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

You can edit a memorized report or chart only if you are the owner or a system administrator, 

even if the report or chart was made public. As the owner, you can change any parameter, 

including who owns it. The only field you cannot change is the report type.  

To edit a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, click the Edit link next to the report or chart that you want to 

change. The Edit memorized report page opens. The fields on this page correspond with 

the report’s type.  

2. 
Update the fields in the General information section as needed: 

• 
In the Report name and Report description fields, type a new name and description 

for the report, respectively.

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here (on page 152) topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report (on page 162) page 

opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report (on page 162) page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by. 

---

If you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears.

### Contact Tax Groups
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 170*



#### Standard Contact Tax Groups
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 170*

Setup 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Contact Tax Groups 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Settings > Contact Tax Groups`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Taxes > Setup > Tax Groups > Contact Tax Groups`


Contact tax groups enable you to apply different taxes to customers, vendors, and their contacts, 

according to their jurisdictions. You associate customers, vendors, and their contacts with contact 

tax groups. Then, you use tax schedule maps to apply different tax schedules to your contact tax 

groups. 

VAT Example for VAT Solution 

VAT is typically different for customers inside and outside your country. You could create two 

customer contact tax groups, one for “In-country customers” and another for “Outside-country 

customers.” You could then apply one tax schedule to all the customers in the In-country group 

and another tax schedule to all the customers in the Outside-country group. 

Taxes 

Standard Contact Tax Groups 

Depending on the tax solution you configured in the Taxes subscription, contact tax groups which 

are tailored to the tax jurisdiction are automatically created. 

If you configured the Taxes subscription to use the United Kingdom tax solution, the following 

contact tax groups were automatically created: 

Contact tax groups 

• 
EC customers 

• 
EC suppliers 

• 
General Export customers 

• 
Import suppliers 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 171*

Chapter 6: Setup 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

• 
UK customers 

• 
UK suppliers 

Assign the applicable customers, vendors, and their contacts to the appropriate contact tax 

groups. 

• 
For Accounts Receivable, the system uses the customer ship-to contact to capture tax. If the 

ship-to contact is the same as the primary contact, it’s sufficient to mark the customer 

record as taxable and assign the customer to a contact tax group. If the ship-to and primary 

contacts differ, make sure the ship-to contact is marked as taxable and assigned to a 

contact tax group. 

• 
For Accounts Payable, the system uses the vendor pay-to contact to capture tax. If the 

pay-to contact is the same as the primary contact, it’s sufficient to mark the vendor record 

as taxable and assign the vendor to a contact tax group. If the pay-to and primary contacts 

differ, make sure the pay-to contact is marked as taxable and assigned to a contact tax 

group. 

To learn more about how contact tax groups are used to capture tax, see Tax schedule maps (on 

page 174). 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

### Tax Schedule Maps List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 174*

Setup 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Tax Schedule Maps List 

These are the most direct options for opening the Tax Schedule Maps list. You may have 

additional options based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > Schedule Maps`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Schedule Maps`


A tax schedule map associates tax schedules with account labels (via account label tax groups) 

and customers (via contact tax groups). The tax schedule contains the tax detail records, which 

define the amount of tax to apply.  

When a user enters an invoice for a customer in a contact tax group and the user enters a line for 

an account label in an account label tax group, the tax schedule map tells the system which tax 

schedules to use for the subtotal tax account label. 

The Memo field displays the names of the tax detail records associated with the tax schedules 

assigned to the tax subtotal based on the tax schedule map.

### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 188*

Appendices 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

---



#### Assigning Permissions for a New Feature
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 189*

Appendix A: Appendices 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

Assigning Permissions for a New Feature 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users > Subscriptions > Permissions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > Permissions`


When RealPage adds a new feature, it often comes with new permissions that you must enable 

before users can use the new feature. 

To add permissions for a new feature: 

• 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

If using Role-based permissions 

1. 
Select Roles. 

2. 
Find the role that you want to change. 

3. 
Click the Subscriptions link.  

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions window opens. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions. 

6. 
Click the Save button on the application’s permissions page. 

7. 
Click the Save button on the Roles subscriptions page. 

8. 
Click the Done button to close the list. 

If using User-based permissions 

1. 
Select Users. 

2. 
Locate the user who needs to be able to use the new feature.  

3. 
Select the Subscriptions link. 

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions.  

6. 
Click the Save button. 

7. 
Click the Save button on the User application subscriptions page. 

8. 
Click the Done button to close the list.

#### Adding a Cloud Storage Target
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 190*

Appendices 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Adding a Cloud Storage Target 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Cloud Storage`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Cloud Storage > Add`


You can define as many cloud storage targets as you need. Multiple targets can be set up for 

different cloud storage sites, or for the same cloud storage site. For example, you can define one 

Dropbox target for an external client, another Dropbox target for internal reports, and a third as a 

DDS delivery destination. 

Defining the Cloud Storage Settings 

1. 
In the Storage type drop-down list, select one of the options: 

• 
HTTP 

• 
Dropbox 

• 
Google Drive 

• 
Box 

• 
Amazon S3 

• 
SFTP 

2. 
Enter a Name for the cloud storage target that you want to appear in the list. This is the 

same name displayed when setting up cloud delivery for a particular report. 

3. 
Verify the assigned Owner.  

• 
If you are an administrator, you have the option to make another user the owner. 

Otherwise, you are automatically the owner. 

• 
If the cloud storage target is marked as “Private,” only the owner and any 

administrators can edit its information. 

4. 
Enter one or more Email addresses where you want the system to send error reports if there 

are any undelivered reports. 

5. 
Select the Private check box if you want the target to be viewed and used only by the owner 

and administrators. Other users will not see private targets in the Cloud-Storage Targets list 

and cannot use them for report delivery.  

6. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists. 

---


<!-- Page 191 -->
Appendix A: Appendices 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

Defining the Storage Type 

If you selected HTTP, go to Setting Up an HTTP Post. 

If you selected Dropbox, Google Drive, or Box, enter the storage Path. 

If you selected SFTP: 

1. 
Enter the SFTP Host name. 

2. 
Enter the Port to connect to the server. 

3. 
Provide the SFTP user name and SFTP password. 

If you selected Amazon S3: 

1. 
Enter the Bucket you created in your Amazon S3 account. 

2. 
In Path, enter an optional location, relative to the top level of the cloud storage target 

where you want reports to be delivered. 

• 
If you don’t enter a path, the system delivers all reports to the top-most level of the 

target. 

• 
To send data to a particular folder, enter the directory path to the folder. For example, 

to save the reports in a Quarterly_reports folder, enter “Quarterly_reports.” 

3. 
Select the Encrypt check box to encrypt the Amazon S3 data. This encrypts the files sent 

from RealPage Accounting to Amazon S3. Currently, server side encryption AES 256 is 

supported. This feature is turned off by default. 

4. 
In the Restrict file access to drop-down list, select one of the options: 

• 
Bucket owner only: Make the files private and available only to the bucket owner. 

• 
Authenticated users: Make files available to users who have permissions to read the 

Amazon S3 account. 

5. 
Click the Save button.

Importing Tax Objects 

If you are using the Taxes application, importing your tax objects for the custom VAT and 

Advanced Tax solutions can be more efficient than entering the data manually through the user 

interface. 

If you’re using United Kingdom VAT, you start with a preconfigured set of tax objects that are 

automatically created for you when you configure the tax solution. If you need to define 

additional tax objects to meet additional business needs, you can import the data or enter it 

manually. 

Tax Objects 

These topics are applicable only if your company is subscribed to the Taxes application. 

---



#### Order of Import
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 193*

Appendix A: Appendices 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

Order of Import 

When importing tax objects into the system, the order in which you import data is the key to 

successful imports. For example, if you import a tax schedule but you don’t have any tax schedule 

records in your company, your import will fail because the Tax schedules field is required. 

Be sure to review the CSV template files before importing information into the system. If a 

required field is left blank, the import will fail. You can get copies of the CSV templates listed 

below on the Import Data page or on the list pages. 

Follow this order of importing to prevent import failures: 

1. 
Contact Tax Groups (a required field in Tax Schedule Maps) 

2. 
Item Tax Groups (a required field in Tax Schedule Maps if using Advanced Tax) 

3. 
Tax Authorities (an optional field in Tax Details) 

4. 
Tax Details (an optional field in Tax Schedules) 

5. 
Tax Schedules (a required field in Tax Schedule Maps) 

6. 
Tax Schedule Maps 

RealPage assumes the most common way data is entered into the system is from a blank CSV 

template. When importing data using CSV files, be sure to: 

• 
Download the most current version of the template from the Import Data page or the list 

pages. 

• 
Review the CSV templates for required fields. 

• 
Review the Prepare your CSV file for import best practices before starting your import. 

You can also export existing data from the system, change the information in the CSV files, and 

then import the new data into the system. 

---

Importing Contact Tax Groups 

You might want to import contact tax groups if you are using: 

• 
Advanced Tax without the Taxes application 

• 
The Taxes application for VAT or Advanced Tax solutions. 

Before You Begin 

You must have Administrator privileges to download the templates that are used to import data. 

Permissions 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with contact tax groups. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Contact tax group 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 189) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 188) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

Appendix A: Appendices

Downloading the Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Settings section, click the Contact tax groups option. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Contact tax groups box opens. 

4. 
Click the Download template link. The file downloads to your browser’s default download 

folder. 

Adding Your Data 

Next you add your data, using the correct formatting as explained in the template. After you’ve 

added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in mind. This helps 

eliminate anything that might make your import fail. 

1. 
Open the downloaded spreadsheet in Excel. 

2. 
Add the data to the template by filling in the Name column with the names of contact tax 

groups that you want to add. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

Importing the Data 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Settings section, click the Contact tax groups option. 

3. 
Click the Import button. The Contact tax groups box opens. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button. 

5. 
Find the CSV file and double-click it.  

6. 
Add your email address to the Email results to this address field. 

7. 
Click the Import button.

Setting Up Your Checking Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > 
 Accounts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > 
 Bank Accounts > Details > 
Default Bank G/L Account`


To create a new checking account, first create the G/L account to which it will be mapped. 

To add a G/L account: 

1. 
Open the General ledger menu. 

2. 
Select 
 Add next to the Accounts option to create the new account. 

3. 
Click Save. 

Next, create your checking account and associate it with the G/L account you just created. 

To create a checking account: 

1. 
Open the Cash management menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
In the Accounts section, select 
 next to the Bank accounts option. The Bank account 

information page opens. 

3. 
On the Details tab, in the Accounting Information section, in the Default bank G/L account 

drop-down list, select the G/L account you just created. 

4. 
Select the Check printing tab, and then set up your checking account to print checks.  

5. 
In Print on, select to print on pre-printed check stock or blank check stock. Learn more 

about these two types of check stock. 

6. 
In the Print settings section, in Next check #, type the next check number you want to print.  

Printing format: For pre-printed check stock, choose between Standard and High-security. 

For blank check stock, choose between Standard, Business, Canadian, or Mexican (if you 

are set up for foreign currency).  

MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) section (for blank check stock only): Specify 

where to align your account number and the length of your check number.  

7. 
Click Save.

Using the Multi-Select Drop-down List 

Use the Multi-select box to select the items that you will act on in the next step. This example 

shows how to select locations. 

• 
Click the drop-down list to open the Multi-select box.  

a) 
Click the arrow to open the drop-down list, and then select the desired item or items. 

You can also start typing the name of the desired item if you know it. When the item 

that you want appears in the list, select it. 

b) 
Type the name of an item to search for. Click the check box when it appears in the list. 

c) 
Select this check box to select all items in the list.  

• 
To add one item, select one check box.  

• 
To add all items, click the Select all check box. 

• 
To remove all items, clear the Select all check box. 

The list closes and shows how many items are selected.

Appendices 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide

Using the Multi-Select Box 

Use the Multi-select box to select the items that you will act on in the next step. The goal is to 

find items in the Available items column that you want to act on and then move them into the 

Selected Items column. 

1. 
Click the Select button to open the Multi-select box. 

• 
To search for an item, type one or more letters in the Search items box. The system 

filters the items in the list to show only items that begin with the characters that you 

type.  

• 
To add an item, click the 
 Add button. The item moves to the Selected items 

column. 

• 
To add all items, select the Add all link. All items move from the Available items 

column into the Selected items column. 

• 
Click the 
 Delete button to remove an item. 

• 
To rearrange the list, drag an item to a new position in the list using the 
 Rearrange 

button. Repeat as necessary. 

2. 
When you have finished selecting items, click the Done button. The Selection box closes 

and is replaced by a smaller box that lists the items that you selected. The number of items 

appears in parentheses. The Select button changes to an Add/Edit link. 

In this box, you can: 

• 
Click the 
 Delete button to remove an item. 

• 
Click the Add/Edit link to reopen the Multi-select box and change your selections.

Supported Currencies and Standard Codes 

RealPage Accounting supports over 190 currencies, from Afghanistan Afghani (AFN) to the 

Zimbabwe Dollar (ZWD). 

After you’ve enabled multi-currency management in the General Ledger, you can select the 

currencies you want to make available in your company by adding them to the Transaction 

currencies list. 

Any currencies you select can be: 

• 
Used in transactions, such as A/P and A/R invoices and expense reports 

• 
(For multi-entity companies) Selected as an entity’s base currency 

Currency codes 

For the most up-to-date list of international currency codes, go to: 

https://www.oanda.com/currency/help/currency-iso-code-country

Filling In the Reporting Accounts Labels Section 

If you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, you can substitute the account 

labels with the reporting account set’s labels in the report. For more information, see Reporting 

Account Sets. 

1. 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts labels 

check box. 

2. 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose labels 

you want to substitute into the report.  

3. 
If you prefer to choose the reporting account set each time that you run the report, then 

select the Prompt on run check box. When you select this option, the system asks you for 

the reporting account set every time you run the report. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report. You can either select the Reporting period and As of date, 

or select a date range to identify the report’s coverage period, but not both. 

To run a report for a reporting period: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the reporting period. 

2. 
In the As of date field, select the date to begin the report coverage.  

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want to be able to choose the reporting period 

and As of date when you run the report. 

To run a report for a date range: 

• 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s period of coverage.  

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set the filters to get the specific data you want. Filters enable you to include or exclude specific 

types of data in the report, such as vendor and location. As a general rule, to get fewer and more 

precise results in your report, set more filters.  

1. 
If your company has multiple reporting books, select the main Reporting book from the 

drop-down list. 

2. 
Select Other books that you want to use for this report. Click the Select button and then 

choose the books to use in your report. Refer to Using the multi-select box (on page 198) 

for instructions.

the period on which you are reporting. More specifically, the net change is the account total 

plus debits minus credits. If you selected the prior year as the period, it is the net change for 

the prior year.

What’s Next?  

After you run the report, you can either email the report to others or return to the report setup

then clicking View to see the report. After you view the results, if you want to refine the report 

further, then click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this process until you’re

#### Exporting from Lists
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 210*

Appendices 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Exporting from Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

To export a list of records from the system: 

1. 
Select the Include inactive check box to include items with an Inactive status in the data 

export results or clear the Include inactive check box to exclude inactive items. 

2. 
Select the Include private check box to include items that are associated with an entity or 

clear the Include private check box to exclude these items. 

3. 
Click the Export button. 

4. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again.

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 212*

Tax Authorities List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Authorities`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Authorities`


Tax authorities are agencies (for example, cities, states, provinces, federal, or HMRC, for example) 

for whom you are collecting sales and other taxes. If your organization uses VAT, the Tax 

authorities list shows all of the tax authorities in your system.  

You can create tax authorities, including hierarchies of tax authorities with parent-child 

relationships, and modify existing ones. Tax authorities are shared between Accounts Receivable 

and Accounts Payable and thus appear on the Setup menu of both applications.  

You use tax authorities by assigning a line item in a transaction to a tax authority when the item is 

taxable. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with tax authorities.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 189) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 188) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

If your organization is using VAT taxes (UK only), the Tax details list shows all the tax details you 

have created to which items can be assigned.  

Use the Tax detail list to view the details of a specific type of tax to be applied to a line item. 

When the system calculates the taxes, the tax schedule map applies the chosen tax details to any 

taxable line items in invoices.  

You assign the tax detail in the tax schedule using the Tax schedules detail tab.

#### Adding Tax Details
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 220*

Appendices 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Adding Tax Details 

These are the most direct options for adding tax details. You may have additional options based 

on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > 
 Details`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > 
 Details`


Not only can you specify the tax rate, but you can also specify a taxable range such that items 

with costs below a minimum are not taxed, and the tax stops when the cost of the item goes 

above the maximum.  

You can also specify an absolute minimum and/or maximum taxable amount. A minimum is that 

which must be paid when the calculated tax on an item is too low; the maximum tax overrides the 

calculated tax if that tax goes above the maximum taxable amount. In addition, you can also 

choose a tax authority (City of San Jose, for example) for whom you are collecting the taxes.  

To add tax details: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu.  

3. 
In the Tax section, click 
 Add next to Details. The Tax details information page opens. 

4. 
In the Detail ID field, type a name for the tax detail. After you save this name, it can’t be 

changed.  

5. 
In the Description field, type a description of the tax, such as Excise tax for Equipment. 

6. 
In the Minimum taxable amount field, If the item is not taxed until its cost passes a specific 

threshold, type that amount in the Minimum taxable amount box. 

7. 
In the Maximum taxable amount field, if the tax tops out at another limit, type that amount 

in the Maximum taxable amount box. For example, say items under $200 are not taxable. 

You enter $200 as the minimum. Taxes will not be added in any document using this tax 

detail for items under $200. However, for items over $200, the tax in the Percent field is 

added.  

8. 
In the Include in taxable amount drop-down list, click one of the following:  

• 
Full amount - include the cost from zero up to the maximum taxable amount.  

• 
Amount within range - include the amount between the minimum and maximum 

taxable amount.  

To save the record and open a new record page, click Save & new.  

9. 
In the Percent field, type the tax rate. For example, type 6 to apply a tax of 6%. 

---


<!-- Page 221 -->
Appendix A: Appendices 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

10. 
In Minimum tax and Maximum tax fields, if an item has a fixed minimum or maximum tax 

regardless of amount, then enter those amounts.  

11. 
In the G/L Account drop-down list, select the general ledger account to which this tax is to 

be assigned. You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s 

record, or find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the 

top level. 

Account label 

Account label 
G/L account

12. 
In the Account label drop-down list, select the account label for the general ledger account 

you selected in the G/L account drop-down list. 

13. 
In the Tax authority drop-down list, select the tax authority to which this tax belongs.  

14. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active to add the new item to the Tax details 

drop-down list. Or select Inactive to prevent the new item from appearing in the list. To see 

the inactive tax details later, select the Show inactive check box in the list page.  

15. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

new. The system saves the record and opens a new blank record.

About Tax Schedules 

A tax schedule is where one or more tax details are assigned. For example, you could create a 

schedule named Los Gatos - State & Local where two tax details (Los Gatos Local and California 

State) are assigned. When this schedule is referenced, both taxes are applied.

Tax Schedule Maps List 

These are the most direct options for opening the Tax Schedule Maps list. You may have 

additional options based on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > Schedule Maps`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Schedule Maps`


A tax schedule map associates tax schedules with account labels (via account label tax groups) 

and customers (via contact tax groups). The tax schedule contains the tax detail records, which 

define the amount of tax to apply.  

When a user enters an invoice for a customer in a contact tax group and the user enters a line for 

an account label in an account label tax group, the tax schedule map tells the system which tax 

schedules to use for the subtotal tax account label. 

The Memo field displays the names of the tax detail records associated with the tax schedules 

assigned to the tax subtotal based on the tax schedule map.

#### Tax Schedule Map Overview
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 232*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 232*

Appendices 

RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Tax Schedule Map Overview 

A tax schedule map shows you which tax schedules apply to which account labels and contact tax 

groups associated with those labels. In other words, if the item is taxable and the contact is in a 

certain city, the system applies a particular tax schedule. 

Example 

When computer hardware is purchased (account label tax group) by a person in London (contact 

tax group), add both a sales tax and value-added tax (tax schedule with tax two details). 

When you create an invoice, the system evaluates all tax schedule maps against the line items in 

the invoice along with to whom the invoice is issued, and then knows which tax schedules to 

apply to each line item. 

The tax schedule map includes the account label tax group, contact tax group, and tax schedule. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with tax schedules and tax schedule maps.

## Glossary of Terms
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 237*



### Elimination Entities
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 237*



### Head lease
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 237*



### HMRC
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 237*



### Rent review
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide.pdf`, Page 237*

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite Value Added Tax User Guide 

Elimination Entities 

Elimination entities are shell companies that are 

used only for posting consolidation entries for a 

consolidation book, and where the Global 

Consolidations application posts consolidation 

journal entries such as currency translation 

adjustments and elimination transactions for 

inter-entity balances. 

Head lease 

This is a type of lease used in the UK where the 

property owner leases a property to an entity 

that will subsequently grant leases to sub-lessees 

who will be the actual tenants. The sub-lessees 

hold underleases which are called subleases in 

the US. The landlord is said to have the superior 

lease.  

Superior lease: This is the lease that the entity 

(landlord) holds with the property owner. 

Underlease: This is a lease that the tenant holds 

with the entity. 

Freehold: A property without encumbrances to 

another entity such as a mortgage to a bank is 

called freehold property. 

Leasehold: You own the property but not the 

land on which it is built. 

HMRC 

The HMRC is the tax authority of the United 

Kingdom government. It stands for Her Majesty’s 

Revenue and Customs. The agency’s 

responsibilities include collecting taxes, and 

enforcing tax and custom laws. 

Rent review 

In the United Kingdom, commercial leases 

undergo a rent review period to allow the 

landlord to re-assess the rent for a property so 

that it keeps pace with the market.

Platform (Customization) Services 

Platform Services, or Customization Services, provides tools that you can use to extend the data and objects that 

are part of RealPage Accounting. You can add fields, create and run custom reports on your data, send automated 

emails, and create rules and warnings that guide users along your unique business practices. 

The documentation for this application is divided into two chapters: 

• 
Introduction to Platform (Customization) Services: (on page 3) This chapter provides an overview of the 

application and its menu options. 

• 
Using Platform (Customization) Services: (on page 7) This chapter describes how to use the application to 

add and manage custom reports, document templates, custom views, custom fields, smart rules, and smart 

events.

#### Application Overview

Introduction to Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide

Application Overview 

What is Platform (Customization) Services? 

Platform (Customization) Services provides the tools to extend RealPage Accounting and make 

new options available immediately. Among other features, you can: 

• 
Create new custom fields. 

• 
Create and run custom reports. 

• 
Automate communications about accounting activities to key associates. 

• 
Automate emails to customers and vendors regarding sales and purchase orders. 

• 
Create rules and warnings that guide users along your unique business practices. 

With these tools, you will be able to better adapt the system to suit your business needs. By 

implementing unique reports, fields, and activities related to your business, you can create better 

business processes that improve profitability and meet growing compliance regulations. 

Who can use Platform (Customization) Services? 

Although many companies rely on their developers to perform customization tasks, any user with 

administrator-level privileges can access this application to adapt the system to their unique 

business processes. If you understand basic accounting reporting principles and the results that 

you want to achieve, then you should be able to use it.

#### Custom Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Custom Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > Custom Reports`


In addition to standard and financial reports, you can build custom reports by adding your 

specific records, fields, and calculations. Custom reports are created with the custom report 

wizard, which walks you through the steps to create a report. 

Create custom reports to get insight and answers from the unique information stored in your 

system. Financial reports are based on account groupings such as assets and liabilities, while 

custom reports and dimension structures are based on records and fields either grouped together 

or separately. 

For example, you can create a custom report that displays vendor contact information. You can 

control which vendors you want to display, such as active vendors in certain regions, and select 

the details to include about the vendors. You can then sort and display the results to highlight 

what is most important to you. 

With a custom report, you can: 

• 
Report on fields from almost any record or transaction in the system, and any related data. 

• 
Customize the report for your needs. 

• 
Run the reports, export them in another format, or add them to dashboards. 

Before you can export a standard report or add it to a group, you need to memorize the report.

The Custom reports list displays all custom reports that have been created for your company, 

including basic information about each report. By default, the list shows only active reports. To 

view all reports, click the Include inactive check box at the top of the list. 

If a report was created and you have full permissions regarding the report and its query items, 

then you can edit, view, run, duplicate, or delete the report from the Custom reports list. If a 

custom report was added as part of package, then it will have a package name, and you will only 

be able to view, run, or duplicate the report.

Create custom reports to get insight and answers from the unique information stored in your 

company. Financial reports are based on account groupings such as assets and liabilities, while 

custom reports and dimension structures (such as operational departments) are based on records 

and fields either grouped together or separately. 

You can add a custom report from the Custom reports list or the Reports center page. 

To add a custom report from the Custom reports list: 

1. 
In the Custom reports list, click the Add button. 

The Custom report wizard opens. 

2. 
Follow the steps in Custom Report Wizard (on page 12) to create your custom report. 

To add a custom report from the Reports center page: 

1. 
On the Reports center page, click the New report button, and then select the Create with 

custom report wizard option in the Custom report section. 

The Custom report wizard opens. 

2. 
Follow the steps in Custom Report Wizard (on page 12) to create your custom report.

##### Selecting the Primary Data Source
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 19*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Selecting the Primary Data Source 

Choose a record or transaction as a starting point for your report.  

Records 

A record is any piece of information in your company. The records available for selection are 

based on your user permissions; you cannot select a record you don’t have access to. When a 

record is selected, other related information is available for inclusion in your report. 

For example, if you select Customer as your primary data source, you can include column 

information from the Contact, Parent customer, or Customer type records. 

Transactions 

You can select a transaction type as your primary data source, such as A/P invoice, A/R 

adjustment, or Deposits. These options include all header information in the transaction record. If 

you want to include the header information plus any amounts and line-item details from the 

transaction, then select the data source option labeled “detail,” such as A/P invoice detail, A/R 

adjustment detail, or Deposits details. This allows you to access transaction amounts and use the 

custom report writer to add calculated columns later in the process.  

For example, to list all invoices with line items over $10,000, you can start by choosing the data 

source A/P invoice detail. Your report can include columns of information from A/P invoice 

details and related data. 
When you run a custom report for User Permission Activity, this custom report only shows permissions which have been explicitly activated by an administrator. There are other permissi ons which are switched on by other applications, called derived permissions. To see a complete list of your permissions, run a 
User Permissionsreport.

Add Calculated Columns 

The custom report writer also allows you to create column calculations based on the columns you 

selected. 

For example, you can calculate an employee’s commission by multiplying their commission rate 

by the total number of sales invoices attributed to that employee. When you run the report, the 

system displays the calculation in the report in a column with the name you assigned. 

You can add calculations by creating a formula uses columns of information from your data 

source. This lets you perform operations on other columns in your data source, and then show 

results in your report. 

The formulas created follow the mathematical order or operations. Keep the following order of 

operations in mind when you create a formula: 

• 
Calculations inside parentheses are performed first. 

• 
All multiplications and divisions are performed next, working from left to right. 

• 
Lastly, all additions and subtractions are performed, working from left to right. 

To create a formula for a calculated column: 
Calculations can only be applied to columns containing numbers.

1. 
Click the Add button. 

The system opens the Formula Editor box. Use this editor to create a formula from any of 

the information in your primary data source. You can add multiple columns and operator, 

depending on the calculation you want to display. 

2. 
In the Available Report Columns pane, select the column containing the data you want to 

include in the calculation. For example, select AP Invoice Detail Total Due. 

---


<!-- Page 22 -->

The system adds an expression in the Formula pane. 

3. 
Use the basic math operators (addition +, subtraction -, multiplication *, and division /) and 

parentheses to create a formula. For example, click the subtraction operator under the 

Operators column. 

4. 
In the Available Report Columns pane, select the column containing the date included in 

the calculation. For example, select AP Invoice Detail Transaction amount. 

The system displays an expression for the transaction in the Formula pane. 

5. 
In the Calculated column type drop-down list, select the formula format. 

6. 
In the Calculated column name field, enter a label for the column. 

Select the Column Sequence 

1.

2. 
Optionally, use the text box to rename columns in the report.

Add Column Totals 

Select the check boxes next to the columns for which you want to display a summary. You can 

only perform mathematical summaries, such as count, sum, average, std deviation, variance, 

largest, and smallest, on numeric data fields. Text fields are limited to count summaries. 

In a report without grouping, the system displays the calculations at the bottom of the report for 

the entire table. In a report with grouping, the system displays the calculations for each subgroup 

and for the entire table. 

Sort the Columns and Set the Priority 

1. 
Click the drop-down list next to each column title. 

2. 
Select whether you want to sort the column in Ascending or Descending order, or None. 
You can assign an ascending or descending order to a maximum of four columns.

3. 
Drag and drop the columns in the list to change the sorting priority. 

The column in the first position will be sorted first, the next column down will be sorted 

within the first, and so on.

##### Filtering the Report
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Filtering the Report 

You can use filters in your report to limit the data the system displays to the criteria that you 

choose. 

Select a Filter 

You set the first group of filters when you select the columns from your primary data source. 

Other information related to your primary data source are available to use as filters as well and 

are listed under the first group of filters as expandable objects. 

1. 
Expand the object that has the column or field you want to filter. 

2. 
In the Columns column, click a drop-down list, and then select the column by which you 

want to filter. 

3. 
In the Operator column, select the operator you want to use to filter the column. 

See the list of available operators (on page 25). 

4. 
In the Value column, enter the corresponding value. 

This can be a number or a string of text depending on the chosen operator. If you choose 

Includes or Excludes, the value could be a comma delimited list of numbers or text strings. 

5. 
Click the Add filter link below the columns to add more filters in the object. 

6. 
Click the Delete last filter link to remove a filter field. 

Refine the Filters 

By default, all filter conditions are combined with an AND logic. In this step, you can apply more 

advanced logic using OR conditions and group filters. 

1. 
Review the filters you added in the previous step. 

The system displays filter position numbers, which you can use to create your advanced 

filter statement. 

2. 
In the Filter expression field, combine filter position numbers using logical operators and 

parentheses.
