##### Grouping Data
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 26*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Grouping Data 

Enable Grouping 

Set the level of detail you want the system to display in your report by selecting the appropriate 

grouping option. 

• 
No grouping: Select this format if you want to display a flat list of information, with the 

option to show a grand total at the bottom. For example, you can use this format to display 

a list of employees with their contact information, or a list of invoices with their total dollar 

value. 

• 
Grouping: Select this format if you want to arrange the information together and show 

subtotals for grouped rows. By default, the report shows subtotals based on the groups you 

select in succeeding steps. The system automatically includes totals by group. For example, 

you can use this format to display invoice subtotals by customer and invoice totals for all 

customers. 

Group Data by Columns 

You can only group data by columns if you enable the Grouping option in the previous step. 

1. 
Expand the object that contains the column by which you want to group the report. 

2. 
Select the column from the drop-down list. 

When you select multiple columns, the system creates subgroups in the report. 
Grouping the data by more than three columns could distort the data. As a best practice, only group by three or less columns.

Order the Groups 

You can set which groups take priority when sorted. The system sorts the items first by the first 

column, and then by the second column, and so on, creating multiple levels of summary 

information. 

1. 
In the Position column, select the button next to the column you want to move. 

2. 
If a column has child columns, select the Include Children check box to enable the feature. 

3. 
Use the 
 Top, 
 Up, 
 Down, and 
 Bottom arrows to change the sorting priority 

of the column. 

4. 
In the Sort column, use the corresponding drop-down list to select whether you want to 

sort your columns in ascending or descending order. 

Group Totals 

In a report with grouping, the system displays the calculations for each subgroup and for the 

entire table. Select the desired column totals in the Add more totals step. For more information, 

see Defining columns (on page 13).

##### Setting the Report Date and Title
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 27*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Setting the Report Date and Title 

You can set parameters for running the report, such as the reporting period and the title of the 

report. 

1. 
Select a reporting period or a range of dates. 

• 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select monthly, quarterly, or annual options 

that include next, current, and past periods. You can modify this time period by adding 

an As of date value. 

• 
In Start date and End date fields, select an exact date range for the report. 

Type “ p ”in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.

2. 
If your company is comprised of multiple entities with multiple base currencies, set the 

location and department. 

• 
Select the Location and Department for which you want to run the report. 

• 
In the Show for drop-down list, select whether you want to display All locations, This 

location, or Child locations, regardless of the location you selected in the Location 

field. 

3. 
In the Show details field, select whether you want to hide or display the detail lines that 

make up the calculated amounts. Hiding the detail gives you a high-level breakdown of the 

data, showing just subtotal and total calculations. 

4. 
Set the report title and footer. 

• 
In the Report title 1 and Report title 2 fields, enter the first and second lines of the 

report title, respectively. 

• 
In the Footer text field, add information you want to display at the bottom of the 

report pages. 

Titles and footers can use letters, numbers, spaces, and most punctuation. The system 

does not support wild cards and variables.

##### Defining the Chart Output
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 28*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide

Defining the Chart Output 

You can choose to run a chart format to visually display your information. 

1. 
In the Chart type drop-down list, select the type that works best for your report. The default 

option is the Column type. 

To view examples of each type of chart, see Creating graphs from custom reports (on page 

28). 

2. 
Select the visual options. 

• 
Y-axis: The summary value that is set along the vertical axis of the chart. 

• 
X-axis: The summary value that is set along the horizontal axis of the chart. 

• 
Grouping: Sets a third parameter (from Grouped by) for stacked and parallel charts. 

• 
X label: Sets the position for the label on the horizontal axis. 

• 
Y label: Sets the position for the label on the vertical axis. 

• 
Legend: Sets the position for the graph legend. 

• 
Font size: Sets the size of the text used on the chart. 

• 
Graph size: Sets the size of the grid the chart is set over. 

• 
Width: Sets the overall width of the chart in pixels. 

• 
Height: Sets the overall height of the chart in pixels. 
Sometimes a graph is an easier way to view report information. After defining the chart output, you can run the custom report and select Graphas the output type.

Adding Prompts 

The additional prompts you can add at runtime are similar to filters, in that they filter the data 

according to the criteria you set. Unlike filters, these prompts are set up as fields that the user 

specifies at the time they run the report. For example, if you want the user running the report to 

specify the A/R status regarding the invoice from which the item comes, you can add a prompt 

for the A/R Account Label object, and then select the Status field. 

To select a runtime prompt: 

1. 
Expand the section for the object that contains the field. 

2. 
Select the check box next to the field for which you want to add a prompt. 

3. 
Repeat the steps to add more prompts. 
You can select up to six runtime prompts.

If you run the report from the Custom reports list, the system ignores the filters and runs the 

report without any prompts. To ensure that all your filters and prompts are applied, run the 

custom report from the application in which you saved it. Learn more about saving a report to a 

menu (on page 24). 

Labeling and Grouping Prompts 

You only need to label and organize prompts if you chose to include additional prompts in the 

previous step of the custom report writer. 

This page allows you to control how a prompt field will be labeled, how multiple fields will be 

grouped, and whether it will have a prompt at runtime. 

Change the Prompt Label 

By default, the name of the field is provided as the Prompt Label. 

To change the Prompt Label, click the Prompt label field and type the label you prefer. 

Group Prompts 

The Group field allows you to present your prompts in groups when you run the report. 

For example, if you want to group several fields together in a section titled A/R Parameters, for 

each field, type “A/R Parameters” in the Group column. 

On a report with several prompts, grouping fields with meaningful labels can save time for the 

person running the report. 

To add a group, click the Group field, and then type the name of the group you are creating. 
To group all prompts under one label, enter one group name in the top Group field. To group 
prompts under different group names, put different group names in the Group field.

Use Prompts in Memorized Reports

 Top,

 Down, and

Saving the Report 

The final step of the custom report writer allows you to save your report and add your report to 

an application menu. This makes it available to other users who have access to that application. 

Save and Deploy Your Report to an Application Menu 

1. 
In the Name field, type your preferred report name. 

2. 
Select the Add to menu check box. 
To access your report only through the Custom reportslist, leave the 
Add to menucheck 
box clear. However, we recommend that you add your custom report to an application menu. If you run the report from the Custom reportslist, the system omits filters and 
prompts. When you run the report from the application menu, the report presentsall prompts and filters.

3. 
In the Application drop-down list, select the application to which you want to add the 

report. 

4. 
In the Description field, enter optional text to describe your report. 

5. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether you want the report to be Active or Inactive. 

New reports are set to Active by default. 

6. 
Click the Save button at the top of the page to save your report.  

Your report is saved and added to both the application menu you selected and to the list of 

reports. 

Make the Custom Report Available in Other Places 

One of the advantages of custom reports is that you can schedule them to run at different times 

with the same settings and make them available in dashboards and report groups. To take 

advantage of this feature: 

• 
Memorize the report so it can be run again with the same settings. 

• 
Add a memorized report to a dashboard or report group. 

• 
Schedule a memorized report.

##### Operator Definitions
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 31*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Operator Definitions 

The following operators are available for use when filtering: 

• 
Equals: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column matches the text or 

number in the Value field. 

• 
Less than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is less 

than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

greater than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Less or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

less than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen 

column is greater than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Not equal to: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column does not match 

the text or number in the Value field. 

• 
Contains: Displays all records in which a character or group of characters in the chosen 

column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The characters must 

match in the same order. For example, “ox” typed in the Value field may return records for 

Oxygen Inc., Boxing Agency, and Clorox, if those were values in the chosen column. 

• 
Does not contain: Displays all records in which no character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. 

• 
Starts with: Displays all records in which the first character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you have an item ID scheme that 

uses initial letters to identify the product type, you can select the item ID column and set the 

Value field to these letters to display all records for that product type. 

• 
Ends with: Displays all records in which the last character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you tag the end of the item ID for 

all custom order items with the letters “CO,” you can select the item ID column and set the 

value to CO to display all records for custom order items. 

• 
Includes: Displays all records that match items in a comma delimited list in the Value field. 

• 
Excludes: Displays all records that do not match items in a comma delimited list in the 

Value field. 

• 
Field equals null: Displays all records that have a null or empty field. 

• 
Field not equals null: Displays all records that do not have a null or empty field. 

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns.

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 

Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 

of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

% bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank”, like Metropolis Bank. 

Running a Custom Report 

When a custom report is created, the report designer has the option to add (or “deploy”) the 

report to an application, such as General Ledger, Accounts Payable, or Accounts Receivable. 

Deploying the report to an application makes the report available from the application menu and 

from the Report Center. 

To run a report from the Reports center page, go to Running a Report from Reports Center. 

To run a custom report from an application menu: 

1. 
Go to the application whose report you want to run, and then click the corresponding link 

for the custom report that you want to run. 

2. 
Set the filters as needed. 

3. 
Do one of the following options: 

• 
Click View to display the report in HTML. 

• 
Click Print to display the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
Click the Export drop-down list, select your preferred format, and then click Go.

Copying a Custom Report from One Company or Entity to Another 

If you’re using the Custom report wizard and have a report that you want to copy from one 

company to another, you can create a custom package document to transfer your custom report. 
You must have administrator-level privileges to access the Platform Services (or Customization 
Services) application.

Creating a Report Definition Package 

1. 
Sign into the company whose report definition you want to copy. 

2. 
In the Applications menu, select Platform Services (or Customization Services), and then 

select the Custom reports option. The Custom reports page opens. 

3. 
Locate the report that you want to copy, and then click the corresponding View link. The 

Custom report wizard opens. 

4. 
In the Step drop-down list, select Save and add to menu. 

5. 
Click the Export def button. The system downloads the report to your local drive as an XML 

file. 

Preparing the Package 

Modify the package to prepare it for importing to the second company or entity. 

1. 
Open a text edit and paste the following XML wrapper text into a new file: 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 

<customErpPackage 
xmlns:xsi=“http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance”> 

<packageDescription> 

<name>INSERT NAME HERE</name> 

<description>INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE</description> 

<author>AUTHOR NAME</author> 

</packageDescription> 


> **Navigation Path:** `<customReports>`


<!-- Paste the contents of the file here--> 


> **Navigation Path:** `</customReports>`


</customErpPackage> 

1. 
Do not close the file. 

---


<!-- Page 36 -->
Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Adding the Definition to the XML File 

1. 
Using a text editor, open the report XML file you downloaded to your local drive. 

2. 
Copy the entire contents of the file. 

3. 
Go back to the XML wrapper file you created in the previous procedure. 

4. 
Paste the report code into the XML wrapper file in the space after the text <!--Paste the 

contents of the file here-->. 

5. 
Delete the following text: 

<!--Paste the contents of the file here--> 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 
Only delete the second instance of <?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?>. 
This is included in the report XML. The first instance at the top of the file should remain.

6. 
Inside the XML wrapper section, replace the following with your own information: 

• 
INSERT NAME HERE 

• 
INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE 

• 
AUTHOR NAME 

7. 
Save the file with a new name. 

The new file should look similar to the following. The actual report definition was edited for 

this example.

Document Templates Workflow 

The workflow for document templates, from creation to delivery, is as follows: 

1. 
Download and install the Word Merge tool. 

2. 
Log in to the Word merge tool. 

3. 
Open a Word file (on page 44) for your template. 

4. 
If you are working with a blank document, add the static text to the Word document such as 

the title, and your business name and address. If you are working with an existing template, 

change the existing text to reflect your business needs. 

5. 
Use the RealPage Word Merge tool to add placeholders (merge fields) to your document 

template.  

6. 
Sync the document template. 

7. 
Assign the template (on page 58) to a transaction or customer in RealPage Accounting. 

8. 
Test (on page 60) and troubleshoot (on page 62) the template as needed. 

9. 
Print or email the documents. 

Choosing a Word File for Your Document Template

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Printed Doc Templates 
> Template`


The first step in creating a document template is to choose a Word file for the template. To do 

this, you can: 

• 
Create a new Word document from scratch. 

• 
Use an existing Word document that you created previously. 

• 
Export an existing document template from the Printed document templates list to use as a 

starting point, and then edit it in Word. 

After you have selected and opened a Word file, you can customize your custom document 

template to suit the needs of your business. 

Exporting a Document Template from the Printed Document Templates List 

To export an existing document template from RealPage Accounting: 

1. 
In the Printed document templates list, locate the document template you want to use, and 

then click the Template link next to it. 

The Word document exports to your local drive. 

2. 
Open the file in Word and edit the file as needed to suit your company’s needs.

##### Customizing a Document Template in Word
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 51*



##### Content Supported in a Document Template
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 51*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Customizing a Document Template in Word 

There are two key components to customizing your document templates: the formatting power of 

Word and the flexibility of merge fields from the system. Add selected merge fields to your 

document template to display data from the system specific to each customer, and then use 

Word to create tables, bold key information, and format your transactional information the way 

you want it. 

When you are done customizing your document template, save it using a descriptive name so 

that you’ll be able to identify it easily in a list. For example, “NY_sales_invoice.doc.” 
Be sure to save your template as a Word 97-2003 file after you finished customizing your 
document, or you might encounter errors when printing your document.

Content Supported in a Document Template 

You can add the following types of content to a document template: 

• 
Static text 

• 
Merge fields 

• 
Images 

Static Text 

Static text is the actual text in the Word file. This text does not change each time you print or 

email your documents, but instead remains the same. Additionally, since the PDF of your 

document is created in the system, only specific fonts are available, which include: 

• 
Arial 

• 
Calibri Family 

• 
Courier New 

• 
Times New Roman 

• 
Tahoma 

• 
Cambria 

• 
Verdana 

• 
Trebuchet 

Merge Fields 

Merge fields are placeholders that get replaced with data from a particular field in the system at 

the time you create and send the statement. You can add both standard and custom fields to 

your document templates. See Statement Merge Fields (on page 46) for a list of available fields. 

Additional fields are available when you use the RealPage Merge tool. 

---



##### Adding Merge Fields to a Word Document
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 52*



##### Statement Merge Fields
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 52*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Images 

You may want to include your company’s logo in the document template to meet your company’s 

branding guidelines. Document templates in RealPage Accounting support the following image 

file formats: 

• 
PNG 

• 
JPEG 

• 
GIF 

Adding Merge Fields to a Word Document 

You can copy and paste any merge field (on page 46) from a Word document directly into your 

own custom document template to display specific account information from the system.  

Be sure to use the merge fields appropriate to each application, or you might encounter errors 

when printing your document. 

Statement Merge Fields 

These fields are available to you when constructing a custom statement.  

MERGE FIELD 
DESCRIPTION 

CUSTOMERID 
This is the unique identifier of the customer. 

NAME 
This is the name of the customer being billed. 

ENTITY 
This is the name of the billing entity. 

LASTSTATEMENTDATE  
This is the date of last statement. 

BILLCOMPANYNAME 
This is the company’s name as it appears on invoices. 

BILLPRINTAS  
This is the company’s name as it appears on printed 

invoices. 

BILLFIRSTNAME 
This is the first name as it appears on invoices. 

BILLLASTNAME 
This is the last name as it appears on invoices. 

BILLADDR1 
This is the first line of address as it appears on invoices. 

BILLADDR2 
This is the second line as it appears on invoices. 

BILLCITY

##### Adding a Custom Field to a Document Template
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 57*



##### Tips for Working in Word
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 57*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Adding a Custom Field to a Document Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Custom Fields`


You can manually add custom fields (on page 87) that you created to your printed document 

templates. Custom fields are specific to their transaction definition and application areas. For 

example, you cannot add a custom field from Sales Invoice1 to your Sales Invoice2 printed 

document template. 

To add a custom field to your printed document template: 

1. 
In the Custom fields list, find the Field ID of your custom field. 

2. 
In Microsoft Word, press CTRL+F9 to insert merge field brackets. 

3. 
Between the brackets, type MERGEFIELD followed by a space, and then type the field ID in 

all caps. Your merge field should look like this:  

{ MERGEFIELD COMPANY_NAME } 
For the merge fields to work, they must be in all caps, and you must insert a space after the first bracket, between each text grouping, and before the last bracket.

Tips for Working in Word 

When working with your content in your Word document, we recommend the following 

guidelines: 

• 
Start small. Add and test information periodically while you create your document. For 

instance, add your company header first, then test it. After, add your table header, and then 

test that. Adding and testing information to your document template incrementally will help 

you identify any problems you may encounter. 

• 
Turn on paragraph markers in Word to see information grouped together. 

• 
Obtain any images you want to use at the correct size before you insert the images into 

Word. Do not use Word to resize images. 

• 
If you want the logo to appear on every page of your document, place the logo in the 

header of the document. 

• 
Use Word headers and footers for static text you want to display on every page. Consider 

using different headers for your first and last page, an option available in Header and Footer 

Tools. 

• 
Layout your content in separate tables. For example, use separate tables for company 

information, customer information, the transaction header, and transaction line item entries. 

• 
Turn on table grid lines for precise tables.

#### Printed Doc Templates List
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 58*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Printed Doc Templates List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Printed Doc Templates`


Use the Printed document templates list to create customized, professional templates for your 

printed invoices, sales orders, purchase orders, and more across Accounts Receivable and Spend 

Management.  

Document templates combine the formatting power of Microsoft Word with the flexibility of 

merge fields. Together, these components display specific account data from RealPage 

Accounting on your printed documents so that you can share the information you want in the 

format you want. At the time of delivery, the system replaces the merge fields in your Word 

document with the data values specific to the transaction you are printing or sending. Then the 

system reproduces the document template with the transaction data in a PDF document that you 

can send to your customers. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
Add and upload new document templates. 

• 
View, edit, and delete existing document templates. 

• 
Duplicate a document template record to reuse the same settings. 

• 
Download an existing document template in Microsoft Word. 

• 
Export the full list of document template records.

##### Adding and Uploading a Document Template
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 59*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Adding and Uploading a Document Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > 
 Printed Doc 
Templates`


To add a new document template record and upload the template file: 

1. 
Open the Platform Services (Customization Services) menu. 

2. 
Click the 
 Add button next to Printed document templates. 

The Printed document template information page opens. 

3. 
In the Template name field, type a unique name for the document template to identify it in 

lists. For example, you might use a name like “A/R Monthly Invoice.” 

4. 
In the Description field, type a brief description of the document template. 

5. 
In the Locale drop-down list, select the native language in which the document template 

was created. 

6. 
Select the Default template check box if you want all printed documents for this type of 

transaction to use this template. For example, all A/R invoices could use this document 

template by default. 
You can override this setting in individual transaction or customer records. 

7. 
In the Application drop-down list, select the application in which the document template 

will be used. 

8. 
In the Template type drop-down list, select the transaction type for which the document 

template will be used.  

9. 
Click the Choose file button, and then find and double-click the appropriate document 

template Word file to select it. 

The name of the document appears in the Upload template field. 

10. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether to activate or inactivate the document template: 

• 
Active: Make the document template available in drop-down lists.  

• 
Inactive: Hide the document template from lists.  

11. 
Click Save.

Exporting a Document Template

To export an existing document template from RealPage Accounting: 

1.

then click the Template link next to it. 

The Word document exports to your local drive. 

2.

Viewing or Editing a Document Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Printed Doc Templates 
> View or Edit`


You can view or edit the details of a document template record—such as the Template name, 

Locale, or Template type—using the View or Edit links in the Printed document templates list. 

To edit a document template itself, you must open the template file in Microsoft Word and then 

re-upload it to the appropriate document template record in RealPage Accounting. 

Viewing or Editing a Document Template Record 

To view or edit the details of a document template record: 

1. 
In the Printed document templates list, select the View or Edit link next to the desired 

document template record. 

The Printed document template information page opens. 

2. 
View or edit the fields as needed. See Adding and uploading a document template (on page 

52) for field descriptions and instructions. 

3. 
Click Save. 

Editing a Document Template in Microsoft Word 

To edit a document template in Microsoft Word: 

1. 
Open the appropriate Word file from your local machine, or export the appropriate Word 

file (on page 53) from RealPage Accounting. 

2. 
Make any changes to your Word file using formatting tools in Microsoft Word. You can add 

or change merge fields as needed; see Statement merge fields (on page 46) for a list of 

available merge fields. 

3. 
Save any changes made to your custom document template in Microsoft Word. 

4. 
In the Printed document templates list, click the Edit link next to the document template 

record. The Printed document template information page appears.

Assigning a Document Template to a Transaction or Customer 

After you have created and uploaded your document template into the system, you must assign it 

to the desired transactions or customers.  

Overrides 

Document templates assigned to transactions override any default templates. Similarly, you can 

override top-level template assignments at the entity level. However, document templates 

assigned to specific customers override all other template assignments. 

Assigning a Document Template to Accounts Receivable Invoices or Statements 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Configuration > Formatting > Printed 
Document Templates`


To assign a document template to an Accounts Receivable transaction: 

1. 
On the Configure Accounts Receivable page, find the Formatting section. 

2. 
In the Printed document templates sub-section, select the desired document template from 

the Invoice or Statement drop-down list. 

3. 
Click Save. 

---



##### Assigning a Document Template to a Customer
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 66*

Using Platform (Customization) Services

Assigning a Document Template to a Customer 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All  > Customers > Edit > Additional Information 
> Printed Document Templates`


You can assign document templates to specific customers for Accounts Receivable invoices or 

statements. Document templates assigned to customers override the default template and the 

assigned transaction definition template whenever the applicable transaction type is printed for 

the customer. 

To assign a document template to a customer: 

1. 
In the Customers list, locate the desired customer, and then click the Edit link next to it. 

2. 
Click the Additional information tab. 

3. 
Find the Printed document templates section, and then select the desired custom document 

template from the applicable drop-down list. Each drop-down list only displays templates 

associated with the corresponding transaction type. 

4. 
Click Save.

Before you send your documents to a customer using a custom document template, we 

recommend that you preview the template first to be sure the data displays appropriately and 

that the formatting of the document is correct. 
Use a test transaction or draft transaction to test a custom document template to avoid setting the Printed flag.

To preview and test a custom document template: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable menu. 

2. 
Select A/R Invoices. 

3. 
In the applicable transaction list, click Print/Email next to the desired transaction. 

4. 
Click the Print option, and then click OK. The system prints the transaction to a PDF file. 
Depending on your configuration, the PDF file may open in your PDF reader or you may need to open your browser’s Downloads folder 
and open the PDF file from there.

5. 
If you need to make changes to the custom document template in Microsoft Word, then 

re-upload the template to the appropriate custom document template record and repeat 

the test. If something went wrong with your custom do
cument template, use the table(on page 62) to troubleshoot your document template, apply the necessary changes, then re-upload the 
template.

The following table lists common custom document template errors and formatting problems: 

In RealPage Accounting 

Problem 
Resolution 

Can’t upload the custom 

document template to the 

system. 

You need to have permissions to Add and Edit custom 

document template records (Custom Documents) to 

upload templates to the system. Ask your administrator to 

ensure that you have the proper permissions. 

Custom document template 

record stops working.

Word file.

template record in the

The Template type of your custom document template 

record does not match the transaction definition class. For 

example, you might be trying to assign a Statement 

template to an Invoice transaction definition. You can 

either edit your custom document template (on page 54) 

record to match the template type and the transaction 

definition, or you can edit the template record in Platform 

Services (or Customization Services).  

Wrong custom document 

template displays when I print my 

documents. 

Check where your custom document template is assigned. 

Custom document templates assigned to transactions 

override any default templates. Similarly, you can override 

top-level template assignments at the entity level. 

However, custom document templates assigned to specific 

customers override all other template assignments.  

In Microsoft Word 

Problem 
Resolution

corrupted when I try to upload 

my custom document template. 

Save your custom document template as a Word 

97-2003.doc file, then re-upload the Word file to your 

custom document template record. RealPage Accounting 

does not support .docx files. 

Image is jagged or distorted in 

some way. 

Obtain any images you want to use at the correct size 

before you insert the images into Word. Do not use Word 

to resize images.

Merge fields aren’t working. 
This could be due to a few reasons: 

• 
The merge field you inserted into your custom 

document template is not supported by that 

particular application or transaction definition. 

For example, if you try to use an Accounts 

Receivable Invoice merge field in your Spend 

Management or Job Cost Purchase Order Invoice 

document template, it may not work.  

Use our list of merge fields (on page 46) for custom 

document templates to make sure you’re using an 

appropriate merge field for your custom document 

template. 

• 
The merge field was not edited correctly. For 

instance, a correct field looks like 

«COMPANY_NAME», but an incorrect field may 

look like «MERGEFIELD COMPANY_NAME».  

To edit a merge field in Word, do one of the two 

following steps: 

• 
Right-click the field and select Edit field, and 

then make your changes in the Field box. 

• 
Press Alt+F9 to expand your merge fields and 

make your changes there. To compress your 

fields after you are done, press Alt+F9 again. 

• 
Your Word template has not been recalculated to 

display the fields you added. To manually trigger 

a global recalculation of your fields in Word, press 

Ctrl + A to select your entire document, and then 

press F9 to update your fields. After Word has 

recalculated your fields, press ESC to deselect your 

document. If you receive an error where your 

merge field should be, edit your merge field to 

correct the error, and then recalculate again.

<!-- Page 71 -->
Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Table header is not repeating. 
Make sure you have selected the Repeat header rows 

option in Word under Table tools > Layout. If you do have 

this option selected, try the following: 

• 
Create separate tables for each section of 

information. For example, use separate tables for 

your transaction header and your line item entries. 

• 
Turn on table gridlines in Word (Table tools > 

Layout > View gridlines) for accuracy and to be 

sure the correct information is in your table 

header. 

Invoice page break is not 

breaking correctly when there are 

many items. 

Try the following tips for formatting the Items table in your 

template: 

• 
Put the column header text in row 1 of the item 

table. 

• 
Put the item data merge fields in row 2 of the item 

table. 

• 
Make sure the PRENTRY row and any SUBTOTALS 

row have the appropriate TableStart/TableEnd 

declarations. These declarations are included in the 

Insert Merge Fields dialog box. 

•

#### Introduction to Custom Views
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 74*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Introduction to Custom Views 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Custom Views`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > [application] > All > Custom Views`


The way a list is arranged, filtered, and sorted is called a view. RealPage Accounting provides 

standard views for displaying list items or recently viewed or modified list items. In addition, you 

can create custom views to display list items the way you need to see them. 

The Custom views submenu appears in an application’s menu when someone has created a 

custom view for a list in the application. 

After you create a custom view, the system adds it to the Custom views submenu in most main 

applications: 

• 
Company 

• 
Cash Management 

• 
General Ledger 

• 
Accounts Payable 

• 
Accounts Receivable 

• 
Property Management (RealPage Commercial Property Management only) 

Exceptions 

• 
Dashboards: Custom views of the dashboard list appear on the Custom views submenu of 

the Company application. 

• 
Reports: Custom views of financial reports and graphs are available only in the Financial 

reports list and the Financial graphs list. They do not appear in the Reports menu in a 

Custom Views submenu. 

Custom Views and Exporting 

When you’ve mastered creating and deploying custom views, you may find them useful when 

exporting lists. When you export a list, the system includes the information in the current view. 

You can use views to include additional fields or exclude information as needed.

List Views 

After you spend time working with a list, you typically develop preferences for how you like the 

list to be sorted and filtered. You can save your preferred list settings as a view. The example 

shows the list controls of the Locations list. 

• 
The (Views) menu opens a drop-down list of available list views. The default view is All, 

which gives you the unfiltered view of the entire list. When you select a different view, its 

name appears at the top of the drop-down list instead of “All.” 

• 
The Manage views menu lets you save current filters and settings as a view. 

(Views) Menu 

The (Views) drop-down menu displays the available list views: 

a) System-standard list views: RealPage Accounting provides standard list views for displaying 

list items or recently viewed or modified list items. 

b) Custom list views: The custom list views vary based on the views that you have created. 

Saved views include these attributes: 

• 
List of columns to include 

• 
Order in which to present the columns 

• 
Filters to apply 

• 
Sort order 

• 
Name and description of the view 
You can export the definition of the saved view in XML format. See Exporting from Lists for instructions.

Accessing List Views 

RealPage Accounting offers lists throughout the system. At the top level, by default, a list includes 

all available items of its type except: 

• 
Private items: Items that belong to an entity. 

• 
Inactive items: Items with a status set to Inactive. 

When you view an entity at an entity’s level, the system includes only the selected entity’s items 

and items created at the top level. The list excludes items created under other entities. 

Standard Views and Custom Views 

The system provides several standard views. You can also make a custom view, created when you 

filter and sort a list, and then save it. 

a) 
(Views) Menu: This menu appears below the page title. The default view is All. This 

means that the first time that you access the list, the All view is displayed.

(Views) menu
’s text changes from 
Allto 
1099.

b) 
Standard Views: Every list has a standard set of views that appear in the (Views) menu. 

As you work with a list, the system monitors the records that you viewed and changed. 

The system can filter the list to show only the most active records. 

• 
All 

• 
Recently viewed 

• 
Recently modified 

• 
All recently modified 

c) 
Custom Views: After creating a custom view, the view appears as a selection at the 

bottom of the (Views) menu.

After you select a view, the view’s name appears at the top of the drop-down list instead of 

. 

Using Standard and Custom Views to Display Lists 

In RealPage Accounting, almost every list page offers a set of standard views for displaying all 

items, recently viewed or modified items. 

Filtering a List for Recent Records 

The system provides a set of standard views for quickly displaying list items that you recently 

modified or viewed. 

To quickly filter or shorten the list to display only recent records: 

1. 
Click the down arrow beside the (Views) menu, and then click Recently viewed, Recently 

modified, or All recently modified. The system displays only those records that you’ve 

recently viewed or modified. The list is associated with your activity within this group of 

records. If you haven’t yet interacted with these records, filtering for recent activity won’t 

return any records. 

2. 
To return to a view of all records, click the down arrow again, and then select All. 

The system makes the last view sticky, which means that the next time you open the list, 
you’ ll see the last view that you displayed.

Custom Views 

When standard views are insufficient for displaying the list items and values that you need to see, 

you can create a custom view. A custom view can be based on a standard view or another custom 

view, or you can create a completely new custom view.

Adding a New Custom View

Include inactive, Include one-time, Include private, and
 Display hierarchyoptions aren
’ t 
available to users of this view. They can switch to View all to see the options again.

1.

1.

text box. 

3.

The third step is to set up any filters that you want to apply to the columns. 

1.

5.

1. 
For each column, select whether to sort the data in ascending or descending order. If you 

do not want to sort the column, leave it as --None--.

Custom Fields 

This section shows you how to create and manage custom fields, which allow you to capture data

#### Custom Fields List
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 94*

Using Platform (Customization) Services

Custom Fields List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Custom Fields`


The Custom fields list displays a list of all custom fields created for your company or installed as 

part of a package. From this list, you can add, edit, view, delete, and export custom fields. Custom 

fields allow you to capture data that is unique to your business practices. When you add a custom 

field, it can become part of standard forms, such as Order Entry. 
Before adding a custom field, we recommend that you review the help for the parts of RealPage Accounting that you want to customize. For instance, if you’re going to create custom fields for 
purchase orders, then review the definitions, data types, and purposes of the existing fields for purchase orders.

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 95*



##### Creating a New Custom Field
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 95*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

User Types 

The user must have limited or full administrator privileges to manage custom fields. 

Subscriptions 

A subscription to Platform Services or Customization Services is required to manage custom 

fields. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Creating a New Custom Field 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> 
 Custom Fields`


The Custom field wizard walks you through the process of creating your custom field. 

To create a new custom field: 

1. 
In the Custom fields list, click the Add button. 

The Custom field wizard opens. 

2. 
Complete the following steps in the wizard to set up your field: 

• 
Choose an object to extend. 

• 
Choose a data type for the custom field. 

• 
Define the field’s properties or characteristics based on the selected data type. 

• 
Configure deployment options for the field.   
You can also manually add custom fields that you created to your printed document templates. Custom fields are specific to their transaction definition and application areas. For example, you cannot add a custom field from Sales Invoice1 to your Sales Invoice2 printed document template. For more information, see Adding a Custom Field to a Printed Document Template(on page 50).

Step 1: Choose Object to Extend 

The first step in the Custom field wizard is to choose the object for which you are creating a 

custom field. Objects are made up of components—such as fields, relationships, and pages—that 

---


<!-- Page 96 -->
Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

define how the system manages and processes the data records in the object. For example, a 

Collections Activity object may hold records about calls and emails regarding collections.  

1. 
In the Object drop-down list, select the object to which you want to add a custom field. 
If you choose Order entry transaction detail, Inventory control transaction detail
, or Purchase 
order transaction detailas your object, then a second selection field labeled Document type 
appears. This represents the various transaction definitions to which the customization will be added. You can configure a customization to apply to multiple transaction definitions at once.

2. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 2: Choose Field Data Type 

The second step in the Custom field wizard is to choose a data type for your custom field. The 

data type determines what kind of information is stored and displayed in the field. For example, 

when a field has the Date type, it displays a calendar tool to select the date, and the system runs 

calculations against the field as a date. 

1. 
In the Data type drop-down list, select the data type that you want to use for your custom 

field. The data type you select depends on the type of data you want to capture and how 

simple you want the interface to be. You can choose from any of the following data types: 

• 
Check box: This option provides a single check box that reports a true or false value. If 

the user selects the check box, then it reports a value of “True”. If the user clears or 

does not select the check box, then it reports a value of “False”. 

• 
Currency: This option provides a text field to enter a currency amount. Currency is 

handled differently than numbers and needs to be stored as such to take advantage of 

multi-currency applications, currency rounding, and currency symbols in reports.  

• 
Date: This option provides an input field for the user to type a date or select a date 

from a calendar. You can set a date field to auto-fill with the current date. Date fields 

should follow a standard input of MM/DD/YY; it may be helpful to add this to the 

description for your custom field. 

• 
Email: This option provides a text field to enter an email address. Email addresses 

should follow a standard format of name@domain.com. You can set an email field to 

validate that the proper format is used. 

• 
Number: This option provides a text field to enter a numeric value. Numbers are 

handled differently than text strings in that they are used for computations. If the 

custom field will be used as part of a mathematical equation, be sure to set it as a 

number data type.  

• 
Percent: This option provides a text field to enter a numeric value expressed as a 

percentage. 

---


<!-- Page 97 -->
Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

• 
Picklist: This option provides a drop-down list to select a predefined option. This data 

type is helpful to maintain a consistent set of variables in your data and save time for 

the person entering the data. Consider using a picklist any time you want to limit the 

user input to a defined set of options. 

• 
Picklist multi-select: This option provides a drop-down list to select multiple options.  

• 
Sequence: This option provides a field that will auto-populate with the next value in a 

sequence, such as inserting an invoice number one number higher than the last 

invoice number. 

• 
Text: This option provides a text field to input a short string of text. You can also use 

this data type for numbers that you do not want to treat as a number. 

• 
Text area: This option provides a multi-line text field to input a long string of text, 

such as a notes field or a description of services. 

• 
URL: This option provides a text field to input a URL. A URL has a unique format and 

properties. By setting a field to this data type, the system is able to treat the data as a 

link and validate its format.  

• 
Password: This option provides a text field to input a password. To protect the privacy 

of the user’s password, the field will display bullets instead of characters as the user 

types their password. 

2. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 3: Choose (Data Type) Field Characteristics 

The third step in the Custom field wizard is to fill in the field properties and characteristics for the 

data type you chose. For a list of fields by data type, see Custom Field Characteristics by Data 

Type (on page 92). 
Use a label and a description that helps your user understand what type of data they need to enter in the field.

Step 4: Choose Deployment Options 

The fourth and final step in the Custom field wizard is to indicate whether the field is required 

and where it should appear in RealPage Accounting. 

1. 
Select the Field is required check box if you want to make the custom field a required field. 

Depending on the field type, the user must enter a value or select an option in order to save 

the object record. 

2. 
Select the Field is hidden check box if you want to hide the field so that it isn’t displayed on 

the page. This option is primarily used by developers. 

3. 
Select the Show in Site View check box if you want the field to display in Spend 

Management Site Experience. This option appears only if you are creating a custom field for 

A/P invoices, purchase orders, service tickets, or expense reports. See Showing Custom 

Fields in the Site View (on page 97) for more information.

##### Showing Custom Fields in the Site View
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 103*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Showing Custom Fields in the Site View 

You can configure custom fields for A/P invoices, purchase orders, expense reports, and service 

tickets so that they display on those transactions in Spend Management Site Experience. Custom 

fields on invoices, purchase orders, and expense reports appear at the header level or the line 

detail level of the transaction, depending on which object you are creating the custom field for. If 

a custom field is marked as required or hidden, then it will be required or hidden in both core 

Accounting and Spend Management Site Experience. 

To show custom fields in both applications, select the Show in Site View check box in step 4 of 

the Custom field wizard (on page 89). This field appears only when you select certain objects and 

data types. See below for more information. 

Objects 

The Show in Site View check box appears when you are creating a custom field for any of the 

following objects in step 1 of the Custom field wizard: 

• 
A/P invoice: When you select this object, the custom field will appear in the header section 

of the A/P invoice in the Site Experience. 
The custom field must be set to show on the A/P invoicetab to display on A/P invoices in 
Site.

• 
A/P invoice detail: When you select this object, the custom field will appear in the line items 

section of the A/P invoice in the Site Experience.  

• 
Employee expense: When you select this object, the custom field will appear in the header 

section of the expense report in the Site Experience.  

• 
Employee expense detail: When you select this object, the custom field will appear in the 

line items section of the expense report in the Site Experience. 

• 
Purchase order: When you select this object, the custom field will appear in the header 

section of the purchase order in the Site Experience. 

• 
Purchase order detail: When you select this object, the custom field will appear in the line 

items section of the purchase order in the Site Experience. 

• 
Service tickets: When you select this object, the custom field will appear in the service ticket 

details in the Site Experience. 

Data Types  

The Show in Site View check box appears when you select any of the following data types for the 

object in step 2 of the Custom field wizard: 

• 
Check box 

• 
Date 

• 
Picklist 

• 
Multi-picklist

Example

set up the field so that it meets the following conditions: 

• 
The field is a multi-line text box that accepts a long string of text.  

• 
The field appears for A/P invoices in core Accounting and Spend Management Site 

Experience. 

• 
The field is required when users enter new invoices. 

•

To do this, the company creates a new custom field with the following settings: 

•

•

• 
Label: Bill type 

• 
Number of rows to display: 1 

• 
Field ID: BILL_TYPE 

• 
Field is required: True 

• 
Field is hidden: False 

• 
Show in Site View: True 

• 
Field is inactive: False 

• 
Show on page: A/P invoice

Maximum Number of Custom Fields 

Generally, you can add up to 25 custom fields per object. However, the objects and object 

combinations listed below support up to 100 custom fields. 
For the object combinations, the system supports a total of 100 custom fields across all objects listed in the combination. For example, you could create 100 custom fields for the A/P Bill object, but then you cannot create any custom fields for the other objects included in its combination, A/P Adjustment and A/P Payables Payment. However, you could have 30 custom fields for A/P Bill, 60 for A/P Adjustment, and 10 for A/P Payables Payment, or any other combination totaling 100.

Objects 

The following objects support up to 100 custom fields:

Customer

##### Custom Field Example
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 107*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Custom Field Example 

Acme Toy and Lumber has been buying lumber from suppliers in various states. It has become 

important to them to track which items use lumber from reusable and sustainable wood sources 

(i.e. tree farms). They want to be able to add labels to products indicating their renewable wood 

source status. The company controller has been given the task of creating a way to show on the 

item page which products use wood that comes from tree farm suppliers.  

To do this, he creates a custom field with the following settings: 

• 
Object: Item 

• 
Data type: Check box 

• 
Label: Tree Farm Supplied 

• 
Default value: Unchecked 

• 
Field ID: TREE_FARM_SUPPLIED 

• 
Description: Wood for product comes from renewable tree farm. 

• 
Field is required: Unchecked 

• 
Field is hidden: Unchecked 

• 
Field is inactive: Unchecked 

• 
Field set: Empty 

• 
Show on page: General Info

*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 108*

*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 108*

Viewing or Editing a Custom Field 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Custom Fields > View or Edit`


To view or edit a custom field: 

1. 
In the Custom fields list, click the View or Edit link next to the custom field record. 

The Custom field wizard opens. 
If a custom field was installed as part of a custom package, then it will have a package name. You can view custom fields that are part of a package, but you can’t edit, delete, or 
inactivate them. If you need to change a custom field that is part of a package, then contact the package creator.

2. 
Use the Next and Back buttons to navigate through the steps of the wizard, or select the 

desired step from the drop-down list to access the page directly. 

3. 
View or edit the field parameters as needed, and then click the Done or Save button.  

See Creating a New Custom Field (on page 89) for field descriptions and instructions. 

Deleting or Inactivating a Custom Field 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Custom Fields > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Edit`


You can delete or inactivate custom fields, depending on whether you want to retain their data. 
You can’t delete or inactivate custom fields that belong to a package. Instead, you
’ll have to edit 
or delete the package.

Deleting a Custom Field 

If you no longer use a custom field and you no longer need to store the previously entered data 

in RealPage Accounting, then you can delete the field permanently. After you delete a custom 

field record, it can’t be restored. If you’re unsure whether you want to delete it, you can set its 

status to Inactive instead. 

To delete a custom field permanently: 

1. 
In the Custom fields list, click the Delete link next to the custom field that you want to 

delete. 

A confirmation box opens. 

2. 
Click OK to confirm. 

---

Inactivating a Custom Field 

Inactivating a custom field removes it from all drop-down lists and prevents you from using it in 

new transactions. Inactivated fields retain all data that was previously entered in RealPage 

Accounting. 

To inactivate a custom field: 

1. 
In the Custom fields list, click the Edit link next to the custom field that you want to 

inactivate. 

The Custom field wizard opens. 

2. 
Select Step 4: Select deployment options from the drop-down list to jump to this step in 

the wizard. 

3. 
Select the Field is inactive check box. 

4. 
Click Save.

##### Adding a Custom Field to a Document Template
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 112*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Adding a Custom Field to a Document Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Custom Fields`


You can manually add custom fields (on page 87) that you created to your printed document 

templates. Custom fields are specific to their transaction definition and application areas. For 

example, you cannot add a custom field from Sales Invoice1 to your Sales Invoice2 printed 

document template. 

To add a custom field to your printed document template: 

1. 
In the Custom fields list, find the Field ID of your custom field. 

2. 
In Microsoft Word, press CTRL+F9 to insert merge field brackets. 

3. 
Between the brackets, type MERGEFIELD followed by a space, and then type the field ID in 

all caps. Your merge field should look like this:  

{ MERGEFIELD COMPANY_NAME } 
For the merge fields to work, they must be in all caps, and you must insert a space after the first bracket, between each text grouping, and before the last bracket.

Smart Rules 

This section shows you how to add and manage smart rules—conditions that trigger warning or 

error messages to the user. 

---



#### Smart Rules List
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 119*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Smart Rules List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Smart Rules`


The Smart rules list displays a list of all smart rules created for your company or installed as part 

of a package. From this list, you can add, edit, view, delete, or export smart rules. 

Smart rules are conditions that generate warning or error messages to the user. They are set to 

respond to three types of user input:  

• 
Add 

• 
Set 

• 
Delete 

You apply smart rules to an object so that when a user does one or more of those things in an 

object and does not meet the condition, the system displays a warning or error message. Smart 

rules are the key to building compliance into your business processes because you can use them 

to ensure that the business practices you want are enforced in your organization. 
If a smart rule was installed as part of a custom package, then it will have a package name. You can view smart rules that are part of a package, but you can’t edit, delete, or inactivate them. If 
you need to change a smart rule that is part of a package, then contact the package creator.

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 120*



##### Adding a Smart Rule
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 120*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

User Types 

The user must have limited or full administrator privileges to manage smart rules. 

Subscriptions 

A subscription to Platform Services or Customization Services is required to manage smart rules. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Adding a Smart Rule 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> 
 Smart Rules`


The Smart rules wizard walks you through the process of creating your smart rule. 

To add a smart rule: 

1. 
In the Smart rules list, click the Add button. 

The Smart rules wizard opens. 

2. 
Complete the following steps in the wizard to set up your smart rule: 

• 
Choose an object to extend. 

• 
Select properties for the rule. 

• 
Configure deployment options for the rule. 

Step 1: Choose Object to Extend 

The first step in the Smart rules wizard is to choose the object to which you are applying the 

smart rule. Objects are made up of components—such as fields, relationships, and pages—that 

define how the system manages and processes the data records in the object. For example, a 

Collections Activity object may hold records about calls and emails regarding collections. 

1. 
In the Owner object drop-down list, select the object for which you are creating a smart 

rule. 
If you choose Order entry transaction detail, Inventory control transaction detail
, or Purchase 
order transaction detailas your object, then a second selection field labeled Document type 
appears. This represents the various transaction definitions to which the customization 

---


<!-- Page 121 -->
Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

will be added. You can configure a customization to apply to multiple transaction definitions at once.

2. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 2: Select Rule Properties 

The second step in the Smart rules wizard is to select properties for the rule. These properties 

define when and how a response is sent back to the user. 

1. 
In the Type drop-down list, select the type of response that the system should send to the 

user when they trigger the smart rule: 

• 
Error: Select this option to require the user to go back and change something before 

they can proceed. For example, you could use an error message when you want to 

make a field required that isn’t normally required by RealPage Accounting. 

• 
Warning: Select this option if you want to point out a rule violation to the user but still 

allow them to continue with the operation. For example, you could use a warning 

message to remind users to upload an external document—such as a work order—for 

the record they are creating. 

2. 
In the Events field, click the Select link to open a multi-select box, and then select which 

user event(s) can trigger the smart rule: 

• 
Add: The system evaluates the rule whenever a user creates a new record for the 

object. 

• 
Set: The system evaluates the rule whenever a user changes a record for the object. 

• 
Delete: The system evaluates the rule whenever a user deletes a record from the 

object. 

You can choose any or all of these options. See Using the Multi-Select Box for more 

information. 
The system does not currently support warnings for Delete events— it converts them to 
errors instead.

3. 
In the Condition field, type the condition(s) that must be met so that the system does not 

send the user an error or warning message. See Writing Conditions and Injections (on page 

116) for instructions and examples. 
This is a required field. You cannot leave this field blank because the system would always evaluate the smart rule condition as true, meaning it would never generate a warning or error message.

4. 
In the Error message field, type the text message that you want to display to the user when 

the rule is violated. You can include injections in an error message. See Writing Conditions 

and Injections (on page 116) for instructions and examples.

##### Writing Conditions and Injections
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 122*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Field lookupbutton to insert injections from RealPage Accounting instead 
of adding them manually. See Adding an Injection Using Field Lookup(on page 123) forinstructions.

5. 
Click the Next button to continue to the next step in the wizard. 

Step 3: Select Deployment Options 

The third and final step in the Smart rules wizard is to indicate whether the field is required and 

where it should appear in RealPage Accounting. 

1. 
In the Smart rule ID field, type a unique identifier for the smart rule. IDs are limited to 

alphanumeric characters and underscores with no spaces. 

2. 
In the Description field, type the purpose of the smart rule and how you intend to use it. 

3. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether the smart rule is active or inactive. 
Inactivating a smart rule retains the event settings you defined, but removes the rule from the Smart ruleslist and prevents it from triggering.

4. 
When finished, click the Done button to save the smart rule. 

Writing Conditions and Injections 

Conditions and injections are at the heart of smart rules and smart events. Conditions are decision 

mechanisms built into activities to determine when they will appear and how they will behave 

according to certain criteria.  

The types of elements that go into a condition are: 

• 
Injections (placeholders for field values) 

• 
Literals 

• 
Operators 

• 
Methods 

Example 

If the rule is that customers with addresses outside the United States require prepayment of 

invoices, you could write a condition to state that the country associated with the Bill to contact 

“equals” United States or the Invoice amount due “equals” zero. The condition would be written 

as follows: 

({!ARINVOICE.BILLTO.CONTACT.MAILADDRESS.MAILADDRESS.COUNTRY!} == 
“United States”) || ({!ARINVOICE.TOTALDUE!} == “0”) 

If this condition is not met (either the country equals United States or the amount due equals 

zero), then the system will display a warning or error message. 

---


<!-- Page 123 -->
Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Alternatively, if you want to bring up a warning message every time an Add or Set event occurs, 

you could set the condition to evaluate a required field for the Owner object as blank. For 

example, if you want a warning message to appear any time a bill is added, you could write the 

condition as follows: 

{!APBILL.WHENCREATED!}==‘‘ 

Because a bill always has a Date, the system will always evaluate this condition as false and thus 

trigger a warning. 
You can find out if a field is required bylooking it up in the Catalog.In the 
Applicationsmenu, 
select Platform Services, and then select the 
Catalog option in the 
Customization toolssection. Click the desired object to expand it and view a full list of fields. If the Required column next to 
t he field is set to 
“ true
”, then the field is required.

Injections 

Conditions can contain values from fields in RealPage Accounting. Placeholders for field values 

are called injections. 

The most basic injection uses the ID of the current object being extended, followed by a period, 

followed by the ID of the field in that object. The {! and !} characters are used as opening and 

closing tags, respectively. An injection is written as follows: 

{!OBJECT_ID.FIELD_ID!} 
You can use the Field lookupbutton in the upp
er-right corner of the 
Smart ruleswizard to insert 
injections from RealPage Accounting instead of adding them manually. This button appears only on the Step 2: Select rule propertiespage. See 
Adding an Injection Using Field Lookup(on page 123 ) for more information.

Literals 

Literals are actual values inserted into a condition. A literal can be a number or a text string. All 

literals are wrapped in quotation marks (single and double quotes are interchangeable). Rather 

than referring to data with an injection, you may want to add a value to your condition. 

For example, in the condition: 

{!ARINVOICE.TOTALENTERED!} > “10000” 

The value 10000 is a literal value. 

An example of a literal as a text string would be: 

{!SHIPTO.MAILADDRESS.COUNTRY!} != “USA” 

The value USA is a literal value. 

---


<!-- Page 124 -->
Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Operators 

Operators are the work horses of conditions. The operator is the character or group of characters 

between the injections or literal values that joins them arithmetically and determines the type of 

comparison being made. Valid operators include: 

• 
Comparison operators 

• 
Arithmetic operators 

• 
Logical operators 

Comparison Operators 

> 
Greater than 

< 
Less than

Greater than or equal to 

<= 
Less than or equal to 

== 
Equal to 

!= 
Not equal to 

Arithmetic Operators 
Arithmetic operators follow the standard order of operations. Use parentheses as needed.

+ 
Added to

Subtracted from

Divided by 

Divide- by
-zero operations are not allowed.

& 
Mod (modulo) 

Modulo- by
-zero operations are not allowed.

^ 
Exponent 

==

Not equal to 

Logical Operators 

|| 

or 

OR (requires one value or condition) 

&& 

and 

AND (requires both values or conditions)

IN 
Shorthand for multiple OR conditions; allows multiple values or 

conditions 

NOTIN 
Allows the exclusion of multiple values or conditions

( ) 
Parentheses (indicates precedence of operations) 

xor 
Exclusive or 

? : 
Ternary operator 

When working with conditions, consider using ternary operators to 

avoid writing overly long conditions. The expression (expr1) ? 

(expr2) : (expr3) evaluates to expr2 if expr1 evaluates to “true”, 

and expr3 if expr1 evaluates to “false”. For example, the following 

expression can be used to display an error when a user posts a bill line 

to account 5000 and location SJC: 

({!APBILLITEM.ACCOUNTNO!} == ‘5000’ && 
{!APBILLITEM.LOCATIONID!} == ‘SJC’) ? false : true 

Methods 

Methods are functions that output a value based on certain input parameters. For a method’s 

parameter, you can use an injection parameter or a literal. The tables below list the methods that 

can be used in a condition. 

Date Methods 
All dates and times are returned in your company’s time zone, as specified in the 
Company 

informationpage.

today() 
Returns the current date in the format MM/DD/YYYY. 

timeofday() 
Returns the current time in HH24:MI:SS format. 

weekday() 
Returns the current weekday in 1-based format. For example: Monday 

= 1 and Sunday = 7. 

year() 
Returns the year in YYYY format. For example: 2015. 

month() 
Returns the current month in 1-based format. For example: January = 1 

and December = 12. 

day () 
Returns the current day of the month in 1-based format. For example: 

1st of the month = 1.
