##### Understanding Injection Parameters
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 127*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Illegal Characters 

Certain characters are illegal in conditions: 

• 
$ (dollar sign) 

• 
; (semi-colon) 

Mixing Data Types 

In general, mixing data types in conditions does not cause errors because conditions are loosely 

typed. You may, however, get some interesting results. 

For example, consider the expression {!VENDOR.VENDORID!} + {!VENDOR.TOTALDUE!}. 

If the VENDORID value is “WIDGETS” and the TOTALDUE value is 950.25, then the expression will 

evaluate to WIDGETS950.25. 

Understanding Injection Parameters 

Injection parameters are the paths and fields that make up an injection. Valid injections can 

contain parameters from the following sources: 

• 
System fields 

• 
Custom fields 

• 
Nexus fields 

• 
Nexus custom fields 

• 
Universal objects 

• 
Universal values 

System Fields 

Every object in RealPage Accounting has an associated set of fields. These are listed below the 

object in the Catalog. A field is described by the object ID, followed by a period, followed by the 

field ID: 

OBJECT_ID.FIELD_ID 

For instance, if you want your injection to reference the due date field for an invoice, then you 

would use the Catalog to look up the INVDOCUMENT object. You would then find the ID for the 

due date field, WHENDUE, and write the injection parameter: 

INVDOCUMENT.WHENDUE 

Custom Fields 

Injection parameters can also reference custom fields the same way they reference system fields. 

Custom fields can be found in the Catalog under the object they extend. 

---


<!-- Page 128 -->
Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Nexus Fields 

Different objects are joined together at their nexus. Injections become more complex as the steps 

increase between the current object being extended and the desired field. In cases where multiple 

steps occur, understanding the nexus becomes important. 

The nexus of an object and the objects associated with it are listed in the Catalog in the Nexus 

(related objects) section: 

The above figure shows the nexus for the INVDOCUMENT object. Even though you have chosen 

to extend this object, you can add injections using any fields that belong to the objects listed in 

the Nexus (related objects) section. To write this path, start with the root object and then add 

values from the Object path column. End with the name of the field from the last related object. 

For example, if you’re extending the INVDOCUMENT object and want an injection to point to the 

Primary URL field of the CONTACT object listed next to the BILLTO object path, you would write: 

INVDOCUMENT.BILLTO.URL1 

Alternatively, suppose you want an injection that points to the Country field for the CONTACT 

object listed next to the BILLTO object path. In this case you would jump from the nexus for 

INVDOCUMENT to the nexus for CONTACT and use a field from the MAILADDRESS object path 

and related MAILADDRESS object. You would write: 

INVDOCUMENT.BILLTO.MAILADDRESS.COUNTRY 

You might use this injection as part of a smart rule that brings up a warning for all invoices where 

the Bill to address is outside of your own country. 

Nexus Custom Fields 

When a custom field is added to an object, it shares all of the nexus relationships of that object. 

You can use a nexus relationship to write an injection for a custom field in a related object. 

Universal Objects 

In some objects, standard and custom user fields may be included as injection parameters 

regardless of the object being extended. Objects that contain fields that can always be used as 

injection parameters include: 

---


<!-- Page 129 -->
Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

• 
CURRENTUSER 

• 
CURRENTCOMPANY 

• 
USERPROFILE 

Universal Values 

You can always use the following injection parameters. 

Parameter 
Description 

{!USERPROFILE.SESSIONID!} 
Session ID 

{!USERPROFILE.LOGIN!} 
User ID 

{!USERPROFILE.NONSTANDARDPERIO

DS!} 

Custom accounting periods 

{!USERPROFILE.EMAIL!} 
User email 

{!USERPROFILE.LOCATIONKEY!} 
Key (not ID) of the current entity, if user slides into it 

{!USERPROFILE.ISMULTIENTITY!} 
If company is multi-entity 

{!USERPROFILE.CONTEXTLOCATION!} 
Returns ROOT if at the shared top level 

Returns [LOCATIONKEY]--[LOCATIONNAME] of the entity if at the 

individual entity level

Formatting Dates in a Smart Rule 

When creating a smart rule, make sure you format any dates in the smart rule expression as 

YYYY.MM.DD. 

For example, if you use a merge field to verify that a General Ledger entry is made on or after 

December 25, 2013, it would look something like this: 

{!GLENTRY.ENTRY_DATE!}>=‘2013.12.25’ 

Smart Rule Example 

A controller at a construction company wants to limit the size of transactions that certain 

employees can enter. To do this, he sets up a currency type custom field, USER_BILL_LIMIT, on the 

user record so he can set the transaction amount per user. He then sets up a smart rule that 

compares the current transaction amount with the limit on the user record.  

The smart rule has the following settings: 

• 
Object: AP Invoice 

• 
Type: Error 

• 
Events: Add, Set 

• 
Condition: {!CURRENTUSER.USER_BILL_LIMIT!} == ‘‘ || {!APBILL.TOTALENTERED!} <= 

{!CURRENTUSER.USER_BILL_LIMIT!} 

• 
Error message: {!CURRENTUSER.LOGINID!} may not enter bills for an amount greater than 

{!CURRENTUSER.USER_BILL_LIMIT!}. This bill total is {!APBILL.TOTALENTERED!} 

• 
Smartlink ID: VALIDATE_BILL_LIMIT 

• 
Description: Rule that displays a warning when the user attempts to enter a bill that exceeds 

their transaction limit. 

• 
Status: Active 

Viewing or Editing a Smart Rule 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Smart Rules > View or Edit`


To view or edit a smart rule: 

1. 
In the Smart rules list, click the View or Edit link next to the desired smart rule. 

The Smart rules wizard opens. 
If a smart rule was installed as part of a custom package, then it will have a package name. You can view smart rules that are part of a package, but you can’t edit, delete, or 
inactiv ate them. If you need to change a smart rule that is part of a package, then contact 
the package creator.

3.

See Adding a Smart Rule (on page 114) for field descriptions and instructions. 

Deleting or Inactivating a Smart Rule 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Smart Rules > Delete`

You can delete or inactivate smart rules, depending on whether you want to retain the event 

settings you defined. 
You can’t delete or inactivate smart rules that belong to a package. Instead, you
’ll have to edit 
or delete the package.

Deleting a Smart Rule 

If you no longer use a smart rule, then you can delete the rule permanently. After you delete a 

smart rule, it can’t be restored. If you’re unsure whether you want to delete it, you can set its 

status to Inactive instead. 
If you delete a smart rule, you’ll lose all settings defined in the rule.

To delete a smart rule permanently: 

1. 
In the Smart rules list, click the Delete link next to the smart rule that you want to delete. 

A confirmation box opens. 

2. 
Click OK to confirm. 

Inactivating a Smart Rule 

Inactivating a smart rule retains the event settings you defined, but removes the rule from the 

Smart rules list and prevents it from triggering. 

To inactivate a smart rule: 

1. 
In the Smart rules list, click the Edit link next to the smart rule that you want to inactivate. 

The Smart rules wizard opens. 

2. 
Go to Step 3: Choose deployment options. 

3. 
Set the Status field to “Inactive”. 

4. 
Click Save.

You can copy a smart rule from one company to another using a custom package file. To do this, 

export the definition of the smart rule, include the exported definition in a package file, and then 

import that package file into the target company. 

Exporting the Definition of the Smart Rule 

Export the definition of the smart rule to an XML file: 

1. 
In the Smart rules list, click the Edit link next to the smart rule that you want to export. 

The Smart rules wizard opens. 

2. 
Click the Export def button in the upper-right corner of the page. 

The definition exports to an XML file. 

Preparing the Package File 

Modify the package to make it ready to import to the second company: 

1. 
Open a text editor and paste the following XML wrapper text into a new file: 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 

<customErpPackage 
xmlns:xsi=“http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance”> 

<packageDescription> 

<name>INSERT NAME HERE</name> 

<description>INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE</description> 

<author>AUTHOR NAME</author> 

</packageDescription> 

<smartLinks> 

<!-- Paste exported definition here --> 

</smartLinks> 

</customErpPackage> 

2. 
Open the exported XML file in a different window and copy its contents. 

3. 
Paste the copied code into the XML wrapper, overwriting <!-- Paste exported definition here 

-->. 

4. 
Replace the following text with your own information: 

• 
INSERT NAME HERE 

• 
INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE 

• 
AUTHOR NAME

Save the file with a new name.

The Smart events list displays a list of all smart events created for your company or installed as 

part of a package. From this list, you can add, edit, view, delete, and export smart events.  

Smart events allow you to trigger a follow-up action to a task if certain conditions are met. For 

example, if you receive a bill marked as urgent, then a smart event could trigger a follow-up 

action of sending an email about the urgent bill. 

Other actions you can take with smart events include: 

• 
API calls to update bill descriptions based on total due. 

• 
HTTP posts to send bill record numbers to an external application. 
If a smart event was installed as part of a custom package, then it will havea package name. You can view smart events that are part of a package, but you can’t edit, delete, or inactivate them. 
If you need to change a smart event that is part of a package, then contact the package creator.

#### About Smart Events
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 144*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

About Smart Events 

Smart events trigger when a given event occurs and certain conditions are met. When users add, 

set, or delete a record in the object to which the smart event was added—and that action meets 

the condition of the smart event—the system sends an email or posts to a web address. 

Smart events allow you to automate communications and processes according to events that 

arise in your financial management. A smart event can be something as simple as an email to the 

sales manager when a sales quote over $10,000 is created.  

Synchronous API Smart Events 

If you create an API smart event, then you can choose to make it synchronous to avoid abnormal 

asynchronous errors. Synchronous API smart events: 

• 
Ensure that a group of events, including the triggering action, are executed in order as a set. 

• 
Eliminate the possibility of collision, concurrency, and overwriting between events since they 

are executed consecutively. 

• 
Provide direct feedback when a synchronous API Smart Event fails through an error 

message. 

This lets you think in terms of a larger task where synchronous API smart events are sub-tasks. If a 

sub-task fails, then nothing is saved (not even the triggering action), and the system issues an 

error message. 

Execution Triggering and Rollback 

When an action triggers a synchronous API smart event, the system attempts to execute all 

synchronous events that are part of the resulting chain of actions in alphabetical order according 

to Smartlink IDs. This happens before the triggering action is committed. If the chain executes 

successfully, then the triggering action is saved and any asynchronous smart events are then 

executed. 

If the chain of synchronous events cannot be executed successfully, then the system rolls back the 

transaction or record, prevents the original trigger action, and displays an error message. Any 

synchronized API smart events or asynchronous smart events (of any type) that would have been 

part of the chain are not executed. 

Best Practices 

Though powerful, using synchronous API smart events adds a level of complexity, so you should 

be thoughtful in your approach. For this reason, we recommend the following: 

• 
Use synchronous API smart events only when you want to ensure that a group of events are 

executed in a particular order. 

• 
Use synchronous API smart events when you want to ensure that the triggering action is 

tied to the event actions in terms of success and failure. 

---

• 
Use a prefix in your IDs to group your related synchronous API smart events and ensure that 

they occur in the correct order. A good format to use is NAMESPACE_PREFIX_DESC. For 

example, you could use a convention like: 

•

then inactivate the synchronous API smart events in the package and create new ones.

The Smart events wizard walks you through the process of creating your smart event.

Step 1: Choose Object to Extend

Collections Activity object may hold records about calls and emails regarding collections. 

1.

event.

, or Purchase

To select the event properties:

enclosed in the body of the request message. An example is a smart event that posts 

bill record numbers to an external app after the bill record number is recorded. 

• 
Log: Creates a log entry in the smart event log file. 

• 
API: Makes an API call to modify data in the company; for example, updating the bill 

description if the total due on a bill is greater than $5,000. 

2. 
In the Events field, click the Select link to open a multi-select box, and then select which 

user event(s) can trigger the smart event: 

•

•

object.

object.

For example, if the event is that the CEO receives an email when a user posts an invoice with 

an amount greater than $10,000, then the condition would be written as follows:

If this condition is met, then an email is sent when the invoice is created.

##### Writing Conditions and Injections
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 149*

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

Step 4: Select Deployment Options

Writing Conditions and Injections 

Conditions and injections are at the heart of smart rules and smart events. Conditions are decision 

mechanisms built into activities to determine when they will appear and how they will behave 

according to certain criteria.  

The types of elements that go into a condition are: 

• 
Injections (placeholders for field values) 

• 
Literals 

• 
Operators 

• 
Methods 

Example 

If the rule is that customers with addresses outside the United States require prepayment of 

invoices, you could write a condition to state that the country associated with the Bill to contact 

“equals” United States or the Invoice amount due “equals” zero. The condition would be written 

as follows: 

({!ARINVOICE.BILLTO.CONTACT.MAILADDRESS.MAILADDRESS.COUNTRY!} == 
“United States”) || ({!ARINVOICE.TOTALDUE!} == “0”) 

If this condition is not met (either the country equals United States or the amount due equals 

zero), then the system will display a warning or error message. 

Alternatively, if you want to bring up a warning message every time an Add or Set event occurs, 

you could set the condition to evaluate a required field for the Owner object as blank. For 

example, if you want a warning message to appear any time a bill is added, you could write the 

condition as follows: 

{!APBILL.WHENCREATED!}==‘‘ 

Because a bill always has a Date, the system will always evaluate this condition as false and thus 

trigger a warning. 

---


<!-- Page 150 -->
Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Catalog.In the 
Applicationsmenu, 
select Platform Services, and then select the 
Catalog option in the 
Customization toolssection. Click the desired object to expand it and view a full list of fields. If the Required column next to 
the field is set to “ tr ue
”, then the field is required.

Injections 

Conditions can contain values from fields in RealPage Accounting. Placeholders for field values 

are called injections. 

The most basic injection uses the ID of the current object being extended, followed by a period, 

followed by the ID of the field in that object. The {! and !} characters are used as opening and 

closing tags, respectively. An injection is written as follows: 

{!OBJECT_ID.FIELD_ID!} 
You can use the Field lookupbutton in the upper
-right corner of the 
Smart ruleswizard to insert 
injections from RealPage Accounting instead of adding them manually. This button appears only on the Step 2: Select rule properties p age. See 
Adding an Injection Using Field Lookup(on page 123 ) for more information.

Literals 

Literals are actual values inserted into a condition. A literal can be a number or a text string. All 

literals are wrapped in quotation marks (single and double quotes are interchangeable). Rather 

than referring to data with an injection, you may want to add a value to your condition. 

For example, in the condition: 

{!ARINVOICE.TOTALENTERED!} > “10000” 

The value 10000 is a literal value. 

An example of a literal as a text string would be: 

{!SHIPTO.MAILADDRESS.COUNTRY!} != “USA” 

The value USA is a literal value. 

Operators 

Operators are the work horses of conditions. The operator is the character or group of characters 

between the injections or literal values that joins them arithmetically and determines the type of 

comparison being made. Valid operators include: 

• 
Comparison operators 

• 
Arithmetic operators 

• 
Logical operators 

---

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide

+

-zero operations are not allowed.

conditions

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

? : 
Ternary operator 

When working with conditions, consider using ternary operators to 

avoid writing overly long conditions. The expression (expr1) ? 

(expr2) : (expr3) evaluates to expr2 if expr1 evaluates to “true”, 

and expr3 if expr1 evaluates to “false”. For example, the following 

expression can be used to display an error when a user posts a bill line 

to account 5000 and location SJC: 

({!APBILLITEM.ACCOUNTNO!} == ‘5000’ && 
{!APBILLITEM.LOCATIONID!} == ‘SJC’) ? false : true 

Methods 

Methods are functions that output a value based on certain input parameters. For a method’s 

parameter, you can use an injection parameter or a literal. The tables below list the methods that 

can be used in a condition. 

Date Methods 
All dates and times are returned in your company’s time zone, as 
specified in the Company 

informationpage.

today() 
Returns the current date in the format MM/DD/YYYY. 

timeofday() 
Returns the current time in HH24:MI:SS format. 

weekday() 
Returns the current weekday in 1-based format. For example: Monday 

= 1 and Sunday = 7. 

year() 
Returns the year in YYYY format. For example: 2015. 

month() 
Returns the current month in 1-based format. For example: January = 1 

and December = 12. 

day () 
Returns the current day of the month in 1-based format. For example: 

1st of the month = 1. 

pastdate(count, 

unit) 

Returns a date in the past as of the number of units specified. Valid 

units are day, month, year. 

String Methods 

strtolower(param

eter) 

Returns the parameter in all lowercase.

eter)

substr(parameter, 

start, [length]) 

Returns a substring of the parameter that is length characters long 

starting from the start character. If the length is not specified, then the 

method returns the entire string beginning at the start character. String 

positions are zero-based, so to start at the first character, start should 

be 0; to start at the second character, start should be 1; and so on. 

right(parameter, 

length) 

Returns a substring of the parameter starting length characters from 

the end. For example, right(‘foobar’, 3) would return ‘bar’.

Returns a substring of the parameter starting at the beginning and 

containing length characters. For example, left(‘foobar’,3) would return 

‘foo’.

within the parameter. This method is case sensitive.

##### Understanding Injection Parameters
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 154*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Mixing Data Types 

In general, mixing data types in conditions does not cause errors because conditions are loosely 

typed. You may, however, get some interesting results. 

For example, consider the expression {!VENDOR.VENDORID!} + {!VENDOR.TOTALDUE!}. 

If the VENDORID value is “WIDGETS” and the TOTALDUE value is 950.25, then the expression will 

evaluate to WIDGETS950.25. 

Understanding Injection Parameters 

Injection parameters are the paths and fields that make up an injection. Valid injections can 

contain parameters from the following sources: 

• 
System fields 

• 
Custom fields 

• 
Nexus fields 

• 
Nexus custom fields 

• 
Universal objects 

• 
Universal values 

System Fields 

Every object in RealPage Accounting has an associated set of fields. These are listed below the 

object in the Catalog. A field is described by the object ID, followed by a period, followed by the 

field ID: 

OBJECT_ID.FIELD_ID 

For instance, if you want your injection to reference the due date field for an invoice, then you 

would use the Catalog to look up the INVDOCUMENT object. You would then find the ID for the 

due date field, WHENDUE, and write the injection parameter: 

INVDOCUMENT.WHENDUE 

Custom Fields 

Injection parameters can also reference custom fields the same way they reference system fields. 

Custom fields can be found in the Catalog under the object they extend. 

Nexus Fields 

Different objects are joined together at their nexus. Injections become more complex as the steps 

increase between the current object being extended and the desired field. In cases where multiple 

steps occur, understanding the nexus becomes important. 

---


<!-- Page 155 -->
Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

The nexus of an object and the objects associated with it are listed in the Catalog in the Nexus 

(related objects) section: 

The above figure shows the nexus for the INVDOCUMENT object. Even though you have chosen 

to extend this object, you can add injections using any fields that belong to the objects listed in 

the Nexus (related objects) section. To write this path, start with the root object and then add 

values from the Object path column. End with the name of the field from the last related object. 

For example, if you’re extending the INVDOCUMENT object and want an injection to point to the 

Primary URL field of the CONTACT object listed next to the BILLTO object path, you would write: 

INVDOCUMENT.BILLTO.URL1 

Alternatively, suppose you want an injection that points to the Country field for the CONTACT 

object listed next to the BILLTO object path. In this case you would jump from the nexus for 

INVDOCUMENT to the nexus for CONTACT and use a field from the MAILADDRESS object path 

and related MAILADDRESS object. You would write: 

INVDOCUMENT.BILLTO.MAILADDRESS.COUNTRY 

You might use this injection as part of a smart rule that brings up a warning for all invoices where 

the Bill to address is outside of your own country. 

Nexus Custom Fields 

When a custom field is added to an object, it shares all of the nexus relationships of that object. 

You can use a nexus relationship to write an injection for a custom field in a related object. 

Universal Objects 

In some objects, standard and custom user fields may be included as injection parameters 

regardless of the object being extended. Objects that contain fields that can always be used as 

injection parameters include: 

• 
CURRENTUSER 

• 
CURRENTCOMPANY 

• 
USERPROFILE 

---

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 
© 2025 RealPage, Inc.

Smart Event Examples 

Email Example 

A common use for smart events is to send an email message when a user action occurs. For 

example, you might want to send out an email when a new vendor is added. 

To do this, create a smart event with the following settings: 

• 
Owner object: Vendor 

• 
Action: Email 

• 
Events: Add 

• 
Condition: (Leave blank to generate for every vendor creation) 

• 
Email: john.doe@example.com 

• 
Subject: New vendor added: {!VENDOR.NAME!} : {!VENDOR.VENDORID!} 

• 
Body: {!VENDOR.NAME!} was added on {!VENDOR.WHENMODIFIED!}. Review new vendor 

process including manager notifications. 

• 
Smart link ID: NEW_VENDOR_EMAIL 

• 
Description: Send email to john.doe@example.com when a new vendor is added. 

• 
Status: Active 

HTTP Post Example 

A lighting manufacturer is running an e-commerce site where they make their products available 

directly to the consumer. They also sell wholesale and direct over-the-phone or fax, which they 

enter directly into RealPage Accounting. They want to make sure that they let web customers 

know in real time if a product will be on backorder. This means that the website’s database must 

keep an up-to-date inventory. 

To do this, the manufacturer creates a smart event that makes an HTTP post to a web application 

that updates the inventory when an order is placed in RealPage Accounting: 

• 
Owner object: Inventory Control Transaction Detail 

• 
Document type: Inventory Transfer Out 
You can create similar events to send inventory adjustment information when an item’ s 
inventory increases by extending the Inventory Transfer Indocument.

• 
Action: HTTP Post 

• 
Events: Add 

• 
Condition: (Leave blank to generate for every sales order creation) 

• 
URL: http://www.example.com/.../example.php 

• 
Method: POST 

• 
Arguments:

##### Deleting or Inactivating a Smart Event
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 160*

Using Platform (Customization) Services 

RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide

Deleting or Inactivating a Smart Event 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Smart Events > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Smart Events > Edit`


You can delete or inactivate smart events, depending on whether you want to retain the event 

settings you defined. 
You can’t delete or inac
tivate smart events that belong to a package. Instead, you’ll have to edit 
or delete the package.

Deleting a Smart Event 

If you no longer use a smart event, then you can delete the rule permanently. After you delete a 

smart event, it can’t be restored. If you’re unsure whether you want to delete it, you can set its 

status to Inactive instead. 
If you delete a smart event, you’ll lose all settings defined in the event.

To delete a smart event permanently: 

1. 
In the Smart events list, click the Delete link next to the smart event that you want to delete. 

A confirmation box opens. 

2. 
Click OK to confirm. 

Inactivating a Smart Event 

Inactivating a smart event retains the event settings you defined, but removes the rule from the 

Smart events list and prevents it from triggering. 

To inactivate a smart event: 

1. 
In the Smart events list, click the Edit link next to the smart event that you want to 

inactivate. 

The Smart events wizard opens. 

2. 
Go to the Choose deployment options page. 

3. 
Set the Status field to “Inactive”. 

4. 
Click Save.

*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide.pdf`, Page 164*

Copying Smart Events to a Different Company 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Object Customization 
> Smart Events > Edit`


You can copy a smart event from one company to another using a custom package file. To do 

this, export the definition of the smart event, include the exported definition in a package file, and 

then import that package file into the target company. 

Exporting the Definition of the Smart Event 

First, export the definition of the smart rule to an XML file: 

1. 
In the Smart events list, click the Edit link next to the smart event that you want to export. 

The Smart events wizard opens. 

2. 
Click the Export def button in the upper-right corner of the page. 

The definition exports to an XML file. 

Preparing the Package File 

Next, modify the package to make it ready to import to the second company: 

1. 
Open a text editor and paste the following XML wrapper text into a new file: 

<?xml version=‘1.0’ encoding=‘UTF-8’?> 

<customErpPackage 
xmlns:xsi=“http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance”> 

<packageDescription> 

<name>INSERT NAME HERE</name> 

<description>INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE</description> 

---

Chapter 2: Using Platform (Customization) Services 

© 2025 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Accounting Platform (Customization) Services User Guide 

<author>AUTHOR NAME</author> 

</packageDescription> 

<smartLinks> 

<!-- Paste exported definition here --> 

</smartLinks> 

</customErpPackage> 

2. 
Open the exported XML file in a different window and copy its contents. 

3. 
Paste the copied code into the XML wrapper, overwriting <!-- Paste exported definition here 

-->. 

4. 
Replace the following text with your own information: 

• 
INSERT NAME HERE 

• 
INSERT DESCRIPTION HERE 

• 
AUTHOR NAME 

5. 
Save the file with a new name. 

The new file should look similar to this: 

Importing the Package File 

Finally, import the package file into the target company: 

1. 
Sign in to the target company. 

2. 
In the Applications menu, select Platform Services, and then select 
 Custom packages. 

The Import customization package page opens. 

3. 
Click the Choose file button, navigate to your package file, and then click Open. 

4. 
Click the Import button. 

The file now appears in the Packages list.

About Platform (Customization) Services

Platform Services, or Customization Services, provides tools
that you can use to extend the data and objects that are part of
RealPage Accounting. You can add fields, create and run
custom reports on your data, send automated emails, or create
rules and warnings that guide users along your unique
business practices. You must have administrator privileges to
use this application.

Adding a Custom Report

1. Add a custom report from either the Custom reports list or the
Reports center page:

▪
In Platform Services (or Customization Services), select
the All tab, and then select 
 Custom reports.
▪
In Reports, select the All tab, and then select Reports
center. Click the New report button, and then select the
Create with custom report wizard option.

2. Follow the steps in the Custom report wizard:

▪
Select a record or transaction type as the primary data
source.
▪
Select columns to add to the report.
▪
Add any calculated columns.
▪
Change the column sequence and labels as you want them
to appear in the report.
▪
Select the columns for which you want to display totals,
such as sum, count, average, and so on.
▪
Reorder columns to set their sort priority and select
whether to sort them in ascending or descending order.
▪
Define filters for columns as needed.
▪
Select whether or not to group data in the report.
▪
Set the default reporting period, report title, and footer text.
▪
Select a chart format to visually display the report data.
▪
Add additional runtime prompts as needed.
▪
Label and organize any prompts you chose.
▪
Save and deploy your report in an application menu.

3. Click Save.

Running a Custom Report

Deploying a custom report to an application makes the report
available from the application menu and from the Reports
center.
To run a report from an application:

1. In the application menu, point to the Custom reports option in
the Reports section, and then select the custom report you want
to run.
2. Set the report date range, filters, and additional options as
needed.

3. Choose a report output:

▪
Click View to display the report in HTML.
▪
Click Print to display the report as a printable PDF file.
▪
Click Export, select your preferred format, and then click
Download the file.

To run a report from the Reports center:

1. In Reports, select the All tab, and then select Reports center.
2. Select the Custom reports tab.
3. Use the drop-down list to filter the list of reports by a specific
application, or use the search bar to search by report name.
4. Click the report name.
The report opens on a separate browser tab.

Choosing a Word File for a Document Template

The first step in creating a document template is to choose a
Word file for the template. To do this, you can:

▪
Create a new Word document from scratch.
▪
Use an existing Word document that you created previously.
▪
Export an existing document template from the Printed
document templates list to use as a starting point, and then
edit it in Word.

After you have selected and opened a Word file, you can
customize your custom document template to suit the needs of
your business.

Customizing a Document Template in Word

You can add the following types of content to a document
template:

▪
Static text: This is text in the Word file that does not change
when you print or email your documents.
▪
Merge fields: These are placeholder fields that are replaced
with data from a field in the RealPage Accounting system. You
can add both standard and custom fields to your document
templates.
▪
Images: Document templates support images in PNG, JPEG,
or GIF file formats.

Adding a Custom Field to a Document Template

1. In the application menu, select the All tab, and then select
Custom fields.
2. Find the Field ID of your custom field.
3. In Microsoft Word, press CTRL+F9 to insert merge field
brackets.
4. Between the brackets, type MERGEFIELD followed by a space,
and then type the field ID in all caps; for example,
{ MERGEFIELD COMPANY_NAME }.

Adding and Uploading a Document Template

1. In Platform Services (or Customization Services), select the
All tab, and then select 
 Printed doc templates.
2. Type a Template name.
3. Type a Description.
4. Select the Locale for which the template was created.
5. Select the Default template check box if you want all printed
documents for this type of transaction to use this template.
6. Select the Application in which the template will be used.
7. Select a Template type.
8. Click Choose file, and then select a Word file for the template.
9. Set the Status to either "Active" or "Inactive".
10. Click Save.

Testing a Document Template

Preview and test your document template before using it in
customer documents.

1. In Accounts Receivable, select the All tab, and then select
A/R invoices.
2. Click Print next to the desired transaction.
The system prints the transaction to a PDF file.
3. Preview the document template.
4. If you make changes to the document template in Microsoft
Word, then make sure you re-upload the file to the appropriate
document template record.
5. Repeat testing as needed.

Assigning a Document Template to a Transaction or Customer

After you upload your document template, make sure you
assign it to the desired A/R transactions or customers.
To assign a document template to an A/R transaction:

1. In Accounts Receivable, select the Setup tab, and then select
Configuration.
2. In the Formatting section, select the desired document template
from the Invoice or Statement drop-down list.
3. Click Save.

To assign a document template to a customer:

1. In Accounts Receivable, select the All tab, and then select
Customers.
2. Click Edit next to the desired customer.
3. Select the Additional information tab.
4. In the Printed document templates section, select the desired
document template from the applicable drop-down list.
5. Click Save.

### Adding a Smart Event
*Source: `RP Accounting Platform (Customization) Services QS.pdf`, Page 2*

Creating a Custom View

1. In any application list, click Manage views, and then select
Create new view.
2. Follow the steps in the Create new view wizard:

▪
Select the columns to include in the view.
▪
Rearrange the column sequence and rename columns as
needed.
▪
Define any filters that you want to apply to the columns.
▪
Set the default sort order for the data in each column, and
then rearrange columns to determine their sort priority.
▪
Name and deploy the view.

3. Click Save.

Creating a Custom Field

1. In Platform Services (or Customization Services), select the
All tab, and then select 
 Custom fields.
2. Select the Object to which you are adding a custom field.
3. Click Next.
4. Select a Data type for the custom field.
5. Click Next.
6. Define the field's properties or characteristics based on the
selected data type.
7. Click Next.
8. Choose deployment options for the custom field:

▪
Select Field is required to make the custom field a
required field.
▪
Select Field is hidden to hide the field from the object
page.
▪
Select Field is inactive if you are no longer using the field
but want to retain data previously entered in the field.
▪
To add the field to an existing page, type the name of the
page section in the Field set field, and then select the tab
on which this section appears from the Show on page
drop-down list.
▪
To add the field to a new section, type a name for the new
section in the Field set field, and then select an existing
tab from the Show on page drop-down list or enter a new
tab name in the text field to add the section to a new tab.

9. Click Done.

Adding a Smart Rule

1. In Platform Services (or Customization Services), select the
All tab, and then select 
 Smart rules.
The Smart rules wizard opens.
2. Select the Owner object for which you are creating the smart
rule.
3. Click Next.
4. Select the Type of system response when a user triggers the
smart rule:

▪
Error: Requires the user to go back and change something
before they can proceed.
▪
Warning: Points out a rule violation to the user but still
allows them to continue.

5. Select one or more Events that can trigger the smart rule:

▪
Add: The user creates a new record.
▪
Set: The user changes a record.
▪
Delete: The user deletes a record.

6. Type the Condition(s) that must be met so that the system
does not display an error or warning.
Conditions are written expressions that contain injections,
literals, operators, and methods.
7. Type the Error message text to display to the user.
You can use the Field lookup button to insert injections in
conditions and error messages.
8. Click Next.
9. Type a unique Smart rule ID.
10. Type a Description for the smart rule.
11. Set the Status to "Active" or "Inactive".
12. Click Done.

Adding a Smart Event

1. In Platform Services (or Customization Services), select the
All tab, and then select 
 Smart events.
2. Select the Owner object for which you are creating the smart
event.
3. Click Next.
4. Select the follow-up Action that the system should take when
the smart event condition is met:

▪
Email: Sends an email.
▪
HTTP post: Sends an HTTP POST request to a web
server to post or retrieve the data enclosed in the request
message.
▪
Log: Creates a log entry in the smart event log file.
▪
API: Makes an API call to modify data in the company.

5. Select one or more Events that can trigger the smart event:

▪
Add: The user creates a new record.
▪
Set: The user changes a record.
▪
Delete: The user deletes a record.

6. Optionally, type the Condition(s) that must be met for the
selected action to occur.
Conditions are written expressions that contain injections,
literals, operators, and methods. You can use the Field lookup
button to insert injections.
7. Click Next.
8. Define the properties of the action type you selected.
9. Click Next.
10. Type a unique Smart link ID.
11. Type a Description for the smart event.
12. Set the Status to "Active" or "Inactive".
13. Click Done.

Getting Started 

RealPage Accounting Mobile is a mobile application available for iOS and Android 

devices that allows you to add, submit, and approve or decline transactions and 

expenses. 

This guide provides instructions for installing and using the RealPage Accounting 

Mobile app. With this app, you can: 

• 
View and approve A/P invoices, purchase orders, expense reports, and A/P 

payments. 

• 
Access Storefront to browse vendor catalogs and submit purchase orders. 

• 
Track charges made using your company-issued debit card and submit 

transactions as expenses.

download from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store, respectively. Make sure that you meet

app’s compatibility information for details about supported devices and software versions.

## Approval Workbench
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 9*

© 2024 RealPage, Inc. 

Approval Workbench 

This chapter provides instructions for reviewing and approving transactions in the 

RealPage Accounting Mobile app. 

Transactions enter the approval process as follows: 

1. 
A user creates a transaction and submits it. (When an approval process is 

configured, transactions are Submitted to the approval process rather than 

Posted).  

2. 
The system evaluates the transaction to see if it requires approval based on the 

policies that your company configured. 

3. 
When a transaction requires approval (because it matches an approval 

requirement), the system puts the transaction into the approval workflow. When 

it does not require approval, the system bypasses the approval process and 

posts the transaction. 

4. 
The system sends email notifications to approvers (if your company chose to 

enable approval notifications), and then tracks the progress of the transaction 

through the approval workflow. 

5. 
The transaction enters the Approval Workbench where it waits to be approved. 

Any A/P invoices, purchase orders, expense reports, or A/P payments that 

appear in the workbench approval queue also appear in the RealPage 

Accounting Mobile app on the corresponding transaction page. 

6. 
Approvers review the transactions in either the Approval Workbench or the 

mobile app, and then approve or decline them as needed. 

7. 
The system stores the history of approval events for auditing purposes on the 

Approval History page.

### Approval Workbench Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 10*

Approval Workbench 

© 2024 RealPage, Inc.

Approval Workbench Page 

 Navigation Menu > Home 

The Approval Workbench page displays a summary of transactions that are pending approval, 

grouped by transaction type and age.  

The list includes three columns: 

a) (Transaction Type): This column is labeled by transaction type, either A/P Invoices, 

Purchase Orders, Expenses, or Payments. Transactions that are fewer than seven days old 

are grouped as “0-7”, while transactions that are greater than seven days old are grouped as 

“7+”. 

b) Total: This is the sum of all transaction amounts for the category. 

c) Count: This is the total number of transactions in the approval queue for the category. Tap 

this number to view the list of transactions on the corresponding transaction page.

### Add A/P Invoice Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 44*

A/P Invoices 

© 2024 RealPage, Inc.

Add A/P Invoice Page 

 Navigation Menu > A/P Invoices >  Add 

Use the Add A/P Invoice page to enter general information about an invoice, define the invoice’s 

line items, apply costs and discounts to each line item, and attach an image of the invoice. From 

there, you can submit the invoice and monitor its status in the A/P Invoices list. If needed, you 

can save the invoice in a draft state to save your progress and submit it later. Draft invoices do 

not affect the General Ledger or any subledgers. 

If the A/P invoice approval feature is enabled, then the status of the invoice changes as it works its 

way through the approval workflow: 

• 
Submitted: The invoice is saved and submitted to the approval queue. 

• 
Partially Approved: The invoice is approved by at least one approver in the workflow, but 

more approvals are required. 

• 
Declined: An approver declined the invoice. 

• 
Posted: The invoice is approved and posted to the General Ledger. 

Posted

---



#### Adding an A/P Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 45*

Chapter 3: A/P Invoices 

© 2024 RealPage, Inc. 

Adding an A/P Invoice 

 Navigation Menu > A/P Invoices >  Add 

To add an A/P invoice: 

1. 
In the 
 Navigation Menu, select the A/P Invoices menu option. 

The A/P Invoice list opens. 

2. 
Tap the 
 Add button. 

The Add A/P Invoice page opens. 

Entering Basic Information About the A/P Invoice 

1. 
In the Invoice Date field, select the date on the invoice. 

2. 
In the Due Date field, select the date by which the invoice must be paid. 

3. 
In the G/L Posting Date field, select the date on which to post the invoice to the General 

Ledger.  

4. 
In the Invoice # field, type the invoice number. 

5. 
In the Total Amount field, type the total amount due for the invoice. 

6. 
In the Vendor field, type the name of the vendor who is the source of the invoice. As you 

type, a drop-down list of matching vendor records appears so you can select the 

appropriate vendor ID. 

7. 
In the Description field, type a description of the transaction. 

8. 
In the Reference Number field, type the reference number from the invoice, if any. 

Entering the Line-Item Details 

You can enter up to four (4) line items when creating an A/P invoice through the mobile app. To 

create an invoice with additional line items, use the core applications in the RealPage Accounting 

system. 

1. 
In the Property field, type the name of the location to which you are assigning the line-item 

expense. As you type, a drop-down list of matching location records appears so you can 

select the appropriate location ID. 

2. 
In the Account field, type the name of the account to which you are categorizing the 

line-item expense. As you type, a drop-down list of matching account records appears so 

you can select the appropriate account number. 

3. 
In the Amount field, type the cost of the line item. 

4. 
In the Memo field, type a brief memo for the line item. 

---


<!-- Page 46 -->
A/P Invoices 

© 2024 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
In the Department field, type the name of the department to which you are assigning the 

line-item expense. As you type, a drop-down list of matching department records appears 

so you can select the appropriate department ID. 

6. 
If a specific unit is associated with the line item, then select the unit from the Unit 

drop-down list. 

7. 
Tap the + Add line link to add a new line item. 

Distributing Costs and Discounts Across All Transactions 

Use these steps to apply costs and discounts and distribute them equally across all transactions in 

the A/P invoice: 

1. 
In the Tax field, type the tax amount for all transactions on the invoice.  

2. 
In the Shipping field, type the shipping cost of the invoice. 

3. 
In the Discount field, type the dollar value of the discount on the invoice. 

4. 
Tap the Distribute button to distribute the costs or discounts evenly across all transactions 

on the invoice. 

Attaching an Invoice Image 

Tap the Attach Invoice button to upload an image of the invoice from your phone’s photo 

gallery, either by choosing an existing photo from an album or by taking a photo as you create 

the invoice. Tap the Delete button to remove an attached image and replace it with a new one. 

Saving or Submitting the A/P Invoice 

When entering the invoice details, you can save it as a draft or submit it for approval. The system 

validates required fields, such as departments and locations, when you submit the invoice. If any 

of the required fields are empty or you have entered invalid information, an error message 

displays. You must address the errors before you can submit and post the invoice. 

• 
Tap the Draft button to save your progress on the transaction without affecting the 

subledger or General Ledger. Later, you can edit the draft (on page 43) and submit it. 

• 
Tap the Submit button to submit the A/P invoice for approval (if A/P invoice approvals are

empty or invalid, an error message will display. You must address the errors before you can 

submit and post the expense report.

subledger or General Ledger. You can then add more line items to the draft before 

submitting it.

approvals are enabled) or post the expense report (if expense report approvals are not

### Storefront Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 72*

© 2024 RealPage, Inc.

Storefront Page 

 Navigation Menu > Storefront 

Use the Storefront feature to browse vendor catalogs and create an online shopping list directly 

in the mobile app. When you first access the Storefront page, a list of properties appears. Select 

the property you want to shop for to access its online catalogs. 

On the Storefront page, you can perform a quick search for an item by product name, product 

type, or stock keeping unit (SKU) across all vendors or select a vendor catalog to shop from a 

specific vendor. There are two types of catalogs: 

• 
Hosted Catalog: These are vendor catalogs that RealPage hosts and maintains. 

• 
Punchout Catalog: These are vendor catalogs that the vendor hosts and maintains. 

From the vendor catalog, you can: 

•

• 
View general product details including the product description, price per unit, and SKU. 

• 
View the product image. 

•

*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 73*

Selecting a Vendor Catalog 

 Navigation Menu > Storefront 

To shop for a property, you must access its catalogs. 

Selecting a Property to Shop For 

When you first access the Storefront feature, a list of properties appears. Select the property you 

want to shop for from the list. The Storefront page loads with all available vendor catalogs for the 

property. 

Selecting a Vendor Catalog 

On the Storefront page, select a vendor catalog from the Hosted Catalog or Punchout Catalog 

section. Hosted catalogs are hosted and maintained by RealPage, while punchout catalogs are 

hosted by the vendor.

selected vendor catalog. If you selected a punchout catalog, then the vendor’s website opens in 

the mobile app.

page. From this page, you can also update item quantities and line items, view your available 

spending budget, and enter promotional codes for the vendor, if any. 

Reviewing the Items in Your Cart

 Delete icon.

In the Order Type field, select the Standard option.

can select a different G/L account. 

3. 
In the Unit field, select the unit associated with the line item.

## PC Charges
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 83*

© 2024 RealPage, Inc. 

PC Charges 

This chapter describes how to submit expenses for petty cash (PC) card transactions. PC cards are prepaid debit 

cards for which you have been issued or authorized to use for unexpected or incidental expenses, such as office 

supplies, meals, and travel expenses. 

In This Chapter 

PC Charges List ......................................................................................................................................... 80 

C H A P T E R 7 

---



### PC Charges List
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 84*

PC Charges 

© 2024 RealPage, Inc.

PC Charges List 

 Navigation Menu > PC Charges 

Property management companies (PMCs) often have petty cash (PC) on hand for unexpected 

expenses. With RealPage Accounting, the company can issue prepaid debit cards to authorized 

users to more easily track and manage purchases made using these funds. When cardholders 

purchase items with the card, their transactions appear in RealPage Accounting so they can 

submit them as expenses. 

If you’ve been issued or authorized to use a PC debit card, then you can view and submit 

transactions as expenses directly from the RealPage Accounting Mobile app using the PC Charges 

list. From this list, you can: 

a) Filter card transactions by a specific property or merchant. 

b) Retrieve a list of your most recent transactions. 

c) View the purchase date, property, merchant, and amount associated with each transaction. 

d) Tap on a transaction amount to submit the transaction as an expense. 

---



#### Filtering Transactions by Property or Merchant
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 85*



#### Retrieving Your Most Recent Transactions
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 85*

Chapter 7: PC Charges

Filtering Transactions by Property or Merchant 

 Navigation Menu > PC Charges 

You can search the PC Charges list by property or merchant to filter the list of card transactions. 

• 
On the PC Charges list, type the name of a property or merchant in the 
 Property / 

Merchant field. 

The list automatically refreshes with any transactions that match or contain the text string. 

Retrieving Your Most Recent Transactions 

 Navigation Menu > PC Charges 

You can tap the Get Charges button to retrieve a list of any new card transactions you’ve made 

that day. Transactions are automatically updated every day. 

---



### Submit Expense Page
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 86*

PC Charges 

© 2024 RealPage, Inc.

Submit Expense Page 

 Navigation Menu > PC Charges > (Amount) 

Use the Submit Expense page to enter the expense type for a petty cash card transaction before 

submitting it as an expense. Optionally, you can enter a memo or add an attachment to the 

transaction, such as a receipt. 

After the expense is successfully submitted, the system creates an A/P invoice with the PC 

Reimbursement invoice type to request reimbursement for the petty cash. 

---



#### Submitting an Expense
*Source: `RP Accounting Mobile App User Guide.pdf`, Page 87*

Chapter 7: PC Charges 

© 2024 RealPage, Inc. 

Submitting an Expense 

 Navigation Menu > PC Charges > (Amount) 

To submit a petty cash (PC) transaction as an expense: 

1. 
In the PC Charges list, tap the Amount of the transaction you want to expense. 

The Submit Expense page opens. 

2. 
Tap and select a category for the expense from the Expense Type drop-down list. 

3. 
Optionally, type a brief Memo for the expense. 

4. 
Optionally, tap the Attach Receipt button to upload an existing photo from your camera roll 

as an attachment or take and upload a new photo. 

5. 
Tap the Submit Expense button. 

The system creates an A/P invoice to request reimbursement for the expense. The card 

transaction is removed from the PC Charges list. 

---
